Until you consider cigars like the fabulous Davidoff 702 Series, it might seem counterintuitive for an industry so rooted in tradition that a cigar company needs to continuously innovate to stay ahead of the pack. Plus, it's doubly confusing when you realize that Davidoff is already light years ahead of the competition. But how do you think they achieved such a feat in the first place? Exactly. Consistently pushing the envelope in both quality and taste, their smokes are always world-class due to an obsessive commitment to a unique experience. That's why several of Davidoff's famous blends have now been transformed by a proprietary '702 Habano' wrapper, an Ecuadorian-grown hybrid of three types of Cuban tobacco. (See more Davidoff Cigars ) The name and size of each cigar in the 702 Series will be familiar to Davidoff aficionados since they are the same as many of their most popular sticks. Indeed, each cigar contains the identical Dominican longleaf filler and binder tobaccos found in the original frontmark, with the succulent '702' wrapper being the one obvious change. What a change it is too because the expected toasty and warm Davidoff flavor is granted a sweeter, chewier dimension thanks to the uniformly thick and dark outer leaf. Expect loads of molasses, stone fruit, cocoa, and spice atop the already complex medium-bodied profile. It's a simple fact of life that stepping into the world of Davidoff is going to cost you somewhat more than you're used to spending, but how often do you have the opportunity to smoke a cigar of such caliber? We've got them at a price you'll have a hard time beating anywhere else so treat yourself to a few Davidoff 702 Series today and don't look back.

Davidoff Nicaragua is a fantastic full-bodied cigar from one of the most legendary names in the business. Developed and constructed in Nicaragua, this gorgeous luxury stick features only the best of the best tobaccos, including rich Nicaraguan ligero fillers from Esteli, Condega, and Ometepe, a binder from Jalapa, and an exquisite 10-year-aged Nicaraguan Habano seed Rosado wrapper. Coming in at #3 on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 of 2013, this cigar continues the Davidoff legacy, extending it now to lovers of full-bodied sticks as well. (See more Davidoff Cigars ) An ultra-complex smoking experience starts with an avalanche of creamy, earthy flavor, coating one's palate from front to back. This soon develops into a ballet of caramel and spice, with noticeable nuances of leather, grass, and coffee. The long, heavy finish leaves a trail of white pepper on the back of the nose, and this cigar only gains intensity as it smokes down. Davidoff Nicaragua is the pinnacle of luxury. This cigar is intended for only the most demanding and experienced aficionados. Beginners should look elsewhere. The rich, earthy flavors of Davidoff Nicaragua pair wonderfully with single-malt scotch or port wine, making this a tremendous way to end a steak dinner. Similar cigars might include Ashton VSG and Oliva Serie V Melanio. Simply put, Davidoff Nicaragua can be best described as smokeable opulence.

It is rare to find something truly unique in the cigar business, where it sometimes seems as though every possible blend of different tobacco types has been exhausted, but the new Davidoff Yamasa cigar is a bold stride into a new world. If you think that is an incredible statement, consider the fact that the name Yamasa comes from a region of the Dominican Republic initially not suited for growing fine longleaf, until Davidoff got involved. Through science, determination, and sheer hard work over the course of 20 years, the result is a robust, flavorful leaf perfect as both wrapper and binder, to complete the decadent Nicaraguan and Dominican tobaccos that serve as filler. (See more Davidoff Cigars ) As attractive as they are tasty, each richly brown, Davidoff Yamasa is subtly sweet through the nose and gives off hints of loam and cedar sawdust during a cold draw test. The tobaccos in the filler, cultivated in Esteli and Condega, add a characteristic Nicaraguan earthiness and spice to the initial profile, while the Dominican Piloto and Mejorado do their part of melding the most robust flavors between layers of creamy leather and vanilla. However, it is the namesake Yamasa-grown leaves, both the San Vicente binder and the sun-kissed wrapper; that bring depth to the medium-full bodied smoke with the tastes of café con leche, almond, oak, and nutmeg. Pricey but worth every penny, the Davidoff Yamasa cigar is an experience to be sought by all aficionados at some point in their smoking career. Why not make that time right now and get some while your SO is looking the other way? We will ship them to you as on the wings of eagles, and then you can both delight in the rich flavor and aroma for which Davidoff is so famous. Just make sure you get at least two sticks, so you will not have to share.

It's finally happened that after so long of a self-imposed rest, the Rocky Patel A.L.R. Second Edition cigar is here. Where else but the cigar world would you find short term gains so easily tossed aside in the hopes for future glory? When first blended by Patel, the secret blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos that form the core of these hefty vitolas could have been an immediate hit, raking in a bunch of 90 ratings and perhaps a Top 25 for the year. Instead, after sealing the luscious longleaf beneath a phenomenally fermented San Andres wrapper, Rocky let the cigars gently age for at least two solid years. His patience has been rewarded with a #4 of 2023 ranking on the back of a stellar score of 96 . You experienced aficionados out there might think you are prepared for the rich depth of flavor provided by the Rocky Patel A.L.R. Second Edition, but you'll be glad to know you're not. Occupying that same heady airspace as the Arturo Fuente Rosado Sungrown Magnum R or the Alec Bradley Tempus, these unique cigars taste like nothing else in the world. Sure, there's plenty of cocoa to be had thanks to the San Andres wrapper and Patel's aging rooms have imparted just the right amount of cedar , but beyond the earth, the malt, the vanilla cream there sits something more. Past the sweet butterscotch, the bitter orange peel, the meaty char, and the hints of spicy red pepper , you'll find those subtle, unnamed, and elusive flavors that all cigar smokers seek. Aged. Limited. Rare. While Rocky had time on his side in creating these medium-full bodied gems, you however do not. Only 120,000 Rocky Patel A.L.R. Second Edition cigars were produced and if that seems like a lot, just wait. They'll be sold out before you know it. Enjoy them while they're here, because we don't know when we'll see their like again.
The Taste Immerse yourself in the opulence and decadence of this medium-plus blend, where notes of caramel, honey, coffee, espresso, and chocolate intertwine harmoniously.

Rocky Patel is one of the most dominant forces in the cigar industry—and for good reason. He has something for everyone, from budget-friendly bundles to ultra-premium, high-priced cigars that only the most adventurous aficionados would dare to try. His portfolio covers the full spectrum, but with the Rocky Patel Conviction, he hasn’t just raised the bar—he’s created a whole new one. This is more than just another cigar; it’s a personal passion project for Rocky Patel, something he’s been dreaming of for decades. Now, that vision has become a reality with this truly special, small-batch, limited-edition release. Crafted at the renowned Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A. in Nicaragua, Conviction is one of the most exciting blends to ever bear Rocky Patel’s name. The filler is a meticulously curated selection of premium long-fill tobaccos from Condega and Estelí—two of Nicaragua’s most fertile growing regions. Sourced primarily from Rocky’s own family farms, this tobacco was harvested in 2014, meaning each leaf has aged for no less than 10 years before rolling. The double binder is also Nicaraguan, while the wrapper is an exceptional Mexican San Andrés leaf, aged for four years in tercios—bundles of tobacco wrapped in royal palm leaves. Sounds intriguing? You’re not alone. Conviction earned a stellar 95 rating from Cigar Aficionado and claimed the #7 spot on the magazine’s prestigious Top 25 Cigars of 2024. The packaging is just as extraordinary as the cigar itself. Housed in a burl-finish cedar chest, each vitola is presented in an elegant golden coffin, adorned with stunning gold and silver double bands. This is some of the most striking packaging Rocky Patel has ever offered—fitting for such a remarkable release. And when we say the construction is flawless, we mean it. Only two pairs of highly skilled bunchers and rollers at the factory were responsible for producing this box-pressed beauty, limiting production to just 250 cigars per day. Between these four artisans, there’s a combined 130 years of cigar-making experience. Still need convincing? Let the effortless draw and razor-sharp burn do the talking. Sit back as thick, silky white smoke envelops your palate in a symphony of complex flavors. The journey begins with bold notes of black pepper and cedar, which soon mellow as rich cocoa and earthy undertones take center stage. Hints of creamy coffee and baker’s spices dance across the taste buds, while a crisp Nicaraguan spice lingers on the tongue. The finish? Clean, sweet, and endlessly satisfying. Medium-full-bodied, perfectly balanced, and undeniably complex, the 6 ½” x 52 Toro delivers an unforgettable smoking experience—one that lives up to the name Conviction. Rocky Patel Conviction falls into a certain category of cigars deemed by many to be “unattainable.” The price point, the severely limited inventory across the board, and the high demand among the most experienced connoisseurs in the world all play together to make this stick just out of reach for most. But if you dare, we sincerely promise it will be a cigar like nothing you’ve ever tried. Conviction pairs well with bourbon, dark rum, or coffee and should be enjoyed slowly, with plenty of time to savor each and every puff. This special occasion smoke can be thought of as being a highly-upgraded version of the famous Rocky Patel Decade , so if you gravitate towards that general flavor category, you have an idea of what you’re getting yourself into. Only 5,000 boxes of cigars were rolled during the production run, so if you stumble upon a chance to grab this, go for it. You likely won’t get another. The word “Conviction” is defined as a firmly held belief or opinion. We may not know for sure why Rocky named this blend the way he did, but after smoking this ultra-premium gem, there is no doubt you will have a firmly held opinion that it was perhaps the best cigar you’ve ever smoked.

Its milk chocolate-brown wrapper hints at the bold and enticing flavors that await . The blend features premium Nicaraguan, Honduras & Paraguay fillers selected for complexity and depth, unraveling layers of flavor with every draw.

Right when you thought Rocky Patel couldn’t possibly come up with something new, along comes the Rocky Patel Dark Star to rock the cigar world in typical Rocky style. Made at Nestor Plasencia’s famed El Paraiso factory in Honduras, the Dark Star incorporates a recipe that includes tobacco never before used in a cigar bearing Rocky’s name. This tobacco is grown on the Plasencia farms in Honduras but comes from a seed originating in Paraguay — of all places. Transplanted and cultivated in Honduras, the Paraguayan tobacco is then blended with leaves from Jamastran, Honduras, and Jalapa, Nicaragua to create the filler recipe. The binder is Honduran, and the wrapper is a dark brown Corojo leaf grown in Honduras. The final product, as Rocky Patel states, is a “meticulously crafted cigar that embodies medium-bodied strength and an array of captivating flavors.” Housed in luxurious wooden chests, each Dark Star wears triple white and gold bands, the main band appropriately adorned with a black star that makes the brand easy to spot. Phenomenal construction means an easy draw, plenty of smoke, and a razor-sharp burn line. Black pepper and espresso are the first notes to greet the palate, soon followed by a multi-layered array of flavors including nuts, cocoa, cedar, and citrus. An earthy raw tobacco note lingers in the background, and the finish is sweet and clean. Medium-bodied and precisely balanced, the Dark Star rivals some of the finest sticks on the market. Made for more experienced connoisseurs, the Rocky Patel Dark Star is one of the more premium offerings in Rocky’s ever-growing lineup. That’s not to say, however, that intermediate-level cigar enthusiasts won’t be able to appreciate this medium-bodied gem — they certainly can and will. This stick pairs well with coffee, dark rum, or scotch and makes for a great, relaxing nightcap. Fans of Rocky’s previous hits, such as Decade or Sixty, will appreciate all the rich flavor and performance this one has to offer. The Rocky Patel Dark Star is a prime example of Rocky’s innovation, demonstrating his immense passion and drive to stay at the top — not to mention it’s yet another rock star addition to one of the biggest portfolios in the business.

Rocky Patel has built a reputation on delivering premium craftsmanship with an endless pursuit of innovation, and the Rocky Patel DBS continues that tradition with a blend that stands apart from the crowd. No, DBS isn’t a nod to a luxury sports car; it stands for Double Broadleaf Selection , a reference to the two distinct broadleaf tobaccos woven into the heart of the blend. Built around complexity and layered flavor, this cigar proves that sometimes the boldest statements are made without saying a word. Cigar Aficionado has awarded the Rocky Patel DBS blend a 90 rating . Handcrafted with the precision cigar enthusiasts have come to expect from Rocky Patel, DBS features a dark and flavorful Mexican San Andrés wrapper that cloaks an intricate blend designed to create richness and balance from start to finish. The wrapper itself carries a beautiful dark auburn appearance with a subtle oily sheen, while the striking navy, orange, and gold bands make it impossible to overlook in any humidor. From the first draw, the Rocky Patel DBS introduces a warm and inviting profile layered with toasty leather and natural sweetness , gradually revealing notes of ginger-molasses cookie, rich chocolate, and sweet raisin . Beneath the surface, subtle earthy undertones and hints of cedar add depth and structure, creating a profile that evolves without becoming overpowering. The draw remains effortless throughout, producing thick clouds of smoke and delivering a smooth, flavorful finish that lingers pleasantly on the palate. Bold without being aggressive and complex without sacrificing balance, the Rocky Patel DBS delivers exactly what smokers have come to expect from Rocky Patel: premium quality, rich flavor, and another unique addition to one of the industry’s most expansive portfolios. Whether enjoyed with a strong coffee, a dark spirit, or simply on its own, DBS proves that sometimes three letters really can make a big statement.

Released to celebrate Rocky's first ten years in the cigar business, the Rocky Patel Decade cigar line might also be the pinnacle of his achievements. By now everyone is familiar with the story of how Rocky left his lucrative gig as an entertainment lawyer to pursue his passion for fine, hand-crafted smokes. Working tirelessly to craft cigars he knew would appeal to post-Cigar Boom smokers, his efforts culminated in a number of 90+ rated cigars including fan-favorites The Edge Corojo and Maduro plus the phenomenal 1990 and 1992 Vintage lines. Seeing his ten years of hard word finally paying off, Patel took the opportunity to create a secret blend of filler and binder tobaccos and layered them beneath a rare Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. And so the Decade was born.

A glorious stogie ready to carry you to a world of ultimate smoking pleasure, the Rocky Patel Disciple is one cigar you’ll want to keep an eye on as it slowly ages in your humidor. This latest medium-full expression of flavor from the tobacco powerhouse that is Rocky Patel Cigars, creators of a multitude of your favorite smokes from the world-changing The Edge lineup to the exquisitely smooth Olde World Reserve and everything in between, aims to be their best cigar ever and it just might be. Containing a succulent blend of rich Nicaraguan longleaf from Condega and Esteli, the Disciple has been finished with an oily and toothy Mexican San Andres wrapper ready to delight your palate now and for many years to come. Don’t get us wrong, this cigar is fantastic as-is the moment it arrives at your door. Each ebony-hued vitola is delightfully aromatic, the aged tobaccos beneath the large black and gold bands are rich with the smells of cedar and dark earth. If testing the open draw before lighting, expect plenty of leather and black coffee to awaken your palate, a mere hint of the flavors to come. Starting with a peppery burst, the creamy and balanced smoke that pours from the Rocky Patel Disciple soon develops a smooth texture full of cocoa and black currant and café con leche and caramel. The flavors only intensify as you explore further into each solidly constructed stick, with the cigar’s signature earthiness matched to marzipan, sourdough toast, cinnamon, and some semi-sweet chocolate. No matter if you’re already on team Rocky Patel or not, and there are so many wise aficionados who are, the Rocky Patel Disciple is a handmade cigar you can rely on to never lead you astray. Why not see where this premium smoke can take you, because it may just be where you’ve wanted to go your entire life.

It can be easy at times to become jaded about the seemingly endless variety of Rocky Patel cigars, but the re-released Rocky Patel Edicion Unica cigar proves the man has got the skills to keep innovating. The all-Honduran blend, including a Jamastran wrapper and longleaf Jamastran and Talanga Valley filler tobaccos, was originally created exclusively for the Honduran Humo Jaguar Cigar Festival of 2011. After taking top honors at that event, Rocky decided to release the cigar into the wild as a limited edition and boy did they go quickly. Fortunately there was enough of the same prime leaf, by now very well rested, to create one more run of these 6 inch by 52 ring gauge toros.

As Rocky Patel himself notes, “It’s the first box-pressed cigar we’ve released that’s on the light side of medium. This combination results in a truly medium-bodied cigar, offering a harmonious balance of flavors.

Rocky Patel is nothing short of an industry icon, and his massive Nicaraguan factory produces more cigars than just about anyone. When one of his many, many new yearly blends rises to the top and stands head and shoulders above the rest, you’d better pay attention. This is precisely the case with Rocky Patel Emerald . Rolled in Rocky’s main factory in Nicaragua, this incredible blend features fillers from Honduras and Nicaragua, double binders from Mexico and Nicaragua, and a dark, leathery Ecuadorian wrapper leaf. Blended to be “on the lighter side of medium,” according to Rocky, this box-pressed masterpiece has taken the cigar world by storm, quickly becoming one of Rocky Patel’s most sought-after blends and earning a stellar 95 rating in Cigar Aficionado, along with a top 10 spot on the magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of 2025 . A white marbled cedar chest with glistening green trim houses the expertly rolled cigars, and each one is most certainly dressed to impress. White and green double bands and a green foil wrapper scream “luxury,” and the seamless roll and dark and oily tobacco simply add to the dazzling appearance. Masterful construction offers an easy draw with rolling clouds of thick blue smoke, with each puff invoking more and more flavor. An opening of rich, earthy raw tobacco mingled with black pepper starts things off. Soon, a delicious array of cocoa, coffee grounds, and hickory builds the complex and incredibly balanced flavor profile. The finish is rich and smooth, and overall, Emerald finishes smack dab in the middle of the spectrum, a medium-bodied stick to the core. Made for experienced connoisseurs, Rocky Patel Emerald includes all the textbook aspects of an ultra-premium cigar. Medium-bodied , complex, and easy to smoke, this luxurious blend pairs beautifully with your favorite bourbon or scotch but also makes a fine companion to a glass of sweet port wine. Fans of Rocky’s other outstanding classics such as Rocky Patel Decade or Rocky Patel Sun Grown should find this one to be quite attractive, even though it may be a bit lighter. For an incredibly opulent cigar experience that won’t break the bank, Rocky Patel Emerald is a “gem” that’s hard to beat. Get your hands on some and see for yourself what has the entire cigar world going nuts.

With a lingering spice, complemented by rich, nuanced flavors, the Fifty-Five is a testament to Rocky Patel’s commitment to innovation and quality in cigar craftsmanship.

Rocky Patel has been cranking out hits for years, and the release of the Rocky Patel Fifty-Five cigar in 2016 shows he isn't planning on slowing down. It can be difficult to keep track of the multitude of Rocky Patel cigars both past and present, but all you really need to know is that the Rocky Patel Fifty is the king of them all and has just been re-released in very limited quantities. His most expensive cigar ever and limited to a mere 2000 boxes, the original Fifty was the result of a four-year-long development project to celebrate Patel’s fiftieth birthday. Containing a proprietary and secret blend of longleaf Nicaraguan tobaccos beneath a double binder and gorgeous Ecuadorian Habano-seed Oscuro wrapper, they were entirely something special. Gold Label delivers a sophisticated taste experience, with earthy nuances, luscious caramel undertones, and the bold flavor of coffee.

The Rocky Patel Gold Label is now available in Germany for selected specialist retailers via the German importer M. K. & Söhne. Gold Label lives up to its name: gold was used in abundance for the elegant box and the opulent belly band – a design characterized by filigree ornaments and an imposing appearance. Inspired by Rocky Patel’s Indian roots, the visual appearance underlines the luxurious character of this cigar line. The exquisite tobacco blend begins with a shiny Ecuador H-2000 wrapper. Two Connecticut tobaccos are used for the binder – Broadleaf and Shade, which provide a gentle yet expressive structure. The aromatic core is formed by the long-matured filler made from premium tobaccos from Jalapa and Estelí, two of Nicaragua’s most renowned tobacco-growing regions. »Rocky had this blend in his drawer for a long time,« explains Nish Patel, Executive Vice President of the company. »He wanted something with a lot of flavor – I think Gold Label has just that. It’s very smooth, very balanced, just a well-rounded smoke.« Despite its classy appearance, Gold Label remains surprisingly accessible in price: it ranges from €8.90/each to €17/each, making it the ideal choice for everyday luxury enjoyment. It is available in four formats: Half Corona, Robusto, Toro and Sixty. . Rocky Patel is known for having more blends and brands than just about anyone in the business, but 2024 was a bit of a different year for the famous tobacco tycoon. One regular production blend was introduced to the world of premium cigars, and that one blend was a darned good one: Rocky Patel Gold Label. Made at Rocky’s own Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A. in Esteli, Nicaragua, Gold Label was built from the ground up to be luxurious and sophisticated, but at the same time reasonably priced for a cigar of its stature. Well, once again, Rocky hit the nail on the head! Double Connecticut binders (both Broadleaf and Shade) hug a blend of filler leaves from Jalapa and Esteli—Nicaragua’s most fertile growing regions. To finish things off, a dark, oily Habano wrapper from Ecuador is applied and the whole package is aggressively box-pressed. The result is a top-shelf gem that has earned numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado and changed the way many people look at Rocky Patel cigars. Brown and gold chests house the beautifully pressed vitolas, and each cigar wears a brown and gold band and a full-length gold foil wrap. Opulent in appearance, the construction matches, as this precision-made beast of a cigar blasts out clouds of thick smoke on each and every puff, never shorting the palate of the complex flavor that was worked so hard for. Toasty, earthy notes are pronounced from the start, along with black pepper and coffee. The coffee note remains throughout the entire smoking experience, and the core of the flavor profile is a nutty, rich tobacco. Hints of cocoa and cinnamon linger in the background, and the finish is sweet and smooth. Medium-full-bodied and beautifully complex, Gold Label is most certainly a cigar made with the true connoisseur in mind. Made for the experienced, Rocky Patel Gold Label is a cigar that further rounds out the higher end of Rocky’s ever-growing portfolio. Layered flavor and medium-full-bodied richness makes it a stick that always satisfies and is always appropriate as a celebratory stick. Pair it with black coffee for a bold and invigorating experience or enjoy it alongside a glass of your favorite dark rum or port wine for a relaxing evening affair. Some have called it a more affordable version of Conviction , others have compared it to the ever-popular Decade . Whatever the case, we can guarantee that Rocky Patel Gold Label is a cigar that once you enjoy, you’ll never forget.

Rocky Patel is one of the busiest men in the industry, and his coveted brand is among the biggest in existence. From humble beginnings, he and his company have grown into a dominant force in the world of premium cigars—so much so that they sometimes don’t even need to give their blends a proper name. Such is the case with Rocky Patel LB1. As noted on the box, LB1 is the “Original Factory Code” assigned to the cigar during the blending process. Made in Honduras at the famed El Paraiso factory, LB1 features a rich recipe of high-priming leaves, masterfully aged over long periods to produce a delicious, well-balanced final product. The filler blend consists of tobaccos from Nicaragua and Honduras, bound by a Nicaraguan binder and finished with a golden brown Ecuadorian Habano wrapper grown in rich volcanic soil. A premium cigar that both looks and tastes the part, LB1 has already surged in popularity and earned a respectable 92 rating from Cigar Aficionado. Unfinished cedar dress boxes house the decadent vitolas, each adorned with a single white and gold band denoting the blend. Construction is precise and consistent, offering a smooth, easy draw every time. Upon the first puff, billowing clouds of white smoke greet the palate with sweet cedar and spicy white pepper. These notes remain throughout, joined along the way by plenty of toasty and earthy nuances. A tobacco-heavy core holds the flavor profile together beautifully, culminating in a rich, medium-full-bodied finish. Made for connoisseurs but enjoyable for just about anyone, Rocky Patel LB1 is as versatile as it is delicious. For a cigar of this stature, the price tag is reasonable, offering significant value compared to similarly priced sticks. It pairs well with bourbon or a medium-bodied beer and is suited for just about any time of day. Cigars such as Oliva Serie O and Perdomo Lot 23 Sun Grown offer a similar experience, so if you enjoy either, LB1 is a must-try. Rocky Patel has long been the people’s champ when it comes to providing a variety of options for cigar enthusiasts of all experience levels, and LB1 is further proof that he has no plans of slowing down.

Rocky Patel is the kind of guy that refuses to let a birthday, anniversary, or any celebratory occasion go unrecognized with a stellar cigar, so it’s no surprise that by the time of his 60th birthday, something big was already long in the works: The Rocky Patel Sixty. In anticipation for this stick, Rocky already had the cigars rolled and was aged the entire batch for over 2 years. Made in his Nicaraguan factory, Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A., the Sixty combines a rich Nicaraguan filler and binder blend with a gorgeous Mexican San Andres wrapper leaf. Though it may be a simple recipe, the aforementioned long aging process has married the characteristics of the different leaves to produce a one-of-a-kind flavor profile that is both refined and eventful. Rocky’s top-secret project would end up paying off big time, as in 2022 the Sixty earned an unprecedented 96 rating and the runner-up spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 Cigars of the Year. Rocky Patel is never shy with the packaging when it comes to special selections. This remains true here, as vibrant red and gold bands clothe each vitola almost entirely, along with ornate photographic sleeves and commemorative foot bands bearing the “60” denotation. A precision roll along with a crisp box press ensures a pleasant smoking experience from beginning to end, including an easy draw and affluent smoke production. It’s no surprise that the initial opening of the cigar is heavy on earth and pepper, something all too common with premium Nicaraguan tobacco. Soon, however, the profile takes a sweet turn as hints of coffee and nuts begin to surface. A spicy cayenne note at the back of the throat keeps it interesting, and a sweet caramel finish ties the package together. Medium-full-bodied and bursting at the seams with flavor, it’s easy to see how the Rocky Patel Sixty practically became an overnight success. The Sixty isn’t for the faint of heart, but if you are brave enough to chop one down, you will experience the size that earned that ridiculous 96 rating ! Rocky has sticks for everyone that has ever considered putting flame to the foot of a cigar, from beginners that have never smoked to seasoned connoisseurs whose number one passion in life is enjoying fine tobacco products. The Sixty definitely falls in the latter category, as with all the exciting complexity and balance it has to offer, smoking one with an untrained palate would be little more than a waste of time. It pairs wonderfully with coffee, bourbon, or dark rum, and is ideal for life’s special occasions (as it was made for Rocky’s own special occasion). Other notable celebration sticks from Rocky include the Decade and the Fifty Five , both of similar stature to the cigar in question. Chances are if you are a fan of either, you’re selling yourself short by not trying a Sixty. Rocky Patel is one of the big ones. He’s been in the game for decades and maintains a permanent residence near the top. The Rocky Patel Sixty is said by many to be his best cigar yet, so grab one today and let us know if they’re right!

Celebrating two decades since work began on the cigar that basically started it all for Rocky Patel, The Edge 20th Anniversary sincerely demonstrates how far the company has come over the years. Since then, the number of cigars bearing the Edge trademark has grown to eight, the blend in question being the eighth installment. For this Honduran-made gem, Rocky went with a delectable blend of Panamanian and Honduran fillers, combined with a Honduran Habano binder. The real star of this show, however, is the wrapper: An Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf aged no less than 10 years. Whether you happen to be a long-time Rocky Patel fan or just love top-shelf cigars, now is the time to celebrate 2 decades of quality, value, and downright great cigars with Rocky Patel The Edge 20th Anniversary.

Packed in simple black wooden chests, each cigar is finished with a distinctive blue foot band denoting the Habano variety. Flawless construction ensures an effortless draw, an even burn, and minimal touch-ups. Dense clouds of white smoke flood the palate with bold Nicaraguan spice and earthy tobacco richness , before transitioning into a complex medley of cedar, cinnamon, and pepper . The finish is crisp, powerful, and remarkably clean, offering depth and balance throughout the experience. Unlike some of its milder Edge counterparts, The Edge Habano is geared toward seasoned smokers who appreciate a robust, high-octane profile. Its strength may overwhelm beginners, but for aficionados who crave intensity, it delivers in spades. Best paired with bourbon, black coffee, or a full-bodied beer, this cigar shines when enjoyed on a full stomach. Thanks to its Nicaraguan DNA, The Edge Habano stands apart from the rest of the Edge family and instead draws comparisons to powerhouse cigars like Don Pepin Garcia Blue Label or Oliva Serie O. Strong, refined, and affordably priced, it’s no surprise this blend has become a staple among hardcore cigar enthusiasts. If you’re a fan of bold, full-bodied cigars that don’t break the bank, The Edge Habano is the one for you.

Rocky Patel The Edge Maduro is not only one of the strongest cigars in the Edge lineup from Rocky Patel, but also one of the most popular. The Edge series is basically what put Rocky Patel on the map, combining quality with an affordable price point and offering no shortage in the flavor department. This Maduro variety is made at Rocky's factory down in Honduras using Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco. The finishing touch is a jet-black Costa Rican Maduro wrapper leaf that adds both body and intense maduro flavor. 92-rated, well-established, and highly celebrated. The Edge Maduro is a classic that has a permanent spot in the humidors of millions of connoisseurs across the globe and has earned ratings as high as 92 by Cigar Aficionado .

Not long after Rocky Patel took the cigar world by storm with the original, beloved Edge Corojo , a new star was born that would capture the hearts of full-bodied cigar fanatics across the globe: The Edge Sumatra . Rolled in Nestor Plasencia’s El Paraiso factory in Danli, Honduras, The Edge Sumatra takes all the sought-after qualities of the original Corojo blend and considerably ramps up the already imposing strength. For this blend, Nicaraguan fillers are combined with a spicy Honduran binder leaf. The wrapper is a dark and oily Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf that really beefs up the flavor profile. Though not as readily available as the other Edge variants, Edge Sumatra is one of the favorites, earning a 91 rating in Cigar Aficionado and a spot on the magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of 2007 .

Thirty years in the cigar industry is no small accomplishment, and the Rocky Patel Thirtieth Anniversary was created to celebrate that milestone in fitting fashion. More than a commemorative release, this cigar represents three decades of passion, perseverance, and an unwavering commitment to premium cigar craftsmanship. From the early days of Indian Tabac to becoming one of the most recognized names in modern cigars, Rocky Patel has built a reputation on innovation and quality, and this anniversary blend serves as a tribute to that journey. This highly acclaimed blend has earned multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado, including a benchmark 93 rating for its exceptional construction and flavor. Expertly handcrafted and elegantly box-pressed , the Thirtieth Anniversary showcases a carefully refined blend built around a dark, beautifully aged Mexican San Andrés wrapper matured for an impressive seven years. Beneath that luxurious exterior rests, a pair of Nicaraguan binders securing a meticulously aged core of Honduran and Nicaraguan long fillers, with the filler tobaccos aged for at least five years. Every component has been selected with purpose, creating a blend designed to deliver richness, balance, and complexity in every draw. From first light, the profile opens with smooth notes of caramel, toasted almonds, and cocoa powder , supported by warm layers of cedar and earth . As the cigar develops, subtle nuances of coffee, sweet leather, and creamy wood begin to emerge, adding depth and refinement to the experience. The expertly aged tobacco creates a smoke that feels smooth and polished while still delivering enough richness to keep seasoned smokers engaged from beginning to end. Impeccably constructed with a firm box-press and flawless draw, the Rocky Patel Thirtieth Anniversary delivers a smoking experience worthy of the milestone it celebrates. Whether you’ve been enjoying Rocky Patel cigars for years or are discovering the brand for the first time, this release offers an opportunity to experience the culmination of three decades of dedication to the craft, one unforgettable puff at a time.

Rocky Patel Cigars and its German importer, M. K. & Söhne, announce the gradual transition of the popular Vintage Series 1990 to box-pressed formats. This change will replace the round formats, which were previously rolled exclusively for the German market. The Robusto will lead the way and is already being delivered in the box-pressed format. This step responds to the increasing popularity of box-pressed cigars. However, Rocky Patel is going beyond merely following a trend. The box-pressed shape aligns with the original concept of the cigar, and Rocky is confident that the carefully balanced blend of the Vintage Series 1990 offers even better aroma development in the box-pressed format. This decision once again highlights Rocky Patel’s uncompromising attention to detail and his constant drive to improve even successful products. »The Vintage Series 1990 is a bestseller in our portfolio, and we always strive to provide our customers with the best possible taste experience,« explains Rocky Patel. »The box-pressed variant enhances the complex flavors of the Vintage Series 1990 and underscores our commitment to the highest quality.« M. K. & Söhne, importer and partner of Rocky Patel in Germany, welcomes this decision: »Box-pressed formats are enjoying growing popularity in the German market, and the Vintage Series 1990 is a top seller in our range. We are confident that the box-pressed version will continue the success story of the Vintage Series 1990.«

The Rocky Patel Vintage 1990 holds a special place in history as the first cigar to officially bear Rocky Patel’s name, marking the brand's transition from the Indian Tabac era to a household name. This medium-bodied, box-pressed classic is defined by its extraordinary aging process. At its core is a blend of 8-year-old Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers held together by a Nicaraguan binder. The star of the show, however, is the 12-year-old Honduran Broadleaf Maduro wrapper . This extensive aging mellows the tobacco significantly, resulting in a rich, smooth, and complex smoke that appeals to both novices and seasoned aficionados.

Would I Smoke This Cigar Again? Maybe. The cigar has good flavor but the tight draw, slight bitterness would make me give pause. note_sources.text: A classic from back in his earlier days, the Rocky Patel Vintage 1992 is still taking names and kicking… well, let's just say you will not be disappointed. Many of you may not remember, but there was a time when there were fewer than a dozen well-known RP cigars. Moreover, that includes his now-defunct Indian Tabac brand! On the heels of the meteoric The Edge, Rocky released the twin threat of the Vintage series to add the 1990 and 1992 (the Vintage 1999, Vintage 2003, and Vintage 2006 would come later), each containing the same blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican Ligeros aged a full eight years. Destined for greatness, the 1992 was graced with a magnificent 10-year-old Ecuadorian Sumatra to give it a style all its own. The Rocky Patel Vintage 1992 blend has earned widespread acclaim for its smooth, sophisticated profile, highlighted by an impressive 92 rating from Cigar Aficionado .

Rocky Patel Vintage 1999 Connecticut is a cigar that was long awaited, as many were anxious for Rocky to bring a mild cigar into his already fantastic portfolio. The final product was well worth the wait. This Honduran masterpiece consists of a heavily aged blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers and a Nicaraguan binder. The finishing touch is a gorgeous golden-brown Connecticut wrapper that is nearly flawless in appearance.

White Label Crafted in our very own factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, this incredible medium-bodied cigar showcases a stunning Connecticut wrapper with a flavor profile so bold, every artist is sure to have their own interpretation. Featuring an iconic complexity, this flawless stick offers rich notes of cedar, cream, and an undeniably sweet finish that lingers long after its buttery bouquet has dissipated.

For over 10 years Rocky Patel tried to find the perfect name and brand to go along with this amazing composition of Nicaragua’s finest, when it dawned on him that no design or label would ever truly showcase the complexities hidden within. True inspiration can only come from a place of artistic expression — that’s when Rocky had an epiphany: the White Label. Nothing captures the possibility and spirit of craftsmanship like the image of a blank canvas. Nor does anything more aptly represent opportunity like this rare piece of art. Every smoke begins with a delicate first stroke, inviting aficionados to become artists. You never know where your work will take you; every journey will be unique and entirely your own. But no matter how you enjoy it, it will always end up a masterpiece. Crafted in Rocky Patel’s Tavicusa factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, this medium-bodied cigar showcases a stunning Connecticut wrapper with a flavor profile so bold, every artist is sure to have their own interpretation. Featuring an iconic complexity, this flawless stick offers rich notes of cedar, cream, and an undeniably sweet finish that lingers long after its buttery bouquet has dissipated. Everything from its white leather case to its rose gold interior, are immaculately crafted and meticulously bespoke. Rocky Patel: “To put it plainly, we’ve never created a cigar with a more breathtaking palette than the all-new White Label by Rocky Patel… It’s as simple as that.” Robusto 5 x 50 Toro 6 ½ x 52 Churchill 7 x 48 Sixty 6 x 60

Rocky Patel is known for having one of the broadest portfolios in the business, ranging from wallet-friendly value cigars to industry-shaking connoisseur specialties. With the Rocky Patel White Label, we have what some are calling the finest cigar ever to bear the company’s unmistakable trademark. According to the company, “For over 10 years, Rocky tried to find the perfect name and brand to go along with this amazing composition of Nicaragua’s finest.” Nicaragua’s finest, indeed—not only referring to its country of origin, home to Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A., but also to the expertly fermented binder and filler tobacco contained within. In addition, Rocky added Jamastran Valley leaves from Honduras to the recipe, along with just a touch of his “undisclosed” secret ingredient. A golden-brown Connecticut wrapper encompasses the whole package, and all the tobacco used in the construction of this luxurious treat has been aged for no less than a decade. Sounds amazing, right? Cedar chests bound in white leather and overlaid inside with rose gold house the precision-constructed vitolas, each one adorned with an ornate white band featuring rose gold accents. Rolled only by Rocky Patel’s finest, this flavor bomb offers a smooth and easy draw, producing immense clouds of thick white smoke with every puff. The journey begins with espresso and white pepper—both in generous measure. This soon settles into an array of creamy tobacco flavors with hints of cinnamon, cocoa nibs, and earthy undertones. A rich core of spicy raw tobacco lies at the center of it all, with a finish that is long, sweet, and beautifully pronounced. Medium-bodied and intricately complex, the White Label is undoubtedly the kind of cigar any connoisseur longs for. Made for the experienced, this aficionado’s gem is the embodiment of exactly what a top-shelf cigar should be. It performs beautifully every time, it is rich, complex, and unique, and its medium-bodied attributes never become overpowering or harsh. It pairs beautifully with scotch or bourbon and makes a fine celebratory cigar for life’s most special events. This high-end Connecticut beauty falls into a special group of connoisseur-level cigars including Diamond Crown and Padron Damaso , both similar in stature and overall flavor, so if you have fallen in love with either, this one is a definite must-try. Whether you are a devout fan of Rocky Patel cigars or just want something exquisite for a formal event, Rocky Patel White Label is a cigar that will doubtless make an unforgettable impression.

The first puffs of the Rocky Patel Winter Collection Toro are also familiar, with a bit of earthiness and black pepper, seemingly a mix of the countries in the blend as opposed to something that indicates a specific origin. It has enough flavor intensity to get the attention of the senses, but far from too much that it is overwhelming. Retrohales are much the same, though with white pepper and a lighter base note that makes them engaging and approachable. The earthiness makes some subtle shifts, ones that make me invoke the word  terroir  as it offers a sampling of its components’ origins. Two of the samples offer more of what I associate with Honduran filler, meaning a drier and dustier profile on the tongue. The third holds on to the mix a bit longer, resulting in a more complex and brain-stimulating flavor to figure out what I’m tasting. Flavor, body and strength all sit right around the medium mark. Technical construction has been great, with the ash standing out for its seeming durability as it passes an inch in length. The second third of the Rocky Patel Winter Collection Toro holds the course, if backing off the overall intensity just a bit. There is a white pepper on the retrohale that is quite enjoyable and hangs around for an extra beat or two to lightly tingle the nostrils. Terroir establishes itself as the biggest variable between samples; the first seemed a bit more Nicaraguan while the second was a bit more Honduran. By the midway point, the white pepper that was only on retrohales has become part of the flavor, with just a bit of chalkiness tagging along. It’s the first shift in the earthy flavor that has been a constant in the cigar, bringing with it a bit of cake donut and a dry dustiness that sneaks in behind the other flavors.  The transition to the final third sees the profile quickly shed its smoothness in favor of something much more raised and pointed, with the beginnings of a red chili pepper flavor taking hold. Flavor is an earthy medium-plus, body stays around medium, and strength is a somewhat surprising medium as well. It’s not fair to say that the Rocky Patel Winter Collection Toro has been slumbering to this point, but it certainly

note_sources.text: The Taste Indulge your senses with the rich and decadent flavors of coffee, espresso, and dark chocolate, balanced by hints of cinnamon, creating a symphony of taste that lingers on the palate long after the final puff. With a strength profile ranging from medium to medium-full, the Rocky Patel Year of the Dragon offers a nuanced yet satisfying smoking journey for connoisseurs and enthusiasts alike.

Rocky Patel is renowned for creating cigars to suit every occasion, and in 2024, he seized the opportunity to craft something truly epic. The Chinese Lunar New Year in 2024 celebrates the Year of the Dragon , a significant event honored across numerous Asian countries and highly revered worldwide. The Rocky Patel Year of the Dragon pays homage to this global celebration and has been hailed by many as one of the most phenomenal cigars Rocky Patel has ever released. Produced at the Nicaragua-based Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A., also known as TAVICUSA, the Year of the Dragon is hand-rolled by some of the most skilled artisans in the world. Its blend is nothing short of extraordinary, featuring Nicaraguan fillers from Condega, Estelí, and Jalapa—Nicaragua’s most fertile growing regions. A touch of Honduran leaf from the Jamastrán Valley adds an extra layer of complexity. The cigar is bound with two Connecticut binders: one Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro and another kept under wraps (Rocky Patel enjoys keeping a few secrets). The wrapper is a dark, oily, and aged Mexican San Andrés Maduro leaf, widely regarded as one of the finest Maduro tobaccos in the world. The Year of the Dragon is available in three sizes globally, but for the U.S. market, a single 6 ½” x 52 toro is offered—and it’s a fantastic choice. The packaging for this cigar is as impressive as its blend. Each ultra-premium vitola is housed in a velvet-lined, shiny red box adorned with a stunning 3-D dragon motif. The cigars themselves are dressed in two ornate red-and-gold bands that proudly display the exquisite Year of the Dragon artwork. When it comes to performance, the Year of the Dragon delivers an exceptional smoking experience. It draws effortlessly, producing thick, white plumes of smoke with every puff while maintaining a sharp and straight burn line from start to finish. The flavor journey begins with a bold introduction of white pepper through the nose and a generous dose of spice across the palate. An earthy core quickly takes center stage, complemented by hints of cinnamon, cayenne, and black cherry along the way. The finish is smooth, earthy, and satisfying, resulting in a medium-to-full-bodied experience. Expertly balanced, intriguingly complex, and just strong enough to keep things interesting, this top-shelf offering is for experienced connoisseurs only. Rocky Patel really does offer something for everyone, and this one is for the true aficionados. Year of the Dragon pairs well with bourbon, dark rum, or medium-bodied beer and makes a fantastic celebration cigar for any special occasion. Fans of some of Rocky’s other famed ultra-premiums such as the top-rated Decade or the celebrated Rocky Patel Sixty should try this one with full confidence that they are in for a treat. You don’t have to celebrate the Lunar New Year to get down on one of the finest cigars of the year. Take it from us, though, when we say smoking Rocky Patel Year of the Dragon is like having your very own fireworks show.
The profile reveals layered notes of sweet spice, earth, espresso, caramel, and white chocolate, culminating in a rich, composed finish.

The Rocky Patel “Year of the Horse” has officially arrived at select retailers. This limited-edition release is handcrafted in Nicaragua. A dark San Andrés wrapper surrounds a Nicaraguan binder and a blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers. The company is incredibly proud of this release and excited for cigar smokers across the country (USA) to experience it finally. Cigar Talk with Rocky Patel: In this new episode of Cigar Talk, Rocky answers one of the biggest questions in premium cigars — which country produces the best tobacco? From Nicaragua and Honduras to Ecuador, Cameroon, Brazil, Connecticut, and the Dominican Republic, Rocky walks through how each region contributes something unique to a cigar blend. He explains how different soils, climates, and tobacco varietals shape flavor, strength, sweetness, spice, and aroma — and why great blending is about harmony, not just origin. For anyone interested in cigar education, tobacco growing, blending, wrappers, fillers, and the craftsmanship behind premium handmade cigars, this is an episode you won’t want to miss. Watch the Episode

Rocky Patel has become known not only for his expansive portfolio of premium cigars, but also for crafting highly anticipated commemorative releases that celebrate milestones and special occasions. The Rocky Patel Year of the Horse marks the third installment in Rocky’s ultra-premium Chinese Zodiac series, following the celebrated Year of the Dragon and Year of the Snake releases. Created to honor the 2026 Chinese New Year, this limited-edition blend celebrates the Fire Horse, a symbol of passion, boldness, strength, and adventure. Handcrafted at Rocky Patel’s renowned factory in Nicaragua, this elegant release arrives in a 7" x 48 box-pressed Churchill format and features a dark, oily Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and a carefully aged blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers , a proven combination found in some of Rocky’s most beloved and award-winning cigars. From first light, thick clouds of smoke introduce notes of sweet spice and roasted earth , gradually evolving into rich layers of espresso, caramel, and velvety white chocolate . The medium-to-full-bodied profile maintains impressive balance throughout, delivering depth and complexity without sacrificing smoothness. The elongated Churchill format allows the blend to unfold naturally, rewarding smokers with a rich and refined smoking experience from start to finish. Presented in ornate 10-count display boxes and adorned with striking red and gold bands, the Year of the Horse is every bit as visually impressive as it is flavorful. With production limited to just 6,000 boxes worldwide, these rare cigars are destined to become prized additions to humidors and collections alike. Made for aficionados who appreciate luxurious complexity and collectible releases, the Rocky Patel Year of the Horse Churchill pairs beautifully with bourbon, scotch, or a strong cup of coffee. Like the spirit it honors, this cigar is bold, refined, and not meant to be overlooked. You owe it to yourself to experience this rare thoroughbred before they gallop away for good!

Wrapper : U.S.: Nicaraguan Habano | International: Nicaraguan Habano 2000 Oscuro Binder : Nicaraguan Broadleaf Filler : Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos TASTING NOTES The Year of the Snake delivers a luxurious flavor journey from start to finish. This rich, dark cigar features decadent tobaccos with notes of coffee and chocolate and subtle floral undertones.

Rocky Patel is known for his huge portfolio and bringing out endless new blends year after year, but he’s also known for making commemorative cigars that celebrate different anniversaries, birthdays, and yearly events. In the case of Rocky Patel Year of the Snake , we have the second Rocky Patel cigar themed around the Chinese Zodiac, following Year of the Dragon, and many would say this one is even better! Made at Rocky’s famous Tabacalera Villa Cuba factory in Nicaragua, this ultra-premium cigar celebrates the 2025 Chinese New Year in quite a delicious way. The filler blend contains leaves from Honduras and Nicaragua, the binder is Nicaraguan Broadleaf, and the wrapper is a dark and oily Nicaraguan Habano leaf that adds a gorgeous depth to the flavor profile. Limited to 60,000 cigars, this project has already proven to be one of Rocky’s craziest yet, and the solid 90 rating in Cigar Aficionado can certainly attest to it. Ornate black chests covered in red and gold decorations house the precision-made cigars, each one wearing double red and gold bands that nearly cover the entire body. 6 ½” x 52 is the size of Year of the Snake, and each stick is rolled to offer maximum performance each and every time. An easy draw produces rich, silky smoke with each puff, at first opening with a blast of black pepper and earthy tobacco flavor . A quick turn sends things into a sweet medley of brown sugar, coffee, and caramel, while a chewy, nutty flavor hangs in the background. An earthy core holds everything together, and a sweet, crisp finish seals the deal. Medium-full-bodied and complex, this special treat is certainly a statement that shows what Rocky can do for the true hardcore connoisseurs. Made for experienced connoisseurs, Year of the Snake demonstrates a level of craftsmanship and blending that only a long-time industry icon can accomplish. This medium-full-bodied masterpiece is rich, sweet, and luxurious, so don’t hesitate to pair it with your favorite bourbon or scotch. Coffee also complements its dark and rich flavor profile beautifully, as well as a medium-bodied sweet red wine. Fans of the Year of the Dragon release will doubtless want to check this one out, as well as anyone that has come to enjoy some of Rocky’s famous top-notch sticks such as Decade or Rocky Patel 50 . If you are in the market for something special, or you are a long-time fan of Rocky Patel, you owe it to yourself to try a Rocky Patel Year of the Snake before they’re gone. We promise it will make a lasting impression!

From their Serie G and Serie V lines, Oliva has a foothold in the strong and full-bodied-cigar market, but when smokers at events started asking for a milder stick, Oliva set its sights on this new area. Oliva's Connecticut Reserve is an amazing mild-to-medium body cigar that hits all the right flavor notes. Made in Nicaragua, this cigar has a surprising blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos given its lighter body. The wrapper is a golden Ecuadorian Connecticut and provides an amazing creaminess to the smoke. Rated as high as 92 by Cigar Aficionado , the Oliva Connecticut Reserve stands alongside many of the brand’s most highly acclaimed blends. A beautiful white band surrounds the Oliva Connecticut Reserve and it is almost as striking as the gorgeous caramel colored wrapper leaf. The wrapper does have some veining, but once lit any concern you may have about an imperfect burn will quickly be erased. Straight as an arrow, this smoke holds onto its ash until you feel obligated to tip it off. The pre light aroma is a tantalizing sweetness and the draw can only be described as perfect. A complexity of flavors are omnipresent as the cigars transform throughout each half. What starts as a nice smooth toastiness transforms into an extremely pleasant spice and wood flavor. Already a master at the full-bodied-cigar market, Oliva has dipped their toe in the milder arena and everyone else better watch out. An amazing cigar that, while mild, still piles on flavor and is constructed with excellence, The Connecticut Reserve is a must try for everyone. This cigar is perfect for anytime of day.

Oliva Master Blends 3 is the pinnacle of craftsmanship from the renowned Oliva Cigar Company in Nicaragua. Produced in small batches with expert precision, this ultra-premium cigar delivers a luxuriously full-bodied experience. The blend features bold Nicaraguan ligero fillers, a Nicaraguan Habano binder, and a dark, rare Nicaraguan Broadleaf sun-grown wrapper. Rated 92 by Cigar Aficionado , Master Blends 3 is a true aficionado’s dream, offering complex flavors and plenty of hearty Nicaraguan strength. Beautifully constructed with seamless rolling and an easy draw, Master Blends 3 is as elegant to smoke as it is to behold, adorned with its exotic, colorful band. The flavor journey begins with a wave of spicy Nicaraguan pepper and rich earth, followed by layered notes of cedar and nutmeg. The finish is bold, spicy, and lingers with a decadent touch of chocolate on the palate. Not for beginners, Oliva Master Blends 3 is crafted for seasoned connoisseurs with refined palates who can fully appreciate its intricate profile. Perfect as a celebration cigar, it pairs exceptionally well with single-malt scotch and carries a richness often compared to the legendary Padron 1964 Anniversary Series. Experience the best Oliva has to offer with the Master Blends 3—a masterpiece worthy of its name.

My initial impression is that this is a unique cigar, as the wrapper smells like the shoreline of a lake: slightly fishy, muddy, and with hints of algae. This isn’t unpleasant, and comes across as an interesting version of earthiness and/or barnyard. I struggle to discern flavors in the cold draw, but notice some Froot Loops and light cedar creaminess. The cigar doesn’t stray from interesting/unique upon lighting, and the first flavors to cross my palate are that of sweet cherry tomatoes! Aside from that, there’s the cedar that is initially close to being the dominant flavor. The draw is perfection, but the lightness in the bunch is evident in how fast the first third flys by, clocking in at just over 13 minutes. The ash isn’t the same perfect, dense stacks that come when smoking a Melanio, but instead are puffy and flakey. Flavor and body are sub-medium at this point. Flavors pick up going into the second third, with layers of baking spices and creaminess. Like a rich chai custard, I notice tingling ginger, cinnamon, and cardamom. The ginger quickly turns up the tingle as it cruises into Spicyville. Spice, in cigars, can mean a lot of things: peppercorn, chile peppers, baking spices, etc.—this is like the burn of a strong ginger beer. Aside from these flavors, and their pleasant meshing, there isn’t a ton of complexity to be had at this point. The flavor has been bumped up into medium at this point, with the ginger and a punchy cedar note, while strength is still below the Mendoza line. The burn line is still impeccable. This cigar is racing by like Lightning McQueen—33 minutes heading into the last third. I’m really enjoying this vitola, as the Sumatra wrapper’s presence is a big part of the unique flavor profile and really shines at this ratio. A savory note joins the fresh, pungent, spicy ginger and creamy cedar, with a lingering finish of butterscotch candy sweetness. There’s something that I’m looking for, some elusive flavor, that I just can’t pinpoint. This, and the general uniqueness of the cigar, really keep me puffing away with interest. This isn’t very complex, nor are there the sort of flavor transitions that evolve and keep one intrigued, yet I just can’t help feeling increasingly tantalized as the blend moves on. The creamy-sweet, ginger-spicy, cedar-savory mixture reminds me of Thai grilled shrimp. And as soon as I think the word “Thai,” that elusive something I was searching for comes across as that “king of fruits,” the mighty durian in custard form. As I get into the last inch, the cream and cedar are the biggest things happening. The nub starts to get soft and warm, so I set it down at the one-hour mark ON THE DOT. Strength made a valiant effort to reach medium.

Hailing from Nicaragua and crafted in one of the most renowned cigar factories in the world, Oliva Serie G delivers rich, medium-bodied flavor at a surprisingly accessible price point. This exceptional cigar features a hearty blend of Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos , offering a satisfying and balanced smoking experience. The blend is wrapped in a toothy African-Cameroon wrapper , contributing a natural sweetness that complements the earthy spice of the filler. The Oliva Serie G is a prestigious blend that has reached a new pinnacle of acclaim with a stellar 93-rating from Cigar Aficionado . The Oliva Serie G begins with a lively burst of cedar and white pepper , immediately engaging the palate. As the smoke develops, nuanced notes of floral aromas, cinnamon, and brown sugar emerge, creating a multi-layered flavor profile that is both complex and approachable. Consistently well-constructed, Serie G offers a reliable draw and even burn, making it an excellent choice for beginners or seasoned smokers seeking a medium-bodied staple. This versatile cigar pairs beautifully with white wine, pale ales, or a light whiskey , and is ideal as an after-dinner smoke . Comparable premium options include Arturo Fuente and Cohiba , but Oliva Serie G stands out for its unique balance of flavor, quality, and value . Whether enjoyed at home or shared among friends, the Oliva Serie G remains a classic in the ever-expanding world of fine cigars, proving that affordability and high-end craftsmanship can coexist in one unforgettable smoke.

The Oliva Serie O stands as a cornerstone blend for the Oliva family, serving as the historically significant predecessor to the acclaimed Serie V. As a true Nicaraguan puro, this blend utilizes a rich, sun-grown Nicaraguan Habano wrapper paired with a select Nicaraguan binder and aged Nicaraguan long-fillers harvested from the primary growing regions of Estelí, Condega, and Jalapa. The careful aging of these distinct Cuban-seed tobaccos results in a smooth yet complex profile that has consistently captured the attention of critics. Cigar Aficionado has awarded this specific blend multiple 90+ ratings , most notably honoring the Churchill vitola with a 94 rating and ranking it 11th on the Top 25 of 2013 list. Upon lighting, the blend delivers a generous draw that coats the palate with dense, flavorful smoke. Connoisseurs will note a balanced complexity defined by elements of dark tobacco, rich earth, and a distinct cedar spine. This foundational structure transitions smoothly into warm, inviting undertones of milk chocolate, cinnamon, and heavy baking spice on the finish. Operating comfortably in the medium-to-full body spectrum, the Serie O maintains an exceptionally smooth and balanced character that never becomes overwhelming, making it an ideal choice for intermediate enthusiasts looking to explore deeper profiles, as well as seasoned smokers seeking everyday consistency. It pairs exceptionally well with a classic single malt scotch or a robust red wine, delivering a premium experience at an accessible price point that compares favorably alongside the Serie V and Flor de Oliva lines.

Originally released as an extremely limited cigar in 2010, the highly acclaimed Oliva Serie V Maduro is now a regular production cigar and available year-round! The Serie V Maduro follows the original Serie V blend, which essentially put Oliva Cigars on the map. Each cigar is constructed by the hands of the very best rollers employed by Oliva, and every leaf of tobacco undergoes years of aging to produce a well-balanced blend of flavor and strength. Serie V Maduro consists of bold Nicaraguan Ligero leaves inside a spicy Nicaraguan binder, finished with a dark and oily Mexican San Andres Maduro wrapper. Similar in stature to the original Serie V blend, Serie V Maduro has added sweetness and complexity, making it a prime choice of discriminating connoisseurs since its introduction. Densely packed and seamlessly rolled, Oliva Serie V Maduro is expertly crafted and built for a slow, cool burn and a more-than-satisfying smoke output. At first glance, packaging included, Serie V Maduro seems identical to its natural counterpart, but closer inspection reveals a darker wrapper leaf with an entirely different texture than the sun grown habano used in the original. Upon lighting, the palate is greeted with a burst of spicy white pepper and cayenne, which is soon followed by rich cedar and coffee. A lingering note of cocoa and cinnamon reside in the background, each characteristics usually associated with top quality San Andres Maduro leaves. The finish is rich and the cigar is bold from the first puff to the last. Though extremely full-bodied, Serie V Maduro, like the original blend, is impeccably balanced and never shows any signs of harshness or bitterness. Undeniably complex and built for that small percentage of cigar freaks that like their sticks as strong as possible, Serie V Maduro was blended with the true aficionado in mind. A beginners' cigar by no means, true strength junkies will appreciate the loud flavor and hefty dose of Vitamin N this stick has to offer. Serie V Maduro pairs wonderfully with coffee, though a stout beer or dark rum will accompany the flavor profile as well. Though a maduro cigar by nature, Serie V Maduro actually compares to such dark and powerful sticks as San Cristobal , Ashton VSG , and Casa Magna Colorado . The fact that Serie V Maduro is now here to stay all year long is some of the best news the cigar industry has received as of late, and many fanatics are already stocking up. Get yours while you can! Enjoy one of the finest cigars on the market with Oliva Serie V Maduro.

Oliva Serie V Melanio Maduro cigars are among the finest offerings from the Oliva Cigar Company in Nicaragua. Made by some of the world's most skilled torcedors and produced in a small batch fashion, Serie V Melanio Maduro cigars combine rich potency with impeccable smoothness and unmatched complexity. Melanio Maduro cigars are constructed of unbelievable Nicaraguan Habano filler and binder tobaccos and dark Mexican San Andreas maduro wrappers. This ultra-premium selection has shaken the entire cigar world, making Serie V Melanio Maduro one of the most sought-after sticks on today's market. This celebrated line has earned an impressive 96 rating from Cigar Aficionado and proudly claimed the #6 spot on their Top Cigars of the Year list. Melanio Maduro starts off with the blast of pepper Serie V smokers have come to know and love, but soon after, the magic happens. Cascades of chocolatey mocha and nutmeg coat the palate as complex nuances of leather, black cherry, and cinnamon pop up. Cedar, earth, and rich spice are all very apparent throughout, and the finish is just as bold as any other Serie V. Absolutely fantastic. Melanio Maduro makes a great cigar for an aficionado-level maduro fan, but can be thoroughly enjoyed by any seasoned cigar smoker as well. Full-bodied and chocolatey, Melanio Maduro pairs well with coffee and port wine and makes a fantastic finish to a steak dinner. Comparable cigars include Serie V Maduro and Padron 1964 Maduro. Any serious smoker can rest assured that he is getting the utmost of quality the minute they light a Serie V Melanio Maduro.

Serie V Melanio is the crowning achievement of the Oliva Cigar Company. Five years in the making, this high-end Nicaraguan masterpiece is lovingly crafted by a select handful of some of the best torcedors the world has to offer, using aged ligero filler and binder tobaccos from Nicaragua and a gorgeous Ecuadoran sun grown wrapper. Ultra-refined, yet powerful and pleasurable. The Oliva Serie V Melanio series has accumulated numerous 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado , highlighted by the Melanio Figurado—honored as the #1 Cigar of the Year for 2014 with a remarkable 96 rating —celebrated for its rich, balanced flavors and exceptional craftsmanship. The first light gives off billows of blue smoke, slathering the palate with a massive dose of ligero spice. The earthy introduction soon turns sweet as hints of coffee and dark chocolate become apparent and the spice further intensifies. Oliva Serie V Melanio is a "connoisseur's only" cigar meant for experienced palates. Similar sticks include Padron 1926 and Rocky Patel Decade. Melanio is the result of decades of ceaseless dominance in all things tobacco by the name any true aficionado always trusts—Oliva. Each cigar is expertly hand rolled for an impeccable draw and smooth, consistent burn. The construction is nothing short of flawless, with a razor-sharp burn line and firm ash that holds steady. As it develops, the profile evolves into a harmonious blend of baking spices, leather, and toasted nuts, all perfectly balanced against the natural sweetness of the sun grown wrapper. The finish is long and satisfying, leaving a warm and memorable impression. This is not a quick, casual smoke—it’s a slow-burning celebration of craftsmanship that demands time and attention. Whether you’re pairing it with a rich bourbon, aged rum, or dark roast espresso, the Melanio elevates the moment and rewards the senses. Simply put, it’s a cigar that belongs in every serious smoker’s rotation.

The notable Oliva Serie V Cigar is the crown jewel of the Oliva Cigar Company in Nicaragua. For years, if not decades, Oliva has been among the very top suppliers of cigar tobacco in the world. When they decided to start making their own brands of cigars, people started paying more attention. Then, when Serie V was introduced, the entire world of cigars went crazy, and for many years this ultra-premium treat was one of the hardest sticks to get a hold of. Made by the top rollers at Oliva, Serie V consists of Nicaraguan Jalapa Valley ligero fillers, a spicy Nicaraguan binder, and a gorgeous sun-grown Ecuadoran wrapper. This is one beast of a cigar, and well it should be, as it helped start the “powerhouse” cigar movement, when tastes went from full-flavored to extremely-full-flavored. Beginning with a powerful blast of white pepper and unmistakable Nicaraguan spice, this oily flavor bomb shows absolutely no mercy as it transitions into a rich, woody adventure speckled along the way with notes of coffee, cedar, and cocoa. It packs a huge punch, both flavor- and strength-wise, and finishes with a thick slathering of earth across the palate. This could be the finest cigar to ever come out of Nicaragua. Long-time aficionados, picky connoisseurs, and hardcore strength junkies will all be able to appreciate the unmatched combination of strength, complexity, and smoothness that Serie V possesses. It pairs well with coffee, Tawny port, and dark beer and is best after a large meal. Comparable super-premiums include Ashton VSG and Padron 1926 Serie. Oliva has always been the cigar company for the true connoisseur, and Serie V has been the “connoisseur's cigar” since its inception.

Drew Estate Cigars is introducing the first-ever Lancero size for both the BLACKENED M81 and BLACKENED S84 cigars—a 7 x 40 vitola . ​Each Lancero expression will be limited in production and presented in 15-count boxes, making this drop an instant collectible for fans of both the M81’s bold Maduro-on-Maduro-on-Maduro profile and the S84’s refined, yet electrifying Connecticut Shade experience. ​“This new Lancero is a guitar solo in cigar form,” says Jonathan Drew, Founder and President of Drew Estate. “It’s long, lean, and delivers deep, concentrated flavor from foot to head. The M81 Lancero slaps with rich, dark, and heavy notes, while the S84 Lancero is like a clean intro riff—smooth, creamy, and soulful—but with that metallic edge.” ​Originally created in collaboration with Metallica’s James Hetfield, BLACKENED’s Master Distiller Rob Dietrich, and Drew Estate, the BLACKENED cigar line has become a sensation among cigar lovers and metalheads alike. The M81’s triple Maduro blend – Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, Maduro binder, and Maduro long-fillers from Nicaragua and Pennsylvania – offers a dark, earthy powerhouse. ​ Meanwhile, the S84, with its Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper and a rich mix of Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler, brings a bright, complex flavor profile with plenty of attitude. ​“The Lancero format showcases the blend in a way no other size can,” explains Dietrich. “You get this incredible ratio of wrapper to filler, making every puff more rich, more refined. Drew Estate announces the rebranding of the Herrera Esteli flagship brand, as well as the national release of the Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro and Herrera Esteli Miami. The entire, updated Herrera Esteli brand will be displayed in Drew Estate’s Booth at the IPCPR Convention and Tradeshow, held July 14-17, 2018 in Las Vegas Nevada. The Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro features a dense Plantation Grown Mata Fina wrapper, over a Connecticut River Valley Broadleaf binder with fillers from Nicaragua. Manufactured at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate, the Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro was blended by Willy Herrera is presented in 5 vitolas: Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Robusto Grande 5 ¼ x 52 MSRP $227.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Toro Especial 6 x 52 MSRP $241.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Lonsdale 6 x 44 MSRP $231.94/Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Fino 6 x 52 MSRP $269.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Short Corona Gorda 5 7/8 x 46 MSRP $203.94/ Box of 25 The Herrera Esteli Miami is crafted by level 9 rollers from Cuba at the El Titan de Bronze on Calle Ocho in Little Havana, Miami, – Willy Herrera’s Family Factory and the oldest remaining Fabrica in Little Havana. Like the Short Corona size featured at the 2016 IPCPR Tradeshow, the complete Herrera Esteli Miami line is expertly crafted with a lavish Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over a rich Ecuadorian Sumatran binder with select fillers from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. The new look of Herrera Esteli Miami features a black and gold color tone and is only available to Drew Diplomat Retailers in the following 5 vitolas: Herrera Esteli Miami Robusto Grande 5×50 MSRP $109.97/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Toro Especial 6×52 MSRP $117.47/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Lonsdale Deluxe 6.5×44 MSRP $112.97/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Piramide Fino 6.5×54 MSRP $127.47/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Short Corona Gorda 5 3/4 x 48 MSRP $97.97/ Box of 10 From Little Havana, Willy Herrera, Master Blender of Drew Estate, “The Herrera Brazilian Maduro is my expression of the floral and earthy Brazilian Mata Fina tobacco. We use it typically as a binder or accent tobacco in the filler but I wanted to showcase its dynamic and unique texture. I really like the black and gold color tone of the Herrera Esteli Miami and how it fits into the brand portfolio with multiple vitola expressions in the Miami blend. Working with my family on this brand takes me back to my blending roots and sincerely excites me.” The Herrera Esteli Habano and Herrera Esteli Norteno are receiving a new look for IPCPR 2018. Each will be presented in unified Herrera Esteli Branding and will now be packaged in 25 count boxes. Willy Herrera adds, “The uniform packaging for the Herrera Esteli line has elements of classic Cuban inspired branding mixed with modern simplicity. I loved the classic cabinet boxes, but it was time to partner with our retail tobacconists and create a more cohesive space for Herrera fans to find my blends on the shelf.” Herrera Esteli Habano blend features an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, Honduran Binder, and filler leaves from Nicaragua, presented in the following core vitolas: Herrera Esteli Habano Robusto Grande 5 ¼ x 52 MSRP $227.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Habano Toro Especial 6 x 52 MSRP $241.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Habano Lonsdale 6 x 44 MSRP $231.94/Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Habano Piramide Fino 6 x 52 MSRP $269.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Habano Short Corona Gorda 5 7/8 x 46 MSRP $203.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Norteno blend showcases extensively aged tobaccos from the Esteli, and Jalapa growing regions of Nicaragua, coupled with a Honduran Binder, and a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper in the following core vitolas: Herrera Esteli Norteno Robusto Grande 5 ¼ x 54 MSRP $227.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Norteno Toro Especial 6 x 52 MSRP $241.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Norteno Lonsdale 6 x 44 MSRP $231.94/Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Norteno Piramide Fino 5 x 50 MSRP $269.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Norteno Short Corona Gorda 5 7/8 x 46 MSRP $203.94/ Box of 25 If you are attending IPCPR stop by for a smoke at the Drew Estate Booth (Booth #1814), and a cocktail under the Water Tower curated by John Drew Brands.
