Nica Rustica Adobe, the second expression in Drew Estate’s value-priced Nica Rustica line, is now shipping to retailers nationwide. Introduced during the May 12 broadcast of “Freestyle Live: Special Edition,” and previewed by guests at the DE25 Exclusive Pre-Party event before the Florida Barn Smoker, Nica Rustica Adobe brings to life the soul of the lively and romantic barrios and colorful colonial houses of Estelí, Nicaragua, home to La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate. While similar to the Nica Rustica Connecticut Broadleaf expression, Nica Rustica Adobe is spicier, made from a Habano wrapper, Brazilian binder and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos from Estelí and Jalapa. Available in three sizes: Toro (6 x 52), Robusto (5 x 54) and Gordo (6 x 60), Nica Rustica Adobe is packaged in 25-count boxes that are adorned with colorful original artwork designed by Subculture Studios, which captures Estelí’s rugged, robust and rustic character. Nica Rustica Adobe’s artwork also features Estelí’s official symbol, El Brujito, an estimated 6,000-year-old petroglyph of a native shaman that was discovered on a rock atop a mountain near the city. Now available at retailers nationwide, Nica Rustica Adobe presents an excellent value for all premium cigar lovers, from beginners to aficionados. Robusto has an MSRP of $129.93/box or $5.20/cigar; Toro has an MSRP of $143.93/box or $5.76/cigar; and Gordo’s MSRP is $161.93/box or $6.48/cigar.

It does not get any better than when My Father Cigars releases a new smoke, and their latest is the My Father El Centurion H-2K-CT. Sure, the name is a bit of a mouthful but so are the reams of smoke that carry this new stogie’s complex and profound flavors directly to the palate. Let’s break it down, shall we? As one of the shining cities atop the hill that is the cigar world, the My Father Cigar company, under the direction of Jaime Garcia and the inimitable ‘Don Pepin’ Garcia, is responsible for some of the best cigars anywhere. The El Centurion Blend, a hearty Nicaraguan mix of Criollo and Corojo rumored to be Pepin’s personal blend, was first released in 2007 to wide acclaim. Now, the H-2K-CT (meaning the Habano 2000 wrapper grown in the Connecticut River Valley) is unleashed to conquer the hearts and tongues of aficionados everywhere. The exclusive sun grown Habano 2000 that graces each box-pressed El Centurion H-2K-CT was developed as a collaboration between Jaime Garcia and a Connecticut farm willing to take on the challenge of departing from the state’s usual shade or broadleaf varieties. With its creamy caramel color and an aroma of toasted malt, we can only say they nailed it. After the expected Pepin-esque blast of black pepper, the wrapper provides a honeyed citrus peel and cedar overcoat to the sultry filler tobaccos full of dark cocoa, vanilla cream, roasted almonds, and cherry stem. Evolving as it slowly burns to include espresso, toffee, and nutmeg, these medium-strength yet utterly full-bodied cigars will leave your senses battered yet crying out for more. Most of the world-class sticks coming out of the Garcia’s Esteli-based factory are surprisingly affordable, and the My Father El Centurion H-2K-CT is no exception. For about less than half the cost of some of the ‘Ultra Premium’ brands, the thrifty enthusiast will have a cigar that can handily beat each and every one when it comes to flavor and satisfaction. Get yours now and prepare to be amazed.

o the beautiful triple cap and give a light tug on the cigar. The pre-draw is of aged tobacco with a citrusy, dark berry fruitiness . The draw is easy. I toast up, and as I’ve always said (starting right now), Pepin puts the “pep” in pepper! There is a blast of pepper, with cedar and leather, billowing in a cloud of chalky white smoke and a finish that lingers in the back of my throat – a great first draw! The flavors continue to be what I would describe as “traditional” aged tobacco , cedar , leather , earthy , and of course, pepper . The smoke is full of texture, probably the most texture I’ve ever experienced in a cigar. It coats my entire palate and lingers for minutes on end. The La Antiguedad is a slow burning, long lasting cigar. I’m able to really enjoy each puff and let the cigar rest for a few minutes at a time. The flavors build up in my mouth, so I’m pairing it with an unsweetened iced tea, and surprisingly it works really well. I’m about an hour in at this point and just passed halfway. It has required one relight and some minor touch ups. The flavors are consistent and still dominant. It is medium to full in body , leaning on the full side, and the strength is a perfect medium . Finishing up now and the cigar has yet to disappoint me, the flavors stay prominent with each draw and the retrohale has been nothing short of spectacular. Smoke billows the entire duration, it is a satisfying smoke and I am left feeling at peace. Sometimes I smoke a cigar that is great but I’m left in want of another one. This cigar is a “one and done” in a good way! Would I smoke this cigar again? Yes, most definitely. The price is right and the flavors are there—while it’s not the most interesting cigar in the MF lineup, I’d recommend buying 5-10 of these for your humidor. Short Link: My Father Cigars La Antiguedad Be sure to eat your Wheaties before smoking the La Antiguedad, because it is a long, luxurious smoke and you will need your stamina. I must mention, I did smoke the bigger 6" x 60 and was not as impressed. I believe the wrapper plays a lot to the flavors in this cigar. I highly recommend smoking the robusto size first to experience this cigar's optimum performance before experimenting with other vitolas. When it comes to top quality and unbelievably great tasting cigars, Don Pepin Garcia is one of the first names people think of, and the new La Antiguedad continues his streak of fantastic smokes. When the Flor De Las Antillas was named the best cigar of 2012 it is hard to believe that something may come out to top it, but we would be very surprised if the new My Father La Antiguedad doesn't get extremely high accolades on the 2014 list. Made in the famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, La Antiguedad has the finest of Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler tobaccos which are aged for a minimum of three and a half years. Double bound in both Nicaraguan Criollo and Corojo leaf, La Antiguedad is finished with a gorgeous Habano Ecuador Rosado Oscuro wrapper. With a name which roughly translates to "The Antiquity", the band echoes this feeling of nostalgia. A gorgeous old style cigar band scene is framed in gold accents which stand out strikingly against the dark rosado wrapper. Rigidly square-pressed, the construction on La Antiguedad is the perfection you would expect from Garcia. With barely a vein to be found and a look that is virtually seamless, this smoke burns as perfectly as any we have lit in a long time. The initial taste of cinnamon spice hits you at first, but after the first few puffs this milds into an astounding medium-to-full-bodied cigar with tons of flavor dancing across your palate. My Father La Antiguedad is another hit for Pepin and all in his amazing Nicaraguan factory. A great medium-to-full cigar which will not knock you down with spice but will make your mind dance trying to nail down all the flavors entering your mouth. This is a perfect mid-afternoon cigar and goes perfectly with a pick-me-up espresso to help finish off the day. If you like these, we would also highly recommend the Flor de las Antillas as well.

When a master of medium-to-full-bodied cigars, such as Don Pepin Garcia , sets his sights on a new market, you bet it gets cigar enthusiasts around the globe salivating. My Father Connecticut is not the spice bomb you may be used to from the famed cigar maker, but it is yet another amazing example of what a cigar can be when put in the hands of someone on top of their game. Mild-to-medium in body, this Nicaraguan beauty uses the finest Nicaraguan Habano and Criollo filler tobaccos bound with a flavorful Nicaraguan Corojo '99 leaf, but the real story is in the wrapper. The blonde Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper provides an amazing smoothness not often paired with a My Father cigar. This blend has been ranked as high as 90 by Cigar Aficionado . The classic My Father band is adorned with a secondary gold band to let you know immediately that you are smoking something unique. Even without this embellishment, any smoker would know, just by looking at the flawless golden-hued wrapper that encases this cigar, how different this is from other My Father sticks. Early notes of cream and nuts fill the palate and only a slight hint of that signature Pepin spice will dance off your tongue. Growing ever so slightly in strength through the cigar, this stick crests at a medium body. My Father Connecticut may be a change in what one would expect from a cigar from the famed maker and factory, but it is still an amazing flavorful cigar with impeccable construction. The lighter flavors on this one make it perfect for anytime of day. A perfect pairing for that morning coffee before you head out into the world. For a slightly different medium body cigar from the My Father factory, we would recommend a Cabaiguan Maduro.

Since its stunning introduction at the IPCPR trade show in 2018, My Father La Gran Oferta has captured the hearts of cigar enthusiasts the world over, firmly establishing a place in Don Pepin's regular production portfolio and quickly becoming one of the most successful blends released by the Nicaraguan giant to date. Literally translated, "The Great Offer," La Gran Oferta not only boasts seemingly unmatched quality, but is also one of the most affordable cigars offered under the My Father trademark. The simple, yet functional blend consists of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a red-hued Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper leaf. Though not as powerful as its My Father counterparts, La Gran Oferta delivers one of the most satisfying smoking experiences available from a new cigar in recent years. So satisfying, in fact, that Cigar Aficionado recently awarded it a 91 rating! As the saying goes, though, the proof is in the pudding, and one must experience this blend in person to truly grasp just how great this offer really is. Packaged in luxurious boxes of 20, La Gran Oferta wears the standard My Father band in addition to a secondary band which, according to the folks at My Father Cigars, "features stunning artwork created after a very old cigar brand that sold under the same name, around 1913." Beautiful in appearance, La Gran Oferta is masterfully rolled and offers an easy draw, producing massive clouds of thick, blue smoke. Black pepper opens the experience, along with hints of cayenne and cinnamon. Spicy and bold, but not overpowering, the flavor profile builds in strength as a definitive dark chocolate note carries along with it nuances of oak and espresso. As for the finish, there is sweet floral flavor and just a touch of black cherry through the nose. Clean, complex, and undeniably satisfying, it is so easy to see how My Father La Gran Oferta as taken off so quickly. A connoisseurs' cigar at a basic price point, you ask? The answer is a resounding YES, and it's something we have waited so long for from My Father Cigars. In fact, the last cigar offered by the company which demonstrated such a combination of quality and value was Flor De Las Antillas , and quite frankly, the two cigars are strikingly similar, though two very different blends. For experienced aficionados, or even someone looking to get into ultra-premium cigars, La Gran Oferta is an absolute no-brainer. My Father La Gran Oferta pairs beautifully with bourbon, dark beer, and coffee, and makes a phenomenal way to end a long week or a simply a productive day at work. Over the years, Don Pepin Garcia and his world-famous team at My Father Cigars have offered some of the greatest cigars ever produced. Now, however, this offer has become even better, and it is easily attained by any serious cigar smoker willing to spend just a bit more on something truly amazing. Don't hesitate to accept that offer; pick up a My Father La Gran Oferta today to experience one of the most acclaimed cigars of the decade.

Pre-light aroma from the foot is straight-up brownie batter, giving way to some cigarette tobacco aroma, followed by a leathery chemical smell. The cold draw offers sensations of sweetness, more of that brownie batter; not much else. As I toast the cigar, the girth, excessive labels, and box-press make it feel clunky and unwieldy—I almost drop it several times as I try to roll it over the soft flame. Smoke output starts out pretty heavy, despite the draw being a touch (or two) looser than what I would like; akin to drinking root beer through a straw with a hole in it, rather than a drinking a milkshake. I used a v-cut, as larger ring gauges with box-press seem to smoke pretty well that way (guillotine-style cutters can occasionally damage pressed cigars, as the square shape of the cigar is met with the rounded blade). Initial flavors are of coffee, black pepper, heavy doses of cedar, and cinnamon bark (to be differentiated from the more pleasant, ground cinnamon flavor). Ten minutes or so in and the pepper has faded into the mix—pretty on-par for a MF release. I’m blasting through this cigar pretty quickly; the light draw starts to seem kind of airy, and after 21 minutes, I move into the second third. Body is not quite medium (I hope it makes it that far), with flavor and strength not far ahead, although they are at least asking to be let into the building where medium resides… The second third brings a pretty enjoyable chocolate shortbread flavor, which is the first hint of the gooey, sweet flavors from the cold draw. Cinnamon has transitioned from the tannic, herbal, medicinal tree bark flavor of the first third into the more pleasant baking spice realm. The mild black pepper sits right on the back of the tongue. Some mild anise and licorice root join the fold (think those little candy-coated fennel seeds you get at Indian restaurants). I feel more like I’m picking flavors out of the ether, than deciphering a palate-full experience. I’m looking, reaching, waiting for the cigar to really present itself. The cigar’s airy draw is really holding it back, I think. Opulence (in reference to the cigar’s title) is typically used to describe extravagance, lavishness, richness; whereas the experience speaks more towards elegance, refinement, or restraint. It’s certainly tasteful, but I was expecting more of a big, chewy, full-bodied experience. The robusto does begin to gain traction, but still not even into medium territory, as the second third closes after a much-improved 35 minutes. Into the final third, the cigar is not as light, both in terms of smoke production and flavor. The draw has firmed up a little, and the spiciness is coming back into the picture. This is more along the lines of what I had expected. There’s big coffee flavor, some creaminess, black tea with garden mint, even a little raspberry jam to kick in some sweetness. There is lots of cocoa going into the final inch, backed by nutty brown butter. Finishing with spice and anise, this cigar completes its nearly two-hour journey into finally reaching medium strength and body, with flavor nearing the medium-full line. The burn was dead straight throughout the experience, with nary a touchup required. Ash was firm and held over an inch throughout.

My Father La Opulencia is among the finest cigars offered by Don Pepin and My Father Cigars down in Nicaragua. Making its debut in 2017 and storming into the world of cigars in full force, La Opulencia has garnered boatloads of positive attention and is quickly becoming a favorite among loyal My Father fanatics. It is, in essence, a box-pressed extension to the world-renowned My Father brand, but is tweaked just enough to be "different." As for the blend, La Opulencia consists of a bold, complex core of Nicaraguan long fillers. A double Nicaraguan binder (Corojo and Criollo), and a gorgeous Mexican Rosado Oscuro wrapper leaf. Though the recipe seems simple, the end result is a work of art that has already earned multiple 90+ ratings, including a more-than-respectable 95 rating from Cigar Aficionado . Expertly rolled and beautifully box-pressed, La Opulencia gleams with natural oils and flaunts a luxurious marbled appearance. The hand-crafted vitolas come elegantly double-banded and sport a green ribbon at the foot. An impeccable level of construction paired with just the right amount of press gives La Opulencia an easy draw, making for massive smoke production and a smooth, crisp burn. A dry puff lends the spicy note of cinnamon that My Father cigars have come to be known for. At first light, the palate is greeted by Don Pepin's signature pepper blast , yet in the case of La Opulencia, it's far from overwhelming. The initial white pepper soon turns earthy and creamy, evolving into a deep, rich profile of spice, sweet tobacco , and bakers' spices. On the finish, a spicy cayenne note tingles the nose as a burst of nutmeg flavor and a hint of cocoa follow. There is also a faint mix of coffee and cedar lingering throughout, making for a delightful multi-layered experience. La Opulencia resides on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied, an interesting contrast to the powerhouse that is the original My Father. From first light to final puff, it's clear that La Opulencia was blended with the most sincere connoisseurs in mind. Only the most seasoned aficionados will truly appreciate the immaculate complexity and superb quality offered by My Father La Opulencia. Similar to My Father masterpieces such as Flor de Las Antillas and Le Bijou 1922 , La Opulencia seems to be on a fast track to the top, putting less emphasis on potency and focusing on satisfying cigar enthusiasts with a delicious flavor profile and layer upon layer of mind-numbing complexity. La Opulencia comes in boxes of 20 and is offered in 6 luxurious regular production sizes. Medium-full-bodied, La Opulencia pairs well with scotch, bourbon, or dark rum, but is not a bad match with creamy coffee or even a cup of espresso after dinner. "La Opulencia" literally translates to "The Opulent," and how appropriate of a name for such a sophisticated cigar! Whether you're a long-time My Father fan or just in the market for the next big thing, My Father La Opulencia is without a doubt the cigar you've been waiting for.

La Promesa’s wrapper gave off notes of peppercorn, leather, and hay, with a faint barnyard aroma. The foot offered notes of baking spice, sweet cinnamon, and nutmeg, while the cold draw tasted of cinnamon toast. The first thing I wrote in my notes was “interesting start.” This was due to an assortment of caramel, mild milk chocolate, and nuts throughout the first third, with a bright white pepper kick on the retrohale. The nutty flavor was in the driver’s seat for the first two inches. The rest of the flavor notes were a distant second to the nutty characteristics and the white-pepper-filled retro. It was a pleasant beginning and I was looking forward to some transitions. The middle third was pretty much the same as the first. Nutty notes were running wild and the white pepper continued its domination of the nostrils. There were some notes of chocolate and caramel, but they were not highlighted and were not gaining any strength. A creamy cedar note arrived at the midpoint and was a welcomed addition. The strength and body picked up a bit crossing the halfway mark, verging into medium-plus territory. The final third was a bit disappointing, unfortunately. Earthy notes picked up and a bitterness kicked in as things came to a close. My second experience smoking La Promesa was a carbon copy of the first. The flavors and transitions were exactly the same.

My Father La Promesa is a cigar behind which is great meaning for Don Pepin Garcia. Literally translated as "The Promise," La Promesa stands as a testament to the promise he made to his family upon leaving his native Cuba. This promise was simple, yet would prove to be a lifelong undertaking: "To prove himself and to make something of himself in the cigar world outside of Cuba." Decades later, My Father Cigars is among the most dominant names in the business, with farms in Nicaragua and factories both in Nicaragua and Miami, not to mention numerous Cigar Of The Year awards to boot. It's safe to say Don Pepin kept that promise, and is now commemorating and celebrating with La Promesa. Made in Don Pepin's state-of-the-art My Father factory in Nicaragua, La Promesa consists of Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos grown on the Garcia family's very own farms. The wrapper is a Nicaraguan Habano Rosado Oscuro, tying the package together and adding richness and complexity. Sounds "promising," doesn't it? The My Father La Promesa series has received high marks from industry experts, specifically with the Lancero vitola earning a 92 rating from Cigar Aficionado for its balanced profile of oak, leather, and bright citrus. Reddish hued, oily, and appearing to be completely seamless, the ultra premium wrapper leaf is quite a sight to behold. It contrasts beautifully with the classic My Father band, and in this case the green and blue secondary band which boldly proclaims "La Promesa." An expert roll leads to an amazing draw, highly productive of billowing clouds of dense, white smoke. To start, the trademark "Pepin Pepper" is definitely there to make an appearance. This blast of spicy Nicaraguan goodness is followed by creamy raw tobacco and cinnamon, with cedar and brown sugar on the finish. Bold and complex, La Promesa has quite enough kick to be satisfying, but is much tamer than some of Don Pepin's previous offerings. Just shy of full-bodied, La Promesa was obviously blended with true aficionados in mind. Whether a seasoned connoisseur or a die hard Don Pepin fanatic, La Promesa is the cigar for you. Medium-full-bodied, complex, and satisfying, the depth of the flavor profile is indubitably Pepin-style. La Promesa pairs well with bourbon, port wine, and sweeter dark beer, and is similar in stature to such other phenomenal My Father masterpieces as La Opulencia and Flor De Las Antillas Maduro . Jose Don Pepin Garcia is one of the most well known, beloved, and talked about cigar makers on the planet. His promise to become great has not only been fulfilled, but surpassed. Experience the greatness of Don Pepin Garcia and be a part of that promise with La Promesa by My Father Cigars.

Steeped in a traditional tobacco family of fathers and sons, the My Father Le Bijou 1922 is a tribute by Don Pepin to his own father. Le Bijou means "the jewel" in French, and 1922 is the year Don Pepin's father was born. The My Father Le Bijou 1922 blend is a Nicaraguan puro that makes use of the delicious Habano Oscuro leaf for its wrapper. The Torpedo (Box Press) was named the #1 Cigar of the Year for 2015 by Cigar Aficionado magazine. The flavors most prevalent after lighting continued to be that of bitter dark chocolate, tobacco, and some baking spices , but the Pepin blast of pepper still never really showed. Sure, there was a bit of pepper here and there, but not what we're used to. Trust me, the cigar is still good. It's just shocking to not have a pepper blast. The My Father Le Bijou 1922, is a beautiful cigar that comes in one of the prettiest boxes I've ever seen, making it a great gift for your father, your son, or even the father of your children. Though on second thoughts, you might just want to keep them all for yourself. This cigar is well deserving of the #1 spot.

E.P. Carrillo Allegiance is the fourth installment in the world famous Perez-Carrrillo lineup, following La Historia , Encore , and Pledge . Some would say this series is one of the most successful ever, as two have earned cigar of the year and one was a close runner-up. That being said, Allegiance had to have a lot to bring to the table. What is interesting about this cigar, however, is that unlike the first 3, Allegiance is made hundreds of miles away from Carrillo’s own Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic. In fact, Allegiance isn’t even made by one of Carrillo’s own factories! You read that right, this stick is actually hand-built in Esteli, Nicaragua at Tabacalera de Oliva! As for the blend, we have Nicaraguan binders and fillers and, of course, an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper leaf (Would you expect anything less from E.P. Carrillo?). The first run consisted of 150,000 cigars, but more may be rolled depending on demand. All things considered; it goes without saying that Allegiance was destined for big things. Soon after its release, it earned multiple 95 ratings from Cigar Aficionado , and the Allegiance Confidant ranked #5 in 2023 , proving it has what it takes to stand among the finest Perez-Carrillo cigars. Bearing the all-too-familiar Perez-Carrillo Series attire, Allegiance stands out from the crowd with bright green and gold colors. The green ribbon around the foot denotes the brand, and the overall presentation is impeccably gorgeous. Looks aren’t where it ends, though. Each and every stick is made to exact specifications, undergoing rigorous quality inspections throughout the production process. This stick performs as well as any other cigar with E.P. Carrillo’s name on it, offering an easy, productive draw and copious clouds of thick, white smoke. This cigar opens up with a burst of spicy Nicaraguan pepper , quickly settling down to an array of cedar, dark chocolate, and cinnamon . The entire flavor profile is built around a rock-solid core of earthy raw tobacco goodness. The finish is long, smooth, and powerful, yet all-in-all Allegiance finishes as a solid medium-full-bodied cigar . While there is nothing particularly fancy about the blend itself, Allegiance, like its other Perez-Carrillo counterparts, is aimed at a more experienced crowd. Considered an ultra-premium offering, this blend is medium-full-bodied, complex and satisfying. It pairs well with scotch, bourbon, or cognac, and is a great way to settle down after dinner. It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to know that this cigar is destined for greatness. Following in some of the biggest footsteps in cigar history, it is already on the right path. Whether you are a long-time fan of E.P. Carrillo cigars or just want to see what a “Cigar of the Year” caliber cigar tastes like, you will never go wrong with Allegiance by E.P. Carrillo.

The three cigars start off pretty much the same, with lots of spice on my tongue and strong notes of anise and black pepper. After more than 15 puffs, the profile transitions to the main flavors of terroir and leather on the first cigar, while the second and third cigars feature a combination of dry cedar and creamy cashews. At various points, secondary notes of cinnamon, toasted bread, gritty earth, bitter espresso, baker’s spices, and a touch of floral show up. While the first cigar has a fairly standard combination of black pepper and vanilla sweetness, there is a distinct but not overwhelming red pepper on the finish of the second and third cigars—it is strongest on the second cigar—and that note also shows up on the retrohale, where it is combined with a light graham cracker sweetness. Flavor for the first cigar ends the first third at medium-full, while the other two cigars are at full, the body is between a strong mild and a solid medium and the strength of all three cigars hits a solid medium. Construction-wise, the first cigar needs two separate burn corrections to stay on track, but that’s the only issue. During the second third, the second Perez-Carrillo Ascend Ridge rises above the other two, mostly due to a new caramel sauce sweetness on the retrohale that combines wonderfully with the red pepper that is still present. The first cigar continues to be less interesting in the flavor department with main flavors of earth and leather, while the second and third cigars have more captivating main flavors of cocoa nibs and creamy cedar. Secondary notes include coffee grounds, baker’s spices, creamy hay, anise and light chalk. On the retrohale of the third cigar, a combination of graham crackers and red pepper is still present—albeit slightly less than what I noted in the first third—while the first cigar sticks with black pepper and sweet vanilla. Flavor intensity does not change—medium-full for the first cigar, full for the second and third cigars—while the body and strength are at a solid medium. note_sources.text: Great rich chocolatey leathery flavor. Full bodied with lots of dark chocolate and espresso notes and a little spice in the background that comes forward on the retrohale.

Some cigars make an impression from the very first draw. Others reveal their true character over time. The E.P. Carrillo Deep Blue Limited Edition was created to do exactly that. Inspired by the unexplored depths of the ocean and the mythology of Hades, where the greatest mysteries lie beneath the surface, Deep Blue reflects Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's long-time philosophy that the finest cigars are those that continue to evolve throughout the entire smoking experience. Every draw invites you to go a little deeper, rewarding patience with new layers of flavor and complexity. Handcrafted at the renowned Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic, this limited-edition release features a beautiful Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper over a Honduran binder and carefully selected Nicaraguan long-fillers. The blend was meticulously developed to progress naturally, allowing each tobacco to contribute its own character as the cigar unfolds. Rather than delivering its full strength immediately, Deep Blue builds with remarkable balance, offering a refined medium-plus profile that grows richer and more expressive from beginning to end. Construction is flawless, reinforcing E.P. Carrillo's reputation for uncompromising quality and exceptional craftsmanship. The experience opens with a smooth sweetness accented by delicate floral notes before richer flavors of earth, cedar, leather, and baking spice gradually emerge. As the cigar develops, the body deepens and the spice becomes more pronounced, while the natural sweetness of the Jalapa wrapper continues to provide balance. Every transition feels deliberate, creating a dynamic smoking experience that rewards those who enjoy complexity that unfolds rather than overwhelms. Produced in just 2,500 individually numbered boxes of 20 cigars , the E.P. Carrillo Deep Blue Limited Edition is a rare expression of Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's mastery of balance, progression, and craftsmanship. Rich without excess, powerful without aggression, and endlessly engaging, Deep Blue is a cigar that reminds us the greatest discoveries are often found by those willing to venture a little deeper.

3 Cigar of the Year – Cigar Aficionado rated 96 Taste – Medium Full-Flavored Encore , a cigar celebrated as Ernesto’s greatest achievement in cigar craftsmanship. This exquisite cigar tantalizes the smoker’s palate with its complex flavor profile and exceptional quality. From the first draw, the Encore cigar delivers an invigorating burst of zesty and spicy flavors, featuring a prominent peppery kick and refreshing citrus zest. These robust woody flavors harmonize beautifully with the initial zestiness, creating a balanced and intricate taste experience.

The first puff is VERY perfumey and excellent construction becomes evident, as the draw produces thick, rich plumes of smoke instantly. The smoke just pours out of the Encore; I get flavors of wild herbs, with some tanginess on the tongue. On the retrohale this cigar has a real bite to it; there is white pepper with some power behind it. Encore is incredibly high on flavor while being a lighter-bodied cigar, it is evident to me why this cigar is beloved by some for these unique qualities. Notes of gin botanicals and some brown sugar are the main flavors at this point, with some tanginess on the back of the palate. The ash is tight and the flavors are rich; some flavors of cedar and red pepper start to appear moving past the first inch. The retrohale still has some sting to it, and the

note_sources.text: A 96-rated Nicaraguan Puro by Cigar Aficionado from one of the most respected Dominican cigar companies in the business, E.P. Carrillo Encore will have you cheering for a second as soon as you finish your first. Yes, all references to a musical encore in both this description and the cigar's frontmark are intentional. What, you didn't know that years ago a young Ernesto Perez-Carrillo was hoping to be a famous jazz drummer before coming back to his roots as a fourth-generation cigar-maker? Well, now you do. Treating tobacco blending as much an art as a science, Carrillo sourced a wide variety of fine Nicaraguan longleaf aged in tercios, meaning tied into bundles within royal palm leaves, resulting in a smooth yet powerful smoke you'll want to revisit again and again. On occasion, the look and feel of a cigar speaks directly to the performance that the lucky smoker is about to experience. Heavily laden with succulent tobacco the box-pressed barrel of an E.P. Carrillo Encore wears its cream-colored foot ribbon and dual copper and gold bands with confidence, reflective of its creator's skill as developed through years of rigorous practice and training. The toothy, oily wrapper contains the aroma of rich tobacco and crisp fresh hay, thrilling the nose while the tongue detects a flourish of pepper during the cold draw test. Beginning dry and with deep notes of turned earth and charred oak when first lit, the cigar's flavor soon brightens and expands to include black tea and sweet cream . Building slowly into full-bodied flavor, the strength remains a firm medium even as a crescendo of leather, citrus, and caramel washes over the palate. Only a virtuoso of tobacco such as Ernesto Perez-Carrillo could create a monumental smoke like the E.P. Carrillo Encore. These premium cigars are a ticket to taste, relaxation, and pure enjoyment so pour yourself a favorite beverage, put on some swinging tunes, and sit back. Just don't be surprised when you light up another.

Featuring the rare Meerapfel Cameroon wrapper, Endure delivers elegance and depth with rich flavors and signature Meerapfel spice.

E.P. Carrillo Cigars announces the launch of Endure, the first release in the Perez-Carrillo Premier Collection. This expertly crafted blend honors resilience, heritage, and unwavering character—values at the core of E.P. Carrillo. Featuring the rare Meerapfel Cameroon wrapper, Endure delivers elegance and depth with rich flavors and signature Meerapfel spice. Initially, Endure will be available in Robusto and Toro vitolas (10ct boxes retailing at $18 and $20 per cigar respectively), with a Corona Gordo size scheduled for release at a later date. Scavenger Hunt Contest Endure Scavenger Hunt – Find the Signature, Win Big! To celebrate the launch of Endure, E.P. Carrillo is hosting a Scavenger Hunt Contest for cigar enthusiasts! Hidden in the first shipment are 30 prize boxes, each containing one special cigar (out of the ten cigars) with a signed band on the back: 25 boxes include a band signed by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo, redeemable for an Endure ashtray and cutter set. 5 grand prize boxes feature a band signed by Ernesto, his son Ernesto III, and daughter Lissette, winning an ashtray, cutter, and a special Endure Humidor. Don’t forget to look behind the band! To claim your prize, present the signed band and proof of purchase at the store where you bought it.

E.P. Carrillo is one of the most dominant names in the world of premium cigars, holding a near-permanent spot on “Best Of” lists and remaining among the most sought-after brands in any humidor. So, it comes as no surprise that whenever a new line is released under the E.P. Carrillo name, the entire cigar industry seems to pause and take notice. That was exactly the case with the launch of E.P. Carrillo Endure , which immediately drew attention as a blend destined for greatness. Produced at the Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic, Endure begins with a filler and binder blend of all-Nicaraguan premium tobaccos. The real standout, however, is the wrapper—an authentic African Cameroon leaf cultivated by the renowned Meerapfel family. Since Ernesto Perez-Carrillo rarely works with Cameroon wrappers, this release is nothing short of a big deal. Unsurprisingly, Endure earned multiple 91 ratings from Cigar Aficionado right out of the gate. Presented in striking orange-branded boxes, these box-pressed masterpieces wear three orange-and-gold bands along with a tissue wrap. The bold E.P. Carrillo logo gleams proudly across the main band, reminding aficionados that when Ernesto puts his name on a cigar, uncompromising quality is guaranteed. Consistency is a hallmark here—each vitola offers effortless draws and produces dense, aromatic clouds of smoke. Flavors begin with cedar and earthy raw tobacco , gradually unfolding into layers of cream, fresh bread, and black pepper , with a subtle sweetness lingering on the finish . Medium-to-full-bodied, Endure is as flavorful as it is balanced, a true testament to its prestigious name. Designed for seasoned enthusiasts, Endure embodies the qualities true connoisseurs look for: depth, complexity, balance, and a strength level that is smooth yet satisfying. It pairs beautifully with bourbon, scotch, or a medium-bodied beer, making it an excellent choice for celebratory occasions. Fans of other renowned Perez-Carrillo blends such as La Historia or Encore will no doubt find Endure to be equally compelling. Genuine Cameroon over Nicaraguan tobaccos, crafted under the watchful eye of one of the greatest figures in modern cigar making—this is the essence of E.P. Carrillo Endure. Experience the future of ultra-premium cigars today.

Few names in the premium cigar industry command as much respect as E.P. Carrillo , a brand synonymous with exceptional craftsmanship, innovation, and some of the most celebrated cigars on the market. The E.P. Carrillo Essence Connecticut continues that philosophy as the fourth addition to the acclaimed Essence Series, joining the Maduro, Sumatra, and Honduras blends with a profile designed to be smooth, balanced, and endlessly enjoyable. Crafted at the renowned Agroindustrias DIADEMA factory in Honduras, only the second Essence blend produced outside of Casa Carrillo, this cigar combines Honduran and Dominican fillers with a Honduran Criollo 98 binder and a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. The recipe may be straightforward, but the smoking experience is anything but ordinary. The presentation is every bit as refined as the blend itself. A pale golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with a gentle sheen gives the cigar an elegant appearance, perfectly complemented by the Essence Series' modern black, gold, and red bands. Construction is impeccable, producing a razor-sharp burn, a firm light-gray ash, and thick clouds of smooth, aromatic smoke. From the first draw, notes of cream , hay , and light pepper establish a mellow foundation. Layers of toasted almond and cedar soon emerge, while a subtle sweetness and classic tobacco character linger in the background. The finish is clean, balanced, and satisfying, settling comfortably at a medium body without ever becoming heavy. Made for smokers who appreciate nuance and craftsmanship, the Essence Connecticut is approachable enough for newer enthusiasts yet refined enough to earn a place in any seasoned aficionado's rotation. Its smooth profile pairs beautifully with a morning coffee, a light bourbon, or a crisp lager, making it one of the most versatile cigars in the Essence lineup. If you're searching for a Connecticut cigar that delivers flavor, balance, and sophistication without sacrificing character, the E.P. Carrillo Essence Connecticut is ready to awaken your senses in an entirely new way.

70 Mad: 7 X 70 Taste – Medium Full-Flavored Born big to smoke bigger, the INCH Maduro stands as the epitome of the big ring gauge experience. The INCH Maduro delights the palate with a rich and bold flavor profile. Smokers will savor the sweet, earthy notes that define this cigar, with hints of spice and cedar adding depth and complexity. This harmonious blend of flavors creates a full-bodied smoking experience that is both dynamic and satisfying.

If you seek massive amounts of sweet flavor from huge cigars, let us introduce you to the immensely tasty E.P. Carrillo Inch Maduro. So, it should be obvious already that these stogies are large, but don’t go thinking of them as a one-trick Clydesdale-sized pony. Oh no, because creator Ernesto Perez-Carrillo has earned his status as one of the biggest names in the tobacco business by churning out hit cigars one after the other, and the Inch Maduro is yet another top-rated colossus. Built using a vast wealth of premium longleaf filler from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic, these hefty vitolas are transformed into enormous triumphs with a flawlessly fermented Broadleaf Maduro wrapper of exceptional quality. Don’t forget to stretch before lifting a heavy E.P. Carrillo Inch Maduro from your humidor and make sure your cutter and lighter are up to the task of granting access to the generous flavors stored at the core. Despite the over-abundance of tobacco skillfully rolled into the barrel, you’ll find a rich draw and sultry flavors within moments of getting the broad foot fully smoldering. The palate will first detect semi-sweet dark chocolate coating thick layers of earth and oak, the cigar’s strength slowly building towards a creamy medium-full. With the latter half of the smoke a slow-burning tour, expect plenty of black coffee spiked with amaretto, some bursts of nutmeg and allspice, and a dollop of salted caramel. The sheer amount of enjoyment to be found in just one E.P. Carrillo Inch Maduro, makes the fact that they come in gargantuan yet affordable cabinets of 24 makes them even more appealing, don’t you think? You’ll need to dedicate plenty of time for the full experience, so make sure you have something smaller but equally as delicious on hand, maybe some cigarillos from Gran Habano or a tin of Davidoff Primeros Maduro, for when a short smoke break is all you’ve got. 70 Nat: 7 X 70 Taste – Medium Full-Flavored Born big to smoke bigger, the INCH Natural is the ultimate choice for aficionados who appreciate a substantial ring gauge. The INCH Natural delights the palate with its full-bodied flavor profile. Smokers will savor the robust spice, earthy undertones, and woody notes that dominate each puff. As you progress through the smoke, a subtle nutty flavor emerges on the back end, adding an intriguing layer of complexity to the overall experience.

The origin of a cigar's name can sometimes be an enigma, perhaps wrapped in history or obscurity, or even a private joke, but not so with the E.P. Carillo Inch Natural. It starts with identifying the creator as none other than the esteemed Ernesto Perez-Carillo, a man who every day honors his four generations of tobacco history but creating some of the world's best handmade smokes. Next, of course, is Inch, easily explained once you realize that the broad ring gauge of each vitola in the line measures close to an inch. Finally, the Natural Ecuadorian wrapper that completes the cigar adds a smooth, medium-strength character to the bold Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco within. Appropriately heavy in hand, you'll marvel at the skill involved in creating such an imposing stogie, the oily barrel sleek and flawless. The well-rolled filler tobacco within gives only slightly to pressure, revealing no soft spots and promising a pleasing draw that is confirmed during a cold draw test. The soft wood and spice detected on the tongue erupt into crisp cedar and fiery black pepper as soon as the E.P. Carillo Inch Natural is lit, thick clouds of smoke pouring forth to fill the room with a floral aroma. Mellowing slightly after the initial rush, the profile is a medley of espresso, tanned leather, earthy-sweet vanilla, warm buttered biscuit, and a touch of citrus peel. You're going to need some extra space to store these imposing 90-rated cigars, but if buying another humidor is not in the cards, be wary of friends offering to lend you room in theirs because they are going to love the E.P. Carillo Inch Natural, too. Maybe splitting a box will be the way to go, that way, you could also buy some El Rey Del Mundo Oscuro and Diesel Esteli Puros to really fill your cache. Each puff provides a symphony of flavors, making it a joy to smoke and a must-have addition to any cigar aficionado’s collection. Its robust and intricate flavor profile ensures that it will quickly become a staple in your regular rotation. Embrace the complexity and richness of the INCH Nicaragua , a cigar that stands out not only for its impressive big ring gauge but also for its unparalleled flavor and quality. Elevate your smoking experience with the full-flavored excellence of the INCH Nicaragua, and discover why it is a quintessential choice for discerning smokers.

Ernesto Perez-Carrillo is best known for his industry-dominating Dominican cigars, but has in recent years started experimenting with Nicaraguan tobaccos, and with great success. One such successful achievement is Inch Nicaragua, the third regular production installment to the well-known, larger-than-life Inch series, following Inch Natural and Inch Maduro . For this blend, Carrillo decided to collaborate with one of the best-known names in all of Nicaraguan tobacco: The Plasencia Family. Made in the Plasencia factory in Nicaragua, also known as El Cathedral, Inch Nicaragua is a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning it is entirely made of Nicaraguan tobacco—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler blend contains aged tobacco from Plasencia’s farms in Condega and Esteli, and the wrapper is a golden brown shade-grown leaf from Jalapa. The result is a spicy, well-rounded cigar set to satisfy the cravings of even the most enthusiastic fan of Nicaraguan cigars . Such a bold cigar should include bold packaging, and this is certainly the case with Inch Nicaragua. The label is simple and loud, yet refined and premium in appearance, a great way to compliment the cigar beneath the band. Construction on each and every stout vitola is immaculate, lending to a soft, productive draw and a tight white ash. The flavor journey, like that of most Nicaraguan puros, starts off spicy and intense. This soon settles to an earthy, chocolaty array of flavor that holds everything together, speckled along the way with blasts of cedar and nuts. A creamy texture overtakes the blend about halfway through, and the finish is dry, clean, and peppery. For an all-Nicaraguan cigar, this blend certainly presents a very interesting and complex flavor profile. Inch Nicaragua finishes on the heavy side, just about a notch below full-bodied. This cigar is by no means a beginners’ cigar by definition, but it sure makes a great way to get into heavier cigars for someone with a bit of experience. It also presents a gateway to get into the shorter, fatter cigars that have become so popular in recent years. Inch Nicaragua pairs well with coffee or full-bodied beer and is appropriate for just about any time of the day. Fans of such fat sticks as Nub Habano or Cain F Nub will definitely be impressed by the stature and flavor profile this cigar has to offer. E.P. Carrillo is one of the best in the business, so you know that any cigar bearing his name is going to be a hit. That being said, what are you waiting for. The time is now to experience one of the hottest new cigars to come out of Nicaragua with E.P. Carrillo Inch Nicaragua. Shop more E.P. Carrillo Cigars:

The well-rounded amalgamation of spice and earthy notes ensures that each draw is a moment to relish, allowing you to fully appreciate the intricate flavor profile of this cigar. The first few puffs of the La Historia are a bit mixed together. The biggest flavor is a smokiness, maybe a burning cherry wood, with a hefty mouthfeel lingering well onto the next draw. The finish does, however, leave a sweetness on the palate, similar to a cherry-like flavor that mixes well with the smoke. The retro-hale provides a nice increase of flavors as well, with a somewhat harsh white pepper, spices, and a very deep wood flavor that I can’t quite identify. The construction is fair so far, providing a good draw, but low smoke output. The ash holds on extremely well, never falling off till I tapped it around the halfway point. The cigar is a solid full body throughout the first third, finishing off with mostly “meaty” flavors, along with dark cherry, a little spice, and the smoked wood. Down to the nub, the La Historia never really changes. Remaining full body and medium-full strength, the lasting impact of flavors are smoked wood, sweet cherry, dark chocolate, a spice infusion, and a decent pepper kick on the retro-hale. The burn is great, lasting a good 1.5 – 2 hours, depending on the smoker, along with a very tight and consistent ash.

In 2010, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr., the architect behind the success of the modern La Gloria Cubana, introduced the E.P. Carrillo Core Line, and announced that a Connecticut cigar was to follow shortly. What Ernesto didn't tell the world was that he was going to try to reinvent the perception of Connecticut shade wrappers. The man that redefined Maduro named his newest line NWC, New Wave Connecticut. The result was a Dominican-made cigar that features an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan fillers offered in five sizes: Briliantes (5" x 50), Stellas (5 1/8" x 42), Divinos (6" x 52), El Decano (6" x 60) and Gran Via (7" x 49). The E.P. Carrillo New Wave Connecticut is not your typical Connecticut. While it's still medium in strength, the body and flavor are anything but strong. Even though most Connecticut's offer some form of pepper, the NWC features a significantly more developed flavor that shows complexities of cedar, leather, earth and cocoa. There's a decent amount of creaminess that begins to remind you that this is still very much Connecticut. While there is no individual flavor that would be considered mystical, it's the overall flavor that is so unique as far as Connecticuts go. Simply put, there is no Connecticut offered on the market that features as much flavor and complexity as the E.P. Carrillo NWC. This is a perfect cigar for those just getting started and great for those experienced smokers who have overlooked Connecticut due to its normal limitations. Check out other E.P. E.P. Carrillo Pledge is one of the most anticipated and coveted releases in the history of the brand. The third installment in the acclaimed Perez-Carrillo series—following La Historia and Encore —Pledge is widely regarded as the crowning achievement of Ernesto Perez-Carrillo, often called “The Godfather of Boutique Cigars.” Hand-rolled exclusively by the expert torcedors at Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic, Pledge features a meticulously crafted blend of ultra-premium tobaccos from three countries: Nicaraguan filler, an Ecuadorian binder, and a rich, dark Connecticut Habano wrapper grown in the U.S.A. Its predecessors set a high bar—La Historia earned a 95 rating and ranked No. 2 in 2014, while Encore reached a 96 rating and topped the charts in 2018. Pledge not only met those expectations in 2020, but surpassed them, achieving a historic 98 rating and claiming the No. 1 spot in the year’s top 25. This is a cigar collectors and aficionados alike are eager to experience. Presented in classic Perez-Carrillo style, Pledge comes in lacquered cedar boxes adorned with luxurious blue and gold artwork and finished with an elegant ribbon around each cigar’s foot. The construction is flawless: an effortless draw produces dense, billowing smoke, a crisp, even burn, and firm, gray ash. The box-press design adds a refined feel in the hand and a comfortable draw in the mouth. On the palate, Pledge opens with bold black pepper and lively Nicaraguan spice, gradually giving way to a smooth blend of earthy tobacco, toasted nuts, and rich espresso. Hints of cinnamon, cocoa, and subtle bread notes weave throughout, while the retrohale delivers a distinctly sweet finish. Medium-full-bodied, Pledge maintains perfect balance from start to finish. Pledge, like all cigars in the Perez-Carrillo series, is designed for experienced connoisseurs. Its sophisticated and multi-layered profile rewards those with a refined palate. Ideal for pairing with red wine, cognac, or bold coffee, it elevates any special occasion. While standing proudly alongside La Historia and Encore, Pledge also rivals other ultra-premium cigars such as Padron 1964 and Diamond Crown Maximus . With each release, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo continues to showcase his unparalleled blending skill and rich heritage. Highly sought-after and limited in availability, Pledge is a must-have for any serious cigar enthusiast eager to experience one of the finest cigars of our era.

The first few puffs bring a lighter body with medium strength; the draw is a little tight but I get a nice white pepper on the retrohale. Right off the bat, there is a zesty spice, almost like wasabi through the nostrils. This cigar is loaded with cabinet spices and there is a dash of nutmeg on the finish. It has some spice to it but is not necessarily full-bodied at this point, which is refreshing. Smooth smoke is pouring out on each puff and I am impressed by how silky and refined this cigar starts. The ash is dark grey and almost Cubanesque in appearance (I’m not saying the cigar tastes Cuban, but I feel like you, the reader, could file this away for future consideration), usually a sign of rich minerals in the soil. There is a chai tea flavor as the cigar develops; it’s this sweet-ish spice that reminds me of warm tea. I have had to do a couple of touchups and the draw is just a tad under what I would consider to be ideal. The burn is slightly wonky, but the peppery, cabinet spice flavor still appears prominently. I like that this cigar is very spice-forward and has a solid bit of strength, yet still maintains a near-medium body and some nuance and refinement. At this point, I’d still consider this a cigar that you could smoke in the morning because it doesn’t have that full-bodied punch that you find yourself seeking as the day winds down. The draw has really loosened moving past the halfway mark. I initially got a somewhat papery flavor with a tartness on the tongue but that quickly dissipates. A roasted nut flavor with some spice starts to move to the forefront; it kind of reminds me of those cinnamon-roasted almonds that you find at a fair. I have had to relight a couple of times—construction has been less than perfect throughout but hasn’t taken away from the performance much. As I approach the band, there is a bit more bitterness; there is kind of a burnt toast quality to the final bit of this cigar. Green chili flavors rush through the retrohale, true to the spicy quality that has been prevalent throughout the cigar. It has a pretty earthy base on the palate and hasn’t had too many noticeable changes from start to finish.

note_sources.text: Second Generation Cigar Makers, Alec and Bradley Rubin announced today that they will be expanding distribution of their inaugural release: Alec & Bradley Blind Faith at the Tobacco Plus Expo (TPE) in Las Vegas, NV- January 29-31. Under the tutelage of their father, Alec Bradley Cigar Co. founder Alan Rubin, the brothers began planning their own brand in 2017. Since they were both untested in the cigar business, they decided to name their cigar Blind Faith. Blind Faith was released to appointed merchants during the International Premium Cigar & Pipe Retailers Association (IPCPR) in 2018. “Alec & Bradley Cigars has grown leaps and bounds since our first introduction,” said Bradley Rubin. “Since the early success of Blind Faith, we had the opportunity to team up with the legendary Ernie Perez-Carrillo for our second release, Gatekeeper. As well, Alec and I are about to release Uru Doshi with Cigar Dojo. Alec and I both feel like we have gained the trust of tobacconists and enthusiasts. We asked for more capacity at Raices Cubanas to increase production of Blind Faith and we got it. Now we have the ability to get Blind Faith in the hands of more cigar lovers.” The Blind Faith blend features a wrapper from Alec Bradley’s proprietary farm in Trojes, Honduras. Three different fillers from Esteli are held together by a double binder combination from Honduras and Nicaragua. Unlike the Alec Bradley tradition of blending for flavor first and strength levels later- Alec and Bradley focused on taking bolder tobaccos and blending them for strength with great flavor and balance. “Bradley and I are very excited to expand the availability of Blind Faith,” said Alec Rubin. “This is the first time Alec & Bradley and Alec Bradley will be exhibiting at TPE; we thought that the show was a great opportunity to share this very special moment in our careers.” Blind Faith Formats and Prices: 5 x 52 Ring, Robusto | MSRP: $8.95 6 x 52 Ring, Toro | MSRP: $10.00 6 x 60 Ring, Gordo | MSRP: $10.95 Packaging: 20-count boxes Shipping: Global sales will begin on January 29

Cigar excellence runs deep in the Rubin family, and there could be no better demonstration of this than Alec & Bradley Gatekeeper. The second cigar line produced by Alec and Bradley Rubin, sons of Alan Rubin, owner of Alec Bradley Cigars, Gatekeeper has taken the cigar world by storm, earning a solid 95 Rating in Cigar Aficionado and a high spot on the famed magazine's top 25 list for 2020. For the blending and production of this project, the Rubin brothers looked to no other than the Godfather of boutique cigars himself, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. This brand was originally produced in his own Dominican factory, Tabacalera La Alianza, but has since moved to Danli, Honduras, where it is now rolled in Tabacos de Oriente, a factory owned by the Plasencia family. The blend remains the same, however, including fillers from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic, a Nicaraguan binder, and a dark, oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. All in all, Gatekeeper is a connoisseur-level cigar that leaves nothing to be desired.

We don't know where you got it from but we hear some of you think that Alec Bradley, the iconic brand behind the new Family Blend Lineage, are in their waning years. Sure, they've had some great cigars in the past such as Tempus or the stick that made Alec Bradley a cigar-smoking household name, MAXX , but those days are behind them, right? There's no illusion or sleight of hand involved when it comes to witnessing the amazing trick that is the Alec Bradley Magic Toast cigar. Instead, this feat of magnificent tobacco prestidigitation is the result of skills and intuition honed over many years of methodical hard work. It is true that brand founder Alan Rubin has been on a hot streak as of late, conjuring up the release of a host of fan favorites, but this may be his most spectacular revelation. Inspired in conjunction with AB partner Ralph Montero during a midnight visit to a Nicaraguan field that now serves as the source of some of the stogie's longleaf blend, each vitola also contains a choice selection of aged Honduran tobaccos beneath a Honduran wrapper as dark as a sorcerer's cloak.

While smaller ring gauges dominated the market, we chose to push back—crafting large-format cigars designed to maximize flavor, balance, and value. You do know there is no person named Alec Bradley behind the Alec Bradley MAXX cigar, right? Well, there ain't no Betty Crocker either, and we don't hear you complaining when you sit down to eat a cake. Not that there's any cause for concern. The fine men and women over at AB, led by founder Alan Rubin, have been cranking out the hits for years, including a large number of very highly rated gems we are sure you're familiar with. The MAXX is an early one, launched in 2005 and containing an amazingly complex blend of Colombian, Mexican, Honduran and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos beneath a Costa Rican binder and Nicaraguan wrapper. If you are a grizzled old-timer, you may cast a cautious eye at the oversized black and white band with MAXX imprinted vertically, the last X a bold red. No, it is not the smaller silver and garnet band you remember, but fear not because the savory flavor of the 91-rated Alec Bradley MAXX is the same as it always has been, so it is time to light up! With a knuckle wrapped around the dark and toothy barrel of the stogie, long and deep pulls of creamy smoke will reveal a pepper-driven profile smoothed with hints of milk chocolate and churned butter. With its strength solidifying at medium-full, the second, third launches with a rush of espresso and cedar while the final stage of the smoke is a long slow slide through earth, cocoa, and spice. During the act of smoking an Alec Bradley MAXX, you will discover why the company has earned the success it enjoys today. Quality, taste, pleasure. These are the hallmarks that make AB cigars beloved worldwide. Those in the know need no explanation. For the few aficionados who have yet to make an acquaintance, we will hold the door open for you.

Never one to shade the truth, owner Alan Ruben crafted the Post Embargo in recognition of the fact that cigar makers of all stripes have been trying to recreate the Cuban experience for decades, but it also reveals a company ready to go toe-to-toe in competing with the legendary island brands. Containing colorful and majestic Nicaraguan and Honduran longleaf as the filler and pulling double duty as binders, each stick is finished with a Honduran wrapper of excellent quality and flavor.

The Alec Bradley Prensado is a cigar that continues to amaze and astound a worldwide array of aficionados to this very day, after its big brother, the 96-rated Churchill was hailed as cigar Numero Uno for all of 2011. It's not like company founder Alan Rubin would just abandon his prized possession after having it reach the top. Through the years, he and all the fine folks at Alec Bradley have worked tirelessly to maintain the taste, quality, and artistry for which they are so well known. It's an incredible feat indeed, what with the challenges of growing tobacco in ever-changing conditions, that the Nicaraguan and Honduran longleaf filler and complimentary Trojes-grown Corojo wrapper crucial to the Prensado's success have maintained the exact palate-pleasing character that made the cigar such a hit in the first place.

Each cigar is rolled using the "entubado" method for ideal airflow, then semi-pressed and finished with a classic triple cap — time-honored techniques that reflect a slower, more deliberate way of making cigars. Alec Bradley Prensado Lost Art is a cigar that pays homage to the "lost art" of handcrafting goods. Built on the platform of the original, highly-celebrated Prensado , the 2011 Cigar Aficionado Cigar of the Year, Prensado Lost Art boasts some added subtle twists and turns that make it a more up-to-date blend, so to speak. Made down in Honduras, Prensado Lost Art brings boatloads of flavor in a full-bodied blend of Nicaraguan and Honduran fillers, a dual binder (once again Nicaraguan and Honduran), and a spicy Honduran Corojo wrapper. As the long-awaited sister cigar to the original award-winning Prensado, Prensado Lost Art has some gigantic shoes to fill. However, a trio of 90+ ratings soon after its release show that Alan Rubin and his team have yet again hit one out of the ballpark. Connoisseurs, get ready. This is the stick you've been waiting for.

A cigar is not necessarily just a cigar when it is an Alec Bradley Project 40 . Where most stogie manufacturers are content with pumping out blend after blend with little regard for the smoker's overall well-being, the Project 40 was designed around the idea that cigar smoking can and should have a positive effect on the aficionado and the goal is to maximize that experience. To that end, a delightful blend of primo aged Nicaraguan longleaf has been captured beneath a potent Brazilian Habano binder to create a wealth of complex flavors suitable for a wide range of palates. This might be enough delicious tobacco for most, but AB's founder Alan Rubin has pushed the boundaries by obtaining a gorgeous Nicaraguan Colorado wrapper so good it's helped propel the stick to be named the #24 Cigar of the Year for 2019 by Cigar Aficionado . If you're in the mood for reading while smoking a cigar, the frontmark's mission statement as printed on the band of the Alec Bradley Project 40 will keep you intrigued just long enough to get the well-packed foot perfectly lit. Burning slow and steady, the cigar at first releases medium-strength clouds of smoke laden with black coffee, cedar, and spice . From these seemingly humble beginnings, the flavors gently begin to expand to include wheat toast, roasted peanuts, salt and pepper, sugarcane, and licorice . Remaining cool and smooth throughout, each stick is a delightful experience that leaves enthusiasts both young and old fully satisfied. Will you find a deeper connection to yourself just by smoking an Alec Bradley Project 40? Perhaps, so go ahead and check it out for yourself. You don't have much to lose because another of AB's plans was to create an excellent smoke for a great price, and here they have certainly succeeded. Who can't feel good about that?

The Alec Bradley Tempus Natural cigar is the real deal, friends. There's no need for hype or bold claims or shouting about ratings (even if it does lay claim to some 94's. Shhhhh). What we've got here is perhaps the ultimate expression of the skill and talent that exists at Alan Rubin's already much-heralded company. Big cigars are the rage nowadays, and Alec Bradley Texas Lancero has come to make its mark on the industry! Made under the supervision of Nestor Plasencia and Alan Rubin, this 7" x 70 monster is expertly crafted to satisfy the cravings of the most severe cigar nuts. Coming out of the Plasensia factory in Nicaragua, Texas Lancero is made with Nicaraguan wrapper and binder tobacco and a filler blend from Nicaragua, Honduras, and Costa Rica. With flavors every bit as huge as the cigar itself, Texas Lancero is a cigar made with the serious smoker in mind. Indubitably medium-bodied, Texas Lancero starts off with meaty, savory flavors along with a lingering earthiness in the background. Smooth, cool clouds of smoke deliver hints of cocoa and cinnamon, and the cigar is never overpowering. It's bold, it's tasty, and it delivers a wonderful 3 hours of smokable pleasure. Although named after the Lone Star State, Texas Lancero is actually available everywhere. With good reason, too! It can be enjoyed by just about anyone, whether newbie or aficionado; whether the preference is mild or strong; literally anyone can and should enjoy a Texas Lancero. Pairing well with beer or iced tea, Texas Lancero is comparable to other monsters such as MUWAT and Asylum . Although quite a cliché, the saying "Everything is bigger in Texas" most definitely applies here!

Considering its age, the Bellas Artes Corona Extra starts with a surprising amount of spice on my tongue, along with strong flavors of both fragrant floral and aromatic cedar followed by lesser notes of leather, earth, hay, cocoa nibs and almonds. There is a faint but distinct jalapeño jelly sweetness on the retrohale, which combines nicely with some black pepper that is also present. Construction-wise, the draw is excellent after a straight cut while the burn is close to razor sharp and there is a large amount of smoke emanating from the foot. In terms of strength, the cigar has issues getting above the mild mark, although it does begin to increase more noticeably just as the first third comes to an end. There is slightly more of the jalapeño jelly sweetness on the retrohale during the second third of the Corona Extra, which brings a bit more complexity to the profile that is now led by creamy cedar and almond flavors on the palate. In addition, other notes of hay, espresso beans, cocoa nibs, yeast, floral, leather and earth flit in and out. While there is not nearly as much pepper on the retrohale compared to the first third, it is still a noticeable amount, but it does seem to be decreasing as it passes the halfway point. In terms of construction, the burn and the draw continue to give me no issues and the smoke production continues to pour from the foot in large doses. Although the overall strength does increase a bit at the end of the second third, it still fails to reach the medium mark by the end of the second third. The final third of the Bellas Artes Limited Edition Corona Extra features a number of changes as the jalapeño jelly sweetness on the retrohale morphs into more of a vanilla bean note along with a bit more black pepper. In addition, the dominant flavors have also shifted to a combination of dark chocolate and cedar with lesser notes of earth, hay, creamy almonds, ground coffee and yeast. The spice on my tongue is long gone. The draw continues to impress, but the burn has become problematic enough that it needs correcting, albeit just once. note_sources.text: The Días de Gloria Brazil Toro starts with plumes of smoke, a creamy undertone in the flavor, and then an explosion of pepper and spice on retrohales that takes the leading role in the experience. One cigar reminds me of a packet of red chili pepper flakes that I put on a slice of pizza the other day in how it adds the same topline sensation and one cigar gets to be a bit too much for me to truly enjoy. Creaminess increases in the flavor, and while I find myself drawn to retrohales, I intentionally skip them to get a better feel for the flavor, and I’m surprised by how mild it is given the liveliness of retrohales. There is some building flavor as the first third progresses, some puffs have more of an earthy aspect, others have more of a cardboard sensation, while touches of black pepper are consistent. But if I had to put a ratio to what’s driving the experience in the first third of the first cigar, I’d say 80 percent is the retrohale and 20 percent is the flavor on my taste buds. If retrohaling and counting that as part of the flavor, there is no doubt this is a full-flavored first third. Without retrohales, it’s more medium in flavor. Body is medium and strength is medium-minus. The cigar flies through the first third with a smooth draw, creating puffs that push the burn line evenly up the cigar’s body. Smoke production remains very good. The second third keeps the retrohales lively and vibrant, though maybe a tick less intense than they were at the start of the cigar. The flavor stays fairly mild, though the creaminess is building in flavor and thickening in texture as the Días de Gloria Brazil Toro progresses, with those same supporting notes that taste like earthiness and almond. Around the midway point, the retrohales become a bit more concentrated and not as much like fireworks in my nostrils in the sense of hitting seemingly every receptor they can find and instead hitting with more of a blunt punch. There’s still more evolution of the creaminess on my taste buds, and I’m enjoying how it has turned into a melted vanilla ice cream sensation, both for its flavor and for how it serves as a counterbalance to the spiciness. A touch of char comes in as this
note_sources.title: Días de Gloria Brazil Toro

note_sources.text: The cold draw brings forth a subtle sweetness, but nothing more. A very nice cedar and hay aroma begins to fill the air during the toasting. On the first draw, a buttery sweet tobacco and graham cracker burst forth. With the figurado shape, there is always an initial blast of flavor in the beginning, where the ring gauge is smaller on the foot. This blast of flavor was simply delicious! I found myself salivating over the thick, creamy smoke and soon wished the entire cigar was a 30 ring gauge. Into the first third, the cigar quickly mellowed out. With the normal 52 ring gauge, there was no more full-body flavors, settling for a medium body. Butter and sweet toast make up the majority of the profile, along with graham cracker, faint chocolate, black pepper, and cedar and spice on the retro-hale. Around the halfway point, the cigar’s first ash fell. It held on nice and tight almost halfway, but after losing the foot, the Enclave never held on more than a half inch after that. Buttery sweetness still controlled the palate at this point, and the retro-hale lost most of the cedar—leaving just a general black pepper and subtle spice. Down to the nub, the flavors remained the same. The graham cracker and toast flavors came back with the added heat, also creating a walnut and pecan contour. The smoke developed a very rich and chewy texture. The

note_sources.text: Starting out, the cigars feature an overwhelming spice on my lips and tongue, along with some very aggressive black pepper and anise. After a longer than average time—around 15 puffs—the spice dies down noticeably and the profile changes to include main flavors of toasted cedar and powdery cocoa nibs. Additional flavors of charred meat, leather tack, gritty earth, chalk and almonds flit in and out, while the finish of all three cigars includes a slight coffee bean note. The retrohales are a bit different: while each cigar has some significant black pepper, the first and last cigars feature a brown sugar sweetness, while the second cigar has more of a milk chocolate note. Flavor is full, the body hits a point just under the medium mark, and the strength lands at a solid medium. Construction-wise, my first cigar needs a quick correction with my lighter, but the draws are excellent, and there is plenty of dense smoke for all three cigars. During the second third, the profiles shift a bit as dry hay and toasted cedar take over the top spots, followed by a still strong cocoa nibs note, cinnamon, earth, sourdough bread, charred meat and generic nuttiness. The note on the finish is now very different for each cigar: the first cigar features cinnamon, the second cigar features cloves, and the last cigar continues with the coffee bean flavor from the first third. There is also an increase in the amount of black pepper on the retrohale, and while that note falls short of being problematically strong, it does drown out the brown sugar sweetness that is now present on all three cigars at times. Flavor remains at full, the body increases to a solid medium, and the strength hits medium-plus easily. Once again, one of the cigars needs a quick touch-up with my lighter to avoid larger issues—albeit a different cigar than the one that needed a correction in the first third—and once again, that is the only construction problem for all three cigars. The final third sees almost no changes in the main flavors, as a combination of toasted cedar and hay continues to dominate all three cigars. However, there is an obvious increase in the amount of both gritty earth and leather flavors i
note_sources.title: New World Decenio Robusto

note_sources.text: Starting out, the New World Cameroon features some typical basic flavors, with some toast and creamy almonds barely taking the top spots. Other notes of hay, leather, earth, oak and coffee are all present, along with a small amount of maple sweetness that ebbs and flows throughout the first third. There is a bit of spice on the tongue pulled over from the cold draw as well as some slight white pepper on the retrohale, as well as a distinct—but far from overwhelming—metallic note on the finish. Smoke production off of the foot is copious and thick, and while the draw is excellent after a straight cut, the cigar has to be touched up once very early on. Strength-wise, the New World Cameroon starts off fairly mild, increasing to a point close about halfway between the mild and medium marks by the end of the first third. The New World Cameroon has few changes in store during the second third, although a dark chocolate note does start to become more noticeable in the profile, albeit not even close to strong enough to take the top spot from the still dominant flavors of toast and creamy almonds. Flavors of roasted coffee beans, leather, earth, oak and hay flit in and out as well, while the metallic note on the finish remains strong enough to be identifiable without being overwhelming. The maple sweetness from the first third is a bit stronger and more distinct as well, and although the spice from the first third is long gone by the halfway point, the white pepper on the retrohale remains fairly constant. Construction-wise, there is still plenty of smoke emanating from the foot and the draw continues to impress, while the burn has evened out nicely, giving me no more issues at all. Although the strength has increased noticeably compared to the first third, it still falls short of the medium mark by the time the second third comes to a close. While the second third of the New World Cameroon held few surprises, the final third changes quite a bit, starting with the fact that the dark chocolate note becomes the dominant flavor, relegating other notes of toast, creamy almonds, earth, leather, coffee beans and a touch of floral to the rear. note_sources.text: The Ramon Allones AJ Fernandez Torpedo begins with some cedar, buttermilk and white pepper, a bit sharper though more restrained than the pre-light notes. Eventually, the core settles to a vibrant mixture of earthiness, creaminess and a bit of a Sprite-like sweetness. The retrohale is even heartier with lots of cedar and a bittersweet cocoa before a massive black pepper takes over the finish. Flavor is full, body is full and strength is medium-plus. Construction is fantastic in the final third: great draw, no touch-ups and plenty of thick smoke. Shortly before the exact point of the second third a sweeter cedar takes over and dominates over a mixture of red and black pepper. It’s hearty, thick, yet somehow balanced, allowing each of the three flavors to hit various parts of the palate without seeming muddy. Even more surprising is the retrohale which begins floral before cinnamon takes over and transitions into a finish. Once there, the floral note returns before Worcestershire and pepper add themselves. It’s an incredibly detailed progression and one that adds a refreshing component to the dominant cedar. Flavor and body both remain full, while the strength lags a bit behind at medium-plus. There’s even more woodiness in the final third of the Ramon Allones AJ Fernandez Torpedo. It’s not the sweet and defined cedar note from the middle portion, but it still has a ton of character. Underneath that is some black pepper and an intense creamy finish. If I let the cigar sit for two minutes—which the burn holds enough to allow me to do—I can find some fruitiness and a generic sweetness over top of a much more restrained pepper note. However, if I puff at anything close to a normal rate and the black pepper is massive. Unfortunately, the complex retrohale is gone, now replaced by massive blows of woodiness and pepper. The flavor and body both remain full, while the strength remains medium-full.
