note_sources.text: The cold draw reveals a decent resistance, with a little cedar and earth resting on my tongue. After a very gentle toasting, the Futuro releases a blast of smoke with an impressive collection of flavors. Cedar, leather, herbal spices, pepper, and sweet wood form a great start to the cigar. A few minutes in, and a smooth cream and musty cocoa join in on the draw, with similar flavors from the start still on the finish. The body is full, with strong flavor and a decent amount of strength already detected. The retro-hale brings in more spices—a small amount of licorice with hints of coffee and herbs. There is also a saltiness that is detectable on the draw, but sadly dies away with the heavy finish. Halfway through and the Futuro is burning perfectly—a continued surplus of smoke, complimented by a superb draw, matched with a razor sharp burn line. The flavors haven’t made any big changes yet, although more wood and earth come in on the finish, overtaking the other, more delicate tones. The Futuro has proven quite impressive thus far. Its medium, but not-too-small size, matched with an excellent draw, delivers a very rewarding smoke—not to mention, fantastic flavor. Nothing transitional has taken place, but there is a vast array of flavors to be enjoyed here. Towards the end, the sweetness picked back up, and made a perfect match for what most cigars leave as a harsh finish.
note_sources.title: Warped Futuro

note_sources.text: Futuro is one of the earliest big hits to bear the name of Warped Cigars, then a respectable, yet tiny and up-and-coming boutique cigar brand with little more than a cult following. Now, nearly a decade after Futuro’s release, Warped is somewhat of a household name among cigar connoisseurs and those that love the tasty and unique creations brought about by boutique companies. Futuro, however, is not a stick that is made in-house, so to speak, by Warped. Rather, it is a collaboration with Max Fernandez Pujals of Casa Fernandez and AGANORSA, a brand that even back in the day had a rock-solid stance in the world of premium cigars. Together, the two names came up with a blend that would basically put Warped Cigars on the map, and appropriately so, as Futuro is literally translated from Spanish as “Future.” Made at Fernandez’s TABSA in Nicaragua, Futuro’s blend consists of Nicaraguan Corojo 98 and Corojo 99 filler leaves, a Nicaraguan Criollo 98 binder, and a spicy Nicaraguan Corojo 99 wrapper leaf. This Nicaraguan puro garnered so much positive feedback that it quickly earned several 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado and has been a staple for the brand ever since its 2015 release. Packaged neatly in classic cedar chests and wearing only a simple band bearing its name, Futuro, like many warped cigars, is for lack of a better term a “sleeper” cigar—one that looks basic and unembellished on the outside but when cut and lit up tells a very exciting story. The construction is impeccable, in true Casa Fernandez fashion, yielding an easy draw, sharp burn, and stable, thick ash that holds on long and tight. Immediately upon lighting, a blast of white pepper greets the palate, soon transitioning into a medley of oak, cinnamon, and sweet bakers’ spices. Creamy vanilla and hints of floral notes dance around in the background, along with a crisp toasty nuance every so often. A core of earthy tobacco holds the package together, and the finish is clean, spicy, and robust. Medium to full-bodied and delightfully balanced, Futuro is a true connoisseurs’ cigar. Made with the discriminating aficionado in mind, Warped Futuro is meant for a more mature and seasoned audience. A well-developed palate is a must if one is to appreciate all the immense flavor offered by the blend of AGANORSA’s most prized “Vault” tobacco featured here. Single malt scotch or port wine would make a fine accompaniment for this stick, and ample time to sit back, relax, and truly enjoy the luxurious flavor profile is a must. Fans of other premium Nicaraguan sticks such as Padron or Casa Fernandez should definitely check out this cigar, as its body and flavor profile certainly is comparable. When it was released, Warped Futuro was meant to be a “Homage to the Future.” Today, it is likely that after trying one yourself, you will make future plans of your own to keep coming back to it.

Oddly, the cigar starts off with a very pronounced mineral note, with a little bit of damp earth and pepper. The retrohale in the early stage has the cinnamon and clove in it that was detected in the pre-light, along with a fairly sharp red pepper. As the cigar burns along, the earth notes fade a little bit, and clove, along with walnut shell, become prominent. The mineral note present at first light still lingers vividly on the tongue. The draw is just about on the money, maybe just a slight bit on the loose side. This leads to a heavy smoke output, being quite easy to get a mouthful of the creamy smoke and enjoy the flavors at hand. Moving along, there is a definite change in profile as the cigar builds noticeably in body and strength. The vegetal note that was noticed in the pre-light appears. This enhances the strength of the red pepper and pushes the cinnamon and clove to the background, but not out of the picture. The aspect of the profile that surprises me, at this point, arrives on the finish—being a creamy-yet-bitter chai spice that sits all the way across the back of the tongue. This is further enhanced by hints of cocoa, adding a little sweetness to the experience. The burn and draw have been right on point, and it is obvious that care was taken in the construction of this cigar. Heading down the home stretch, we get yet another profile change, though a little more subtle than the first. Vegetal notes fade and the chai and cocoa move to the front. The mineral note on the retrohale fades to the background, with the cinnamon moving to the front. The cigar finishes in pretty much this same manner, with the pepper returning for a sharp burn in the last few puffs. The cigar smoked flawlessly from start to finish, with a solid burn line and minimal waviness.

Composed with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper surrounding a Nicaraguan binder and long-leaf Nicaraguan filler, the original release was produced in four sizes sporting spiffy names—the Atom (5 1/2” x 46), the Napalm (5” x 52), the Atomic (6” x 60), and the Nuclear (6” x 50). The vitolas were visually unique with a pigtail cap topped off with a long twist of tobacco, designed to resemble a fuse. With their uncommon names and appearance, the La Bomba cigars quickly gathered momentum through frequent posts on social media sites. In 2012, the 601 La Bomba Napalm was reviewed on Cigar Dojo , receiving a 87-point “POWERHOUSE” rating. Over the next few years, the company continued to introduce additional vitolas under the La Bomba banner. At the 2013 IPCPR Trade Show and Convention , Espinosa Cigars introduced the limited-edition 601 La Bomba Warhead. Instead of the Nicaraguan Habano wrapper used on the original La Bomba cigars, the Warhead was constructed with a Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. Additionally, the Warhead featured new artwork and creative packaging. In the original press release for the cigar, the company stated— “The packaging is inspired by several themes in the World War II era. When unraveled, the foot band on the cigar is revealed to be in the form of a bomb. This “bomb” features nose art or aircraft graffiti, which was common in this era. Most prominent is the shark-face which is a reference to the Flying Tigers, the 1st American Volunteer Group, who would paint the shark-faces on their military aircrafts.” Click images below for full resolution 601 La Bomba Warhead III Breakdown Wrapper: Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro Binder: Nicaraguan Filler: Nicaraguan Factory: La Zona (Nicaragua) Production: Limited Edition (1,000 boxes of 10 cigars) Vitola: 7½″ × 38 Lancero Price: $10.95 (MSRP) The Warhead III is the third 601 La Bomba cigar to carry the Warhead designation. The first Warhead was introduced four years ago—a 6 1/2″ x 54 ring gauge, soft-pressed cigar composed with a Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper, a Nicaraguan binder, and long-leaf Nicaraguan filler. The production was limited to two-thousand boxes containing ten cigars (twenty-thousand total cigars). In 2014, Espinosa Cigars released the Warhead II. One inch shorter and two points wider (5 1/2” x 56), the cigar shared the same general composition as the original, except for the fact that the blend was slightly tweaked to accommodate it’s new size. Once again, the production was limited to two-thousand boxes containing ten cigars. SEE ALSO: 601 La Bomba Warhead cigar review 601 La Bomba Warhead II cigar review Last year, the company introduced the Warhead III—a soft-pressed lancero with the initial production limited to five-thousand cigars (eventually becoming ten-thousand cigars total). The cigars are arranged horizontally in ten-count dress boxes with a hinged lid. Additionally, the blend was modified a bit from the previous Warhead releases to fit with the thin lancero format. Appearance Click images below for full resolution The 601 La Bomba Warhead III is a unique looking lancero-sized cigar, with a short torpedo cap which bears resemblance to a diminutive Hershey Kiss. Unlike the original La Bomba releases, it lacks the long tobacco twist at the top of the cap. The cigar’s Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper is a bit battered—with two raised seams, one long keloid scar vein, and sandpaper tooth in several areas. Softly pressed, the color of the lancero is a mixture of dark chocolate and chestnut, with contrasting splotches of Phthalo green appearing in several areas across the face. A medium amount of oiliness produces a burnished sheen in the late-afternoon sunlight. The Warhead III is encased with a rectangular foot band printed in the colors of black, green, red, and white. Lightly embossed, the “601 La Bomba” logo resides in the center with “Warhead III” printed underneath a black laurel leaf. Fairly firmly packed from the foot to the cap—with two discernible soft spots in the middle of the cigar—the wrapper aroma is a faint assortment of damp soil, leather, and pepper, while the open foot smells of barnyard and a touch of cedar. After the cap of the lancero is opened with a double guillotine cut—to ensure the maximum amount of taste from the wrapper, binder, and filler—the initial cold draw is just a bit resistive. Flavors of dried fruit, grass, light chocolate, and natural tobacco immediately touch the palate, while a touch of spiciness formulates on the upper lip. Smoking Experience After toasting and lighting the cigar with a soft double-flame lighter in the traditional manner (see: The Cigar Enthusiast’s Guide to Soft Flame Lighting ), the first few draws deliver a cornucopia of flavors—earth, light espresso, powdered cocoa, Napa leather, and spices. These initial notes are quickly enhanced with a bit of sweetness from the burning of the Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. The draw of the Warhead III is nearly perfect—which is not the case with many lancero cigars—generating an unexpected amount of smoke output from both the cap and the foot. Additional aromas and flavors of anise and Canadian maple syrup mingle with the primary notes to produce a creamy and smooth smoking experience, while assorted spices, a touch of chocolate, and white pepper are dominant on the retrohale. As with most fairly complex cigars, focused concentration and retrohaling is an essential part of the smoking experience (see: How to Retrohale a Cigar ). As the lancero enters into its second third, it begins to display the following general characteristics—full in body, medium-to-full in flavor, and nearly full in strength. The aromas and flavors present in the first third of the cigar continue to build, while the initial light espresso note shifts toward an a ristretto shot pulled onto a small brown sugar cube residing at the bottom of a cup. Subtle flavors and aromas of cedar, dark chocolate, dried mango, salte

The flavor profile on this cigar was of berries , nuts , and a distinct anise flavor and to be honest those are not my favorite flavor combinations. note_sources.text: Gran Habano Corojo #5 cigars are the fullest of the Gran Habano “core” blends and are a great choice for any fan of full-bodied cigars . They are handmade in Honduras under the supervision of front man George Rico using Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler tobaccos and Nicaraguan Habano binders. They are finished off with a spicy Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper leaf for a heavy, rich smoke. The wrapper leaf is very oily and shiny and has a reddish tint. The smoke is thick and white and full of heavy spice and rich, earthy flavor . There are notes of cinnamon and grass and a long, sweet, floral finish . Definitely full-bodied. The Gran Habano Corojo #5 Series has earned multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado , praised for its rich, balanced flavors and exceptional craftsmanship. Gran Habano #5 Corojo is a great choice for anyone looking for a strong, rich premium cigar that isn't too pricey. They are great for any time of day, but really hit the spot after a heavy meal. Red wine and bourbon pair well with the #5 Corojo, and they can be compared flavor-wise to Flor De Oliva Corojo and Romeo y Julieta Habana Reserve. Keep in mind these are fairly heavy cigars and intended for a more experienced audience. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars )

After an unusually long toasting/lighting process, the cigar kicks off with a very Dominican feel, having equal parts sweetness and zest through the retrohale, as well as a peculiar note that I’d sum up as grandma’s coat closet (dust/wood/perfume/musk/Carmex?). There’s a balanced sweetness to the smoke, hitting the tip of the tongue, followed by the back sides and front sides. This sweetness lingers, and can even be felt on the lips, though nothing in the realm of artificial (i.e. sweetened cap territory). Cola syrup is a unique and welcomed ingredient, being joined by raisin sweetness and sesame honey cashews (à la Trader Joe’s). The cigar seems to require some babysitting in the first inch, with a canoeing burn warranting touchups and having a difficult time settling down. The draw is on the firm side (though nothing too concerning), giving off medium amounts of smoke on each puff. The wonky burn is accompanied by a flakey, medium-gray ash, which clings on for about an inch at a time. The firm pre-light feel translates into a very slow burn rate, giving an

note_sources.text: Crafted from an extraordinary 2012 tobacco harvest, the Montecristo Epic Vintage 12 Blue stands as one of the most refined and luxurious cigars ever to carry the legendary Montecristo name . Only the finest seeds were cultivated in select, nutrient-rich soils during that exceptional growing year resulting in tobacco so remarkable that Montecristo chose to showcase it in this limited, vintage driven masterpiece. Handmade at the world renowned Tabacalera de García in the Dominican Republic, this cigar is the product of unmatched expertise, meticulous craftsmanship, and generations of perfected technique. Every leaf, every stage, every detail is handled with an unwavering dedication to excellence. The blend is nothing short of epic: a dark and elegant Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, Dominican and Nicaraguan binders, and a rich, harmonious core of Dominican long fillers, all nurtured from the prized 2012 crop. Once lit, the Montecristo Epic Vintage 12 Blue unveils a silky, medium-to-full-bodied profile layered with depth and sophistication. Expect a cascade of cocoa, cinnamon, sweet spice, leather, nuts, and oak , delivered with smoothness and balance that only truly well-aged tobacco can achieve. The finish is long, refined, and deeply satisfying, making it an ideal cigar for slow, indulgent moments or as a flawless companion after a hearty meal.

The first light opens with a clean, straightforward profile. Toasted hickory balanced by lightly creamy dark-roast coffee leads the way, supported by a dry earthiness and a restrained black pepper that sits more on the lips than the tongue. The flavor and body are mild/medium at best, and the strength is mild. The finish is clean and moderately long, leaving behind a lingering wood and light spice note. The smoke output is impressive and, even with the snug draw, I am having no trouble getting copious smoke output with each puff. As the cigar settles in, additional layers begin to emerge. The hickory note deepens and takes on a slightly charred edge, while a subtle ground-cinnamon note begins to round out the coffee profile, balancing the pepper and keeping the cigar from feeling sharp or aggressive. Retrohales bring a bit more white pepper into the mix, but it remains controlled and modest. The burn line is wavy, which isn’t surprising from a “Cuban sandwich” roll, though it’s not in need of a touchup at this time. The ash is very firm, holding tight to the cigar. Flavor is medium, body is mild/medium, and strength is mild/medium. Approaching the midpoint, the cigar is feeling like it’s missed its stride. The profile has barely moved—what has changed is not necessarily for the better. The hickory wood is turning into an over-charred and slightly acrid note. It’s reminiscent of the smell that your backyard fire pit gives off the morning after a rainstorm. The creamy coffee note has gotten sharp, giving more of a “latte that woke up and chose violence” vibe. The espresso portion is overdrawn, and the cream is unable to cut it. On a positive note, the burn is slow, and the first ash finally drops into my tray. In the final stretch, the Series P Honduras stays true to itself. The char and coffee notes dominate the profile but aren’t becoming any harsher. Strength creeps up slightly yet remains comfortably below medium. The cream has completely faded, and gone is the ground cinnamon note.

note_sources.text: Altadis U.S.A. is introducing Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto, the third release in the award-winning Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua family. This new release from Rafael Nodal, in collaboration with his friend and cigar master AJ Fernandez, continues to push the boundaries of excellence in the premium cigar industry. Nodal, creator and co-owner of Aging Room Cigars and Vice President of Product Capability at Tabacalera USA, explains the inspiration behind the cigar: “The Concerto, inspired by classical music compositions, represents a harmonious collaboration between a solo instrument and orchestral accompaniment. In this blend, the ‘solo instrument’ is the exclusive hybrid wrapper from one of AJ Fernandez’s most exclusive farms, Finca La Lilia, and the selected extra-aged tobaccos represent the accompaniment to create a Concerto of flavors.” The Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto also includes leaves from the first harvest of AJ Fernandez’s Finca Los Espejos almost 12 years ago. The Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto is a testament to the enduring partnership between Nodal and Fernandez, who together have previously produced two #1 cigars: the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua in 2019 by Cigar Aficionado, and the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata in 2023 by Cigar Snob. This new addition is poised to define the future of the Aging Room and the Quattro Nicaragua line. This medium-to-full-bodied cigar is soft box-pressed with a caramel color wrapper. Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto is available in six sizes and boxes of 20 cigars, except in the case of the Impromptu, which is available in boxes of 10, and the Maestro, which is available in boxes of 10 and 20. The MSRP ranges from $14.84 to $17.08. Wrapper: Nicaragua Binder: Nicaragua Filler: Nicaragua Strength: Medium-to-full Origin: Nicaragua Sizes and Pricing:

Experience the pinnacle of cigar artistry with the Concerto—a striking masterpiece born at the renowned AJ Fernandez factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. Crafted by Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Experience the pinnacle of cigar artistry with the Concerto—a striking masterpiece born at the renowned AJ Fernandez factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. Crafted by master blender Rafael Nodal, this extraordinary creation harmonizes nearly 12 years of meticulous aging with a legacy of bold creativity and refined elegance. The Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua line has always represented a symphony of flavors that comes to life with every puff. With the introduction of the Concerto, cigar lovers are invited to experience the crescendo of this award-winning line—a blend that harmoniously balances boldness with elegance. Crafted at the renowned AJ Fernandez factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, the Concerto showcases the artistry of master blender Rafael Nodal, whose passion for music inspired the very rhythm and harmony of this cigar. Every leaf used in the Concerto blend, which features a full Nicaraguan puro, has been carefully hand-selected and aged to perfection for nearly 12 years, capturing the essence of the Los Espejos Farm’s rich, volcanic soils.

Unless you’ve been living under a rock for the past decade or so, you probably know where the Aging Room brand stands as a whole, and more specifically the Quattro Nicaragua series . Not only have they been the brand’s best-selling lineup, but the original Quattro Nicaragua earned the coveted Cigar of the Year award back in 2019. Sounds hard to improve upon, huh? Well, when brand owner Rafael Nodal and industry icon AJ Fernandez get together, somehow something incredible happens every time. After all, it happened the first time around, right? Now, years after the original Quattro Nicaragua that shook the cigar world, the third and arguably best installment in the series is here: Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto. Blended by and crafted under the strict supervision of AJ Fernandez himself in his own world-renowned Nicaraguan factory, this top-shelf creation is a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning every single leaf used in the blend is grown in Nicaraguan soil. We aren’t just talking about any leaves, either, the tobacco used for this one comes from AJ Fernandez’s personal farms, and his most prized farms of all, as far as that goes. The Nicaraguan filler and binder blend is from the first harvest of the exclusive Los Espejos farm, while the gorgeous Criollo 98 hybrid wrapper leaf is grown on AJ’s lush Finca La Lilia farm in the fertile growing region of Esteli. We could talk for days about the accolades this cigar has received, but for now we will let the numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado do the talking, including an incredible 95, along with a spot on the magazine’s Top 25 of 2025 . Beautiful blue boxes house the expertly crafted cigars, each one wearing double bands, one black and one blue to signify the blend. Built to exacting standards set forth by AJ Fernandez, this box-pressed package offers immense clouds of thick, silky smoke on every puff, with an easy draw and a straight burn. Initial flavors include cedar, black pepper, and spice . Soon enough, this opening turns rich, as hearty Nicaraguan tobacco forms the nucleus of the flavor profile, and notes of nutmeg, cinnamon, and black cherry begin to surface. A crispy finish of white pepper ties everything together, and all-in-all, this incredible gem of a cigar finishes on the very heavy side of medium-full-bodied . Made for the experienced, Quattro Nicaragua Concerto is a masterfully blended example of what an ultra-premium cigar should be. Depth, balance, complexity—it’s all right here, in one place at one time. Medium-full-bodied, this prize pairs beautifully with the finest scotch or bourbon, but also goes well with a hot cup of black coffee. Fans of the celebrated original Quattro Nicaragua blend will surely want to check this one out and see for yourself which one you think is better. When the Aging Room lineup started years ago, nobody could have ever imagined it would end up as big as it is today. Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Concerto is certainly becoming one of the premier cigars in the series, and it indubitably deserves a spot in the humidor of any truly discerning cigar connoisseur.

The latest in an award-winning line – the Aging Room Quattro Sonata – will be available in June 1. From his early classical music studies, Rafael Nodal, Head of Product Capability for Tabacalera USA, has always been fascinated by famous sonatas. “Beethoven’s Moonlight and other sonatas from Mozart, Schubert, Chopin and Rachmaninoff are among my favorites,” he says. This love of music is one of the reasons why, after many accolades and high ratings for his Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Maestro, Nodal wanted to compose a Nicaragua Sonata to celebrate the Nicaraguan people and their land. “Not with notes or to be played on the piano, but with tobacco leaves to be enjoyed by adult consumers looking for something unique,” he says. “The Aging Room Nicaragua Sonata is composed with leaves grown in the valleys and mountains of Nicaragua and nurtured by the dedicated people of Nicaragua.” As in previous collaborations, for the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata, Nodal has teamed up with his long-time friend and cigar master, A.J. Fernandez. Together they have created one of their richest and most unique cigar blends to pay homage to the fertile and hospitable country of Nicaragua, a land known for its memorable lakes and volcanos. Made at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez and box pressed with all Nicaraguan tobaccos, the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata will be available to purchase at retail June 1. Sonata will be available in boxes of 20 (except for Impromptu, which comes in a box of 10), in a variety of vitolas and MSRPs, noted below for each individual cigar. Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata: Espressivo 50 x 5 MSRP $13.02 each cigar Maestro 52 x 6 MSRP $13.13 Vibrato 54 x 6 MSRP $13.24 Concerto 50 x 7 MSRP $13.37 Impromptu 52 x 6.5 MRSP $14.98 each cigar (Figurado Box of 10) Grande 60 x 6 MSRP $13.55

Discover Every Single Note Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Produced in collaboration with Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez, the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua is a premium cigar of the finest pedigree. This perfectly rolled Nicaraguan puro provides the cigar connoisseur with rich and rewarding flavors of white pepper, nuts, spice, earth, and espresso, accented by a rich tobacco sweetness throughout. The Maestro was named Cigar Aficionado’s No. 1 Cigar of the Year of 2019 with a 96 rating.

When the original Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua earned Cigar Aficionado's coveted 2019 Cigar of the Yea r honors, Rafael Nodal and A.J. Fernandez set a new standard for what a Nicaraguan puro could achieve. Rather than resting on that success, the duo returned to the drawing board with a new vision—one inspired not by repetition, but by refinement. The result is the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata , a cigar designed to showcase the complexity, balance, and harmony that made its predecessor famous while introducing an entirely new expression of Nicaraguan tobacco . The Sonata has added to the brand's legacy by securing multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado , reinforcing its status as a highly successful follow-up blend. Handcrafted at the renowned AJ Fernandez factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, the Sonata is a true Nicaraguan puro , utilizing tobacco grown exclusively on Fernandez's farms. While it shares the same all-Nicaraguan foundation as the original Quattro Nicaragua, the blend takes a different approach. With longer fermentation periods, carefully selected seed varietals, and extensively aged tobacco, the Sonata delivers a profile that is slightly more refined and nuanced without sacrificing flavor or character. Like the musical compositions that inspired its name, the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata unfolds in distinct movements while maintaining a cohesive theme throughout the smoking experience. The first draws introduce notes of roasted nuts, oak, and espresso , supported by a rich core of natural tobacco sweetness. As the cigar develops, layers of leather, nutmeg, and peppery spice emerge, adding depth and complexity without overwhelming the palate. Hints of chocolate and earth linger beneath the surface, creating a balanced and sophisticated profile that rewards slow, attentive smoking. Construction is everything cigar enthusiasts have come to expect from the Nodal-Fernandez partnership. The draw is effortless, the burn razor-sharp, and the smoke production abundant from beginning to end. Medium-to-full-bodied and beautifully composed, the Sonata offers an elegant smoking experience that showcases the remarkable versatility of Nicaraguan tobacco. For fans of the original Quattro Nicaragua, the Sonata provides a fascinating new chapter in the Aging Room story. For everyone else, it serves as a masterclass in blending from two of the industry's most respected names. Complex, refined, and deeply satisfying, the Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua Sonata proves that some encores are every bit as memorable as the original performance.

Alec Bradley Filthy Hooligan and Filthy Hooligan Shamrock are shipping now, marking the twelfth and sixth release of the annual, limited edition take on the brand’s popular Black Market blend, respectively. For 2024, 5,000 boxes of each blend will be released. Bradley Rubin, brand ambassador for Alec Bradley cigars said, “Anticipation continues to build each year for the release of Filthy Hooligan and Filthy Hooligan Shamrock. With their bright green wrappers and fresh herbal notes, these candela smokes offer a great change of pace at a time when spring’s on everyone’s mind. The blends have become part of the cigar community’s annual ritual and we’re pleased that we have once again been able to source the perfect aged candela wrapper to make this year’s release a reality.” Filthy Hooligan and Filthy Hooligan Shamrock are based on the popular Alec Bradley Black Market blend which has been tweaked to complement the multiple wrapper format. Filthy Hooligan features a Honduran Candela and Nicaraguan Habano Oscuro barber pole wrapper, while Filthy Hooligan Shamrock is triple-wrapped with the same Honduran Candela and Nicaraguan Habano Oscuro wrapper as Filthy Hooligan, with the addition of a claro shade Nicaraguan Habano leaf. Both blends feature an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder, with Honduran and Panamanian filler. Handcrafted at Tobacos de Oriente in Danli, Honduras, both blends are available exclusively in 6” x 50 toro formats. Filthy Hooligan is presented in a handsome green and black striped box containing 24 cigars, which will sell for an MSRP of $12.69 per cigar. Filthy Hooligan Shamrock comes in an attractive, 10-count gray box with a large shamrock on the lid. The cigars will sell for $15.09 apiece. The release of Filthy Hooligan and Filthy Hooligan Shamrock paves the way for the upcoming release of Uru Dushi, a blend developed in partnership between Alec Bradley and Cigar Dojo to commemorate Leap Year. Originally released on Feb. 29, 2020, the 2024 Uru Doshi blend features unique Honduran and Nicaraguan leaves that comprise the cigar’s filler and double-binder recipe. Uru Doshi 2024 employs subtle tweaks to the tobacco primings, making for a slightly amped-up take on the 2020 edition. Additionally, the Jamastran wrapper of the original cigar has been swapped with a Honduran Criollo ’98, selected from Honduras’ Trojes region. Uru Doshi (2024) was crafted at Raíces Cubanas. A total of 3,000 cigars will be released in a 6″ x 52 toro format and sold exclusively through online retailer Smoke Inn Cigars for an SRP of $9.00 per cigar. Tying into the leap-year theme, Uru Doshi 2024 will launch on Thursday, Feb. 29th, 2024 (also known as Leap Day).

Alec Bradley Cigar Co. will begin shipping the Limited Edition, Collector’s Series Trilogy to tobacconists next week. Trilogy Authentic Corojo, Exotic Maduro and Native Cameroon are being released in their own “cigar-press” shaped boxes, paying homage to the triangular mold created by Alec Bradley brand owner, Alan Rubin in the early 2000s. Only two thousand collectable 10-count boxes of each of the tree cigar blends are being presented in the triangle pressed, 6 x 52 Toro format. “Trilogy has been a passion project for me since I started with Alec Bradley in 2017,” said second generation cigar maker, Bradley Rubin. “I’m honored that my dad, Alan, finally allowed me to move forward with the project; and now we have the opportunity to share a part of Alec Bradley’s history with our brand advocates, old and new.” Introduced in 2002, Alec Bradley Trilogy was the first triangular shaped cigar to hit the premium cigar market. Although Alec Bradley Trilogy may still be found on some tobacconists’ shelves, sales for the line took a decade’s long hiatus. In August of this year, the company collaborated with a Florida tobacconists to resurrect the line in a sampler featuring 6 Robusto shaped cigars of each blend. All three Trilogy cigars have been blended to mirror their original flavor profiles. The iterations share the same Honduran Connecticut seed binder and fillers from Nicaragua and Honduras. Exotic Maduro features a Maduro wrapper from Jalapa, Nicaragua; Authentic Corojo features a Corojo wrapper from Jamastran, Honduras; and Native Cameroon features a true Cameroon wrapper from the central African nation of the same name. MSRP has been set to USD15.00 per cigar/ USD 150.00 per box, before any applicable taxes. Trilogy will begin shipping next week to appointed tobacconists. Alec Bradley Trilogy cigars are being produced at Tobacos De Oriente, Danlí, Honduras.

The new Asylum 13 Megalophobia is a 134 x 13. These giants are packed in boxes of two cigars and only 400 cigars were made. The MSRP for each cigar is $ 125.00. An interesting side note: Look at the weight of this cigar in grams and then ounces!

Heads up: This isn’t your average smoke. The Megalophobia is a 13-inch long, 134-ring-gauge monster built more of a collector’s novelty, not an everyday smoke. It’s big, bold, over-the-top, and guaranteed to turn heads, so make sure you know what you’re signing up for before you light it! “Enough is Enough.” That’s the bold declaration stamped across the lid of the box, and it says it all. From the fearless minds at C.L.E. Cigar Co ., the Asylum 13 Megalophobia isn’t just a cigar, it’s a jaw-dropping spectacle of cigar-making excess. Measuring a mind-bending 13 inches long with a 134-ring gauge (yes, that’s more than two inches thick), this Honduran-made beast redefines “big cigar.” Created as a tongue-in-cheek response to the ever-growing competition of massive smokes, Megalophobia is Tom Lazuka’s playful way of saying the giant cigar craze has officially peaked. Under the hood, this monstrous smoke carries a refined, medium-to-full-bodied blend . A silky Ecuadorian wrapper, Honduran binder, and a flavorful mix of Colombian and Honduran fillers. Despite its intimidating size, the flavor profile remains balanced, smooth, and impressively well-constructed, proof that Asylum not just knows how to blend humor with craftsmanship, but Megalophobia is a reminder that Asylum is still king of the giants. Each box comes with two colossal cigars and a special custom quad flame lighter powerful enough to set this titan ablaze. Production is said to be limited to 250 boxes worldwide , making this one of the rarest, most collectible novelties ever rolled , so grab yours before they’re gone. Whether you light it up or just show it off, the Asylum 13 Megalophobia is a reminder that in the world of cigars, sometimes, enough really is enough.

Cigar Company announces the unveiling of the Asylum April Fools’ 2024 “Year of the Dragon” at the PCA in Las Vegas. The Asylum April Fools’ 2024 Year of the Dragon is the fourth in a series of cigars that are released yearly on April Fools’ Day (April 1 st ). Last year’s version celebrated the Chinese Zodiac. Asylum cigars will continue this trend showcasing this year’s version. In true Asylum style, the blend will come in a massive 90X9 vitola. Blended by Christian Eiroa this Honduran puro is a full-bodied blend featuring bold flavors throughout the smoking experience. The blend will come in updated packaging, as cigars will be housed in tubes, and set in a six-cigar tray. The black box is adorned with blood red print. The image of the Dragon is prominently displayed on the packaging. The MSRP for the Asylum April Fools’ 2024 Year of the Dragon is $42.36 per cigar and $251.16 per tray of six. Tom Lazuka, co-founder of Asylum Cigars said:” The Asylum cigar brand is meant to be fun and experimental. The April Fools blend is not for the faint of heart. It is truly a powerhouse of a cigar with very bold flavors. We look forward to presenting the April Fools 2024 at the PCA in Las Vegas.”

Once a year, Asylum Cigars throw subtlety out the window and dare cigar smokers to do the same. The Asylum April Fools line is an annual, limited-style release that celebrates April Fools’ Day and the Chinese Lunar New Year, delivering some of the largest, boldest cigars ever made, both in size and personality. First introduced in 2021, the April Fools series has become a highly anticipated tradition among collectors and seasoned smokers alike. Each yearly release features the same jaw-dropping 90x9 format, an astonishing 9 inches long with a massive 90 ring gauge , paired with a rotating Lunar New Year theme. Past and current releases honor the corresponding zodiac animal, such as the 2023 Year of the Rabbit and the 2025 Year of the Snake, with unique artwork, bands, and packaging that make each edition instantly recognizable and highly collectible. Despite their novelty-level proportions, these cigars are anything but gimmicks. Every Asylum April Fools cigar is handcrafted at C.L.E. 's factory in Honduras and blended as a Honduran puro, using wrapper, binder, and long-filler tobaccos grown on the family’s own farms. Construction is taken seriously, delivering a surprisingly smooth draw, massive smoke output, and a steady burn, no small feat for a cigar of this scale. These cigars are marathon smokes, often burning for hours and demanding both time and commitment. Equal parts conversation piece, collector’s item, and smoking challenge, the Asylum April Fools line is perfect for gifting, collecting, or conquering, if you’re bold enough. As new years and zodiac themes are released, the legacy continues to grow.

The Bolivar portfolio will soon expand to include a three-cigar collection called Bolivar Cofradia Oscuro. The new medium-plus blend now shipping to retailers. Joe Krzyston, assistant brand manager for Bolivar said, “Bolivar Cofradia Oscuro brings a new dimension to Bolivar by introducing a US-grown Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper to the portfolio. The blend is rich and rewarding and it’s priced in line with the existing Bolivar offerings, making it among the best values in any humidor. This new line is yet another reason for cigar smokers to explore this legendary brand, and we expect that the blend will be very well received.” Bolivar Cofradia Oscuro is a complex, five-country blend. It is made with an aged Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. Handcrafted at Hatsa in Honduras and presented in old-world-style wooden packaging, Bolivar Cofradia Oscuro is distributed by Forged Cigar Company. Each of the three Bolivar Cofradia Oscuro frontmarks comes in 25-count boxes. Bolivar is marching forward with Gran Republica, a new, three-cigar collection named in honor of the great South American liberator Simon Bolivar. In a nod to the pivotal role Bolivar played in shaping South America, the four-country blend features tobacco grown on land liberated by Bolivar himself. The medium-to-full-bodied cigar represents the finest tobacco from the continent’s most respected growing regions. Crafted with a blend of filler tobaccos from Colombia, Brazil and Nicaragua, and featuring a Brazilian Arapiraca binder and Ecuadorian wrapper. Steve Abbot, director of marketing for Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG) said, “With Bolivar Gran Republica, we are continuing to build the legacy of this important brand. This is a bold blend for the initiated smoker, one that not only deepens the range of offerings from Bolivar but that also highlights the best of South American tobacco. We’re confident that Gran Republica will be a strong addition to the growing Bolivar portfolio.” Handcrafted at HATSA in Honduras and presented in old-world-style wooden boxes, Bolivar Gran Republica will ship to retailers on June 1. The brand is distributed by Forged Cigar Company. Bolivar Gran Republica comes in 20-count boxes. Bolivar Gran Republica Robusto (4.5” x 50); SRP per cigar $7.99 Bolivar Gran Republica Toro (6” x 54); SRP per cigar $8.29 Bolivar Gran Republica Gigante (6” x 60); SRP per cigar $8.49

This October Oliva Cigar Company will release the Cain Daytona Limitada 7 x 70. This version was developed particularly to appeal to race car enthusiasts. One cigar even has a miniature rubber tire cigar ring above the standard Cain Daytona ring and is presented in a rally-inspired orange wooden box. Each box contains 10 cigars. Cain Daytona is blended with the Jalapa Ligero . Together with Cain’s triple fermentation process, the result is a medium to full-bodied, smooth, rich, and flavorful smoke. This 7 x 70 Limitada is a much larger cigar than any of the others in the Cain portfolio. The Cain Daytona Limitada will be displayed for the first at the InterTabac Fair in Dortmund, Germany this coming September 21st–23rd.

The Cain Daytona is one of the latest offerings from Studio Tobac. While it is still a mostly ligero cigar, this Daytona is not nearly as powerful as its brothers, the Cain Maduro and the Cain F. One reviewer noted that it should have been named "Abel". The Cain Daytona 550 blend is a distinct entry in the Oliva Cigar Company’s portfolio, designed to offer the complexity of the "Straight Ligero" concept with a more approachable medium-bodied strength. Handcrafted at the Tabacalera Oliva factory in Nicaragua, this 5 x 50 robusto is a Nicaraguan puro featuring a smooth, golden-brown Nicaraguan Habano wrapper leaf. The blend is unique for its exclusive use of ligero tobaccos from the Jalapa Valley , a region celebrated for producing leaves that are rich in flavor and natural sweetness but lower in nicotine intensity than those from Estelí. This technical choice results in a balanced profile that opens with white pepper and earth , transitioning into refined layers of coffee , sweet cream that reminds me of a Werther's Orginal , and cinnamon . It earned a 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado , which highlighted its flawless construction and "woodsy undertones" complemented by hints of apple cider and dried fruit . All in all, the Cain Daytona is an excellent addition to the Cain line and in many ways shows that the Cain isn't all about strength; it can be about flavor too.
Pepper , Sweetness , Coffee , Sweet Tobacco Available. Learn about Cain by Oliva Daytona Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Daytona

Camacho Cigars is excited to announce a new line to its portfolio: Camacho Broadleaf. The distinctive feature of Camacho’s newest cigar line is its oversized Honduran Broadleaf wrapper packed with giant flavor and crafted with precision and passion. In the brand’s quest for excellence, no corners were cut: Decades of expertise and Honduran craftsmanship converged to produce the new addition to the offering. “I am thrilled with the amazing work our Master Blenders in Honduras have done. They created a cigar line which is not only excellent in taste, but also bold and fearless in attitude – exactly what our aficionados are searching for”, says Edward Simon, CMO at Oettinger Davidoff. “The darker Broadleaf wrapper in particular adds a lot of excitement to the cigar experience, as it endows every format with an oily, almost silky appearance and a creamy note to the taste profile.” The cigar with the dark and oily Broadleaf wrapper features a diverse blend of tobaccos from Honduras and the Dominican Republic. Camacho Broadleaf will be available in 20-count boxes of Robusto, Toro and Gordo and come with eye- catching bands which highlight a fearless and daring Honduran spirit. Launch & availability The new Camacho Broadleaf line will be available* as of 21 July 2023 for the US market. The launch for Germany and Switzerland is on 15 September 2023.

Camacho Broadleaf cigars are a commanding addition to the distinguished Camacho lineup, meticulously crafted to deliver a bold and satisfying smoking experience. Each vitola showcases the same expertly blended tobaccos, crowned with a rich Honduran Broadleaf wrapper—a testament to decades of Honduran craftsmanship and expertise. While the dark, oily wrapper may suggest a singular intensity, the complexity within this cigar exceeds all expectations. A masterful fusion of Honduran and Dominican tobaccos, perfectly balanced by the leathery Broadleaf, takes cigar complexity into uncharted territory. The Camacho Broadleaf offers a medium-intensity journey, revealing deep layers of leather, a peppery kick, and subtle hints of sweetness that linger on the palate. This bold and captivating smoke features rich notes of dark chocolate and espresso, elevated by a creamy sweetness that enhances the robust flavor profile. As you indulge, aromas of leather and oak emerge, guiding you through an evolving and immersive experience. Perfectly paired with smoked meats, Camacho Broadleaf finds its ideal companion in the rich, savory flavors of slow-cooked barbecue—a mouthwatering harmony of smoky indulgence. And if that sounds like your kind of vibe, pour yourself a stiff Scotch, kick back, eat well, and enjoy the ride.

Camacho, the brand of bold cigars, announces the nationwide return of Camacho Coyolar. Born from the volcanic soils of a small 15-acre farm found at the base of the mountains joining Nicaragua and Honduras, this spicy and flavorful smoke is built from “Single Farm Vintage” Criollo tobaccos. The land’s distinctive and mineral-rich soil provides the tobacco its unique color, texture, and intense flavor. Camacho Coyolar is offered in its five original formats ranging from the 4 1/2 x 50 Perfecto #1 to the 6 x 60 Titan, each one delivering an intense and full flavored experience. While the blend and formats remain the same, Coyolar makes its return with a bold new look, outfitted with revamped black bands and packaged in 25-count grey and black lacquered boxes featuring an abstract design of the mountain ranges in Honduras and Nicaragua. “After several years of requests, there was no better time than now to bring back the original Coyolar. We stepped outside our traditional Honduran farms to revisit the special 15-acre plot of land where Coyolar was first born. The exclusive Criollo tobaccos harvested from this area give Coyolar’s ‘Single Farm Vintage’ blend its legendary intensity and bold character.” states Scott Kolesaire, Director of Marketing at Davidoff of Geneva USA. “We are thrilled to add this powerhouse to the current Camacho lineup. Get ready to experience boldness without boundaries!” The Camacho Coyolar will begin shipping this week in the United States only. Wrapper: Honduras (Single Farm Vintage) Binder: Honduras (Single Farm Vintage) Filler: Honduras (Single Farm Vintage) The Camacho Coyolar Line-up Perfecto #1, 4 1/4 x 50, SRP per cigar $8.50 Rothschild, 4 1/2 x 50, SRP per cigar $8.50 Super Toro, 6 x 52, SRP per cigar $9.00 Titan 25, 6 x 60, SRP per cigar $10.00 Figurado, 6 1/8 x 54, SRP per cigar $9.50

The myth, the legend, the Camacho Coyolar cigar. Last seen 'round these parts circa 2013, it has returned in our time of greatest need, assuming that need is for a smoke built for massive amounts of flavor and body while still remaining approachable to most aficionados. As part of the early lineup that first put Camacho on the map, the Coyolar quietly faded into the background as newer, flashier sticks were released to further cement the brand's legacy as a purveyor of some of the most deliciously potent sticks on the planet. Now, with filler, binder, and wrapper handmade into splendid vitolas using the original recipe of Criollo tobaccos still grown on the same small 15-acre plot in Honduras, this cigar has returned to claim its spot on the roster as a first-stringer. For the old school smokers out there, even if disregarding the red triangle embossed foot band there's no mistaking the frontmark's modern and oversized black and gray 'Camacho' band for the diminutive original, but the scents wafting from the Coyolar's barrel will bring you right back home. Redolent of alfalfa and exotic spices, the bright fragrance is more reminiscent of a sweet, fresh-rolled stogie than a well-aged cigar. As soon as the foot is ablaze, however, the Camacho Coyolar proves to be no flash in the pan. At once peppery and bold, there's an undercurrent of smooth leather and buttery biscuit to soften the blow. A syrupy mocha on the tongue adds cream to the cinnamon and nutmeg found in the retrohale, while the smoke's floral aroma adds a nice counterpoint to the later stage earthy peat, molasses, orange peel, and walnut that make themselves known. Camacho is well regarded for their skills when it comes to fiery Corojo tobacco, but the Camacho Coyolar shows they also know their way around the less familiar yet equally rewarding Criollo. A delectable medium-full in strength that should appeal to the masses, this cigar is still able to deliver enough complexity to challenge the most jaded of palates. Feel free to try out some other sticks that feature Criollo longleaf such as the Curivari Reserva Limitada or La Galera Maduro to see if they measure up.

CAO is about to put the pedal to the metal with a souped-up follow-up to the V-19 blend. Called CAO Flathead V21, this new release was created by Rick Rodriguez and the CAO blending team in Nicaragua. Rick and the team selected a Mexican San Andres wrapper for the blend which also includes a Connecticut Broadleaf binder, and a bold selection of Nicaraguan and Dominican ligero tobaccos. They then gave each of the filler leaves an abbreviated fermentation to lock in the tobacco’s native characteristics and added a secondary aging process to the filler to bring everything together. The result is a cigar with a medium to medium-full profile brimming with distinctive molasses and leather notes, this time with even more depth and complexity. “For Flathead V21, we wanted to give our fans a cigar that’s bold and complex, and still perfect for any smoking occasion,” said Rick Rodriguez. “We see this as the ultimate cigar for the CAO smoker who wants to experience the complexity of each tobacco with every draw. I’ve personally enjoyed V21 on its own and with a drink and have experienced different notes every time I smoke it. To me, that means we’ve done our job.” Crafted at STG Estelí in Nicaragua, CAO Flathead V21 will be released in two sizes, and production is limited to just 2,000 boxes per size. The blend will only be available for a limited time and begins shipping to retailers on August 3. The boxes that house CAO Flathead V21 are racecar red, with a bold black sash that culminates in the brand’s logo on the front of the box. Each box contains 27 cigars. Carb V21 (6 x 60) – SRP per cigar USD 13.99 Big Block V21 (7 x 70) – SRP per cigar USD 14.99
Fruit , Leather , Rich , Sweet Drink. Inspired by hot rods and pin-up girls, CAO Flathead is a box pressed collection that hits on all cylinders

CAO Flathead is the newest cigar from CAO, made in Nicaragua at the Scandinavian Tobacco factory in Esteli. Inspired by grease monkeys and rock 'n roll, Flathead is box-pressed, flat-headed, and funky. All sizes are named after car parts, and the box has a removable top that can be used as wall décor. This hot new stick has Nicaraguan ligero and Dominican fillers, a Habano Connecticut binder, and a dark, well-marbled Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. Buckle up, because this hot rod gives one heck of a ride. The CAO Flathead line, earned an impressive 95 rating , with the V660 Carb securing the #3 spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 Cigars of 2015 list . (Shop other CAO Cigars ) CAO Flathead starts its ignition with a strong, thick river of sweet, chocolatey flavor. The overall base is earthy, with just a few hints of pepper and coffee sprinkled about. As it evolves, a rich sweetness begins to dominate the flavor profile, giving bursts of floral and cocoa notes. Flathead is maduro and ligero at its best, with a wonderful mix of sweet, spicy, and strong. CAO Flathead is not your typical maduro. It's complex, full-bodied , and blended to appeal to seasoned aficionados. Flathead pairs well with coffee, dark rum, and dark beer, and can be enjoyed at any time of the day. Comparable cigars include Oliva Serie V Maduro and LFD Double Ligero Maduro. CAO Flathead has without a doubt put CAO cigars back in the spotlight, as nobody can wait to get their hands on one.

note_sources.text: Cavalier Genève Cigars announced that it is bringing Tres Delincuentes by Cavalier Genève to the market. This brand is an addition to the core Cavalier portfolio and will be showcased at TPE this year. Tres Delincuentes by Cavalier Genève, in the same spirit as the Inner Circle by Cavalier Genève, is a new brand in the Cavalier portfolio, showcasing a new facet of the company. Tres Delincuentes, influenced by art and music, is graphic and bold – a new offering that continues to build the multifaceted Cavalier subculture. This new brand in the Cavalier portfolio showcases another face of the company. Bold visuals, flavorful cigars, and a reflection of what cigar culture can also mean to the Cavalier team when parting from classics. Tres Delincuentes offers three blends, three sizes for each blend based around three iconic wrappers/shades, Connecticut, Habano, and Maduro. Tres Delincuentes Connecticut · Robusto, 5×50, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 6.95 USD per cigar · Toro, 6×54, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 7.60 USD per cigar · Gordo, 6×60, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 7.90 USD per cigar Blend Wrapper: Connecticut Ecuador Binder: Habano Ecuador Filler: Habano Nicaragua, Piloto Dominicano, Habano Honduras Tres Delincuentes Habano · Robusto, 5×50, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 6.95 USD per cigar · Toro, 6×54, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 7.60 USD per cigar · Gordo, 6×60, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 7.90 USD per cigar Blend Wrapper: Habano Honduras Binder: Connecticut Honduras Filler: Habano Nicaragua, Piloto Dominicano, Habano Honduras Tres Delincuentes Maduro · Robusto, 5×50, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 6.95 USD per cigar · Toro, 6×54, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 7.60 USD per cigar · Gordo, 6×60, 24 count cabinet – Retail price: 7.90 USD per cigar Blend Wrapper: San Andres Mexico Binder: Connecticut Honduras Filler: Habano Nicaragua, Piloto Dominicano, Habano Honduras All cigars are produced at Cavalier Genève Cigars’ own factory, FCT (Fabrica Centroamericana de Tabaco SA) in Danlí , Honduras. Cavalier has announced that the cigars will start shipping immediately after TPE.

Cohiba announces the release of Cohiba Rubicon, a full-time addition to its portfolio and an evolution of the brand’s blending philosophy. The cigar has been handcrafted at the HATSA factory in Danlí, Honduras. Rubicon is built from six tobaccos sourced from five of the world’s growing regions. The blend is crowned with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, laid over a U.S. Broadleaf binder and filled with a combination of Dominican Piloto, Honduran tobaccos from La Entrada and Jamastran, and Nicaraguan Estelí leaf. “Rubicon gave us the opportunity to offer a cigar without boundaries,” said Sean Williams, Cohiba Brand Ambassador. “The blend was thoughtfully created with intention. The result is a cigar that bridges tradition with a more modern expression of complexity. It rewards a practiced palate while remaining accessible to emerging enthusiasts.” Cohiba Rubicon ships to retailers in August 2025. Each box contains 20 cigars, available in three vitolas: Box-Pressed Robusto (5.5 x 55) | MSRP $8.49 Toro (6 x 54) | MSRP $8.99 Gigante (6 x 60) | MSRP $9.49

Drew Estate and Crowned Heads announced their partnership in the release of La Coalicion , manufactured by La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate and sold through Crowned Heads. La Coalicion will be displayed in the Crowned Heads Booth at the IPCPR Convention and Tradeshow. La Coalicion is wrapped in rich, dark Connecticut Broadleaf, with a Sumatran binder and aged fillers from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. La Coalicion is available in 4 sizes: Corona Gorda (5” x 46), Gordito (5 1/2” x 50), Siglo (6” x 52) and Sublime (6 1/2” x 54). Each vitola brings a very specific and unique nuance and complexity, blended by Willy Herrera and Jon Huber. From Little Havana in Miami, Willy Herrera Master Blender at Drew Estate highlights, “Huber and I have always had a similar palate for what notes we are looking for in our blends. Working together, we knew from the beginning we wanted to utilize the dense, oily Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, which is the inspiration for this killer smoke. La Coalicion is a passion product that Huber and I are really proud of.” From Crowned Heads HQ in Nashville, Jon Huber adds, “I’ve personally wanted to work with Willy for years now, as I feel that our aesthetic towards cigars are similar and we also share a common respect and passion towards the tradition of premium cigars. Further, being able to tap into the creative juggernaut that is Drew Estate has been an amazing experience. I’ve long respected what the DE brand has achieved, and I believe their personal brand extends far beyond just ‘cigars;’ they’re truly an innovator, disruptor, and a game changer within our industry.” From the Wynwood Safehouse, Jonathan Drew President and Founder of Drew Estate notes, “I am proud to report that Drew Estate always remains “Boutique in the Heart” in everything we create. This collaboration with Crowned Heads has been gratifying, mostly because of their passion and intensity. Plus, their hat game is on point!” La Coalicion Corona Gorda: 5 x 46 | MSRP $219.00/box of 20 Gordito: 5 1/2 x 50 | MSRP $245.00/box of 20 Siglo: 6 x 52 | MSRP $270.00/box of 20 Sublime: 6 1/2 x 54 | MSRP $299.00/box of 20 La Coalicion will be shipping in October.

When Drew Estate and Crowned Heads team up to make a cigar, only something awesome can come of it, and that is exactly the case with La Coalicion. Jon Huber, co-founder of Crowned Heads, admits to sharing a similar vision towards the tradition and artistry of cigars with Willy Herrera, the man behind Drew Estate masterpieces Herrera Esteli and Norteno. Collaborating together, Huber and Herrera were able to concoct a blend that was nothing short of a masterpiece. La Coalicion is made at the world-famous La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate down in Nicaragua using extremely high-end filler tobacco from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. The binder is Indonesian Sumatra and the wrapper is a dark, oily Connecticut Broadleaf. This blend is both classic and refined at the same time, and is sure to appeal to the most discriminating of connoisseurs. Bearing classical gold and red bands over a dark, toothy wrapper leaf, La Coalicion certainly has the old-school look going on. The construction is on-point as well, as each La Coalicion sports a near-seamless roll and offers an easy draw. Billowing clouds of thick, white smoke ignite the palate with bold flavors of earthy raw tobacco and spicy peppers from the get-go. Hints of raisin and chocolate join the party, along with a faint coffee note in the background. More spice on the retrohale combines with a thick, creamy finish, pulling the whole package together. La Coalicion begins on the heavy side of medium-full, but by the end is an all-out monster. Bold, flavorful, and complex, La Coalicion is by no means a beginner's cigar. There is plenty of strength, as well as a lot going on from start to finish, so to truly enjoy all this blend has to offer, one must have quite the developed palate. La Coalicion pairs nicely with dark beer or bourbon and makes for quite a conclusion to a long day. Though it may not be completely accurate, one might say La Coalicion is a cross between Herrera Esteli and Jericho Hill , perhaps the two most successful blends of each side of this collaboration. Speaking of that collaboration, who wouldn't want to try the product of a collective effort between one of the biggest boutique brands on the market and an industry giant like Drew Estate? If you would like to, you had better get your hands on La Coalicion ASAP!

Davidoff Cigars continues to expand its Winston Churchill «The Late Hour Series» line to provide passionados with a wider choice of formats for their enjoyment. In 2026, the line welcomes a medium-filler Belicoso – the first figurado in the series. «The Late Hour Series» «The Late Hour Series» offers an intense experience, crafted with a blend and a curated choice of formats. Its multi-origin blend contains a Condega visus filler tobacco aged in whisky casks. New Belicoso Format The Belicoso is ideal for moments when time is limited yet the desire for a special cigar remains. It offers the same taste experience as the other cigars in «The Late Hour Series», while its figurado format adds a new dimension. The tapered head channels the blend directly to the palate. The Belicoso is presented in a matte tin of four cigars – conveniently sized to be carried in one’s pocket.
Wood , Pepper , Dark Chocolate , Espresso Available. Learn about Davidoff Winston Churchill Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Winston Churchill

Next month Diesels new release “Estelí Puro” will make his debut. This addition to Diesels lineup was created in collaboration with AJ Fernandez. The collection harnesses the strength and complexity of Estelí’s renowned tobacco which comes from the darkest and most dense of Nicaraguan soils. Each of the tobaccos that comprise Diesel Estelí Puro were hand-selected from AJ’s farms to meet specific requirements set forth by the Diesel team. The wrapper was harvested from La Lilia, the binder from San José and the fillers from several plots including AJ’s celebrated San Lotano farm. Senior Brand Manager Justin Andrews said, “Estelí Puro represents the future of Diesel in that the story of the blend is told by the tobacco itself. With Estelí Puro, we made a collection that is completely unique in its bold flavor profile, yet has many of the attributes that have made the other Diesel expressions a cigar of choice among dyed-in-the-wool smokers. This is a cigar that demands the smoker’s full attention with deep and balanced flavor, a strong presentation and an attractive price point.” Blended by AJ Fernandez, handcrafted at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Estelí, Nicaragua and developed by General Cigar’s Justin Andrews, Diesel Estelí Puro is made with hand-selected leaves that are cultivated, processed and aged by AJ’s team. Heady aroma and spice dominate, lending body and dimension to the cigar, and delivering a smoke for experienced palates. Diesel Estelí Puro Format: Robusto 5.25” x 54 — SRP per cigar $8.99 Toro 6” x 54 — SRP per cigar $9.49 Gigante 6” x 60 — SRP per cigar $9.99 Packaging: 20-count box Shipping : shipping to retailers on September 1, 2020

Nutty , Molasses , Cocoa , Creamy Drink. Diesel Estelí Puro a full-time addition to the Diesel lineup was created in collaboration with AJ Fernandez.  The collection harnesses the strength and complexity of Estelí’s renowned tobacco which comes from the darkest and most dense of Nicaraguan soils

Refuel your love of potent, full-bodied cigars with the amazing Diesel Esteli Puro. Crafted by none other than the incomparable A.J. Fernandez, this Nicaraguan beauty puts the pedal to the metal when it comes to hearty flavor and robust character. Each time you smoke one it's like taking a road tour of A.J.'s most prized tobacco farms, with a generous portion of the longleaf filler sourced from the iconic San Lotano, the binder coming from San Jose, and the wrapper grown at the acclaimed La Lilia. So take a seat and enjoy this full-strength excursion to Esteli. Despite the cedar sleeve covering most of it's length, there's no denying the power beneath the hood of the cigar as you slowly heft it from your humidor. With spice and chocolate fumes wafting from the well-packed barrel as it is revealed, you'll find a smooth sheen of oil running the length of the toothy vitola. Once cranked with a steady flame, the Diesel Esteli Puro will fire off bouts of pepper and dark earth as it heads for the sweet spot, the flavors accelerating even as the burn settles into a slow cruise. Comfortable leather, vanilla cream, and sticky candied orange peel sit shotgun beside the rich, semi-sweet mocha that drives the profile long into the journey. Come along for the ride of your life with a Diesel Esteli Puro. Although best enjoyed by pro-level travelers, an amateur tourist looking for a thrill might as well buckle up and take a spin around the block. For more Esteli goodness, stop by the lot and test drive some La Gloria Cubana Esteli and Herrera Esteli Miami.
