note_sources.text: To celebrate Corona Cigar Co.’s 25th Anniversary, Drew Estate is adding a Belicoso (7 x 54) to its newly released “20 Acre Farm” brand. Available exclusively at Corona Cigar Co., the 20 Acre Farm Corona Cigar Co. 25th Anniversary Belicoso will debut during a marquee event on March 3. 20 Acre Farm is crafted with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade Grown wrapper, a Sun Grown Habano binder, and a filler blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos from Estelí and Jalapa, coupled with Florida Sun Grown leaf. Drew Estate introduced 20 Acre Farm cigars in November 2021. Packaged in 20-count boxes, 20 Acre Farm first launched in three vitolas: Toro (6 x 52), Robusto (5 1⁄4 x 54) and Gordito (6 x 60). The Corona Cigar Co. 25th Anniversary Belicoso is the first addition to the original 20 Acre Farm lineup. “My farm team and I worked years to massage the soil to produce a tobacco that’s flavorful, intense and aromatic,” Jeff says. “The hard work has been rewarded by Drew Estate showcasing Florida Sun Grown tobacco as a key component in its 20 Acre Farms cigars. I’m very proud that it chose to make the Belicoso vitola exclusively for Corona Cigar Co.’s 25th Anniversary. Our customers can join our 25th Anniversary celebration by enjoying 20 Acre Farm in a format that accentuates the cigar’s sophisticated smoking characteristics.” “20 Acre Farm is a milestone achievement in Drew Estate’s history,” adds Drew Estate Founder and President, Jonathan Drew. “This ultra-premium cigar pays homage to the famed Cuban cigars of yesteryear as well as Florida’s cigar and tobacco heritage. This very special Belicoso is our strong statement of love and support for what Jeff, Tanya, and Team have achieved, and for their contributions to the premium cigar industry. I look forward to being at the farm with you lunatics during Barn Smoker in May. Gonna be amped.” Only available at Corona Cigar Co., the 20 Acre Farm Corona Cigar Co. 25th Anniversary Belicoso is packaged in 20-count boxes and has an MSRP of $280/box or $14/cigar.

Emilio Cigars is proud to announce the release of the Limited-Edition SUAVE SUMATRA. The Cigar is crafted in Estelí, Nicaragua, at the Fábrica Oveja Negra. Master blender and owner of BLTC and Fabrica Oveja Negra, James Brown, lent his expertise to the creation of Suave Sumatra’s blend and artwork. Reflecting on this release, Mr. Brown stated, “Suave has been the cigar line that really put Emilio on the map. It’s not only a great introduction to the brand but also a great introduction to smoking cigars in general. Featuring a Sumatra wrapper highlights the balance of spice, flavor, and complexity. The finish is long, with the signature subtle sweetness Suave is known for.” SUAVE SUMATRA Country of Origin: Nicaragua Wrapper: Sumatra Binder: Ecuador Habano Filler: Nicaragua Robusto – 5×50 (20 count) MSRP $10.00 Toro – 6×50 (20 count) MSRP $10.50

Emilio Cigars (Emilio) will be showcasing a new release at this year’s PCA in Las Vegas: Suave Maduro. Suave Maduro will be added to the core-line production with shipping to commence later this summer. The artwork and cigar blend for Suave Maduro were created by James Brown. Brown, owner of BLTC and Fabrica Oveja Negra, stated, “Suave has been a staple in the Emilio line since the beginning. With the success of the Connecticut Suave over the years, we felt it was time to expand the line and add a Maduro version. The Maduro Suave is a medium bodied, medium strength and full of both flavor and complexity.” SUAVE MADURO: Country of Origin: Nicaragua Wrapper: Ecuador Maduro Binder: Nicaraguan Habano Filler: Nicaragua & Dominican Robusto – 5×50 (20 count) MSRP $10.00 Toro – 6×50 (20 count) MSRP $10.50 Churchill – 7×48 (20 count) MSRP $10.50

Ferio Tego continues its expansion with the introduction of the Metropolitan Petites, a trio of small, handmade cigars that deliver the familiar experience of the Metropolitan Selection in a new, compact size. Available in the Metropolitan Connecticut, Maduro, and Host blends, these 4″ x 34 handmade cigars are the ideal choice for those who value convenience without compromising quality. Designed for moments when time is limited but flavor shouldn’t be, the Metropolitan Petites bring a sophisticated take on small-format cigars. Michael Herklots, co-owner of Ferio Tego, shared his enthusiasm for the launch: “These petite cigars are completely hand made, and consist of 100% premium tobacco, bringing an elevated level of quality to the experience of enjoying small-format cigars.” Each blend in the Metropolitan Petites lineup is meticulously crafted to ensure a balanced draw, even burn, and exceptional flavor, making them a seamless addition to the Ferio Tego portfolio. The Metropolitan Connecticut is smooth and mellow, the Maduro is smooth with a slightly richer flavor, and the Host is creamy and slightly sweet. “When the temperatures are low, or time is short, these petit formats are the perfect solution,” said Herklots. Offered in packs of five cigars, and finished in units of five 5-packs, the Metropolitan Petites are perfect for on-the-go lifestyles, fitting easily into a pocket or travel case. Each 5-pack has a suggested retail price of $24.95 before applicable taxes. The Ferio Tego Metropolitan Petites will be previewed at the Total Products Trade Show in Las Vegas and will be shipping nation-wide in February 2025.

The Ferio Tego Metropolitan Connecticut marks the return of a true classic, reborn for a new generation while staying true to the blend that made it a favorite among discerning smokers for decades. Originally developed under the Nat Sherman legacy, this timeless Connecticut blend has been thoughtfully preserved by Michael Herklots and Brendan Scott, ensuring that its smooth, balanced character remains exactly as aficionados remember. Handcrafted in the Dominican Republic, the Metropolitan Connecticut features a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over a core of aged Dominican binder and long-filler tobaccos. The result is a refined, mellow-bodied cigar that delivers both approachability and depth—hallmarks of a well-executed Connecticut profile. From the first draw, expect a smooth, creamy introduction with notes of sweet cream, cedar, and light coffee . As the cigar develops, subtle layers of toasted nuts, soft leather, and a touch of cocoa emerge, all supported by a gentle natural sweetness . The finish is clean, balanced, and satisfying, with just enough nuance to keep seasoned smokers engaged while remaining accessible to those newer to premium cigars. Consistent, elegant, and effortlessly enjoyable, the Metropolitan Connecticut is ideal for any time of day, whether paired with a morning coffee or enjoyed as a relaxing, easygoing smoke. It’s a classic Connecticut done right: smooth without being simple, refined without sacrificing flavor, and a dependable staple for any humidor.

Ferio Tego is expanding the Timeless Prestige blend with the addition of a lancero format. The Ferio Tego Especiales measures 6 1⁄4” in length with a 38 ring gauge and is finished with a classic pig tail cap. The blend features a Honduran-grown wrapper, over a Dominican binder and fillers from Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. “The Especiales is an extraordinary expression of the Timeless Prestige blend,” says Michael Herklots, co-owner of Ferio Tego. “Thinner ring gauge cigars have a unique delivery and focus to their flavor and have a higher concentration to the smoke. The Prestige blend in this format is just spectacular!” The Ferio Tego Timeless Prestige blend is handmade in the Dominican Republic by the Quesada family. The Especiales will be an ongoing size in the line joining the Churchill, Hermoso, No. 2, Robusto, and Gordo, all offered in boxes of 20 cigars with a suggested retail price of $11.00 per cigar. The cigars will begin shipping this week and will be on display at the PCA convention and Tradeshow in Las Vegas next month. Ferio Tego is distributed by Davidoff USA in the United States.

Ferio Tego cigars have been getting a ton of attention in recent years, and much of that attention is focused on the Timeless lineup. The sticks in this series obviously hit a sweet spot for long-time connoisseurs, and Timeless Prestige seems to be the biggest hit of all. For those who don’t know, Ferio Tego cigars are resurrected blends of what were formerly known as the Nat Sherman Exclusives. The bands are very reminiscent of the Nat Shermans of old, and the cigars themselves are almost the same, if not better. For Timeless Prestige, we have a premium cigar rolled by the Quesada family at their Tabacos de Exportacion factory in the Dominican Republic. As for the blend, a Dominican binder embraces a 2-country blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler leaves, and the wrapper is a dark brown Honduran leaf that has undergone extensive aging and fermenting to become silky smooth in every way. This blend seems to work beautifully, as the Ferio Tego version of Timeless Prestige has earned as high as a 90-rating in Cigar Aficionado . Red-topped cedar chests house the gorgeous vitolas, and each one wears double gold and black bands. The Timeless logo is unmistakable, and simply laying eyes on it is sure to bring back a vivid array of memories for anyone that was fortunate enough to enjoy the Nat Sherman era. Beautiful construction offers an easy, productive draw, while the burn line stays sharp all the way down. Cedar and white pepper start things off, soon followed by a warm array of cocoa beans, coffee, and earthy raw tobacco . The finish is sweet, spicy, and crisp, and overall, this captivating adventure finishes at the medium-full-bodied mark. Made for connoisseurs, by connoisseurs, Timeless Prestige is complex and balanced, and medium-full-bodied to the core. Those with well-developed palates will surely appreciate all the rich complexities offered by the blend, along with the classic nature of the smoke. This beauty is paired well with coffee, bourbon, or full-bodied beer and is an elegant way to spend an evening relaxing. Fans of other Timeless blends such as Timeless Sterling or Timeless Supreme will want to be sure to check this one out, as it certainly seems like an upgrade to an already stellar blend. Whether an old school Nat Sherman fan or just someone who enjoys trying the latest and greatest ultra-premium cigars, Ferio Tego Timeless Prestige is a stick you will want to get your hands on.

Nicholas Melillo’s Foundation Cigar Company will introduce a new blend at the 2018 IPCPR trade show: Tabernacle Havana Seed CT #142. Nicholas Melillo explains, “It’s unknown exactly who brought the seed to the River Valley or its origin in Cuba from where it came, although we do know it arrived between 1870 and 1880. It is somewhat smaller and smoother than broadleaf and grows upright on the stalk making for better yields. On one hand it reflects characteristics that are very different from broadleaf; while it’s spicy and earthy like Cuban tobacco, with hints of cedar, it also has a pronounced sweetness like Connecticut Broadleaf.” The Havana Seed CT has been evolving in the Connecticut River Valley for well over 100 years. “I’ve been working with particular farmers in the valley since 2014 to help optimize the plant’s overall health while maintaining the seeds unbelievable flavor characteristics. The culmination of these efforts involved combining the seed with Havana Seed #38 and Havana Seed #1207, also known asPage-Comstock-The end result is Havana #142.” “While the leaf is incredibly oily and full flavored, the leaf itself is quite thin, making for an extended fermentation process, and at lower heat. The tobacco has been curing for almost 3 years in Nicaragua under the watchful eyes of Abdel Fernandez and myself. The tediousness involved in developing Havana Seed CT #142 is well worth it, as the leaf is incredibly flavorful and unlike any other tobacco in the world.” The box depicts Ras Tafari Makonnen as King Regent before he was crowned as the Haile Selassie, and the brand will consist of four sizes to include a 6 x 52 Toro, 5 x50 Robusto, 5 ¼ x 46 Corona, and a 7 x 54 Double Corona. Wrapper – Havana Seed #142 Grown in Connecticut Binder – San Andres Mexico Filler – Esteli, Jalapa and Jamastran The brand will be displayed at the IPCPR 2018 in Las Vegas, and begin shipping to retailers throughout the country in late September/October.

Quite the long name, and quite the scrumptious treat, the Tabernacle Havana Seed CT No. 142 is a medium-full-bodied temple of deliciousness. Earning a 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado , this blend showcases the artistry of creator Nick Melillo , whose Foundation Cigar Company is also behind the 93-rated Charter Oak and the 95-rated El Güegüense . It should come as no surprise that Melillo loves great tobacco—but this might just be his most ambitious project yet. Deciding that standard Connecticut Broadleaf wasn’t grand enough to serve as the wrapper for his latest masterpiece—a blend of Nicaraguan and Honduran longleaf filler bound by a robust Mexican San Andrés—Nick developed a brand-new hybrid of Havana and Connecticut tobacco that more than rises to the occasion. If the only remarkable quality of Nick’s new Broadleaf wrapper were its appearance, it would already be good enough for most. After three years of aging, it has taken on a sleek, oily, near-black sheen. Add to that a crisp, woody aroma that whets the appetite, and you’d already have a cigar worth noting. But with the Tabernacle Havana Seed CT No. 142 , these surface delights are just the beginning. As soon as the sturdy vitola is lit, a rich chocolate core emerges, quickly blooming into flavors of walnut, rye toast, earth, and sweet buttercream. Increasingly complex yet surprisingly smooth the further down it burns, this is a cigar you’ll want to savor to the very last puff. We see you admiring the stature of these premium Tabernacle Havana Seed CT No. 142 smokes and already thinking our price is more than fair for what you’re getting. Now consider this: instead of just twenty, each cabinet-style box comes packed with a full two dozen of these beauties. Suddenly, “reasonable” feels like an understatement. Hallelujah! Let wonders never cease!

After a year of being distributed by Miami Cigar, Foundation Cigar Company will be bringing their Upsetters brand in-house for domestic distribution. “Foundation Cigars has distributed The Upsetters brand internationally during the past year and decided it was time to add the brand to our core distribution portfolio here in the U.S. We are extremely thankful and appreciative for all of Miami Cigar Company’s efforts during the Upsetters’ first year ,” says Melillo. He adds, “Prior to The Upsetters’ release we had no outside sales team and knew that a brand of this nature required instant coverage nationally. Jason Wood and his team at Miami Cigar Company stepped in and solved the problem, graciously agreeing to help us with distribution until we built a rep force, which we fortunately now have.” “I thank Nick and the entire team at Foundation for entrusting the brand with us during its infant stages. I expect nothing but the best for the brand and the entire team moving forward “, said Wood.

Known for crafting some of the most respected traditional cigars in the industry, Foundation Cigars turned heads with the release of The Upsetters , a bold, culture-driven line that redefines what an infused cigar can be. According to Foundation, “ The Upsetters represents the next level in the evolution of the infused-cigar smoking segment, ” and one light-up is all it takes to understand why. Inspired by the people, heritage, and history of Jamaica, The Upsetters line honors centuries of tobacco tradition while delivering a modern, flavor-forward experience. Each cigar is handcrafted in Nicaragua and blended around a rare and highly sought after core of Jamaican Cow Tongue tobacco , an heirloom varietal grown in the hills of Jamaica, where the indigenous Arawak people cultivated tobacco long before modern cigar making existed. Supporting this unique Jamaican core are premium Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos, selected to provide balance, depth, and structure. The non-Maduro Upsetters lineup spans multiple sizes and wrapper styles, each offering its own nuance while maintaining a consistent identity: medium-bodied, smooth, aromatic, and unmistakably distinctive. The infusion process is carefully controlled, delivering an inviting pre-light aroma without overpowering the tobacco itself. Once lit, these cigars offer an effortless draw and generous smoke output, opening with subtle spice before evolving into layers of cream, vanilla, earth, and natural tobacco sweetness . The finish is refined and lingering, often accented by a signature herbal note that ties the experience together without veering into artificial territory. Wrapped in eye-catching black, gold, and multicolor packaging that proudly nods to Jamaican culture, The Upsetters manages to be both expressive and premium at the same time. It’s a line built for smokers who want something different without sacrificing craftsmanship or balance. Approachable yet intriguing, The Upsetters is a natural fit for fans of refined infused cigars like Drew Estate’s Larutan and ACID, but it also appeals to traditional cigar smokers looking to shake up their routine. Whether paired with coffee, dark rum, or enjoyed during a celebration, these cigars bring flavor, culture, and individuality to every occasion.

One hundred and eighty years after the establishment of one of the oldest cigar brands in the world, H. Upmann is bringing to life the H. Upmann 1844 Special Edition Barbier, a premium cigar that pays homage to the innovative craftsmanship and a favorite pastime of the brand’s founding brothers. The 1844 Special Edition Barbier (German for “Barber”) uses a unique combination of two Ecuadorian wrappers – Connecticut and Sumatra – with a Java binder and a blend of Nicaraguan, Dominican and Broadleaf fillers. “The use of these contrasting shades of wrappers makes for an eye-catching, barber-pole-like presentation,” says Pedro Ventura, Hand Made Operation and Product Development Manager of Tabacalera de Garcia in La Romana, Dominican Republic where the cigar is being produced. “The wrappers work together to add an entirely new flavor profile to the cigar, making one’s smoking session a lot more interesting as well,” he says. The cigar industry will get its first look at the H. Upmann 1844 Special Edition Barbier, along with a showcase of other releases from Altadis U.S.A., at the 2023 Total Product Expo in Las Vegas, February 22 – 24. The H. Celebrate the Richest Moments of Life with The Banker by H. Upmann. The Banker by H. Upmann – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 In 1844, German bankers Carl and Herman Upmann traveled to Cuba where they created an exceptionally unique cigar. They securely locked it away in their vaults to be gifted to their most important clients. Now, over 170 years later, that award-winning blend has been recreated in The Banker by H. Upmann. An attractive dark-brown, oily wrapper is just the beginning of the beautiful premium cigar. A mellow aroma highlights the rich and robust nutty taste profile that is complemented with well-balanced notes of spice, coffee and leather.

The Banker is a restoration of an award-winning, pre-turn of the century H. Upmann cigar originally reserved for wealthier clientele. Hitting their stride early and often, the Upmann brothers, Carl and Herman, began their long association with quality stogies back in 1844 to the delight of generations of aficionados. The succulent filler tobacco stuffed into each well-appointed The Banker is quality longleaf sourced from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic before being aged, blended, and expertly rolled beneath a sturdy yet elegant Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Decorated to the nines in gold, white, and emerald green, even just a glimpse of the cigar beneath the multiple bands can set the mouth to watering. The lips might tingle during a cold draw test, while a woody aroma off the barrel accents the spice and earth on the tongue. Blossoming into a syrupy, spicy flavor-bomb full of molasses and red pepper , the strength is kept in check by soothing cedar and toasted almonds . Even as the flavors caramelize into black licorice, smoked bitters, and leather , you still find hints of citrus to refresh the palate for the next slow puff. Even though there is plenty of green in the packaging of an H. Upmann The Banker, you won't have to spend much of your own green to get your hands on a stack of these premium sticks. Imagine the good luck these might bring you on your next Vegas trip with the gang. You'll feel like a million bucks!

Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro is the latest cigar to join the highly acclaimed Herrera Esteli lineup from Drew Estate. Released in 2018, Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro follows the original Herrera Esteli blend and Herrera Esteli Norteno , both highly-rated cigars and both cigars which have earned spots on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 list . That being said, any new addition to the lineup would have some big shoes to fill, but Willy Herrera was more than confident in blending this dazzling Brazilian Maduro blend. Made in Nicaragua, Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro consists of a stout blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican filler tobacco and a robust Connecticut Broadleaf binder. What really makes the blend interesting, however, is the use of plantation grown Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper leaf. This type of leaf is rarely used as the outer layer of a cigar and is more popularly used as a filler component or even a binder in some cases. However, Willy Herrera desired to "bring the Mata Fina to the forefront of the blend," thus ending up with an end result that is bold, interesting, and mysteriously intriguing. Apparently the blend works, as it recently received a 90-rating in Cigar Aficionado. Boasting all-new packaging that "combines classic Cuban style with modern simplicity," as Herrera notes, this particular cigar could not have a more fitting theme. Blue and white on gold denotes the blend, as opposed to the standard red on white bands worn by the original blend. Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro is unusually well-crafted, offering a crisp burn and easy draw, despite the interesting choice of wrapper leaf. Thick clouds of dense, white smoke massage the palate with an early storm of black pepper. Cedar and cocoa soon take over, as the earthy spiciness continues throughout the smoke. Hints of sweetness appear along the way, and the finish is clean, yet intensely peppery. A faint coffee note hangs in the background as the cigar burns down, but the main theme is pepper and sweetness. Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro is a solid medium-full-bodied cigar from beginning to end, and beautifully balanced. It's well-known that when Drew Estate releases a non-flavored premium cigar, beginners need not apply. This particular collaboration with Willy Herrera, like the first two Herrera Esteli brands, is intended for experienced connoisseurs. The flavor profile is medium-full-bodied and complex, pairing beautifully with bourbon, scotch, or a dark beer. Strong coffee also makes a great companion to this cigar, though the blend may be a bit bold as a morning smoke for some. Although Liga Privada No. 9 doesn't use the same type of wrapper leaf as Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro, its flavor profile and construction compare quite well to the cigar in question, so if you have tried a No. 9 and loved it, this is likely a stick for you. "Combining classic Cuban style with modern simplicity." Willy Herrera couldn't have hit the nail any better than that. Give Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro a shot and experience the passion, expertise, and ingenuity of one of the best collaborations in the cigar business

If you worked at a prestigious and widely heralded cigar company, you too might get access to the absolute best tobaccos available and be able to create a world-class smoke like the Norteño by Willy Herrera . Rising from humble origins crafting quality cigars for a small Miami boutique, Herrera is now a master blender at famed Drew Estate in Nicaragua. With this access to the La Gran Fabrica factory's vast stores of quality leaf, he was given ample time after joining the team to prove his mettle and he took full advantage. First blending a collection of aged Esteli and Jalapa tobacco for the filler, Willy then selected a Honduran binder to add a spicy kick to the rich San Andres Maduro wrapper he laid over each box-pressed vitola. Cigar Aficionado has awarded Herrera Estelí Norteño multiple 90+ ratings, reaching as high as a 94 rating and securing it the number 7 position on the Top 25 of 2016 list. Packed into boxes of ten without cellophane, each Norteño is decorated with a simple green and cream-colored band bearing the embossed image of Nicaragua's national bird, the Guardabarranco. The rounded-square profile of each heavy stick fits nicely in the hand, and the triple cap applied to the toothy, mocha-hued wrapper mirrors the overall quality of the rest of the cigar. Not content to play it safe, Herrera decided to go all out on his inaugural effort and so the Norteño is a full-bodied and full-flavored treat loaded with earth and cedar and a black peppe r at the base but enlightened with buttered toast, sweet currants, and a luscious floral aroma .

Based in Reno, Nevada, Illusione Cigars is something of a host manufacturer whenever the PCA Show comes to Las Vegas and this year was no different. Founded by Dion Giolito, the company sponsored the PCA cocktail party on the evening of the show’s first day and used the occasion to introduce two new cigars and new packaging for its Epernay brand. Dubbed as the first of Illusione’s Limited Release Series, the One Off black Robusto (5 x 52) is made using a new varietal seed that Giolito specifically set aside for this project. The tobaccos have been aged for three years to produce a mild- to medium-bodied smoke with complex flavors. Only 1,000 10-count boxes are available in what will prove to be a very popular smoke for those lucky enough to enjoy one. Illusione’s The Group of Five RB is the initial release in a new cigar line that will eventually grow to five vitolas. The RB (5 x 52), is made with a blend of high primings of Criollo ’98 and Corojo ’99 tobaccos and a new varietal seed that had never been grown in Nicaragua before. The cigars are made by Aganorsa Leaf in Nicaragua and are packaged in 15-count boxes and that’s all the news that Illusione is willing to share at this time. Indeed, the band hints at the mystery behind the cigar with the phrase “Whispering Tongues are Treachery” emblazoned in English and Latin. More will certainly be reveals as other vitolas get released over time. Finally, the company’s iconic Epernay line is getting an update to bring it closer in line with its “Marquis Deluxe” standing in the premium cigar industry according to a press release announcing the change. Illusione introduced Epernay to pay tribute to the French town where many of the world’s most famous champagne producers are based.

There's not much more to it other than the Illusione Epernay cigar is good. Really good. Like, rated 94 good. Ranked in the top 3 worldwide the year after it came out good. Sell your possessions, ship the kids to grandma's house, and lock yourself in while you smoke each and every one you have good. Sure, we get that there are some of you not already familiar with Illusione, and that's something that needs to be remedied with the quick review. Enigmatic brand owner Dion Giolito is a quiet man who creates the kind of big sticks you definitely want to carry. His various blends have won accolades and acclaim the world over. And of course here we have the Epernay, a Nicaraguan Puro chock full of Corojo and Ciollo longleaf that is his crowning achievement. (See more Illusione Cigars ) With a Café Rosado wrapper that's oilier and darker than you might expect, an Illusione Epernay is an impressive sight even when sitting among many others in a crowded humidor. On its own, each vitola exerts an influence over the aficionado to cause the mouth to water and the eye to gleam. Cut, light, sit back and enjoy. Discover rich and savory cream and toasted nuts. Some nutmeg and other baking spices enter at the sweet spot, not overwhelming but warm and inviting. Lush, floral-scented clouds of smoke introduce the arrival of leather and stone fruit flavors that flourish during the second third, while the last long moments of the cigar are full of mocha, cedar, and honey.

Kristoff launched their new line, Kristoff Vengeance, at this year’s IPCPR in Las Vegas. Now it hits the shelves in Europe. “The response in the US has been insane,” owner Glen Case says. “I still can’t wrap my head around it. We did a pre-release at the Tobacconists’ Association of America’s convention in May and we sold out 150,000 cigars in about two months. We had to go back to press and print out new rings and labels.” The Vengeance line is produced in the Dominican Republic. It has a Broadleaf Connecticut wrapper, an Indonesian binder and fillers from Estelí, Jalapa as well as a Habano from the Dominican Republic. “It’s medium to medium plus. It has rich notes of dark espresso bean, a sweet mocha flavor, a little bit of spice and a coco finish.” It comes in four sizes, Robusto, Perfecto (6 ¼ x 60), Toro and a 6 x 60. In the US it costs USD 8.25 to 10, in Europe EUR 8.20 to 8.90.

Lately, the trend of bringing back old cigar brands from the dead has been all the rage, and Kristoff Vengeance is one particularly enticing example. When brand owner Glen Case began Exclusive Brands, which would eventually become Kristoff Cigars, Vengeance was one of the first blends to get the ball rolling. Later, that blend would be renamed the GC Signature Series and still remains in the Kristoff portfolio. Fast forward about a decade, and we have the introduction of a "new" brand bearing the Kristoff name: Kristoff Vengeance. This stick is made at the Charles Fairmorn factory in the Dominican Republic and consists of an entirely new recipe. Differing from the GC Signature Series, today's Vengeance blend is made up of Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, Indonesian binder, and a dark, oily Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Vengeance is the first Kristoff cigar to feature a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, a decision that has indubitably proven to be a good one. The packaging for Vengeance includes all the Kristoff signature touches one might expect, from the rugged gray box to the sinister black and silver bands. The dark, marbled wrapper looks imposing, yet upon first light it becomes clear that this concoction is made to be smooth and satisfying. The flavor profile starts off with a burst of classic maduro sweetness, followed by black pepper, coffee, and dark chocolate. A backbone of cedar and earth carries through to the end, and the finish is heavy and chocolaty. Medium-full-bodied and expertly balanced, this blend is made for the true connoisseur. Though not technically a beginner's cigar, Kristoff Vengeance is an excellent way to step into the realm of heavier, darker cigars and makes a great choice for a first maduro. Blends of this stature pair beautifully with coffee, making Vengeance a great way to start the day. However, dark beer and red wine pair well also, and as we all know, maduros are good any time of the day. If you have come to enjoy such maduro blends as CAO Maduro or Partagas Black Label , or maybe even have tried the classic GC Signature Series from Kristoff, this cigar should be right up your alley. With a stick this versatile, easy to smoke, and undeniably satisfying, cigar freaks should take pleasure in knowing that Kristoff Vengeance is back—with a vengeance!

For its newest cigar, introduced at this year’s PCA Show, La Flor Dominicana (LFD) returned to its first cigar, released way back in 1994. Known then as “Premium Line,” that first cigar was a very mild and delicate smoke, and the cigar later became known as Suave. But over the years, LFD’s Litto Gomez’s blending sensibilities have changed, as have many passionado’s palates—with both preferring something with a little more meat on its bones. Hence this year’s PCA Show release, the reimagined Suave. LFD switched out the old Ecuadorian Connecticut seed wrapper for an Ecuadorian Corojo for the new Suave. Utilizing a Mexican San Andres Negra binder and filler tobaccos sourced from Gomez’s La Canela farm in the Dominican Republic, the new Suave Natural is available in three sizes: Maceo (6 x 48), Máximo (6 x 54) and Gobernador (6 ¼ x 60). Packaged in 20-count boxes, MSRPs range from $8.40 – $12.80 per cigar. Additionally, LFD introduced a Maduro variant. The Suave Grand Maduro features a Mexican San Andres wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican filler tobaccos. Available in two sizes, No. 5 (6 1/4 x 52) and No. 6 (6 ¾ x 54 Torpedo), the Suave Grand Maduro MSRPs are $11.80 and $12.80 per cigar and are packaged in 20-count boxes. Both the new Suave Natural and Grand Maduro cigars will be available beginning in July.

La Flor Dominicana Suave cigars have made a comeback from the dead. These cigars, once discontinued by Litto Gomez are back, for how long is anyone’s guess. We would like to think that these Dominican Republic produced cigars will be with us for some time now that the FDA is regulating premium cigars. These Suave cigars have come back almost exclusively as a result of those FDA regulations. Many cigars that were popular years ago are returning to market due to the “grandfather date” of those FDA regulations. All that was old is seemingly new again.

A favorite of reviewers, bloggers, and regular BOTLs and SOTLs of all stripes, the La Gloria Cubana Serie R Maduro cigar is an aromatic and sweet, full-bodied delicacy. This dark and toothy gem is truly the smoke that put the name of La Gloria Cubana on everyone's lips, right after the first puff. Created by the ever innovative Ernesto Perez Carrillo Jr . in 1999 as his final solo venture before being brought into the General Cigar family of brands, the Serie R Maduro contains a proprietary blend of tobaccos from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic coated with what is perhaps the hottest type of tobacco in use today, a thick and rich Connecticut Broadleaf. Easy to pick up and hard to put down, the La Gloria Cubana Serie R Maduro is tailor made for afternoon or evening enjoyment by any smoker who is capable of standing firm again the cigar's many charms. Better yet, stay seated and let yourself be carried away by great clouds of mind-clearing smoke. A smoke which is chewy and dense in all the right places, like a salted-chocolate covered caramel bar, if the caramel was made from smoky Scotch and the chocolate harvested from earthiest of black soils. If you're looking for a full-bodied smoke that really satisfies , this stick is it!

In a nod to the past and present, an old-world technique is being used in the latest release from La Gloria Cubana, just as the brand’s modernized new logo makes its debut. Called Spanish Press, the three-cigar collection is handcrafted at the El Credito Cigar Factory. There, artisans place the freshly-rolled cigars into wooden trays with dividers that apply uniform pressure to the cigars. The trays are then pressed to define their shape. Once pressed, the cigars are placed in specially sized boxes that apply slight pressure to maintain their shape. Yuri Guillen, production manager for El Credito said, “This method eliminates air pockets to deliver an optimal draw and output of smoke, resulting in an enhanced smoking experience. We developed a very special blend to showcase our unique technique, and believe we have delivered a fantastic addition to the La Gloria Cubana portfolio.” The Nicaraguan-forward blends features tobaccos from four countries. The filler is comprised of Nicaraguan Jalapa, Dominican Piloto Cubano and Olor, and Brazilian Mata Fina, with a Mexican San Andreas binder. The cigar is wrapped in a rich Nicaraguan leaf from Jalapa. Rarely does the construction technique of a specific cigar merit much attention, but when the cigar in question is the La Gloria Cubana Spanish Press, suddenly every detail is meaningful. Of course, as any experienced enthusiast already knows, with LGC, the result is going to be majestic no matter what. Here, in a process similar to traditional Cuban box-pressing methods, once the Nicaraguan Jalapa, Brazilian Mata Fina, and Dominican Olor and Piloto Cubano longleaf fillers are masterfully rolled beneath a juicy Mexican San Andres binder and after the Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper is applied, the vitolas are packed together in an actual box and placed under pressure to create a premium smoking experience time after time. While the sharp corners of the mahogany-colored stick are visually impressive, the 'Spanish Press' process is mostly designed to facilitate the perfect draw through what might otherwise be an inordinate amount of fine tobacco. Fortunately, the Nicaraguan-focused blend that comprises each La Gloria Cubana Spanish Press cigar is more than up for the challenge. Great reams of fragrant smoke billow from the cigar as soon as it is lit, filling the room and setting the mouth and eyes to water. Coffee with sweet cream, dark chocolate and malt, salt and black pepper, almonds coated in toffee, seemingly every flavor that washes over the palate is complimented by yet more flavor. Starting and remaining a smooth medium in strength and body, this is a smoke every aficionado should crave. Cigars with unique production methods usually sell out quickly, sometimes forever if you remember the too-soon-gone CAO Fuma Em Corda, but we have a good feeling about the longevity of La Gloria Cubana Spanish Press. However, if you want to play it safe then go ahead and stock up now. These beauts are only going to get better with age, so you'd be doing your future self a massive favor.

La Palina will be introducing the KB series at the PCA show in Las Vegas, NV. “We felt that this powerhouse blend should be paired with truly memorable brand imagery, if not a bit of tongue-in-cheek to match the astonishing flavor profile. Furthermore, the addition of new sizes and new packaging in the KB series is a direct response to fan requests worldwide. I always knew that the KB series had more to offer our customers. This is why we tweaked the blends in the new larger sizes, adding higher primings of ligero in KB (Part 3 & Part 4) to offer a full-bodied yet succulent smoking experience.” – Bill Paley Part One: 4.25 x 40 Part Two: 6 x 52 Part Three: 5 x 52 Part Four: 6 x 54 Blend Wrapper: Honduras Binder: Nicaraguan Fillers: Nicaraguan

During its June 8 broadcast of “Freestyle Live: Special Edition,” which aired from 7 to 9 p.m. Eastern on the company’s Facebook Live page ( facebook.com/drewestatecigar ) and YouTube channel ( youtube.com/drewestatecigar ), Drew Estate revealed the secret identity of the mystery cigar inside its latest Freestyle Live Event Pack … the all-new Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas (115mm x 44). Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas marries two of Drew Estate’s most popular cigar concepts—its exclusive hybrid H99 Connecticut Corojo capa leaf and the Papas Fritas vitola. Since its debut more than a decade ago, the distinctive Papas Fritas vitola has become one of the most beloved Liga Privada Único Serie cigars due to its quick smoke format, making it the ideal choice for on-the-go cigar lovers who want to savor a rich Liga Privada cigar. Working side-by-side with H99’s exclusive tobacco farmer, Drew Estate has slowly increased its yield, year-over-year to expand the rare H99 tobacco’s availability. The hybrid H99 Connecticut Corojo capa is born from a union of Stalk-Cut Habano and Connecticut Corojo seeds to produce a luxurious tobacco. A robust Mexican San Andres Otapan Negro Último Corte capote contrasts perfectly with the H99 capa; and dense and earthy well-aged Nicaraguan, Honduran and Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker tripa tobaccos complete Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas’ complex and deceptively full-bodied blend. The all-new Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas will be available exclusively at participating Drew Diplomat Program partners beginning on June 9. Packaged in 25-count boxes, the cigars’ MSRP is $7.50 per cigar or $187.50 per box.

It’s been quite some time since Jonathan Drew and his team shook the premium cigar world with the release of Liga Privada. Now, the bar has been raised even higher with Liga Privada H99. The first addition to the Liga Privada family in nearly a decade, H99 hails from Nicaragua, where it is handcrafted at the world-famous La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate. Let’s be honest—this is a Drew Estate cigar, and it’s in the Liga family. There’s no way it could be anything less than spectacular. And spectacular it is. The recipe for this incredible blend tells a big part of the story. The filler consists of leaves from Honduras, Nicaragua, and the good ol’ USA. That third component? Pennsylvania Broadleaf—specifically, the fabled Green River One Sucker, regarded by many as the most potent tobacco in existence. The binder is a San Andrés Negro Ultimo Corte leaf from Mexico, while the wrapper is a hybrid, stalk-cut Habano Corojo-seed leaf grown in the Connecticut River Valley. Sounds intriguing, doesn’t it? Well, the folks at Cigar Aficionado thought so, awarding it a very respectable 91 rating. It comes in the same cedar chests as the Liga Privada we know and love, with the same simple, utilitarian white bands on every vitola. This time, though, the ink is a deep red—signaling that you’re about to experience the H99 series, and that you’d better get ready. The roll is flawless, the wrapper oily and dark, the draw effortless, and the smoke production immense. From the first billowing cloud of silky blue smoke, the palate is greeted with a burst of pepper mingled with cinnamon. This opening quickly gives way to a rich medley of dark chocolate, espresso, and clove. An earthy tobacco core holds it all together, lending bold strength to the blend, while the finish is long, rich, and sweet. Complex, balanced, and just a hair shy of full-bodied, Liga Privada H99 proves itself a worthy addition to the legendary Liga Privada family. Made specifically for the most experienced and discerning connoisseurs, H99 is not a stick for just anyone. A years-long history of tasting and dabbling in the world of premium cigars is simply a requirement if someone is going to truly enjoy such a treat. Paired with scotch or your favorite bourbon, this cigar is a beautiful way to relax after a steak dinner or any one of life’s special events. Compared to the original T52 or No. 9 , this one seems to do its own thing. It has all the good parts of both, and then some more on top of that. For an unforgettable cigar experience and something that will satisfy even the priviest cigar freak, Liga Privada H99 by Drew Estate is certainly a choice one cannot afford to miss out on.

Drew Estate introduces the Liga Privada Unico Serie Bakkwa, a cigar crafted to honor Lunar New Year traditions, exclusively available through CoH Cigars in Hong Kong. This full-bodied Churchill-sized cigar features a Connecticut Stalk Cut wrapper, delivering a robust, complex flavor profile, designed to echo the festive Lunar New Year spirit. Inspired by the Chinese delicacy Bakkwa, a symbol of good fortune and prosperity, this cigar aims to blend cultural significance with a luxurious smoking experience. Jonathan Drew, Founder and Presidente of Drew Estate highlights “I’m inspired by Bakkwa’s role as a cultural bridge, encapsulating festivity and indulgence in the form of a premium cigar. Drew Estate is so diverse as a company and as a brand, our people and our philosophies. Our zest for life and passion is embodied beautifully in this new offering. It’s dope.” Presented in 12-count boxes, the Liga Privada Unico Serie Bakkwa is priced at retail of $235 per box. Bakkwa is a nod to the Unico Serie’s tradition of pork-themed cigars, poised to be a coveted item for Hong Kong’s cigar enthusiasts.
Pepper , Cedar , Sweetness , Nutty Available. Learn about Liga Privada Unico Serie Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Unico Serie

Crowned Heads is showing a new cigar by Luciano and Ace Prime Cigars called the Fiat Lux. The name comes from Genesis and the phrase “let there be light”. According to the company, when you taste a great blend you can be enlightened by delving into the complexity of the flavors and with the possibility of introspection as you enjoy the smoke. Fiat Lux is a blend that generates that deliberation. As a result, the four sizes are named for the mindful journey. They are Insights 5.625” X 46, Intuition at 5” X 50, Genius measuring 5.5” x 52 and Acumen at 6 X 56. The blend is a high priming of Ecuador Sumatran for the wrapper, over Nicaraguan Pueblo Nuevo binder and fillers from Nicaragua — Condega, Ometepe and Jalapa. The cigars come in 20 count boxes with prices ranging from $8.75 to $10.75

Luciano Cigars is excited to announce the launch of Chicos, a new size of the acclaimed UNDERRATED by Luciano Cigars. A 4 x 40 cigar tailored for brisk winter outings and those seeking a high-quality, quick smoke. Designed with the same attention to detail and superior blend as their flagship offerings, Chicos is crafted to deliver robust flavor in a compact, convenient format. Engineered for the outdoors, Chicos features their celebrated long-filler blend composed of Connecticut Broadleaf fillers, Ecuadorian HVA, and Pueblo Nuevo tobaccos, all enveloped in a classic San Andres wrapper. Packaged in a 50-count box and priced at an attractive MSRP of only $6, this cigar combines exceptional value with uncompromised quality. While some have playfully dubbed it the “Dog Walker” cigar, they proudly call it Chicos—a nod to its approachable, spirited character. Chicos is not only launching now but is also available for immediate shipment. Their warehouse is fully stocked, and their most preferred retailers are already receiving their orders. Pre-releases in Luciano Cigars branded lounges and through their preferred partners have paved the way for a smooth, enthusiastic market entry.

Macanudo is expanding its sophisticated Emissary lineup with a new cigar featuring rare tobacco grown near Bordeaux, France. The star of the release is French tobacco cultivated in the Mugron River Valley, where it is nurtured by the Atlantic sea breeze. Emissary France is crafted with an Ecuadorian Habano Wrapper (10-Year Aged), a USA Broadleaf Binder (10-Year Aged), and a filler blend composed of Dominican Piloto (10-Year Aged), USA Broadleaf (8-Year Aged), Brazilian Arapiraca (7-Year Aged) and French (4-Year Aged). The Emissary series was created to showcase rare and distinctive European tobaccos, and Emissary France is no exception. Following the critically acclaimed debut of Emissary España, this latest release furthers Macanudo’s commitment to crafting cigars that highlight the elegance and depth of unique terroirs. Emissary España featured tobacco grown in Riolobos, Spain. Matt Wilson, Senior Brand Manager for Macanudo, said, “After the success of Emissary España, we knew we had high expectations to meet. Going to France, with its incredible flavors and deep-rooted tradition of sophistication, felt like a natural next step. We were inspired by the richness and refinement that define French craftsmanship and set out to create a cigar that embodies those same qualities. Emissary France is the perfect expression of that vision, delivering an experience that is both refined and unforgettable.” Handcrafted at HATSA, Macanudo Emissary France is a full-time release available in four vitolas. All sizes come in 16-count boxes. Emissary France will begin shipping to stores March 3, 2025. Macanudo Emissary France Robusto (5” x 52) – SRP per cigar $14.99 Macanudo Emissary France Toro (6” x 52) – SRP per cigar $15.99 Macanudo Emissary France Churchill (7” x 48) – SRP per cigar $16.99 Macanudo Emissary France Perfecto (5 ¾” x 50) – SRP per cigar $17.99

note_sources.text: Macanudo Inspirado Green will launch its fourth frontmark in February with a large format cigar called Gigante. At 6 x 60, Gigante will round out the Inspirado Green line which debuted 2020 and currently consists of a Robusto, Toro and Churchill. Laurel Tilley, brand ambassador of Macanudo said, “Macanudo Inspirado Green Gigante brings together the unique experience of Brazilian tobacco with one of the cigar industry’s most in-demand sizes. We’re confident that this new and distinctive smoke will deliver increased excitement to the top-selling Macanudo brand.” Handcrafted at General Cigar Dominicana in Santiago, D.R., Macanudo Inspirado Green is a medium-bodied collection that features hand-selected tobaccos from four countries. A rich Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper serves as the foundation of the blend. Beneath an Indonesian binder is a blend of Dominican and Colombian filler leaves that mingle with the wrapper to create a full-flavored, medium-bodied smoke brimming with earth and pepper. Macanudo Inspirado Green Gigante will ship to retailers on February 15, 2022 and will come in boxes containing 20 cigars. SRP per cigar USD 8.29.

Earth , Nuts , Sweet , Black Pepper Drink. Inspirado Green is a robust, full-flavored blend that delivers the unique flavors of Brazilian tobacco. Using the rich and lustrous Arapiraca tobacco, this is the first Brazilian tobacco used in Inspirado and opens up a whole new flavor experience within the Inspirado line of cigars. This four-country, medium-bodied smoke is loaded with flavors of earthy sweetness and black pepper

For a famous brand once known mostly for producing the best-selling yet one of the mildest premium cigars in town, Macanudo sure has been hitting it out of the park lately with more complex cigars like the radiant Macanudo Inspirado Green. Much of this success can be attributed to new tobacco varieties being added to their roster. Slammed full of carefully aged Dominican and Colombian longleaf filler beneath an exotic Indonesian binder, this fine stogie is certainly not your father's cigar. No doubt Ol' Dad would enjoy one very much too, so make sure to recruit enough so both you and he can marvel at the shimmering and near-perfect Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper that fits each vitola like a well-worn leather glove. The bright green and silver band that proudly wears the frontmark of the Macanudo Inspirado Green shares the modern look of the rest of the Inspirado lineup, a comparison which continues on to the quality of tobacco in and construction of each cigar. A pre-light test reveals a toasty, nutty aroma wafting to the nose while the smooth draw delivers the promise of cocoa and cream. Leading off with a solid run of espresso, soft pretzel, and oak, you'll also witness a nice raw sugarcane sweetness sliding into the aftertaste. On deck for the middle third are roasted peanuts, brown butter, cinnamon, and dried fruit. Expect a home run in the final innings as chocolate malt, salted caramel, earth, and bright citrus clinch the pennant. Step up to the plate and grab a box-full of these cigars to become a welcome addition to your humidor. Once the inevitable happens and you're a fan of the Macanudo Inspirado Green, go ahead and schedule an all-star tournament with the other Inspirado players: the Red, the Black, the Orange, and the White. Hand them out to your friends, light up, and play ball!

The Macanudo Inspirado White line is expanding with two new sizes. Steve Abbot, senior brand manager of Macanudo said, “The Macanudo Inspirado White portfolio had consisted of six popular sizes, yet our retailers and cigar smokers wanted more. We responded by creating a Corona and Cigarillo and are confident that the new sizes will become fast-selling additions to this highly successful brand.” Introduced in 2017, Macanudo Inspirado White is counted among the top-sellers in the Macanudo portfolio. Macanudo Inspirado White is made with a proprietary Ecuadoran Connecticut wrapper developed by General Cigar’s agronomists. Aged for six years and refined to a creamy shade of gold, the wrapper crowns an Indonesian binder. The blend features Nicaraguan Condega and Mexican San Andres leaves, each aged for four years and Nicaraguan Jalapa aged for two years. Both new formats have begun shipping to retailers. The Corona is handcrafted at HATSA in Danli, Honduras and the Cigarillo is made at General Cigar Dominicana in Santiago, D.R. Macanudo Inspirado White Corona (5.5” x 42) – SRP per cigar $5.49; 20 cigars per box Macanudo Inspirado White Cigarillo (4 3/16” x 32) – SRP per 10-cigar tin $15.99.
Creamy , Spice , Cedar Drink. Beautiful, yet complex. Sweet, with spice. Rich, but nuanced. Macanudo Inspirado White is a study in contrasts. Learn more on Cigar World

At first glance, the arrival of another mild cigar from a brand already famous for them might not seem like headline news—but that changes the moment you light up a Macanudo Inspirado White . Because in this business, experience matters. And when you've spent over 50 years crafting cigars—when you've created an icon like the Macanudo Café , which arguably introduced more people to premium handmades than any other—then even a mild cigar has the potential to surprise. Fortunately, there’s nothing ordinary about the tobacco in the Inspirado White. This blend brings together four-year-aged Nicaraguan and Mexican fillers, an Indonesian binder, and a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper that's been resting for six years. The result? A smoke that even the most seasoned aficionado will appreciate. This refined vitola is wrapped in a flawless, premium shade-grown leaf, and while that may be expected, what surprises is the depth and complexity that follows. From the first draw, your senses are treated to an earthy barnyard aroma and crisp cedar flavor. As it burns slowly and evenly, the profile evolves—creamy cedar gives way to bright white pepper and finishes with layers of dark cocoa and warm nutmeg. All of it delivered in a smooth, belly-friendly smoke that stays cool to the finish. And while the experience is premium, the price isn’t. The Inspirado White is priced for everyday enjoyment—ideal alongside your morning coffee, yet still elegant enough to mark life’s big moments. Whether you're celebrating a birth, a wedding, or just another day well-lived, this cigar fits the occasion. And we’re confident you’ll make the right call. If you love the White then try the Inspirado Orange or Inspirado Black .

note_sources.text: The world’s first Vintage cigar was created by Macanudo more than 40 years ago to spotlight an exceptional wrapper produced in part by Mother Nature. The Vintage tradition marches on with Macanudo Vintage Maduro 2013. The five-country blend reflects optimal climatic conditions and calls upon meticulous curing and precise maturation techniques perfected by the artisans of Macanudo. The 2013 growing season saw some of the highest temperatures on record in the Connecticut River Valley, with soaring humidity and optimal rainfall that yielded an exceptionally brawny Broadleaf tobacco. Cured and aged for an entire decade to bring forth an array of undeniably diverse notes on the palate, this singular tobacco makes its debut in Macanudo Vintage 2013. Ernest Gocaj who oversees the Connecticut growing operations for Macanudo said, “The growing season in 2013 was one of the best I’ve ever seen. The crop was exceptional at harvest, which meant that we had to be obsessive when it came to monitoring the tobacco during the eight-week curing process. That’s how important curing is. Our hard work paid off because we ultimately brought the tobacco’s very best attributes to life.” A master blender’s assortment of tobaccos complement this exceptional wrapper to create the rich indulgence that is Macanudo Vintage 2013. The filler is made up of Dominican Piloto Cubano from two different primings, along with Brazilian Mata Fina and Nicaraguan Jalapa. The binder is Honduran OSA. Macanudo Vintage 2013 is shipping to retailers July 3 and will be released in three sizes, each chosen to enhance the superlative blend. The cigars are individually encased in cedar wrapping and are presented in handmade, solid wood boxes that protect 20 expertly-crafted cigars, each made by artisans at General Cigar Dominicana in Santiago, DR. Robusto (5” x 50); SRP per cigar $11.99 Toro Grande (6” x 54); SRP per cigar $12.99 Churchill (7 x 49); SRP per cigar $13.29

Cinnamon , Chocolate , Coffee , Cedar Drink. Learn about the Macanudo Maduro, a mild to medium bodied smoke handcrafted with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. It is one of the richest maduros available

The Macanudo Maduro is a premium cigar designed for smokers who crave the rich, bold flavor of a maduro without sacrificing smoothness. Expertly crafted in the Dominican Republic, this cigar features a meticulous blend of top-tier Dominican and Mexican fillers and binders, all wrapped in an extra-fermented Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. The result is a rich, flavorful cigar with an ultra-mild profile that delivers an exceptionally smooth and enjoyable smoking experience. Upon lighting, the Macanudo Maduro releases thick, white smoke that carries notes of sweet wood, warm spice, and a subtle underlying cocoa richness . Its mild-to-medium body makes for a clean, crisp finish, free from the bitterness or harshness sometimes found in other maduro cigars. The even burn and open draw enhance the smoking experience, making it perfect for both beginners seeking a gentle introduction to maduro and seasoned aficionados who appreciate a refined, flavorful smoke. This versatile cigar pairs beautifully with mild red wines, light beers, or even a smooth cocktail, making it ideal for casual afternoons, social gatherings, or quiet moments of relaxation. Smokers who enjoy the Macanudo Maduro may also appreciate similar premium options such as Punch Maduro or Ashton Aged Maduro, offering comparable richness with subtle variations in flavor. For anyone seeking a mild maduro cigar that balances richness, sweetness, and smoothness, the Macanudo Maduro is a standout choice. Elevate your next smoke and experience the perfect harmony of flavor and finesse that only Macanudo can deliver.

The world’s first Vintage cigar was created by Macanudo nearly 40 years ago to spotlight an exceptional wrapper developed in part by Mother Nature herself. Today, the Vintage tradition continues with Macanudo Vintage 2010. The 2010 growing season saw the highest temperatures in 25 years in the Connecticut River Valley, with high humidity and optimal rainfall that yielded an exceptionally silky shade-grown wrapper tobacco. Cured and aged for an entire decade, this singular tobacco makes its debut in Macanudo Vintage 2010. Ernest Gocaj who oversees the Connecticut growing operations for Macanudo said, “We could not have asked for a better growing season than we had in 2010. Yet this is only part of the story. After such a beautiful crop is harvested, the hard work begins again because the most critical process for growing tobacco is curing. Given how unique and special this crop was, we were obsessive in monitoring the tobacco throughout the eight-week curing process, and ultimately brought its very best attributes to life.” A deeply-aged assortment of tobaccos complement this wrapper. The blend features Dominican Piloto Cubano 94, a proprietary Cuban-seed varietal regenerated by General Cigar’s agronomists over a ten-year process. The Dominican Piloto Cubano 94 is married to Nicaraguan and Honduran leaves, aged three and five years, respectively. The blend is bound with a Honduran leaf. Macanudo Vintage 2010 will be released on August 17 in three sizes. The cigars are presented in handmade, solid wood boxes. Toro Grande (6 5/8 x 54); SRP per cigar USD 11.99 Torpedo (6 1/4 x 52); SRP per cigar USD 11.99 Churchill (7 1/4 x 48); SRP per cigar USD 12.29

If there's one thing Macanudo is known for aside from being one of the best-selling cigar brands of all time, it would have to be the fact that nobody does "Vintage" like Macanudo. In the case of Macanudo Vintage 2010, we can all agree that we have a true gem on our hands. According to the company, the 2010 growing season saw the highest temperatures in over two decades in the Connecticut River Valley. Add optimal rainfall and humidity, and you get a "perfect storm" for tobacco growing. Well, the folks at Macanudo saw this as an opportunity to make future plans, plans that would take over a decade to come to pass. Macanudo Vintage 2010 contains quite a bit of tobacco from that legendary 2010 crop, specifically the silky Connecticut shade wrapper leaf and a good deal of the filler blend. Also contained in the recipe is Dominican Piloto Cubano 94, Honduran, and Nicaraguan tobacco, aged 5 and 3 years respectively. The binder is from Honduras, and the whole package is produced down in the Dominican Republic. The tobacco used for the wrapper leaf has been aged for over 10 years and is considered by some to be one of the finest Connecticut leaves ever used in a cigar. Classic cedar chests, ornate red, white, and gold bands, and "VINTAGE" displayed on just about everything, screams nostalgic goodness to long-time Macanudo fans. The construction is impeccable, the draw is productive, and the burn is sharp as a razor. Robust cedar is the welcoming note upon lighting, soon joined by a creamy array of vanilla, coffee, and cinnamon. The earthy tobacco core holds it all together, and there is a hint of citrus and floral sweetness on the finish. Medium-bodied, flavorful, and velvety smooth, Macanudo Vintage 2010 is exactly what an ultra-premium cigar should be. While newbies can certainly tolerate the smooth medium-bodied goodness this cigar offers, it's best left to the experienced. Only a well-seasoned connoisseur will be able to appreciate all the things that make this blend so incredible. Macanudo Vintage 2010 pairs beautifully with bourbon or cognac and is the latest addition to the Vintage section of the company's portfolio, following Vintage 2006 and Vintage 1997 Maduro . Whether you are among the millions of cigar enthusiasts that has come to favor the beloved Macanudo brand over the years or you just want to find out what a rare Connecticut leaf aged over 10 years tastes like, Macanudo Vintage 2010 will doubtless provide you with an experience that is both notable and memorable.

note_sources.text: The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua is now available in a 52 x 4 ½ size, the “Exclusivo.” The size – created exclusively for Casa de Montecristo’s retail stores and lounges – is now available. Like its predecessor, the Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Exclusivo pays tribute to the original 1935 blend that made Montecristo the icon it is today. To fully honor Montecristo and the original tobaccos used in that first Montecristo cigar, Rafael Nodal, AJ Fernandez and the Grupo de Maestros worked to find a precise and exquisite proprietary blend of aged tobaccos. “At Casa de Montecristo,” said CEO Brad Winstead, “we are continuously looking for ways to offer our adult clientele the highest quality premium products. The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Exclusivo is a perfect fit for our brand and we look forward to providing our guests with this exclusive size. We are honored to be able to offer cigar lovers something they can’t get anywhere else.” The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Exclusivo is offered in 10-count boxes and priced at an MSRP of $15.00 per cigar. Limited quantities will be available for purchase starting June 11 exclusively, as noted above, at Casa de Montecristo. Size and Frontmark: 52 x 4 1/2, Exclusivo Price: USD 15.00 Origin: Nicaragua

Fernandez for the brand's 80th anniversary (1935). 'Savory flavors of wood, coffee, cinnamon, earth, and spice, all enhanced with a long-lasting sweet tobacco finish'; medium to full bodied.

halfwheel (No. 2 redux, 90): upper-mild rising to between medium and full; sweet oak and espresso beans lead, with cocoa nibs, leather, pencil lead, toasted bread, gritty earth, slight cinnamon; maple syrup sweetness and black pepper on the retrohale; later powdery cocoa, bread, popcorn. Cigar Aficionado (Espeso, 97 pts, #2 cigar of 2024): 'big, box-pressed, chunky and delightful', capturing the coffee, earth and spice of the original sizes.

We are pleased to announce Cigar Aficionado has recognized the Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua No. 2 as the #2 Cigar of the Year in 2021!  The Montecrist Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 We are pleased to announce Cigar Aficionado has recognized the Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua No. 2 as the #2 Cigar of the Year in 2021! The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua is presented as a soft-pressed series of four luxury sizes that combines classic craftsmanship and the finest tobaccos the Nicaragua region has to offer. Celebrating 85 Legendary Years of Montecristo with a first-ever, tribute blend of the iconic cigar that started it all. The first Montecristo cigar was handcrafted in 1935 using a signature blend of tobaccos that has become the standard by which the brand still lives up to today. Now, 85 years later, tobacco and blending powerhouses Grupo De Maestros, Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez transport us back to that iconic moment in history with a first-ever interpretation of the original blend that made Montecristo the icon it is today. We are pleased to announce Cigar Aficionado has recognized the Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua No. 2 as the #2 Cigar of the Year in 2021!

When it came time to celebrate the 85th anniversary of the world-famous Montecristo brand , the celebration cigar had to be something special, and Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua certainly fit the bill. Released in late 2020 as a collaboration between brand ambassador Rafael Nodal, the Grupo de Maestros, and none other than the infamous AJ Fernandez, this cigar is extraordinary to say the least. Each stick is born in the San Lotano Factory in Nicaragua and is rolled under the supervision of Fernandez himself, using 100% Nicaraguan leaves from his very own family farms—wrapper, filler, and binder. It may seem a bit ironic that the anniversary cigar for a Dominican brand is a Nicaraguan puro, but just about anyone would agree that they really did hit it out of the ballpark with this one. The folks at Cigar Aficionado certainly think so, as this blend has already earned a very respectable 97 rating and the #2 Cigar of the Year in 2024 ! Each vitola is softly box pressed and rolled to precision. The elegant gold and black band look lovely against the beautiful dark and oily wrapper leaf. In typical AJ Fernandez fashion, the draw is soft and easy, the smoke production is superfluous, and the flavor is impeccably rich and exciting. An enormous burst of Nicaraguan spice greets the palate on the opening puffs, soon settling down to a bold medley of black pepper, caramel, and cinnamon. Notes of earth and coffee hang in the shadows as a woody core of flavor emerges to take over the blend. A solid level of spice remains throughout the cigar, and the finish is sweet, speckled with light floral notes. Medium-full-bodied and strikingly complex, this cigar is no doubt a connoisseur-level stick. Tailor-made for seasoned cigar veterans, Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua contains all the bells and whistles one would expect for an anniversary edition bearing the Montecristo name. As mentioned earlier, it finishes as a solid medium-full-bodied stick and the flavor profile is incredible from all aspects. This type of cigar pairs well with just about any fuller-bodied libation, though coffee, port wine, or dark rum would probably compliment it best. As we all know, this is not the first time AJ Fernandez has been involved with Montecristo, and it is a safe bet that if you enjoyed either Montecristo Crafted by AJ Fernandez or Monte by Montecristo AJ Fernandez, you will probably love this one. Whether you are a long-time Montecristo or AJ Fernandez fan or simply want a top-shelf cigar to commemorate your own special events in life, celebrate the 85th birthday of one of the world's most beloved cigar brands with Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua today.

note_sources.text: Odyssey is adding a bold, new line to its accessibly-priced portfolio with Odyssey Full. The five-cigar collection of Nicaraguan-made smokes rounds out the Odyssey portfolio with a rich, fuller-bodied profile and marks the sixth collection of Odyssey cigars. Odyssey Full is handcrafted by artisans at STG Estelí in Nicaragua. The blend is centered on Cuban seed tobaccos and features a high concentration of ligero leaves from Nicaragua and Colombia in the blend for a memorable smoking experience. With a Nicaraguan Habano binder and Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper, Odyssey Full delivers a robust yet balanced smoke that’s earthy and spicy with a hint of leather on the finish. Ed Lahmann, senior brand manager for Odyssey said, “Given its accessible price point, Odyssey Full is a great option for the tried and true cigar smoker who’s looking to add variety to their go-to set of brands. We’re confident that this new line is going to catch fire quickly.” Shipping this month, Odyssey Full will be available in these five sizes, each in 20-count boxes: Gigante (6 x 60); SRP per cigar USD 2.69 Churchill (7 x 48); SRP per cigar USD 2.49 Toro (6 x 50); SRP per cigar USD 2.19 Corona (5 1/2 x 42); SRP per cigar USD 1.69 Robusto (5 x 50); SRP per cigar USD 1.89

Partagas is launching Cortado, the brand’s first Connecticut Shade-wrapped offering and the first Partagas line to be handcrafted by artisans in Nicaragua. The new, four-cigar collection has just begun shipping to retailers. Matt Wilson, senior brand manager for Partagas said, “With interest in the Partagas brand continuing to grow, we felt it was the right time to expand the brand portfolio with a mellow-to-medium-bodied blend. The team and I are especially proud of Partagas Cortado’s incredible versatility when it comes to pairing. The blend is creamy and complex, and its taste notes can push forward or bow to other flavors, depending on the pairing. We feel our Nicaraguan artisans did a wonderful job with the blend and look forward to sharing it with Partagas fans, old and new.” Handcrafted at STG Estelí in Nicaragua, Partagas Cortado is wrapped in a silky Ecuadoran-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper and features an Indonesian binder over a blend of Honduran Jamastran and San Andres tobacco, with Nicaraguan Condega and Jalapa. Cortado is presented in wooden wrap-set boxes that align with the aesthetic of Partagas Black Label and Yellow. The blend is being released in four sizes to complement a range of smoking occasions. Corona (5 1/2 x 42) – SRP per cigar USD 6.39 (20 cigars per box) Robusto (5 x 50) – SRP per cigar USD 7.19 (20 cigars per box) Toro (6 x 52) – SRP per cigar USD 7.59 (20 cigars per box) Presidente (8 x 54) – SRP per cigar USD 8.99 (10 cigars per box)

A groundbreaking new offering from a brand steeped in tradition, the Partagas Cortado will exceed every smoker's expectations for a delectable mild-medium cigar. Even with a legacy stretching back nearly two centuries and spanning multiple countries across the globe, Partagas still has new frontiers to conquer. To that end, the Cortado is the company's first vitola to carry a shade wrapper, in this case a sultry and golden-hued Ecuadoran Connecticut, and also their first cigar produced in Nicaragua. Such an occasion requires all players to pull their weight, and so a wealth of homegrown Nicaraguan Condega and Jalapa tobaccos, plus plenty of Honduran Jamastran and Mexican San Andres longleaf, merge to provide a cocktail of flavors beneath an Indonesian binder. Close inspection of a Partagas Cortado reveals a sweet aroma reminiscent of dried alfalfa mixed with strong cedar wafting from a dense vitola decorated with the new frontmark's large ornate red and gold band. After tasting hints of roasted peanut through the barrel, slowly puff while applying a steady flame to the foot to release the first layers of palate-pleasing smoke ripe with chocolate, white pepper, and toasted marshmallow. A silky blend of amaretto and vanilla cream elevates the midpoint to just below medium in strength, a touch of cinnamon in the gentle retro hale. The finale lingers with a rich flavor like a milky cappuccino spiked with dark rum and dusted with dark cocoa powder. Wonderful in both value and quality, you'll desire more of these great stogies from the moment you light your first. We're certain that a Partagas Cortado will delight not only those aficionados who prefer complex shade-wrapped cigars like AVO Classic or San Cristobal Elegancia, but smokers of all stripes. Check them out today.

Tabacalera Perdomo announced the release of the new Perdomo Reserve 10th Anniversary Box-Pressed Maduro and Sun Grown in August 2020. The Perdomo Reserve 10 th Anniversary Champagne, awarded Best Brand Nicaragua in 2018 by Cigar Journal, continues to be one of the top-selling premium cigars on the market and the new Maduro and Sun Grown are sure to compliment the line and capture the hearts of cigar enthusiasts worldwide. “Our Perdomo Reserve line has been on the market for over 20 years. We wanted to come out with something really special to honor the history of the brand and offer a cigar that every cigar smoker would truly fall in love with,” states Nick Perdomo, Jr., President, and CEO. “We blended these cigars with 6-year aged Cuban-seed wrapper, binder, and filler tobaccos that we carefully hand-selected from our most prestigious farms located in the Estelí, Condega, and the famed Jalapa Valley in Nicaragua. We blended these cigars to not only be rich in flavor, but also to be very smooth on the pallet with slight hints of sweetness. Our tasting panel with over 250 years of cigar making and premium tobacco experience was amazed at how great this blend tastes.” The Perdomo Reserve 10 th Anniversary Box-Pressed Maduro is a medium to full-bodied Nicaraguan “puro” blended with a dark, oily 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan wrapper that has been bourbon barrel-aged for an additional 14 months and is paired with 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos to create naturally sweet flavors with hints of dark cocoa and espresso on the finish. The Perdomo Reserve 10 th Anniversary Box-Pressed Sun Grown is a medium to full-bodied Nicaraguan “puro” blended with a beautiful 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan wrapper that has been bourbon barrel- aged for an additional 10 months and is paired with 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos to create a rich core of earthy flavors with hints of spice and sweetness on the finish. Both are packaged in 25 count boxes in the following sizes: ITEM DESCRIPTION QTY PER UNIT DIMENSION MSRP PER CIGAR MSRP PER BOX FIGURADO 25 4 3/4 X 56 $7.25 $181.25 ROBUSTO 25 5 X 54 $8.25 $206.25 EPICURE 25 6 X 54 $8.75 $218.75 CHURCHILL 25 7 X 54 $9.25 $231.25 TORPEDO 25 7 X 54 $9.50 $237.50 SUPER TORO 25 6 X 60 $9.75 $243.75 The manufacturer’s suggested retail prices are $7.25 to $9.75 per cigar, excluding state and local taxes.

The Ace Prime completes the trilogy of the Clasico line. Firstly with Pichardo Clasico Toro, with a Sumatra wrapper; then Pichardo Clasico Maduro with a Brazilian wrapper (recently Launched on Nov 2020) – now, the classic line receives a new addition: The Pichardo Clasico Natural. Pichardo Clasico Natural Size:61/2x 50 Wrapper: Habano Sun Grown Ecuador Binder: Nicaragua Fillers: Nicaragua MSRP: $ 9.00 *Shipping on March 2021 “The Pichardo Clasico Natural is the fruit of a master craftsman – producing a medium cigar full of flavor, smooth, and perfectly balanced. The amazing result is not a surprise for us. Pichardo is a fourth-generation tobacconist: heir to more than a century and a half of knowledge in the world of tobacco,” says Luciano Meirelles (Co-Founder ACE Prime and Tabacalera Pichardo). “It was a difficult journey, but we knew this cigar needed to be very special to complete the trilogy of the Clasico line,” Eradio Pichardo (Co-Founder ACE Prime and Tabacalera Pichardo).

Previously released in limited quantities every year, Rare Corojo is now a regular-production cigar within the Punch portfolio. In addition, Punch is also launching a new, limited-edition Rare Corojo size just for 2025. That cigar, a Box Pressed El Gordo (6 X 60), features the same blend as prior Rare Corojo limited-production releases. Rare Corojo includes an extra-rich Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a distinctive reddish hue and uniquely smooth taste. It has a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Dominican Piloto Cubano filler tobaccos. Punch’s brand manager, Scott Abney, said, “For years, Punch fans have clamored for more Rare Corojo, and we’re excited to deliver it to them as a regular-production line. The classic blend will be available across nine frontmarks in addition to the limited-edition Box Pressed El Gordo for 2025. You’ve waited patiently for this day to arrive; now it’s time to celebrate with a Rare Corojo or two.” Punch Rare Corojo is produced at the STG Danlí factory in Honduras. The limited-edition Box Pressed El Gordo will begin shipping in early January, and it contains 20 cigars per box. (Note: some Rare Corojo sizes contain 20 cigars per box, while others have 25, and the Rothschild frontmark includes 50 cigars per box.)
