The Punch Rare Corojo is one of those cigars that quietly built a cult following long before “small batch” was a buzzword. First released in 2001, this annual limited edition arrives each spring with almost no fanfare, just enough boxes to satisfy the diehards who wait for it all year long. The magic lies in its specially cultivated Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed wrapper, grown in limited quantities and aged until it reaches the perfect level of richness, spice, and signature Punch character. The Punch Rare Corojo blend has also earned an impressive 92-point rating from Cigar Aficionado , further solidifying its status as a must-smoke cigar. But the wrapper isn’t the only star of the show. A sturdy Connecticut Broadleaf binder and a bold mix of Dominican Piloto Cubano, Honduran, and Nicaraguan long fillers round out the blend, creating a profile that’s both deeply flavorful and unmistakably Punch. From the first inch, expect a strong opening of earth, leather, cedar, and a touch of natural sweetness . Once it settles into the heart of the smoke, the Rare Corojo reveals its true personality: full flavor, smooth, and loaded with notes of cocoa, roasted nuts, and gentle pepper . It’s a dynamic cigar that rewards both seasoned smokers and curious newcomers. Fans of corojo-forward cigars, especially those who enjoy blends like Don Pepin Garcia Black Label or El Baton will feel right at home here. And when it comes to pairings, this cigar shines alongside a mellow, well-aged bourbon, though it plays beautifully with a wide range of drinks. The only catch? Once the limited supply is gone, that’s it until next year. If you see Punch Rare Corojo in stock, don’t hesitate to grab a box and enjoy one of the most anticipated annual releases in the Punch lineup.

Noel Rojas, recently featured in Cigar Journal’s Spring 2026 issue, continues to build a reputation as the “King of the Small Gauges,” favoring slimmer vitolas that emphasize wrapper-driven complexity. “We focus on smaller ring gauges because over 80 percent of a cigar’s flavor comes from the wrapper,” Rojas says, presenting his new Quiet Morning cigar. Though wrapped in Connecticut leaf, its blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican Ligero delivers a medium-to-full-bodied profile that defies the category’s milder expectations. Also debuting at PCA 2026 is the limited-edition Cinco de Mayo, featuring seven-year-aged Connecticut broadleaf filler, a Nicaraguan binder, and an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, an indication of Rojas’s continued focus on depth and balance. His booth in New Orleans maintained a steady buzz, reflecting a boutique brand clearly on the rise.

The next Firecracker will be a limited release for 2016 and as usual it will be released just before the 4th of July. This year’s production will be The CroMagnon Firecracker from RoMa Craft Tobac out of the Nica Sueno factory in Esteli Nicaragua. The CroMagnon Firecracker will measure 3.5” x 50, using a U.S. Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro Wrapper. The filler leaf for the new CroMagnon blend was acquired from three separate growing regions in Nicaragua: Esteli, Condega and a small farm north of Esteli on the Honduran border. The blend is expected to be full bodied and full flavored. There will be just 200 boxes made with 20 Firecracker Cigars in each box all adorning the CroMagnon name. The first Firecracker cigar was released on May 19, 2007 at a cigar rolling event at Two Guys Smoke Shop in New Hampshire featuring Jose Don “Pepin” Garcia. David Garofalo, owner and founder of Two Guys Smoke Shop asked Pepin to roll him a short cigar and to put a long pig tail on it. Pepin followed the direction and The Firecracker Cigar was born. Over the years limited releases of The Firecracker Cigars were made and most commonly released near the 4th of July and made by various cigar manufacturers. Past Firecracker Cigars include Don Pepin and Tatuaje (M80) at My Fathers Cigar Factory, Jose Dominguez, Iconic Leaf, at Leyendas Cubanas and La Flor Dominicana. The filler leaf for the new CroMagnon blend was acquired from three separate growing regions in Nicaragua: Esteli, Condega and a small farm north of Esteli on the Honduran border. Prices for the 2016 CroMagnon Firecracker are expected to be $119.99 per box of 20 ($6.99 a cigar) and available only at Two Guys Smoke Shop sometime in late June or early July.

Me no like the name RoMa Craft CroMagnon cigar. Too long. Too hard to say. Me call it Cro. Or Mag. Either way, mmmm, good smoke. Friend smoke. Happy smoke. The good humans at RoMa know what I like, know how to make fine sticks of yummy tobacco. Search like hunters over faraway places to bring just the right leaves back for extended rest. Mystic places like Connecticut for wrappers dark as night. A land across deep waters named Cameroon for binders that hide like sneaky rabbits between the outside world and the deep. Epic journeys to three Nicaraguan temples of longleaf where the magic words of 'Viso' and 'Seco' and 'Ligero' summon ancient forces of powerful flavor. The RoMa Craft CroMagnon cigar is a totem. A talisman that guides you into the past, where craftsmanship and pride reign supreme, while at the same time leading you into a future where enlightenment awaits. Heavy with a weight and bearing beyond its aged years, you will marvel at the ingenuity and skill of the human hands that created each perfect vitola. Rich with the tastes of smoky mesquite, well-worn leather, coffee bean, exotic vanilla, and ripe stone fruit, each passing moment spent with a lit cigar will seem like a lifetime of satisfaction. A top-15 for 2016, from the moment you first puff a RoMa Craft CroMagnon, your way of both tasting and thinking about cigars, will evolve. Even if your experience is previously limited to 'good' or 'bad' smokes, or even just 'happy' ones, in the future, you will marvel at the depth of available flavor buried within each of these 93-rated cigars and will find yourself standing at the dawn of a new era of enjoyment. If nothing else, you will find no better finale after a delicious meal of roasted mammoth.

Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua is the latest expansion of the premium cigar line. As the name implies, the Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua is a blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos, but this special collaboration with Plasencia Cigars includes tobaccos from the family’s own private reserves. The cigar is wrapped in a Connecticut seed leaf grown in Nicaragua and aged more than three years. Connecticut seed wrapper – originally from the rocky, rich soil of New England in the United States – is now harvested in other key cigar regions of the world, such as Ecuador and Honduras. Continuing to expand flavors and characteristics of their tobaccos, the Plasencia family began growing Connecticut seed tobaccos in Honduras and Nicaragua. Rafael Nodal, Head of Product Capability for Tabacalera USA, collaborated for almost two years with the Plasencia family in creating this cigar. “Getting to work with the Plasencia family on this cigar which uses a Connecticut seed wrapper grown in Nicaragua, is for me an honor. Having the opportunity to take the Romeo y Julieta consumer on a journey of discovering new flavors and new experiences, is a real privilege,” Nodal said. “This cigar is intriguing,” he explained. “It’s not a Connecticut cigar, nor is it a Nicaragua cigar. It is the first Connecticut-Nicaragua Cigar. And that makes for a big difference.” The Romeo Y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua will be available in four sizes. The cigar will be available in a Toro (52 x 6), Bully (50 x 5), Magnum (60 x 6) and Churchill (50 x 7). The price of the cigar will range from $7.20 to $8.35.

A premium cigar with a storybook ending. Romeo y Julieta 1875 – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Romeo y Julieta is an iconic cigar named after a literary favorite. The 1875 cigar’s beautiful Indonesian Shade Grown TBN wrapper surrounds a classic Dominican binder and a blend of Dominican long fillers that burn with a characteristic white ash, providing a smooth, mellow taste with medium body.

1875 by Romeo y Julieta is an all-new addition to the already world-famous Romeo y Julieta lineup of cigars. Not to be confused with the other 1875 cigars such as the Original line and Reserve line, 1875 by Romeo y Julieta is brand new, released in 2014 as a retailer exclusive, and blended from scratch using Dominican filler and binder tobaccos and a gorgeous Indonesian shade wrapper leaf. Like other cigars from the famous Flor de Copan factory, 1875 is always consistent in construction, flavor, and overall enjoyability. Perhaps made to mimic the classic Romeo y Julieta Cuban cigars, 1875 by Romeo y Julieta starts off with a spicy blast of white pepper, which stays with the smoke throughout the duration of the cigar. Along the way, a bouquet of earth and tobacco flavors coat the palate and are accompanied by hints of cocoa and leather. Medium to full-bodied, 1875 by Romeo y Julieta makes a great starter cigar for a beginner looking to get into premium cigars. In addition, experienced aficionados will appreciate the rich history of the brand and the all-new flavor profile. 1875 pairs nicely with bourbon and scotch, making it a wonderful after-dinner treat. Other cigars by the famed brand, such as the original 1875 line and the 1875 Reserve , are also worth trying, as they are what made Romeo y Julieta what it is today. Always catering to the most discriminating palates, Romeo y Julieta has hit another one out of the ballpark with 1875.

A Nicaraguan born Connecticut. Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua cigars are a groundbreaking project from Altadis U.S.A’s master blender Rafael Nodal that creatively combines premium Nicaraguan and Connecticut seed tobaccos. This is a Nicaraguan puro that uses the finest vintage binder and filler tobaccos grown on the famed Plasencia farms.

Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua is a unique cigar in that despite the fact that it uses a Connecticut wrapper, it is still considered a Nicaraguan puro. It is the result of a collaboration between Aging Room’s Rafael Nodal and legendary tobacco grower and blender Nestor Plasencia. This line is produced in the massive Plasencia Cigars S.A. factory in Nicaragua using all Nicaraguan leaves—filler, binder, and wrapper. The wrapper is the star of the show, however, and up until now has been nothing more than an experiment of sorts. It is a Nicaraguan Connecticut-seed leaf grown on Plasencia’s own farms that has been aged for more than 3 years. This cigar is not “quite” a Nicaraguan cigar, but not “quite” a Connecticut cigar, but rather a true “Connecticut Nicaraguan.” So how did it work out, you ask? The Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut blend has earned widespread acclaim, receiving multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado , including a high score of 92 . The packaging and branding is both classic and luxurious. Cream colored bands featuring gold and black lettering really add to the appeal of the line in question, and the construction of the cigar itself screams quality—just as one would expect from two of the best names in the business. The draw is just right, providing a superb amount of thick, white smoke from the very first puffs. The Romeo 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua starts off with a defined toasty note, soon turning to hay and cedar as the burn continues. Cream and white pepper become apparent very early off, sticking around until about the final third. A faint espresso note lingers in the background, and the retrohale is sweet and slightly spicy, yet unusually clean. This blend starts off quite mild, growing to a definitive medium-bodied cigar by the end. Tame, tasty, and suitable for all experience ranges, 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua proves to be quite the versatile package. Mild-medium-bodied, it boasts a flavor profile that is both intriguing and complex, yet at the same time everything you might expect from a Connecticut-wrapped stick. This cigar pairs nicely with sweet beverages such as Champagne or cognac, but a good mild-medium-bodied beer wouldn’t hurt, either. If you happen to be a fan of the legendary Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real or Plasencia Cosecha 146 , you could probably consider the cigar in question to be something of a halfway point between the two. For an unforgettable smoking experience that is both modern and classic in every way, look no further than Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua and taste the world’s first true Connecticut Nicaraguan cigar!

A robust Nicaraguan puro that exudes the classic complexity. Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 This incredible Romeo selection is a robust Nicaraguan puro that exudes the classic complexity of the original best-selling 1875 cigar. The Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua is dubbed with the bold and zesty hints of Nicaraguan tobaccos, which modern connoisseurs have come to appreciate. The cigars come handcrafted by Plasencia Cigars S.A., within their renowned Nicaraguan factory, showcasing a lush medley of sweet, spicy, and earthy Plasencia tobaccos. The Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua is adorned with vibrant orange bands, which perfectly complement the cigar’s refined medium-brown wrapper. Rich, robust and entirely satisfying, the Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua is a spicy treat with the strength to spare for any adult cigar enthusiast looking for a full-flavored cigar. With impeccable construction and unprecedented Plasencia-quality, this exquisite Nicaraguan puro promises to distinguish itself as a modern-day classic for all cigar connoisseurs; and introduces an exceptional profile of contemporary flavor to the myriad of Romeo y Julieta faithful across the globe.

Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua is the Nicaraguan counterpart to the original core cigar from Romeo y Julieta, the 1875. Slated for regular production, 1875 Nicaragua is the second of 2 cigars released in 2018 bearing the Romeo y Julieta name, the first being the Fernandez-made San Andres by Romeo y Julieta . In order to follow such a masterpiece, the folks at Altadis knew they had to go big or go home, so they turned to none other than the famed Plasencia family to take on this new project. Made at their immense factory in Nicaragua, Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua is rolled using all Nicaraguan leaves—filler, binder, and wrapper. The resulting Nicaraguan puro is a phenomenal concoction of flavor and complexity, with just enough power to keep things interesting. Once again, the Plasencias have hit a home run, and once again, Romeo y Julieta remains in the limelight. The Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua has solidified its reputation as a premier Nicaraguan puro by earning a distinguished 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado , a testament to its complex, spicy-sweet profile and impeccable construction. Orange, white, and gold bands clothe each cigar, a stark contrast to the red and gold bands worn by the original 1875. The packaging is a simple Cuban style dress box bearing the brand logo along with “1875 Nicaragua” underneath. Each masterfully constructed cigar offers an easy draw, plenty of rich smoke, and a sharp burn line. The simple, yet satisfying theme doesn’t stop at the packaging. The flavor profile is straightforward and no-nonsense, opening up with a hefty dose of Nicaraguan pepper and soon settling into a toasty, earthy array of raw tobacco and cedar. Woody, sweet, and just spicy enough to entertain the palate, 1875 Nicaragua is a solid full-bodied choice for those looking for a curiously satisfying smoking experience. While the heavier strength of the blend and the classic feel of the flavor profile would likely appeal mostly to seasoned connoisseurs, Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua can doubtless be enjoyed by a wide variety of cigar enthusiasts. In the case of those looking to make a substantial step into the realm of fuller-bodied cigars, this particular stick is ideal. Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua pairs well with bourbon or fuller-bodied beer and makes a great choice for just about any occasion. It would be easy to picture 1875 Nicaragua as a “go-to” cigar, as its versatility rivals that of such humidor mainstays as Rocky Patel Edge Corojo or even Padron . The good people at Altadis continue to impress cigar fanatics across the country with both innovative new cigars and modern takes on old classics, and Romeo y Julieta 1875 Nicaragua could be considered one of the most exciting releases to date!

The redux of Room101 Hit & Run will soon hit retail, with the new blend created by the dynamic duo of Matt Booth and Robert Caldwell. Matt Booth said, “I’m thrilled to bring another Room101 sub-brand back to life with this expression of Hit & Run. The brand was born of a collaborative seed between myself and Robert Caldwell. It’s about our creative process as much as it is about two-like minded psychopaths who’ve stuck together over the years. This cigar is the physical and combustible manifestation of an intergalactic connection which proves that an authentic friend and a good cigar can help more than you may imagine.” The blend is made with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and a blend of Nicaraguan C-98 and Pennsylvania filler with an added layer of Nicaraguan leaf. Matt Booth describes the experience as being “sophisticated with depth and transition,” and notes that it “blends power with balance.” He says Hit & Run “pairs well with your favorite memory of the DMV.” The line is crafted at William Ventura in Tamboril, DR, where four frontmarks have been made: Robusto (5” x 50); SRP per cigar $12.99 Toro (6” x 50); SPR per cigar $13.29 Gordo (6” x 60); SPR per cigar $14.39 Perfecto (5.12 x 60); SRP per cigar $16.99 The Robusto, Toro and Gordo come in 20-count boxes, while the Perfecto comes in a ten-count box. All Room101 Hit & Run packaging features colorful Room101 branding.

Quintessence is the fifth line within Ashton Cigars’ San Cristóbal brand and was preceded by the Revelation, Ovation, Elegancia and original San Cristóbal lines. (For legal reasons, the brand is marketed outside of the US as Paradiso.) Master blender José “Pepin” Garcia from Estelí, Nicaragua, has once again gone above and beyond and created a cigar that we consider the year’s best. Priced at USD $8.00 (EUR 7.40), it also earned our Best Buy rating. The Quintessence line includes four formats: Robusto, Epicure, Majestic and Belicoso. Tasting notes: This perfectly rolled cigar is impressive in its sweetish coffee taste and dried fruit. The fruity notes come into their own wonderfully in the silky smoke. The light peppery spice is stimulating. Medium+. #1 | San Cristóbal (Paradiso) Quintessence Robusto Size: 140 x 19,8 | 5 1/2 x 50 Origin: Nicaragua Wrapper: Ecuador Binder: Nicaragua Filler: Nicaragua Factory: My Father Cigars S.A. Release: 2016

San Cristobal Quintessence is the fourth regular production cigar in the ultra premium San Cristobal lineup from Ashton, following the original San Cristobal release, Elegancia, and Revelation. Blended by Don Pepin Garcia with more focus on flavor and balance, rather than raw strength like its predecessor, Quintessence is produced in the world famous My Father factory in Nicaragua. The wrapper leaf is a beautiful reddish brown Ecuadorian Habano and the filler and binder blend consists of premium Nicaraguan leaves from the Garcia family farms. Since its release in 2016, Quintessence has garnered numerous accolades including a pair on 92 ratings in Cigar aficionado and a spot on the 2018 Top 25 list. The packaging follows suit with the other San Cristobal releases, presented in a luxurious wooden chest and each vitola bearing the gorgeous San Cristobal parrot band. The pre-light aroma is pleasantly intoxicating, indicating a blend that is doubtless complex and robust. Solid construction means plentiful draw and razor sharp burn with minimal need for touch-ups. Thick clouds of silky blue smoke present a lovely introduction of cedar and bread notes, followed up promptly by a rich core of spicy Nicaraguan pepper. A main note of refined raw tobacco lingers throughout the experience, while hints of cinnamon and nutmeg are detected through the nose. The finish is sweet and clean, and the body of the cigar reaches medium-full by the second third, remaining there throughout the rest of the cigar. The flavor profile is impeccably fine-tuned and frankly out of place for a cigar at this price point. If the original San Cristobal blend was a high-powered muscle car, Quintessence would be comparable to the agile roadster driving circles around it. Complex and satisfying, it is truly a blend geared towards highly experienced connoisseurs. Like any high-end stick, Quintessence pairs wonderfully with single malt scotch or cognac-based drinks and is ideal for special occasions and celebrations. If you have found yourself fond of such cigars as Ashton ESG or Arturo Fuente Sungrown , Quintessence should be right up your alley. The dictionary defines Quintessence as "the most perfect or typical example of quality or class." How fitting that such a premier specimen of a cigar as this would bear such a name! If you want to experience one of the finest cigars Ashton has to offer, trying San Cristobal Quintessence isn't merely an option, it's a necessity!

Villiger Cigars announces that the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan will be presented in a special edition Lancero Especial size, at the 2018 IPCPR in Las Vegas this coming July. A cigar- years in the making, Heinrich Villiger and Master Blender Matias Maragoto felt that the best version of the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan had yet to be released. The new Lancero Especial size is described as providing a more intense smoking experience in both flavor and smoke. Only 500, 25 count boxes yearly will be produced for this special edition Lancero Especial vitola. The Villiger La Flor De Ynclan Lancero Especial is a 6 ¾ x 43 with an MSRP of $11.00 Chairman of the Board Heinrich Villiger said, “As I have stated in the past, the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan cigar has been an ongoing labor of love for us, and we feel that we have further refined the blend with the addition of the this special edition lancero vitola. “ About the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan: Diligently crafted by Heinrich Villiger and master blender Jose Matias Maragoto of ABAM Cigar Factory in the Dominican Republic, the Villiger La Flor De Ynlcan was a cigar 10 years in the making. Villiger Cigars produced a small batch of La Flor De Ynclan over a decade ago. Unsatisfied with the final result; the decision was made to cease production. The tobacco was set aside and aged, while Matias meticulously tweaked the amount of the Indonesian, Dominican, and Nicaraguan tobacco within its Ecuadorian wrapper. Present day, the La Flor De Ynclan is what both imagined it could be.

Artesano Del Tobacco is proud to announce that the Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill began shipping on July 2nd to all retailers who placed pre-orders during the 2026 PCA Trade Show. Following the success of the Viva La Vida Connecticut line, Artesano Del Tobacco is expanding the collection with a new 7 x 54 Churchill vitola. The addition of this size is especially meaningful, as it was developed in direct response to recommendations from the company’s valued retail partners and consumers.“Our clients have always played an important role in helping shape our brands,” said Billy Fakih, Gus Fakih, and Ivan of Artesano Del Tobacco. “We can’t wait for everyone to experience this new Churchill. It took a little longer to bring it to market because we wanted to give the tobacco all the time it needed to develop the flavor profile we envisioned. Working alongside our good friend AJ Fernandez in Estelí, Nicaragua, we created a Churchill that is exceptionally creamy, smooth, naturally sweet, and beautifully balanced. This blend performs incredibly well in this vitola, and we are extremely grateful to everyone who shared their feedback and encouraged us to add this size to the line.” Crafted at AJ Fernandez Cigars in Estelí, Nicaragua, the Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill features the same blend found throughout the Viva La Vida Connecticut portfolio. It is made with premium Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos wrapped in an aged Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Product Information * Vitola: Churchill * Size: 7 x 54 * Wrapper: Aged Ecuadorian Connecticut * Binder: Nicaraguan * Filler: Nicaraguan * Factory: AJ Fernandez, Estelí, Nicaragua * Packaging: White wooden boxes of 10 cigars * Suggested Retail Price: $16.00 per cigar

Viva La Vida by Artesano Del Tobacco has taken off since its debut, and the rave reviews never seem to stop coming. It’s no surprise, therefore, that AJ Fernandez and his team went forward with yet another incredible addition to the Viva La Vida family: Viva La Vida Connecticut. Rolled by the skilled hands at the world-renowned Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars, S.A. in Nicaragua, Viva La Vida Connecticut uses a hearty filler and binder blend of all-Nicaraguan tobacco from the Fernandez family farms. The wrapper is a golden-brown Connecticut seed leaf grown under cloudy shade in the volcanic soils of Ecuador, making this one just a bit lighter, but still flavorful enough to already have the cigar world going nuts. White and black boxes stash the precision-built stogies, each one wearing an elaborate pair of bands embossed with intricate artwork. Construction-wise, there is little to be desired. In typical AJ fashion, each stick offers maximum performance, which means billowing clouds of dense smoke from every puff. Creamy cedar and raw tobacco open things up, and are soon joined by notes of cinnamon, toast, and cayenne . A spicy core of heavily spiced earthy flavor holds the package together, and the finish is toasty and peppery. Not your typical Connecticut cigar, Viva La Vida Connecticut finishes as a flavorful medium-bodied cigar. Appropriate for smokers of all experience levels, Viva La Vida Connecticut offers a satisfying medium-bodied smoking experience that combines complexity with balance in such an amazing manner. It pairs well with your favorite scotch or medium-bodied beer, but also beautifully accompanies a hot cup of coffee. Fans of the original Viva La Vida should be sure to try this one for a change of pace, though we assure you, it’s by no means just another boring Connecticut stick. “Viva La Vida” means “Live The Life,” and we urge you to do so, especially when it comes to premium cigars. That being said, live your best cigar life with Viva La Vida Connecticut, and experience a Connecticut cigar that takes flavor to entirely new levels.

West Tamp Tobacco Company is excited to announce that Chef Rick has begun to ship and will be available both in the US and international markets. Like its predecessors Boliche Blvd. and Devil Crab, Chef Rick serves up a flavorful third course in West Tampa’s food inspired line. “A great culinary chef requires technical mastery, immense passion and creativity” said Rick Rodriguez of the inspiration behind this blend. “I also wanted to take the opportunity to partner with a young up and coming factory, Tabacalera Pages de Nicaragua S.A., to close out this trilogy. Having the opportunity to work along side Raymond Pages Raffo allowed me to bring something new and unique to my fans”, Rodriguez continued. West Tampa Tobacco Company’s Chef Rick will be a limited release of 1,000 boxes, available in one size and packed in a box containing 50 cigars: Toro (6X52)- $12.99 SRP(USD)

At InterTabac, Rick Rodriguez from West Tampa Tobacco introduced his new cigar, Circle of Life. Circle of Life is a story of everyone’s life. The cigar is a medium-strength cigar with a dark wrapper that has been aged for 18 months. An ideal cigar for after dinner. Now available in Robusto (5×52), Toro (6×54), and Gigante (6×60) formats, priced between €18 and €20. Produced at Casa Carrillo in Santiago, Dominican Republic, the cigar is intended to represent the tradition, present, and future of West Tampa. Another new release is the Devil Crab cigar. The cigar is available as a Figurado (4.5×60) and is manufactured by Garmendia Cigar Company in Estelí. West Tampa produces this cigar as a tribute to Tampa’s great cigar history and as a token of appreciation to all those who made this development in Tampa possible. The cigar, which can be enjoyed at any time of day, combines sweetness and delicate spiciness with up to an hour of smoking pleasure. From January 2026, the Figurado will be available at a price of €18 and, in addition to the 20-piece box, also in a 50-piece box.

A limited amount of boxes that have been kept for a decade exclusively for the Spanish market. Tabacalera releases exclusively for the Spanish market a limited batch of Montecristo Open Junior (format “trabuco” 4 1/3 x 38 – 110 mm x 38), that have been aged for ten years in their box. The cigars have been subjected to a decade-long aging in the company’s warehouses, which rounds off the flavor and nuances any edges. The presentation is the same as regular production tobacco, except that a gold sticker has been added to the face of the box, where those ten years of aging stand out. The price of the cigars in stores is 8.50 euros (170 euros for a box of 20), one euro above the regular Montecristo Open Junior.
같은 마르카/라인(Montecristo open) 형제 비톨라(Open Eagle, Open Master) 노트에서 추정. Habanos 정규 라인은 마르카별 단일 블렌드.

Tabacalera presents the new edition of Tauromaquia, exclusive for the Spanish market, which pays tribute to the legendary Sevillian bullfighter Juan Belmonte, also known as “El pasmo de Triana”, one of the greatest bullfighters in history. Tauromaquia y Juan Belmonte gives us another opportunity to explore the historical relationship between habanos and bullfighting. Previously, in 2019, the first edition of Tauromaquia was dedicated to Morante de la Puebla and Montecristo Double Edmundo, while in 2020 the protagonists of the second edition were Joselito el Gallo and Partagás Serie P No.2. The brand and vitola chosen for this third edition is Romeo y Julieta Wide Churchills (55 ring gauge x 130 mm long). These cigars have gone through a delicate aging process of at least 5 years, thanks to which the wrappers get slightly darker, smoother and silkier, the flavour settles, and the aroma, strength and body reach a perfect balance. This special edition consists of 1,000 numbered boxes. On the lacquered wooden lid of each box stands out an evocative illustration of the bullfighter. It is available only in Spanish tobacconists at a price of 20 euros/cigar and 200 euros/box of 10 cigars. Info: Romeo y Julieta Wide Churchills, Vitola de galera: Montesco, ring guage 55 (21,83 mm) x 130 mm
같은 마르카/라인(Romeo y Julieta core) 형제 비톨라(Julieta, Exhibición No.4, Belicosos, Cedros de Luxe No.2) 노트에서 추정. Habanos 정규 라인은 마르카별 단일 블렌드.

The XXV Festival del Habano began with a spectacular opening night. The event celebrated the 150th anniversary of Romeo y Julieta. The exclusive Salón de Protocolo Cubanacán hosted 1,200 guests. Distributors, experts and enthusiasts from all over the world were in attendance. The theme of the evening was Venice, with a romantic atmosphere. The colour red dominated, reflecting the passion of the brand. The new Amantes vitola has a ring gauge of 53 and a length of 153 mm. It was specially designed for the 150th anniversary. The vitola combines tradition with excellent craftsmanship. It offers medium strength and the classic Romeo y Julieta aroma. It is ideal for experienced passionados and newcomers alike. Vice President Jorge Pérez Martel presented two formats: the elegant box of 20 is ideal for collectors and enthusiasts, and an exclusive gift box of 5 was offered in advance to festival guests. The gift box will be available in Switzerland at La Casa del Habano on 17 February 2026 and at Habanos Specialist on 24 February 2026. Romeo y Julieta Amantes – Gift Box with 5 cigars will retail at 372.- Swiss Francs, representing 74.40 Swiss Francs per cigar.

A twist to the well-known story of excellent, smoother cigars. The passion burns within, now brighter than ever. ROMEO by Romeo y Julieta – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Romeo by Romeo y Julieta is a bold and robust cigar unlike any Romeo y Julieta to come before it. Made with the rarest and finest tobaccos carefully selected and delicately aged, Romeo cigars are meticulously crafted by a special team of the most accomplished artisans at the famed Tabacalera de García factory. The select Dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper is handpicked for its dark, rich color and robust taste. The slightly mellow Dominican Piloto binder works harmoniously with the bold wrapper, and the unique filler blend of Dominican Piloto and Olor tobaccos completes this wonderfully complex full-bodied cigar that culminates in an unforgettable smoking experience.

Le Hoyo de San Luis joins the prestigious Le Hoyo Series, celebrated for its aromatic finesse and exeptional craftmanship-hallmarks of the Hoyo de Monterrey brand. Meticulously « Totally Handmade with Long Filler », this new vitola delivers a balanced and smooth smoking experience, featuring leaves exclusively sourced from San Luis, epicenter of tobacco culture in Vuelta Abajo, Pinard el Rio, Cuba. The launch took place on 12 November 2025, during an exclusive dinner show at the famous Alexander Kunz Theatre in Thunstetten, one of Germany`s most exceptional cultural and gastronomic experiences. Presented in boxes of 10, the Le Hoyo de San Luis (Ø52x 160 mm) promises a long and elegant smoking experience, with every draw revealing the refined balance and nuanced character of Hoyo de Monterrey. In Switzerland, they will be available from 21 st of April 2026 at La Casa del Habano stores and from 28th of April 2026 at Habanos Specialist. Le Hoyo de San Luis SLB: 29.03 Swiss Francs per cigar.
같은 마르카/라인(Hoyo de Monterrey lehoyo) 형제 비톨라(Le Hoyo de San Juan, Le Hoyo de Río Seco) 노트에서 추정. Habanos 정규 라인은 마르카별 단일 블렌드.

A new wooden humidor box with five H. Upmann Magnum 54 cigars is now available in Spanish tobacconists’ shops, standing out as an ideal gift for any Habanos passionado. The Magnum 54 is one of the most emblematic vitolas of the H. Upmann brand. It is a 120 mm long, 54 ring gauge and mild-medium strength vitola. For the final stretch of 2024, this cigar arrives in a special presentation: a new wooden case with a humidifier bearing the brand’s insignia and containing five cigars, already available only in Spanish tobacconists at a price of €120. This is certainly a very interesting idea for those who want to give Habanos as a gift during the upcoming Christmas season, or on any other occasion. H. Upmann is one of the oldest and most prestigious Habanos brands, founded in 1844 by Herman Upmann, a German banker who was also a great lover of Cuban tobacco. The brand is known for its exceptional quality in crafting cigars of mild-medium strength.

Punch Cigars is honoring its iconic (and “devastatingly handsome”) mascot, Mr. Punch, with a new cigar that bears his name. Mr. Punch by Punch Cigars is a full-time blend that delivers a signature Punch smoking experience with a flavor profile tailored to the modern smoker. Mr. Punch by Punch features an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, a Nicaraguan Jalapa Seco binder, and fillers from Nicaragua. The cigar was produced at the Scandinavian Tobacco Group Factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. Mr. Punch by Punch is available in three sizes: Toro (6 X 54), Gigante (6 X 60), and the largest Punch Cigar ever released, The Big Slapper (7 X 70). SRPs (suggested retail price) for the respective cigars are $7.89, $8.99, and $10.09. Each size is packaged in boxes of 20. Scott Abney, Brand Manager for Punch Cigars, said, “Mr. Punch is a true icon not just in the cigar industry, but in pop culture. So it only made sense to create a cigar that captures his spirit. This new blend delivers a classic Punch smoking experience with a flavor profile tailored to the modern consumer. We know it’s going to be a hit.” Mr. Punch by Punch is a full-time release. It will begin shipping to retailers in July 2026.

After Romeo y Julieta ” Club Kings “, Partagas ” Capitols “, H.Upmann ” Regalias ” and Hoyo de Monterrey ” Souvenir de Luxe “, the Punch brand has also received a Retro Line Habanos edition with the ” Triunfos “. The Petit Corona format has a length of 129 mm and a ring gauge of 42. The tobacco blend comes from the Pinar del Río /Vuelta Abajo region and scores points with its leaf selection. The “Souvenir de Luxe” is rolled into a soft cigar with a light, fruity and honey-like taste. The light taste of its blend is an attractive alternative for those who like a light, tasty and aromatic Habano with elegance and complexity. Suitable as a permanent guest. The Punch “Triunfos” is offered in a color-coordinated aluminum box in retro design with 5 cigars. They will be available from 05.03.2024 in the Swiss Casa del Habano and from 12.03.2024 in Habanos Specialist stores. Punch Triunfos, tin of 5 cigars, has a RSP of CHF 80.-

Serie Sevilla is the name of a collection, exclusive to the Spanish market, of Habanos cigars presented in English earthenware jars. The jars, made by “La Cartuja de Sevilla”, are a replica of those made by the same firm in the middle of the last century for the Partagás and Ramón Allones brands, which are now genuine museum pieces. The first edition of Serie Sevilla, produced in 2016, featured Montecristo No.3, followed in 2017 by Hoyo de Monterrey Epicure Especial, H. Upmann Magnum 50 in 2018, Partagás Serie P No.2 in 2019, Romeo y Julieta Short Churchills in 2020 and Ramón Allones Allones Specially Selected in 2021. This 7 th edition consists of 1,000 numbered pieces. Each of them contains 21 Únicos, the brand’s Pirámides (156 mm in length and 52 filler), entirely hand-rolled and preserved in the best conditions. It is priced at €25 per cigar and €525 per box.

Launched in 1996, Vegueros was born to pay homage to all the Cuban farmers who, from generation to generation, have grown tobacco in Pinar del Río*. The place where the Vegueros brand is made today is the Rolling Tobacco Factory “Francisco Donatien,” a solid building in Pinar del Río* built in 1868 and which became a tobacco factory in 1961. The brand, which completely renewed itself more than fifteen years after its creation by adding innovative formats to its portfolio, now enriches the range with the CentroGordos vitola (54 ring gauge x 100 mm length), an attractive option for those looking for a Habano with a medium to strong flavor, accessible and renewed. Vegueros CentroGordos is presented with the new brand image and in a 16-unit metal can. It is a trendy format, much appreciated by smokers these days and will be accessible to a broader spectrum of smokers. All the Habanos of this brand are made “Totalmente a mano con tripa larga” – Totally Handmade with Long Filler -, with a medium to full flavour. Vegueros Centrogordos will be available in Switzerland on the 24 th of October 2023 in the Casa del Habano and on the 31 st in the Habanos Specialist stores. The box of Vegueros Centrogordo of 16 cigars is proposed to a RSP of 142.40 Swiss Francs.
같은 마르카/라인(Vegueros core) 형제 비톨라(Entretiempos, Tapados, Centrofinos) 노트에서 추정. Habanos 정규 라인은 마르카별 단일 블렌드.

The 601 Habano Oscuro Green Label cigar is intact despite circumstances that would make it difficult for anything to survive. First launched under the EO Cigars company owned by Erik Espinosa and Eddie Ortega, it remained an important part of the portfolio even as EO was partially bought out by Rocky Patel, primarily for distribution and packaging reasons, so fortunately the blend stayed the same. Now, Erik Espinosa has started his own company, not surprisingly named Espinosa Cigars, and in addition to new blends he is developing ( La Zona, etc) he has also brought with him some of the original players that made EO a hit, and the Nicaraguan Puro, that is, the '601 Green' is a star among stars.

It may seem like a relic from another era, but the 601 Habano Red Label cigar is still in production and seeking to recapture its former glory. Birthed during those early, heady days at EO Cigars, when Erick Espinosa and Eddie Ortega could do no wrong, all of the cigars created by the pair were in trouble of going extinct when the two parted ways. Fortunately for everyone, those two men were practical realists, so instead of holding grudges they divvied up their holdings and wished each other well. For his part, Espinosa retained the 601 line, among others, and so this Habano-wrapped Nicaraguan dude still abides.

After the success of cigars like 601, Mi Barrio, and Murcielago, many wondered what the future would hold for EO Brands. In early 2011, Eddie Ortega (the O in EO) announced plans for a new powerhouse cigar named, "La Bomba." While La Bomba debuted in late spring/early summer, early demand far exceeded supply and La Bomba has been difficult to get a hold of. Offered in four sizes, all with unique pigtails that look like wicks of dynamite, the 601 La Bomba is made at Jaime García's My Father Cigars factory in Estelí, Nicaragua.

Sweet chocolate, oranges, earthiness and some creaminess are the first flavors that hit the palate, with the citrus—orange and lemons—continuing into the finish. I was expecting the draw to change once the cigar got going and the covered foot was turned into ash, but it doesn’t change much at all. Milk chocolate and dry crackers are the two most obvious notes, but there’s a long list of secondary flavors including bitter creaminess, leather, newspaper, white pepper, herbal flavors and some mustiness that reminds me of new carpet. The finish has a lot of dry crackers over a mustiness that makes me think of Dominican olor tobaccos, followed by white pepper, pink salt and some lime. Retrohales have a donut-like pastry flavor over creaminess, along with a short-lived acidity and some citrus. On some puffs, the citrus seems to supercharge the acidity, which makes it stronger than the donut flavor. The acidity picks up during the finish though a muted nutty flavor is the strongest singular flavor. Other flavors include sawdust and black pepper, though the acidity is the strongest sensation. Flavor is medium-full or full depending on the cigar, body is medium-plus and strength is medium-plus. For the most part, construction is good, though one cigar has a tight draw. While it doesn’t happen in the same place of each cigar, the mustiness removes itself from the fray, taking the newspaper and some of the carpet-like flavors along with it. There are some puffs where the lack of mustiness allows for the other flavors to really shine, but a toastiness emerges and begins to overwhelm those other flavors. Leather, bread, black pepper and sesame seed combine into a very compact profile with little separation between them. The deeper I puff, the better the flavors are as the shorter puffs can have an added bitterness and some metallic flavors. I find a hot dog bun-like bread flavor during the finish, joined by leather and acidity. Retrohales have a great creamy bread flavor along with some peculiar flavors like burning rubber or paper. The finish has cinnamon, even more of the creamy bread flavor, peanut shells and black pepper. If I take a dry swallow shortly after a retrohale

note_sources.text: The first puffs of the first ADVentura Blackfin’s Parlay Robusto cause me to do a bit of a double-take, as they have a chalky and slightly mineral flavor that doesn’t sit well on my palate. The second cigar starts on a heartier, earthier note; not full-on robust but leaning that direction, while some chewy wheat bread softens the flavor. The third cigar is the best of the three, rounding off the rougher edges while keeping the wood, nuttiness, black pepper, a bit of toast and some of that dry Cheerios flavor. Retrohales are consistently peppery, starting bright before mellowing out a bit while also thickening up. Flavor is medium-plus, body is medium and strength is mild. Construction is very good, though there’s something about the second cigar that seems amiss; more on that in the notes. At the start of the second third, some creaminess takes the reins, but there’s still plenty of accents from wood, nuttiness and a light, black pepper. There continues to be a bit of an edge to the flavor, and at this point, it manifests on the finish more than anywhere else, a sensation more prominent on the first and second cigars. The profile begins to put the flavors on a bit of a carousel, keeping the intensity the same but rotating which flavor is in the lead role and moving others to the background for a bit. I get the start of a slightly funky flavor on the center of my tongue toward the end of this section, a sensation that harkens back to the start of the first cigar. Flavor is medium-plus, body is medium and strength is medium-minus. Construction remains very good, and I have no issues with the draw, burn line, or smoke production. The final third starts off without much of a change from the second third, a generally smooth transition that I have to be mindful of, otherwise I would just keep smoking without even noticing where the burn line is. There’s a touch less creaminess, as the flavor that falls back and becomes one of several contributors, along with more dry wood, black pepper, mixed nuts, and now a little bit of light earthiness, the latter of which feels like a new spin on an earlier component. The AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Connecticut Tubo opens with a light, tongue-tingling pepper and a fairly hearty, chewy base note that reminds me a bit of a pretzel bun, with a touch of creaminess in the mix as well. There are touches of earthiness at times, along with a little peppery heat that appears only in the third cigar, but I wouldn’t classify either as a core component. Retrohales have a very enjoyable and long-tailed black pepper, sticking around and tingling my nostrils for a few seconds after the smoke passes through my nose. I appreciate how dialed in the flavor seems, not trying to do too much, keeping its components balanced, and delivering a smooth and enjoyable flavor. That flavor rates around medium-plus in intensity, while the body of the smoke is also medium-plus, and nicotine strength is mild. Construction is very good, with the draws smooth, the smoke plentiful, and the burn lines even. The second third starts with a little more edge to the flavor, as the creaminess has largely departed, and something about the pepper has changed to give the profile a bit more character. Retrohales see the same change, and in the third cigar, I get a bit of eye irritation from the smoke. The creaminess returns ahead of the midway point, this time with some dry wood accents, giving the cigar some serious complexity. The cigar continues toying with the intensity of the pepper, and the first cigar has me jot down the word aggressive,  something I don’t think about the other two quite as much, but it definitely has some more character than earlier, making for an interesting contrast with the otherwise smooth and complex flavors. Flavor alternates between medium-plus and medium-full, body is medium-plus, and strength is medium-minus. Construction remains very good, and I don’t find any notable issues. The final third of the AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Connecticut Tubo shuffles the flavors a little bit, starting with a combination of creaminess and peanut shells, followed by a really enjoyable, rich earthiness that isn’t too heavy for the blend, with some black pepper sprinkled in and leading the finish. note_sources.text: Those two new vitolas in the AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Maduro were a 5 3/8 x 48 Short Churchill and a 6 x 54 Toro, limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 and 1,500 boxes of 10, respectively. While both new sizes shipped to retailers in November 2021 , the Toro was offered exclusively to retailers who attended the 2021 PCA Convention & Trade Show , while the Short Churchill was sold only to AGANORSA Leaf Select Accounts. “The Aniversario Maduro blend was a massive hit last year and there was great demand for this cigar to return to the market,” said Terence Reilly, vp of sales and marketing for AGANORSA Leaf, in a press release . “We also updated the packaging to make it clear this is an AGANORSA blend when consumers see it in the humidor.” As with the rest of the AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Maduro line, the Toro incorporates a blend that includes a Nicaraguan shade-grown maduro wrapper covering Nicaraguan tobacco used in both the binder and filler. It had an MSRP of $13.75 per cigar and was rolled at AGANORSA’s Leaf small factory in its Miami headquarters. Here is what I said about the AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Maduro Toro in my original review back in February 2022 : While the AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Maduro Toro starts out with an aggressive spice, pepper and earth combination, it was never overwhelming enough to push out the other main flavors in the profile, a list that includes cashews, charred meat and oak. In addition, there were some very interesting additional parts of the profile, including some distinct vanilla bean sweetness—which gets more distinct as the cigar burns down—and a green pepper note on the finish in the final two-thirds. In the end, the AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Maduro Toro is an impressive addition to the company’s portfolio: strong yet smooth, well-balanced and quite well-constructed. Last year, AGANORSA Leaf announced that it was making the Aniversario Maduro a regular production line with three new vitolas, one of which is a Toro. The regular production version is 6 1/4 x 52, while the limited edition 2021 vitola was 6 x 54. As was the case with the cigars I smoked for my first review, it is hard to discern much about the AGANORSA Leaf Anivers
note_sources.title: AGANORSA Leaf Aniversario Maduro Toro (2021)

note_sources.text: Every major cigar manufacturer has cigars that just seem to stand out as the “special” ones. For the Fernandez family and their famed Aganorsa brand, one such cigar is the Aganorsa Leaf Buena Cosecha Corojo . Rolled at the family’s TABSA factory in Nicaragua , this flavorful treat is a true Nicaraguan puro , blended entirely with Nicaraguan tobacco grown on the famed Aganorsa farms —wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler contains Criollo ‘98 , the binder is Corojo ‘99 , and the finishing touch is the beautiful, red-hued Nicaraguan Corojo ‘99 wrapper leaf —one that has been extensively aged and offers rich, classic Nicaraguan flavor. “Buena Cosecha” literally translates to “Good Harvest,” and we can fully attest to the fact that whatever harvest this tobacco came from is very good indeed. Cedar chests give this blend a classic, traditional feel, while the updated, gold-accented maroon band hugging each stick reminds us how far Aganorsa Leaf has come as a brand. A luxuriously smooth draw produces no shortage of silky smoke, and the flavor is immense from the first puff. Red pepper, heavy on the spice, is the first big slap in the face. This soon smooths out as the earthy core of rich Nicaraguan tobacco comes to the forefront. Hints of cinnamon, nutmeg, and cocoa emerge along the way, and the finish is heavy and sweet. Ending up on the heavy end of medium-bodied , Buena Cosecha Corojo is a classic Fernandez stick that still pulls its weight today. Made for fans of rich and spicy cigars , Buena Cosecha Corojo should appeal to experienced enthusiasts and intermediates alike. It is a fabulous blend of flavor, strength, and complexity—all without a hefty price tag. This one pairs well with medium-to-full-bodied beer, coffee , or dark rum , offering enjoyment at any time of the day. Fans of traditional Nicaraguan Corojo cigars , such as Don Pepin Blue Label or Gran Habano Corojo , should certainly make a point of giving this one a try, as hefty spice and a blend of sweet and savory flavors are a common theme with cigars of this nature. Whether or not you are already a fan of Aganorsa Leaf and their exciting, decorated journey, the Aganorsa Leaf Buena Cosecha Corojo is a Nicaraguan puro you won't want to miss.

By now, most serious cigar enthusiasts have at least heard of AGANORSA Leaf , but it is almost a sure thing that if you have been enjoying premium cigars for even a short period of time, you have probably tasted the famed AGANORSA Leaf tobacco. Once strictly a tobacco supplier for other top names in the industry, AGANORSA Leaf began production of their own cigars in the mid-2000s. Though the name of their first big hit has changed a couple of times over the years, the blend hasn’t, and the 91-rated enigma still satisfies a great many connoisseurs across the globe. That enigma is the AGANORSA Leaf Signature Selection Corojo . Part of the original Signature Series, this incredible blend takes things back to the company’s Nicaraguan roots, from which head honcho Eduardo Fernandez emigrated from Cuba in the late 1990s. A classic Nicaraguan puro, this blend is all-Nicaraguan—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler blend contains both Corojo ‘99 and Criollo ‘98 leaves, along with a dose of rare Nicaraguan Medio Tiempo for extra power. The wrapper leaf is a red-hued Corojo ‘99 grown on the AGANORSA farms in Nicaragua, and all production of this intense blend takes place at Fernandez’s own TABSA factory in Nicaragua, also known as Tabacos Valle de Jalapa, S.A. Freshly updated packaging includes clean, decorated cedar boxes adorned with the AGANORSA Leaf arm logo, this time in red and gold. Red and gold bands clothe each vitola, along with a foiled tissue wrap covering most of the cigar’s body. The construction is immaculate, and each cigar performs beautifully. Dense clouds of smoke coat the palate with rich, robust flavor, at first starting off with a burst of spicy white pepper . This soon settles into a flavorful melody of baking spices, cocoa, and nuts, with a lingering cedar note in the background. Powerful, earthy tobacco flavor sits at the core, and the finish is crisp and spicy. Medium-full-bodied , complex, and balanced, Signature Selection Corojo certainly lives up to both its name and heritage. Made for the most experienced and discerning connoisseurs, AGANORSA Leaf Signature Selection Corojo is a modern classic that deserves to be enjoyed respectfully and properly. Medium-full in strength, this complex masterpiece pairs exceptionally well with a glass of your favorite scotch or dark rum. Coffee, full-bodied beer, and red wine all make fine accompaniments as well. Fans of blends such as Guardian of the Farm or the massive JFR Lunatic will surely come to enjoy this one, not only because they all sport similar tobacco from the same farm, but because the robust flavor profiles, though unique, tend to share the same DNA. Taste a true Nicaraguan puro with a rich history, and enjoy one of the finest all-Nicaraguan blends on today’s market with the AGANORSA Leaf Signature Selection Corojo.

Aganorsa Signature Selection Maduro is by no means your typical maduro cigar. Part of the first series ever released under the Aganorsa Leaf name, the Signature Series; Signature Selection Maduro is made by the skilled hands at Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. in Nicaragua, also known as TABSA. A true Nicaraguan puro , this stick, like the others in the Signature Series, is made entirely of tobacco grown on Aganorsa’s own farms. As a puro, the blend consists of all-Nicaraguan tobacco, wrapper, filler, and binder, with the wrapper leaf being a gorgeous shade-grown Corojo ‘99 Maduro . Rich, flavorful, and beautifully balanced, this rare maduro cigar is sure to intrigue even the pickiest cigar snob. With newly updated white and gold boxes and black and gold bands, the Signature Series Maduro now certainly looks more like a top-notch premium cigar should. A body-length gold tissue wrap and elegant foot band finish off the look, but even without any of the above, it would be easy to tell how incredible a cigar this is. The construction leaves nothing to desire, and the draw is spot-on every time. An ongoing rush of silky blue smoke offers a complex flavor profile of cedar and nuts to start things off, of course backed by a solid base of white pepper . As things progress, more familiar maduro flavors of dark chocolate and espresso form the core of the flavor profile. Sweet brown sugar, cinnamon, and black cherry are background notes, and the finish is dark and spicy. Medium-full-bodied , this rich blend is undeniably satisfying from all angles. Made for more experienced maduro fans, Signature Selection Maduro is a blend that steps outside the usual box of classic maduro flavor. Medium-full-bodied and delicately complex, it pairs well with coffee or dark beer and is great for just about any time of the day. Fans of the original Aganorsa Leaf Maduro will surely come to enjoy this one but be ready for just a bit more kick. It isn’t every day that you come across a Nicaraguan puro that wears a maduro wrapper. With Aganorsa Signature Selection Maduro, bold Nicaraguan flavor meets the dark and delicious Maduro flavor profile we have all come to know and love.

Smooth and creamy are the name of the game when it comes to the Aging Room Core Connecticut cigar. An integral part of Rafael Nodal's vast stable of scrumptious cigars, his three Core varieties form the foundation of a boutique brand that's pure in quality and taste from top to bottom. With a silky golden Ecuadorian shade wrapper overlaid onto a rich, complex blend of Dominican tobaccos, the Aging Room Connecticut is the mildest of the bunch even as it possesses a wealth of delicious flavor you'll be reaching for morning, noon, and night.

You should understand by now that the search for your holy grail cigar is a never-ending quest, but that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t stop and just enjoy the journey with a mouthwatering smoke like the Aging Room Core Habano Mezzo. Crafted of the finest aged longleaf from the Dominican Republic, including the nut-brown Habano wrapper, there’s plenty of exciting character to be discovered along every inch of these luminous 6” x 54 vitolas. Creator Rafael Nodal has created a roadmap for the palate with three Core varieties and the medium-plus-strength Habano is arguably the best path to follow first for smokers of all dispositions.

Freshly overhauled and ready to deliver even more robust flavor than ever before, the Aging Room Core Maduro is about to become a necessary addition to your humidor. Whether or not you are already familiar with brand founder Rafael Nodal's various renowned Aging Room frontmarks, they're once again getting ready to rocket to the top and you'll want to be along for the ride. Fueled by a high-octane blend of Dominican longleaf as filler and binder beneath a dark, sticky-sweet San Andres wrapper, these medium-full strength stogies will carry you and your palate to new heights of flavor and satisfaction.

The Aging Room La Boheme features a Nicaraguan binder and filler, along with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Under AJ Fernandez’s care, the leaf found sa Aging Room La Boheme – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The Aging Room La Boheme features a Nicaraguan binder and filler, along with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Under AJ Fernandez’s care, the leaf found sanctuary in Nicaragua’s fertile soil, mingling with select tobaccos, each nurtured by time’s tender touch. Crafted in the renowned Aging Room by the esteemed Rafael Nodal, the Aging Room La Boheme revives a cigar with a distinguished history. This cigar honors the remarkable journey from a 15-year-old Cuban immigrant to a master cigar blender, featuring a distinctive Nicaraguan filler and binder, enveloped in a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Each draw reveals a story— robust notes of espresso and cocoa interwoven with subtle florals, complemented by hints of vanilla and almond that gently caress the palate.

Indubitably, Aging Room Cigars has become a household name to cigar connoisseurs in recent years, and in 2018, the company unveiled Small Batch Pura Cepa, the second Nicaraguan puro to bear the Aging Room name. Unlike the vast majority of Aging Room cigars that are native to the Dominican Republic, Small Batch Pura Cepa is hand crafted in Nicaragua. Even more interestingly, the chosen birthplace of this particular puro by brand owner Rafael Nodal is none other than the revered Plasencia factory, overseen by Nestor Plasencia himself. Utilizing Nicaraguan tobacco for all three components, Pura Cepa includes top grade leaves from all 4 major growing regions of Nicaragua: Condega, Esteli, Jalapa, and Ometepe. Pura Cepa is built for serious cigar enthusiasts, and has taken off with quite a bang, earning a solid 90 rating in Cigar Aficionado soon after its debut. Aging Room Small Batch Pura Cepa is a gorgeous specimen. Oily and veiny, the texture resembles high grade Cuban cigars, yet the construction is nothing short of incredible. Pura Cepa burns slow and crisp, draws easy, and holds a solid, chunky ash. Beginning with spicy Nicaraguan white pepper, and lots of it, Pura Cepa is built around a solid core of raw tobacco flavor. Cedar is strong in the background, along with a subtle bread note and definitive meatiness. Spice is strong on the retrohale, along with a toasty, clean finish. Earthy and robust, Pura Cepa boasts all the characteristics to be expected from a top shelf Nicaraguan cigar. Pura Cepa is undeniably full-bodied, yet smooth, complex, and balanced through and through. The Aging Room lineup is made for aficionados. Every single offering is built for the most discriminating cigar lovers with the most sophisticated tastes. Pura Cepa is no different, constructed to compete with some of the greatest cigars on the market today. Small Batch Pura Cepa pairs well with bourbon, full-bodied beer, or port wine, and makes a great way to celebrate any special occasion. If you haven't tried some of the other masterpieces offered by Aging Room, we can sincerely recommend such sticks as Quattro or Aging Room Maduro in addition to this particular stogie. "Pura Cepa" translates as "Pure Bred," no doubt a play on words referring to its nature of being a Nicaraguan Puro. When Nestor Plasencia produces a cigar for Aging Room, good things are doubtless going to happen. If you are on the lookout for your next "special" cigar, look no further than Aging Room Small Batch Pura Cepa.

If you are in search of a premium cigar that is both mild and wild at the same time, you need Aging Room Quattro Connecticut in your life. After converting the famous F55 line into what is now the Quattro series, Rafael Nodal pleased Connecticut fans the world over when he decided to team up with the same folks that brought you Montecristo and Romeo y Julieta to come up with Quattro Connecticut. The core blend is Dominican filler and binder tobaccos and the wrapper is a sleek, top-grade Ecuadorian Connecticut. With precision blending expertise, Nodal and friends were able to concoct a stick that combines flavor and mellow body in beautiful harmony.
Chocolate , Nuts , Spice , Espresso Available. Learn about Aging Room Quattro Maduro Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Quattro Maduro

Aging Room has become a household name in recent years to those who love premium cigars, and though the recent special releases have been hogging all the attention as of late, the core brands such as Aging Room Quattro Maduro are truly what the legacy has been built on. Made in the Dominican Republic, Aging Room Quattro Maduro was second to be released after its 95-rated Natural counterpart. For this blend, Rafael Nodal and Jochy Blanco took their game to the next level, incorporating a gorgeous Mexican San Andres wrapper leaf into the already mouthwatering mixture of Dominican Habano filler and binder tobaccos. The result is a maduro lover’s dream come true, and a stick that quickly earned a rock-solid 90-rating right out of the gate. In fact, this cigar has become one of the best-selling sticks to bear the Aging Room name.
Coffee , Cedar , Sweetness Available. Learn about Aging Room Quattro Original Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Quattro Original

If you say the name of the latest Aging Room cigar around acquaintances, don't be surprised if they think you are bragging about some new Italian sports car, the Quattro Original. But while you can't drive this cigar down the highway, it will drive you crazy with flavor and at a much more palatable price. Aging Room cigars are by design very limited productions, blends that found favor with the Oliveros cigar company that just couldn't be turned into full releases due to tobacco shortages. For the Quattro Original, the bottleneck is the small batch of Sumatra used for the wrapper, a once-in-a-lifetime find from a closed cigar factory and used exclusively to cover the Dominican filler and binder of the Quattro Original.

note_sources.text: The Días de Gloria Brazil Toro starts with plumes of smoke, a creamy undertone in the flavor, and then an explosion of pepper and spice on retrohales that takes the leading role in the experience. One cigar reminds me of a packet of red chili pepper flakes that I put on a slice of pizza the other day in how it adds the same topline sensation and one cigar gets to be a bit too much for me to truly enjoy. Creaminess increases in the flavor, and while I find myself drawn to retrohales, I intentionally skip them to get a better feel for the flavor, and I’m surprised by how mild it is given the liveliness of retrohales. There is some building flavor as the first third progresses, some puffs have more of an earthy aspect, others have more of a cardboard sensation, while touches of black pepper are consistent. But if I had to put a ratio to what’s driving the experience in the first third of the first cigar, I’d say 80 percent is the retrohale and 20 percent is the flavor on my taste buds. If retrohaling and counting that as part of the flavor, there is no doubt this is a full-flavored first third. Without retrohales, it’s more medium in flavor. Body is medium and strength is medium-minus. The cigar flies through the first third with a smooth draw, creating puffs that push the burn line evenly up the cigar’s body. Smoke production remains very good. The second third keeps the retrohales lively and vibrant, though maybe a tick less intense than they were at the start of the cigar. The flavor stays fairly mild, though the creaminess is building in flavor and thickening in texture as the Días de Gloria Brazil Toro progresses, with those same supporting notes that taste like earthiness and almond. Around the midway point, the retrohales become a bit more concentrated and not as much like fireworks in my nostrils in the sense of hitting seemingly every receptor they can find and instead hitting with more of a blunt punch. There’s still more evolution of the creaminess on my taste buds, and I’m enjoying how it has turned into a melted vanilla ice cream sensation, both for its flavor and for how it serves as a counterbalance to the spiciness. note_sources.text: The first puffs have more pepper than I would have been led to believe based on the aroma and cold draw, yet it’s not overbearing with pepper out of the gate. Dry earth is the main backing flavor, then a bit of wheat bread, with some hints of creaminess developing in the first inch. There’s also a rather long, pepper-driven finish that is aimed squarely at the top of my throat. As the first third progresses, the cigar gets toasty, with a bit more wood in the equation and the emergence of some of those cereal notes, but they get overshadowed by the pepper. Retrohales have a nostril-opening amount of pepper to them; were I feeling congested, this would seemingly be as effective of a remedy as anything I’d have on hand. A bit of heat tags along with the pepper, the combination lingers clearly on the palate as this section finishes. One sample has a slightly sour finish, but it’s fairly minor and only appears one time. Flavor sits between medium and full in the first third, body is medium-plus and strength is mild thus far. Construction is very good in all categories and in all three cigars. Creaminess and pepper start the second third of the New World Dorado Corona, with a custard-like first impression that quickly turns peppery while the smoke is in my mouth and then on the exhale and retrohale. While I enjoy the pepper in the profile, the finish is a bit less enjoyable as that pepper is quite focused on a single spot at the top of my throat, almost like it’s boring into it with some heat. It isn’t as noticeable in the first cigar, but in the other two, it becomes notable and almost expected, as it is one of a handful of consistent experiences across the three cigars. The pepper in one cigar becomes particularly strong, almost as if a higher priming of tobacco found its way into the blend, and it intensifies both puffs and retrohales. By the midway point, the creaminess is out of the lead flavors, now more of an accent to an increasingly robust and earthy core profile, and that change sticks around for the rest of this section. It also takes the flavor up to medium-full, while the body of the smoke sits closer to medium, while strength is now closer to medium. Con
note_sources.title: New World Dorado Corona

note_sources.text: The Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill starts much like many modern Connecticut-wrapped cigars: toasty, a bit peppery, with some well-microwaved popcorn, and then a slight imbalance among the components that makes me wish for a bit more harmony. I’ve often found a bit of disconnect in the flavors of a cigar that uses a Connecticut-seed wrapper over seemingly fuller tobaccos as companies try to make this current iteration of the profile. The first and third cigars exemplify this familiar experience, while in the second cigar, there are a handful of puffs that suddenly get very light in body and flavor, almost an airy, vanilla dessert flavor. Some creaminess joins the profile next, and with it comes something that reminds me of a smoked peppermint sensation. It’s nowhere near as crisp as a candy cane or an Altoids mint, but like someone took some peppermint bark and figured out a way to get some wood chip smoke into it. While I wouldn’t want to say that the profile gets sharp, it does develop a bit of a peppery edge. Flavor is medium-plus, body is medium-plus and strength is mild. Construction is very good, with smoke billowing off the cigars at points, providing plentiful amounts to take in. Creaminess leads the start of the Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill’s second third, with a little black pepper on the finish and in the retrohales, but this is now an experience driven by thick, creamy smoke. After that, I start getting a little bit of earth, and that flavor begins to wrest some of the control from the creaminess. As it continues to develop, it gets a little bit of a soft char, not quite the hard char of a pepper-crusted steak. That said, pepper begins to really develop, especially through the nostrils, where it absolutely lights up my nose at the midway point. After the pepper does its thing, the profile begins switching to a mellower profile, turning down the pepper, thinning out the creaminess, and just turning the overall intensity for a few puffs. But around the midpoint, things change once again as the black pepper returns and now has a bit of sharpness to it; not a bad flavor, but not the palate-coating pepper found in heartier cigars. The flavor also
note_sources.title: Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill

note_sources.text: Cigar Coop 92: natural tobacco, apple/caramel sweetness, earth, black pepper, baking spices, cedar. BMP 93: cinnamon, black coffee, earth, leather; cedar, orange zest, peanut, graham cracker, honey; oak, tea, cherry chocolate.

The first two Camp Aladino Corojo Gorbustos start with quite a bit of black coffee flavors, though the accents are different: sharp horseradish and acidity on the first, and more earthy and toasty on the second. The third is different, more earthy and grassy, a softer version of the medium-full profile. That grouping continues for the rest of the first third. The first two cigars have coffee with a wide-ranging list of accents, including earth, straw, nuttiness, creaminess and bread. The third cigar is much softer with sourdough bread flavors leading earth and acidity. Each cigar’s finish differs: saltier and sharper in the first, more burnt pepper in the second, and a balanced mixture of starch and pepper in the third. Retrohales are pretty similar. They initially bring a softer creamy or bread flavor before acidity emerges, which can bring some milder sweet flavors, like floral flavors or cranberry in tow. The finish adds woodiness—oftentimes like sawdust—though the rest of the list of flavors is very familiar. Flavor is medium-full, body is medium and strength is medium. Construction is great in the first third, with no complaints about any aspects. While the third cigar had been a bit different in the first third, the three cigars now taste remarkably similar. Nuttiness—more cashew than anything else—is present at the front of each cigar. There’s bread, creaminess, a mild sugar sweetness, saltiness and varying amounts of pepper, but the profiles have the same vibe: smooth, relatively balanced and just a bit of sting. During the finish, each cigar finds a slightly different path. The first gets a bit sweeter, the second gets somewhat harsh and less detailed, and the third gets more peppery. That said, the flavors are similar: coffee, nuttiness, black pepper, saltiness. Retrohales take the list of flavors and transforms them. It tastes like there’s more separation between the nuttiness and other flavors like brown mustard, pretzels, saltiness and pepper. note_sources.text: As the company has expanded its offerings and gotten older, there was bound to be an exception and last week I opened up a humidor at home and was reminded of one, the Aladino Corojo Reserva Corona No.4 Limitado. It debuted in 2019 and has since become an annual release . The 5 x 44 corona is a Honduran puro that is said to use higher priming leaves, meaning the tobaccos come from higher up on the plant. Those leaves tend to be smaller and stronger and are oftentimes referred to as ligero tobaccos. When I reviewed the cigar three years ago , I liked the flavor but was troubled by an open draw: I’m not sure how much better this cigar would have been if the draw was where it should have been. There were times in which the flavors showed moments of greatness, but it lacked the dynamic profile I was hoping it could have been. As the score will inevitably indicate, the Aladino Corojo Reserva Corona No.4 Limitado is still a good cigar, just not a great one. A few months ago, I stumbled across some of these while doing some humidor reorganization and decided to snag one for a redux. *There were 16,000 total cigars released for the original 2019 release, there have since been additional shipments. This particular cigar is still covered in tissue paper, albeit, the paper has come loose and isn’t really touching most of the cylinder of the cigar. Between the bands—which have a design that looks like it’s from a couple of decades ago—and the faded medium brown wrapper, if I didn’t know the backstory of this cigar, I would believe you if you told me this cigar was 20-years-old. Speaking of the wrapper, it’s got some discoloration and mottling, but there aren’t very many veins. This cigar has a weird bump on the side of the cigar, almost like a minor tumor. I’m not really sure what to make of it, but it’s pretty small and I figure it shouldn’t affect the cigar all that much. In what’s becoming a trend of late, I can’t smell much of anything from the wrapper. There are some faint touches of leather and cedar, but the lack of cellophane makes it difficult. Alec Bradley Tempus Maduro cigars are among the crowning achievements in Alan Rubin's portfolio. The cigar has received numerous accolades over the years, including a high placing in the prestigious Cigar Aficionado Top 25. It is a top-shelf stick made from Nicaraguan and Honduran fillers, an Indonesian binder, and a rich Honduran wrapper, aged 7 years. This is a cigar for experienced palates. (Shop other Alec Bradley Cigars ) This cigar is cloaked in a dark, oily wrapper leaf and topped off with a luxurious silver and black band. The initial light-up shoots forth a burst of black pepper followed by an instant mellowing into smooth, rich chocolate and molasses flavors. There is a subtle spice throughout, especially on the finish. Medium to full-bodied and very heavy on flavor. The Tempus Maduro is a cigar that is made with connoisseurs in mind. It is rather complex and on the fuller end of medium-full. Strong red wine or a stout beer will make a great companion for enjoying alongside the Tempus Maduro. Similar cigars are the Alec Bradley Prensado and Casa Magna Oscuro. Tempus is Latin for "time," and it's always a good time to enjoy this top-notch offering from Alec Bradley Cigars.

note_sources.text: I am not expecting a lighter start to the Dedicación Habano and I am not let down in that regard. A leather note with some noticeable spice on my tongue transitions to flavors of espresso beans and hay that remain the top notes in the profile for the first third. Secondary flavors of earth, lemon peel, cedar, cinnamon and a slight floral note flit in and out, while the retrohale features both black pepper and a small amount of raisin sweetness, the latter of which seems to be getting a bit stronger as the first third burns down. After a straight cut, both the draw and the smoke production is excellent on all three samples, and while one cigar does need a correction early on, it is relatively minor in nature. Flavor is just under medium but rising, body is between mild and medium and the strength is under the medium mark by the end of the first third. There is still plenty of spice present on my tongue as the second third of the cigar starts, but a strong cashew flavor has taken the top spot in the profile, followed by notes of cedar, wet hay, cinnamon, lemon peel, earth, nutmeg and the same light floral flavor from the first third. While the retrohale still includes some noticeable black pepper, the raisin sweetness increases a bit, although it does seem to be leveling out. Thankfully, the burn on the problematic cigar evens up nicely—the other two have no issues at all in that regard—while the draw and smoke production continue on their excellent path for all three. Both flavor and strength easily hit a solid medium by the time the second third comes to an end, while the body has increased to a point just under medium.
