note_sources.text: The All Saints St. Francis Colorado Robusto starts out pretty easy on the palate; there’s no bang of pepper or flavor, but rather a profile that’s just shy of medium with a light earthiness, a bit of black pepper, and more of the bread texture that I picked up on the cold draw. While smoking the first cigar, I take my first retrohale around the half-inch mark and am greeted with a ton of nose tingle, driven largely by white pepper but the sensation suggests a pinch of bright red chili pepper is in the mix as well. Some earlier retrohales in the other two samples don’t deliver much sensation, leading me to think the profile may be easing me into the experience. As if on cue, the second sample picks up its pepper offering when the burn line is close to the half-inch mark as well, both on the palate and through the nose. Beyond that pepper, the flavor is largely a dry and earthy sensation, accented by some toast and mixed nuts. Other than causing some drying of the mouth and being a somewhat linear flavor, it’s an enjoyable first third. While the draw was a bit firm before I lit the cigar, it’s now quite smooth and easy, producing a decent amount of smoke with each puff. The smoothness is a bit of a contrast to the building black pepper that tingles my tongue and gives the smoke some character. After starting just a bit over the mild mark, flavor is medium-plus, body is medium-plus, and strength is almost at the medium mark. The All Saints St. Francis Colorado Robusto is burning a bit faster than what I would consider average, something that at first thought leads me to suppose that there isn’t a lot of heavy tobacco being used in the filler. Flavor-wise, the pepper continues to drive the profile, while the dry earthiness pulls even at times but never quite overtakes it. As the burn line moves through the midway point, the flavor picks up a bit more sharpness, further reminding me of the red chili pepper flavor by how it hits my palate, though only one cigar gives me the related heat. It’s a sensation and flavor that is not too far away from what you might sprinkle on your pizza, and if you’re like me, would also taste on its own. I also get a flavor and aroma that

note_sources.text: We've all heard of turning life's lemons into lemonade, but the story behind the Arturo Fuente Añejo cigar is just amazing. Back in 1998, when the Arturo Fuente Opus X was just as big of a deal as it is now, Hurricane Georges ravaged the Dominican Republic and caused a shortage in the cigar's wrapper, being grown only at one small Chateau de le Fuente farm. With the expertly-fermented Dominican filler and binder still safe and raring to go, someone had the inspiration to substitute a dark and sticky-sweet five-year-aged Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper which had been further rested in used Cognac barrels. The result is a 93-rated gem the likes of which may never be equaled. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars )
Spicy , Earthy , Floral Available. Learn about Arturo Fuente Casa Cuba Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Casa Cuba

Casa Cuba is the first new cigar brand out of the Fuente factory in the Dominican Republic since 1995, and the first blend directly made by Carlos Fuente, Sr. in decades. A cigar talked about behind closed doors for years, it was finally debuted in 2013. Named after a brand Fuente purchased in 1958, the Casa Cuba is a look back at how the company blended cigars in the pre-embargo days. Cuban-seed Dominican filler and binder tobaccos are wrapped in a Ecuadorian Havana wrapper. A medium-bodied cigar much different from other limited production Fuente cigars, Casa Cuba will have older smokers thinking about those first cigars they smoked, and newer ones wondering why today's cigars are so different. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) The most notable thing one will notice is the band. This is the first Fuente brand not to have the Fuente name anywhere on it. The wrapper is smooth and noticeably missing any toothiness. Small veins can be found if searched for long enough, but what is most striking is the thinness. Despite this, we didn't have any cracking throughout the entire cigar. On first puff a strong, but not unpleasant, bitterness surrounded our palate. This quickly subsided but returned for the middle half of the cigar. Strong earthy flavors of wood are throughout the smoke and there is an extremely welcome sweet aroma. The draw was good, and despite some flaking, Casa Cuba held onto its ash very well. Casa Cuba from Fuente is sure to have some smokers remembering the bygone days of cigar smoking. Blended by a master, this proves that Carlos, Sr. has not lost one step when it comes to making a fantastic cigar. With a body just a hair less than medium, we found a well aged scotch or single barrel bourbon to be the perfect compliment. We also suggest trying one of the cigars blended by Carlos, Jr. such as the Fuente Fuente Opus X or Don Carlos for a heavier fuller-bodied smoking experience.

Arturo Fuente Don Carlos is a true cigar lover's cigar. No introduction is essential, as anyone who has been in the cigar game for any length of time has heard the name a time or two. As a brand, Arturo Fuente is among the best-selling cigar brands in America and usually, sits at the very top. There's a reason for that. No other brand offers such a phenomenal combination of immense quality, variety, and affordability as Fuente. In the case of Don Carlos, we see an aficionado's dream come true. Blended by and named after the brand's patriarch, Carlos Fuente Sr., Don Carlos uses ultra-premium Dominican filler and binder tobacco beneath a one-of-a-kind Cameroon wrapper. These tobacco leaves are aged as long as 10 years before rolling, and the finished cigars spend much more time maturing before being shipped out. The finished product is what many consider to be one of the finest cigars ever made. The Arturo Fuente Don Carlos blend was ranked as high as 94 by Cigar Aficionado. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) Now boasting new black and gold packaging and bands, these golden-brown beauties are every bit as pretty as they are tasty. An opening blast of cedar starts things off, quickly, followed by a vast array of sweet, nutty flavors that dance around on the palate as if performing a skilled ballet routine. Earthy, rich tobacco flavor holds the blend together, followed by a sweet burst on the finish. The underlying floral goodness from the Cameroon wrapper is notable, and the overall strength is a definite medium-full. For any experienced connoisseur, Don Carlos is a no-brainer. Don Carlos offers an experience incomparable to any Cameroon cigar on the market. Whether as a celebration cigar, a gift, or just a way to close out a busy work week on Friday night, Don Carlos fits the bill as a go-to ultra-premium stick. It is best enjoyed with a premium beverage such as single malt scotch or aged port wine, though many simply enjoy it alongside a glass of water to fully appreciate the delicate complexity of the blend. Don Carlos stands as a symbol of what the Fuente brand is all about. Most folks familiar with the name have tried the Gran Reserva , Sungrown , and maybe even a Magnum R or two, and those are all fantastic cigars. However, the Fuente brand is all about being the best. When that is the goal, the brand's flagship cigar has to be not only good, but mind-blowing. We have all heard of the fabled Opus X , which many consider to be the Fuentes' crowning achievement, and without a doubt, it is. However, the actual "top-tier" offering from the Fuentes, as far as the general cigar smoking population goes, is the Don Carlos, no-ifs, ands, or buts. For a taste of pure quality and craftsmanship, as well as a cigar made with unmatched passion and ambition towards perfection, reach no farther than Arturo Fuente Don Carlos.

note_sources.text: Leather , Cedar , Sweet Tobacco Available. Learn about Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Maduro Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Gran Reserva Maduro

If you prefer the syrupy and rich flavors provided by cigars coated in dark, oily wrappers, then you are going to absolutely love the Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Maduro. Each exquisite vitola starts with a hefty portion of longleaf filler and binder from the Fuente family's own Chateau de la Fuente fields, Dominican wonderlands of agriculture famous for their ability to produce tobaccos of unmatched flavor and quality. After extensive aging and blending to just the right profile, the carefully bunched leaves are rolled by AF's skilled torcedors into a plethora of sizes beneath a beautiful Connecticut Broadleaf loaded with sweet aroma and taste. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) Mild-Medium Bodied Cigars Attractively dressed in a simple red, gold, and green band, an Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Maduro becomes even more appealing as the cigar is prepped for smoking by clipping or punching the triple cap and giving the foot a gentle toast. The wisps of smoke give hints to the earthy, pungent flavors yet to come even as the wrapper wafts cocoa to the nose just before lighting. Oak, black coffee, and sweet spice coat the palate during the first few puffs, the thick smoke creamy and smooth. The sweet spot folds in chocolate-covered almonds and plenty of leather and cane syrup. Remaining medium in strength even as the nub approaches, the stick will release vanilla, molasses, and a touch of white pepper before all is said and done. Being a part of the world's best-selling line of cigars certainly hasn't done anything to diminish the Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Maduro. If anything, the fact that it is so beloved and so affordable means it's going to be here for the long haul. If it does become your favorite smoke, a distinct possibility, you will be enjoying them for years to come. They do age well, so stock up now to make sure they have the chance.

note_sources.text: This cigar is an absolute icon in the world of fine tobacco. Not only has it been revered as one of the world's finest cigars; it is backed by nearly a century of rich history and blending excellence. The Fuentes are the undisputed masters of cigar making and the best of the best among the world's great tobacco producers. Much can be said about their long history, their legendary blending prowess, and their exotic high-end cigars, but the Gran Reserva is the one that started it all. Made entirely by hand in the infamous Tabaclera Fuente in the Dominican Republic, the Gran Reserva consists of fine specially-selected tobaccos from a private family reserve, grown on Chateau de la Fuente. A blend of rich Dominican filler and binder tobaccos are embraced by a sultry African Cameroon wrapper leaf, bringing together what to this day stands as the best-selling cigar in America. After rolling, the cigars are extensively aged in Cedar vaults to bring about the trademark Fuente "marriage of flavors." (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) Mild-Medium Bodied Cigar The Gran Reserva Natural is a cigar for the ages, adorned with a classy red, green, and gold band bearing the Fuente trademark. The caramel-brown wrapper leaf is rough and veiny. The construction is absolutely matchless. An easy draw provides a plethora of heavy white smoke. Smooth, crisp, classic. There is a presence of spice, as with most Cameroon sticks, but nothing overpowering. The rich floral notes leave behind a hint of the customary Fuente sweetness on the palate, along with a kiss of white pepper at the back of the throat. Indubitably medium-bodied. The Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Natural is a must-try for any cigar smoker, whether young or old, new or experienced, and it's a definite mainstay in any serious connoisseur's humidor. Great for any time, the Gran Reserva Natural makes a wonderful morning cigar, or a terrific choice after dinner. Medium-bodied red wine or bourbon would be a wonderful pairing with this stick. Although nobody can come close to duplicating what comes out of Tabaclera Fuente, similar choices to this might include the Partagas -- another timeless classic, or the Ashton Heritage Puro Sol. The Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Natural is a cigar that is loved by many and shows no sign of going anywhere in that respect.

These cigars are arguably one of the best cigars for the money available in today's market. Part of the Chateau series, this line of super-premium cigars was inspired by Chateau Fuente, home of the Arturo Fuente tobacco plantation. The cigars are comprised of luscious Dominican filler and binder tobaccos from the Fuente family's private reserve of specially aged tobacco. To top them off, the Fuentes selected a very special Ecuadorian Sungrown wrapper leaf to add a considerable amount of heavy-hitting strength and smooth, luxurious spice. As with all Fuente cigars, the Sungrown is unparalleled in terms of construction and consistency, carrying on the family tradition of superb quality. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) The Arturo Fuente Sungrown cigars come wrapped in a very fragrant cedar sleeve and finished with the Chateau Series badge of honor, the black ribbon. Oils seem to ooze from the dark, gorgeous sungrown wrapper leaf, well marbled and road-mapped with dark veins throughout. The pre-light aroma is distinctly raw cedar, no doubt from aging under the cedar sleeve since their birth at Tabaclera Fuente. Of course, the draw is on-point and easy, and at first light this piece of tobacco artwork slathers the palate with a warm greeting of cedar and oak. Soon, the crisp, grassy flavors evolve and bring about hints of herbs and very strong spices. Carlos Fuente Jr. has a trademark, almost customary sweetness that is a mainstay in just about all of his blends, and this one is no different. Although not quite as sugary-sweet as his other premium blends, the Sungrown keeps that hint of lingering honey-like sweetness on the tip of the tongue, just enough to bring the whole package together. Very strong floral notes when exhaled through the nose and a continual presence of cedar remain throughout the smoke. This cigar has a very clean finish for being so heavy. Full-bodied Cigars Overall, the Arturo Fuente Sungrown is quite a pleasurable and enjoyable smoke. It is very full-bodied, so by no means is it a beginner's stick, but for any intermediate to experienced aficionado, this one is most definitely one to try. Most Fuente fanatics call this cigar a cheaper alternative to the Opus X because of the smooth, spicy attributes it carries with it. Perhaps a wonderful evening cigar, the Fuente Sungrown pairs great with a cappuccino or even a solid bourbon. Fans of this cigar might also find pleasure in the Ashton VSG or the Oliva Serie V, both cigars with comparable flavor profiles under the sungrown category. For the price, the Arturo Fuente Sungrown is tough to beat.

Few cigars are as instantly recognizable as the Arturo Fuente Hemingway Maduro . Each size in this legendary line is a flawlessly rolled perfecto, featuring a closed cap and foot for a traditional look and exceptional burn. Produced in very limited quantities and released only twice a year, these super-premium cigars are among the most sought-after Fuentes in the world. The Hemingway Maduro shares the same perfect construction as the original Hemingway line, but its dark, rich wrapper adds a layer of complexity and strength. Expect the signature Fuente earthiness intertwined with natural sweetness that only the finest maduro wrappers can deliver. Every puff is smooth, flavorful, and perfectly balanced, making this cigar a true connoisseur’s delight. As Ernest Hemingway himself believed in keeping things simple yet masterful, the Fuentes follow the same philosophy. The Hemingway Maduro Series is a shining example of Arturo Fuente’s craftsmanship—classic, consistent, and timeless. Whether enjoyed slowly after dinner or shared with fellow aficionados, this limited-edition perfecto is a cigar worth savoring.

If you had to pick only one cigar to smoke for the rest of your life, we doubt you could do any better than an Arturo Fuente Hemingway Natural cigar . Think about it. First of all, every stogie carrying the famous frontmark is a perfecto, that classic shape where the barrel flares dramatically right past the foot to then taper ever-so-gently to the head. It's just what a cigar should look like. Now, consider the fact that these smokes contain nothing but delectable Fuente-grown Dominican longleaf tobaccos for the filler and binder. Mmmm, that's a scrumptious thought. Finally, each curvaceous stick is finished with a bold Cameroon wrapper tailor-made to inject flavor directly into your soul. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) Since most of us like variety and thus are not going to go all-in on only one cigar, the decision on what stick to pull next from the humidor comes down to many factors. Too bad for those other stogies that the Arturo Fuente Hemingway Natural has all the boxes checked. Immediately eye-catching in shape and color, the solid heft of each vitola lends further credence to the choice. Wafting an aroma of sweet cedar, the wrapper will provide the lips with some promising nutmeg and fresh hay during the draw test. Alight, and as the full width of the barrel begins to smolder, thick reams of smoke will flood the palate with pepper, sweet cream, and warm spice . A splash of citrus will join the dark chocolate that enters at the halfway mark, followed by oak and espresso as the final third is reached. Easily carrying the weight of a 95-rating and 2018 # 6 Cigar of the Year by Cigar Aficionado that still seems too low considering the enjoyment to be found within, the savory Arturo Fuente Hemingway Natural will seem much heavier than its medium-strength until you realize you're still standing upright after smoking and are ready for round two. You don't have to be an 'Old Man' to 'Sea' you need to get you some of these right away.

The legendary Arturo Fuente Opus X is legendary for one reason and one reason only, and that is because it is freaking delicious. Now, you could name any number of other peripheral causes for it to be the most famous of cigars within the small world of true aficionados (ask a Regular Joe to name a stogie and invariably Macanudo or perhaps Cohiba will be invoked), but it always comes back to taste. The relative rarity of the stick certainly comes into play, as does the academic appreciation for the exclusive and expertly aged all-Dominican longleaf that comprises this one-of-a-kind experience. For those in the know, however, the proof is in the pudding. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) For the experienced smoker, there may be no tastier treat that a full-bodied Arturo Fuente Opus X. That’s not to say a more novice smoker can’t find something to love about these fine Puros, a trial by fire we heartily recommend that you undertake sooner rather than later, but such is the complexity of the cigar that it is best when able to be compared to as many other cigars as possible. Bold and earthy from the start yet with a sweet floral aroma, the rich flavors only intensify the further down the barrel the burn line gets. Espresso and cedar and leather and cream and clove are readily apparent, with hints of citrus, honey cake, and black currant available to the discerning palate. A meaty, peppery char builds in as the nub approaches, the strength kicking to high gear to ward off any pretenders. Earning its place in history as the first cigar to use nothing but Dominican tobaccos in its construction, the Arturo Fuente Opus X is so much more than either a novelty or an expensive luxury. It is an expression of pure passion and skill, and with each silky puff you’ll come to appreciate more and more what the fine folks at Arturo Fuente have accomplished. Honor their work often, and you’ll be rewarded with true satisfaction.

Everyone knows what an Opus X is. This creme de la creme brand is always at the top of everyone's must-have list. But what a lot of people do not know is that a regular Opus X is sometimes so strong that it needs time to rest and really mellow. To celebrate Arturo Fuente's 100th anniversary in the cigar industry, the company has released the Opus X Angel Share, a variation on the cadillac of cigars that is ready to smoke right from the box. The main difference is the gorgeous Dominican Sun Grown wrapper. This Fuente Fuente OpusX Angel’s Share earned #9 on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 Cigars of 2025 , boasting an impressive 96 rating . The ornate and beautiful Opus X band is adorned with a secondary band with the name Angel Share emblazoned across it. The toothy mocha-brown sun grown wrapper will be the first thing to catch your eye. At first light, there no longer is a blast of pepper that will make you need to find a comfy chair but instead an amazing sweetness that will brush past your palette. This note continues the length of the cigar and mixes perfectly with an earthy cedar taste that comes through on the back half. The Arturo Fuente Opus X Angel Share has made the famed cigar much more accessible to almost all cigar smokers. Still a medium-full bodied cigar , the strength no longer will blow you away right out of the box. Named for the classic winemaking term for the alcohol that evaporates during aging, these cigars are certainly something to keep around for a special occasion. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars )

As if the regular production Arturo Fuente Opus X cigars weren't rare enough, enter the Destino al Siglo, quite possibly one of the rarest in the Opus X stable. Roughly translated, the name of this cigar means "Destiny of the Century" and this was supposed to be released in 2012 to celebrate the 100th anniversary of Arturo Fuente. Like most guests of honor though, the Destino al Siglo arrived a little late, but the wait was more than worth it. This Dominican puro uses only the finest wrapper, binder, and filler tobacco from the famed Chateau de Fuente. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) The gorgeous Opus X band is embellished with a secondary band exclaiming how special this cigar is. The medium brown hue of the wrapper is perfect and the prelight taste is one of fruit and spice. With each draw a taste of raisins mingles with white pepper and cedar notes. These flavors play off each other throughout the entire smoke with each one taking the forefront only to switch to another. The Arturo Fuente Destino al Siglo may have been late for the 100th anniversary party, but that extra time has made one heck of an amazing cigar. The complexity in flavor and the impeccable construction makes this a full-bodied-cigar smokers dream come true. Each inhale brings more and more flavors until the next thing you know you are at the nub. This cigar pairs amazingly with a well aged single malt scotch.

This is an impressive cigar with a unique blend and extraordinary flavor. Named for the 2005 Andy Garcia movie about a Cuban tobacco farmer who was forced to give up his farm to the Castro regime, this vitola boasts as uncommon a story as it does taste. While filming at the Fuente farm in the Dominican Republic, Garcia had the idea of a scene in a tobacco field. Unfortunately for him, the harvest was just completed. Carlito Fuente offered a field to replant despite the off season. What resulted was an extremely exclusive, summer-grown, wrapper leaf that provides this cigar with its outstanding spiciness. This Dominican Republic puro is a very limited release and something every full-bodied-cigar lover should experience. On Garcia's suggestion, a portion of the proceeds from this cigar are given to the Cigar Family Charitable Foundation, which benefits families in the Dominican Republic. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) The grandiose Opus X band is adorned with a secondary Lost City one which surrounds a beautiful matte brown wrapper leaf. While some have called this cigar medium-to-full-bodied, we found it much closer to the full side than in the middle. That being said, the smoothness of the smoke is extremely satisfying. The wrapper imparts a zest that is tantalizing on the tongue but never bites. This complex and sophisticated smoke leaves notes of jasmine in the air. As with all Fuente cigars, the construction is impeccable and the ash will hold until the nub. This rare cigar is not just about the story behind it, but the amazing flavors it produces. Perfect for the lover of cigars that pack a ton of flavor and body. We prefer to enjoy this cigar after a large meal, sitting with a nice single malt scotch or espresso. If you like this cigar, we would also recommend the Camacho SLR or the Ashton VSG, although nothing truly can match the magnificence of the Fuente Fuente Opus X.

Born from the magic soils of Chateau de la Fuente comes another enchanting taste profile to the most sought-after premium cigar brand in the world, the prestigious Fuente Fuente OpusX. All of these fine cigars are composed of the highest quality binder, filler, and wrapper tobacco cultivated from the heart of the Dominican Republic.

The 1960's - A Time for Change - JFK, MLK, Love, Peace, Vietnam, the Stones, Joplin, Woodstock. The 60's was a decade full of "The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly," when experimentation ran rampant, yet consciousness rose to the highest levels. People sought meaning, guardrails were broken, and pink flowers bloomed. This era marked a young Carlito Fuente for life, becoming an out-of-the-box artist who changed norms and set new standards in the cigar industry. With these lifelong reflections both in mind and soul, The Toymaker created his latest cigar gem - the Rare Pink - with the hope that it reminds us all that no matter how tough the times get, Love Conquers All! (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars )

However, that was not the last time the blend was seen, as another version was released seven years later. In 2009, when Fuente rereleased an unknown number of the 8-5-8 Rosado Sun Grown cigars, this time in smaller 20-count boxes. Retailers at that year’s IPCPR Convention & Trade Show were able to purchase a variety of special boxes in exchange for purchasing 25 boxes of regular Fuente product. One of those special boxes was a box of 8-5-8 Sun Growns. There have now been three different Arturo Fuente 8-5-8 Rosado Sun Grown releases. In terms of non-Cuban cigars, the original Arturo Fuente Flor Fina 858 Rosado is on the holy grail lists of many cigar smokers, mostly because if its rarity. I really wish I could give it an amazing score, and tell you these are worth the considerable time, effort and money that they command, but sadly, that is not to be. This is, at best, a nice, mildly pleasant, fairly one dimensional cigar that is extremely easy to smoke, but leaves you wanting more after it is over, like when you eat sugar free ice cream. They may have been a better smoke when first released, but at this point, they are more hype than substance. As with the samples I smoked in 2002, the Arturo Fuente 8-5-8 Rosado Sun Grown is covered in a pale milk chocolate brown wrapper that is smooth to the touch, although the cedar wrap covering the bottom two-thirds of the cigar is quite a bit lighter than the past two releases. In addition, there is a touch of oil noticeable as well as a multitude of prominent veins, and the cigar is quite spongy when squeezed. The aroma from the wrapper is a combination of cashews, dark chocolate, manure, popcorn, hay and leather while the cold draw brings flavors of aged and aromatic cedar, baker’s spices, nutmeg, freshly brewed coffee, white pepper and a touch of floral. There is no way to say this nicely, but the Arturo Fuente 8-5-8 Rosado Sun Grown starts out extremely slow, with muddled and indistinct flavors throughout that initially has me quite worried about where it is going to end up. Thankfully, that does not last long, as the profile ramps up significantly in terms of complexity and distinctness after about 15 puffs, with aged
note_sources.title: Arturo Fuente Flor Fina 8-5-8 Rosado Sun Grown (2018)

note_sources.text: Few cigars have intrigued long-time connoisseurs over the years more than the fabled Arturo Fuente Rosado Sun Grown 8-5-8. Technically part of the immensely popular Flor Fina series, this blend is among the rarest cigars in the world, with only an extremely small amount released once every few years. In fact, the original release in 2002 only consisted of 87 boxes of 50 cigars, sent out to a mere 29 retailers across the country that were chosen by way of a contest. What makes it so rare in comparison to other 8-5-8 variants is the Ecuadorian Sun Grown Rosado wrapper leaf, something we have seen in other offerings from Fuente such as the King T and Magnum R series. However, paired with the 8-5-8's unique size and luscious blend of Dominican filler and binder tobaccos, this beautiful leaf completes the recipe for one of the most delicious and sought-after cigars on the planet. Due to its rarity, this cigar is a treat that many cigar enthusiasts may wait their whole life to enjoy. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) Nestled neatly in gorgeous mahogany boxes, each vitola sits individually cloaked in a cedar sleeve, bearing the Flor Fina band and the infamous red ribbon at the foot denoting that it is in fact part of the Rosado Sun Grown series. The size, keeping with 8-5-8 tradition, is 6 ¼" x 47, a cross between a toro and a corona gorda. This revered size has more than proven itself over the years, providing a fairly lengthy smoking time along with a pronounced flavor from the wrapper leaf due to its smaller, more classic ring gauge. In the truest Fuente fashion, Rosado Sun Grown 8-5-8 is expertly constructed to deliver a streamlined smoking experience, with an easy draw, razor sharp burn, and the ability to hold a long, solid ash. Starting off, the cedar is the star of the show. Mature raw tobacco flavor soon becomes the focus, something the blend is built around. Hints of honey and cognac tickle the palate alongside mild white pepper and earth, and the finish is rich, sweet, and heavily floral, no doubt a trademark with any textbook rare Fuente. Medium-full-bodied and impeccably balanced, this blend leaves nothing to be desired and is a sheer pleasure to smoke. Experienced connoisseurs delight in enjoying cigars such as this, whose flavor profile is both classic and exciting at the same time. Hefty in body and sweet, yet never overpowering, Rosado Sun Grown 8-5-8 pairs beautifully with cognac or dark rum, but also goes well with scotch or even port wine. With its Rosado Sun Grown wrapper and Dominican core, it is safe to say that this blend is as close to an Opus X as it gets without actually being one. As the saying goes, "Only Fuente is Fuente," and there is no cigar company on earth that does rare cigars the way the Fuentes do. If you haven't gotten your Rosado Sun Grown 8-5-8 by now, it is time to stop reading and hit the order button if you want to grab a piece of cigar history and experience one of the world's finest cigars!

It's one thing to be at the top of your game and able to compete with anyone, but when a cigar company like Arturo Fuente can produce an instant classic like the Rosado Sungrown Magnum R seemingly without even trying, you know they're so far in the zone it's almost supernatural. How else to explain a 94-rating and the sudden appearance of this fine smoke in Top-25 of the Year lists so soon after release and at one the best price points ever for an AF stick? Truthfully, all credit should be given to the special blend of Dominican filler and binder tobaccos that combine with the dark, 10-year-aged Ecuadorian wrapper to create an unstoppable wave of flavor. (Shop other Arturo Fuente Cigars ) You could be forgiven for thinking that an Arturo Fuente vitola at such a bargain price might be a lesser cigar for it, but that is certainly not the case when you're about to enjoy an Arturo Fuente Rosado Sungrown Magnum R. From the beautifully styled band to the ruddy and oily slick wrapper to the hefty weight of the solidly packed filler, each of these sturdy stogies embodies quality and attention to detail. Applying a steady flame to the broad foot first releases a hearty supply of leather, cinnamon, cream, and marzipan . A sweetness like maple syrup enters during the second third, accompanied by layers of cedar and nutmeg . The profile turns earthy and peppery near the finale , still medium in strength, but turning even richer, deeper, and more complex. This is one cigar you cannot do without in any respectable, well-stocked humidor. Affordable enough to enjoy frequently but able to fulfill all the requirements for a special occasion smoke, an Arturo Fuente Rosado Sungrown Magnum R will only grow better with age so make sure you have enough. As if there are ever enough.

While Maduro cigars are widely available, the Ashton Aged Maduro stands as a sophisticated outlier that demands to be experienced. Ashton is globally recognized for its high-end Sun Grown offerings, but this dark, enticing line proves the brand’s mastery extends across all profiles. The blend's reputation is well-earned, having received multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado . The Aged Maduro derives its signature character and striking visual appeal from a meticulously selected Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper , which undergoes a lengthy, natural fermentation process to achieve its iconic near-black hue.

The Ashton Cabinet cigar stands on its own against any other world-class mild cigar. Built by Tabacalera Fuente for brand owner Robert Levin, this classic take on Connecticut-wrapped cigars has as its foundation six different well-aged Dominican tobaccos, all at least 4 to 5 years removed from the day of harvest. The fine shade wrapper is even older, fermented to a deep, golden hue and patiently stored until needed by rolling room craftsmen.

As one of the best selling cigars in the USA , sometimes it seems like the Ashton Classic cigar has been around since the beginning of time, yet here it still stands to beat the pants off of more rookie mild smokes left and right. Crafted during the heady days of the mid-90's cigar boom by Robert Levin and the geniuses at Arturo Fuente, it has survived and thrived despite the onslaught of hundreds of upstarts in the revitalized tobacco business. How it has accomplished the feat is a fairly simple matter of taking the best Dominican tobacco, carefully fermenting and aging them for three to four years, then marrying them within an ultra-silky and flawless Connecticut Shade wrapper. New cigar lovers and seasoned connoisseurs discover and relive their affinity for premium cigars with the 92-rated Ashton Classic by Cigar Aficionado. We all know that a large amount of skill and a bit of luck go into creating a truly world-class cigar. But when you lay your eyes for the very first time on an Ashton Classic cigar, you will begin to realize just how special they are. Glossy and golden, each vitola carries a regal bearing beneath the simple white and black bands they proudly wear. Crisp aromas of fresh hay and peat roll off the seamless outer layer and the cold draw reveals hints of nuts and citrus . The thick smoke provided by the Connecticut leaf is appropriately grassy once alight, with the rich interior offering café con leche, orange peel, almond, and vanilla . Towards the nub you are likely to discover some caramelized sweetness and soft spice keeping any bitterness at bay, so definitely watch your fingers. Delicious and smooth from top to bottom, this is a cigar capable of satisfying everyone. The complete novice will delight in the rich taste that doesn't overwhelm the senses, while the depth of complexity creates a savory treat for the grizzled veteran. Always good to have on hand, you will be richly rewarded each time you grab an Ashton Classic.

There are few names synonymous with premium cigars like Ashton. For those moments when you do not have the time to smoke a full-sized Ashton Classic or Cabinet, the Aston Connecticut is the perfect cigar. Made in the European style, these small cigars use only the finest aged Dominican tobacco and are wrapped in an exquisite, mild Connecticut wrapper.

An ultra-premium in every sense, the Ashton Estate Sun Grown (ESG) cigar was created to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Ashton brand and represents the best of the cigar-making craft. The pinnacle of a collaborative effort between tobacconist Robert Levin and Tabacalera Fuente, it contains a unique blend of artfully aged tobaccos from the Dominican Republic. But what makes this cigar special is the wrapper, culled from only the highest primings of plants located within the Chateau de la Fuente estate and grown only for the ESG in very limited quantities. (Shop other Ashton Cigars ) The highly stylized band of the Ashton ESG adds glamor to an appearance otherwise in need of little enhancement. Minimal veining adds texture to a flawless, chewy leaf that exudes scents of spice and peat. The first few puffs deliver wood and coffee notes in a balanced and smooth manner, with a sweet caramel added into the first third. The taste shifts to spice and almond as the smoke progresses, the salt and pepper ash is somewhat flaky but strong. The final third of the cigar is a crescendo of flavors, heavily influenced by the return of the caramel now toasted to a crisp toffee. Priced for special occasions, the Ashton Estate Sun Grown will be hard to resist even after a lunch of burgers and fries on the patio of the local country club, but having a box available in the humidor will make it easier to indulge for even the most mundane of celebrations. A medium to full cigar on par with the Arturo Fuente Opus X or Padron Anniversary 1964, it will delight even the most jaded of cigar aficionados.

One of the best cigars on the planet, you shouldn't consider yourself a true aficionado until you've experienced an Ashton Heritage Puro Sol for yourself. No matter how much we are going to gush about it right here and now, there's just no substitute for the pleasure to be derived from puffing on one of these ultra-premium jewels. Blended and rolled by the masters at Arturo Fuente, each quality handmade cigar is comprised entirely of Sungrown tobaccos, as noted by the cigar's name. The longleaf filler and binder hail from the Dominican Republic while the wrapper is a sultry and rich Habano from Ecuador.

Ashton Symmetry is an amazing premium cigar that is full of "firsts". Not only is this the first new line from Ashton since the much heralded ESG line in 2006, but it is also the first line from Ashton that uses Nicaraguan Tobacco. Made in the Dominican Republic at the Fuente factory, Ashton Symmetry is a mild-to-medium bodied cigar comprised of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler tobacco, a Dominican binder, and an oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.

Released in 1999, the Ashton Virgin Sun Grown (VSG) cigar represents the evolution of Ashton Cigars from a respectable Cigar Boom-era line into a premium brand capable of satisfying smokers who prefer modern, fuller-bodied blends. An early 93 rating has consistently been upheld by more recent reviews, and continued demand has proven the VSG capable of finding new fans as well as keeping knowledgeable aficionados coming back for more. Blended by Carlos Fuente Jr. of Tabacalera Fuente, the cigar utilizes 4 and 5 year old Dominican tobacco tucked into a redolent Ecuadoran wrapper hailing from a private estate held by the Oliva family and produced specifically for the VSG.

Taking a fan favorite cigar to an insane new level is the whole purpose behind the Asylum 13 Corojo. The original Asylum 13 was a big hit with lovers of full-flavored treats, but in the fevered minds of Asylum Cigars co-founders Tom Lazuka and Christian Eiroa lives the drive to craft ever bigger flavors, ever better smoking experiences. To this end, the talented torcedors at Eiroa's Fabricas Unidas factory have subverted the original's Nicaraguan puro roots by blending and bunching a plethora of all-Honduran tobaccos for the filler. A Honduran binder is applied and then they complete the transformation by straight-jacketing each vitola in a thick Corojo grown in the sultry Jamastran Valley in Honduras.

When it comes to the world of cigars, the Asylum blends have been having their run of the place lately, and with delicious smokes like the recently released Asylum 13 Connecticut, it is easy to see why. One has to be a little off their rocker to thrive in the tobacco biz, but fortunately, co-founders Christian Eiroa and Tom Lazuka have the perfect mix of cunning and skill to accomplish great feats of flavor. Using senses honed by years of hard work, the two have entwined juicy Honduran Corojo among the Habano leaves that serve as the rest of the filler and binder to give this glorious stogie plenty of strength and character. They then temper the insanity with a creamy Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper for an entirely balanced, medium-bodied experience.

Released in 2013, the Asylum 13 Ogre is an extremely unique take on an already unique idea in cigar making… the barber pole. Most barber pole designed cigars utilize both a lighter Habano or Connecticut wrapper with a darker maduro leaf in order to give it that characteristic striped design, but the ogre went a little further. Instead of a maduro, Christian Eiroa decided that his barber pole design would have a candela wrapper paired with the more traditional habano to give the Ogre a striking brown and green stripe.

You'll first go wild trying to wrap your head around the enormous Asylum 13 Pandemonium, but soon enough you'll be yet another maniac raving about a powerful cigar smoking experience unlike any other. The latest Asylum release from those wardens of superior tobacco over at CLE Cigars, AKA Christian Eiroa and Tom Lazuka, you'll have as hard of a time standing up after you've started puffing like a lunatic as you will fitting a collection of these full-strength 8 1/2" vitolas into your humidor. They're worth the trouble, though. Chock full of premium aged Nicaraguan longleaf from beginning to end, this is one long-burning stick you won't want to put down.

In an effort to try to taste as much of the tobacco as I can, I don’t actively lick my lips during the first puff. It means that the first few seconds tend to be without the flavoring—it’s a very generic woody and dry tobacco flavor—but after three or four seconds, the banana kicks in and then if I lick my lips and get the sugar, it tastes close to the banana split flavor that is the clear goal. Unfortunately, on the first cigar, there’s just something weird happening where those two flavors are creating some bizarre vegetal flavor, almost like mushy asparagus. Fortunately, if I want it to go away, I can just lick my lips and the sugar takes over, but during the first cigar, I’m confused as to what CLE has done. The other two cigars are much better because the asparagus combination never emerges. Instead, the non-flavored parts provide some woody flavors with earth, leather, aged tobacco and hints of ketchup. The flavoring is a lot stronger and delivers more sugar than banana, but there’s also some candied walnuts and vanilla. Without licking the lips, the finish tends to be bitter but there’s some nice nuttiness. Retrohaling is far and away the most interesting, especially when I can get what I imagine is the intended combination: waffle cone, banana, leather, white pepper, saltiness and varying amounts of woodiness. With the exception of some puffs when the woodiness dominates or when I lick my lips, the retrohales tend to be much more balanced. They finish drier and spicier, though sometimes get a bit metallic. Flavor is full, body is medium-plus, and strength is mild. While I don’t have to make any corrections with my lighter, the burn line is below average, and I’m puffing a bit quicker due to my concerns with the soft spots. As is the case with most cigars with a sweetened tip that I’ve smoked, as I smoke, there’s a very sharp decline in the sugar on my lips. By the midpoint of the cigar, it’s probably less than half of the intensity it initially was, and it’s only declining with each puff. Occasionally, puffs will have a very distinct artificial banana flavor, but for the most part, the flavoring is gone unless I lick my lips and really go searching for i
note_sources.title: Asylum 13 Split Personality 50×5

asylum-april-fools-2026-year-of-horse.name: April Fools 2026 Year of The Horse

note_sources.text: Starting out, the cigars each have a combination of light spice and pepper, combined with a small amount of burnt bread flavor. Gradually, the profiles shift to include main flavors of powdery cocoa nibs and coffee beans, a combination that reminds me of drinking a mocha coffee, albeit sans most of the sweetness. At various points, secondary flavors of aromatic cedar, roasted peanuts, gritty earth, sweet barnyard, sourdough bread and light cloves show up, and while there is a nice amount of spice on my tongue for the first two cigars, the third one has almost none. On the retrohales of all three cigars, there is some light black pepper, but the sweetness is a bit different: the first and second cigars feature a rich fudge flavor, while the third cigar has a light but distinct blackberry flavor. Flavor is full and by the end of the first third, both the body and strength land at just under medium. When it comes to the construction, my third cigar needs a quick touch-up to stay on track, but the draw resistance is excellent for all three cigars after straight cuts, and there is an abundance of thick, off-white smoke. During the second third, the profiles of two of the three cigars go through some changes, starting with the main flavors. While the second cigar continues to exhibit the same powdery cocoa nibs and coffee bean combination that it had in the first third, the first and third cigars now feature a new combination of sweet cloves and creamy cedar that is no less enjoyable. Secondary flavors include creamy leather, toasted bread, chalk, roasted peanuts, dry earth and a touch of cinnamon, while a lemongrass note emerges on the finish of two of the three cigars after the halfway point. Retrohales remain consistent with what was present in the first third—rich fudge and black pepper for the first and second cigars, blackberry sweetness and black pepper for the last cigar—which is not a bad thing. Flavor is still at full, the body remains at a point just under medium and the strength increases to land at a solid medium. The burn line on my second cigar runs into enough trouble to warrant a minor correction with my lighter, but that is the only construction issu
note_sources.title: Asylum 13 Arabian Nights 54 × 6 Belicoso

note_sources.text: Coffee has long been known as one of a cigar’s best friends, and although many attempts have been made over the years to combine the flavors of the two, only a few have seen real success. However, when Christian Eiroa and his famed Asylum brand decided to make a coffee-infused stick, even cigar snobs that steer clear of flavored cigars started getting excited. Behold, Asylum Cool Brew! The second Asylum cigar to offer a flavor-infused profile, following the successful 867 series, Cool Brew is a true Honduran puro made at the El Aladino factory in Honduras. Wrapper, filler, and binder tobacco for this blend all come from the family farms in Honduras, and the wrapper leaf is a well-aged dark brown Maduro. What sets this cigar apart from the pack is the unique steeping method used to flavor the tobacco. The cigars are stored in a closed environment to absorb the flavors of whatever is the targeted result. For this case, a minty coffee/espresso note seems to be the main goal. Packaging for this blend keeps in tune with most of the Asylum cigars, including a modernized cedar chest adorned with the famed Asylum skull motif. The bands are traditional Asylum style as well, and for this case the color of choice is teal to denote the Cool Brew blend. Construction, as usual, is incredible for each and every cigar, as Christian Eiroa and his team take quality and consistency very seriously, even of fun projects like this. An easy draw produces dense clouds of ultra-flavorful smoke, each puff seemingly introducing new notes. The sweet coffee note is pronounced from first light and carries on throughout the duration of the cigar. The core of the flavor profile is earthy tobacco flavor with classic maduro notes including espresso, dark chocolate, and cinnamon. Hints of cream and mint pop in and out as the cigar progresses, and the finish is long and thick, leaving a trace of sweet milk chocolate. Very flavorful but easy on the palate, Cool Brew finishes as a medium-bodied cigar. One of the reasons Eiroa and his team decided to go with an infused cigar was to attract new cigar enthusiasts. This stick couldn’t be a better option as far as beginners’ cigars go, as it is medium-bodied at its strongest point and very easy to enjoy. Pair it with your favorite coffee concoction or just enjoy it alongside a glass of cold water in order to truly appreciate all the interesting flavor notes it has to offer. Fans of mildly-infused cigars such as Drew Estate Larutan would definitely appreciate what this cigar has to offer, but if we are being honest, just about anyone will likely enjoy Cool Brew. The infused flavors are nothing to be afraid of, and at the end of the day, it will probably stand out as a solid, flavorful maduro cigar. Whether you are a coffee freak or just want to experience the new, even crazier side of Asylum Cigars, Asylum Cool Brew is a cigar that you’ll likely be trying more than once.

Creeping into your subconscious from the moment you open this page, the Asylum Insidious cigar is a gateway to another dimension of taste and experience. Well known for crafting powerful and impressive expressions, Asylum's founder Tom Lazuka has trained his sights on the acolytes of the cigar smoking realm, those less experienced yet enthusiastic aficionados who want maximum flavor and complete satisfaction. And so the Insidious was brought into the world to subvert traditional ideas of what a mild cigar could be. Containing an expertly cured blend of Honduran tobacco as filler and binder, each stick is finished with a smooth, creamy Ecuadorian wrapper topped with a lightly sweetened cap resulting in a flavor-bomb that won't leave you crying for mommy.

Erupting with a ridiculous amount of flavor and power, the Asylum Insidious Habano cigar will quickly lodge into the back of your skull as an all-time favorite. What else to expect from Christian Eiroa, the king of awesome-good smokes who has joined forces with Asylum cofounders/co-conspirators Tom Lazuka and Kevin Baxter to keep the brand's hits coming from the Eiroa's El Aladino factory. Able to maintain the hunt for exceptional long leaf close to home, the tobaccos used to create the Insidious Habano are all Honduran, including the expertly fermented Jamastran wrapper that is finished with a lightly sweetened tip.

The Asylum Insidious Maduro cigar is what happens when the so-called “good twin” turns out darker than the evil one. A sibling to the original Insidious, this stick carries the same sweetened cap and is packed with a hearty blend of rich Honduran tobaccos, hand-selected for their flavor-packed appeal. But instead of wearing a cool-as-a-cucumber Connecticut Shade wrapper, the Maduro steps to the shadowy side with a toothy Mexican San Andrés wrapper —so dark and oily it feels like staring into the abyss of an empty humidor. Thankfully, Asylum offers these in big 25-count boxes perfect for daily indulgence, so you can stockpile your own horde to burn through at will. It should come as no surprise that a cigar crafted at Christian Eiroa’s Fabricas Unidas comes out nothing short of flawless. A skull-adorned cream label, echoing that of the Connecticut Insidious, pops even more boldly against the Maduro’s ebony wrapper. The pre-light aroma has plenty of funk—not foreboding, but instead promising a good time ahead. On the draw, the nectar-like sweetness of the cap quickly fades yet lingers as an influence, weaving into a flavor profile rich with cream, cocoa, and spice . The strength builds from a mild start to a steady medium near the midpoint and holds strong through the finish. You don’t need to be a master sorcerer to conjure up the Asylum Insidious Maduro—even the most novice smoker can call or click, and soon have these beauties in hand, ready to become a new favorite sidekick. Fans of infused blends like Acid Opulence 3 or premium classics such as Zino Grand Classic Brasil will find common ground in every sultry puff.

Asylum 867 Midnight Oil is the first flavor-infused cigar to bear the Asylum name. This blend was brought about when masterminds Tom Lazuka and Christian Eiroa wanted to do something different with their already hugely successful Asylum brand. The goal was to attract a new audience, people who may not have had much exposure to the world of premium cigars. The result was astounding, and to this day fans of both traditional and flavored cigars revere this stick as one of Asylum’s most innovative lines. Originally marketed as Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon, the Asylum 867 now sports new packaging but still offers the same 3 originally offered varieties: Midnight Oil, Auntie, and Zero. The Midnight Oil is the line where you get the big sizes, including a 6” x 54, a 6” x 60, and a massive 7” x 70, all offering varying renditions of the flavor profile. Made in Honduras under the supervision of Christian Eiroa himself, the 867 series are all Honduran puros, meaning all tobacco used in the production of the cigar is from Honduras. The cigars are infused using a method called steeping, which is similar to aromatherapy. The cap is also sweetened to further influence the unique flavor profile. A highly decorated black and gold box adorned with the Asylum skull logo and a variety of Chinese calligraphy characters houses the expertly rolled vitolas, each one wearing an ornate band along with a tissue wrap covered in Asylum skulls. Each skull clearly displays “Midnight Oil,” denoting the line. Phenomenal construction means an easy and productive draw, a straight burn, and no shortage of thick, blue smoke on each and every puff. Black pepper mingled with hints of cherry sweetness is the opening flavor, soon followed by an earthy array of Honduran goodness. As the cigar progresses, the flavor-infused sweetness seems to diminish and the raw flavor of the tobacco seems to take point, but there are plenty of spikes throughout the smoke where delightful notes of raspberry, green tea, and citrus are undeniably noticeable. The sweet cap ensures the cigar never enters bitter territory at any point. Overall, 867 Midnight Oil finishes as a medium-bodied cigar. Appropriate for both experienced and new cigar enthusiasts alike, 867 Midnight Oil is quite an innovative project. Medium-bodied and uniquely flavorful, this stick is great for just about any occasion. It takes many things the Asylum brand has come to be known for and turns them upside down. The 867 series was the first flavor-infused line offered by Asylum, followed by Cool Brew. Fans of mildly-flavored cigars such as Larutan may want to check this one out, but let’s be honest, Midnight Oil is really in a class of its own. Whether you are a long-time fan of flavored cigars or just want something new and different, Asylum 867 Midnight Oil might just be the next big thing you’re looking for.

Asylum Cigars have officially had their darkest moment, and believe it or not, that’s a good thing! Asylum Nyctophilia takes everything you have come to know and love about the famed original Asylum premium brand and turns it to the dark side. Made in Honduras at Christian Eiroa’s El Aladino factory, this flavor bomb is lavishly layered with only the most premium aged maduro leaves from the inside out. The filler blend consists of dark Nicaraguan leaves, and the binder also hails from Nicaragua. The wrapper is a chocolate brown San Andres wrapper from Mexico, which some consider to be the finest maduro tobacco in the world. This blend mixes classic maduro flavor with bold Nicaraguan body and spice, producing one of the biggest, baddest, most powerful sticks to ever bear the Asylum name. At first glance, the bands closely resemble those worn by the original Asylum blend. The black cedar chest neatly nestling the beautiful vitolas is nearly humidor-grade, and it, too, bears the unmistakable Asylum winged skull motif. Each cigar is expertly rolled and undergoes rigorous quality control measures to ensure maximum performance, and that is exactly what you are going to get every time. An easy draw effortlessly produces copious clouds of thick, white smoke, each puff pounding the palate hard with new flavors as the slow-burning cigar tells its story. The initial blast consists of earthy black pepper and cinnamon, with a heavy oak note lingering in the background. The rich tobacco core dominates throughout the experience, forming a solid backbone for the vast array of both sweet and savory notes as the cigar progresses. Dark chocolate, espresso, and cayenne dance around on the back of the tongue, and the finish is long, earthy, and spicy. Overall, Asylum Nyctophilia finishes as an in-your-face full-bodied powerhouse, something quite reminiscent of the relentless monsters blended by Christian Eiroa in his early years. It is clear to see that Christian Eiroa and his partner in crime, Tom Lazuka, had a blast coming up with this one. It is an all-out awakening of the senses to enjoy such a powerful specimen, and for most, this one should be quite a welcomed change-of-pace. Beginners need not apply; this bad boy is reserved for the experienced. This stick pairs well with a solid bourbon or a cold, dark beer, but strong black coffee would quickly make friends with it, as well. Full-bodied maduro sticks such as Padron Maduro or La Historia by EP Carrillo share similar attributes, so it’s safe to say that if you gravitate towards either, this one is a must-try. Nyctophilia is literally defined as “The love of darkness,” or “being happy or comfortable in the dark.” Don’t be afraid of the dark—embrace it! At least when it comes to Asylum Nyctophilia, that is.

There are basically two images of cigar smokers in popular culture, where you're either a snobby sophisticate or a rowdy badass, but the new Asylum Schizo gives you a chance to be both at the same time. A Nicaraguan puro designed by company co-founder Christian Eiroa in the 'sandwich' style using trimmings from the Asylum Premium, each stogie contains a plethora of medium-bodied flavors entrusted by their creator to defy convention. Proud to hold its own among even the most renowned of vitolas, a smoldering Schizo will bring to mind lofty ideals and a love for your fellow man despite a price so affordable it's downright subversive. You might just lose your mind trying to reconcile the two.

Asylum Schizo is the economical bundle cigar from Christian Eiroa. The Maduro version is very different from the regular Asylum Schizo line. Rather than being a Nicaraguan Puro like the original, Asylum Schizo Maduro is made in Eiroa's Honduran factory using a filler blend of Honduran tobaccos and a dark San Andres Maduro wrapper.

The first puffs of the Asylum 13 Signature Series by Tom Lazuka 46×6 are right where I like them in terms of flavor and intensity; familiar and approachable, yet still lively, dynamic, and offering me a bit of a flavor puzzle to solve. Some black pepper comes along next with varying intensities, an accent in the first two cigars and a spotlight-stealing stage crasher in the third. There’s something in the profile that I can’t quite place, other than to say it’s like an Altoids peppermint wrapped in some light earthiness. It appears on retrohales as well, giving me plenty of chances to figure it out. Flavor is medium, body is medium, and strength is mild. Construction is great thus far, with none of the three cigars giving me any issues. Retrohales at the start of the Asylum 13 Signature Series’s second third are more peppery than they were for most of the first third, filling my nostrils with a tingling sensation and a warm smoke. I also get a bit of a woody cologne aroma in the third cigar, which adds another unique layer to a profile that has already established itself as having something unique about it. That said, I find that the base notes are becoming both less distinctive and intense. There’s still some earth, but it feels like it’s turning into handfuls of plain, dry Corn Flakes. That said, the profile is still very good and it’s remarkably smooth. Flavor sits around medium, body is medium and strength is mild. Construction remains very good as well, and I have no issues with combustion or any other issues. The final third of the Asylum 13 Signature Series by Tom Lazuka 46×6 starts by getting more earthy and a bit more robust overall. It’s a subtle change, but the pepper has been turned up ever so slightly, while I also get a bit of rockiness from the earth. However, it’s still a very smooth profile, as I don’t get any real roughness from the change, and certainly nothing irritating. From there, I get a bit of smokiness both in the flavor and aroma, much like a neighbor firing up a charcoal grill or a fire pit. The Asylum 13 Signature Series by Tom Lazuka 46×6 finishes with a bit more edge, ramping up its flavor intensity to a new high but also staying v
note_sources.title: Asylum 13 Signature Series by Tom Lazuka 46×6

note_sources.text: When Asylum Cigars began as a pet project from Tom Lazuka and former Camacho head man Christian Eiroa, nobody would have ever expected it to take off the way it did. Now, over a decade later and with countless spotlight cigars and awards bearing their name, Asylum continues to wow the cigar world with each and every new release, the most sought-after being the yearly anniversary cigars. Released in 2024, Asylum Twelve celebrates the company’s first 12 years in business, and does so in typical dominating Asylum fashion. This blend is made at the company’s home factory in Honduras using a mostly secret recipe for tobacco from an undisclosed Eiroa-owned farm in South America. While nobody knows for sure exactly what type of tobacco is used, suffice it to say this cigar is an absolute banger. The packaging for the yearly Asylum Anniversary Cigar never leaves anything to be desired, and this remains true here. Stepping aside from the usual wooden coffins, each Asylum Twelve comes snugly nestled in its own aluminum tube. Black and blue is the color scheme, and the eerie color combination no doubt fits the bill for such an imposing beast of a cigar. The construction is phenomenal, and each stick offers a smooth and easy draw producing billowing clouds of thick smoke on every puff. Black pepper and cedar are the first to greet the palate, soon followed by a beautifully dark array of sweet and earthy flavors. Notes of espresso and cocoa wrap around a core of hearty, spicy raw tobacco. The finish is smooth and creamy, and delightful in every way. Medium-full-bodied, Asylum Twelve is certainly one of the company’s crowning achievements. Made with the experienced in mind, Asylum Twelve is a cigar that should only be enjoyed by the true connoisseurs. A well-seasoned palate will surely appreciate all the dark, sweet, and creamy flavors this stick has to offer, and the medium-full-bodied attributes will surely satisfy even the pickiest enthusiast. Pair this stick with coffee, dark beer, or port wine for a truly extraordinary experience. Fans of Asylum’s recent projects including Medulla and Nyctophilia will likely appreciate the Asylum DNA packed inside this one, but make no mistake about it, this cigar is about as refined as it gets. Whether you are a long-time Asylum fan or just like big-ring sticks that offer immense flavor, Asylum Twelve is a special cigar that guarantees satisfaction.

Some would say the original Ave Maria cigar was as close to perfection as a medium-bodied smoke could get. It is hard to believe a stick as good as that could get any better, but the first few puffs on the Ave Maria Reconquista will have you singing hymns from whatever soapbox you can find. This Nicaraguan beauty screams special occasion smoke from its entombed packaging, beautiful Brazilian Habano wrapper, and amazing earthy pre-light aroma. Nicaraguan Habano Ligero binds together a tantalizing blend of Nicaraguan fillers from not one but three different and very unique areas of the tobacco-growing nation. A medium-to full-bodied masterpiece, this stick should be in everyone's humidor for those celebratory moments.

Avo Classic is a cigar that hardly needs an introduction. It's one of the most iconic cigars ever made, from one of the most widely recognized brands in the market. As the top seller of all Avo cigars, the Avo Classic gained fame through the collaboration between Avo Uvezian and Davidoff front man Hendrik Kilner. The blend is simple, yet refined: ultra-premium Dominican filler and binder tobaccos are encased in a golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, carefully aged and fermented to deliver the finest flavor. Having stood the test of time for decades, Avo Classic continues to reign as one of the great cigars of our era. Its slew of 90+ ratings and consistently glowing reviews speak for themselves. Expertly constructed and flawlessly rolled, Avo Classic produces thick, billowing clouds of white smoke. Creamy and earthy, its flavor profile offers subtle notes of light caramel, soft pepper, and raw tobacco . The finish is clean and delicate, and the cigar carries a mild-to-medium body. Despite its gentle nature, the smoothness of Avo Classic is extraordinary, delivering a velvety experience with every puff. While beginners and intermediate smokers can certainly enjoy Avo Classic, its mild profile and nuanced flavors are perhaps best appreciated by experienced connoisseurs with well-developed palates. It pairs beautifully with white wine or champagne and is versatile enough for a relaxed afternoon or as a premium celebration cigar. Comparable cigars include Davidoff Classic and Zino Platinum Crown, both also crafted by Hendrik Kilner alongside Avo Classic. The story behind Avo Classic is as compelling as the cigar itself. Avo Uvezian, frustrated with the high prices of Cuban cigars, decided to create his own brand. The result was Avo Classic—a cigar that, decades later, remains one of the finest and most celebrated sticks on the market.

note_sources.text: The opening puffs are woody with some pepper, and I’m wondering if some habano-seed tobacco is in the blend. It’s pretty lively for the first puffs, as the flavor gets full pretty quickly after being lit. This is especially true for the third cigar, which elicits some coughs and irritates my eyes with its smoke right from the first puff, easily making it the punchiest of the bunch. Early retrohales are peppery and have a bit thinner smoke than what I get from puffs; they are also just a touch sharper and crisper, and in the case of the third cigar, they are fuller. A little earth comes in next, initially reminding me of pretty typical Dominican terroir before it gets heavier and then finishes very dry on my tongue, seemingly soaking up every drop of moisture and leaving me with a very dry mouth and flavors of wood and saltine crackers. Flavor is either medium-full or full, body is medium-plus, and strength is medium-minus. Construction is very good thus far, and all three cigars burn well, produce plenty of smoke, and maintain an even burn line and smooth draw. The second third picks up some creaminess; it’s pretty mellow and not doing much to the profile, but it’s easy to notice the change from the first third. That change becomes more obvious as the intensity of the flavors of the first third gets turned down to a more enjoyable and balanced level, not too far into this section, and I like the softer, sweeter earth that becomes the base of the flavor, while the other flavors take their place in a layered structure. The same change happens to the retrohale, but the result is a little different: the supporting notes remind me of a cake donut, while the pepper hits my nostrils with a quick, sharp, but not particularly strong sensation, one that dissipates fairly quickly. As this section of the AVO Expresivo Robusto comes to a close, there’s still some pepper and a lively woodiness in the flavor, while a bit of mouth-drying continues, though creaminess contributes a good bit to the third cigar’s flavor. That flavor intensity has ranged from medium and back to medium-full, while the body is medium-plus, and the strength is medium-minus. The first two cigars have so
note_sources.title: AVO Expresivo Robusto

When thinking about a cigar's creator it is easy to focus only on the brand or master blender, especially if they are famous, but the AVO Heritage seeks to honor the vast amount of human effort that goes into making our favorite hobby possible. From the farmers around the world who cultivate the best tobaccos in enormous fields before they are harvested, fermented, and aged, to the factory blenders who must faithfully recreate the original recipe for each cigar season to season, to the torcedors who skillfully roll each timeless vitola, to those who band and package each stick, and beyond. Without these fine men and women, you would be unable to enjoy the Heritage's delicious Dominican longleaf filler harmoniously layered beneath the magnificent Ecuadorian Sungrown wrapper.
Wood , Spice , Dried Fruit Available. Learn about AVO XO Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on XO

Avo XO by Davidoff Cigars is a masterful creation that proves a cigar doesn’t need an exotic blend to be extraordinary—it just needs to be crafted by a cigar lover, for cigar lovers. Widely regarded as one of the finest cigars Avo has ever produced, the XO is a richer, more refined evolution of the classic Avo Classic. Made in the Dominican Republic, Avo XO features a premium blend of high-grade Dominican filler and binder tobaccos, finished with a luxurious Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Extra-fermented and long-aged, the tobacco in XO is exceptional, offering a flavor profile that is both complex and unique. Even after years on the market, Avo XO continues to impress enthusiasts worldwide, cementing its status as a timeless classic from the legendary Avo Cigar Company.
