note_sources.text: Earth , Cocoa , Leather Available. Learn about Camacho Criollo Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Criollo

In this ever-changing world in which we are all living, a reliable and delicious cigar like the Camacho Criollo can make every moment worth it. Whether enjoyed with a morning mug of coffee when the day's possibilities are an open book or as an evening's pairing with a rugged Bourbon after a job done well, you'll find an incredible amount of complex flavor packed into each thick vitola. Crafted top to bottom of only the best longleaf tobaccos that have been fermented and aged to perfection, from the Honduran and Dominican Piloto Cubano filler to the succulent Honduran Criollo '98 wrapper, you will find the medium-plus strength Camacho Criollo an essential member of a well-stocked humidor. Putting a large bright yellow and black band on any cigar is a bold decision, but this is a bold cigar and we are talking about Camacho and they are not going to let their reputation die by a thousand small cuts. Instead, as soon as you pull a Camacho Criollo from its cellophane and take a big whiff of the oaky aroma flowing from the vitola, you'll know this ruddy stick means business. Oils will tingle on the lips as the first steady pulls of smoke flood the palate with black pepper and earth, yet there is a creamy undertone of milk chocolate to steady the nerves. Espresso and brown bread drive the second half of the cigar's flavor, with honeyed praline and some bursts of fresh ginger keeping any bitterness at bay to the very end. Give in to your cravings today and order a choice selection of Camacho Criollos to fill those gaps in your stogie collection. You'll be crying tears of joy when they arrive fast and fresh, ready to smoke now or willing and able to be aged for however long you can keep your hands off them. A tough choice, but it's OK to live a little. If you like these, consider adding some Monte by Montecristo AJ Fernandez or Liga Undercrown Shade to your order.

specs.wrapper: that cloaks a spellbinding blend of Honduran Corojo

note_sources.text: Earth , Spice , Espresso Available. Learn about Camacho Triple Maduro Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Triple Maduro

The cigar that started a revolution, the Camacho Triple Maduro cigar is about to knock your socks off once again. Never ones to rest on their laurels, the fine ladies and gents at Camacho cigars are giving all of their cigars a makeover, but don't worry. While many of the core Camacho recipes have been tweaked to bring out, even more, character, the Triple Maduro remains the same blend of ultra-bold, ultra-dark leaves you have come to know and love. It is all still here, from the expertly aged San Andreas wrapper to the dense Corojo Maduro binder, and all the way down into the reams of lush Dominican, Honduran, and Brazilian filler. So what is different about the 'new' Triple Maduro? Well, once you lay eyes on the packaging you will understand. With a new scorpion logo and expressive typography on the band, this is a brand meant to catch the eye and start the mouth to watering before it is even in hand. We know that taste is what really counts though, and this is where the cigar seriously shines. The flavors of toasty cedar and oak fill the mouth with each puff, with the nose discerning loads of spice on the exhale. The further into the cigar the smoker travels, the richer the experience becomes, with dark espresso layered with earth and sweet cocoa . The finale is a crescendo of strength and savory goodness, all packed into thick, creamy smoke. Considered one of the best cigars ever by its legions of fans, any experienced smoker who has yet to try this smoke is encouraged to stop whatever else they are doing and buy some now. There's plenty for all. See Cigar Aficionado Ratings.

Earth , Fruit Drink. Grown in a remote region in the Amazon Rainforest, CAO Amazon Basin uses a rare tobacco called Braganca that is organically grown on unspoiled tropical land and harvested only once every three years

The CAO Amazon Basin is one of the most sought-after limited releases from CAO—a cigar as rare and exotic as the rainforest from which it was born. Debuting in 2014 as a limited-edition cigar, its popularity has led to several subsequent releases. Now, CAO is thrilled to present this special blend in a 6” x 52 Toro edition for 2025 and 2026 . At the heart of this blend lies the rare Bragança tobacco, cultivated deep within a remote region of the Amazon Rainforest . Grown on pristine tropical soil and harvested only once every three years, this leaf is organically grown and truly unique in flavor. The tobacco plants are spaced further apart than normal—about a full yard according to General Cigar Co.—and once harvested, the leaves are rolled into tubes called carottes for six months of aging. Legend has it that the tobacco is then transported out of the rainforest via canoes—a logistical challenge as wild and untamed as the jungle itself. To complement the Bragança’s earthy richness, CAO masterfully layers in tobaccos from five different countries, finishing the cigar with a dark, oily Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The result is a bold, earthy, and complex smoke brimming with natural sweetness, deep spice, and rustic character—unlike anything else in the world of premium cigars. The packaging is as distinctive as the cigar itself, featuring coiled tobacco in place of a traditional paper band, and rustic-inspired boxes. Limited in production and extraordinary in taste, CAO Amazon Basin is a must-have for enthusiasts seeking a one-of-a-kind smoking experience. Untamed, rare, and exotic, this cigar won’t stay in stock long—secure yours before it disappears back into the jungle.
Cream , Oak Drink. Learn about the CAO America - A combination of two American wrappers, Connecticut Broadleaf and Connecticut Shade, for an eye-catching "pinstripe" effect

A tribute to the good ole red, white, and blue, CAO America is a unique dual-wrapped cigar which smokes like a dream. Just as America is called a melting pot, so is CAO America. An extremely unique blend of filler tobacco from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic is paired with tobaccos from Italy as well as America. A spicy Brazilian binder holds it all together. Just as one-of-a-kind as the filler blend is the wrapper. A dual wrapper of Connecticut shade as well as Connecticut broadleaf maduro are utilized to create a barber pole effect. While most list this cigar as a medium-to-full-bodied cigar, the few that we have smoked have resided closer to the medium end of that range. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) CAO America has a beautiful band with an American flag design and a secondary blue and gold band around the foot accented with stars and the eagle seal of America. As striking as this presentation is, what really sticks out is the striped effect the two distinct wrapper leaves give. Mostly visible is the dark and toothy Connecticut broadleaf maduro with a small stripe of the pale and smooth Connecticut shade poking through. CAO America is one of those cigars that builds in strength as you smoke it. On first light we were surprised at the mild but flavorful smoke, but were wondering about how this was listed as medium-full everywhere. The more we puffed, the more we understood. Each draw builds on the last until it hits a crescendo of medium-full-bodied smoke. Burn was perfect, the draw was only slightly tight, but that is to be expected of a cigar with a double wrapper and a thick binder such as this one. It never once distracted from the wonderful taste, and in fact cooled the smoke down to an incredibly tasty level. CAO America is a cigar that will make you want to stand up and salute. A unique looking cigar, with a special blend and a fantastic full flavor. Perfect cigar for an all-American BBQ or a great steak dinner. Other great cigars to try on CAO's hop around the world are their Italia and Brazilia lines. Shop other CAO Cigars:
Herbal , Cocoa , Hazelnut , Raisin Drink. CAO Arcana Thunder Smoke is a transcendent journey for the palate, encapsulating the essence of discovery and the thrill of uncharted flavors

CAO has been a household name in the cigar business for decades. During the cigar boom, and for years after, the brand took off and became a fan favorite worldwide. Despite falling out of the limelight for a short time after, the monster has made a full comeback and is now better than ever. Some would say the highly limited Arcana series is among their best to date, and CAO Arcana Thunder Smoke is doubtless at the top of the list. For this extraordinary cigar, the folks at CAO went to great lengths to find the rarest, most unconventional mix of tobacco to create a blend unlike anything anyone has ever tasted. Well, they hit their mark! Made at the famed General Cigar Factory in the Dominican Republic, Thunder Smoke’s recipe includes a Mexican San Andres binder and a beautiful Olancho San Augustin wrapper leaf from Honduras. The real interesting part, however, is the filler blend, and here we have rare tobacco grown in Cameroon, South Africa, and Zimbabwe. A first for cigars in this part of the world, but the result is nothing short of incredible. Housed in a cedar chest embellished with zebra stripes on top, each 6 ½” x 52 Thunder Smoke wears a massive band that nearly covers the entire cigar. The precision roll is done under exacting standards, and a draw test on every stick ensures a comfortable, productive draw each and every time. Thick clouds of silky white smoke pour from the head of the cigar, pounding the taste buds hard with flavors of espresso and cedar. Notes of hazelnut and raisin linger in the background as an earthy foundation develops that holds everything together. The finish is thick, with notes of fig and cocoa, and overall, Thunder Smoke finishes as a medium-full-bodied cigar with no shortness in terms of complexity. Made for the experienced, Thunder Smoke embodies the vision that the team at CAO set out to achieve when the Arcana series started. This rich, medium-full-bodied flavor bomb is satisfying to the last puff, and never disappoints. Pair it with aged rum or stout for an evening full of excitement, or enjoy it along with a hot cup of espresso to start any day off right. Fans of other unique CAO concoctions such as CAO Brazilia or CAO Session will doubtless enjoy this blend and all the unfamiliar twists and turns it has to offer. This cigar is named after Africa’s famous Victoria Falls, whose native Bantu name is Mosi-Oa-Tunya, literally translated “The Smoke That Thunders.” Whether you are looking for the next big thing from CAO or just want to try a cigar unlike anything you’ve ever smoked, CAO Arcana Thunder Smoke will surely leave a lasting impression.
Cream , Spice , Vanilla Drink. A true CAO Classic,  Black offers the best Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, and pairs perfectly with IPAs or Aged Rum. Check out CAO Black on Cigar World

CAO Black cigar is one of the huge mega-hit cigars that put the CAO Cigar Company on the map. Originally a high-dollar stick made in very limited quantities, CAO Black has become the backbone of the company, so to speak. Made in Honduras originally under the supervision of legend Tim Ozgener, CAO Black consists of a hearty blend of long fillers from Nicaragua, Honduras, and Mexico. A Nicaraguan binder and a beautiful golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper team up to finish the package, creating what has been called a timeless cigar hall-of-famer. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Showing off the precise construction that made CAO what it is today, CAO Black always pours out massive plumes of thick, white smoke, which spills flavors of cedar, vanilla, and earthy tobacco across the palate. The finish is spicy and clean, the body is medium-full, and the texture is always creamy and luxurious, and never overpowering. Beginners can appreciate the smokability of CAO Black, while long-time aficionados love the classic flavor profile that is reminiscent of the great cigars of yesteryear. CAO Black goes well with bourbon, scotch, or even red wine, and is surrounded by a wonderful array of brothers and sisters in the breathtaking CAO lineup, including CAO Gold and CAO Osa Sol. CAO Black has always been a go-to cigar for fans of CAO, and it shows no signs of slowing down from here on out. Shop other CAO Cigars:
Earthy , Nutty , Floral , Toasty Drink. Learn more about CAO Brazilia, Brazil's most outstanding crop of beautiful, seamless wrappers in a masterful, perfectly aged blend with striking flavors

The CAO Brazilia cigar was not the first cigar from the Ozengers, a family that got its start in the tobacco business making pipes and humidors. But it was the one that vaulted the CAO company into a major player in the years after the Cigar Boom, a position they hold to this day. For the Brazilia, CAO partnered with the Toraño family to create something special; a cigar with a dark and spicy Arapiraca wrapper from Brazil to encircle the filler and binder from Nicaragua. This blend has been rated as high as 91 by Cigar Aficionado . Even the band on the cigar is a tribute to its origins, with the Brazilian flag and the 'Handmade designation written in Portuguese: 'Feito á mão'. As if to signify its unusual character, the smooth and finely veined Arapiraca leaf exudes a unique, earthy and phenolic, almost medicinal, aroma. The cigar is soft without being spongy, but the draw after sniping the large cap is nice and firm. A testament to talented torcedors. Not content to be ordinary, the CAO Brazilia starts with a bang as soon as it is lit, offering up coffee and black pepper . This settles after the first inch, but some additional spiciness is added for the second half, including hints of clove as the flavor develops. The CAO Brazilia is certainly a full-flavored cigar , but the strength is not so potent that inexperienced smokers should stay away, as long as they remember to eat well first. A strong cup of coffee or an icy rum and Coke pair marvelously with this cigar. You can find more of the Brazilian magic in the Le Vieja Habana Brazilian Maduro.
Nutty , Toasty , Coffee , Cocoa , Dried Wood Drink. Get a pick-me-up from this exciting, bold blend in the CAO Cameroon and taste its unique combination of cocoa, coffee bean and cedar flavors

CAO Cameroon, also known as CAO L’Anniversaire, was released in observance of the 30 th anniversary of CAO Cigars. Once a giant in the industry, CAO as a company has undergone many changes over the years. For a while, some may even say the brand fizzled out, faltering beneath the hundreds of new names that have risen to fame over the years. However, recent years have proven that this giant was merely taking a nap, and now the brand is as strong as it ever was. As for this classic specimen, we have a delicious cigar made in Nicaragua using an all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend. The wrapper is the star of the show, an aged authentic Cameroon leaf from Africa that delightfully balances the recipe and takes what would be another strong Nicaraguan stick into the realm of mellow, complex, and satisfying. CAO Cameroon has earned a mountain of high ratings over the years, the summit of which was a rock-solid 92 in Cigar Aficionado. A cigar for the ages, this masterpiece is beloved by both aficionados and beginners alike. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) CAO Cameroon has recently undergone a much-needed packaging update, and we can honestly say its new clothes are quite stunning. Green cedar chests and metallic green, white, and red bands make the cigars almost as appealing visually as they are flavor-wise. Speaking of flavor, the thick, white smoke produced with each easy puff of this stick is never short on it. The initial puffs yield a dense woody flavor, with blasts of cedar readily detectable through the nose. Nutty, earthy flavors make up the bulk of the flavor profile, while hints of coffee and cocoa dance around in the background. The finish is sweet and toasty, with just a hint of floral essence on the retrohale. Medium-bodied and immensely balanced, this blend is truly the epitome of a classic Cameroon masterpiece. Whether you are just starting out in the world of cigars or you have been smoking for decades, CAO Cameroon is simply a delight. Medium-bodied and straightforward, it is one of the most versatile offerings from CAO and has been enjoyed by millions over the years. The unique Cameroon flavors of this blend go well with stout, red wine, or whiskey, so no matter what type of libation you enjoy, it’ll likely pair just fine. If you haven’t tried CAO Cameroon, we can tell you that if you have enjoyed such Cameroon sensations as Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva or Oliva Serie G , you’re probably going to take a liking to this one. Don’t let the beautiful new packaging fool you. CAO Cameroon was a classic from day one and remains one of the most popular Cameroon cigars in the world to this day. Shop other CAO Cigars:
Cinnamon , Toasty , Almonds Drink. CAO Fasa Sol emerges as a cigar that not only pays homage to the rich tobacco heritage of Honduras but also showcases the blending prowess of CAO

Don’t let anyone tell you that a CAO FASA Sol cigar should only be smoked during the day—not just because you’re a grownup who can do whatever you want, but also because why rush the enjoyment of one of these Honduran-made delights? We didn’t think so. Any time is the right time to savor the well-aged tobaccos that fill each hearty stogie from tip to toe—a complex blend of Dominican Piloto Cubano and Nicaraguan longleaf from Jalapa, Estelí, and Condega, all of the highest quality. With this succulent filler barely contained beneath a spicy yet smooth Cameroon binder, each medium-full CAO FASA Sol is finished with a ruddy, oily, and flawlessly gorgeous Honduran Olancho San Agustín wrapper, giving this premium stick its delectable kick. Solidly constructed and expertly rolled, each CAO FASA Sol is distinguished by Art Deco-style bands in bright orange with crisp white details, the primary band featuring a crescent-shaped cutout reminiscent of the rising sun. The cigar itself exudes aromas of cedar and alfalfa, while hints of cinnamon and cocoa shine brightly on the tongue during a smooth, effortless draw test. Taking readily to a flame, the well-packed foot ignites to soak the palate with waves of espresso, rich earth, toasted almonds, and vanilla bean. Bursts of baking spice and molasses introduce a deep, luscious sweetness in the first half of the experience, followed by a richer flavor profile loaded with tanned leather and robust dark chocolate. Yet, even as thick clouds of smoke pour from every inch of the vitola, the draw remains lush and cool. A welcome companion to a morning coffee or tea, this gem is just as fitting for an evening indulgence. Don’t hesitate to pair one with your favorite nightcap, whether a brisk gin and tonic or a hearty dram of briny Islay Scotch. Favorably compared to high-end stogies like the Partagas Heritage, the CAO FASA Sol is an excellent choice for nearly every aficionado—so be sure to grab some for yourself before the day is done.

The original CAO Flathead earned its reputation the same way legendary muscle cars do, with big horsepower, bold styling, and enough torque to pin you back in your seat. But not every drive calls for maximum acceleration. Sometimes the open road is best enjoyed with the windows down, the engine humming, and every mile savored. That's exactly where the CAO Flathead Speed Shop Habano shifts into gear. Built with the same unmistakable Flathead attitude, this latest addition to the lineup delivers a smoother, more refined ride while never losing sight of the performance that made the series famous. Handcrafted at STG Estelí in Nicaragua, the Speed Shop Habano is powered by a premium blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican long fillers, secured by a flavorful Mexican San Andrés binder, and wrapped in a gorgeous Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The result is a medium-bodied cigar that trades brute force for balance, allowing every component of the blend to work together with precision and purpose. Like a finely tuned performance engine, the Speed Shop Habano runs effortlessly from start to finish. The draw is smooth, the burn steady, and thick clouds of smoke pour from every puff. Early notes of cedar, roasted nuts, and white pepper establish a solid foundation before giving way to layers of earthy leather, vanilla, and subtle citrus . As the smoke progresses, hints of peanut and natural tobacco sweetness emerge, creating a balanced finish that is rich in flavor without overwhelming the palate. Whether you're already a devoted Flathead fan or looking for an easier-going introduction to the brand, the CAO Flathead Speed Shop Habano proves that performance isn't measured by horsepower alone. Smooth, refined, and built for the long haul, it's the kind of cigar you'll reach for day after day. Fire it up, settle into the driver's seat, and enjoy a premium smoke engineered to keep the good times rolling long after the checkered flag falls.

When CAO Flathead cigars were introduced, they paid homage to our fascinations with hot rods and muscle cars. CAO is now hitting the road on two wheels with the new CAO Flathead Steel Horse . Rigidly square-pressed like the original, Steel Horse are full-bodied sticks featuring a unique blend of Honduran, Dominican, and Nicaraguan filler tobacco, a Brazilian Arapiraca binder, all wrapped in a dark Connecticut Habano Oscuro wrapper. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) CAO Flathead Steel Horse is a very complex cigar which has flavor notes that change as you smoke it. What starts out as a strong full bodied peppery blast , mellows to a nice mocha and earth by the second half. Each puff transforms and blends perfectly with the last. While the pepper may mellow, this cigar stays full and robust the whole way through. You may or may not be a motorcycle enthusiast, either way this is a great cigar for after dinner or after a long ride. CAO is constantly trying new things and the 5-country blend on the CAO Flathead Steel Horse is something everyone who likes heavier cigars needs to try.
Vanilla , Rich Drink. Have a smooth CAO Bella Vanilla, infused with the natural flavors of vanilla bean extracts from Madagascar and wrapped in exotic African Cameroon leaves

CAO Bella Vanilla is considered by many to be among the very best vanilla flavored cigars available. Made in CAO fashion in the Dominican Republic using Cuban seed long fillers, Bella Vanilla is infused using some of the finest vanilla beans in the world: Madagascar vanilla. CAO Cigars didn't overlook any small aspect while blending this cigar, and it is every bit as premium as the rest of the fine cigars that come out of the CAO factory. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Because of the Cameroon wrapper, Bella Vanilla is not only infused with vanilla flavor, but the blend shines with the trademark sweet-spicy profile of the tobacco. Mellow, mild, and delightfully tasty, Bella Vanilla provides a deep, sweet vanilla flavor that pairs wonderfully with the taste of the premium tobacco used in the cigar. Popular among younger smokers and women, CAO Bella Vanilla is very pleasant for just about any palate. It pairs well with coffee and hot chocolate and is a part of the world-famous CAO Flavours series, including Caramelo Joe and Eileen's Dream. For a change of pace, reach for a CAO Bella Vanilla today! Shop other CAO Cigars:
Cherry , Vanilla , Citrus , Sweet Drink. Ignite your palate with CAO Cherrybomb and its bold, yet refreshing notes of cherry and black currants, mellowed by smooth and creamy vanilla

Cigar lovers with a huge sweet tooth and an insatiable desire to try new and different things should look into trying a CAO Cherry Bomb . Made originally under the supervision of Tim Ozgener and friends and coming out of the Dominican Republic, Cherry Bomb is the standard CAO blend of Nicaraguan Cuban seed tobacco and Cameroon wrapper leaf infused with intense cherry flavor. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Medium in body and always smooth, Cherry Bomb begins with huge blasts of cherry sweetness but quickly settles to a very pleasant array of sweet floral flavors including hibiscus, honey, and vanilla . The cherry note remains throughout the experience, gradually building back to the dominant flavor as the cigar progresses. CAO Flavours are considered some of the finest flavored cigars in the business. Cherry Bomb is particularly favored by female cigar connoisseurs due to its intensely sweet nature. It pairs well with fruity cocktails and shares the prestige of all the various blends in the CAO Flavours collection, including Eileen's Dream and Bella Vanilla. Looking for something different? CAO Cherry Bomb is a great place to start!

CAO Eileen's Dream is the most popular cigar of the CAO Flavours Collection. A unique blend enjoyed by many cigar and pipe enthusiasts, Eileen's dream mixes masterful CAO tobacco blending with extreme flavor infusing that never disappoints. Consisting of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco and a Cameroon wrapper, this medium-bodied stick will put a smile on just about anyone's face. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Complexity is the name of the game here. Eileen's Dream starts off with a smooth tobacco flavor laced with hints of coconut and hazelnut. Moving further, heavy notes of whiskey and creamy vanilla become noticeable, along with cocoa and almonds on the finish. Eileen's Dream is for sure a cigar that presents a very memorable smoking experience. It's no wonder why Eileen's Dream has become so popular. It makes cigar connoisseurs wonder how the folks at CAO cram so much flavor into one small package. Eileen's Dream pairs well with Irish whiskey and sweet wine and is a member of the hugely successful CAO Flavours Collection, which includes other cigars such as Earth Nectar and Moontrance. CAO Eileen's Dream is a huge hit among cigar smokers and deserves to be tried at least once by any serious aficionado. Shop other CAO Cigars:
Rich , Sweet , Honey Drink. Experience the variety of Nicaraguan and Connecticut leaf tobaccos that give Gold Honey its sweet flavor and subtle nuances of Florida oranges

The CAO Gold Honey cigar stands as the most refined and nuanced offering within the celebrated CAO Flavours Collection. While many infused cigars lead with an aggressive sweetness, the Gold Honey maintains a masterful balance, featuring a core of premium Dominican and Nicaraguan long-fillers cloaked in a high-quality, golden Cameroon wrapper . This series is designed for the enthusiast who appreciates a mild, mellow smoke that complements—rather than masks—the natural elegance of fine tobacco. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) The defining characteristic of this line is the infusion of artisanal honey harvested from the nectar of Florida orange blossoms . The experience begins with a delicate hint of citrus on the palate, which gradually develops into a rich, floral sweetness derived from this specific regional honey. This evolution culminates in a beautifully defined, natural honey note that remains clean and refreshing from the first light to the final puff. The use of a genuine Cameroon leaf provides a creamy, slightly spicy counterpoint to the infusion, creating a remarkably smooth body and a room note that is famously pleasant. CAO Gold Honey is the definitive "bridge" cigar, making it an ideal choice for traditional connoisseurs curious about infusions or newcomers seeking an approachable starting point. Its understated profile ensures the tobacco base remains the star of the show, providing a sophisticated stepping stone between classic blends and bolder aromatics like Moontrance or Earth Nectar . To fully elevate the floral and honeyed nuances, pair these sticks with a glass of sweet wine, a light rum, or a smooth Highland scotch .
Caramel , Sweet , Bourbon Drink. Light up the CAO Moontrance and taste its notes of exotic fruit, bourbon-vanilla and Georgia peach nectar, finished by sweet Hawaiian white honey

CAO Moontrance is, in essence, a flavored cigar to end all flavored cigars. Made in the Dominican Republic as part of the hugely popular CAO Flavours Collection, Moontrance adheres to the same Dominican, Nicaraguan, and Cameroon blend as the others in the series, and is infused with such exotic elements as fruit, bourbon-vanilla, and Georgia peach. Very interesting and unique, as with all of the CAO Flavours cigars, Moontrance always delivers an ultra-premium experience to the fan of flavored tobacco products. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Moontrance is rich and sweet all the way through. Almost immediately, a blast of vanilla screams across the palate, leaving a trail of sweet, fruity nuances behind. On the finish, sweet honey is noticeable on the tip of the tongue, as well as a rich bourbon note through the nose. Complex, smooth, and very enjoyable, Moontrance has become very popular among younger connoisseurs. It's mild enough for anyone to try and pairs well with white wine or orange juice, as a compliment to the citrus flavors that make this cigar so interesting. If you like Moontrance, you will no doubt love cigars such as Eileen's Dream and Earth Nectar. See what everyone's been talking about and try a Moontrance tonight!
Earth , Pepper , Cocoa , Nut Drink. Experience the CAO Gold, it enjoys a devoted fan base receives some of the highest ratings in the industry, boasting 90 ratings from multiple sources

Updated packaging offers a new look for this classic cigar, but the CAO Gold is just as lip-smacking as the day it first rocked the mellow-smoking world. Lost to the mists of history is whether the Gold was the first early CAO mega-hit, and there were many, yet this 90-rated treasure can even now become your all-time favorite mild-medium stogie. Properly classified as a member of the brand's Classic lineup, it is a premium cigar filled to the brim with an alluring blend of Nicaraguan longleaf as both filler and binder to prompt a rush of excitement from every type of smoker. The shimmering Ecuadoran Connecticut wrapper will drive even the most jaded of tobacco prospectors into a fever of delight and desire. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) The new band design that adorns each expertly constructed vitola certainly adds an updated touch of style to the silky and golden-brown Shade wrapper. But the CAO Gold needs little help in drawing your attention. A cold draw allows an aroma like warm pastry to entice the nose while spices sparkle on the tongue. Leather and cedar predominate the creamy smoke soon after lighting, but you won't have to dig deep to find richer veins of flavor. Nutmeg and marzipan swirl together to keep the hints of black pepper and licorice from becoming overwhelming, while vanilla and orange peel join to create a rich, warm undercurrent. Heavy in hand, yet light on the wallet, building up a cache reserve of these great cigars is the type of planning ahead anyone can appreciate. Take a trip down memory lane or forge new friendships with the CAO Gold, but don't forget to expand your holdings into other CAO gems like the stunning MX2 or the potent Flathead. Diversification of your smoking choices is always the smart move. Shop other CAO Cigars:

note_sources.text: Coffee , Cream , Butter Drink. Learn about the CAO Gold Maduro - An exciting blend with a smooth, buttery character of CAO Gold with refined flavor of an oily Brazilian maduro wrapper

It's pretty obvious from the name alone that the CAO Gold Maduro cigar is the CAO Gold with a different wrapper. What isn't so easy to see is what this type of change can do to a smoke's profile. It's a good thing that the brains behind CAO know that to make a Maduro it's not just a matter of finding a dark wrapper and throwing it on top of an existing blend. You need to make sure that the flavor of the new wrapper pairs with that of the filler and binder. So, while the original Gold contained a rich concoction of Nicaraguan tobaccos beneath an Ecuadorian shade , the Gold Maduro adds potency and kick with a Brazilian wrapper aged what may have been forever before being applied. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) What results is a smooth, balanced flavor able to be appreciated by each and every smoker, from the most grizzled of daily smokers to being a good choice as the first smoke ever for a budding aficionado. Between the rich tobacco taste and a refreshing coffee and wood backbone, there's a lot to love and very little to critique, even for those so inclined. Solidly packed with an open draw and a sweet aroma, you may wonder why it's taken so long for you to try one. Having been around long enough to have garnered plenty of press, when you kick back with a CAO Gold Maduro, don't worry about taking notes or trying to determine which field each leaf came from. Instead, the only things you'll have to think about are enjoying your time, your company, and your beverage. Just make sure you have plenty of each, since they burn slow, are perfect for handing out to buddies, and pair well with everything from a cold lager to a hot coffee to a whiskey sipped right around room temp. CAO Gold Maduro cigar review.

Handmade in Nicaragua, Havana Daydreamin' presents a dreamy medium-bodied package consisting of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco hugged tightly by a gorgeous Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf. With Havana Daydreamin' CAO Cigars continues their legacy of amazing high-end tobacco products. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Named after the famous Jimmy Buffet song, Havana Daydreamin' brings a pleasurable smoking experience from beginning to end. Starting with smooth, toasty notes, it evolves into a simple, yet refined and flavorful package of spicy cedar and creamy, grassy notes. It's ideal for someone looking for a medium-bodied cigar that's packed with a ton of character. Perfect for a cool night on the beach or the boat, Havana Daydreamin' is a fantastic smoke for just about anyone, beginner or connoisseur. It pairs well with bourbon or light beer and can be compared to other CAO cigars such as Cameroon and Osa Sol. Take a quick trip to your personal island paradise with CAO Havana Daydreamin'. CAO Italia is an infamous outside-the-box cigar from a company known for its innovative blending techniques. After searching long and hard for new ways to blend a great-tasting cigar, the team from CAO stumbled upon a part of Italy known as Benevento, where cigar tobacco not only grows, it flourishes! Taking what they found in Italy and combining it with a blend of Peruvian and Nicaraguan filler, an Honduran binder, along with a Honduran habano wrapper, CAO created the Italia, a cigar that has turned out to be one of the most successful cigars CAO has ever brought out. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Flavorful, rich, and potent, CAO Italia begins with a chocolatey sweetness that intensifies as the cigar progresses. There are bold, earthy flavors, along with an array of spicy pepper and some sweet floral notes as well. This cigar is inevitably unique and very satisfying in the flavor department. CAO Italia is medium-full in body and flavor, making it a great cigar for intermediate and experienced smokers alike. A complex cigar like this combines beautifully with red wine and bourbon. Enjoy after a pasta dinner for a true Italian experience! Other great and unique cigars from CAO include Brazilia and America. Italian tobacco in a premium cigar? You better believe it! CAO Cigars is known for keeping up with the times, and La Traviata Maduro has come to be a huge hit among die-hard maduro fans everywhere. It consists of a rich blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican filler tobaccos, a cameroon binder, and a deep, dark Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper. Medium-full in body and flavor, La Traviata Maduro is a must-try offering from the legendary CAO Cigar Company. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) CAO La Traviata Maduro oozes natural oils and boasts seamless construction. A steady stream of gray smoke brings forth a hearty, sweet flavor profile with notes of chocolate and coffee. Spicy white pepper tickles the palate and the finish is snappy and clean. Once again, CAO has produced a masterpiece. La Traviata Maduro is a great cigar for everyone. Never overpowering and very decently priced, it is a safe bet for any occasion. La Traviata Maduro pairs well with coffee and dark beer. Similar cigars include CAO MX2 and Casa Magna Oscuro. A great new cigar from a well-known, classic brand, CAO La Traviata Maduro has proven to be a hit. Shop other CAO Cigars:

CAO Maduro is one of the finest cigar offerings from tobacco giant CAO in Nicaragua. Born in the 90s and still going strong, CAO Maduro continues to reunite cigar freaks everywhere with the classic, elegant maduro taste from the cigars of old. This gorgeous black beauty has a hearty blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers, an Ecuadorian binder, and a beautiful triple-fermented Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) When it comes to an old-school maduro flavor profile, CAO Maduro is tough to beat. Beginning with rich chocolate and coffee notes, CAO Maduro progresses with nuances of white pepper, earth, and raw tobacco. The finish is long and spicy, and the cigar gains strength as it's smoked. If you haven't tried CAO Maduro, yet, love maduro cigars, you're missing out. Very few specialty blends from the 90s have survived to see today's market, yet CAO Maduro keeps impressing connoisseurs everywhere, old and new. It pairs well with coffee as a morning smoke or port wine as a relaxing cigar before bed. Similar cigars include Punch Maduro and Hoyo de Monterrey Maduro. CAO Maduro captures the true essence of what a maduro cigar should be. Shop other CAO Cigars:

CAO MX2 is one of the most unique maduro cigars available. Hand crafted in Nicaragua, MX2 is a special maduro in that it has not one, but two different maduro wrappers—a juicy, black Connecticut broadleaf on the outside, and a spicy Brazilian leaf on the inside. The filler and binder blend is a robust mixture of tobaccos from Peru, Nicaragua, Honduras, and the Dominican Republic. Very potent and full of flavor, the MX2 is a satisfying cigar for more experienced smokers that want a little more kick to their maduros. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) This dark beauty starts off with a rich combination of coffee and cocoa . Underlying nuances of caramel, cinnamon, and earthy tobacco round out a complex, spicy flavor profile , and the finish is long and heavy. MX2 makes a wonderful change of pace to any maduro fanatic's arsenal. The CAO MX2 is a different style of maduro, but it still is, well, a maduro. Expect a classic maduro flavor profile with all the exciting extras the good folks at CAO have thrown in. It pairs well with dark beer and coffee and can be compared to CAO Brazilia and Hoyo de Monterrey Double Maduro. Step outside the box and try a CAO MX2 today.

CAO Osa Sol is among the newest and hottest cigars from CAO. "Osa Sol" literally translated "Sun Bear," aptly named in reference to the gorgeous one-of-a-kind sungrown wrapper leaf used on this fine cigar, grown in the Olancho Valley in Honduras. A delicious mixture of Nicaraguan and Honduran fillers, along with a broadleaf binder, make Osa Sol a truly fantastic cigar, especially for fans of fuller, more Cuban-style blends. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) Osa Sol burns clean and tight, with a draw producing billowing volumes of heavy, silky smoke. Overall, the flavor profile is simple, with a main note of earthy tobacco and copious amounts of spice. Undertones include honey, black cherry, and leather, with a clean, peppery finish. CAO Osa Sol is a great cigar for intermediate connoisseurs looking to step up to a full-bodied cigar. Rich and spicy, Osa Sol pairs well with coffee and bourbon. Fans of Osa Sol might be interested in the CAO LX2 and Punch Upper Cut. Always on the cutting edge of cigars, CAO scores big once again with Osa Sol. Shop other CAO Cigars:
Spice , Cedar , Pepper , Nuts , Cocoa Drink. CAO Pilón uses a time-honored method to give you a cigar with deep, rich colors and unprecedented depths of flavor

It's strange to be living in a time when CAO, creator of the new Pilon cigar, is considered an old-school establishment brand. Fortunately they are not stuck with the name of some company that first existed a century ago and has long since lost its mojo, because the company founded by Cano A Ozgener is still going strong and innovating in a business where tradition is usually the most powerful motivator. To encompass both desires, the Pilon is both named after and utilizes an old and nearly forgotten method for slowly fermenting tobacco in small batches which mellows the robust Nicaraguan filler and binder just enough to compliment the spicy Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. (Shop other CAO Cigars ) The CAO Pilon is a gorgeous cigar to behold, with a smooth golden brown wrapper highlighted by a few thin veins. The cream colored wrapper is both elegant in design and amazingly informative: 'Loté Pequeño' (or small batch) to indicate the small batch status, a listing the various tobaccos used for each component, the name and size of the particular vitola, and even a pictogram of the Pilon circular fermenting process. How cool! With this wealth of knowledge to guide you, it's still the flavor which will astonish and amaze. Full of dark cocoa, toasted nuts, sweet cedar and warm spices, these medium strength delights will never disappoint. Yeah, sorry to say you're going to have to pay a hefty price if you want to stash some of these away for a special… wait, what? They're how much?...Sorry, had to get up off the floor. Ok, so wow. These CAO Pilon cigars are like the deal of the century and we're far enough into the new millennium to where that means something. Don't worry, there are still a few years left for other brands to catch up. Shop other CAO Cigars:

Earthy , Smooth , Spicy , Caramel Drink. We know a thing or 2 about making great cigars. I mean we’ve been doing this a long time. Some may even say we’re the best in the universe. But, hey, who are we to disagree. So, to celebrate the fact that Pilon Anejo is an exquisite blend that pushes the envelope of flavor. 

An oily Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper covers a rich Honduran Habano binder, filled with seco and ligero leaf from the Dominican and Nicaragua.

This spicy cigar blend was rolled in 2019 and intentionally aged for an extra 2 years to let the complex blend continue to evolve and mature. These cigars are super savory, rich, with a hit of spice. 

Pilon Anejo is an exercise in patience…we wanted to bring this out earlier because it was so good, but we had to remind ourselves that good things happen to those who wait.

In the world of premium cigars, CAO is a name that has come and gone over the years, so to speak, in that at times they seem to disappear into the background, but out of nowhere they’re again riding the crest of the wave. The latter is certainly the case with cigars like CAO Pilon Anejo , a special blend that was originally intended to be a one-time offering but has now been given a permanent spot in the company’s star-studded portfolio. “Pilon Anejo” literally translates to “aged pile,” and it refers to the centuries-old curing technique the folks at CAO and STG Danli in Honduras decided to use to get the tobacco just right for the blend. As far as the blend goes, the filler blend consists of Seco and Ligero leaves from Nicaragua. The binder is Nicaraguan Habano, and the wrapper is an exquisite, matured Ecuadorian Habano leaf that pulls everything together. The tobacco has undergone extensive aging and curing prior to rolling, but even still, after manufacture, the cigars rest another 2 years to fully mature, making this project a very long time in the making. Crisp and clean cedar chests house the expertly rolled vitolas, each one wearing a black and white band depicting the pile of tobacco leaves referred to as a “Pilon.” Precision rolling ensures an easy draw that offers plenty of smoke on each and every puff, along with a straight burn and a long, tight ash. The flavor journey begins with a hefty dose of spicy pepper, a note that remains throughout the duration of the smoke. This intensity soon settles, however, and the spicy attributes join a medley of smooth caramel, fragrant cinnamon, and aromatic cedar . Everything wraps nicely around an earthy raw tobacco core, bringing about a true homage to the classic Cuban cigars of old. Medium-full-bodied, Pilon Anejo is expertly balanced and never overpowering. Though straightforward enough for a newer cigar enthusiast to enjoy, the CAO Pilon Anejo is far more appropriate for more experienced connoisseurs. Its medium-full-bodied nature, along with the classic and robust flavor profile, demands a well-seasoned palate to truly appreciate the goodness this stick has to offer. It pairs well with dark rum, porter, or any medium-full-bodied beer, and is best enjoyed after a meal or in the evening. Fans of CAO’s other flavor bombs such as Flathead or Consigliere will likely enjoy this blend, and perhaps even prefer it. Whether you are a long-time fan of CAO and have been burning them since the Cigar Boom days, or you just want the next premium stick that is going to take things to another level, CAO Pilon Anejo is a choice that you will by no means regret making.
Earthy , Woody , Toasty , Nutty Drink. CAO Vision was named one of the top ten cigars of 2007 by Cigar Aficionado

Rising from the ashes of the Cigar Boom of the early 1990’s, the CAO Cigar Company took a visionary approach to tobacco perfection, and it may have finally been achieved in the CAO Vision 2022 cigar. After quickly building an intricate portfolio of world-spanning and world-class cigars, CAO’s founders elevated the concept of cigars to heights of flavor never before achieved with the first CAO Vision in 2007, a rare ultra-premium. The spectacular and updated 2022 release contains a hearty medium-full blend of Nicaraguan longleaf from Condega, Jalapa, and Esteli beneath a well-aged Honduran Jamastran wrapper. Toothy and coated with an oily sheen, each exquisite 6” x 52 toro smells of the volcanic soil itself from which the tobacco grew and ripened in sweltering heat. Through a steady draw, the taste of the unlit stick is rich with cedar and raw spice. A thick flame brings out the first hints of a caramel-like sweetness that will linger throughout the entire smoke, but the primary flavors are espresso, fresh-grated nutmeg and cocoa and red plum. During the second half, the profile shifts to another spectrum full of dark earth, toasted almonds, leather, sea salt, and a touch of cinnamon. You only live once, and this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, because just 2,700 boxes of these stogies were produced. Envision smoking a CAO Vision 2022 and then become that future version of yourself. Do be aware that even if you’re looking to buy just one of these delicious handmade, it is time to make your move – our supply is very limited. note_sources.text: Guardian of the Farm is an ultra-premium cigar made by connoisseurs, for connoisseurs. Produced by one of the industry's premier boutique brands, Warped Cigars , Guardian of the Farm is the second blend in a star-studded collaboration with Casa Fernandez , following the popular 2015 release, Futuro . The masterminds behind the project are Kyle Gellis of Warped Cigars and Max Fernandez of AGANORSA . Given the opportunity to pool their talents and utilize some of the finest Nicaraguan tobacco on the planet, these two phenoms produced something truly extraordinary. This delicious Nicaraguan puro combines an all-Nicaraguan blend of premium aged filler ( Corojo '99 and Criollo '98 ) and binder ( Corojo '99 ) leaves beneath a stunning Nicaraguan Corojo '99 wrapper . The result speaks for itself—backed by a 93 rating and the No. 8 spot on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 of 2017 ! The name Guardian of the Farm , along with the bulldog depicted on the band and packaging, pays homage to the American Bulldogs used to guard the AGANORSA tobacco farms in Nicaragua. The roll is impossibly precise, the draw is spot-on, and the burn is razor-sharp. An unfinished foot provides a head start on t he combustion of the world-class wrapper leaf, further intensifying the initial flavor. Enormous plumes of white smoke greet the palate with an opening burst of woody spice and creamy raw tobacco , quickly followed by a medley of sweet, bready notes alongside hints of cinnamon and pepper . The finish is long and smooth yet impeccably clean, leaving subtle traces of creamy vanilla and cayenne on the tip of the tongue. Medium-full-bodied and meticulously complex, Guardian of the Farm delivers one of the most unique smoking experiences of recent years. Built specifically for a highly experienced audience, Guardian of the Farm is a stick where beginners need not apply; its subtle complexities and rich, silky flavor profile demand a discerning palate. Sitting comfortably at a medium-full body , it serves as a fantastic match for a special bottle of single malt scotch . Smokers who enjoy the original Casa Fernandez Aganorsa Leaf Miami will be thoroughly pleased, as will fans of classic Nicaraguan Corojo sticks like Don Pepin Blue and My Father . Guardian of the Farm was bound for greatness from the start, and it continues to expand its fanbase among the world's most serious smokers. Seize the opportunity today to experience one of the finest premium cigars in recent memory.

It has been nearly a decade since AGANORSA Leaf rocked the cigar world with the introduction of Guardian of the Farm, an ultra-premium line named after the hounds that guarded the famed AGANORSA farms in Nicaragua. Several spin-offs have come about, many highly regarded, but in 2021, the blend that would garner the most attention of all made its earth-shaking debut: Guardian of the Farm Cerberus . A true Nicaraguan puro, this blend is rolled at the AGANORSA factory in Nicaragua using only the finest Nicaraguan leaves—wrapper, filler, and binder. What makes this blend so special is the inclusion of a Corojo 2012 wrapper leaf, one that has never before been used in an AGANORSA blend. Well, they hit the nail on the head, as to date this top-shelf stick has yet to receive any ratings lower than 90 . If you don’t trust numbers, though, don’t worry. We can just about guarantee that you are going to fall in love with this stick from the very first puff. A beautiful black and gold box makes a splendid presentation for this luxurious cigar, and the black and gold bands on each cigar match the motif, each one depicting the mythical 3-headed dog after which the line is named. Expert craftsmanship means the cigars aren’t just beautiful, but functional as well. A smooth and productive draw offers an easy way to enjoy the flavor profile to the full, as each puff douses the palate with volumes of silky blue smoke. Spicy white pepper combines with cedar to create a gorgeous opening. Soon after, the earthy core of the flavor profile comes to the forefront, offering dense flavor spiked with hints of nuts and black cherry . Spice builds throughout the experience, coming to a climax about halfway through and remaining until the end. Hefty doses of red pepper are noticeable on the finish, and overall Guardian of the Farm Cerberus finishes as an impeccably balanced full-bodied cigar. Made for experienced connoisseurs , Guardian of the Farm Cerberus can be thought of as the most exclusive of the series, offering depth, complexity, and balance while providing a satisfying full-bodied smoking experience every single time. It pairs beautifully with scotch or bourbon and presents as a wonderful celebration cigar. Heck, even the artwork alone is sure to start conversations. Compared to the original Guardian of the Farm, this stick can be thought of as just a bit stronger and more refined, but we urge you to give it a try, especially if you are a fan of the original. Looking for the next ultra-premium Nicaraguan puro that will never leave you disappointed? Look no further than Guardian of the Farm Cerberus and experience a cigar whose bark certainly matches its bite!

casa-fernandez-guardian-of-farm-night-wa.name: Guardian of the Farm Night Watch

note_sources.text: Guardian of the Farm Night Watch is the second cigar in the Guardian of the Farm lineup from AGANORSA Leaf and Casa Fernandez , and this time the famed blend features a maduro wrapper . Made in Nicaragua at Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. under the watch of head honcho Max Fernandez Pujals , Nigh t Watch continues the Guardian of the Farm theme of commemorating not only the four hounds guarding the Fernandez family tobacco farms, but, in the words of Fernandez himself, "Every dog, whether it is one of ours or your own". As for the blend, this example sports a hearty mix of Corojo and Criollo filler and binder leaves from Jalapa an d Est elí , along with a dark and very unique Jalapa Corojo Maduro wrapper leaf . The result is a much stronger blend than the original, made for those who loved the first stick but wanted just a little more "oomph." Lovingly packed in crisp white cabinet chests and wearing luxurious white and gold bands, Night Watch certainly appears to be quite the high-end cigar . The mottled dark brown wrapper leaf glistens with oil and it is readily apparent that the construction is impeccable. As for the smoking experience, a productive draw gives off rich, blue smoke, beginning with a bl ast of Nicaraguan pepper and soon relaxing into a stunning array of earthy tobacco , dried fruit , and coffee . Hints of chocolate and brown sugar linger in the background, all the while building up to a dry, clean finish. Night Watch resides on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied , combining strong flavor with balance and complexity in true AGANORSA Leaf fashion. While the cute pup on the band may suggest that the cigar in question is fun and friendly to everyone, Night Watch , like the original Guardian of the Farm release, is in fact an ultra-premium cigar meant for experienced connoisseurs . Just a notch or two shy of full-bodied , this blend boasts subtle complexities and a flavor story that can on ly be truly appreciated by a well-developed palate. N ight Watch pairs well with dark beer , coffee , and tawny port , and makes for a great end to a hectic day. It should appeal quite nicely to fans of fuller-bodied dark cigars such as La Mission du L'Atelier or Roma Craft CroMagnon , but tru ly Night Watch is in a class of its own. They say every dog has its day. In the case of Guardian of the Farm Night Watch , this dog promises to have not only a day, but many years of being in the spotlight of modern premium cigars .

The Casa Fernandez Miami Reserva cigar is a Nicaraguan puro released as part of an effort by Tabacalera Tropical to benefit from their own success. Well known for strict quality control throughout the entire cigar production cycle; Tropical has produced a number of highly-rated smokes for others and the gained experience has resulted in a line of super-premium cigars under their own Casa Fernandez label. The Miami Reserva is one of these chock full of Aganorsa tobaccos from the higher primings, from Seco on up to include the rare Medio Tiempo. Sprouting on less than a quarter of tobacco plants, these two small, sun-soaked leaves are found above the Ligero and impart a unique robustness. (Shop other Nicaraguan cigars ) The Miami Reserva has a rugged yet elegant appearance, with a thick and gnarled wrapper that glistens with oils. Proper storage of this cigar is a must to ensure a straight burn from the beginning, but the diligent aficionado will be rewarded with a pleasing draw and mouth-watering plumes of fragrant smoke. The initial flavors are definitively Nicaraguan, rich and spicy, but not harsh. With an initial strength hovering around medium, the cigar begins to pick up strength during the second half when some raisin-like sweetness can be detected against a leathery core. The finish is a full bodied affair that rewards experienced smokers and humbles the rest.

Made in the heart of Miami, Florida, the Casa Fernandez Miami Reserva Maduro is an amazing flavorful cigar. Using the same wonderful blend as the natural Miami Reserva line, this cigar adds a level of complexity to the flavor with a beautiful San Andres Maduro wrapper. The filler is the same rare Medio Tiempo leaves from the famed Aganorsa SA farms in Nicaragua. This medium-to-full bodied smoke is something to be experienced. (Shop other Medium-Full bodied cigars ) Usually the top leaves of a tobacco plant are the ligero, but on rare occasions there are a few that grow above these. These Medio Tiempo leaves are very rare, but also extremely coveted due to the amount of flavor that they impart. In the Casa Fernandez Miami Reserve Maduro, these top primings are used in the filler and the flavor is unbelievable. The addition of the maduro wrapper brings flavor notes of sweet chocolate into an already prominent leather and spice profile. The Casa Fernandez Miami Reserva Maduro takes an already outstanding cigar and kicks it up a notch with added complexity and flavor. If you are looking for a more heavy peppery cigar then the regular Miami reserva is perfect, but if you want to experience what a great maduro wrapper brings to the table, you will not be disappointed by this.

The Casa Magna cigar was named Cigar of the Year by Cigar Aficionado in 2008 . It is a Nicaraguan puro using leaves from both Esteli and the Jalapa Valley. The robusto garnered an unbelievable rating of 93 points, which is made even more special given its LOW price tag. Created by two cigar industry superstars, Manuel Quesada and Nestor Plascencia, the Casa Magna certainly delivers in the bang for your buck department. (Shop other Nicaraguan cigars ) It has a very earthy flavor profile which shifts on it's own over the course of the cigar with highlights of creaminess, almond butter, sweet cherries, caramel, warm spices, cedar, and leathery notes all joining the earth's profile. This Casa Magna has many nuanced flavor notes and one really needs to pay attention while smoking to taste them all. Any cigar rated #1 by Cigar Aficionado is one that you should try but even more so when it is a stick that just about anyone can get their hands on. The Casa Magna is pretty much a sure thing.

I’m not surprised to find that the draws of all three cigars each feel just a bit labored right out of the gate, not plugged or obstructed, but not moving as freely as might be ideal. I’d call it equivalent to walking through a fairly full sports venue; you’re moving but you’re not at full stride. Flavor-wise, there is some creaminess, a bit richer spin on the bread flavor, some dry earthiness, and just a bit of white pepper that takes the finish into a sensation that slightly dries out the mouth. There are a few puffs that have an interesting richness that almost tastes like the bread got soaked in room-temperature cola, a standout flavor both for its uniqueness and that it seems like a counterbalance to the rest of the profile. But otherwise, it seems like a profile tailor-made for a latte or other coffee drink with a bit of milk in it. Past the one-inch mark, there are a few puffs where I pick up some lightly buttered popcorn, a familiar and enjoyable flavor, even if I don’t eat the stuff regularly. The first third ends up being largely a mix of subtle creaminess, some bread-like chewiness, a very light bit of dry earthiness, and a fairly steady amount of light pepper that only occasionally stands out as more than an accent. It’s a medium-minus flavor profile with medium body and mild strength. In terms of construction, one cigar develops a massive split in its wrapper, while the other two remain intact. Beyond that, all three samples burn well with a razor sharp burn line and decent smoke production, though the draw still tends to be a bit firm. If there’s one thing that I wasn’t expecting to pick up from the Casa Magna Connecticut Toro, it’s the light terroir that it has offered, and the second third continues with it as a notable part of the profile. It’s not a dominant part of the profile—though nothing really is at the moment—but it has an aspect that reminds me of Honduran terroir, which helps it to stay close to the forefront. While the first third had been on the smoother end of the spectrum, the second third starts to toast the flavors, starting with the bread and moving to the wood, which dries out that aspect and gives it a touch of char. The black
note_sources.title: Casa Magna Connecticut Toro

note_sources.text: Casa Magna took the world by surprise when Cigar Aficionado named it the top cigar of 2008 beating out the likes of Fuente, Padrón and Pepín. While there have been small additions to the core line itself, there really hasn't been a big splash for the past three years, until now. The Casa Magna Domus Magnus cigar was released at the 2011 IPCPR show, the first major addition to the partnership between Manuel Quesada and Nestor Plasencia. Casa Magna is blended by Manuel Quesada and made at Plasencia Cigars S.A. The Domus Magnus project was originally a limited release of one-hundred thousand cigars split between two Optimus and Primus vitolas. The insane popularity of these cigars and apparently just enough tobacco left over for another 30,000 or so cigars led to a 2nd release of the Domus cigars, only this time they were released in 3 different vitolas than the initial release, limited to 1,000 boxes of each. They were the Centuriones, Praetores and Bellatores. (Shop other Cigar Aficionado Top Rated Cigars ) Now Casa Magna is back and at it again with the Domus Magnus II cigars. They're out of the original Domus Magnus wrapper leaf but they're using the same Jalapa Sun Grown leaf from the 2007 crop this time around. They'll now be a regular production cigar and that is great news for smokers everywhere. For now, only the original Optimus and Primus vitolas will be available but it's always possible they will add more options for us in the future. The flavor notes of the original Domus are present with a mix of acidic citric sweetness, pepper and chocolate and with a lingering caramel coffee note to balance it all out. Many bloggers have rated this cigar in their Top 25, Top 10 and even Top 5 lists over the last 2 years and it isn't hard to see why. Give them a shot and we're sure you'll be waiting to see what Casa Magna comes up with for Domus Magnus III.

The Casa Magna Oscuro cigar shows lightning can strike twice when two of the greatest men in the tobacco business join forces to rain down succulent and powerful enjoyment onto the masses of flavor-hungry smokers. Following on the success of the original Casa Magna, christened 2008's Cigar of the Year by Cigar Aficionado Magazine, MATASA head Manuel Quesada once again called on Nestor Plascencia's Segovia Cigar Factory to create a smoke of exceptional craftsmanship using a jet-black Nicaraguan Oscuro wrapper to further enhance the lush blend of Nicaraguan and Honduran filler tobaccos. If you can resist getting it lit a close examination of the cigar yields a funky barnyard aroma emanating from the smooth wrapper, the color so dark it seems to absorb light. The body of the cigar resists all but the firmest of pressure, and the draw once the cigar is aflame works through the dense leaves slow and cool bringing flavors of mild spice and anise. The clouds of smoke build in strength and carry charred oak to the palate, showering vanilla and coffee throughout. In one last feat of cigar-making talent, the finale of the experience is full-bodied while the strength remains a couple of notches above medium to remain accessible to all smokers. Eat a fine meal, mix up an Old Fashioned using a classic Rye, and sit back with good company while enjoying the Casa Magna Oscuro. An Ortega Serie D Maduro cigar is similar on the lighter end, and a Camacho Triple Maduro is more of the same goodness on the heavy side.

Earlier this year, the family announced it would be selling a new brand of cigars, bearing its name, separate of Altadis U.S.A.: Casa Turrent. At the 2015 IPCPR Convention & Trade Show , the Casa Turrent Serie 1901 was made available to retailers in the U.S. for the first time after two years on the market outside the U.S., launching domestically in three sizes. While the Casa Turrent is made in Mexico at a factory owned by the family, it’s not a Mexican puro. It uses a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper, San Andrés criollo and Nicaraguan double binder with a mixture of San Andrés criollo and negro in the filler along with some tobacco from Nicaragua. The shape sort of looks like a Padrón with a fairly aggressive box press complimented by some rounder edges. Because of the dual bands and somewhat shorter size given the amount of length taken up by the tip, there’s quite a bit of cigar covered up by gold paper. There’s a medium aroma with a lot of leather, some charcoal and cocoa. The Casa Turrent’s foot is interesting with some sweet strawberries, Ritz crackers and some dry pasta. Some of that manages to finds its way on the cold draw, notably the strawberries and pasta, but it’s overwhelmed by a sweet milk cocoa and some floral flavors. While it’s not a bad start, the promise of the cold draw isn’t fulfilled. There’s a sweet cocoa, nuttiness, meatiness and some orange peel. It’s medium, but somewhat dry and not as rich as the cold draw was. As the cigar burns down, the cocoa remains on top surrounded by some woodiness that shifts between oak and cedar. There’s some sort of funky, salty meatiness that I can’t quite place. At times it tastes like some of the more tender pieces of generic store-bought beef jerky, but other times, it’s not a flavor I specifically recognize. By the end of the first third, the Casa Turrent is full in flavor, medium in body and medium and strength. For the most part, construction is great. Both samples burn extremely evenly, but one starts tunneling in the beginning of the second third. A quick touch-up fixes that and construction is fully back on track. There’s a harsh earth that emerges out of the meatiness and starts to overtake the
note_sources.title: Casa Turrent Serie 1901 Torpedo

specs.filler: Mexican San Andrés Corojo & Criollo, Nicaragua

note_sources.text: Starting out, the Casa Turrent Serie 1973 has a fairly simple profile with a creamy oak and leather combination that is effortlessly dominant, followed by much lessor flavors of anise, tobacco, dark chocolate and earth. There is a slight—and I do mean slight—indeterminate sweetness and some white pepper on the retrohale that both become a bit more evident as the first third burns down, but neither are strong enough at this point to really affect the profile in any significant way. Construction-wise, both the burn and draw are excellent so far and smoke production is above normal. The strength in the blend is noticeable, but not aggressive, and ends the first third noticeably short of the medium mark. Unfortunately, the sweetness remains virtually hidden during the second third of the Casa Turrent Serie 1973, while the dominant flavors are still the same creamy oak and leather combination. Other notes of espresso, hay, bread, gritty earth and cocoa flit in and out, and there is a huge uptick in spice that comes out of nowhere right around the halfway point. Construction-wise, the burn and draw continue to impress and the smoke production seems to have fallen off a bit compared to the first third. In terms of strength, the Casa Turrent Serie 1973 hits the medium mark early on in the second third, but seems to stall out there, and shows virtually no signs of going much further. The final third of the Casa Turrent Serie 1973 seems to be a carbon copy of the second third, with the same creamy oak and leather combination that has dominated the profile since the beginning remaining on top, with other flavors of earth, hay, tobacco, oak and dark chocolate noticeable at different points. Thankfully, the spice on my tongue has receded noticeably by this point, but the indeterminate sweetness is still not strong enough to make any sort of impact on the profile. Both the burn and the draw continue to give me no issues, while the strength ends the cigar in pretty much the same place it started by the time I put the nub down with a little less than an inch to go.
note_sources.title: Casa Turrent Serie 1973 Robusto

note_sources.text: The Inner Circle by Cavalier Genève Petit Robusto begins with an open draw that delivers flavors of crisp earthiness over milder sensations of saltiness, acidity and leather. I’m not sure whether it’s the physical effects of the open draw or a mental correlation, but it feels like parts of the flavor profile are missing. A combination of hickory and something that reminds me of the smell of birdseed lead the profile over some mineral and off-putting herbal flavors. The finish sees the mineral flavors pick up a lot, slowly joined by saltiness, leather, white pepper and, at times, some isolated sugar. Retrohales are stronger with herbal and floral flavors leading peanuts, hickory, oak and touches of raspberry. The finish has earthiness over some mineral flavors and something that reminds me of stale bottled water. All parts of the profile are dry, though the finish—of both the main flavor and retrohale—are drier than the other parts. Flavor is medium-full, body is closer to full and strength is medium-plus. With the exception of the draw, construction is great—the volume of smoke production can be massive if I push the cigar a bit, and the ash forms very consistently. Right around the point when I need to remove the secondary band, I find myself needing to touch up two of the cigars. Flavor-wise, that hollowness I found in the first third has been resolved thanks to a chewy peanut butter flavor. Unfortunately, that seems to come at a cost of the crispness that I admired in the first third. Secondary notes include earthiness, sunflower seeds and hickory. The finish is rather similar to when the smoke is in my mouth, but I get some sugar sweetness. Retrohales have a balanced mixture of sunflower seeds, saltiness, peanuts, leather, mineral flavors, black pepper and a mild grapefruit-like tartness. The finish has a rich nuttiness over black pepper, hay and some saltiness. Flavor and body are both medium-full and strength is medium-plus. Unfortunately, the decline of the crispness seems to be in a linear relationship with the length of the cigar. Flavor-wise, there’s earthiness leading some of the stale water, nuttiness, saltiness, creaminess and an occasional hickory
note_sources.title: Inner Circle by Cavalier Genève Petit Robusto

specs.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto), Honduras (Jamastran Valley), Nicaragua (Habano Jala

note_sources.text: Chillin' Moose is a new cigar from Michael Giannini and company in Nicaragua. Introduced as a value-priced addition to an otherwise higher-end portfolio, Chillin' Moose has proven to be hugely successful, garnering the attention of numerous publications and bloggers everywhere and making its presence felt in retailers nationwide. Handmade in Nicaragua , this long filler cigar consists of a 4-country filler blend containing tobacco from Nicaragua, Mexico, the Dominican Republic and the USA. An Ecuadorian binder, along with an exotic Connecticut Habano Rosado wrapper leaf, make this one heck of a masterpiece, despite the funny name. So simple, yet so complex, Chillin' Moose is aptly named as this mellow stick makes for a very relaxing experience. Beginning with a classic raw tobacco flavor, Chillin' Moose then rounds out with hints of earth and citrus, as well as a bit of sweetness on the finish. Indubitably mild-medium-bodied , Chillin' Moose is great for those late nights after a long day at work. Beginners can enjoy the mild manner of the smoke , while serious connoisseurs will no doubt appreciate the subtle complexities that Chillin' Moose has to offer. Not only that, but everyone will be thrilled at the ridiculously low price of such an extraordinary cigar as this! Chillin' Moose pairs well with light beer and is in a comparable league to Hoyo de Monterrey and Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real . Funny name, serious flavor: That's the name of the game when it comes to Chillin' Moose.

There was a time when smoking a premium hand-rolled cigar was seen as a pretentious hobby only for the rich and powerful, but the new Chillin' Moose Too stomps that view into the mud. This is a stick for everyone, with a delightfully delicious taste and a price that can't be beat. Following on the success of the original Chillin' Moose, they have upped the strength and doubled the flavor by blending a variety of juicy and robust Nicaraguan tobaccos and stuffing them into a leathery Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper carrying a hefty amount of tooth. Plus, the band has a cigar-chomping moose pulling an angry rabbit out of a top hat! Not really sure why but hey, we're not here to ask questions. Once you get past the wildly illustrated and rather large bright red band, you'll notice the Chillin' Moose Too is a quality stick with some moderate veining and a nice shine. The aroma is of rich tobacco and cedar overall but some chocolate can be discerned wafting from the foot. Budget cigars can sometimes feel soft and under-filled but here each vitola is nicely firm and sits heavy in the hand, the thickly bunched filler also providing a smooth draw that fills the mouth with smoke. Sweet with vanilla and spice up front, it doesn't take long for beefier flavors to come charging out of the wilderness: coffee, cocoa, and black pepper the most obvious. Through to the end, the cigar remains a steady medium in strength and pairs equally well with either coffee or whiskey. It's easy to identify those thrifty and wise aficionados who own a collection of Chillin' Moose Too cigars by their fat wallets and wide grins. Join their ranks today and we predict you'll be racking up some serious time in your favorite chair enjoying each and every one. Grab some now, you crazy animal!

The CLE 25th Anniversary TAA 2025 starts with a fairly mellow Honduran terroir that leads a touch of pepper and a very subtle but rich sweetness. The second cigar has some creaminess, which mellows the pepper but adds some depth, but unfortunately, I don’t find it as early in the other two cigars. Retrohales are consistently more intense and concentrated than the flavor, offering a dense earthiness and a vibrant black pepper, regardless of how the flavor starts. There’s some dryness to the flavor in the first inch, reminding me a bit of a handful of Wheat Chex. While there are some vibrant flavors, I’d also consider the profile to be pretty refined, not trying to overwhelm with intensity, but trying to impress with finesse, balance, complexity and restraint. In the final puffs of the first and third cigars’ first thirds, a little creaminess emerges, though they are quickly dashed by the dry, peppery finish. The second cigar continues to keep its creaminess as a more significant contributor to the profile. Flavor is medium-plus but with a good bit of restraint, body is medium and strength is mild. Construction thus far is pretty much flawless; I could say the burn line isn’t perfectly even, but that’s a minor note. Tingling nostrils seem to be an integral part of the CLE 25th Anniversary TAA 2025 experience, even when I’m not retrohaling, as the ambient smoke gets the job done just fine. A wood and cream combination hits my taste buds at the start of this section, while a bit of terroir drives the finish, making for two linked but distinct sensations coming from each puff. The aroma has a mix of rich wood and smokiness that, for a few moments, reminds me of the first whiff of a smoked cocktail. Around the midpoint, the profile begins to get quite dry and toasty, and calls back to the Wheat Chex, but now with the texture of those squares being broken up and the different sensation those two forms produce. The drying out the flavor has shifted the profile in a way that’s hard to sum up; it’s still a medium-plus intensity, it just gets to that point differently than it did earlier. Body is still medium and strength is still mild. Construction remains very good, thou
note_sources.title: CLE 25th Anniversary TAA 2025

note_sources.text: C.L.E. Connecticut is the latest cigar from Christian Eiroa and the good folks at C.L.E. Cigars that is aimed at fans of mild-to-medium sticks, rather than the ultra-full choices that the Eiroa family has come to be known and loved for. Made in Honduras like all C.L.E. cigars, this version boasts a golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf and a smooth blend of Honduran filler and binder tobaccos. It's much tamer than the Habano or the Corojo and can be enjoyed by most anyone. Opening with a rich and woody profile, the C.L.E. Connecticut soon throws out some hints of spicy pepper, along with earthy notes and a touch of coffee in the background. C.L.E. Connecticut is a cigar that any cigar fan can relax with. Versatile enough to be smoked at any time of day, this cigar pairs well with medium-roast coffee, bourbon, or even white wine. Comparable sticks may include Oliva Connecticut and Camacho Connecticut. Whether a novice or an experienced aficionado, C.L.E. Connecticut will fit the bill as a truly luxurious cigar.

C.L.E. Corojo is among the first cigars released by power junkie Christian Eiroa under his new brand, C.L.E. cigars. Best known for his work with Camacho and Room 101, Eiroa has been credited with some of the finest work in the industry regarding ultra-full-bodied sticks and boatloads of flavor. This cigar is can basically be considered an homage to the original Camacho Corojo introduced by the Eiroa family years ago, using Honduran filler and binder tobaccos and a spicy corojo wrapper grown in Ecuador. Buckle up, because this cigar takes any connoisseur for one wild ride. The first few draws are easy and spicy, and the CLE Corojo soon settles to a full-bodied mix of earthy and nutty flavors. It pairs nicely with bourbon and should never be smoked on an empty stomach. Comparable cigars include C.L.E. Cuarenta and Camacho Corojo. Christian Eiroa is back, and perhaps better than ever. Now is the time to kick back, relax, and enjoy some full-bodied pleasure.

The CLE Habano holds a special place in history as the first cigar to ever wear a CLE band , and it has remained a steadfast all-star in Christian Eiroa’s portfolio since day one. Originally known as CLE Cuarenta , this delicious Honduran puro is lovingly handcrafted at Eiroa’s own factory, El Aladino , in Danlí, Honduras, under his precise supervision. This blend was the catalyst that put Christian Eiroa back on the map after he departed from the Camacho brand to pursue his own visionary ventures. As for the blend, it consists of 100% premium Honduran tobacco —wrapper, filler, and binder. The standout feature is the beautiful, golden-brown Honduran Habano wrapper leaf, which has been extensively aged to deliver a sophisticated and succulent flavor profile. Simple yet enticing, this 90-rated gem continues to dominate even in today’s fiercely competitive premium cigar market, proving that classic construction and quality tobacco never go out of style. The signature renovated orange packaging makes the CLE Habano instantly recognizable, and it remains one of the few elite brands still available in traditional 25-count boxes .
