Case in point, in 2017, the company released 17 new cigar lines  that spawned 104 SKUs when taking into account all of the sizes being released. One of those new lines was an addition to the company’s Achilles line, an extension called La Iliada. Like 14 of the 17 new lines released that year, it was a Nicaraguan puro, though there are still no specifics as to what kind of tobacco is used, be it region or varietal. The line was released in an astonishing 12 sizes, numbered sequentially in a manner that would suggest from least to most amount of tobacco used. Curivari’s owner, Andreas Throuvalas, has often incorporated his Greek heritage and culture into his cigar releases, and this is no exception. Achilles is the hero of the Trojan War and the central character in Homer’s Iliad , which forms the second part of this line’s name. Achilles’ name is still uttered on a regular basis for the tendon in our lower legs, named by way of the legend lives on to this day as he was said to be invulnerable in all part of his body except one, his heel, which is where we get the term “Achilles’ heel” for someone’s weakness. It’s also the quasi-medical term Achilles’ tendon, the commonly used term for the calcanea tendon that sits at the back of the leg and attaches several muscles to the heel bone. It’s also the thickest tendon in the human body. Here’s what I said about the Curivari Achilles La Iliada No.2 when I reviewed it in Feb. 2018 : For as little is known about Curivari and its cigars, I’ve rarely been let down when I’ve chosen to light one up, and the Achilles La Iliada No.2 preserves that trend. It can be a bit linear, but as I’ve praised other cigars for, when it hits the handful of puffs that are complex and balanced, it makes the entire experience enjoyable. The dryness of the profile, and its drying effect on the mouth, were one of the main drawbacks, while the looseness of the draw on the third sample cost it some construction points and probably affected the flavor as it was the roughest of the three samples. Yet for those problems, the profile has enough in terms of flavor and strength that I could easily see this earning some humidor space. Now onto the other
note_sources.title: Curivari Achilles La Iliada No.2

note_sources.text: Everyone knows that when it comes to premium cigars, a well-done maduro blend is tough to beat. Buenaventura Maduro by Curivari is not just an amazing premium maduro cigar, but a premium maduro cigar that is available at a fantastic price point. This Maduro version was introduced over a decade after Curivari unveiled the original Buenaventura line, one that not only nailed a 94 rating, but completely changed the way we look at value priced cigars. Like its non-maduro counterpart, this blend consists of all Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco and is produced by Curivari in Nicaragua. The one thing stopping it from being a Nicaraguan puro like its predecessor, however, is the dark, oily San Andres Maduro wrapper from Mexico. The addition of this incredible wrapper leaf completely changes the taste of the blend, turning it into a favorite among maduro fans worldwide. One of the things Curivari is known for is their Cuban style packaging, and this couldn’t be any more evident with Buenaventura Maduro. Small cedar chests and a simple, classic design on the band make it appear to be some type of clone of an old school Habana. The construction on this line is both consistent and precise, meaning an easy draw and sharp burn every time. The rich, silky smoke that comes from each puff greets the palate with immense flavors of earth, white pepper, and cayenne. This loud opening quickly settles down into a sweet and spicy medley of dark chocolate and raw tobacco, with just enough sweetness on the finish to tie everything together beautifully. Medium-full-bodied, flavorful, and smooth, Buenaventura Maduro couldn’t be more satisfying. Experienced connoisseurs love the Buenaventura cigars due to the quality to price ratio, and those just getting into the world of premium cigars appreciate how user-friendly they are. As for the medium-full-bodied Buenaventura Maduro, hot coffee makes a great accompaniment, but dark beer and red wine work just as well. Of course the original Buenaventura blend is similar, but other San Andres Maduro cigars such as La Historia or Liga Undercrown compare well also, so if you have come to enjoy either (who doesn’t?), this blend is likely one for you. Value, quality, and consistency are all attributes that make Curivari cigars stand out from the crowd. With Buenaventura Maduro, it is all included, along with a Cuban style smoking experience that will doubtless keep you coming back for more.

It’s always refreshing to stumble upon a hidden gem in the cigar world that is not only easy on the wallet, but turns out to be surprisingly good, and such is precisely the case with Curivari Gloria de Leon. Literally translated “Glory of the Lion,” this high-quality stick comes from the same folks that produce the celebrated Buenaventura brand. That being said, this is no doubt a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning that not only is it made by hand in Nicaragua, but all tobacco used in the blend is Nicaraguan as well—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler and binder consist of authentic Cuban seed Corojo, and the wrapper leaf is an aged Nicaraguan Criollo leaf. Simple, right? Well, the flavor profile tells an entirely different story. Everything about this cigar screams “Cuban”. From the precise construction to the triple cap, to the simple, yet beautifully classic Cuban style band, anyone that didn’t know any better would doubtless swear up and down they stumbled upon a genuine Habana. The draw is easy and delightfully productive, ensuring boatloads of flavor with each and every puff. The cigar starts off spicy, with no shortage of cedar in every puff. Very quickly, however, the pepper settles down and sweet floral flavor takes over to dominate the flavor profile. The core is earthy, with hints of nutmeg and cinnamon floating around in the background, but there is a heavy presence of sweetness from beginning to end. After all is said and done, Gloria de Leon finishes as a solid medium-full-bodied cigar. With a flavor profile very reminiscent of any number of genuine Cuban cigars, this stick should appeal to just about any experienced connoisseur. However, it is easy both on the pallet and the pocketbook at the same time, so even beginners and intermediate cigar enthusiasts can come to enjoy it all the same. Gloria de Leon pairs well with the sweet nuances of bourbon or red wine and is a great cigar to enjoy any time of the day. Such sweet and smooth flavors offered by the cigar in question compare to such classic cigars as Partagas or Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970 . A Cuban style cigar with great consistency, solid construction, and amazing flavor, all at a great price point? On today’s market, such a package may seem next to impossible, but Curivari Gloria de Leon is proof that such a treasure really does exist.

A true boutique cigar among the many pretenders, the Curivari Reserva Limitada Café Cigar is a medium-full Nicaraguan Puro offering an incredible amount of old-school flavor at a price you didn't know was possible. That's because the hermit-like geniuses at Curivari are more interested in creating the finest smokes possible, instead of churning out blend after blend of mediocre schlock or pushing their brand as a 'lifestyle'. Instead, expert blenders quietly select the choicest Corojo and Criollo longleaf filler tobaccos that are then skillfully rolled into a succulent binder before being finished with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper of supreme quality. Yeah, sure, the whole point is to smoke the thing, but holding an unlit Curivari Reserva Limitada Café Cigar is a transcendent experience unto itself. The Habano wrapper is utterly flawless, with a pungent aroma, an oily sheen, and a rich brown color highlighted by diamond-like glints that promise good things to come for those wise aficionados who know how to properly age a cigar until the cellophane is yellow and stiff. The rest of us impatient enthusiasts will have to settle for one of the better smokes of our lives, with enough dark earth, gingersnap, espresso, toasted oak, black walnut, plum pudding, red wine, allspice, and cream to satisfy even the most jaded of palates. We might think we're being over-enthusiastic in describing these succulent boutique cigars, but that's only because Curivari has kept such a low profile and we're here to sing their praises. How can you resist? Try just one Curivari Reserva Limitada Café Cigar for yourself, and you too will be out there on the streets spreading the news. Don't say we didn't warn you.

Curivari Reserva Limitada Cafe Noir is the third cigar in the Reserva Limitada lineup from Curivari, blended for those who want rich, bold, dark flavor from a truly Cuban-style stick. The predecessor to this cigar, Reserva Limitada Cafe, focused more on crisp, classic cigar flavor. Cafe Noir, however, takes it one step further, presenting a more mature flavor profile and one that has just a little more “oomph.” Of course, this stick is a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning that aside from being made in Nicaragua, all tobacco used in this blend, filler, binder, and wrapper, is grown in Nicaragua as well. For this package, only the choicest Cuban seed Criollo and Corojo leaves are used. The wrapper is a dark, heavily aged Nicaraguan leaf that gives the cigar its incredible bold flavor. Such flavor, in fact, that it earned a very respectable 90 rating in Cigar Aficionado. As is always the case with Curivari cigars, the packaging screams “Cuban.” From the handsome cedar dress boxes to the simple, classic bands on each vitola, one who didn’t know better would swear up and down they were about to enjoy a classic Cuban luxury. Well, in a way they wouldn’t be wrong, as Cafe Noir is constructed to the “T” with Cuban craftsmanship in mind, from the seamless roll to the unmistakable triple cap. A clean cut reveals an easy draw that produces massive amounts of silky white smoke. The cigar starts off with a blast of cedar from the get-go, soon followed by spicy black pepper and a hint of citrus. Moving on, the earthy core of the flavor profile is speckled with beautiful notes of fudge brownies, espresso, and cinnamon. The finish is quick and spicy, with every puff bringing in a new handful of sweet, dark flavor. Medium-full-bodied, Cafe Noir is right in the sweet spot for fans of dark, balanced cigars that are plenteous in the flavor department. Made for connoisseurs, but appropriate for just about any fan of medium-full-bodied cigars, Cafe Noir is a great choice for those seeking premium sticks at a friendly price point. It pairs well with black coffee, espresso, or dark beer, and is appropriate for any time of the day. Fans of bold Nicaraguan cigars such as Oliva Serie V or Padron should find this lower-priced alternative to be right up their alley. Curivari has been making some of the best hidden gems in the cigar world for years now, and they show no sign of stopping. If you are in the market for an incredible Cuban style cigar that won’t break the bank but will definitely leave a lasting impression, look no further than Curivari Reserva Limitada Cafe Noir.

For those smokers looking for a cigar that’s all about hype and flash and how cool it will make you look while puffing, we would advise you to stay far away from the Curivari Reserva Limitada Classica. However, if what you’re seeking is a unique and supremely flavorful boutique cigar that’s been quietly building a dedicated fanbase beneath the radar, then this might just be the stick for you. Not much is known about Curivari except for their enthusiasm for the highest quality and most flavorful Nicaraguan longleaf tobaccos fermented and aged to perfection. These Puros contain a rich blend of Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo to create a medium-full profile you’ll want to revisit over and over. The minimal red and gold band which adorns each robust cigar should be considered a reflection of Curivari’s overall commitment to letting the tobacco do the talking when it comes to their skills. Just as you haven’t seen much in the way of marketing, social media, or other overbearing efforts to push the brand’s various frontmarks in your face, the simple yet stunning visual impact of a Reserva Limitada Classica's dark, sleek, and oily vitola is enough to set your mouth to watering. After inhaling the intoxicating aroma and testing the smooth draw, the senses will delight at the explosion of spice, dark chocolate, French-roast coffee, black cherry, leather, and sweet buttercream to be found in abundance throughout the entire slow-smoldering journey to the amazing finale.

As with the cigars from my original review, this Curivari Seleccion Privada Lancero Limited Edition 2021 is covered in a milk chocolate brown wrapper that is smooth to the touch, despite the obvious lack of oil. However, there are quite a few more major veins on this cigar compared to the previous three, and while the cigar is round, the foot has a square shape. A combination of cocoa nibs and earth lead the aromas from the wrapper, followed by generic woodiness, barnyard, dry hay and a light floral note. Creamy woodiness and sweet raisins are the main notes emanating from the foot, with earth, toasted bread, peanuts, herbs and cinnamon all in the mix as well. After a straight cut, the cold draw is full of strong oak, cinnamon, gritty earth, plain popcorn, leather tack and light brown sugar. The cigar starts off with a combination of bitter espresso and black pepper, along with some noticeable spice on my tongue. As the burn line progresses, the spice continues to be a staple on my tongue, but flavors of toasted bread and oak take over the profile. Secondary notes of creamy almonds, gritty earth, dark chocolate, sawdust and light nutmeg show up at various points, while an interesting combination of semisweet chocolate chips and black pepper is evident on the retrohale. The finish features a light anise note, but it is just not strong enough to really affect the profile in any major way at this point. Flavor ends the first half at full, the strength hits a solid medium, and the body hits a point just under the medium mark. When it comes to construction, the draw is giving me excellent resistance, there is plenty of smoke, and while the burn line is never close to razor sharp, there is only one minor correction needed in the second third. During the second half, the profile shifts a bit, as a combination of oak and almonds becomes the main flavor, followed by coffee beans, sourdough bread, gritty earth, powdery cocoa nibs, wet hay and light cinnamon. The anise that was present on the finish in the first half begins to recede after the halfway point, and is sadly nowhere to be found around the time the final third begins. While the amount of black pepper on the ret
note_sources.title: Curivari Seleccion Privada Lancero Limited Edition 2021

note_sources.text: Small batch cigar companies attempting to mimic Cuban flavor is certainly nothing new but sticks like Curivari Seleccion Privada take the idea to a whole new level. Rolled in Nicaragua at the Tabacalera de Nicaragua S.A. factory, Curivari Seleccion Privada was a masterpiece from the start, and to this day flies off the shelves whenever it becomes available. It is a Nicaraguan puro, meaning all tobaccos used in the production process are Nicaraguan —wrapper, filler, and binder. The reddish brown Habano Maduro wrapper leaf is grown from genuine Cuban seed, adding the finishing touch to this gorgeous gem of a cigar. Each vitola is rolled with expert craftsmanship and triple capped in Cuban fashion, the roll being nearly seamless and offering just the right amount of draw. The red and gold bands resemble those of one of the most famous Cuban cigars in the world, though we will let you be the judge of just which one. Copious amounts of smoke pour from the head of Seleccion Privada, laying the foundation of a spicy, earthy flavor profile. White pepper and cedar start things off, while cocoa and nuts appear spontaneously throughout the remainder of the experience. The finish is clean, yet spicy, and overall this cigar finishes as medium-full-bodied. It's obvious that the folks at Curivari were going for a true Cuban experience with this package, and it's safe to say they hit the nail on the head. Simple, satisfying, and rich, Seleccion Privada fits the bill as a boutique cigar for the textbook discriminating connoisseur. It pairs well with bourbon, coffee, or full-bodied beer and makes a great finish to a weekend dinner or social event. Fans of such popular Cuban style Nicaraguans as Don Pepin Blue or Flor de Las Antillas will likely find the cigar in question to hit the spot, and the price point leaves no excuse for not trying one. In a world where fine cigars are beginning to cost an arm and a leg with no guarantee of satisfaction, it is refreshing that sticks like Curivari Seleccion Privada are there to offer a classic Cuban experience at a fraction of the price.

Once a well-kept European secret, Curivari Buenaventura Cremas cigars handmade by Plasencia Cigars in Nicaragua have exploded in popularity among discerning smokers in the U.S.—and for good reason. Although Curivari made its stateside debut back in 2010, it wasn’t until the introduction of the Buenaventura line that the brand truly took off. Now, the Cremas stands tall as a shining example of ultra-premium Nicaraguan craftsmanship at a surprisingly accessible price. This blend has recieved a 93 rating from Cigar Aficionado ! Handcrafted in Nicaragua, the Curivari Buenaventura Cremas feature all-Nicaraguan fillers and binders, elegantly cloaked in a silky-smooth Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. This combination delivers a refined, medium to full-bodied smoking experience that punches well above its weight class—both in complexity and value. While many cigars in this category command a hefty price tag, the C300 remains a true hidden gem for those in the know. All the vitola is expertly rolled, boasting a flawless appearance and a draw that produces thick, aromatic clouds of smoke. Flavor-wise, expect a luxurious profile filled with earthy undertones, roasted nuts, black cherry, and creamy cedar , all laced with subtle leather and spice . It’s smooth, balanced, and delightfully rich from start to finish. Aimed at experienced smokers but approachable for any intermediate aficionado looking to step up their game, the Buenaventura Cremas pair beautifully with bourbon or dark rum. Comparable to top-shelf favorites like Four Kicks and Casa Magna, this stick proves you don’t have to break the bank to enjoy boutique quality. Curivari Buenaventura Cremas is the cigar that overdelivers—and once you light one up, you’ll see exactly why it's become such a fast favorite in the humidor.

Curivari Buenaventura Favoritos Connecticut is the second release of the Favoritos lineup, this time offering something on the milder side for fans of mellow, yet flavorful cigars. For those who don’t know, the Buenaventura Favoritos is an extension to the hugely popular original Buenaventura brand, a wallet-friendly project Curivari has been generous enough to offer to the world of premium cigars. Nicaraguan-made in a small, cozy factory, Buenaventura Favoritos Connecticut consists of all Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco beneath an Ecuadorian Seed Connecticut wrapper. Blended to satisfy even the pickiest Connecticut fanatics, this stick may just become everyone’s new favorite. Beneath the unmistakable Cuban-style Buenaventura band sits a secondary yellow band, denoting the Connecticut variety. Unbelievable construction means each and every Favoritos cigar offers a smooth and easy draw with no shortage whatsoever when it comes to smoke production. Initially, a blast of nutty goodness greets the palate, followed by a beautiful mixture of cedar, tea, and earthy tobacco flavor. Hints of cinnamon and bread linger in the background, and the finish is crispy and clean. Medium-bodied and incredibly easy to smoke, Buenaventura Favoritos Connecticut is bold proof that a Connecticut cigar can be delightfully flavorful. Medium-bodied , packed with flavor, and easy to enjoy any time of the day, Buenaventura Favoritos Connecticut is a cigar that can be enjoyed by just about anyone. It’s easy on both the palate and the wallet alike, and makes a particularly great choice for a beginner or anyone looking for a mellow, flavorful cigar. Pair this one with your favorite scotch or bourbon for a luxurious experience, or simply kick back, light up, and enjoy it alongside a cup of hot coffee in the morning. Fans of the original Buenaventura brand will definitely want to check this one out, but we warn you, this one might be your new preference! For a wonderful cigar experience that won’t break the bank but will keep you coming back for more, try a Curivari Buenaventura Favoritos Connecticut and be amazed at how delicious a value-priced cigar can be.

Rounding out the 3-part Buenaventura Favoritos series from Curivari , Buenaventura Favoritos Maduro is a cigar that will doubtless have maduro fans rejoicing. Moreover, it might be baffling to try to figure out how a cigar so incredible can be so affordable. Well, that’s why the Buenaventura Favoritos series is here in the first place: To offer affordable premium cigars that deliver quality each and every time. This cigar is handcrafted at Curivari’s Tabacalera de Nicaragua in Nicaragua by the skilled hands of a small number of artisans. The filler and binder blend is all-Nicaraguan, while the wrapper leaf for this variant is a dark and oily Mexican San Andres leaf. Considered by many to be the world’s best maduro, San Andres tobacco is typically used in only the finest maduro cigars, so seeing it in a package in this price range is absolutely bonkers. Packaged in a classic cedar dress box, this Maduro version of the Favoritos series wears both a classic Buenaventura band and a blue secondary band to identify the blend. Masterful construction lends itself to an easy draw and amazing smoke production, making every stick an absolute pleasure to enjoy. Spicy white pepper starts things off, soon settling into a medley of creamy, chocolaty flavors mingled with cinnamon, oak, and black cherry. Hints of espresso and brown sugar linger in the background as the raw tobacco backbone holds everything together. Medium-bodied and complex, this Maduro is one that’s sure to leave a lasting impression. Suitable for all audiences, Favoritos Maduro is sure to please both the beginner and experienced connoisseur alike. The bold flavor profile and medium-body make it easy to enjoy at any time of day. Best paired with coffee, dark beer, or red wine, this rich Maduro cigar will have you feeling luxurious every time. Fans of the original Buenaventura Maduro will love this one, along with anyone that has been searching for an affordable high-quality Maduro cigar. Don’t overlook or underestimate this one! Curivari’s Buenaventura Favoritos Maduro is the price conscious Maduro freak’s dream-come-true.

Let’s face it, we live in an age where premium cigars are rarely seen with affordable price tags. When accepting that reality, it’s quite refreshing to stumble upon something good that doesn’t hurt the wallet too much. Cigars like Curivari Buenaventura Favoritos Natural certainly fit this bill. A new extension to their incredibly price-conscious Buenaventura line , Curivari’s Favoritos offer new sizes and a new spin on flavor, all while keeping things economical. Available in 3 different wrapper variations, the Favoritos line, like the original Buenaventura, is handmade in a small factory in Nicaragua where attention to detail is never taken for granted. The recipe for this Natural variant includes Nicaraguan filler and binder leaves along with a golden-brown Nicaraguan wrapper from the Jalapa region. That’s right, a premium hand-made Nicaraguan puro available at a price that rivals that of some bundle cigars. We can hardly believe it, either! Each wrapper variation is color-coded by the secondary band. In this case, a red band beneath the gold and brown primary shows that it is the Natural. Construction is phenomenal, with each cigar offering a productive draw and razor-sharp burn every time. White pepper and cedar open things up , soon settling into an earthy medley of deep tobacco flavor mingled with savory spices . The spicy pepper intensifies just a bit as the cigar burns, and the finish is crisp, with just a hint of sweetness. Cuban-style flavor is obviously the goal here, and Curivari has done it quite well. Balanced, flavorful, and boasting alluring simplicity, Buenaventura Favoritos Natural finishes as a medium-full-bodied cigar. Made for the experienced, but easily enjoyable by all, Buenaventura Favoritos Natural is more than just a bargain, but a memorable smoking experience each and every time. Its medium-full body and spicy characteristics make it a great stick to pair with your favorite bourbon or scotch, but a simple cup of coffee also makes a great accompaniment. Fans of the original Buenaventura line will doubtless come to love this version, as it retains quite a bit of the original flavor DNA. Incredible cigars don’t always have to break the bank, and if you can’t believe it, one taste of Buenaventura Favoritos Natural by Curivari should be all the proof you need.

There are many cigars described as containing "extensively-aged" tobaccos when they are perhaps four or five years old, but the Cusano 18 cigar can make the claim better than most. As might be expected, the 18 in the title signifies how many years the filler has been resting, resulting in a taste profile both complex and sophisticated. Starting with the same base Dominican Oro and Seco filler, the Cusano 18 comes in two different varieties: the Double Connecticut mixes in some Ligero and Olor beneath the dual USA Shade wrapper and binder, while the Paired Maduro has added Brazilian Mata Fina cloaked in a San Vicente Olor binder and all of it finished by a darker and toothy Connecticut Broadleaf. (Shop other Cusano Cigars ) Both cigar styles offer a pleasing aesthetic with the Shade-wrapped being a smooth and flawless golden stick exuding mild, earthy aromas and the Maduro a chocolate candy bar of pungent goodness. They both light and draw easily, the tobaccos having spent so much time together it seems they want to postpone the inevitable just a bit longer with a solid, long-lasting ash. The Connecticut starts out creamy with a flavor like butter on toast and builds into a medium-bodied experience with hints of black tea and almonds. The two well fermented leaves of the Maduro variety offer mocha and mild spices on top of leather and a touch of sweetness. All smokers will find something to appreciate in either Cusano 18, perhaps smoking the Double Connecticut with tea after an English breakfast or the Paired Maduro with coffee and dessert. An incredible value either way so be sure to stock up.

The profile of the El Borracho Belicoso starts out with some obvious notes of both black pepper and toasted bread just after lighting the foot, but the main flavors of cedar and leather tack take over the profile within a few puffs. Additional notes of cashews, gritty earth, cinnamon, espresso beans, cocoa nibs and the aforementioned toasted bread flit in and out at different points, while the retrohale is nicely balanced with small but equal amounts of both black pepper and brown sugar sweetness. Flavor ends the first third at just under medium, while the body struggles to leave the mild mark and the strength hits a mild-plus. In terms of construction, one of my cigars runs into minor trouble early that involves a quick correction with my lighter, but the other two sticks are fine in that regard, and all three cigars feature the same excellent combination of a great draw and plenty of smoke. A creamy cashew flavor joins the cedar note from the first third—pushing the leather flavor to secondary status—to become the main combination in the El Borracho, followed by notes of dark chocolate, earth, cinnamon, roasted coffee beans and hay in various amounts. One cigar develops a distinct floral note on the finish, but there is no sign of it on either of the other two sticks. The retrohale for all three cigars is visually the same, with a slightly increased amount of black pepper and a bit less of the brown sugar sweetness compared to the first third. Flavor increases to a solid medium, while the body ticks up to mild-plus and the strength to just under the medium mark. Construction-wise, the draw and smoke production remains excellent on all three cigars, but two sticks have an issue that necessitates a touchup each to stay on track. There are not many changes in the profile of the cigar during the final third, as the creamy cedar and cashew combination remain the top notes, easily beating out secondary flavors of earth, tobacco leaves, cinnamon, roasted coffee beans and toasted bread. The floral note on the finish that provided a bright spot to the profile during the second third of one cigar is long gone—it never appeared on the other two cigars—while the retrohale

note_sources.text: The remarkably complex and delicious Davidoff Colorado Claro is what happens when you take an already iconic cigar to the next level. An extension of their ever-popular Special Series, this cigar contains the same astounding filler blend of Dominican longleaf comprised of smooth burning Olor Seco and two types of robust, spicy Ligero tobaccos: Piloto and a double-dose of San Vicente. The Special's sweet Dominican Piloto Seco binder also makes a return, but what the fine folks at Davidoff have brought to the table for the Colorado Claro is a dazzling sun-grown Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper of impeccable quality. (See more Davidoff Cigars ) If you're going to change what is already a top-tier smoke for many an enthusiast, the reason must either be as an improvement or an entirely new experience. Since there is little fault to be found in the original Special Series, the ruddy and sleek sun-grown Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper on the Davidoff Colorado Claro needs to live up to the latter. And does it ever. Genuinely medium-full in body, this cigar is nonetheless able to maintain a balance and charisma difficult to find in lesser stogies. Expect each puff to be loaded with some combination of dry cedar, sweet tobacco, salt, loamy earth, bright citrus, black pepper, cocoa, and graham cracker. Those familiar with the Davidoff brand are no longer surprised at the price they command and know them to be worth every dime, but the strength of these cigars may come as a shock to some. For the full enjoyment of a Davidoff Colorado Claro, we recommend a stiff drink as a companion after a hearty meal. A special occasion smoke you'll nonetheless find mundane reasons to light up, you should plan on keeping some in reserve

There are few cigars that are more synonymous with luxury than the ones made by Davidoff, and the Millennium Blend is another great example. Most Davidoff cigars are in the mild-medium body category, but the Millennium blend pushes the boundary to the full bodied side. Like all Davidoff cigars, the blend consists of some of the finest quality Dominican filler tobacco which has been aged for 4 years. Draping this exquisite blend is a beautiful, chocolate brown Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper leaf. (See more Davidoff Cigars ) The classy white and gold bands play perfectly off the medium brown hue of the wrapper. The initial tingling of spice that crosses your lips makes you aware that this isn't your everyday Davidoff. Once lit that spice intermingles perfectly with subtle coffee and cocoa notes. The more you puff on this fine piece of craftsmanship the more the power builds but it never overpowers. Davidoff Millennium was originally introduced in 1999, and was such a hit that they couldn't just limit it to that one year. These full body masterpieces should grace the humidor of anyone who likes big flavors and impeccable construction. After a great meal and with a smokey tumbler of single malt, the Davidoff Millenium would be the perfect end to an evening. For a slightly milder medium-bodied smoke we would also recommend the Davidoff Nicaraguan cigars.

You may be wondering while checking out these sticks what it is that makes Davidoff Special Series cigars so, well, special. From a purely practical standpoint, when Henke Keller and his team of skilled torcedors set out to create a unique experience for Davidoff fanatics the 'easiest' way to set these smokes apart from the crowd was to focus on traditional and sometimes uncommon shapes and sizes. However, the various figurados into which the four-year aged Dominican tobaccos are formed are anything but easy to accomplish and require many years of experience to do just right. Good thing that Davidoff employs some of the best rollers in the business. (See more Davidoff Cigars ) While the name refers to the various vitolas available, the term 'special' can also be used as a description for the flavors provided by each cigar. Whether the short corona format of the Entreacto, the cone-like torpedo shape of a Special T, or the classic Short Perfecto, each heavy Davidoff starts of buttery smooth and rich with creamy leather and bright cedar. Making a turn towards the bold without harshness or unrefined strength, the middle third lays on black pepper and roasted nuts, each silky puff encouraging the next. A touch of allspice during the final third keeps each cool burning stick firmly in your hand until the last possible moment. Style and class are an integral part of all Davidoff cigars, but as with all of their refined smokes the Davidoff Special Series is even more about taste and a passion for the good life. Aficionados who are looking to supplement their enjoyment of cigars like Diamond Crown and Ashton Cabinet will find much to appreciate. Regular Joes who want a special occasion stick that will certainly impress friend and foe alike, you need to search no further. Just pick your favorite special size and go to town.

The Deadwood girls just got a brand-new sister! From the sunny fields of the Dominican Republic to the dusty streets of Deadwood, the new vixen at the core of this tale is so alluring, so smooth, that she’ll steal your heart the moment you discover hers. Deadwood Dominicana invites you with a sweet kiss from her “Capa Dulce” and then takes you deeper into her web. With each draw, the irresistible taste of her filler-forward blend of premium Dominican tobaccos will beam into your soul. A daring, lighter evolution of the traditional expression in the Deadwood Tobacco Co. portfolio, blending tradition with attitude, Dominicana also represents a true milestone for Drew Estate, marking it the first blend crafted and rolled at La Gran Fabrica in Nicaragua that is focused on Dominican tobacco. Dominicana features a creamy Connecticut Shade wrapper and a bold Mexican San Andres binder, but it is Dominican at the heart, featuring a rich, complex core of the island’s finest tobacco. Caressing the palate with a silky draw while delivering deep notes of honey, cream, and cocoa, with a smooth, buttery finish. Dominicana is sure to turn heads and captivate you without even trying. And while the Deadwood sisters may roll their eyes in envy, they know—this island beauty is easy to love but impossible to forget.

When the sun dips below the horizon, the newest vixen in the Drew Estate Deadwood lineup makes her entrance. Meet the Deadwood Dominicana Buenas Noches - the darker, richer, after-hours evolution of the original Dominicana blend. Where the first Dominicana welcomed you with smooth Dominican-forward charm, Buenas Noches turns up the intensity with a deeper Maduro character built for late nights, lingering conversations, and one more cigar before calling it a day. Handcrafted at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate in Nicaragua, Buenas Noches is wrapped in the same luxurious Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper used on the legendary Liga Privada No. 9 blend, but with a sweet cap. Beneath that dark, oily exterior lies a hearty Mexican San Andrés binder and a carefully selected mix of Dominican and Nicaraguan long-fillers , creating a smooth yet layered smoking experience that remains unmistakably Deadwood. Like her seductive Dominicana sister, Buenas Noches greets the palate with Deadwood’s signature Capa Dulce sweetened cap, delivering a soft sweetness before deeper flavors begin to unfold. Notes of cocoa, earth, cedar, coffee, and warm spice build throughout the smoke, balanced by creamy texture and subtle natural sweetness. The result is a mellow-to-medium bodied cigar that feels richer and more indulgent while remaining remarkably approachable. Jonathan Drew described the concept best: “Buenas Noches is a sophisticated, intriguing companion. She’s your ride or die, your boo.” That personality comes through in every draw, smooth, mysterious, and impossible to ignore. Bold yet refined, sweet yet earthy, the Deadwood Dominicana Buenas Noches delivers a flavorful after-hours smoking experience that deepens the Dominicana story while bringing an after-dark adaptation to the Deadwood family.

Deadwood’s infamous vixens are welcoming a mysterious and enchanting new stranger to their enthralling lineup: Deadwood The Girl With No Name cigars, the latest captivating creation from the mad scientists over at Drew Estate. Despite an identity shrouded in mystery, it’s important to know that these sultry smokes are not infused in the usual Drew Estate fashion; instead, they bear only a lightly sugared tip to complement the natural sweetness of the rugged and exotic longleaf tobaccos that form the core of these succulent treats. For those who are familiar, think of the Deadwood series as a descendant of the famed Larutan frontmark. Always looking to keep things interesting, Drew Estate has dressed The Girl With No Name in a brash Sumatra wrapper, making this medium-bodied vitola a perfect companion for any occasion. An oily and well-built cigar that slides easily from its protective cellophane, The Girl With No Name invites you in with sultry eyes watching from the cigar’s gold-trimmed band. Even before you hold the stick to your lips for a draw test, the luxurious aromas of pipe tobacco and crisp cedar fill your nose and set your mouth watering. A clean cut and a solid flame will coax these fine stogies into pouring delicious clouds of smoke onto the palate, starting with a syrupy molasses essence that quickly invites complementary tastes of buttery shortbread, dark earth, and luscious vanilla cream. Spending quality time with this stogie reveals even deeper flavors, such as roasted pecans, fresh-hewn oak, nutmeg, semi-sweet hot chocolate, and English toffee in abundance, while the smoke remains smooth and delicious down to the nub. Sweet and approachable, Deadwood The Girl With No Name Cigar follow in the footsteps of cigars like the Asylum Insidious and the legendary Baccarat — but be warned: just one of these honeyed delights won’t be enough to satisfy most enthusiasts. Our low prices make buying more an easy decision, so make the first move and grab yourself a handful or a box before these beauties get away.

The Diamond Crown Julius Caeser cigar is not named after the famed Roman emperor as might be expected. Instead, this exquisite example of tobacco-rolling mastery memorializes Julius Caeser Newman, founder of the only premium cigar company still owned by its original family: the J.C. Newman Cigar Company. Founded by J.C. in 1895 and faithfully ruled by his descendants ever since, the company created this, the third Diamond Crown style, in 2010 to honor their patriarch using a blend of five year aged leaves from around the Caribbean basin of Central America which are bound in a Dominican leaf itself contained within one from Ecuador. A marble bust of Julius himself peers from the band, and you will have no trouble meeting his gaze as you appraise the quality of construction. The chewy, rich, chocolate-brown leaf with aroma to match clips easily to reveal darker tobacco at the core of the vitola. The first third of the cigar coats the tongue with biscuit and crisp white pepper, more smooth than spicy. Overarching flavors of cocoa and nuts enter once the sweet spot has been passed, supported by a column of mellow woodiness. The cigar remains easy to smoke to the end as all the prior flavors congress with a flourish. Smokers who enjoy mild cigars will wish the Diamond Crown Julius Caeser could be their daily smoke despite the price, but as an occasional treat it is definitely worth having in your humidor. If the price is above your rank, save some coins and substitute the CAO Gold cigar for similar enjoyment.

The Diamond Crown Maduro cigar is, in considering the name as prosaically as possible, a rare gem that stands as a king among medium ultra-premium smokes. Fortunately, the cigar can make its own claim to the throne as its rightful heir, the offspring of two cigar-making royalties. Handmade by Tabacalera A. Fuente to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the J.C. Newman Cigar Company using Dominican tobaccos enrobed in an exclusive Connecticut fermented wrapper, this cigar is simply damn good. With a hefty 54 ring gauge across the entire line (with one larger exception), the Diamond Crown Maduro series is built to deliver a rich, leaf-packed smoking experience. When first unwrapped from its protective cellophane, the cigar’s color and aroma might remind you of a light Corojo wrapper. However, this impression comes from its double-fermented Connecticut wrapper, carefully crafted to enhance flavor without sacrificing smoothness. Once lit, any expectations of spice or harshness disappear, replaced by mouthfuls of creamy smoke with notes of mace and buttered toast. As the Diamond Crown Maduro, develops, the flavor shifts elegantly—almond undertones emerge, accompanied by hints of exotic spices. Stay the course, and the final stretch rewards you with a luxurious finish of cream and nutmeg. Pair it with a gin and tonic, and you’ll find yourself transported to a palace balcony, indulging in life’s finer pleasures. Though once considered pricey, the Diamond Crown now holds its own among other premium cigars like the Ashton Classic and Zino Platinum Scepter. So go ahead—try on the Crown. Savor the majesty.
Sweetness , Coffee , Leather Available. Learn about Diamond Crown Maximus Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Maximus

An ultra-premium of the highest caliber, the Diamond Crown Maximus cigar will rouse your senses and astound your expectations. As you may know, the venerable J.C. Newman Cigar Company, America's oldest family-owned manufacturer, has been steadily creating some of the world's finest smokes for over a century. To celebrate their 110th anniversary, they partnered with the renowned Fuente and Oliva families to create this flawless and full-bodied masterpiece of quality tobacco. Utilizing a secret Newman-crafted filler blend of Dominican longleaf, the master torcedors at Tabacalera A. Fuente y Cia finish each stick with an incomparable Ecuadoran Sungrown wrapper cultivated on Oliva's exclusive El Bajo farm. There's a confident sophistication carried by each stick unable to be hidden by the apparent ruggedness of the oily, veiny, and chocolate-hued Sumatra-seed leaf that sits beneath the cigar's heavily decorated band. Redolent with the aromas of expertly fermented tobacco and sweet alfalfa, the slight flex within the vitola's barrel promises the excellent draw proven by a cold test. The 93-rated Diamond Crown Maximus' true character presents itself as the first sips of cool, spice-laden smoke reach the lips, with white pepper, vanilla cream, and espresso coating the palate soon after. Honeyed biscuit and golden raisins offer syrupy counterpoint to the earthy leather, oak, sea salt, and black cherry, which form the flavor profiles foundation from head to foot. Treat yourself today to some Diamond Crown Maximus as they are well worth every hard-earned cent, and you deserve it. Indulge even further by hosting a friendly inter-collaborator competition between your stash of Maximus, a few Arturo Fuente Rosado Sungrown Magnum R, and a solid handful of Oliva V Maduro. Your enjoyment in determining the favorite will be epic.

Following the success of his Unholy Cocktail and Shorty, AJ Fernandez brings us the Diesel Unlimited cigar. The Diesel Unlimited cigar brings us long filler leaf from Nicaragua and Mexico while wrapping this bad boy, we have a Ecuadorian Habano. This Ecuadorian Habano Ligero is an awfully pretty shade reminiscent of a well-worn brown leather chair. The wrapper has a small bit of tooth that screams, "grip me." Like the Unholy Cocktail, the Unlimited gets one simple, effective, no frills band wrapped around the foot of the cigar. The Diesel Unlimited is a full flavored, full bodied cigar. The 1st third brings us intense pepper with a spicy sweet tang that I just can't place. This Unlimited is well packed and burns slow. I made the mistake of trying to smoke it fast and it became bitter. So I purged and slowed down to fix that problem. The 2nd third brings a pepper spice bomb that takes me by surprise. The ash is medium gray and holds well. The smoke production so far has been great and the draw is perfect with my punch. The last third down to the nub brings a peppercorn encrusted meaty steak flavor to the table. At this point, I'm just wondering if AJ Fernandez can do anything wrong. The Diesel Unlimited has superb construction, no burn issues, great flavors, excellent body, and an unbelievably low price, making this a great cigar for experienced smokers. Newer smokers should stick to the Unholy Cocktail for now. It has less body and won't leave you with "the spins."

Diesel Unlimited Maduro is a cigar for fans of big, bad, bold flavors that want just a bit more bang for their buck. Made in Nicaragua by none other than A.J. Fernandez and Company, Diesel Unlimited Maduro is not only one of the newer additions to the Diesel portfolio; it is quickly becoming one of the most popular. Honduran and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos rest inside a luscious San Andres binder. The package is finished with a rich, oily Pennsylvania Broadleaf Maduro wrapper leaf, making for one heck of a stout cigar. However, then, if you are a fan of Diesel cigars, you must already know a thing or two about stout cigars, eh? Gleaming with natural oils and masterfully rolled in typical Fernandez fashion, Diesel Unlimited Maduro practically begs to be smoked. An easy draw produces billowing clouds of thick, white smoke, opening with a burst of spicy pepper and raw tobacco. Sweet, chocolatey flavors collide with subtle savory notes throughout the smoke, along with hints of coffee and a leathery aroma. A sweet touch of cocoa on the finish seals the deal. Indubitably full-bodied from the get-go, Diesel Unlimited Maduro makes a serious impression. Obviously, Diesel Unlimited Maduro is not for the faint of heart. It is full-bodied, full-flavored, and ready to satisfy even the most hardcore strength, junkies. It pairs well with dark beer, coffee, or bourbon, and makes an excellent choice for after a hearty dinner. If you love the original Diesel blend, or some of the other great sticks from A.J. Fernandez, including New World or San Lotano Maduro , chances are you are going to go crazy about Diesel Unlimited Maduro. The best part is, Diesel Unlimited Maduro is just as affordable as it is delicious, so why not grab some today?

The Diesel brand was born in 2009, and since then has grown to be a household name among long-time cigar fanatics. Nearly a decade and a half later, the brand introduced what some would call their flagship, while others just call it a flippin’ good cigar: Diesel Vintage Series Maduro . Made at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, this modern day classic is called Vintage for a reason: The rich Nicaraguan filler leaves are all aged no less than 5-8 years. Pair this stellar filler blend with a Nicaraguan Habano binder and a dark, oily San Andres wrapper leaf from Mexico, and you have the blend that would become one of the finest ever to be called a Diesel, and one that scored a rock-solid 91 in Cigar Aficionado magazine . Gray and gold boxes, gold accented bands, fancy script logos on every cigar, it all screams “luxury.” And that is exactly what this one is! While Diesel has been known for years to be big, bold, and rough around the edges, so to speak, this one shows the brand’s finer side, aligning more with AJ Fernandez’s typical style. An easy draw produces thick smoke with each puff, and the opening flavors are white pepper and rich coffee. An earthy core holds everything together, and heavy notes of cocoa, black cherry, and spice round out this classic maduro flavor profile . Spicy, heavy, and superbly balanced, Vintage Series Maduro finishes as a no-nonsense full-bodied cigar. Though it’s made for experienced enthusiasts, Vintage Series maduro is a great way for intermediate smokers to get into stronger blends. Full-bodied, this undeniably smooth blend pairs well with black coffee, dark beer, or your favorite dark rum. Fans of the original Diesel blend are sure to enjoy this one, as well as anyone who has enjoyed some of AJ’s famed maduro concoctions such as Enclave Broadleaf or San Lotano Maduro . Kick back, relax, and enjoy a whole new side of Diesel that we promise you’ve never seen, with Diesel Vintage Series Maduro.

Cream , Earth , Hazelnut , Spice Drink. A collaboration between Justin Andrews and AJ Fernandez, the Vintage Series provides exceptional quality, flavor, and value while staying true to the foundation that has and continues to set Diesel…

As a premium cigar brand, Diesel has come a long way since their introduction in 2009. Once more “under-the-radar,” the name is now recognized as one of the big ones in the business. That being said, it was no surprise when they introduced the original Diesel Vintage just a couple years ago, a luxury style cigar made with extensively-aged tobaccos through and through. Fast forward just a bit, and we have yet another variation: Diesel Vintage Series Natural. Made at the famed Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, this top shelf offering uses filler leaves from Jalapa, Nicaragua, all aged no less than 5-7 years. The binder is from Esteli, and the wrapper is a golden brown Ecuadorian leaf. This recipe combines to make one of the tastiest cigars to ever sport the Diesel name. Oh, and did we mention the 91 rating in Cigar Aficionado ? Luxurious gold-accented boxes with individual slots lovingly cradle the expertly-constructed vitolas. Each stick wears a single white and gold band depicting a unique take on the standard Diesel insignia. Rolled to perform, this monster draws easily to give off massive plumes of dense, flavorful smoke. Earthy tobacco is the dominant flavor in this one, and it starts from the very first puff. Early on, it’s mingled with chocolate and nutty flavor , with just a hint of cedar in the background. Black pepper joins in after a bit, and the finish is crispy and spicy, with just a touch of sweetness . Full-bodied after all is said and done, this Diesel takes all the good things about the classic blends and fully refines them. This blend is obviously aimed at intermediate to experienced cigar enthusiasts. A seasoned palate is certainly desirable in order to be able to thoroughly appreciate this complex full-bodied beauty. It pairs well with your favorite scotch, dark rum, or full-bodied beer and is best enjoyed after a meal. Fans of the original Diesel or Diesel Whiskey Row are sure to enjoy this one, as it seems to keep the essential DNA of the flavor profile and expand on it. Once again, AJ Fernandez and company present a flavorful treat that won’t break the bank and satisfies every single time. Try a Diesel Vintage Series Natural today and experience it for yourself.

Since Diesel began collaborating with Rabbit Hole Distilling back in 2018, some of the most notable releases in the history of the brand have come into existence. One such release, the star of 2025, is Diesel Whiskey Row Founder’s Collection Raceking , the latest of the red-hot Founder’s Collection series that has been ongoing for some time now. This blend, made at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua like all Diesel sticks, consists of a Nicaraguan filler and binder blend combined with a beautiful Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The key to the blend, surprisingly, is the binder leaf, a premium Nicaraguan varietal that has been extensively aged in barrels that previously held Rabbit Hole Raceking bourbon. This gentle infusion of bourbon flavor into the binder leaf gives the whole flavor profile a unique note that sets it in a class of its own. Packed in dressy brown and gold cedar boxes, each 6” x 52 Raceking cigar wears a solid gold main band in conjunction with a blue and orange foot band denoting the blend. The skilled team under the keen supervision of AJ Fernandez never skimps on construction, so rest assured that each and every cigar will perform phenomenally, offering thick, billowing clouds on every puff. Spicy white pepper is the opening note , no doubt a result of the hearty Nicaraguan fillers. The initial intensity smooths out into a medley of earth and cocoa, with hints of nuts and coffee along the way. The finish is sweet, with a touch of bourbon and cedar , and after all is said and done, Raceking finishes as a stout, full-bodied cigar. Though Diesel cigars have historically been appropriate for a vast array of cigar enthusiasts, the Founder’s collection is aimed at a more experienced group. Raceking, along with all the Founder’s Collection sticks, are made for the discriminating connoisseur that finds ultimate pleasure in a fine cigar. Full-bodied, intense, and flavorful, the sweet and spicy Raceking cigar pairs well with bourbon or coffee but can also accompany a full-bodied beer quite nicely. Fans of the original Diesel Whiskey Row and its variants will surely come to enjoy the flavorful profile offered by this modern day masterpiece. Barrel-aged tobacco, world class blending and rolling, and a name that means business—Diesel Whiskey Row Founder’s Collection Raceking is certainly a stick that deserves attention.

Hailing from the Miami-based El Rey de los Habanos factory, the Don Pepin Garcia Black Label cigar, also known as the Cuban Classic, represents one-fifth of the realization of a young boy's dream. Let me explain. Young José Garcia began rolling cigars in Cuba in 1961 when he was just eleven years old, eventually becoming one of the top torcedors in that island country. Thirty years of immersion in the world of the leaf later he fled the Castro regime to make his own fortune, eventually ending up in Miami's Little Havana district where he started his cigar company. To this day, after all of his successes creating cigars for others, only five cigars have earned the right to bear the Don Pepin Garcia name. The all-Nicaraguan Black Label is one of them. Adorned with an elegantly scripted band replacing the more simple label of years past, the rich brown Habano Rosado wrapper firmly embraces expertly bunched fillers that reek with coca-like aromas. When smoked, the first third of the cigar is loaded with coffee and woodsy notes, the perfect draw pumping smoke. Some of the characteristic Don Pepin black pepper enters during the second third right about the time the cigar goes full-throttle, and it keeps the pedal down throughout the last half when some leather and spice are added to the ever-shifting mix. You'll nub this cigar, no doubt. A feast for all five senses. The Don Pepin Garcia Black Label is recommended for more experienced smokers, particularly those who enjoy Joya De Nicaragua Antaño or Cain Habano .

Don Pepin Blue Label is the one that started it all for Jose "Don" Pepin Garcia. Once a master roller in Cuba, Don Pepin has been involved in the business since age 11 and now owns and operates My Father Cigars, a state-of-the-art factory in Nicaragua responsible for some of the most sought-after cigars in the world. Blue Label is his personal favorite blend, using Nicaraguan fillers, Nicaraguan Criollo binders, and Nicaraguan Corojo wrappers. This blend was made to mimic the old time Cubans that Don Pepin grew up with. The elegant blue band hugs the reddish, veiny cigar that is masterfully constructed to have an easy draw from which billowing clouds of bluish gray smoke plentifully flow. From first light, the smoker is greeted by the infamous "Pepin Pepper," a blast of intense spice across the entire palate. The smoke settles into a full-bodied array of nutty and spicy flavors with heavy pepper and sweetness on the finish. This stick is very full-bodied and is by no means a beginner cigar. It pairs well with scotch or bourbon and makes a wonderful weekend smoke for any experienced connoisseur. Comparable cigars include San Cristobal and Don Pepin Black Label—both additional masterpieces blended by Don Pepin himself. It doesn't get much closer to the taste of a full-bodied Cuban than Don Pepin Blue Label.

Don Jose Pepin Garcia is arguably making some of the finest cigars in the world right now. Whether it is with Pete Johnson for Tatuaje, with his son Jaime for My Father, or his own Don Pepin Garcia label, they all have amazing flavor, flawless construction, and copious amounts of smoke. When he came out and said the Serie JJ was the best of all his brands, it was definitely something to take notice of. Made in Miami to the company's highest standards, this Nicaraguan puro has the best filler and binder, and is wrapped with a light Nicaraguan Corojo Rosado wrapper leaf. Medium-to-full in body, Serie JJ hits all the right notes for full flavored cigar lovers. The beautiful white and gold band and secondary Serie JJ label have almost a regal appearance, making us aware from the start we were going to be in for an excellent experience. The first thing we like to do with a smoke is smell the foot, and surprisingly the Serie JJ was lacking any sort of aroma pre-light. Any worry we were about to embark on a flavorless journey was quenched as soon as the flame touched foot. The signature Pepin blast of pepper hit us square in the face, but quickly subsided to reveal a very complex and earthy cigar. Don Pepin Garcia Serie JJ is a fantastic cigar which morphs in flavor with every few puffs. What starts as a full-bodied spicy cigar soon mellows into a medium-to-full-bodied smoke with notes of wood and coffee. The full nature of this cigar lends itself to being enjoyed after a meal and with a nice bitter espresso. Other great cigars to smoke are the Tatuaje Miami or the lighter in body La Duena.

They say the third time's a charm, and Don Pepin Vegas Cubanas proves that this can be true even when it comes to premium cigars. In 2023, the Don Pepin brand celebrated twenty years since its humble beginnings. Back then, Jose "Don" Pepin Garcia and his small team produced cigars in a tiny boutique shop in Miami, nobody imagined that one day their brand would become one of the most dominant monsters the industry has ever seen. One of the first cigars rolled in that small shop was Vegas Cubanas, but unfortunately the brand fizzled out as Don Pepin's other brands took flight. Fast forward to 2017, and we see Don Pepin bring back the brand, this time produced in his massive, world-renowned My Father factory in Nicaragua. The brand took off briefly, even earning some respectable ratings along the way, but history would repeat itself as it died off again a few years later. Then 2023 came along. There was one final attempt to resurrect one of Don Pepin's oldest blends, and this time, he got it right. A Nicaraguan puro, Vegas Cubanas contains all Nicaraguan tobacco—filler, binder, and wrapper. The wrapper leaf is a premium aged Corojo Rosado leaf grown on Don Pepin's own farm. This blend has quickly risen to the top, with a solid 93 rating in Cigar Aficionado and acceptance with open arms from Don Pepin fans the world over. Sometimes in the cigar world, packaging can have a huge impact on how people view the brand, and the folks at My Father Cigars seem to know that. For this installment, the packaging is in line with Don Pepin's other core lines, including Cuban Classic, JJ, and the infamous Blue Label blend. This time, the bands are green and gold, offering a fresh new look and an appropriate theme, as Vegas Cubanas is literally translated "Cuban Farms." The construction is typically high-end, as one would expect from My Father Cigars, meaning a beautiful roll and a Cuban style triple cap. A smooth draw, a sharp burn line, and billowing clouds of silky, thick smoke are constant with each stick. The cigar starts off with a signature Pepin pepper storm, though this one is a bit tamer than most other cigars bearing the My Father name. Quickly, an earthy, woody profile is established, speckled along the way with simple hints of cedar, brown sugar, and coffee. The body is creamy and easy-going, and the finish is crisp and clean, with just a hint of red chili. Simple, yet just complex enough to be interesting throughout, this medium-bodied cigar alludes to many famed Cuban brands of old. Medium-bodied and easy to enjoy, Vegas Cubanas are appropriate for just about anyone. Beginners have nothing to fear in terms of it being overpowering, and established cigar enthusiasts will no doubt appreciate the Cuban style flavor profile. This stick pairs well with coffee, bourbon, or medium-bodied beer and is a great cigar to enjoy any time of the day. Similar in stature to Don Pepin Cuban Classic or My Father Flor de Las Antillas , it is sure to appeal to a very wide variety of cigar nuts. It's safe to say that the new Vegas Cubanas are here to stay, so what are you waiting for? Grab some today and experience the old-fashioned Cuban style flavor that Don Pepin and company have become known for, and all at a fantastic price point.

In 2023, My Father Cigars , formerly known as Don Pepin Garcia Brands, celebrated its 20th anniversary, and to say it was celebrated to great lengths would be an understatement. One of several incredible offerings to come from that lasting celebration was the company’s contribution to the yearly TAA Exclusive Series Program, and a cigar that would become an ongoing celebration of its own: Don Pepin Vintage Edition . Defined by old-school packaging and a retro-style flavor profile , this cigar is made in the world-famous My Father Factory in Nicaragua under the supervision of Jose “Don Pepin” Garcia himself. A Nicaraguan puro to the fullest degree, Vintage Edition uses only the finest all-Nicaraguan tobacco recipe—wrapper, filler, and binder. For a wrapper leaf , the Garcias went with a gorgeous Corojo 99 leaf grown on the family’s own farms. A pair of 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado right out of the gate kick-started its popularity, but since its debut, this blend has become incredibly popular, especially among Don Pepin’s original audience that enjoyed the early blends back in the day. A cedar cabinet box houses the gorgeous cigars, each one reddish-brown and rolled to surgical standards. The bands are the real standout here, modeled after the very earliest Don Pepin brand nearly a century ago but very similar to the ones worn by the Miami-made original Don Pepin sticks that put the brand on the map in the early 2000s. Maroon and cream is the color profile, and the classic-style band just seems to give the cigar a lovely enigma. Cedar and pepper start things off, along with a definitive toasty note that lingers throughout the transition into the earthy Nicaraguan part of the flavor profile that tends to dominate things for the rest of the smoke. Creamy around the edges, with hints of baking spices and frequent blasts of white pepper , this puro takes you back to some of Don Pepin’s early blends. Oh, and it just wouldn’t be a classic Don Pepin stick if it wasn’t definitively full-bodied , so that part goes without question. Full-bodied, smooth and spicy , and complex to about the same degree as the world’s finest Cubans, Don Pepin Vintage Edition is the quintessential connoisseurs’ cigar . Made for the experienced, this Nicaraguan puro pairs beautifully with your favorite scotch or bourbon but also goes well with coffee or full-bodied beer. Fans of the famed blends that sent My Father Cigars into the big leagues, such as Don Pepin Blue Label or Don Pepin Black Label , will surely want to take a stroll down memory lane while enjoying this potent concoction. Whether you are a long-time fan of Don Pepin cigars or happen to be a seasoned cigar enthusiast that wants to try the hottest sticks out there, enjoying a Don Pepin Vintage Edition is certainly an opportunity you won’t want to pass up.

Carrillo Cigars has had immense success over the past few years, finally coming to a high point by having his ultra-premium Encore named Cigar of the Year, but lurking behind the more popular cigars in the E.P. Carrillo lineup is a truly hidden gem every bit as capable of garnering attention: Capa de Sol. Made by skilled hands in the Dominican Republic at Carrillo's own factory, Capa de Sol is a firecracker of a cigar, using top-grade filler and binder tobacco from Nicaragua and an Ecuadorian Sun Grown wrapper leaf. Ernesto Perez-Carrillo doesn't mess around when he comes out with a new blend, so rest assured that Capa de Sol is built to please. (Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) Golden brown and oily, Capa de Sol wears an elegant gold and orange band and sports impeccable construction. A gentle roll ensures an easy draw with a ton of smoke output along with a razor sharp burn. Starting off, Capa de Sol is nutty and spicy. Bursts of Nicaraguan white pepper tickle the tongue while a heavy cedar note begins to take over. Earthy tobacco and spicy cayenne contend with each other on the retrohale, and the finish is crisp and clean. Capa de Sol resides on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied, but is beautifully balanced to ensure a velvety smooth experience. Over the years, E.P. Carrillo Cigars has released some of the most sought-after connoisseur cigars on the market. Such sticks as La Historia and the aforementioned Encore were intended for mature audiences, so to speak, as beginners would simply miss out on everything that makes them special. With Capa de Sol, however, we have a medium-full-bodied cigar with plenty of complexity and the balance that Carrillo cigars are so well-known for, yet at a reasonable price point and easily enjoyable for palates of all experience levels. Try pairing Capa de Sol with a medium-bodied beer or red wine to get a luxurious one-two punch of flavor and intensity. Literally translated "Wrapper of the Sun," Capa de Sol is aptly named, as it proves to be one of the hottest offerings from E.P. Carrillo on today's market. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. A decadent and full-bodied treat, the E.P. Carillo Cardinal Impact Maduro cigar is another hit for its maker. Ernesto Perez-Carillo is renowned for his ability to create small-batch boutique smokes that rival anything the big producers can muster, and the Cardinal line is his gift to aficionados who seek out the heaviest and most robust stogies they can find. With its ligero-laden blend of Nicaraguan filler and toothy Connecticut Broadlead wrapper this is easily the strongest blend to come from Carillo's E.P.C. Cigar company, but the man's genius is on display by not sacrificing complex and satisfying flavor in the quest for more power. (Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) Providing leathery, spicy flavors punctuated with notes of oak wine barrel, cinnamon, and cream, the cigar stays cool burning and sweet to the end. For those not quite ready to take on the Cardinal Impact Maduro, some of Ernesto's other creations offer the perfect opportunity to experience his talents. Fans of mild cigars will love the New Wave Connecticut while those who prefer bolder smokes should go for the Core Line Maduro. Ready to go all out? Order some Cardinal Maduros today and get ready to be amazed by its strengths. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. Carrillo Allegiance E.P. Carrillo Capa De Sol E.P. The E.P. Carillo Cardinal Natural cigar fills the one remaining gap left by the other fantastic smokes coming out of the E.P.C. Cigar company. From the mild and oh-so-tasty New Wave Connecticut to the medium-strength Core Line and Inch and even the more robust Elencos, there had not been an E.P. Carillo branded stick aimed squarely at the heart of those who favor full-bore strength and taste in their cigars. The Cardinal Natural corrects this, being billed as the most full-bodied in their lineup and boy does it deliver. A rich and creamy blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican tobaccos was expertly blended to meld with the peppery Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper to become the cigar that dreams are made of.(Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) Just in case you're unfamiliar with what Ernesto Perez-Carillo is capable of when it comes to full bodied smokes, check out the La Gloria Cubana Serie N and Serie R. The Cardinal Natural is easily on the same level and might even be Carillo's best ever with a profile awash in brown sugar, charred wood, sweet biscuit, and dark fruit prevalent from the beginning through to the cool burning nub. For deepest satisfaction, pair with a spiced rum, a hammock, and a warm afternoon. Just be prepared to stay put. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. Carrillo Allegiance E.P. Ernesto Perez-Carrillo is a master of Maduro who has created some of your favorite dark cigars over the years, but the E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Maduro might just be the best of them all. After finding fame and fortune with the ever-popular La Gloria Cubana line, the time came for Ernesto to return to his roots as head of a boutique brand, this time heralding his name. A slew of highly-rated and award-winning smokes soon followed, but Ernesto knew what the world really wanted from him was a Maduro. To that end, he crafted blend after blend until finding just the right combination of Nicaraguan tobaccos to pair with an Ecuadorian binder to create the perfect foundation for the expertly fermented American Connecticut Broadleaf used as the wrapper. Oily, ebony in color, and with a rich tobacco aroma, the Broadleaf wrapper that coats each muscular vitola seems nearly overflowing with juicy filler. Silky to the touch while hiding the few visible veins and seams with precision, an E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Maduro provides a smooth and steady cold draw which both preps the palate with hints of minerals and chocolate and shows the care with which each and every torcedor employed at his Tabacalera La Alianza factory fulfills Ernesto's vision. Frontloaded with coffee beans, dark cocoa, and a hint of cherry, the profile nonetheless remains a steady medium in body. It does ramp up slightly near the finale, after leather, cinnamon, maple syrup, and cedar have all had a chance to impress. It's truly amazing that in this day and age, a cigar of this magnitude can be had for less than double digits. But that's the way Ernesto rolls, if you'll excuse the pun. Fill that empty space in your humidor and your life with as many E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Maduros as you can get away with. We guarantee they're worth it. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P.
