note_sources.text: Though newer cigar enthusiasts may not realize it, El Rey del Mundo was once one of the biggest names in the world of premium cigars. A dominant force during the Cigar Boom era, El Rey del Mundo eventually settled toward the bottom of an ever-growing list of premium cigars that now steal the spotlight. However, the Honduran giant isn’t dead yet. Not long ago, a dazzling new addition was made to the brand’s portfolio: El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown . Made in Honduras, this is the first El Rey del Mundo ever to be wrapped in a Connecticut-seed wrapper. This wrapper leaf is grown under shade in Honduras’s Talanga Valley. It is then combined with a Honduran Jamastran binder and Honduran fillers from Jamastran and Copan. This stick, therefore, is a Honduran puro—an unusual one, as Honduras isn’t typically known for producing Connecticut-seed wrappers. Classic cedar chests house the precision-built vitolas, each one bearing the unmistakable El Rey del Mundo gold-on-gold band. A secondary “Shade Grown” band distinguishes this particular variant. Designed to perform, El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown offers a smooth and productive draw while holding a long, firm ash. Beginning with a bold cedar flavor, the cigar transitions into a creamy medley of cinnamon, cocoa, and brown sugar. A grassy undertone weaves throughout, balancing the sweetness and adding an earthy backbone to the profile. Mild to medium-bodied, this cigar is as easy on the palate as it is on the wallet. Ideal for beginners, loved by connoisseurs, El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown is an extremely versatile cigar. Mellow, mild, and delightfully flavorful, this stick pairs well with white wine, bourbon, or even a simple cup of coffee. Fans of milder Connecticut cigars such as Perdomo Champagne or Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real will likely enjoy the calm and easy-going nature of this particular offering. El Rey del Mundo, as a brand, may not be as popular as it once was, but with cigars like El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown, we are reminded that sometimes the classics can surprise us, even in today’s unbelievably competitive cigar industry.

It’s always exciting when a well-known celebrity gets involved with a cigar brand, especially when that brand happens to be one of the best in the business. In early 2022, photos of Erik Espinosa of Espinosa Cigars and celebrity chef/television personality Guy Fieri sparked a frenzy of social media speculation about the two doing a project together. It wasn’t long before that project came to fruition. Behold, Espinosa Knuckle Sandwich Habano ! This is actually the 92-rated blend that put the Knuckle Sandwich series on the map, earning a spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 of 2022 . There have since been several releases, now totaling 5 different blends within the Knuckle Sandwich umbrella. This knockout stogie is made by the skilled hands at the world-famous San Lotano factory in Nicaragua, overseen by none other than AJ Fernandez himself. Nicaraguan fillers combine with a Nicaraguan binder, and the wrapper is a gorgeous reddish-hued Habano leaf grown in Ecuador. With so many names involved in one cigar brand, one would expect something huge. Well, you’ve got it! Shiny, clean red cedar chests house the precision-built vitolas, and each one sports a black and gold band and a tidy black ribbon around the foot. Made for optimal performance, Knuckle Sandwich doesn’t play around when it comes to smoke production, and the output is phenomenal. White pepper and cedar open things up, but soon a tongue-tickling array of almond, cinnamon, and cocoa spices things up. Earthy to the core and boasting a backbone of spicy Nicaraguan flavor , this explosive concoction finishes on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied . Purely balanced and delicately complex, it’s easy to see how a famed chef was quick to put his name behind this one. Made for the experienced , Knuckle Sandwich Habano is a top-rated treat that is sure to satisfy any experienced fan of medium-full-bodied, complex cigars. Pair this one with your favorite medium-full-bodied beer, bourbon, or even some of Guy Fieri’s famous Tequila, and enjoy a trip to Flavorville, USA. Fans of such sticks as San Lotano or 601 Red Label are sure to take a liking to this one, along with anyone that simply loves a cigar that tells a story with its flavor profile. You don’t have to be a chef to know good flavor when it’s there. One taste of Knuckle Sandwich Habano and you’re sure to see what you’ve been missing all this time.

When Erik Espinosa and AJ Fernandez teamed up with celebrity chef Guy Fieri to make the original Knuckle Sandwich, there was little doubt that it would be a hit, but few would have guessed it would come this far. In 2025, however, some three years after the original came into existence, the one that many would call the best of the bunch made its debut: Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua . Like its sister cigars, Puro Nicaragua is made at Fernandez’s San Lotano factory in Nicaragua. This one differs from the others, however, in that every single leaf used in its production is grown and cultivated in Nicaragua, wrapper, filler, and binder. Blended to be a bit stronger than the others, this variation seems to be geared even more towards the seasoned connoisseur. Numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado prove that this stick is more than worthy of being part of the Knuckle Sandwich series. The wooden chest is rustic and the black, red, and silver bands adorning each cigar come together to give serious biker bar vibes. Each box-pressed vitola bears the all-too-recognizable skull in a chef’s hat, and each stick wears a silver band at the foot. An easy, productive draw offers plenty of smoke, and the opening is spicy and meaty . A nice dose of white pepper opens things up, followed by a cascade of rich Nicaraguan tobacco goodness. Notes of nutmeg and cinnamon are detectable, but the main core is toasty and rich. A dose of cedar and spice on the finish wraps things up, and all-in-all Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua finishes strong at the heavy end of medium-full bodied . Made for the experienced, Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua is built from the ground up to cover all the bases. Strong, complex, balanced, and smooth, this medium-full-bodied masterpiece is sure to impress any fan of spicy Nicaraguan cigars. While this one pairs well with your favorite scotch or bourbon, black coffee makes a fine accompaniment as well. If you tried the Knuckle Sandwich Habano and took a liking to it, you certainly owe it to yourself to give this one a try. Fieri, Espinosa, and Fernandez have done it again, and this time it’s bolder than ever. Try an Espinosa Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua today and experience the true greatness of a Nicaraguan puro.
Leather , Earth , Hazelnut , Molasses Drink. Crafted with precision and wrapped in a decadent Maduro broadleaf, Excalibur Maduro is the perfect follow-up to the classic Excalibur

Just one Connecticut Broadleaf wasn't enough to contain the chocolaty goodness packed into the Hoyo de Monterrey Excalibur Maduro cigar so General Cigar added a second as the binder. The result is an earthy, medium-bodied cigar that it is complex and creamy in all the right ways. The recipient of a Cigar Aficionado top-25 in 2007, this smoke still compares favorably with many of today's popular brands and stands as a preeminent example of a solid, classic Honduran maduro. It certainly doesn't hurt that the three-country filler tobaccos beneath the dual Connies are the direct descendants of the seed Estelo Padron smuggled out of Cuba after the revolution. The flavor is rich with cocoa and coffee, yet at the same time tangy and sweet. 90+ rated and amazingly affordable, you can't afford to not have a box comfortably aging right now for future enjoyment. Just don't expect to have them sitting in your humidor for that long, but they're so good you won't mind buying them again and again. Luckily, these cigars have staying power so they should be around to satisfy for years to come.

The Hoyo de Monterrey Excalibur Natural cigar is a perfectly balanced smoke, offering clean, flavorful tobacco brought to life through time-honored aging and rolling techniques. Building on the already exquisite Hoyo de Monterrey Natural, the master blenders at General Cigar created the Excalibur line using only the finest tobaccos, selected for their smooth and mellow character. With a paired Connecticut shade wrapper and binder to temper the hearty blend of Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Dominican filler, the cigar maintains plenty of complexity and a satisfying kick for even the most discerning aficionados. This blend has been rated 91 by Cigar Aficionado . The twin Connecticut leaves provide a solid canvas for the rich flavors that emerge upon lighting: notes of leather and espresso dominate the opening, while the second third introduces a honeyed sweetness that excites the palate. As the cigar approaches the nub, layers of nutmeg and allspice add a refined spice to the experience. Medium-bodied and approachable for any smoker who appreciates classic tobacco flavors crafted by skilled artisans, the Excalibur is both affordable and rewarding. Fans of Connecticut-wrapped cigars, from the mild Cusano 18 to the more robust Berger & Argenti Entubar, will find much to enjoy here. Pair it with a cold lager or iced tea and savor the finer things in life.

The Ferio Tego Metropolitan Host completes the revival of a classic lineup, bringing back one of the most approachable and beloved blends from the original Metropolitan portfolio. Carefully preserved by Michael Herklots and Brendan Scott, this blend remains true to its roots, offering the same smooth, easygoing character that made it a staple for everyday enjoyment. Handcrafted in Honduras, the Metropolitan Host feature a silky Connecticut Shade wrapper over a core of Honduran binder and long-filler tobaccos, creating a mild, creamy profile with exceptional balance. Finished with a lightly sweetened cap, this cigar delivers a touch of added sweetness that enhances, rather than overwhelms, the natural tobacco flavors. From the first draw, expect a soft, inviting profile layered with notes of cream, light cedar, and subtle cocoa , complemented by a gentle natural sweetness . As the cigar develops, hints of leather, soft spice, and toasted nuts emerge, all wrapped in a smooth, mellow texture that remains consistent from start to finish. The finish is clean, slightly sweet , and satisfying. Designed for versatility and ease of enjoyment, the Metropolitan Host are an ideal choice for a morning smoke, a casual afternoon break, or a relaxing evening wind-down. Smooth, balanced, and highly approachable, it stands as a perfect everyday cigar—one that delivers classic flavor with a modern touch of sweetness.

The Ferio Tego Metropolitan Maduro continues the legacy of a beloved classic, reintroduced for today’s smokers with the same blend integrity that made it a staple in humidors for years. Originally part of the Nat Sherman portfolio, this time-tested Maduro has been carefully preserved by Michael Herklots and Brendan Scott, delivering a familiar, refined experience with a deeper, richer profile. Handcrafted in Honduras, the Metropolitan Maduro features a dark, flavorful Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over a core of Honduran binder and long-filler tobaccos, resulting in a smooth, medium-bodied cigar with added depth and character. From the first draw, expect a warm and inviting profile layered with notes of earth, cocoa, and toasted nuts , complemented by a natural sweetness that lingers on the palate. As the cigar develops, flavors of coffee, light spice, and cream emerge, creating a balanced interplay between richness and smoothness. Despite its dark Maduro appearance, the body remains approachable, offering complexity without heaviness. Consistent, flavorful, and easy to enjoy, the Metropolitan Maduro is a versatile cigar suited for both newer smokers exploring Maduro profiles and seasoned aficionados seeking a reliable, everyday option. Whether paired with coffee or dark rum, or simply enjoyed on its own, it delivers a satisfying experience rooted in tradition and craftsmanship.

While Ferio Tego Timeless Panamericana may be a relatively new cigar brand, it has actually been around for over a decade. Originally released in 2014 as an exclusive for the Nat Sherman Townhouse, the brand’s signature store located in Manhattan, this cigar became a nationwide offering just 4 years later, though still only at Nat Sherman retailers. Fast forward, and it is now a permanent part of the Ferio Tego portfolio, available for whoever wants it. Timeless Panamericana is produced by the skilled artisans at the world renowned Plasencia Cigars S.A. in Esteli, Nicaragua, and the original recipe remains the same to this day. That recipe includes a filler blend from Costa Rica and Nicaragua, a Nicaraguan binder, and a beautiful Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Old school appeal meets modern blending here, and the result is spectacular. So much so, in fact, that Timeless Panamericana has earned numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado since its re-release. The cedar chest housing the cigars is stunning. The cigars, each wearing black and gold double bands, almost appear too beautiful to smoke. The main band displaying the “Timeless” logo is quite reminiscent of the classic Nat Sherman version of this stick, and to anyone not paying close attention, they might think that’s what they’re getting. But low and behold, this Plasencia-made gem of a cigar is built for maximum performance, offering an easy draw and a razor-sharp burn every time. White pepper greets the palate with authority on the opening puffs, but the smoke soon settles into an earthy array of cedar, nuts, and rich raw tobacco flavor. A crisp backbone of spice holds the flavor profile together, and the finish is smooth and peppery. Medium-full-bodied and just complex enough to keep any connoisseur on their toes, Timeless Panamericana is certainly a cigar that you won’t forget. Made for seasoned cigar veterans, Timeless Panamericana is a cigar that can truly be considered “ultra-premium.” Medium-full-bodied, intensely flavorful, and satisfying to the max, this refined Nicaraguan heavy hitter is loved by aficionados all over the world. It is wonderfully paired with scotch or bourbon, but a simple cup of black coffee compliments it just fine. Fans of Nicaraguan flavor bombs such as My Father or Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua will likely enjoy the spicy, earthy attributes this stick has to offer. The folks at Ferio Tego couldn’t have come up with a better name for this blend. It is everything any cigar fanatic could want, and it has certainly stood the test of time. Ferio Tego Timeless Panamericana is truly a cigar that is, well, timeless!

In recent years, there has been a trend of celebrated cigar brands coming “back from the dead,” and one cluster of cigars that has proven hugely successful is the Timeless blends by Ferio Tego, formerly sold under the Nat Sherman umbrella. This specimen, Ferio Tego Timeless Sterling, resurrects the beloved Nat Sherman Sterling cigar that was once such a treasure in the humidors of many a connoisseur. This blend is made at the famed Quesada factory in the Dominican Republic using a heavily aged blend of Dominican filler and binder tobaccos. The finishing touch is a golden-brown Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper leaf. Of the four different variants in the Timeless series, Sterling is easily the most recognizable, and it certainly provides a nostalgic experience for those who enjoyed the blend in the Nat Sherman era. Black and silver boxes done with modern décor house the beautifully hand-crafted vitolas. A gold main band with the unmistakable Timeless logo is followed by a golden secondary bearing the Ferio Tego name. Construction is precise, allowing for a seamless and enjoyable smoking experience each and every time. A productive draw offers no shortage in smoke production, and the first flavors to greet the palate are nuts and herbs. This flavorful opening is soon followed by an array of black pepper and cedar, and a smoky, spicy finish rolls out of the nose on the retrohale. A sweet floral note lingers in the background, and after all is said and done Timeless Sterling finishes as a medium-bodied cigar. Made for true connoisseurs, Timeless Sterling has all the attributes that a classic high-end cigar would be known for. Delicately complex flavor, medium body with a creamy texture, and beautiful balance and construction make this treat something to look forward to. It pairs well with bourbon or scotch and can certainly be used for any of life’s celebratory purposes. Fans of sticks such as Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real or Montecristo Classic will surely enjoy the familiar flavor profile provided by such a rich Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf. The Timeless blends are back, and they seem to be living up to their name! Enjoy a Ferio Tego Timeless Sterling today and soak in all the opulent characteristics that only a true classic premium cigar can provide.

After the demise of the Nat Sherman cigar lineup in 2019, many long-time fans were a bit disheartened, to say the least. That’s when former Nat Sherman executives Michael Herklots and Brendon Scott stepped up to the plate, bought rights to the two biggest lines (Timeless and Metropolitan Selection), and kept the heartbeat of the projects going, now sold under the new brand name, Ferio Tego . Though all the Timeless variants have done exceptionally well, one seems to stand out just a little in front of the rest: Timeless Supreme . This Nicaraguan puro, made by the Plasencia family down in sunny Nicaragua, contains 100% Nicaraguan tobacco through and through—wrapper, filler, and binder. This top-grade tobacco is grown on the Plasencia farms and delicately aged and cured to be used in only the finest projects, and we assure you; this one certainly qualifies. The Timeless Supreme turned out so well it earned a stellar 95 rating in Cigar Aficionado and #10 Cigar of the Year by Cigar Aficionado , and appropriately so. Black-topped cedar chests house the gorgeous box-pressed works of fine tobacco art, each one dressed in double black and gold bands. Precision rolling provides a phenomenal smoking experience every time, with an easy and productive draw offering immense clouds of dense smoke from each puff. Spicy white pepper and a hint of herbs opens things up. Soon after, the earthy raw tobacco backbone makes its presence felt, becoming the dominant part of the flavor profile. Notes of cinnamon, leather, and cedar are easily detectable, and the finish is crisp and toasty. When all is said and done, Timeless Supreme finishes as a stout full-bodied cigar. Made for those with years of experience, Timeless Supreme is nothing short of a connoisseur-level cigar. Full-bodied and complex, with well-rounded twists and turns throughout the flavor profile, this rich treat leaves very little to be desired. It pairs well with bourbon or scotch, but a hot cup of black coffee makes for a lovely pairing as well. If you’ve already re-visited the Nat Sherman era by enjoying Timeless Sterling or Timeless Panamericana , you definitely owe it to yourself to give this edition a try. Maybe you are an old school Nat Sherman fan. Maybe you just like full-bodied sticks that are made with some of the world’s finest tobacco. Maybe you just like sticks with cool bands and boxes. No matter how you put it, Ferio Tego Timeless Supreme is a cigar that is doubtless going to leave a good impression.

The new Flor De Las Antillas Maduro cigar has a lot of legacy to live up to, what with coming from the venerable My Father Cigars and all that, but it handles the pressure cool as a cucumber. Never mind that the natural-wrapped version of this blend was named #1 Cigar of the Year in 2012. Pass over the fact that the near-twin My Father Le Bijou 1922 won the same honor in 2015. Here we stand at the dawn of a new day, the moment of opportunity for the Ecuadorian-grown Habano Sun Grown Oscuro wrapper to shine a light all its own onto the masses of eager smokers chomping at the bit. How will the savory and robust Nicaraguan fillers and binders, sourced from three of the Garcia family's best farms, react to the newcomer? They rise to the occasion, of course. Sniffed straight from the humidor, the broad and red-banded foot of the Flor De Las Antillas Maduro cigar allows earthy, woody aromas to flow from the thickly layered tobaccos within, while the shimmering Oscuro wrapper smells more of fresh hay and chocolate. The gorgeously decorated primary label is an instant classic, while impeccable rolling technique pleases the eye, the hand, the lips. Crisp yet robust from the moment it is lit, the smoke pours from the cigar lush with spice, oak, dark berries, cocoa, and salt. Further expansion of flavor will seem impossible until later appearances of black coffee, leather, citrus, and red licorice fill the mouth and the nose with wave after creamy wave of delight. Solidly medium-full in both strength and body this is not a cigar for the meek but should appeal to any enthusiast with a desire to taste the best in life. Exquisite when paired with hefty a pour of VSOP or even XO cognac, the Flor De Las Antillas Maduro is well prepared to take over the world even when all by itself. Come along for the ride.

Created by cigar master Manuel Quesada, the Fonseca Classic line of fine premium cigars is expertly handmade of long-filler leaf from the Cibao region of the Dominican Republic. The Fonseca Classic is a medium-strength cigar that is hand-rolled in the Dominican Republic. It features a light-brown Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper that covers a binder and filler made of tobacco from the Dominican Republic. (Shop other Fonseca Cigars ) The Fonseca Classic is a well-balanced cigar with notes of cedar and cream. If you want an easygoing yet elegant, mellow yet mouthwatering smoke, fill your humidor with the Fonseca brand of premium handmade cigars.

Fonseca has an image problem, they are known for making amazing mild cigars. Doesn't sound like too much of a problem right? Well it is when you are trying to build your market into more robust flavors but too many smokers shrug you off as the mild cigar company. When Fonseca released the Cubano Limitado, fans of the brand thought that Fonseca went too far in the opposite direction. Now with the release of the Cubano Exclusivo, they have found a happy medium. (Shop other Fonseca Cigars ) The Fonseca Cubano Exclusivo is a wonderful blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos bound in a Dominican leaf and wrapped in a smooth Dominican Havana Vuelta Arriba wrapper. This cigar starts off firmly as a medium bodied smoke, but inches just slightly higher the more you smoke. Notes of the earth, wood, and pepper greet you and play off each other throughout the entire cigar. The final third brings more pepper to the forefront and downplays the other complexities but never drowns them out. If you have disregarded Fonseca before because you thought they were too mild a smoke for you, this is the cigar to try. Much more evenly flavored and bodied than anything from the fabled brand's past, the Cubano Exclusivo is a perfect medium-bodied stick.

More known for their milder cigars, Fonseca has created a medium-to-full-bodied masterpiece with their Cubano Limitado. Have you always wanted to smoke a Cuban cigar but keep letting those pesky customs laws get in your way? The Fonseca Cubano Limitado is about as close as you're going to get. Blended by the legend of the industry, Manuel Quesada, a filler of fantastic leaf from the Dominican Republic, a binder of strong Nicaraguan Ligero, and a beautiful dark and oily Honduran Habano wrapper perfectly mesh to give this cigar just the right amount of power and flavor. (Shop other Fonseca Cigars ) A minimalistic band of black and gold truly makes the complex flavors that await a hidden gem ready to be unearthed. The smooth, oily wrapper with hardly a vein to be seen is the first hint at the quality found beneath. First light brings on a spiciness which quickly gives way to a creamy cedar flavor. The aroma on the Fonseca Cubano Limitado is just as enticing as the flavors. Almost perfect construction, we found a slightly tight draw for the first few puffs, but that quickly opened up to a fantastic smoke. While there is some debate on whether this cigar is medium or full on the strength scale, we found it closer to the medium end. Fonseca's Cubano Limitado may be the closest you will get to tasting something similar to a cigar from that island south of Miami. Flavor, just enough power, and near perfect construction is what you can expect from the master behind this fantastic stogie, and it is exactly what you will get. The smoky cedar qualities of this cigar meshed perfectly with a nice sweet barbeque sauce, and is perfect for gatherings around the grill.

My Father Cigars is one of the most dominant giants of the cigar industry, so when they acquired the rights to Fonseca back in 2019, it was nothing short of a big deal, to say the least. Not only did the renowned Garcia family bring new life to the brand, so to speak, but they now had a new name in the company’s portfolio to expand on, and that they did. Behold, Fonseca Mexico Edition! Also known as Edition MX, this line extension puts Mexico in the spotlight by combining a gorgeous Mexican San Andres wrapper leaf with the all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend that put My Father Fonseca at the top of the charts to begin with. Made at the world-famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, this all-new Fonseca brand has taken off, earning multiple 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado and becoming a fixture in millions of humidors worldwide. A beautiful cedar chest decorated with both My Father and Fonseca logos houses the beautiful, handcrafted cigars, each vitola wearing 2 bands, the secondary designating the MX Edition. Built for maximum performance, this blend offers a smooth and productive draw that leaves nothing to be desired. White pepper is the opening flavor, and there is no shortage of it. A storm of spicy white pepper bombards the palate before the flavor profile opens up to a colorful array of savory spices wrapped around a dark, earthy core. Hints of coffee and cocoa dance around the outside of the flavor profile, and the finish is sweet, spicy, and smoky. Full-bodied to the max and balanced with precision, My Father Fonseca Mexico Edition is certainly a cigar that demonstrates what a classic Garcia family cigar should be. Fonseco Mexico Edition is made for the experienced. Newbies should look elsewhere. It takes a well-seasoned palate to be able to enjoy all the beautiful attributes that make this cigar as special as it is. Full-bodied and dark, this stick pairs well with dark beer, coffee, or dark rum. It compares to such full-bodied San Andres cigars as La Historia by EP Carrillo or Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 3 , so if you enjoy either, this might be your next big purchase! My Father Cigars took Fonseca to an entirely new level, and Fonseca Mexico Edition is a level that you simply have to experience to understand.

Foundation Cigars may not be the most talked about name in the business, but over the years the brand has more than proven itself to be connoisseur-worthy and then some. Aksum Claro is a re-branded blend that was previously offered by Foundation as Metapa Claro, and to this day it remains one of the company’s most sought-after brands. Made in Nicaragua by none other than AJ Fernandez, Aksum Claro pays homage to the history of the Aksumite Kingdom, a civilization of the ancient world located near modern-day Ethiopia. Legend has it that in ancient times, the Ark of the Covenant was brought to Aksum by Menelik the First, the supposed son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. Local lore tells that the Ark remains there to this day, where it is guarded day and night by a single priest. Representing a blend of rich flavors and artisanal expertise, Aksum Claro couldn’t be a better fit to allude to such a story. As for the blend, the filler is from Nicaragua, the binder is Connecticut Broadleaf, and the wrapper is a gorgeous Sumatra Claro leaf grown in the volcanic soil of Ecuador. Though brand owner Nicholas Melillo’s blend may seem straightforward on paper, something magical happens when you set fire to it, and apparently the folks at Cigar Aficionado wholeheartedly agree, as they were quick to give Aksum Claro multiple 90+ ratings, the best being a very respectable 93. The same year, this blend made it into the famed magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of the Year. A refined cedar chest topped with a black and gold lid houses the expertly rolled vitolas, each one wearing a single blue and red band including a portrait of Ras Makonnen, a 19th Century governor of the Aksumite Kingdom. The construction is incredible on each cigar, and the draw is always easy and productive. Spicy Nicaraguan pepper explodes like a bomb upon lighting, soon followed by a blast of espresso and nuts. Woody nuances decorate the outer bands of the flavor profile, while an earthy raw tobacco core binds everything together in beautiful harmony. The finish is spicy, with no shortage of white pepper on the tip of the tongue. All-in-all, Aksum Claro finishes as a complex and well-balanced medium-full-bodied cigar. Not for newbies, Aksum Claro is geared towards the experienced. A well-developed palate and no shortage of patience are required to be able to fully enjoy all the good things this stick has to offer. Paired with bourbon or dark rum, Aksum Claro makes a fine treat at the end of a busy work week, but it is equally enjoyable with a cup of your favorite coffee or espresso after dinner. Cigars such as New World Dorado or San Lotano come to mind when thinking about similar stature, so if you have enjoyed either AJ Fernandez specialty, odds are you’re going to like this one. This cigar may pay homage to a story about the most sacred treasure of all time, but if we are being honest, Aksum Claro is a treasure in and of itself.

Nicholas Melillo and his Foundation Cigars have been on somewhat of a rampage in recent years, steadily gaining momentum with each and every new and delicious blend. One such blend is Aksum Maduro , the AJ Fernandez-made masterpiece coming out of Nicaragua that has been raising the eyebrows of maduro fans across the globe. Named after the fabled Aksumite Kingdom, where, according to legend, the Ark of the Covenant is located, this rich and tasty blend is already esteemed as one of Melillo’s best, and for good reason! The unique blend consists of Nicaraguan fillers from the fertile regions of Jalapa and Esteli, a Connecticut Broadleaf binder, and a dark, oily Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper leaf. Heavily aged and fermented to exacting standards, all tobacco used in the production of this cigar is considered to be ultra-premium and is selected by AJ Fernandez himself. Not that this cigar needs any further accolades, but its rating history in Cigar Aficionado is nothing short of stellar, with its highest rating yet being a rock-solid 92 . Black and gold cedar chests house the intricately crafted vitolas, each one wearing a simple gold, red, and blue band. Box-pressed, seamlessly rolled, and sporting a pigtail cap, Aksum Maduro is every bit as beautiful as it is delicious. Cedar and red pepper open things up at first light, soon settling into a scrumptious array of nuts, cocoa, and molasses . All this is wrapped around a core of earthy tobacco flavor, and the finish is sweet and crisp. Medium-full-bodied, Aksum Maduro tells one beautiful story as it smokes. Made for experienced connoisseurs, Aksum Maduro is one of the most easily recognizable Foundation cigars. Its complex and refined flavor profile, its medium-full-bodied feel, and its expert construction make it a cigar lover’s dream-come-true. It pairs well with black coffee, dark beer, or port wine and is certainly enjoyable at any time of the day. Fans of dark Nicaraguan sticks such as Oliva Serie V or My Father will definitely come to enjoy the rich and spicy flavor profile this cigar has to offer. Whether you are looking for something new and hot or care to follow Nicholas Melillo on his inevitable journey to the top, Aksum Maduro is a cigar you won’t want to pass up.

Nicholas Melillo of Foundation Cigars has more than rocked the world of premium cigars with his Charter Oak lineup, a collection of top-shelf, AJ Fernandez-made masterpieces that are all hit and no miss. In recent years, however, he wanted something more for the brand, something “special,” so he once again collaborated with AJ Fernandez to create Charter Oak Pegnataro, also known as Charter Oak Especiales CT Shade Pegnataro. Released alongside a darker, more robust sister cigar known as Pasquale, this Pegnataro blend uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut Seed Shade wrapper leaf over a Nicaraguan filler and binder blend. Incredibly flavorful for a Connecticut-wrapped cigar, this blend certainly personifies what a “fancy” Connecticut cigar should be. According to Melillo, “The Charter Oak core line would have been the everyday cigar, and these new blends (Pegnataro and Pasquale) would be for the weekend or a special occasion.” Whatever occasion you happen to choose, this choice of cigar is right. Both Pegnataro and Pasquale are available in one size, a 5 ½” x 48 Corona Gorda , or “long robusto,” as some call it. Rustic wooden boxes contain the expertly crafted cigars, made in the world-famous Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua. Each stick wears a classic Charter Oak band, but in gold and navy blue, with the addition of “Pegnataro” beneath the branding. A pigtail cap adds character to the cigars’ rustically beautiful appearance, and the construction is second to none. Billowing clouds of smoke massage the palate with a burst of cedar on the opening. Notes of leather and hay begin to hint towards an earthy main note, and before long, Pegnataro becomes a creamy dose of Connecticut goodness, combined with an earthy core of Nicaraguan tobacco flavor. Hints of white pepper on the finish round things out, and overall, this blend finishes on the heavier end of mild-medium-bodied . Crafted for long-time connoisseurs of mild-medium-bodied cigars, Pegnataro is rich, flavorful, and impeccably balanced. Easy on the palate, this Connecticut-wrapped beauty pairs well with scotch, cognac, or your favorite white wine. It is part of what has become an entire genre on today’s market, Ecuadorian Connecticut flavor bombs, sharing a place with the likes of Oliva Connecticut Reserve and Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real . For an unforgettable top-tier Connecticut smoking experience, you owe it to yourself to try Charter Oak Especiales CT Shade Pegnataro and find out just how flavorful and satisfying a simple Connecticut cigar really can be.

You may not know much about the Foundation Cigar Company right now, but you're sure as heck going to want to find out after trying the phenomenal Charter Oak Connecticut Shade cigar. After setting out on his own from Drew Estate and then stunning the world with the El Gueguense, Foundation founder Nicholas Melillo decided to honor his home state of Connecticut with a rich and creamy medium-bodied smoke coated in the only tobacco that would suffice: a flawless and golden Connecticut Shade. Named after a legendary tree that stood for centuries in Hartford as an icon of freedom, these affordable sticks are comprised of lush Nicaraguan filler, a spicy binder from Sumatra, and the aforementioned glorious wrapper. Melillio has made perhaps the wisest of choices by having each and every Foundation Charter Oak Connecticut Shade constructed at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua, one of the highest-quality cigar factories on the planet. This means you can expect a level of craftmanship and smoking enjoyment far beyond that found in most other budget stogies. In perfect compliment to the sunny hue of each vitola, the band is a simple black and white affair decorated with an image of its namesake monument. Thick smoke pours easily through the well-balanced longleaf at the core of each stick, at first ripe with dark chocolate and nutmeg before mellowing slightly with cedar and cream. Some toasted almond enters near the halfway mark, joined soon after by a flourish of spice to keep the palate in thrall all the way to the nub. Priced for everyday enjoyment, you'll still find a reason to mark special occasions with one of these delectable treats. Not just another one of the forgettable mild stogies that litter the tobacco landscape, a Foundation Charter Oak Connecticut Shade cigar will be sought out again and again for their smooth, delightful character. Grab yourself a handful or a box today and get to having a grand old time.

Foundation Cigars is a name that has really picked up momentum in recent years, and some would agree that Charter Oak Especiales Pasquale is one of their best releases to date. Named after Foundation founder Nicholas Melillo's grandfathers, this line pays homage to the two men that introduced him to cigars and inspired him to be who he is today. In addition to paying homage to Melillo's grandfathers, this series also commemorates the company's new office on a 300-acre farm in the middle of the Connecticut River Valley growing region. Made at the famed AJ Fernandez factory in Nicaragua, the Especiales line consists of two variants (one for each grandfather): Pregnataro, a medium-bodied stick draped in a golden Connecticut shade wrapper leaf, and the cigar in question, Pasquale, a bolder, richer, fuller-bodied cigar boasting a nearly black Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. The filler and binder blend is made up entirely of aged Nicaraguan tobacco. Both variants are available in one size, a 5 ½" x 48 robusto size that offers a beautiful take on the flavor that Melillo and company worked so hard to achieve. Packed in humble cedar chests of 12, each vitola wears a single band depicting the Charter Oak tree the brand was originally inspired by, representing Melillo's home state of Connecticut. Meticulously crafted to offer a soft and abundant draw and an even burn, Pasquale starts off by sending billowing clouds of thick smoke to greet the palate. The first flavors include what one would expect from a dark Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro cigar: cocoa, espresso, and spicy black pepper. A soft dark chocolate note seems to be the core of the flavor profile, and the whole package is spiked with accents of sweet brown sugar throughout. The finish is long and heavy, yet all-in-all, the medium-full-bodied flavor profile is delicately balanced. As Melillo said in a press release, "The Charter Oak core line would have been [his grandfathers'] everyday cigar, and these new blends (Charter Oak Especiales) would be for the weekend or a special occasion." Well said, and we can't help but agree. This pair of beauties is called "Especiales" for a reason, and we can wholeheartedly recommend either blend to be a great special occasion accompaniment. Pasquale pairs well with coffee or dark beer and is similar in stature to such other fuller-bodied maduro cigars as Oliva Serie G Maduro or San Lotano Maduro , so if either fits your fancy, why not give Pasquale a shot? Nicholas Melillo is known for adding special meaning to his cigars, and Charter Oak Especiales Pasquale not only serves to commemorate his beloved grandfathers, but to provide the cigar world with an amazing maduro cigar that never disappoints.

The Charter Oak series from Foundation Cigars has proven that an incredible cigar doesn’t have to cost an arm and a leg, and with both a Connecticut and Broadleaf option in the lineup, there was something for almost everyone. The cigar world rejoiced when Nicholas Melillo announced a third option: Charter Oak Habano . This blend bridges the gap, presenting a medium-bodied option with a classic flavor profile that will appeal to smokers of all experience levels. For the recipe, we have Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco finished with a golden brown Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. Like its counterparts, Charter Oak Habano is expertly crafted at the renowned Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars in Nicaragua. So let’s put it all together, a premium cigar rolled at one of the finest factories on the planet, using top shelf tobacco and blended by AJ Fernandez, all for a price that rivals most “bargain” cigars? What if we said it has earned as high as a 92 rating in Cigar Aficionado as well? By this point, there is little need for more convincing that this is anything short of a stellar offering. Wooden dress boxes house the single-banded cigars, each one wearing a white and black band depicting the centuries-old tree from Hartford, Connecticut after which the blend is named. The roll is velvety smooth, and the wrapper has a light sheen from the natural oils. A clean cut reveals an easy draw, one that produces delightful volumes of silky, white smoke. Black pepper is the dominant opening note, soon joined by a heavy presence of nuts and cream. Earthy tobacco undertones hold the profile together, as hints of cedar and bakers’ spices add to the complexity. A sweet, smooth finish rounds things out, and this blend settles precisely in the middle of the spectrum, the very definition of a medium-bodied cigar. Suitable for all audiences, this fantastic option is as versatile as it is delicious. More experienced connoisseurs will appreciate the subtle complexities and the overall value, while beginners will enjoy the easy, satisfying medium body. Pair this one with your favorite bourbon or scotch or simply enjoy it alongside a cup of hot coffee for a simple, yet memorable experience. Fans of the original Charter Oak lines, including CT Shade and CT Broadleaf , will definitely want to try this one for comparative purposes. A top-notch premium cigar from one of the finest brands, made by one of the best in the business, all for an affordable price? We agree, it sounds too good to be true, but you have to try one to believe it. No doubt, Charter Oak Habano will change the way you think about wallet-friendly cigars.

Ten years ago, Nicholas Melillo founded Foundation Cigar Company with a simple mission: honor the traditions of premium cigar making while telling stories rooted in history, culture, and exceptional tobacco. In the years that followed, Foundation became one of the industry's most respected boutique manufacturers, producing acclaimed blends that seamlessly combine old-world craftsmanship with modern innovation. To commemorate this remarkable milestone, Melillo presents the Foundation 10 Year Aniversario Salomon , a limited-edition release that celebrates a decade of dedication, creativity, and uncompromising quality. This cigar earned an outstanding 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado , affirming Nicholas Melillo’s legacy of crafting top-tier, highly acclaimed releases. Handcrafted at the renowned AJ Fernandez factory in Nicaragua , this commemorative blend showcases some of the finest tobaccos Foundation has ever assembled. At its core lies a rich combination of premium Nicaraguan fillers from Estelí, Jalapa, and Condega, secured beneath a flavorful Brazilian Mata Fina binder. The finishing touch is a truly distinctive Connecticut Broadleaf and CT Havana Seed hybrid wrapper , cultivated in Connecticut's famed River Valley on the very farm that also serves as Foundation's corporate headquarters. The result is a cigar that pays tribute not only to the company's heritage, but also to the tobacco-growing traditions that helped shape Nicholas Melillo's career. Presented in an elegant 7" x 58 Salomon vitola, the cigar allows the blend to evolve gradually as the smoke progresses. The tapered foot delivers a focused, concentrated opening before the wider body fully reveals the blend's remarkable complexity. Thick, velvety clouds of smoke introduce rich notes of dark chocolate, espresso , and earthy tobacco , followed by layers of cedar, black pepper, and baking spice . As the cigar develops, subtle natural sweetness emerges, balancing the richer components and creating a smooth, refined finish that lingers long after the final draw. The presentation is every bit as meaningful as the blend itself. Inspired by Saint George and the Dragon, the commemorative artwork symbolizes courage, perseverance, and triumph, qualities that have defined Foundation Cigars since its inception. Produced in an extremely limited run of just 35,000 cigars , the Foundation 10 Year Aniversario Salomon is far more than a celebration of the company's past. It is a statement of everything Foundation has become and a fitting tribute to one of the most influential boutique cigar makers of the modern era. Whether you're a longtime Foundation devotee or discovering Nicholas Melillo's craftsmanship for the first time, this exceptional anniversary release is destined to become one of the crown jewels of your humidor.

Master Blender Nick Melillo has been around tobacco all his life, a charmed existence indeed culminating in the remarkable Charter Oak Connecticut Broadleaf cigar. Gifted with an innate taste for good longleaf, Melillo wasn't long out of school before finding himself at Drew Estate, where he would rise to VP. The desire to create his own brands necessitated a gracious departure and soon the Foundation Cigar Company was started in the same lush tobacco-growing region of Connecticut where Melillo grew up, which also happens to be the source of the magnificent Broadleaf wrapper that so gracefully covers the rich Nicaraguan filler at the core of each vitola. It is obvious that a lot of love went into the creation of the Charter Oak Connecticut Broadleaf, for each solidly-built cigar exudes a character that can't be accounted for simply by the quality of its construction. Or maybe it's just the heady aroma of sweet cocoa and ripe tobacco that wafts from the shimmering outer leaf. The foot is rolled closed, but the draw through an unlit stick is open enough to provide hints of cedar and dried fruit. Easily lit, this smoke factory of a stick opens semi-sweet with dark chocolate and earth atop more subtle flavors of citrus and hazelnut. Becoming somewhat peppery at the midpoint, this is also where coffee and a touch of caramel enter to keep the strength hovering just above the middle mark. The low price we have listed for these fine smokes is no typo, ladies and gentlemen. Designed as a bargain cigar from the get-go, the folks at Foundation have simply outdone themselves. A Charter Oak Connecticut Broadleaf cigar can rise to your most demanding occasion but serves just as well each day with a morning Cup o' Joe or two (maybe three) fingers of whiskey in the evening. Take advantage of this great deal before we all come to our senses.

When George Carnarvon, the Eighth Earl of Carnarvon, commissioned Foundation Cigar Company to make a cigar named after his famous English castle in Highclere, Hampshire, Highclere Castle Victorian was born. The project is actually a collaboration between Foundation and AJ Fernandez, who makes the cigars at his state-of-the-art factory in Nicaragua. The blend is comprised of Nicaraguan filler tobacco, a Brazilian Mata Fina binder, and a dark, oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. Every bit as luxurious as the castle it's named after, Highclere Castle Victorian has earned a 93 rating from Cigar Aficionado and a spot on the Top 25 Cigars of 2020. Simple, yet fancy red and gold bands hug each expertly crafted vitola. A nearly seamless roll ensures an even burn, sharp ash, and an easy draw that produces plenty of silky white smoke. Black pepper is the first thing to hit the palate, bringing about the familiar Nicaraguan spice that AJ Fernandez is so well-known for. Shortly thereafter, earthy tobacco flavor, cream, and cedar join the mix, with a sweet finish through the nose. Notes of chocolate, cinnamon, and red pepper are noticeable throughout the delightfully simple smoking experience, and by the end Highclere Castle Victorian finishes just above medium-bodied. Made with the discriminating aficionado in mind, Highclere Castle Victorian is an upper tier cigar aimed at more experienced smokers. The profile is quite simple, yet the subtle complexities contained therein call for a well-seasoned palate for true enjoyment. This blend pairs well with bourbon, red wine, or even coffee, and is appropriate for any time of the day. Fans of AJ Fernandez sticks such as New World or Bellas Artes will likely thoroughly enjoy the blend in question. For some of us, a good cigar gives us the taste of luxury we need to enjoy the fruits of our labor. That taste of luxury gets a whole lot better with Highclere Castle Victorian, so don't hesitate to try one the next time you are in search of something new!

Headlining the award-winning Highclere Castle series from Foundation Cigars, Highclere Castle Edwardian is a refined cigar made with the sophisticated connoisseur in mind. The Highclere Castle project is a collaboration between brand owner Nick Melillo and the Earl of Carnarvon, paying homage to the cigars enjoyed by British Nobility in the early 20 th Century. Made at the AJ Fernandez’s famed factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, this meticulously crafted blend contains a spicy Brazilian Mata Fina binder along with a filler combination of hybrid Nicaraguan Corojo and Criollo leaves known as Nicadan, cultivated in Jalapa and Ometepe. The wrapper is a Connecticut shade leaf grown in the volcanic soil of Ecuador. Simple, yet intriguing, this mix works together to create a 92-rated masterpiece that is sure to leave a lasting impression. Blue and gold cedar chests, white and gold bands, and expert craftsmanship combine to make a product that looks every bit as good as it tastes. A smooth draw produces dense ribbons of silky smoke, while a razor-sharp burn and firm ash provide a classic experience every time. An initial greeting of spicy white pepper soon settles into a creamy, flavorful mixture of cinnamon, citrus, and earth , all culminating into a core of classic raw tobacco flavor. The finish is creamy and crisp, and altogether Edwardian finishes as a solid medium-bodied cigar. Made for the most demanding aficionados, Highclere Castle Edwardian is a top-tier cigar that offers a complex medium-bodied smoking experience like the premium cigars of old. Pair this one with your favorite scotch, white wine, or hot tea and be sure to set aside plenty of time to take in all the subtle nuances this blend has to offer. Fans of Foundation’s other Connecticut highlights such as Charter Oak Connecticut or The Tabernacle No. 142 are surely going to want to give this one a try. If you’re in the market for something special, try a Highclere Castle Edwardian and smoke like the nobility, and don’t hesitate to enjoy every second of it.

Olmec Claro by Foundation Cigars demonstrates the true beauty of Mexican tobacco while paying homage to one of the most ancient civilizations of North America. Named after the natives indigenous to the area where today’s Mexican tobacco is grown and harvested, Nicholas Melillo’s Olmec series is available in 2 variations: Maduro and Claro. This Claro version has a lighter wrapper leaf and offers a more crisp and light-hearted smoking experience. Like all Foundation cigars, Olmec Claro is made by the skilled hands at AJ Fernandez’s factory in Nicaragua. The blend consists of select 3 year-aged Nicaraguan filler leaves from Esteli and Jalapa, a Nicaraguan binder, and a caramel brown Mexican San Andres Claro leaf. Sounds tasty, right? The folks at Cigar Aficionado certainly seemed to think so, as in 2023 Olmec Claro earned a stellar 93 rating, along with a spot on the magazine’s prestigious Top 25 Cigars of the Year list. Handsome cedar chests house the single banded vitolas, each dressed in black, yellow, and gold. Construction leaves absolutely nothing to be desired, as each mildly pressed oily beauty is rolled precisely to offer an easy, productive draw every single time. Cocoa and pepper open things up, followed up by a one-two punch of cedar and raw tobacco . Sweet bakers’ spices decorate the edges of the flavor profile, and a definitive ginger note is detectable on the crisp, clean finish. Medium-full-bodied and delicately complex, Olmec Claro is a cigar built for the most discriminating connoisseurs. Made for the experienced, Olmec Claro follows suit behind its Foundation Cigars brothers and sisters. It is uncannily refined, astonishingly complex, and offers a satisfying experience guaranteed to please any palate that yearns for a luxuriously delicious smoking experience. Pair it with your favorite bourbon, scotch, or medium-bodied beer for a relaxing and unforgettable smoking session that will have you coming back for more every time. Fans of cigars such as New World Decenio or San Lotano will definitely appreciate the AJ Fernandez DNA incorporated into the blend. Take a journey into the world of how premium cigars should be. Try an Omec Claro and celebrate the heritage of Mexican Tobacco the Foundation way.

Foundation Cigars and AJ Fernandez have teamed up once again, and this time the masterpiece is of the maduro variety! Behold, Olmec Maduro ! This stick is part 2 of a 2-cigar series which pays homage to the land of the ancient Olmecs, now modern-day Veracruz, Tabasco, and San Andres Tuxtla. In other words, it is the part of Mexico that is known for growing some of the best maduro tobacco on the planet. Olmec Maduro is handmade at the AJ Fernandez factory in Nicaragua using only the finest Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco. This extensively aged package is then finished with a dark, oily, and absolutely gorgeous San Andres Maduro wrapper leaf grown in the very region the brand honors. Spicy, flavorful, and rich, Olmec Maduro has garnered quite a bit of admiration, not to mention multiple 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado , the highest being a very respectable 94 . Housed in a beautiful cedar chest, Olmec Maduro wears a yellow and black band reminiscent of a classic Cuban cigar at first glance. The construction leaves nothing to be desired, as this cigar is produced at one of the world’s foremost cigar factories, and AJ Fernandez leaves no detail overlooked. An easy draw produces thick bursts of smoke, which at first puff offer astounding flavors of spice and coffee. Cedar, cocoa, and cinnamon are quick to join the party, and as the cigar progresses, the rich, earthy core makes its way to the forefront. A black cherry finish ties the package together, and overall Olmec Maduro finishes strong as a full-bodied cigar . Well-balanced, complex, and packed with flavor, Olmec Maduro is a connoisseur’s dream-come-true. This especially applies to cigar fanatics that tend to lean towards maduro cigars, as we all know there is just something special about a good San Andres Maduro. Pair this flavor bomb with black coffee or tawny port for a truly invigorating experience, and feel free to see how it stacks up to such other top San Andres sticks as La Historia or The Wise Man Maduro . Whether a long-time supporter of AJ Fernandez, a fan of today’s Foundation Cigars, or just someone that appreciates a good, solid maduro stick, Olmec Maduro by Foundation Cigars is a gem that deserves a spot in your humidor.

The Tabernacle is a cigar made for aficionados, by an aficionado. The second line in the Foundation series, The Tabernacle brand encompasses themes from the Bible, King Solomon, and the Ark of the Covenant. The Foundation brand is owned and operated by former Head of Production at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate, Nicholas Melillo. After spending over a decade in Nicaragua while working for Jonathan Drew and company, Melillo built quite the reputation for himself, becoming known as somewhat of a master at blending hearty Nicaraguan tobaccos and producing amazing blends, some of his more notable accolades being none other than Liga Privada No. 9, UF-13, T52, and of course, Nica Rustica. After parting ways with Drew Estate, Melillo began the Foundation brand, his first release, El Gueguense, garnering unusually high ratings and even a spot on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 list. Then came The Tabernacle, a sort of collaboration with industry rock star AJ Fernandez. Made down in Nicaragua at the famed Tabacalera Fernandez; The Tabernacle is rolled using some of the finest tobacco in the world, a good bit of it coming from AJ's personal farm, La Soledad. Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers, a Mexican San Andres binder, and a dark, toothy Connecticut broadleaf Maduro wrapper make this cigar as flavorful as it is beautiful. The Tabernacle blend has received a multiple prestigious 90 ratings from Cigar Aficionado magazine. Rolled in typical AJ Fernandez fashion, The Tabernacle is precisely constructed to offer a smooth, easy draw and a plethora of thick, flavorful smoke. Beginning with a blast of white pepper, The Tabernacle quickly transitions to a smooth, pleasant, classic Maduro flavor profile. Chocolate, espresso, nuts, and spice massage the palate as a raw tobacco presence in the background holds it all together. A sweet finish and a smooth retrohale further add to the depth and complexity of the blend. Overall, The Tabernacle is an amazing display of blending prowess and tobacco expertise. It takes Maduro into a whole new dimension. As one may conclude, Foundation The Tabernacle, is not a beginners' cigar, like the other masterpieces on Melillo's resume. It is an ultra-premium blend made with discriminating palates in mind. In other words, only true connoisseurs need to apply. Sitting at the high end of medium-to-full, The Tabernacle pairs wonderfully with coffee, port wine, or dark beer, and is best enjoyed after a good meal. Similar sticks may include Liga Privada No. 9 and Nica Rustica, both of which Nicholas Melillo had a huge part in producing. When asked about the name of this stick, Melillo described how when he was growing up in Connecticut; he began smoking cigars with his grandfather. He considered their time spent smoking together to be sacred, and his humidor became his "tabernacle." Quite the story, really, and quite a cigar as well. Nicholas Melillo has nothing to prove. He has already had a hand in some of the most famous cigars in history. However, now it is his time to truly shine, and Foundation The Tabernacle is doubtless destined to be something huge.

Foundation Cigars is best known for their upper-tier creations geared toward serious aficionados, but they have stepped outside of the box to offer something edgy, fun, and downright delicious: The Upsetters Maduro . For those who don’t know, the Upsetters is a series of Nicaraguan-made cigars that pay homage to the rich history of Jamaica. In addition to a premium blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco, each and every Upsetters cigar contains a dose of Jamaican Cow Tongue leaf, tobacco native to Jamaica and grown in the very region where the indigenous Arawak people grew tobacco centuries ago. The Upsetters series contains 8 sizes, each sporting a different wrapper leaf. This Maduro variant is cloaked with a dark and oily Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper, and like all cigars in the series, the tobacco has undergone “Caribbean Atmospheric Herbal Fusion” to give it a uniquely beautiful, infused aroma and flavor profile. Black boxes and bands with rainbow accents and logos are the common denominators across the board with the Upsetters series. To make it easier, however, each cigar wears a secondary band denoting both the size and title. The pre-light aroma may seem a bit overwhelming at first, something like stepping into a herb shop or tropical greenhouse but relaxing. This intense bouquet is only on the surface. The easy draw provides plenty of smoke on every puff, and just a hint of the pre-light aroma is detectable amid the rich maduro flavor profile. Notes of rich tobacco, coffee, and cocoa dazzle the taste buds as peppery spice lingers in the background. Medium-bodied, the Upsetters Maduro really shines as the go-to Maduro of the bunch. Suitable for all audiences, the Upsetters Maduro tells a story with its flavor profile. Unlike other infused cigars, the surface aroma doesn’t translate much into the actual flavor of the smoke, making it a great choice for anyone who may have given infused cigars a try but quickly ran the other way, so to speak. It pairs well with black coffee, dark beer, or dark rum, and is a great choice for any fan of mildly-infused cigars such as Larutan or Isla Del Sol . The motto of the brand is “Dare to be different.” It goes without saying that if you do in fact dare to be different and grab an Upsetters Maduro, your taste buds will thank you!

It’s been over a decade since Nicholas Melillo’s Foundation Cigar Company debuted with El Gueguense and rocked the world of premium cigars. Now, more blends are being introduced year by year, and El Gueguense is now represented in its English translation: The Wise Man. 2024 marked the release of The Wise Man Corojo cigar , a Nicaraguan-made masterpiece that seriously spiced things up for the brand (literally). Formerly made by Aganorsa Leaf, The Wise Man, along with all Foundation cigars, are now produced at the world famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, with blending and production being overseen by none other than Don Pepin and Jaime Garcia. That being said, it’s not surprising that Foundation now offers a top-notch Corojo stick, and a darned good one at that. In fact, this package is a Nicaraguan puro, meaning all tobacco used for the blend comes from the fertile soil of Nicaragua—wrapper, filler, and binder. Every leaf is grown in Nicaragua’s finest growing regions of Esteli, Jalapa, and Condega, and the wrapper leaf is a gorgeous red-hued Nicaraguan Corojo, one of Don Pepin’s favorites. Not that such a stellar concoction needs any additional selling points, but The Wise Man Corojo has earned multiple high ratings in Cigar Aficionado, including a very respectable 91 in early 2025 . The cedar chest housing the cigars is exquisite, adorned in striking blue and gold. Matching blue and gold bands accented with a green cross distinguish the Corojo variant of the brand, while the construction leaves absolutely nothing to be desired. The easy draw produces thick, billowing clouds of white smoke that initially hit the palate with a blast of bold, spicy Pepin pepper . The intensity lingers for a while before giving way to a refined medley of coffee, tea leaves, and baker’s spices — flavors often found in ultra-premium Nicaraguan Corojo cigars. A subtle touch of cocoa on the finish rounds out the experience, and when the smoke clears, The Wise Man Corojo lands just a notch below full-bodied. Made for the most experienced connoisseurs, The Wise Man Corojo is alluring in every aspect, from its complex, classic Nicaraguan flavor profile to its stout body and rich, powerful undertones. It pairs beautifully with bourbon, dark rum, or full-bodied beer, but can accompany a hot cup of black coffee just as well. Similar in stature to Don Pepin Blue or the celebrated Flor de Las Antillas , this spicy Corojo creation is sure to satisfy even the pickiest cigar freak. Do you consider yourself to be wise? If so, your best bet at this point is to try a Wise Man Corojo and experience what the new, improved Foundation Cigar Company has to offer.

When Nicholas Melillo left his long-time position with Drew Estate and started Foundation Cigars , his first release made massive waves throughout the industry. That release was El Gueguense , an ultra-premium cigar named after a Nicaraguan folk dance which translates literally to “The Wise Man.” Soon after, those waves became tsunamis with the introduction of The Wise Man Maduro, the dark, sultry follow-up to the original. In addition, blending and production has now shifted to the watchful eyes of Jaime and Don Pepin Garcia, two of the biggest names in the business. Now rolled by the skilled hands at the world famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, The Wise Man Maduro begins with an all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend, including leaves from all 3 major growing regions: Jalapa, Condega, and Esteli. This package is then topped off with a gorgeous Mexican San Andres Maduro wrapper leaf, something long-awaited from someone with a nickname like “Chief of the Broadleaf.” Was the final product as good as everyone was expecting? Well, a stellar 95 rating in Cigar Aficionado and a top spot on the famed magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of 2018 list pretty much says it all! Newly done bands of maroon and gold adorn each hand-crafted masterpiece, each cigar oozing with natural oils and glistening in the light. As one would expect from a cigar rolled under the supervision of the Garcias, construction is phenomenal, and the draw is easy and productive every time. White pepper mixed with dark chocolate opens things up, and there is a hint of cayenne on the tip of the tongue. A dark, earthy core of rich, spicy tobacco is at the center of the show, and notes of caramel, toast, and cinnamon dance around the outside of the flavor profile. The finish is clean and sweet, and overall, The Wise Man Maduro finishes at medium-full-bodied, with no shortage of delicious complexity. Made for more experienced connoisseurs, The Wise Man Maduro is a more-than-worthy follow-up to its natural predecessor. Complex, velvety smooth, and medium-full-bodied, it is everything a discriminating cigar enthusiast could ask for. It pairs beautifully with coffee, port wine, or dark rum and is certainly suitable for use as a celebratory cigar. Fans of the original El Gueguense should be quite pleased at the flavorful differences this cigar brings to the table. Would it be foolish to pass up a cigar this good? Well, we will let the name of the stick answer that question. Make a wise decision: Try The Wise Man Maduro today and experience one of Nicaragua’s most luxurious offerings.

Fratello Oro is the first cigar in the Fratello portfolio to be produced outside the Joya De Nicaragua factory. This time, Fratello founder Omar de Frias went across the map to the Dominican Republic, assigning the task to La Aurora, the country's oldest cigar factory. Not only is Oro the first Dominican-made Fratello, but it is also the first to use a Connecticut shade wrapper, in this case a golden Ecuadorian variety. This, combined with a Cameroon binder and a filler blend from Nicaragua, Colombia, and the Dominican Republic, makes for an amazing mild-medium-bodied smoking experience that even seasoned connoisseurs can appreciate. For a premium Connecticut-wrapped stick, Fratello Oro is rather rustic in appearance. Despite the glistening gold bands, the classic Cuban style roll and textured wrapper leaf add a unique amount of old school character. Speaking of that roll, it is just right, lending to a great draw and a solid ash to boot. As for flavor characteristics, Oro is all that one would expect from a designer Connecticut cigar: creamy, earthy, and nutty. A bit of cedar adds something extra to the blend, as well as hints of spicy white pepper and a tangy citrus note in the background. A bread note is noticeable on the retrohale, as well as just a bit of sweetness on the tip of the tongue. Beginning as a very mild cigar, this stick in particular builds just enough intensity throughout the smoke to bring it into medium-bodied territory by the closing puffs. Like most mild-medium-bodied cigars, Fratello Oro is most definitely suitable for beginners, though its subtle complexities, velvety smoothness, and all the other bells and whistles included in this price point will likely go to waste on an inexperienced palate. Of course, the usual white wine, light beer, and even Champagne all go well with Oro, but oddly enough the notes in the flavor profile actually pair beautifully with orange juice, making it a great breakfast cigar. If you have come to enjoy such Ecuadorian Connecticut beauties as Montecristo Classic or Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real , perhaps it would be worth your while to check out Fratello Oro and compare it. "Oro" is Spanish for "gold," and this golden beauty is most definitely a fantastic choice for any lover of fine mild-medium cigars.
