The end result of a collaboration of giants, the Gispert Intenso cigar takes taste, strength, and pure smoking enjoyment to the next level. It's an old brand name to be sure, one not everyone will know, but rest assured that a Gispert frontmark has always represented succulent, satisfying flavor. Now, bringing his particular brand of magic to the table, the incomparable AJ Fernandez worked side by side with the masters of tobacco at Grupo de Maestros to create a new and potent blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan longleaf tobaccos, far greater than the sum of its parts. The addition of a perfectly aged and fermented Ecuadorian Connecticut Broadleaf as the wrapper seals the deal to make the Gispert Intenso a powerful delight. Carrying a light box-press, each solidly crafted Gispert Intenso vitola is a toothy and dark brown love note written by skilled hands to your eyes, nose, and palate. Heavy and solid, the oily barrel of the cigar wafts a mouth-watering aroma of cedar and chocolate even before being lit, but it is after a flame is applied that this cigar really demands your attention. Fernandez has taken the seemingly commonplace individual longleaf tobaccos within and married them in such a way as to create a complex and rich flavor profile loaded with oak, bittersweet cocoa, black pepper, leather, and cream. Take this full-bodied treat for a spin and give your taste buds the kick they are craving. A Gispert Intenso is not so overpowering that less experienced smokers need to shy away, so don't be afraid to load up your cart. At the same time, this cigar offers true aficionados much to explore through wise beverage pairings and contemplative puffing. The best part is, they're priced so affordable to where anybody who wants to enjoy them can. Want in on the action? Get yours now.

God of Fire 2014 Serie Aniversario cigars are finally here and they are true world-class smokes that should be on every aficionado's bucket list. Originally announced as a 2012 release to celebrate Prometheus International's 20th year, some unfortunate delays have morphed them into signifying their God of Fire brand's 10 year anniversary. Not that it matters why they're here or what year is on the label because holy moly are these some delicious sticks. Crafted by the incomparable Fuente family, each Dominican-filled treasure is coated with a savory Ecuadorian wrapper of such exquisite quality you might think you've died and gone to heaven. (Shop other God of Fire Cigars ) There's just something immediately sophisticated about a figurado cigar, that classic and difficult to roll shape given to all three God of Fire 2014 vitolas. Redolently earthy in aroma and with cocoa and mesquite cold-draw flavors, it's almost possible to overlook the impressive design and construction that went into each stick, but there is nothing wrong with spending time in quiet appreciation before lighting that flame. Anticipation builds as the narrow foot gives hints of sweet vanilla and white pepper, but once the main body of the cigar starts to slowly smolder these are joined in full force by creamy leather, espresso, and oak backed by an amazing floral aroma. The second half adds toasted peanuts, a meaty char and a whisper of mint through the nose before reaching a spicy finish that is a religious experience all in itself. Despite the complexity of flavor to be found, expect an eventful medium bodied experience perfect for acolytes and masters alike. The God of Fire 2014 Serie Aniversario is a special occasion cigar that you will find no excuse not to smoke, so take advantage of our amazing prices and join this cult of personality today.

Gran Habano 3 SLS Robusto cigars are cigars that have a fascinating and decorated history behind them. Made down in Honduras by the George Rico and his famed Gran Habano Cigar Company, 3 SLS is a hearty blend of Costa Rican and long Nicaraguan fillers wrapped with a Nicaraguan binder and finished with a dark, oily Habano wrapper leaf. Formerly known as "3 Siglos," 3 SLS won many honors, the best of which was in 2007 when it was named one Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 cigars with a stellar rating of 92. Once highly regarded as a super premium, 3 SLS is now discontinued by the Gran Habano Company and is available at absolutely killer prices. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) Gran Habano 3 SLS is constructed to the famous Gran Habano standards, with a firm draw that produces clouds of thick white smoke. From the very first puff, 3 SLS is rich, powerful, and full-bodied, opening with a blast of cedar and continuing with cinnamon, cocoa, and earthy goodness. A woody sweetness on the finish makes 3 SLS a well-rounded experience, finishing off a flavor bouquet that is both complex and bold at the same time. Gran Habano 3 SLS was designed initially as a cigar for connoisseurs, sitting at the top of the Gran Habano portfolio. However, at today's prices, it is readily available and affordable to just about everyone. Seasoned smokers will appreciate the rich complexity, while those who do not quite have a finely-tuned palate will get a rush from the full-bodied power the stick offers. 3SLS pairs well with dark beer and coffee, and it is a good chance that if you are a fan of Oliva Serie V or Casa Magna , you will probably fall in love with it at the first puff. Get it while it is still available, as Gran Habano 3 Robusto will doubtless go down in history as one of the great cigars made by George Rico and company.

An early example from the 2010's Double Maduro frenzy, the Gran Habano Azteca Gran Robusto stands the test of time. Following on the success of their Gran Habano #1, #3, and #5 blends, the father and son team of Guillermo and George Rico crafted their first Maduro smoke with an eye on the future even as they held firm to the Rico family's connection with tobacco that stretches back four generations. Starting with a succulent blend of Nicaraguan, Habano, and Panamanian longleaf filler, they fed the growing appetite for stogies rolled with paired Maduros with the fateful decision to use juicy, well-fermented Mexican San Andres leaves, a regional variety destined to become near-dominant in today's dark cigar world, as both wrapper and binder. The oils that glint off of the sleek umber brown Maduro wrapper should please Tonatiuh the Sun God as he gazes from the stick's golden band upon the fortunate enthusiast holding a Gran Habano Azteca Gran Robusto. A pungent aroma foretells the pre-light flavor of loamy earth, which in turn prepares the palate for thick clouds of smoke full of espresso and rye toast. A creamy caramel sweetness can be detected from the midpoint all the way to the finish alongside more robust flavors of oak, chocolate covered almonds, and leather.

George Rico has some interesting ideas when it comes to boutique cigars, but we'll let him do what he does as long as he keeps releasing gems such as the Gran Habano S.T.K. Black Dahlia. Much of the time, so-called 'boutique' stogies come from small, often obscure companies and while they can sometimes be fantastic sticks, they don't always live up to the hype. Then there's the other common usage for the term, of which Rico's various 'Gran Habano S.T.K.' frontmarks are a part: Cigars from known makers that for valid reasons are limited or short run batches. The S.T.K. Black Dahlia is a regular, albeit small, production run containing Nicaraguan Cubita and Habano, Colombian, and Costa Rican longleaf filler beneath dual Habano binders and a creamy shade-grown Corojo wrapper, all from Nicaragua. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) The multi-pedaled and ebony-hued namesake flower that adorns the otherwise white and gold band just below an embossed S.T.K. (Stay True Kid) label is the only thing actually black about a Gran Habano S.T.K. Black Dahlia, the solid barrel of which is simply a rich light-brown color. After inhaling the crisp and sweet tobacco aroma that wafts from the vitola, the wise enthusiast will quickly move to the lighting stage to release the first bursts of black pepper, cracked wheat, and sweet cream delivered by a near-overwhelming amount of thick smoke. Easily medium-full from the beginning, this savory cigar stays cool burning as the flavors of espresso, cedar, almond paste, gingerbread, raisins, and orange peel all take turns wowing the tastebuds. One of the best things about the widening of the boutique description is when it merges new tastes with quality and affordability, all traits the Gran Habano S.T.K. Black Dahlia carries in spades. Dig yourself out of that cigar rut you've somehow found yourself in and try one or more of these quality stogies before we run out. Not that we will, but it can happen.

Gran Habano #1 Connecticut cigars are the smoothest, mildest, most easy-to-smoke blend from the otherwise high-powered Gran Habano brand. Handmade in Danli, Honduras, these beauties include a concoction of medium-bodied Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a golden brown Ecuador Connecticut wrapper leaf. Like all Gran Habano blends, the #1 Connecticut is the product of brand owners Guillermo and George Rico. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) This top-rated blend, which earned an impressive 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado , showcases the expert craftsmanship and consistency that have made Gran Habano a respected name among cigar enthusiasts worldwide. These cigars are well-made with an easy draw. The smoke is thick and gray, coating the palate with creamy, earthy flavors including hints of nuts and vanilla. The finish is short and clean, leaving behind a tiny hint of grass. They are pleasant, smooth, and well-balanced. Medium-bodied. The #1 Connecticut cigars are a terrific, wallet-friendly choice for beginners and intermediate smokers. They are wonderful for any time of day and pair well with white wine. They are comparable to Oliva Connecticut Reserve and Camacho Connecticut, two other fine Connecticut-wrapped medium-strength sticks. Take it easy, relax, and grab a Gran Habano #1 Connecticut cigar today!

Gran Habano Corojo Maduro #5 is a cigar with a long name, a long history, and most likely a long future ahead of it. Made down in Honduras under the supervision of George Rico, Corojo Maduro #5 is the maduro-clad sister cigar of the celebrated classic Corojo #5 that seems to have been around forever. The Gran Habano name is synonymous with value, quality, and versatility, and appeals to cigar smokers of every stature. For most, the maduro version of Corojo #5 is a welcomed addition to the lineup. It consists of a filler and binder blend of Nicaraguan and Costa Rican tobaccos married with a dark, toothy Nicaraguan Corojo Maduro leaf. The result is a unique cigar that's sure to leave a big impression. Modern, Cuban-style packaging and bands give Corojo Maduro #5 a high-end feel, ideally complementing the superb construction and gorgeous Nicaraguan Corojo Maduro wrapper leaves. A firm draw delivers ample amounts of heavy white smoke, coating the palate with a spicy array of nutty, earthy flavors. Coffee, black pepper, and chocolate are the main notes , along with a hint of cherry and floral flavor on the retrohale. A spicy, clean finish ties the bold, rich package together very nicely. Gran Habano Corojo Maduro #5 is very full-bodied. There's no way around it. The original Corojo #5 was full-bodied, to begin with, but this one takes it a step further. Experienced cigar connoisseurs should be the main crowd for this one. It pairs beautifully with tawny port and dark rum and can even be enjoyed with coffee. Corojo Maduro #5 can be compared to Camacho Triple Maduro and Partagas Black, other full-bodied maduro cigars that, like this one, just seem to be put together beautifully. If you love maduros, if you love full-bodied cigars, if you love value, and if you love quality, look no further than Gran Habano Corojo Maduro #5. We promise you won't regret it. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars )

When Guillermo Rico and George A. Rico had a falling out, George created a new brand G.A.R. Cigars. While the father and son are back together again, G.A.R. continues to be made to this day. The G.A.R. White is the original blend, packaged in unique white boxes of twenty cigars featuring simplistic white foot bands. G.A.R. White is offered in four box-pressed sizes from the Rico's Honduran factory: Gran Consul (4 3/4" x 60); Corona Gorda (6" x 46), Rico Grande (6" x 54) and Robusto Grande (5 1/2" x 52) with an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan fillers. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) For fans of Corojo, you'll notice cedar, pepper and leather. However, it's joined by sweetness, a more generic woodsiness, and a bit of earth. While George Rico claims this is a full cigar, it's more medium-full in body, medium in strength, and medium-full in flavor. Don't shy away from the dark wrapper; this is a great cigar to pair with coffee or enjoy through out any part of the day. For those that have enjoyed Gran Habanos over the years, G.A.R. might be a step up in strength, but the quality remains the same.

After slowly working their way into our hearts and minds by releasing wave after wave of affordable yet beloved smokes, the cigar fanatics at Gran Habano are coming to take over our humidors with the 93-rated Gran Habano La Conquista. Flush with expertly fermented and finely aged longleaf perfect for creating a medium-to-full bodied experience, these sturdy sticks will delight the palate in myriad ways. Complexity is assured through the inspired inclusion of Colombian, Costa Rican, and Nicaraguan tobaccos as the action-packed filler nearly bursting from beneath the leathery and slick Nicaraguan Corojo binder and wrapper. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) Thickly bunched yet able to provide smooth airflow during all draws both before and after lighting, the core of each crafted vitola tempts the nose with spice and dry cocoa while the golden and oily outer Corojo sets the lips to tingle ever so slightly. If you discover the initial flavor of a lit Gran Habano La Conquista is overwhelmingly of charred wood then you didn't remove the cedar sleeve which protects the lower bout of each stick, a mistake you only make once. The actual profile, while certainly containing warm bursts of cedar, is heavily laden with black pepper, French roast coffee, molasses, peat, whipping cream, and cinnamon. Like all of George Rico's cigars, the premium Gran Habano La Conquista is a remarkable bargain for any enthusiast looking to take their smoking game to the next level. With a generous 24 sticks loaded into each box, just think of them as long-term investments in your daily enjoyment. Don't worry, we'll be here waiting when you need to re-up sooner than expected.

With all due pomp and circumstance as befits such royally delicious cigars, let us introduce you to the Persian King Natural and Maduro . Brought to you by Gran Habano’s Guillermo and George Rico , you can be assured the famous father and son duo have spared no effort in crafting a stogie that is set to rule the mid-priced cigar empire. To accomplish this coronation, the Rico’s have recruited a variety of the lushest aged Nicaraguan tobaccos to come together in blended harmony. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) Persian King Natural: As though a paper band carrying its frontmark were beneath it, the Persian King Natural instead identifies itself with a bright and golden strip of pigtailed Connecticut Shade tobacco that decorates the foot in stark color contrast to the rich brown Habano which coats the rest of each stout vitola. The scents and flavors of a cold draw are reminiscent of cedar, cocoa, and hay, but a flame releases the cigar’s true majesty. A sweet grassiness awakens the palate, a delightful taste soon to be expanded with loamy earth, oak, black pepper, cream, cinnamon, and plum. Persian King Maduro: The gleaming and uniformly dark Maduro wrapper that graces each solid vitola needs no band to signal its sovereign nature, but what good is a fancy cloak if it doesn’t have some decoration? Instead of a trimmed foot or even the shaggy tobacco you’ll occasionally see, the foot of each Persian King Maduro is closed with an inch-wide strip of light brown tobacco which is pigtailed into a fancy coil. Very stylish. Clipping both ends reveals a well-packed core while a flame brings forth a wealth of rich flavor. Earth and oak and cocoa in spades, but behind these bold elements quietly sit walnut, toasted oats, cinnamon, malt, and cherry stem ready to engage the wise palate. Full-flavored and full-bodied from start to finish, you may want to kneel while enjoying this regal stick if you’re not already kicked back in your favorite chair. Come visit the court of the Persian King, and reap the benefits of Gran Habano’s commitment to flavor and quality that won’t cost you a king’s ransom. Go for the glory by buying a full box of fifty, but if your castle can’t quite hold that many we do carry them in five packs and singles. Either way, you’ll feel like a monarch each time you light one up.

Persian Queen is the long-awaited offshoot of Persian King, the rustic value-priced cigar from the father and son team of George and Guillermo Rico of Gran Habano. Hailing from Honduras and limited in production to just 500 boxes of 50 cigars, Persian Queen is rather special in that it is a true limited edition. Not only that, but it is also draped in two different wrapper leaves in barber pole fashion, making it as beautiful in appearance as it is delicious. For the blend, the binder and filler tobacco are from Nicaragua and the two wrappers are Ecuadorian Connecticut and Nicaraguan Corojo. The result of this blend is a medium-bodied masterpiece suitable for cigar freaks of all calibers. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) The box is plain and simple, and the cigars wear no bands. Each stick is lovingly constructed and rolled with precision. The result being a seamless barber pole cigar with an unfinished foot. The draw is highly productive, offering plentiful opportunities to take in all the wonderful flavor and aroma produced by this exciting blend. Immediately upon lighting up, a quick burst of cedar and white pepper, started things off. Soon, notes of bread and cereal oddly form the core of the flavor profile, surrounded by an earthy aroma and crisp raw tobacco flavor, likely coming from the Connecticut side of the wrapper. The puffs are creamy and smooth, and the finish is short and clean. Persian Queen ends up residing as a true medium-bodied cigar. Tasty, enjoyable, versatile, and suitable for all audiences. Persian Queen is a cigar for everyone. The price to quality ratio is amazing, especially for a limited production stick. Its flavor profile is simple, yet interesting, and its medium body pairs well with white wine, light beers, or any decent whiskey. If you tried the Persian King back in the day, or simply are a fan of George Rico's other projects such as La Conquista or Gran Habano Vintage 2002 , you should give Persian Queen a try. We live in a time when prices are going up on everything, including cigars. How refreshing it is to know that there are cigars like Persian Queen out there that combine quality and value and can be enjoyed by just about anyone! Long live the queen!

When George Rico introduced the Gran Habano Corojo #5, the cigar world rejoiced in its full-flavored and bodied taste. It is hard to believe this stick could get any better, but the Gran Habano Vintage 2002 does just that. Not only is the blend improved with the introduction of an aged Corojo wrapper from 2002 but the price is much easier to look at as well. This medium-to-full-bodied cigar is perfect for anyone to try, whether you love heavier sticks, or you are looking to step up your flavor profile. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) These super-oily dark and rich Nicaraguan Corojo 2002 wrapped beauties are packed to the gills with Cuban seed long filler tobacco from the finest fields in Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. These sticks are chock full of hearty nutty flavors balanced with notes of cream, coffee and dirt making this a medium-to-full-bodied blend that nearly everybody will enjoy. The construction is flawless as one would expect from a George Rico cigar, and despite the price, the flavors match up with some of the much higher cost cigars on the market, even ones from Gran Habano themselves At such a low price per stick, people will be hard to find a cigar that is this flavorful, this well made, and this cost effective. You can even fool your friends at your next herf by making them think you are passing out much higher priced sticks. Given the heavy nature of the smoke it is best enjoyed after a good meal with a nice glass of red wine or a stout which can hold up to the flavors.

Gurkha owner Kaizad Hansotia dates the name being associated with cigars back 125 years, and for this incredible anniversary a special cigar was needed to celebrate. When Gurkha sets out to make a special stick, the eyes of the cigar world take notice. The 125th Anniversary Gurkha cigar is certainly something to celebrate. Named the 9th best cigar of 2013 by Cigar Aficionado, this standout cigar is made in the PDR factory in the Dominican Republic. A truly international blend of Nicaraguan, Brazilian, and Dominican filler tobaccos and bound with a Ecuadorian leaf and wrapped in a beautiful Brazilian wrapper. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) With a beautiful large Gurkha band embellished with gold and the 125th anniversary moniker on the side, you are sure to know you are in for a special smoke. While the Brazilian wrapper has a somewhat dry appearance, the construction was impeccable and there was no veining to speak of. Before lighting there is an almost citrus aroma of orange and this carried over to the flavor afterward. On top of this tantalizing note, there was also great tastes of leather and spice. 125 years in the cigar industry is something to be very Proud of, and Gurkha has made a perfect cigar to celebrate. Gurkha's 125 Anniversary cigar is an amazing medium-to-full smoke with very complex flavors and fantastic construction. These citrus notes pair wonderfully with a nice gin and tonic on the deck as you forget about the day and wonder what the next will bring.

If you've been casting about for a unique and flavorful cigar to break you out of a smoking rut, then the Gurkha Barracuda is going to be a prize catch. as with the regular cellar reserve, this cigar is full of flavor and complexity with an added layer of sweetness and body on the finish.

Mild enough to enjoy with a morning cup of coffee, this cigar is also flavorful enough to stand out after a nice dinner. If you are looking for something that will never overpower but will still make your taste buds sing, this is the cigar for you.

Gurkha Legend is a cigar that certainly lives up to its name, as it's probably the most famous of all that Gurkha has offered over the years, and that is no small statement. It is just a cigar for the ages, and that simply can't be refuted. Legend consists of a smooth blend of Dominican fillers inside a genuine Cameroon binder. Simple, refined, and downright enjoyable, Gurkha Legend is a cigar that will go down in history as exactly that: a true legend.

The Master Select line of Gurkha Cigars features wrappers made from extra-select six year-old vintage Habana 2000 tobacco. These are powerful and very complex cigars. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Gurkha Cigar history: In 1989, Kaizad Hansotia decided to resurrect a cigar brand rich in tradition and steeped in legend and history. Gurkha cigars were created more than a century ago and were known for their meticulously and artisanaly handcrafted cigars, but when Hansotia revived the brand, there was no way he could have known that the cigar industry was about to experience a boom and he would have the perfect product to attract the new cigar consumer. In realizing that there were no super premium cigars, he created the association with elegance for which the cigars have become known. In reviving Gurkha, Hansotia created cigars that were not a necessity but rather a luxury and an indulgence. Today, Gurkha makes a cigar for all price points and all palates, but when it began, Gurkha cigars were unlike other cigars in the market. They also came in highly ornate packaging and with a steep price tag. Hansotia felt that there was a market for more luxurious and exclusive cigars for those with tastes for only the finer and more elusive products. In focusing on this segment, Hansotia created the ultra premium cigar category.

For years, when you thought of Gurkha , you didn't think of affordable cigars. Kaizad Hansotia spent years developing Gurkha into a company known for its extravagant creations like Black Dragon and His Majesty's Reserve. So when Gurkha's team told Kaizad that they had developed an affordable cigar, he was a bit taken back. It was the Gurkha Ninja XO cigar, and after a few months on the market Kaizad was convinced. Offered in five sizes: Churchill (7" x 52), Knife (5" x 55), Perfecto No.2 (6" x 60), Torpedo (6" x 52) and XO (6" x 60) and made in the Dominican Republic, the Gurkha Ninja was one of the top selling cigars. Offered in boxes of 20, the Gurkha Ninja features a Brazilian Maduro wrapper, a Cameroon binder and Nicaraguan fillers. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Cigar Aficionado has given Gurkha Ninja multiple 90+ ratings , reaching as high as a 91 rating. This is what you would expect from the Dark Brazilian wrapped cigar, it's got some sweetness, leather, earth and roasted nuts with pepper. It's full in body, full in flavor and medium-full in flavor, but where the Gurkha Ninja sets itself apart from the rest of Beach Cigar Group's line-up is the price and the delivery. Ninja is a solid cigar without the high price tag and bit of gimmicks that go along with most of Gurkha's branding. The 91 point rated Gurkha Ninja is presented simply and offers affordability.

Gurkha Pan American cigars are somewhat Kaizad Hansotia's way of paying tribute to early America when railway travel was common and times were simpler. Produced down in Nicaragua using Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a gleaming Ecuador Connecticut wrapper leaf, Pan American is a mild-medium connoisseur-level cigar made to impress discriminating fans of milder cigars that stay flavorful and complex while smoking easy and cool. Pan American is quite classic, in fact, in that it does not put much emphasis on raw strength, but rather the intricate blending skills of Mr. Hansotia and the folks at Gurkha are clearly displayed in a well-balanced, easy-smoking package. Connoisseurs will appreciate this luxury stick as well, as it is deliciously creamy and easy to pair with white wine or champagne. The good people at Gurkha Cigars continue to offer new top-notch sticks at affordable prices every year, and Pan American is one more hit to add to the list. Pick up a couple today and take a vintage train ride to cigar dream land! All aboard!

Over the years, the legendary Gurkha name has become known for producing some of the finest and most expensive cigars in the world. Rolled by his most skilled torcedors down in the Dominican Republic, Royal Reserve consists of a simple blend of 3-year-aged Dominican fillers and binders and a dark, rich 5-year-aged Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. The catch? Each cigar is triple-infused with Louis XIII cognac, which many connoisseurs claim to be the finest cognac on the planet. This isn't your typical infused cigar, however, as this is an ultra-premium exotic concoction that only the most sophisticated cigar junkies will ever have a chance to enjoy. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Highly-limited and difficult to come by, Gurkha Royal Reserve Maduro comes packaged in gorgeous 22-count chests. The box alone can easily become a centerpiece in any man cave or smoking lounge, and to add to the rare feel, each chest comes with its own certificate of authenticity. A beautiful glass tube encompasses each and every cigar, finished with a classic wax seal. If the presentation doesn't floor you, maybe the flavor will. Upon lighting, Gurkha Royal Reserve Maduro offers billowing ribbons of blue smoke, greeting the palate with a mix of dark chocolate and earth. Immediately, the velvety cognac flavor makes its presence felt, carrying all the way through the experience. This brings about a lingering sweetness and hearty feel on the palate, beautifully combining with the classic maduro profile offered by the Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. The finish is long, chewy, and sweet, and the body is medium-full. This blend offers quite the opulent smoking experience. It would be not only wasteful, but foolish to consider a cigar of this caliber if you are a beginner or intermediate cigar smoker. Only the most experienced connoisseurs with the most developed palates will truly be able to enjoy everything this stick has to offer. It smokes long, so make sure there is plenty of time to sit back and savor the luxurious nuances and complexities before lighting up. And don't forget to pair it with a fine beverage. What would go better with a cognac-infused cigar than, well, cognac? Those who may enjoy this cigar the most are likely those who enjoy the likes of Arturo Fuente Opus X Lost City or Ashton ESG —both cigars sporting massive complexities and hints of cognac in the flavor profile. If you are a true connoisseur and think you are ready for a cigar fit for royalty, don't hesitate to pick up a Gurkha Royal Reserve Maduro Torpedo while they're still around!

Every cigar you smoke is trying to entice you. Each brand is trying to convince you that it is better or different than all the other cigars on the shelf that day. The Gurkha Seduction is aptly named because it does just that. Wrapped in a dark and mottled Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf that has been aged for three years, the filler is an extremely unique blend of Colombian corojo tobacco. This really is an amazing full-bodied smoking experience. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) A play off of the classic Gurkha band, this one is embellished with a golden S. Just like most Gurkha cigars the Seduction is beautifully packaged in gorgeous black and classy boxes. Each part of this smoke provides an incredible transformation which each third playing off the flavors in the last. At first you get a nice bittersweet dark chocolate taste which transforms into earthy tones and cinnamon, and the final third provides a peppery punch to tie the whole cigar together. Gurkha is a cigar that has a lot of fans, and the seduction is the perfect cigar to justify their adoration. This full bodied stick has so many different flavor notes that it is hard to imagine that all powerful cigars like this cannot be just as complex. With so many different flavors, this cigar pairs well with so many different things, and the subtle power makes this the perfect compliment to an afternoon espresso. We would also highly recommend the Gurkha Ghost.
The Gurkha Sniper offers a flavorful profile consisting of pepper, chocolate, and leather.

Same 7 1/2" length, same 52 ring gauge, same Dominican and Nicaraguan core, same Indonesian binder but it is different wrappers that bring about a bit of a change of pace from the Connecticut Broadleaf wrapped, Gurkha Spec Ops No. 1 to the all-new Dominican wrapped Gurkha Sniper cigars. The almost famous Gurkha Pelican case, 7 7/8" fixed blade knife with leg sheath and challenge coin even come back for a return with 20 quality Gurkha cigars all featuring that particular new Dominican wrapper. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Notes of earth, oak, raisin, spice, and tea are all present as you kick into this smoke with light nuances of pepper on the retrohale probably coming from the Nicaraguan filler leaves. The dark, drab brown wrapper is rough to the touch, and the draw is easy and smooth with lots of smoke coming up from the foot. As one continues to burn through, coffee, cocoa powder, tobacco and tea leaf notes continue with that sweet raisin balancing them out nicely. This stick never makes it much stronger than a medium, and that is great news for everyone looking for a great first cigar of the day, a great cigar to share with their buddies, or something for those times when you know you will be smoking a few sticks back to back. Besides with all the bonus items, these 20 smokes come with, what are you still thinking about, these are a steal!

The Gurkha Special Ops is one of the most unique forms of packaging of any cigar, even for Gurkha. Cueing inspiration from Navy SEALs, Kaizad Hansotia and the team at Beach Cigar Group released Special Ops in yellow and orange Pelican cases. But that wasn't all, inside, Kaizad has included a seven inch tactical knife and challenge coins, in addition to the twenty cigars. The Spec Ops is a 7 1/4" x 54 double corona made in the Dominican Republic featuring a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) For those that are attracted solely because of the packaging, you might be surprised by the cigar. Despite the dark wrapper, this is a medium cigar that has sweet earth, bitter cocoa, cedar and tons of creaminess. The Gurkha Special Ops is medium in strength and medium-full in both flavor and body. Despite the dual bands and special packaging, this is a Gurkha that is truly unique outside of the packaging. It's flavorful, smooth and consistent, regarded as one of the better cigars Gurkha has put out in the past few years. The best part is once you are done, you have a waterproof humidor that holds up to thirty cigars, a great knife and a limited edition travel humidor. Gurkha has trouble keeping these in stock, so get them while you can.

Just when you thought you could make a cigar like Gurkha Titan any more intimidating along comes the XO, a 6 inch by 54 ring gauge behemoth of a smoke. Gurkha chairman Kaizad Hansotia is nothing if not concerned with the happiness and wellbeing of his customers, and when the people want big cigars by the gods, are they going to get big cigars. The pricey Titan line was already a fan favorite when Hansotia decided to broaden its horizons and so he simply added an extra dose of 5-year-old and cedar-aged Columbian, Dominican, and Honduran tobacco beneath the cigar's Nicaraguan binder and jet-black Costa Rican Maduro wrapper until it was nearly bursting at the barely visible seams. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Unlike some Gurkha cigars, where it can be difficult to determine exactly which blend you're holding because of the similar bands, the Titan proudly and boldly declares its moniker on a silver-embossed second band above a small sleeve of cedar. Of course, the size and heft of the vitola itself, along with its dark chocolate color and aroma, makes identification a no-brainer. Also a matter of no debate is just how much flavor and smoke Titan is capable of producing. Toasty at the start with mocha, cedar, and stone fruit soon after, the cigar finishes clean and dead center of medium-full. With a boxed price in the clouds, you may have planned on hiding these in your deepest humidor and breaking them out only for those once in a lifetime events. Now that we have them in bundles for prices on the ground, you can look to enjoy them on the golf course, at the beach, or even while walking the dog. Just make sure it's a long walk because these Gurkha Titan XOs are huge.

It is amazing that a brand known for unique packaging and limited release cigars can keep innovating, but Gurkha has done it again with the Triad. With the quality and flavor you would expect from Gurkha, the Triad is an amazing stick which will make you sit down and take notice right from the first puff until you are ready to nub it. An astounding 10-year-aged Connecticut broadleaf wrapper surrounds the maduro and a sultry 10-year-aged Ecuadorian Connecticut is on the natural. Aged filler and binder tobaccos round out this amazing limited release smoke. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) An ornate black, gold, and red band greets you and the cigar is hugged by a beautiful cedar sheath with a black footband. Once clipped, a wonderful taste of earthiness comes through with an extremely easy draw. These amazing notes follow through with the first few puffs and are complimented with a slight black pepper finish. The more you smoke the more the cedar comes out and what started as earth ends with a sweetness that needs to be tasted to be believed. As you would expect from Gurkha, the burn is perfect, the draw is amazing, and the taste is unbelievable. Truly a limited release cigar, Gurkha triad is presented in wonderfully ornate chests and limited to only 300 boxes made. With a price that screams special occasion, the Triad will enhance any sort of special day. This is a medium-to-full body masterpiece that is never harsh and bursting with complex flavors which is perfect after a nice celebratory meal.

Gurkha Trinity cigars are the latest and greatest from K. Hansotia and company down in Nicaragua, the same folks that knock out some of the biggest, baddest limited release cigars on the market. Trinity is not only special but super cool! The Gurkha Trinity set consists of 3 cigars, all different configurations, in their own special wooden box. The best part is that these 3 ultra-premium sticks cost less than just 1 or 2 typical cigars of similar stature, making them very economical and attainable for just about anyone that wants something amazing from Gurkha. The inner blend remains the same for all 3 cigars: Nicaraguan and Dominican long fillers and a Nicaraguan binder. For the wrappers, one cigar is Nicaraguan Habano, the second is Nicaraguan Maduro, and the third is a barber pole made with the two. This set of cigars looks great, but they taste even better! (See all Gurkha Cigars ) All of the Gurkha Trinity cigars are expertly constructed and smoke like a dream, delivering medium-bodied flavor profiles that are just a wee bit different from cigar to cigar. The main makeup of the subtly complex flavor profile consists of earth, leather, and cedar, with plenty of raw tobacco and black cherry notes. A pronounced white pepper blast and a grassy core flavor are noticeable on the natural version. For the maduro, there are hints of coffee and sweet spices that linger in the back of the throat. As for the barber pole variety, you basically get the best of both worlds. Its main attributes are a very strong earthiness and cinnamon, nutmeg, and cocoa on the finish. Regardless of the cigar you smoke, each of the Trinity cigars is mellow, pleasant, and very easy to enjoy. Gurkha Trinity is a set of cigars aimed at more experienced smokers, but that's not to say a newbie wouldn't be able to enjoy them to the max. They all carry a distinct medium body and very simple flavor profiles that are easily identified. Regardless of the blend, Gurkha Trinity is a stick to pair with bourbon, scotch, or a medium-bodied wine to fully complement the flavor profiles. Similar cigars may include Gurkha Cellar Reserve and Gurkha Beauty , other fine sticks made by the famous Gurkha Company that seems to have been around forever. Whether purchasing for yourself or looking to make a cigar freak very happy with a killer gift, Gurkha Trinity is a perfect way to experience the masterful blending abilities offered by the fine folks at Gurkha Cigars.

Like a warrior crossing the mountainside to rampage the next village, Gurkha's Warlord will attack your senses. A limited release, as with a lot of Gurkha's offerings, the Warlord is a powerhouse. This is not a cigar for everyone and definitely not for the novice, this stick will be the perfect addition to the collection of the lover of fuller-bodied cigars. This Nicaraguan puro features some of the finest aged tobaccos in the industry. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) As with most Gurkha cigars, the Warlord is eloquently packaged in a beautiful chest reminiscent of a crate a warring nation would take their spoils home in. The treasure is not just the chest though but also the wonderful smokes inside. The toothy Nicaraguan wrapper is extremely aromatic of freshly cut grass and earthiness, while the pre light draw seems slightly loose. Despite this the cigar smokes very cool and slow, which is a good thing or the power behind the tobaccos could overwhelm. Taste of cedar and earth mixed with a slight spice but nothing overpowers the wonderful natural tobacco taste found within the leaves. Gurkha Warlord is a special cigar and one not to be taken lightly. Without a full meal, this cigar will definitely cause you to want to take a seat. After a nice dinner with a good strong espresso is where this cigar really shines. If you love a nice full-bodied smoke, The Gurkha Warlord would be a great stick to add to your rotation.

The phenomenal Gurkha Warpig goes to show that when you put as many troops onto the cigar world's field of battle as Gurkha does, you're bound to score a major victory every now and again. Flush with both strength and character, these thick vitolas can stand up to the most discerning aficionado's palate to leave them thrilled and satisfied. This triumph is accomplished thanks to the juicy Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler shielded by a thick, coffee-colored Nicaraguan Maduro wrapper. Even more amazing is the fact that this isn't one of K. Hansotia's famously high-dollar Gurkha frontmarks, but a medium-full strength stick that doesn't break the bank. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) It should come as no surprise that the Gurkha Warpig presents a formidable appearance when viewed among the other, wimpier stogies in your humidor. The large double bands which decorate each cigar are almost like a suit of armor, which when removed reveals a sleek and dark Maduro wrapper just as suited to protecting the vital longleaf tobaccos within. Once cleanly clipped and alight, a smoldering Warpig first develops the robust tastes of a high-quality mocha with a backbone of leather before slowly releasing additional flavors of cream, black pepper, mesquite, and a touch of cinnamon. A cigar with this much flavor for such a small amount of cash doesn't come along very often, and that goes double for Gurkha branded smokes. Take advantage of this opportunity before someone realizes each sleek black box of 12 Gurkha Warpigs could easily fetch twice the current price or more. You'll be glad to have these fierce warriors on your side when you need them.

Gurkha Xtreme cigars are exactly what the name implies: EXTREME! If you are a Gurkha fan and love rich, full-flavored Nicaraguan cigars, Gurkha Xtreme is definitely the cigar for you! Made in Nicaragua using a high-grade Nicaraguan wrapper leaf and a delicious proprietary blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos, Gurkha Xtreme is made especially for those who want just a little bit more out of their premium cigars. Released in 2015, Xtreme has garnered much attention from cigar fanatics, including a 90 rating and numerous accolades from top authorities on all things tobacco. Buckle up and get ready for a ride, as Gurkha Xtreme is just the ticket for hardcore cigar freaks from every corner of the planet. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) The packaging is radical, as with most Gurkha cigars. The box resembles the likeness of a popular video game console, the bands are futuristic and loud, and the cigars, well, they are about as gorgeous as they come. Oozing with oils and expertly rolled, Gurkha Xtreme burns razor sharp and offers a firm draw that allows jets of thick white smoke to bombard the palate with spicy Nicaraguan goodness. Beginning with a classic Nicaraguan white pepper, Xtreme evolves into a complex bouquet of both sweet and savory flavors. Earth and grass mingle with cocoa and mocha, the hints of pepper linger in the background, and a creamy vanilla note is introduced on the smooth finish, all while Gurkha Xtreme burns effortlessly and evenly down to a nub, staying velvety smooth the whole way. The folks at Gurkha really hit a goldmine with this one! Intermediate smokers and seasoned aficionados will come to appreciate the bold, complex flavors Gurkha Xtreme has to offer. Full-flavored, medium-full-bodied, and delicious to the max, Xtreme is nothing short of a show-stopper. It pairs well with bourbon or cognac and can be compared to other bold hits from Gurkha including Ghost , Titan , and of course the infamous Gurkha Beast . If you are a fan of Gurkha, or even if you have been away from the brand for some time, Gurkha Xtreme is definitely a welcomed addition to your humidor. Try one today and see what all the fuss is really about!

In 2019, the legendary H. Upmann brand recognized its 175th anniversary, and what better way to celebrate than with an H. Upmann 175th Anniversary cigar, blended and rolled by some of the most gifted cigar experts on the planet? The primary release of two separate celebratory cigars released in 2019, H. Upmann 175th Anniversary is a made for Altadis U.S.A. by the infamous AJ Fernandez, in collaboration with the world famous Grupo de Maestros. To say they went all-out is no doubt an understatement. Rolled in the state-of-the-art Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A., this gorgeous specimen is a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning every single component is grown in Nicaragua. The unique wrapper is a Nicaraguan medio tiempo leaf—one of the highest primings on the plant—fermented while sandwiched between broadleaf tobacco. It is offered in one size, a luxurious 7" x 50 Churchill, and a relatively modest 14,750 boxes were produced. That's right, it is a single-run limited edition, so when they're gone, they're gone! Thankfully, though, if you are reading this, you still have a chance to indulge in one of the most amazing cigars of recent years. So amazing, in fact, that it earned a rock-solid 93 rating in Cigar Aficionado and a high spot on the widely recognized Top 25 Cigars of the Year list for 2019. Everything about the cigar is beautiful, from the oily dark wrapper leaf to the glistening golden band, to the luxurious packaging and the unique foot band noting the incredible collaboration between AJ Fernandez and the Grupo de Maestros. A straight cut unveils an easy draw which produces baffling clouds of rich, blue smoke. The burn is razor sharp, the ash is dark and flaky, and the burn is slow and velvety smooth. Beginning creamy and rich, with a few blasts of cedar and cinnamon, the elegant flavor profile of H. Upmann 175th Anniversary begins to emerge into a story of spicy white pepper, rich cocoa, and bold, powerful raw tobacco. At first light, this is a medium-full-bodied smoke, but by the end, it is an absolute full-bodied powerhouse of a cigar. Words cannot describe the incredible richness and balance displayed by this unmatched beast of a cigar. Beginners should look elsewhere. This is a cigar for true connoisseurs. It is a celebration stick, something to wow the cigar freak that is in constant search of the "best smoke ever." Bold, easy to smoke, and topped off with mind-numbing complexity, H. Upmann 175th Anniversary is that cigar you save to enjoy alongside XO Cognac or aged tawny port. It's the cigar you would reach for if you crave the likes of Padron 1926 or Ashton VSG . It is all things classic, yet so refined and special that it can't help but be set apart from the rest. Whether celebrating the nearly 2 centuries the H. Upmann name has adorned top-shelf cigars, or celebrating one of your own lifetime achievements, celebrate with an H. Upmann 175th Anniversary and rest assured you are smoking one of the finest cigars money can buy.

The H. Upmann 1844 Añejo will join a newly repackaged 1844 line as the latest addition to the iconic H.Upmann portfolio.  H. Upmann Añejo – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The H. Upmann 1844 Añejo will join a newly repackaged 1844 line as the latest addition to the iconic H.Upmann portfolio. The 1844 Añejo is a complex, medium to full bodied cigar that uses a rich, well-balanced filler that is perfectly blended with tobaccos originating from Nicaragua, Honduras and the Dominican Republic.

A new cigar that is a combination of an old, well-regarded brand and old, finely aged tobacco the H. Upmann 1844 Añejo is a creamy smooth and medium-bodied treasure sure to delight both adventurous and mild-mannered smokers alike. As the name embossed in the brown and gold label suggests, H. Upmann stogies have been around in one form or another since 1844, but this succulent treat is the first of the brand to be classified 'Añejo', which those rum or tequila aficionados among us will recognize as signifying 'Vintage' (Hint: great beverage pairing choices!). What it means is each leaf of the Dominican, Honduran, and Nicaraguan filler and every oily inch of the Pennsylvania Broadleaf binder and Ecuadorian Habano wrapper have all been aged at least five long, leisurely years. There's something special about the smell of expertly fermented tobacco that's been allowed to rest for extended lengths of time. Instead of a bright, pungent scent that shocks the senses, mature cigars like the H. Upmann 1844 Añejo caress the nostrils with a rich, warm, and earthy aroma reminiscent of baking spices and brown ale . The smoke that pours through the steady draw is equally as fragrant, all while the tastes of oak, tanned leather, black tea, gingerbread, buttercream, and dried stone fruit flow across the palate in waves of ever-shifting complexity. For those excited enthusiasts who are just beginning to discover long-aged cigars, you'll learn like the rest of us that there is often a remaining core of strength behind the genteel first impression, so expect the H. Upmann 1844 Añejo to peak medium-full if you're aiming for the nub. Once you've gotten the itch, however, it's time to meet some of the other rocking old-timers like the Rocky Patel Vintage series and AJ Fernandez' Dias De Gloria.

A next level shade that presents a medium-bodied strength cigar featuring an impeccable, Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper with perfectly balanced flavors of H. Upmann 1844 Classic – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 A next level shade that presents a medium-bodied strength cigar featuring an impeccable, Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper with perfectly balanced flavors of toasted almonds, cocoa flavors with a subtle spicy nuance. The H. Upmann 1844 Classic joins the already versatile H. Upmann 1844 Heritage line of premium cigars to offer cigar enthusiasts an elevated complexity rarely found in shade wrapper cigars. This next- level shade appeals to experienced premium cigar smokers who enjoy a smooth cigar without being too overpowering as well as, novice consumers looking for a rewarding cigar with an effortless draw. The 1844 Classic is medium-bodied strength cigar that features an impeccable, Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper with perfectly balanced flavors of toasted almonds, cocoa flavors with a subtle spicy nuance. The H. Upmann 1844 Classic : A Shade Above Others

Embodying H. Upmann’s long tradition of fine cigar making, the H. Upmann 1844 Reserve might possibly be the finest H. Upmann yet. H. Upmann 1844 Reserve – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 From its intricate and complex flavor sensation to the even burn and classic ash that been the hallmark of H. Upmann’s incredibly fine cigar making, the 1844 Reserve captures everything aficionados have loved about H. Upmann cigars – and then some. This superb, medium-bodied smoke, expertly crafted in the Dominican Republic, features a robust Ecuadorian Cubano wrapper, Nicaraguan binder and Dominican filler tobaccos.

Hailing from the Dominican Republic and newly revamped and re-blended, H. Upmann 1844 Reserve is the signature cigar from H. Upmann, and now they're better than ever. H. Upmann is a brand with strong Cuban roots and is iconic among long-time cigar smokers. This is their core line and consists of a Dominican filler blend, a binder from Nicaragua, and a jaw-dropping Habano wrapper from Ecuador. This is the classic cigar flavor profile that every cigar, fanatic, young or old, should be required to try at least once. 1844 Reserve opens with a solid central flavor of earthy raw tobacco. There is white pepper both on the inhale and the finish and a vast array of creamy, nutty flavors in-between. A constant aroma of cedar lingers in the background throughout the smoke, making this classic a true replica of the Cubans of old. H. Upmann 1844 Reserve is medium-bodied and a great beginner cigar. Many long-time connoisseurs still keep a steady supply of 1844s in their humidors for those special occasions that call for classic cigar taste. 1844 Reserve pairs well with coffee and scotch and is in the same category of Cuban-rooted cigars as Punch , Romeo y Julieta , and Partagas. H. Upmann 1844 Reserve is among the legends of the cigar industry.

At first glance they may not seem like a cigar to get excited about, but as you think about an H. Upmann Connecticut your mouth will water, your heart will race, and you may have trouble sleeping tonight if you don't snag some right now. How could this be? First, the H. Upmann brand has been synonymous with tasty tobacco since, well, since 1844 as proudly proclaimed on their bands. Second, shade-wrapped stogies, those creamy and smooth smokes perfect for every occasion, are experiencing a resurgence after too many years of ultra-strong profiles ruling the land. Finally, with a complex blend of aged Nicaraguan and Dominican longleaf nestled beneath the silky Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, there's plenty of medium-bodied flavor to be found in each vitola. Like a sign of things to come, there is a small scrap of Maduro leaf covering the head of the otherwise uniformly golden barrel of each H. Upmann Connecticut. Once this ebony cap is clipped to expose the equally hued interior for a cold draw test, the tongue will taste the same warm nutmeg, cedar, and fresh hay the nose has been enjoying. For those expecting a simple profile full of empty promises and thin air, the flavors that pour from a freshly lit stick are a revelation. Leather, white pepper, coffee, cocoa, and earth rule the day, with a touch of molasses and orange zest just to keep things interesting. Released as the mildest smoke in H. Upmann's Grupo de Maestros selection of fine cigars, though packed into boxes of 20 instead of 100 like the others, as you can see there is a whole lot of something going on with the H. Upmann Connecticut. Hearty enough to stand up to a smoky Scotch after dinner, the experienced enthusiast will find them an excellent start to the day's smoking as well. Don't deny yourself any longer, it's almost quitting time and your humidor is calling for a restock.

A new classic in every sense of the word, the H. Upmann Herman's Batch cigar has been over a century in the making. That's because these succulent parejos, filled to the brim with prime filler tobaccos from the Dominican Republic and two distinct Nicaraguan growing regions beneath a Dominican binder and four-year-aged Ecuadoran Habano wrapper, are designed to replicate the original Cuban-made H. Upmann from 1844. It was then that brand founder Herman Upmann, recently arrived on the island from Germany, launched the first tasty vitola in what would soon become a veritable tobacco empire. Herman's legacy continues to impress to this day. We can't know for certain if those original stogies were as visually appealing as the golden-brown H. Upmann Herman's Batch, but we do know if these cigars taste even half as good as they look then you are in for a real treat. Looking like suede beneath the simple yet elegant gray and gold double bands, the sturdy Habano wrapper is toothy yet soft with a nice little pigtail to finish the cap. Aroma and cold draw flavors of an unlit stick are complimentary, both a little nutty and with a strong cocoa presence. The lit profile flourishes with oak, earth, vanilla, and Turbinado sugar during the cool-burning first half, while the lengthy second is rich with leather, marzipan, café con leche, and cinnamon. A gentleman's cigar even you ladies are going to want to horde, these medium-strength and full-flavored handmades are tastefully packaged in sturdy boxes bearing the likeness of Herman himself. Similar in style to other recent smokes in the old-world style like Monte by Montecristo, you'll want to break out your best aged rum or heartiest ale to ride shotgun whenever you smoke an H. Upmann Herman's Batch. A top hat is recommended, but not required.

H. Upmann Hispaniola by Jose Mendez is among the most recent cigars to bear the coveted H. Upmann name, and this time the blend is from the Dominican Republic! Over the past several years, Altadis USA has teamed up with some big names in attempts to re-kindle the classics. Of all the recent remakes, however, the H. Upmann blends seem to garner the most attention. Just a couple years back, H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez took things to a whole new level, and now Altadis has given another rising star in the cigar world a chance to put his own twist on things. Jose "Pepe" Mendez is best known for a recent addition to the Montecristo portfolio: Montecristo Pilotico Pepe Mendez. After the success of that particular offering, he had the chance to recreate the H. Upmann blend at the famed Tabacalera de Garcia in the Dominican Republic using his own recipe. Speaking of the recipe, this cigar consists of a filler blend from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua, a Dominican Olor binder, and a golden brown Ecuador Sumatra wrapper leaf. Not your typical H. Upmann, this stick is made to be a whole new animal. Classic packaging was a must for this release. Retro style cedar chests contain the gorgeous vitolas bearing rustic red and gold bands. The cigar itself is rustic and oily, boasting fine yellow veins throughout the surface. Impressive construction leads to a dense roll and a generous draw, yielding an opening of black pepper and toasty cedar. Creamy tobacco and roasted nuts are the stars of the show, along with hints of tangy citrus and spicy cayenne. A clean finish seals the deal on this medium-full-bodied blend, which is eerily reminiscent of the Cubans of old. H. Upmann Hispaniola by Jose Mendez is certainly a stick to try if you are looking for something different. Any intermediate-level connoisseur will be able to thoroughly enjoy the classic, yet complex profile, while more experienced cigar freaks should be impressed by its Cuban style flavor. This blend pairs particularly well with scotch or bourbon due to its medium-full-bodied nature. Somewhat similar in stature to the classics such as Romeo y Julieta or Punch, H. Upmann Hispaniola tells quite a story with each puff. If you are a fan of the recently revamped classics or even if you just want to try a new blend that seems to really stand out, it is without a doubt in your best interest to try an H. Upmann Hispaniola by Jose Mendez.

H. Upmann Legacy cigars are cigars that have literally been more than a century in the making. From its Cuban inception back in 1844, the H. Upmann name has become a household name among cigar lovers worldwide. Whether Cuban or non-Cuban, cigars bearing the H. Upmann trademark have been beloved by countless aficionados, celebrities, and even political figures. It's not just about being well-known and favored by many, however, as plenty of brands have come to match such a description. With H. Upmann, it's about being one of the oldest, most sought-after and appreciated cigar names in the world. It's about being more than just infamous, but rather legendary. H. Upmann Legacy commemorates such an achievement. Made down in Honduras, unlike its Dominican counterpart, the 1844 Reserve, Legacy is lovingly handmade using the finest Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco, along with a dark brown Ecuador Sumatra wrapper leaf grown under the shady cloud cover deep in the mountains of South America. It may have different packaging, and it may be produced in a different part of the world, but H. Upmann Legacy undoubtedly continues the tradition of masterful quality and superb taste. (Shop other H. Upmann Cigars ) Chocolate-brown and dripping with natural oils, H. Upmann Legacy is the definition of a classic Cuban-style cigar. Silky, creamy smoke delivers a well-refined bouquet of earthy flavor, coating the palate with bold white pepper and earthy tobacco goodness, while more delicate nuances of nuts and cedar tie the package together. A hint of cocoa and crisp sweetness rolls through the nose on the finish, making a wonderful accompaniment to the otherwise heavy, classic flavor profile. It's this complex, savory-sweet flavor profile that helped H. Upmann Legacy to earn multiple 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado. Medium-full-bodied, while full-flavored from start to finish, H. Upmann Legacy is without a doubt a solid choice for experienced connoisseurs. However, the strange simplicity of the otherwise extraordinarily complex blend makes it a great cigar for just about anyone, even semi-seasoned beginners. H. Upmann Legacy, being a classic Cuban-style cigar, pairs well with bourbon or dark rum and proves to be a wonderful dessert to a hearty meal. H. Upmann Legacy will be appreciated by fans of Punch Signature and Romeo y Julieta 1875. Many cigars are smoked to celebrate something profound. With H. Upmann Legacy, it's about celebrating more than 150 years of cigar excellence. Its about celebrating a Legacy.

The legendary H. Upmann name has stood among the cigar world’s most respected brands since 1844, and with the H. Upmann Nicaragua by AJ Fernandez Sunrise , that legacy enters an exciting new chapter. Crafted in Estelí, Nicaragua, by master blender AJ Fernandez in collaboration with Rafael Nodal, Sunrise marks the third regular-production H. Upmann blend produced by Fernandez for Tabacalera USA, bringing a smoother, more approachable profile to the acclaimed Nicaragua series. Wrapped in a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and hand-selected Nicaraguan long-fillers, Sunrise offers a medium-bodied experience that goes far beyond the traditional Connecticut cigar profile. Every tobacco used in the blend is grown, fermented, and aged by AJ Fernandez, ensuring the depth, consistency, and craftsmanship cigar enthusiasts have come to expect from his work. From the first draw, the cigar opens with smooth, flavorful notes of coffee, sweet vanilla aroma, cedar, toasted nuts, and creamy earth , balanced by a subtle natural sweetness and gentle white pepper spice . While Sunrise is the mildest blend in the H. Upmann Nicaragua lineup, it never lacks character, delivering a rich, nuanced profile that remains flavorful from start to finish. As Gabe Diaz, brand manager for Altadis U.S.A., described it, “The Sunrise is our take on a Connecticut done right. It’s smooth and easy to enjoy, but it still has flavor and character.” That philosophy shines through in every puff, making this cigar an excellent choice for both seasoned smokers and those exploring premium Connecticut-style blends for the first time. Balanced, versatile, and refined, the H. Upmann Nicaragua by AJ Fernandez Sunrise is equally at home with a morning coffee, an afternoon round of golf, or a relaxing evening smoke, proof that smooth cigars can still deliver bold personality.

A must-have in any humidor – this cigar boasts complex aroma and smooth, unique flavor.  H. Upmann Vintage Cameroon – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 A must-have in any humidor – this cigar boasts complex aroma and smooth, unique flavor. The H. Upmann Vintage Cameroon is a throwback to the early days when all H. Upmann cigars in this legendary line were wrapped with Cameroon leaves.

A triumphant return to form for one of the world's great frontmarks, the H. Upmann Vintage Cameroon cigar recaptures a long-forgotten magic. First introduced to the world in the 1970's, the original and stunningly delicious Dominican-born H. Upmann stogie owed much of its heralded success to its trademark African Cameroon wrapper. The infamous Cigar Boom of the mid 1990's led to such severe tobacco shortages that an Indonesian-sourced wrapper had to be substituted and while still wonderful, H. Upmann smokes had lost a piece of their soul. Now, the medium-strength Vintage Cameroon, containing a revamped blend of longleaf filler from Peru, Nicaragua, and the Dominican Republic, plus a Nicaraguan binder, has righted the wrongs of the past. The cedar sleeve which decorates and protects the lower portion of each Cameroon-enveloped vitola might also be considered a shield for the senses, for once the shimmering oily barrel is revealed your mind will reel with desire, your hands will shake while searching for the nearest lighter, and your mouth will salivate in anticipation of a luxurious experience. Creamy, nutmeg-and-cardamom-flavored smoke fills the room and the mouth right out of the gate, with some citrus in the aftertaste and an earthy black pepper in the retrohale. The profile wavers as you puff, even as the burn does not, with rich dark chocolate-covered almonds one moment followed by rich cedar and espresso the next. Come discover for yourself why a Cameroon wrapper was once the leaf of choice for the discerning aficionado with the surprisingly affordable 92-rated H. Upmann Vintage Cameroon, then expand your horizons to old classics like Arturo Fuente Gran Reserva Natural and Cohiba or with more recent converts such as AJ Fernandez' New World Cameroon. Suitable for pairing with a morning cup of Cuban coffee but able to stand up to finishing that bottle of bourbon-barrel Cabernet, you'll be needing another humidor just to hold your budding stash of these fine sticks.

A complex blend, boasting unique flavors, with plenty of spice. Henry Clay War Hawk – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Henry Clay rose to Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives in the early 1800s, and was known above all, as a staunch U.S. nationalist. Clay believed strongly that military force was the only option left to fight British imperiousness. The term “War Hawk” was coined and now used in political circles to describe one who favors war as an ultimate resolution of a conflict. The Henry Clay “War Hawk” is a dedication to Henry Clay’s lasting influence. The War Hawk cigar is aptly named, as it is a bit rebellious in going against its own tradition by not using a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper – as do most other Henry Clay brands. The “Hawkish” cigar is a complex blend, boasting unique flavors, with plenty of spice.

It's not like the long and interesting history behind a delicious cigar like the Henry Clay War Hawk is going to distract you from reaching for one every day at smoking time anyway, so we'll give a brief synopsis and then get to the good stuff. Henry was a famous American Senator in the early nineteenth century, notable for being prominent among a group of nationalist 'War Hawk' politicians. First appearing in the 1840's, cigars bearing the Henry Clay moniker were once popular enough to require a Cuban factory dedicated to their creation. Most importantly, now crafted in Honduras, these premium medium-bodied stogies are loaded with choice Honduran longleaf filler layered within an oily Broadleaf binder and held firm by a velvety Connecticut wrapper from Ecuador. We think the old man himself would be rightly proud of the cigar that bears his name and reputation. Showing no sign of softness beneath the leathery, caramel-colored Shade wrapper, the generously packed core is ripe with a rich chocolate aroma and tastes of minerals and oak during a cold draw test. Built on a foundation of flinty earth enhanced by cracked pepper, the profile of a lit Henry Clay War Hawk also displays an unexpected gentleness by layering in sweet cream butter, sourdough toast, raw cane sugar, and cinnamon. Black coffee and cashew provide depth during the latter stages of the smoke, any lingering sweetness thickening to a slightly bitter molasses that keeps you returning for just one more puff. More flavorful than the usual Connecticut-wrapped stogies but not so potent that it will ruin your morning if paired with a cup o' Joe, you might just nominate the Henry Clay War Hawk to compete to be your new favorite. Put them up against the likes of Ashton Classic, Perdomo Reserve Champaign, or Zino Platinum Crown and just see if they can't hold their own. It will be a battle for the ages.

With just 1,200 boxes produced, This special cigar is in available in one size in 20-count boxes.

Herrera Estelí Habano cigars follow Liga Privada and MUWAT as non-infused, ultra-premium offerings from Drew Estate. More importantly, this line marks the first blend created by Willy Herrera—the first true Cuban influence at Drew Estate. After joining the company, Jonathan Drew gave Herrera a year in Nicaragua, full access to his tobaccos, and complete creative freedom. Countless trials later, Herrera delivered a masterpiece that earned a spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 of 2013 . That cigar was Herrera Estelí. Crafted with a Nicaraguan filler blend and Honduran binder, the cigar is finished in a silky Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The Herrera Estelí Habano Robusto Grande was rated 93 and named the #15 Cigar of the Year 2021 by Cigar Aficionado , securing its reputation as one of Drew Estate’s finest releases. From its Cuban-style packaging to its flawless construction, Herrera Estelí exudes quality. Each cigar offers a firm pack, seamless roll, and effortless draw. The first puff greets the palate with a creamy, spicy bouquet of pepper, cedar, and earth, with subtle raw tobacco sweetness weaving throughout. Medium-to-full in body, it remains smooth and refined, delivering a classic Cuban-style experience with modern complexity. Like many of Drew Estate’s ultra-premium cigars, Herrera Estelí is best enjoyed by seasoned aficionados with developed palates. It pairs exceptionally well with bourbon or scotch and draws comparisons to celebrated Cuban-inspired blends such as Don Pepin Blue Label and Padrón. For a full appreciation, many enthusiasts enjoy comparing the original with the follow-up blend, Herrera Estelí Norteño. Whether you consider it a Cuban in disguise or a benchmark for modern premium cigars, Herrera Estelí is a must-have for every serious connoisseur.
Chocolate , Cedar , Almonds Available. Learn about Herrera Esteli Miami Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Miami

It's not often you come across a handmade cigar rolled in the US, but it's even more rare when one is as impressive as the Herrera Esteli Miami cigar. As master blender for Drew Estate , Willy Herrera is personally responsible for many of the masterpieces coming from their Nicaraguan-based La Gran Fabrica, including the original Herrera Esteli. However, for this fine smoke Willy wanted to return to the place where he began his meteoric rise to the top of the cigar stratosphere, the diminutive El Titan de Bronze factory in Miami's Little Havana. There, some of the world's best torcedors use traditional methods to bunch the longleaf Dominican and Nicaraguan filler beneath two different types of Ecuadorian tobacco: a Sumatra binder, and a ruddy Habano Oscuro as the wrapper. Those of you who pay little attention to the aroma of an unlit cigar should really take some quality time to get acquainted with the rich and spicy odors wafting from the flawless barrel of this gem to gain some hints of what is to come. The leather, earth, toasted malt, cocoa, and cinnamon that form the base profile are all there just waiting to be unleashed as soon as the Herrera Esteli Miami is slowly smoldering. The fun doesn't stop while the strength gradually shifts from medium to just below full as your palate will delight to bursts of espresso, plenty of creamy goodness, hints of red pepper, and enough salted caramel to satiate even the sweetest tooth. The worthy recipient of a shiny and new accolade of being named as number 24 in the 2020 Cigar of the Year rankings by Cigar Aficionado , the Herrera Esteli Miami should be on every aficionado's short list of must-haves for 2020 and beyond. Far more affordable than anyone could have guessed for such a great cigar, there's no reason to turn back now.

Hoyo La Amistad Silver is the second cigar in three Hoyo collaborations between General Cigar and AJ Fernandez. Released in 2017, one year after Hoyo La Amistad Gold, Hoyo La Amistad Silver is comprised of 100% Habano tobacco, intended for more experienced connoisseurs and fans of fuller-bodied cigars. AJ Fernandez takes special delight in blending and putting his name on these special cigars because he actually grew up near the actual Hoyo de Monterrey tobacco farms in Cuba. In his own words, he "put his heart and soul into this blend" and it "represents the best of the Fernandez family and factory." This, of course, is referring to the umbrella of all 3 blends in the Hoyo La Amistad series, but Fernandez's words go to show that this blend was by no means thrown together. For the Hoyo La Amistad Silver, the actual blend consists of an Ecuadorian wrapper, Nicaraguan binder, and a rich filler blend from two of the most popular tobacco regions of Nicaragua: Esteli and Condega. All tobaccos used in Hoyo La Amistad Silver are grown from Habano Cuban seed, making this fine product the strongest offering in the series.

Pete Johnson of Tatuaje said in a recent interview, "Dion made Candela cool again." He was referencing Dion Giolito's Illusione and his three green creations: ~88~, ~888~ and ~hl~. For the early part of Illusione's storied rise to the top of the cigar world, Dion stuck with using Nicaraguan Colorado Claro among his lines, which made sense given that he had access to Nicaragua's best tobacco. However, realizing that he had some extra boxes for his Lancero, the Illusione ~hl~, Dion decided that he would put both a Maduro wrapper and a Candela wrapper in those boxes just to see how things would go. (See more Illusione Cigars ) Originally planned for four-hundred boxes, the Candela and Maduro caught on well enough that he soon began to offer it as a regular production. Fast forward to the beginning of 2011 and the ~88~ (Robusto) and these ~888~ Necessary and Sufficient Candelas (Churchill) had been made available as well. The Illusione ~888~ Candela cigar wrapper gives off a sweet grassy flavor and unique aroma to three of Illusione's classic cigars, creating a completely different profile. The cigars are still full-bodied, full-flavor and medium-full in strength, but it's a much different smoking experience. However, due to the extremely difficult nature of fermenting the Candela tobacco, the Illusione Candelas are difficult to make and even more difficult to keep in stock. Don't let the color fool you, these are still some of Nicaragua's finest.

Illusione Rothchildes Connecticut is the latest offering from the beloved Illusione Cigar Company down in Nicaragua. While not much is said about Illusione, they know their cigars, and the history of this ultra-premium boutique brand speaks for itself. Over the years Illusione Cigars has collected dozens of accolades, including numerous 90+ ratings and even a spot on the celebrated Cigar Aficionado Top 25. Now, following up their hugely successful Rothchildes line, Illusione introduces Rothchildes Connecticut. This blend consists of a spicy Nicaraguan filler and binder blend combined with a vintage Connecticut wrapper leaf. This golden brown leaf is heavily aged and imparts truckloads of flavor to the blend, putting a pleasant twist on the original Rothchildes blend from Illusione. (See more Illusione Cigars ) In proper boutique cigar fashion, Illusione Rothchildes Connecticut is beautifully crafted and features a smooth, heavily-productive draw and a sharp burn. Initial notes of cedar and honey open up for a gorgeous flavor profile of earthy, spicy raw tobacco mixed with hints of cocoa and nutmeg. A sweet finish beautifully ties together the medium-full-bodied bouquet of amazing complexity. Illusione is the epitome of a high-end boutique cigar company. From the beginning, the good folks at Illusione aimed particularly at an experienced crowd of connoisseurs wanting superior quality. Rothchildes Connecticut is by no means an exception. Medium-full-bodied, this 4 1/2" x 50 petite robusto packs quite a punch and pairs well with bourbon or scotch for a sophisticated experience. Fans of the original Illusion lineup will take a particular liking to Rothchildes Connecticut, as well as those who may have enjoyed the original Rothchildes edition. Years in the making, Illusione Rothchildes Connecticut proves to be a standout stick among the cigar snob crowd for years to come.

Dion Giolito's Illusione has been one of the most highly regarded lines of cigars made today. The Nicaraguan puros are made at the Raíces Cubanas factory in Danlí, Honduras. This is the same factory responsible for producing the award-winning Alec Bradley, Padilla and Viaje cigars, which are some of the hottest in the world. People wondered when Dion would introduce a Maduro wrapper across his entire line, as he previously restricted it to a special version of his ~hl~ Lancero. In early 2011, the announcement came that the entire Illusione core line, known as The Original Document, would be getting a Maduro wrapper. Dion chose a dark and hearty Maduro wrapper from the San Andrés Valley in Mexico to place over his AGANORSA Nicaraguan binder and fillers. (See more Illusione Cigars ) One of the greatest strengths of the Illusione line-up has been the ability to create unique flavor profiles for each individual size and that extends to the Maduro line. The Mexican Maduro adds leather, cocoa and earth to the Nicaraguan fillers which are noted for their nuttiness, cedar and black pepper. It's a great contrast of sweet and spicy with solid earth notes underneath. Strength and body are both increased a bit, but the Illusione Maduros are closer to the Illusione Original Document than the Illusione ULTRA. For many, this was one of the most exciting releases of the year, and Dion definitely delivered on the high expectations.

In the world of premium cigars, it’s usually an instant success when an old, dead brand is resurrected by one of today’s major players. However, when that resurrected brand starts having spin-offs, big things start to happen. Such is precisely the case with OneOff Black and Tan. Once an under-the-radar brand kept in business by its cult following, the original OneOff brand stuck around for a little over a decade before fizzling out. Then, in 2018, the OneOff name was given new life by Dion Giolito of Illusione cigars , this time as a mainstream ultra-premium stick. Skip ahead a few more years, and OneOff Black and Tan becomes the star of the lineup, a line addition for the pickiest of connoisseurs that is absolutely built to impress. Little is known about the recipe for this Nicaraguan-made masterpiece, other than that it uses a type of Nicaraguan tobacco that “hasn’t been grown recently.” How mysterious! Does it even matter, though? The folks at Cigar Aficionado don’t seem to think so, as OneOff Black and Tan has earned numerous 90+ ratings , the best being a rock-star 94 , not to mention a spot on the Top 25 Cigars of 2024 and 2025 . Certainly, one of the biggest eyebrow raisers to ever be called an Illusione, OneOff Black and Tan delivers an unforgettable smoking experience every time.
