Black and tan boxes come as no surprise, and a single, nondescript peace sign adorns the plain black band hugging each vitola. Expert construction includes a nearly seamless roll and a draw that would impress even the most critical of cigar snobs. Layers of rich white smoke paint the palate with rich, spicy flavor from the very first puff. Earthy tobacco mixed with crisp white pepper are the opening duo, and this combo quickly establishes itself as the backbone of the flavor profile. Notes of caramel and almond dance in the background, and hints of chocolate and cinnamon roll off the tongue on the finish. Complex, bold, and rich, OneOff Black and Tan offers a luxurious smoking experience that finishes on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied. Made for the experienced, OneOff Black and Tan is sure to quickly rise to the top of any aficionado’s favorites list. Flavorful, complex, and impeccably balanced, this medium-full-bodied gem has every single angle covered. Pair this stogie with your favorite dark rum or black coffee and set aside plenty of time to kick back, relax, and enjoy every second, because trust us, you aren’t going to want to put this one down. Fans of spicy Nicaraguan sticks such as My Father or Tatuaje would probably be the biggest fans of this blend, as the spice and complexity seem to hit just right every time. Don’t let the odd name fool you. There is definitely nothing “off” about OneOff Black and Tan. Try one today and you might just decide to make it your new favorite premium smoke.

When you think of value sticks, one of the last names you will think of is Illusione, but Dion Giolito always likes to push the envelope and his Rothchildes will change the way you think about affordable cigars. Made in Esteli, Nicaragua, this wonderful cigar is filled and bound with amazing Nicaraguan tobaccos and wrapped in a rustic Mexican San Andres leaf. At this price point, this medium-to-full bodied stick is always a good cigar to have on hand not just to smoke but also to hand out among your friends. (See more Illusione Cigars ) The red, white, and gold band has a retro feel, and the rustic nature of the wrapper gives you a feeling of nostalgia as well. The first thing you will notice is the amazing aroma this cigar gives off before you even torch the foot. A strong floral note mingles in the air with a tinge of cedar and leather. The taste is just as tantalizing as you go from beginning to nub. Citrus mixed with a sweeter spiciness than you would expect from a cigar from this region will play games with your palate as you take each puff. The affordable market seems to be coming into full swing with the Illusione Rothchildes, Tatuaje Tattoo, and other brands looking to fill this market. This breath of fresh air for your wallet doesn't mean you have to take a step back in quality one bit. This cigar smokes like a much higher priced stick and is well-deserving of a spot in your humidor. At this price you can officially call an Illusione your everyday stick and not have to worry about it.

Illusione Slam is a cigar that isn't talked about much, but is a well-known ultra-premium among serious cigar connoisseurs. Made in Honduras under the supervision of Dion Giolitto, Illusione Slam is a Nicaraguan puro made with all Nicaraguan tobaccos, and top-shelf tobaccos at that. The "Slam" refers to the fact that it is box-pressed, or rather "bench" pressed as Giolitto explains. Very refined and superbly complex, Illusione Slam is one of today's finest Nicaraguan cigars. (See more Illusione Cigars ) Masterful construction and a delightful draw bring forth massive amounts of silky blue smoke. From the get-go, Illusione Slam pounds the palate hard with rich Nicaraguan spice while creating a cascade of cedar and tobacco flavors across the taste buds. The finish is clean, crisp, and sweet, similar to that of a fine wine. Overall a medium-full-bodied experience, Illusione Slam is a connoisseur's dream. Illusione cigars have always been made with the serious aficionado in mind, so beginners need not apply. Delicate complexities and a rich, luxurious flavor profile are just a couple ways Illusione Slam guarantees to impress the hardcore smoker. It pairs well with bourbon and port wine and can be compared to Oliva Serie V Melanio and Flor de Las Antillas. No advertisement is necessary with Illusione Slam—those in the know already enjoy it!

The Illusione Ultra cigar was conceived out of brand owner Dion Giolito's most popular cigars. Originally a product Dion thought was too strong for the market, the Illusione ULTRA was released in small quantities in 2008 in the size. After much demand, Dion announced plans to offer ULTRA again in 2011. Like the rest of the award-winning Illusione line these are made at the Raíces Cubanas factory in Danlí, Honduras using all Nicaraguan tobacco. Raíces Cubanas is responsible for award-winning Illusione products like the Epernay, as well as Viaje cigars and Alec Bradley's popular Family Blend, Prensado and Tempus lines. (See more Illusione Cigars ) ULTRA uses a dark oily Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper with Nicaraguan fillers, mainly Jalapa and Estelí Ligero. The goal with ULTRA was to create a full-bodied, full flavor and full strength cigar, and Dion did just that. It starts with a heavy dose of spice, hearty earths, rich cedars, great leathers and complex chocolate. For those that enjoyed the original ULTRA, the new versions of the ULTRA are a great reminder of one Dion Giolito's classic cigars. If you are expecting anything other than full flavor and full strength, the Illusione ULTRA will leave you highly confused.

The J. Fuego Gran Reserva Corojo #1 cigar is the one that started it all. After years of working to craft some of Rocky Patel's highly acclaimed blends, third-generation tobacco man Jesus Fuego left to start his own company, J. Fuego, in 2006. A year later he introduced the Gran Reserva Corojo No. 1, the first major step in cementing Corojo with Fuego. Since then, Fuego has introduced a handful of highly-acclaimed lines featuring Corojo, including the Corojo puro "Origen" and most recently Sangre de Toro, but Gran Reserva was the first. (See more J Fuego Cigars ) The Gran Reserva would be introduced on the heels of major recognition in the form of back-to-back Top 25 Cigar of the Year honors for partnerships with Nestor Plasencia. These J. Fuego Gran Reserva Corojo #1 cigars feature Honduran Corojo wrappers, Costa Rican Corojo binders and Honduran, Nicaraguan and some super secret proprietary fillers. Flavor is a slight tweak on classic Corojo with a bit more depth and a bit less rawness. Delicate peppers, hearty woods and sweet earths are the main flavors, with nuts, floral notes and cocoa appearing at times for the seasoned palate. Dark ash and great smoke production adorn the well-made Honduran cigar, but you remember the 90+ point Gran Reserva Corojo #1 for one reason, flavor.

In 2009, Jesus Fuego's Tabacos S.A. introduced its newest line of cigars, J. Fuego Origen. After years of working for Rocky Patel, Jesus Fuego, a third generation tobacco man, set out on his own partnering with Nestor Plasencia to create a variety of new cigars. At Plasencia's Tabacos de Oriente factory in Danlí, Honduras the two would craft award-winning blends such as the J. Fuego Gran Reserva Corojo #1, J. Fuego Sangre de Toro and Xikar HC. The J. Fuego Origen is offered in six sizes: 7 1/2" x 38 (Lancero), 6" x 50 (Toro), 5 1/2" x 52 (Belicoso), 4 7/8" x 49 (Robusto), 5 1/2" x 46 (Corona Gorda) and the popular 5" x 44 (Original). For the Origen, Fuego crafted a blend of only Corojo. Four different nationalities are represented: a Brazilian Corojo wrapper, a Costa Rican Corojo Binders and Nicaraguan and Honduran Corojo fillers. (See more J Fuego Cigars ) For those that enjoy full flavor and medium-full cigars, Origen is one of the best lines on the market. There's great rich notes of cedar, coffee, earth and classic Corojo pepper. In 2010, Fuego added the Original size, a free-rolled Cheroot size offered in packs of five. While it's not the prettiest of cigars, the smallest size has become the most popular because of its ability to deliver large amounts of flavor in a small format, perfect for those moments when you don't have time for a regular cigar, but don't want to sacrifice quality.

At the 2010 IPCPR trade show in New Orleans, Jesus Fuego's Tabacos S.A. introduced a host of new products, but none to the fanfare of the J. Fuego Origen Originals cigar. This newest addition to the J. Fuego family picks up right where the "origin" of the Origen left off, only this time Jesus Fuego kicks up the flavor a notch a two with a bold, bright and banging Brazilian Maduro wrapper. (See more J Fuego Cigars ) The Origen Maduro line followed in the footsteps of its early 2010 release, releasing his most popular sizes but the third-generation tobacco man didn't hesitate to release the Origen Maduro in a full complement of vitolas including, what has become his now-signature vitola, the "Original," tiny little Cheroots. The concept is the same one Jesus uses when testing tobaccos for blending in the factory. In the small 5" x 44 size as well as all of the others in the line, Fuego packs five different nationalities worth of tobacco leaves: a Brazilian Mata Fina Maduro wrapper, a Costa Rican Corojo Binder and Nicaraguan Criollo, Honduran Corojo and Mexican San Andres fillers. Expect highly-developed notes of Mexican hot chocolate sweetness along with dry summer dust bowl earthen notes and rich black motorcycle leather scents and tastes. Any concerns about construction are laid to rest pretty quickly: tons of smoke production, a near perfect draw and a consistent burn that usually leads to finger burning. These Origen Maduros are the next evolution of what was once the beginning for a man that is now a Master Blender. Kick back, light one up and let him take you on a world tour!

The J. Fuego Sangre de Toro is one of the most popular selling cigars in the J. Fuego line-up. After years of working to craft some of Rocky Patel's highly acclaimed blends, third-generation tobacco man Jesus Fuego left to start his own company, J. Fuego, in 2006. A year later he introduced the Gran Reserva Corojo No. #1, the first major step in cementing Corojo with Fuego. Since then, Fuego has introduced a handful of highly-acclaimed lines featuring Corojo, expanding to include the Corojo puro "Origen" and many more since. (See more J Fuego Cigars ) Sangre de Toro translates to "Blood of the Bull" and the use of the Corojo leaf here is dominant for sure. These Sangre de Toro cigars feature Nicaraguan Colorado wrappers, Nicaraguan Corojo binders and Nicaraguan Colorado and Corojo filler tobaccos. As strange as it sounds, and our Ninja swears she isn't the only one, these cigars have a distinct dill/pickle aroma at the foot. Mouth warming peppers, hearty, head-clearing woods and sweet-smelling earths are the main flavors with nuts, herbal, floral notes and cocoa caramel swirls appearing at times for the seasoned palate. Dark ash and great smoke production adorn the well-made Honduran cigar, but you'll remember the 90-point Sangre de Toro for more than just the pretty yellow, black and blood red band.

Jaime García has spent years helping craft some of the most celebrated cigars in the premium tobacco industry alongside his father, the legendary José “Pepin” García. While the original Jaime Garcia Reserva Especial earned widespread acclaim for its rich, robust flavors and balanced complexity, the Jaime Garcia Reserva Especial Connecticut takes a decidedly different approach. Created by the father-and-son duo at the renowned My Father Cigars S.A. factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, this blend offers a smoother, creamier interpretation of the line's profile while maintaining the exceptional flavor and craftsmanship that have made the García family a household name among cigar enthusiasts. The Reserva Especial Connecticut begins with a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper draped over a carefully selected blend of Nicaraguan binders and long-filler tobaccos grown on the García family's private estates. The result is a premium cigar that delivers the approachable character Connecticut smokers appreciate without sacrificing structural depth or complexity. Rather than relying on raw strength, this blend showcases the family's talent for creating balance and nuance from properly aged leaves. From the first draw, the cigar greets the palate with smooth notes of cream, cedar, and roasted nuts . As the smoke develops, intermediate layers of coffee bean and sweet almond emerge, accompanied by subtle touches of earth and white pepper that add depth without overwhelming the profile. A delicate note of smoked butterscotch lingers in the background, enhancing the natural tobacco sweetness and contributing to a remarkably refined finish. Operating at a definitive mild-to-medium body but remaining full in flavor, the experience remains engaging from first light to the final third. Handcrafted with the same meticulous attention to detail found throughout the My Father portfolio, the Jaime Garcia Reserva Especial Connecticut delivers an effortless draw, an even burn line, and impressive consistency. Whether enjoyed with a morning coffee, an afternoon bourbon, or as an easygoing evening smoke, this vitola proves that Connecticut wrappers can be every bit as flavorful and sophisticated as their darker counterparts. For admirers of the family's historic portfolio, this blend provides a highly refined, character-driven addition to the humidor.

It's not often enough in today's fast paced, technology-driven world that you see a son following in the footsteps of a famous father in an old school business, or at least being able to achieve the same level of quality work, but with his Reserva Limited Edition 2012 cigar, Jaime Garcia easily lives up to his genetic potential. Year after year the My Father factory continues to release some of the best cigars from any nation and this release does nothing to diminish that reputation. By carefully selecting only the finest tobaccos and blending them with an expert's touch, each and every vitola is stacked with complex flavor and exceptional balance.
Sweet , Spicy , Red Pepper , Black Pepper Available. Learn about Joya de Nicaragua Antano Connecticut Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Antano Connecticut

Joya de Nicaragua Antano Connecticut is one of the most highly esteemed Connecticut cigars in recent years. Manufactured for Drew Estate in the Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua factory in Nicaragua, this phenomenal concoction is essentially one of the world's strongest cigars, Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970, draped in a Connecticut wrapper. Neither mild like a Connecticut nor strong like the original, this upscale blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos along with its Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf combine to make a beautiful flavor profile built to impress fans of the former and the latter alike. Even the folks at Cigar Aficionado seem to think so, as a prompt pair of 93 ratings tells the story.

Sometimes, we tend to forget about things that happened in the past, even important things, things that likely changed the course of our lives and shaped things into what they are now. In the case of Joya de Nicaragua cigars, the Clasico Original is that important thing. It was the stick that put the company on the map many, many decades ago, and was even deemed the official cigar of the Nixon White House in the 1970s. It is the only cigar to be officially recognized as Nicaragua’s national cigar. It is what laid the foundation for everything that Joya de Nicaragua has become. Despite being off the American market for about 15 years, it’s back, and it’s every bit as good today as it was 50 years ago. Made in Nicaragua, this blend contains Nicaraguan binder and filler tobacco and a caramel brown Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper. This is said to be the same wrapper leaf used for the company’s celebrated Numero Uno line, but with an obviously different internal recipe. Simple and straightforward, there is something seriously satisfying about this old school blend. Housed in beautiful white and gold cedar chests, the gorgeous cigars each wear 2 bands: a primary gold and brown band with the unmistakable JDN tobacco leaf and a secondary band denoting the blend. Expert construction continues the brand’s legacy, and each puff is smooth, easy, and satisfying, bathing the palate in silky blue smoke. Crispy cedar and white pepper open things up, soon followed by a delicious combination of raw tobacco, cinnamon, and hints of caramel and coffee . A sweet floral note dances off the nose, and the main accord is a toasty cedar flavor that pulls everything together. Mild-bodied, yet flavorful, this cigar is the very definition of what a classic Connecticut cigar should be. Suitable for everyone, Clasico Original appeals to both newbies and connoisseurs alike. New cigar enthusiasts will likely appreciate the mild body and easy-smoking aspect of the blend, while those with more experience will be reminded of a simpler time when cigars weren’t so wild and crazy as they are today. This blend pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or coffee, and is comparable to such other classic Connecticut blends as Montecristo Classic or Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real. This is the taste of Nicaragua as you’ve never experienced before, so don’t hesitate to celebrate with one of the cigars that made Nicaragua famous: Joya de Nicaragua Clasico Original.

Originally made to celebrate its 45th year of existence, Joya de Nicaragua Cuatro Cinco Reserva Especial cigars just fit the bill as a celebratory cigar for the ages. As the first Nicaraguan cigar factory in 1968, the Cuatro Cinco needed to be a unique cigar to honor not only the company but also all the wonderful people that have worked for them. Since it was so successful, Joya de Nicaragua decided to come out with a slightly altered version of that special edition cigar for the masses. They added a Dominican volado binder to the original Nicaraguan puro that may be more on the medium side in terms of body but it is very full of flavor. The 5-year-aged filler tobaccos from Esteli and the Jalapa Valley spend an extra year fermenting in rum oak barrels to impart an extra woodiness to the flavor profile. See all Joya De Nicaragua cigars. With a gorgeous and unique band of black and gold atop a band of white, this is definitely made for a special occasion. The dark Nicaraguan wrapper has an unbelievable aroma of fruit and cedar which carries through to your first few puffs. While there is a spiciness on the finish, nothing overpowers the wonderful earthiness that is present from beginning to end. Rigidly square-pressed, the draw and the burn were nothing short of spectacular. Presented in boxes of 10 these cigars are definitely within reach of most aficionados. If you are looking for a little more body, the Joya de Nicaragua Dark Corojo is another outstanding smoke. Check out other Joya De Nicaragua cigars: Joya De Nicaragua Antano 1970 Joya De Nicaragua Antano Connecticut Joya de Nicaragua Antano Dark Corojo Joya de Nicaragua Antano Gran Reserva Joya de Nicaragua Black Joya De Nicaragua Cinco Decadas Joya De Nicaragua Cuatro Cinco Reserva Especial Joya De Nicaragua Joya Red Joya De Nicaragua Joya Silver Joya de Nicaragua Número Uno

The talented team at Kristoff really knew what they were doing when they came up with the Kristoff Cameroon cigar. A new blend for the increasingly prolific boutique cigar company founded in 2004 by Glen Case, it takes all of the hallmarks they are known for; quality tobacco complex tastes, solid value; and raises the bar on them all. The headliner is an African Cameroon wrapper which has been aged a full 7 years to bring out every nuance of flavor possible. A Habano binder from the Dominican Republic is a solid team player, melding perfectly with the filler, which is partly Dominican Habano seed but also contains a good portion of Nicaraguan Habano to maximize the deliciousness factor. Cameroon cigars are usually a mottled tan to light brown. But the leaf used for this cigar really shows its age by bearing a black-streaked burnt sienna countenance, which makes the stick almost Maduro in color. Construction-wise, the cigar yields ever so slightly to pressure without being soft, and pigtail cap give each vitola a strikingly classic appearance. Cameroon cigars are known for being 'spicy' but once again the long rest gifted to the wrapper has transformed this characteristic into something more. Baking spices such as nutmeg and cinnamon are clearly evident, but there is a full roster of almonds and earth and creamy cedar to round out the profile. They are packed into sturdy rough-finished boxes of 20. Medium-full in strength, they pair well with whiskey or with wine to make them a perfect way to end an evening. If you want a cigar to go with your morning coffee, try the sweeter, slightly milder Kristoff Maduro.

The hits just keep coming from Kristoff and now we have the Classic Reserva cigar to deal with and it might be too much for us to handle. Brand founder Glen Case and company have been going about their business since 2004 like it ain't no thang, forging a solid portfolio of smokes and a devoted fan base. The Classic Reserva, released just in time for the 2015 IPCPR Convention, is a callback to traditional tastes but stays on the cutting edge by being rolled at Abe Flores' modern PDR factory in the Dominican Republic. The filler blend contains luscious Dominican, Nicaraguan, and Honduran tobacco finished with a Habano binder and wrapper; the former Nicaraguan, the latter Ecuadorian.

With a knuckle curled around a smoldering Kristoff Connecticut cigar, the smoker finds their consciousness transported to a place of comfort, quality, and taste. Since the company's inception in 2004, each passing year has provided a widening array of delicious Kristoff smokes, and this glorious example of fine craftsmanship is no exception. Loaded with a scrumptious blend of filler tobacco enigmatically labeled 'Quad Dominican Habano Seed,' each sturdy vitola is next layered with a Nicaraguan Habano long leaf binder that adds a spicy kick to the rustic Ecuadorian Shade-Grown wrapper which completes this medium-bodied delight. There are a few other cigar companies that still roll some of their sticks with a classic pigtailed cap, but because most of their front marks are rolled as such, Kristoff's skilled torcedors are arguably the undisputed masters of the style. Shade-grown wrappers are notoriously fragile, but the hay-scented Kristoff Connecticut is a golden-brown work of art that sets the mouth to watering even before unleashing the nutty, cocoa-dusted flavors revealed during the beginning puffs. Warm caramel sweetens the more pungent nutmeg and black coffee that appear during the first third, ripening toffee, marzipan, and espresso. The flavors presented to the palate around the halfway mark while carrying you through to the end on smooth clouds of bright white. Although a little more on the adventurous side than many of the milder cigars out there, the Kristoff Connecticut is still a pitch-perfect companion for all sorts of aficionados. On the next sunny day, fire up the grill, sip on a margarita, and chow down on one of these stogies. Oh man, is that gonna be good!

Kristoff Corojo Limitada cigars have quietly become one of the great boutique cigars of our time. One of the latest additions to the Kristoff portfolio, the Kristoff Corojo Limitada, sports 85 percent Cuban-seed, Nicaraguan tobacco—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler blend is smoothed out, however, by filling in the other 15 percent with luscious Dominican long-fillers. This stick, born in the Dominican Republic, has become a proud member of Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 Cigars of 2012. Kristoff Corojo Limitada cigars, though on the fuller-bodied side, are great for smokers of all experience levels. They are wonderful gateway cigars to get into the fuller, Cuban-esque boutique genre. They pair nicely with heavy beer or bourbon. Comparable cigars today include Cubao and Kristoff Ligero. Enjoy a taste of Cuba today with a Kristoff Corojo Limitada!

Kristoff aims to have a taste and a richness in each of their cigars that a true lover of the leaf is looking for, and the Criollo is no different. Made in the same nature as an elite Cuban smoke, Kristoff Criollo is a wonderful medium-bodied cigar which is very full of flavor. Made up of Cuban-seed Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, Olor Dominican Binder, and an oily Honduran Criollo wrapper, this Dominican-made stogie is a perfect cigar for all hours of the day. Despite being medium-bodied, the flavors are plentiful and the complexity of the smoke is outstanding. This blend has garnered significant acclaim, including a 91 rating from Cigar & Spirits Magazine and a 90-point "Best Buy" distinction from Cigar Journal . By capturing the essence of an elite Cuban smoke, these gems offer a sophisticated, medium-bodied profile that is exceptionally rich in flavor. The traditional Kristoff band adorns the Criollo and almost blends into the wrapper leaf. Beautifully packaged in cedar boxes, Kristoff Criollo has a tight pigtail on the cap. The pre-light aroma had a very floral note and this continued after the first couple of puffs. Strong aspects of cedar and earth were mixed with an almost citrus nature which was very pleasant. By the last half of the Criollo, the floral tendencies became muted and we were left with an amazing smoke with a wood-like quality. With each draw an amazing amount of velvety and smooth smoke entered our palate to give us the best possible smoking experience we could have. Kristoff Criollo has an amazing complex flavor that changes with every third of the cigar, yet maintains a medium-body throughout. The floral and citrus accents paired perfectly with a red wine or possibly a stronger, dryer white. For a heavier smoke we would highly recommend the Kristoff Ligero.

It’s always exciting when a famed ultra-premium cigar brand comes out with a value-priced stick, and such is exactly the case with Kristoff Cuban Selection. Made down in the Dominican Republic, this no-nonsense blend is crafted to replicate all the classic flavors of the Cubans of old. Impressively, this bundle cigar is a Dominican born cigar using Dominican and Nicaraguan filler tobacco, a fine Indonesian binder, and Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. The tips are sweetened for added flavor, making this blend irresistibly pleasant on all fronts. The packaging is simple: wrapped bundles of 20 cigars, each bearing a nicely done classic band. Despite the “bundle cigar” classification, Cuban Selection is still a Kristoff brand, meaning precise construction is never overlooked. A soft draw produces silky smooth smoke, greeting the palate with buttery cream and hints of cedar, earth, and cinnamon. In the background, grassy tobacco flavor and a faint white pepper note linger, all being rounded out by the unmistakable sweetness provided by the flavored tip. Mild-bodied and easy to smoke, Cuban Selection is quite a relaxing, satisfying concoction. Kristoff Cuban Selection makes for a great beginners’ cigar, but just about anyone would agree that the easy, mild flavor it provides makes it a stick to keep on hand for those occasions where something more “exciting” just isn’t applicable. Whether on the golf course, doing yard work, or simply entertaining friends, this stick is a great fit for the occasion. This blend is comparable to such other bundle cigars as Flor de Oliva Gold or Perdomo Fresco and pairs well with light-bodied accompaniments such as white wine, light beer, or iced tea. Whether a first cigar for someone just starting out or a knock-around stick for the experienced connoisseur, Kristoff Cuban Selection is a fantastic cigar to keep in the humidor year-round.

Founded by Glen Case in 2005, Kristoff Cigars is a rapidly growing boutique cigar brand. Though their product names and similar packaging can sometimes be a little confusing, there is one thing that is for certain; their cigars are exceptional. Following the success of the previous Kristoff brand lines including the Kristoff Criollo, Kristoff Ligero Criollo, Kristoff Maduro, and the Kristoff Ligero Maduro, in 2011, brand owner Glen Case released his newest blend, the Kristoff GC Signature Series at the IPCPR 2011. The Kristoff GC Signature Series is described by Kristoff as being for the serious cigar smoker only. This is a Brazilian Maduro wrapper, Cuban Seed Honduran bound and Cuban Seed from Honduras, Nicaragua and Dominican Republic tobacco stuffed monster of a stick. It is available in 3 sizes including robusto, torpedo and six by sixty. This GC Signature Series has a sweet and spicy finish that is loaded with big flavors of espresso, dried apricots and berries while balanced with rich chocolatey flavors from the Brazilian Maduro wrapper. If you are a fan of the Diesel Shorty, Man O'War or Jaime Garcia cigars, this is gonna be a great way for you to try.

In the world of premium cigars, it isn't uncommon for the inspiration behind a special cigar to come from a significant life event. In the case of Kristoff Guardrail, that significant event happens to be the near-death experience of brand owner Glen Case. When riding his motorcycle one night, the back tire gave out during a 65-mph curve and the bike went crashing into a guardrail. Thankfully, Case survived, and after much healing, decided to name this cigar after the horrific events of that fateful evening. The good news is that there is nothing horrific about the blend! Made at the Tabacalera von Eicken factory in the Dominican Republic, Kristoff Guardrail consists of a very special filler blend including long leaves from the Dominican Republic and Zimbabwe, of all places. The binder is Dominican, and the dark, oily wrapper comes from Brazil. Such an interesting blend makes for a great smoking experience and has become quite a success for the boutique cigar company. Modern, refined, and dripping with premium quality, the packaging for Kristoff Guardrail is simply beautiful. Black boxes and chrome bands definitely seem appropriate for the occasion, and the construction of each vitola is exquisite. After the trademark pigtail cap is clipped, a smooth, luxurious draw offers rich smoke production. Soon after lighting, chocolate and caramel flavors greet the palate, along with subtle pepper and creamy raw tobacco. An earthy core holds everything together, and blasts of nuts and cedar constantly appear throughout the experience. Tame, yet complex, Guardrail finishes as a distinctly medium-bodied cigar. Not a beginners' cigar by any means, Kristoff Guardrail is aimed at a more mature audience. The rich complexities and unique flavor profile are certainly geared towards well-developed palates. Medium in body, this stick pairs very well with coffee or medium-bodied beer and is appropriate for just about any time of the day. Fans of similar dark Brazilian-wrapped cigars such as CAO Brazilia or Trinidad Espiritu Series 2 should greatly appreciate what the folks at Kristoff have done here. One of the best ways to deal with tragedy is to turn it into a story of triumph, and that is exactly what Glen Case and his team have done with Kristoff Guardrail.

Kristoff Habano is a cigar put out by one of the most famous boutique companies of all time, and over the years it's garnered quite a reputation. Handmade in the Dominican Republic, Kristoff Habano is one of the newest offerings from the Kristoff Cigar Company, utilizing a stout blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, a Brazilian Sumatra binder, and a dark, oily Brazilian Habano wrapper leaf. Blended for maximum flavor and a medium body, Kristoff Habano will appeal to anyone looking for something with a bit of kick, but not something that's going to cause a blown gasket. Relaxing, pleasant, and uber-flavorful, Kristoff Habano is perhaps one of the better-known cigars to bear the Kristoff name in recent years. Beginning with wood, white pepper, and dark, earthy flavor, Kristoff Habano mellows out to a fabulous concoction of subtle taste notes, including cocoa, nuts, and cinnamon. Spicy on the draw, sweet on the finish; Kristoff Habano is smooth, balanced, and just complex enough to stay interesting along the journey. Those used to ultra-complex cigars may even consider Kristoff Habano to be pleasantly simple, which is a bit refreshing in a world of overly complicated blends that many times end up running together on the flavor end. Kristoff Habano will appeal to just about anyone. It's a solid medium-bodied stick, combining flavor and balance with amazing smokability and versatility. Many will find that Kristoff Habano pairs well with coffee and makes a great start to the day. Other Kristoff cigars worth trying if you like this blend include the original Criollo and Maduro blends. There isn't much to say in terms of fancy packaging or mind-blowing complexity when it comes to this wonderful stick, but what can be said is that for a simple premium cigar that can be enjoyed at any time of the day and for any occasion, Kristoff Habano really is tough to beat.

Born in 2019, the Kristoff JT Signature Series is a premium boutique cigar named after Jarrid Trudeau, Vice President of Sales at Kristoff Cigars. Originally, a retailer had to obtain rights to sell this blend by having a special event with Trudeau, meaning this stick has quite an interesting background. It is rolled by hand at the Charles Fairmorn factory in the Dominican Republic, the site of production for many of Kristoff’s higher-end cigars. As for the blend, JT Signature Series begins with a unique filler blend of aged Mexican San Andres and Dominican leaves. This package is then wrapped in a Sumatra binder and finished with a rare Ecuadorian HVA(or Havana Vuelta Abajo) Habano wrapper. This cigar is considered by many to be one of the best Kristoff has ever released, and with good reason. It is a cigar made for connoisseurs, by connoisseurs. The packaging is both modern and rustic, from the blue wooden chest to the grey and gold band adorning each vitola. The royal blue foot band denoting the blend is a luxurious finishing touch to this box-pressed beauty, making a fine contrast to the wrapper leaf’s gorgeous deep golden brown hue. Oily and finely crafted, Kristoff JT Signature Series is rolled to perform, providing a smooth draw and a tight grey ash. After clipping the trademark pigtail cap and firing up this masterpiece, the first puffs are pretty much what you would expect from a blend such as this, meaning a deep, earthy core is at the forefront from the very beginning. Notes of black pepper and cinnamon are the stars of the show, with spicy blasts from time to time and a delicious hint of graham cracker that lingers on the tip of the tongue. The finish is clean, but bold, and after all is said and done, the Kristoff JT Signature Series finishes as a heavy medium-bodied cigar. Intended for a mature, well-seasoned audience, JT Signature Series is by no means a beginners’ cigar. Then again, if you are part of the cult following that regularly enjoys Kristoff cigars, you probably aren’t a beginner anyways. This medium-bodied cigar pairs well with single malt scotch or red wine and makes a great special occasion smoke. If you are a fan of such medium-bodied Kristoff sticks as Kristoff Sumatra or CG Signature Series , this might be something you want to give a try. Whether you are a die-hard fan of Kristoff cigars or just looking for something premium to wind down with on a Friday night, Kristoff JT Signature Series is guaranteed to be a flavorful gem that provides a smoking experience you won’t forget.

Kristoff is a super-premium cigar brand that competes with the likes of Arturo Fuente and Davidoff. Usually known for their mind-blowing full-bodied blends, Kristoff Kristania is a departure. Made in the Dominican Republic, Kristania is a wonderful medium-bodied, maybe just slightly higher, smoke with Dominican Habano filler and binder tobacco wrapped in a dark and oily Nicaraguan Criollo wrapper. While most Kristoff cigars need to be reserved for after dinner, this one is perfect for a mid-day smoke and will never overpower. Like all Kristoff cigars, the Kristania Band is very indistinct and almost matches the wrapper, making it camouflaged against the cigar. The Nicaraguan Criollo wrapper has a very mottled appearance and is not something that is overtly beautiful. But as they say, beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and we don't buy cigars to just look at them any way. While there is some spice in the initial puffs, this quickly subsided to reveal a cocoa and cedar core. This densely packed smoke had an easy draw and seemed to last forever. Kristoff Kristania is a cigar more for the medium-bodied cigar fan than the powerhouses the brand is known. If you are already a Kristoff fan, Kristania would be a perfect change of pace, or a cigar that can be smoked all day. We enjoyed ours with our mid-morning coffee and it really hit the spot. For something more powerful, give the Kristoff Ligero a try.

We're always on the lookout for the next great cigar no matter the price, and we're thrilled to be able to offer the delectable Kristoff Kristania Maduro as your next daily indulgence. Following on the success of the original Kristania, brand owner Glen Case entrusted the crack team of skilled torcedors at the Dominican-based Charles Fairmorn factory to further enrich the already well-loved blend. This was accomplished by swapping in a supremely oily and toothy Brazilian Arapiraca Maduro wrapper to coat the rich Dominican Habano longleaf tobacco employed as filler and binder. The result is an affordable medium-bodied stogie to be enjoyed on a regular basis. This is a refined and aromatic vitola displaying expert construction with an elegant triple cap to either reveal or conceal the thickly bunched filler within, respectively. Clipped with a sharp blade and lit by a strong flame, the Kristania Maduro releases lush velvety smoke filled with the flavors of semi-sweet cocoa, black pepper, espresso, sweet vanilla cream, orange peel, and a touch of toasted coconut. Satisfying without being overwhelming, you'll be reaching for another soon enough. Good thing these fine handmade stogies are so affordable because you'll want some on hand at all times. The only thing that might help keep a few Kristoff Kristania Maduros in your humidor is having some other equally dark, delicious, and delightful goodies to keep your palate occupied. Options include the Four Kicks Maduro, the Alec Bradley Project 40 Maduro, and the La Gloria Classic Maduro.

If you like cigars with a blast of spice and power, Kristoff Ligero Criollo is a perfect addition to your humidor. A rare powerhouse from the Dominican Republic, this smoke has Dominican and Honduran fillers followed by a Dominican binder. The beauty of the Kristoff Ligero Criollo is in the wrapper. A gorgeous Honduran Criollo leaf with barely a vein to be seen. A deep chocolate brown tobacco leaf that borders on a maduro in hue leaves a slight spice on the lips which is very pleasant. A wonderful full-bodied smoke, this cigar is not for the light-hearted. The exterior of this cigar has no bearing on the complexity found within its leaves. The filler is made up of delicious Cuban Seed Dominican and Honduran ligero, giving this stogie a blast of spice which never lets up from foot-to-nub. What is most surprising is that the powerful pepperiness never overcomes all the other wonderful flavors this cigar presents to your palate. We noticed definite cedar and leather notes lingering after the spice subsided with each puff. Do you love full-bodied cigars or possibly want to step up the flavor profile in what you normally smoke? Kristoff's Ligero Criollo is a fantastic cigar to add to your arsenal, especially at its fantastic price-point. Due to the strength of this beast, we recommend it as a nice after-dinner smoke following a large dinner with a nice glass of port. Another great smoke with a similar flavor is the CAO Criollo.

Kristoff Ligero is a powerful line of cigars which uses twice the strong ligero tobacco as their normal line. A Dominican made beauty, the core of this cigar is Dominican and Honduran tobacco and a binder of Cuban-seed Dominican. The maduro wrapper is an almost black, striking Brazilian maduro leaf. An oily appearance greets the smoker at first glance and a strong cocoa and cedar aroma is present before the flame is ever introduced. While the Criollo of this line is closer to the full-bodied end of the spectrum, Kristoff Ligero Maduro is more in the middle of the medium-to-full-bodied scale. A dark brown band almost blends perfectly in with the hue of the wrapper leaf, and a secondary band lets the smoker know it is a maduro, if the dark color wasn't a first hint. Where the Criollo of this line had a spicy blast at first, the Maduro was a much more subtle first puff. The more we smoke, the more flavors and complexities come through. Strongly prevalent throughout this cigar were tastes of dark chocolate and espresso. The fantastic sweetness found in a Kristoff Ligero Maduro is a welcome change of pace from the Criollo version of this same cigar. Still present is the pepperiness, but it is overwhelmed with the cocoa and coffee overtones. Still much higher than a medium-bodied, Kristoff Ligero Maduro is the perfect cigar to enjoy with a dessert or an after dinner cordial. If spice is what you are looking for, the Ligero Criollo will be right up your alley or a Tatuaje Miami.

Known mostly for their spicy and full-bodied smokes, Kristoff Maduro is a wonderful variation. Made in the Dominican Republic with a wonderful blend of well-aged Dominican and Nicaraguan long-filler and a Dominican binder, the key to this cigar's flavor is a super dark and oily Brazilian maduro wrapper. The Maduro has the same construction and flavor that fans of the brand have come to expect. Despite the rich maduro wrapper, this stick is just a hair above a medium body. As with all Kristoff cigars, the Maduro has a very understated band, but due to the dark nature of the wrapper, this one does not blend in. Pre-light inspection revealed a flawless wrapper that appeared almost seamless. A densely packed cigar, there was a sweet almost chocolaty aroma before lit. After the first few draws, which were effortless, this sweet flavor continued and mixed with a slightly bitter espresso note. From foot to nub, this smoked easily and straight with the same flavor profile carried right through to the end. Kristoff Maduro is a wonderful change of pace from the other cigars of this brand. The sweetness is a wonderful addition and never off-putting. The chocolate and coffee notes paired with a nice after dinner drink such as a Sambuca. For other cigars in this profile we would suggest the CAO La Traviata Maduro.

Kristoff Pistoff is a firecracker of a cigar that might just get under your skin a little bit! Since the inception of Kristoff cigars in 2004, brand owner Glen Case has been making leaps and bounds, bringing up the Kristoff brand as one of the largest, most recognized boutique brands in the business. This latest release, Kristoff Pistoff, is perhaps the brand's strongest blend to date, aimed at fans of powerhouse sticks that just want a bit more out of their cigars. Well, this is the answer! Built in the Dominican Republic, Pistoff consists of a hearty blend of double- and triple-fermented Nicaraguan filler tobacco, an Indonesian binder, and a spicy Mexican San Andres wrapper. Aged to meld the flavors just right, the final result is the first powerhouse cigar from the Kristoff Cigar Company, and it is a darned good one at that. Rated 91 by Cigar Journal as a best buy cigar. Oily, dark, and rustic in appearance, Kristoff Pistoff is a beautiful specimen of a cigar. The best part is that it tastes even better than it looks! A spicy opening of white pepper greets the palate upon first light. This heavy pepper remains in the background throughout the smoking experience. Following is a bouquet of chocolate, toffee, nuts, and a hint of licorice . The finish is sweet and thick, tying the whole package together. Full-bodied may just be an understatement on this one.

An everyday smoke that feels just as at home at the yacht club as it does on the back porch, the Kristoff Premium Selection bundled cigars proves that not all bundled cigars are created equal. While many bargain sticks use low-grade or leftover tobaccos, Kristoff maintains its reputation for quality by crafting even its budget cigars with well-fermented, premium leaves. Each cigar features a blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers bound by a Dominican binder. The Natural version is wrapped in a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut, while the Maduro uses a dark and flavorful Brazilian wrapper. Despite their affordable price point, these Kristoff cigars deliver quality construction. Expect a rustic appearance with the occasional vein or blemish, but rest assured that performance and flavor remain uncompromised. The draw is easy, producing clouds of rich, flavorful smoke. The Natural wrapper offers a mild, creamy profile with smooth tobacco notes , while the Maduro leans fuller-bodied with flavors of coffee bean, cedar, and sweet chocolate . For cigar lovers seeking budget-friendly Dominican cigars without sacrificing quality, the Kristoff Premium Selection is a must-try. Ideal for fishing trips, golf outings, backyard barbecues, or even a special occasion, these bundled cigars deliver exceptional value with classic Kristoff flavor. Stock up today and enjoy one of the best cigar deals available.

New for 2015 from a rapidly rising star in the boutique cigar world is the fantastic Kristoff San Andres . After quietly building a cult following over many years, and racking up 90-plus ratings like it's the easiest thing ever, Kristoff and their stellar stable of blends are getting noticed more and more by aficionados tired of being disappointed by marketing hype. These smokes are the real deal. Crafted in the Dominican Republic, the name comes from the Mexican San Andres wrapper, which many of you should recognize as one of the most popular tobacco for Maduros in recent years. For good reason, too, because it adds a gorgeous sweet and spicy flavor to the Ecuadorian Habano binder and triple-fermented Nicaraguan Habano filler. The Kristoff San Andrés Robusto earned high acclaim in the industry when it was officially named the #13 Cigar of 2016 by Cigar Journal , with judges specifically praising its "complex and harmonious" profile and exceptional value. The simple brown and gold band promises 'Elite Cuban Taste', and while this is certainly a bold claim, we know you'll be completely satisfied whether you're able to make the comparison or not. Awash with thick smoke, your palate will delight in the coffee and crème brulee that accompany the black pepper and rich earthiness forming the foundation of the flavor profile. Bittersweet mocha and sweet spices flow freely during the steady second half of the stick, culminating in a medium-full finish as cool and smooth as the beginning. The Kristoff San Andres is an impressive smoke to behold after breaking the seal. You're certain to be even more enthralled once you are actually smoking one, so don't be surprised when you go reaching for another soon after. Surprisingly affordable for a cigar of this caliber, you'll soon be returning to explore more of Kristoff's fine smokes. Guaranteed.

Kristoff Shade Grown is among the most recent releases from Kristoff Cigars out of the Dominican Republic. For years, Kristoff Cigars has been hanging in the background of the cigar industry, mainly supported by somewhat of a cult following. It seems like the brand gets bigger and bigger every year, with new blend after new blend coming out on a fairly regular basis. As for this Shade Grown blend, it is said that it’s actually a re-release of what was once known as Kristoff Britannia, a line that came out over a decade ago. Regardless of whether or not that is the case, Kristoff Shade Grown is a solid blend, made at the Charles Fairmorn Factory in The Dominican Republic using Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers, a Dominican binder, and a Connecticut Seed wrapper leaf from Honduras. This blend is unique in that despite the fact that it uses a Connecticut Seed wrapper, it is far from what many would consider to be mild. Kristoff Shade Grown begins with a deep, earthy flavor that remains until the end of the cigar. Creamy sweetness hangs in the background, along with hints of nuts and meaty undertones. Black pepper ties the package together, along with some cayenne on the finish. This is certainly not a typical “shade grown” cigar, as the body is heavy and the flavors are quite bold. After all is said and done, this is a firm medium-full-bodied cigar. Kristoff cigars are made for a particular audience, though this blend should be well-accepted by the majority of cigar fanatics. The flavor profile is simple, and though a bit on the strong side, it is nothing overpowering or too intense. Kristoff Shade Grown pairs well with dark beer, red wine, or coffee, and is comparable to fuller-bodied Connecticut blends such as Camacho Connecticut and Liga Undercrown Shade . Whether you are a long-time fan of Kristoff cigars or just want something new and different, Kristoff Shade Grown makes a great choice.

The Kristoff Sumatra is a medium-bodied cigar with woody, grassy, sweet dried fruit, spice, and cinnamon flavors blended with a smooth sweet touch of leather. The spices in this stick have a tendency to sit at the back of your throat throughout the smoke. The Kristoff Sumatra is constructed with Cuban seed Dominican and Cuban seed Nicaraguan long fillers, Brazilian binders and Ecuadorian Sumatra wrappers. The Kristoff Sumatra wrapper is rough, thick-veined, and reminds me of an old, well-loved, dark brown leather recliner. The Kristoff Sumatra burns evenly, though VERY SLOWLY. The smoke is thin and the draw can be tight if you try to rush through this one.

One of the two value brands to come out, of the newly formed L'Atelier company, the El Suelo cigar is the one that tacks more towards owner Pete Johnson's natural talents. Fans of Tatuaje cigars know that Pete loves bolder cigars, and that's just what the El Suelo offers to the bargain-conscious smoker. Add in the fact that the cigars are blended by Jaime Garcia and rolled in his My Father factory and you've got a winner you'll be happy to smoke whenever the urge hits. And why not? With a prime mix of fine Nicaraguan leaf and Connecticut Broadleaf as the filler, and an additional Broadleaf as the binder, this Ecuadorian Habano-wrapped beauty is as long on quality as it is short on cost. (See more L'Atelier cigars ) If the goal was to create a Tatuaje-style cigar that anyone could afford, where the first plumes of smoke are thick with familiar Pepin spice before becoming loaded with leather and coffee and a mineral earthiness, then Pete Johnson has met that objective. If all he was looking to do was create a delicious stick that aficionados could call upon when they needed a reliable daily smoke with a medium to full body and a plethora of tastes, then he has exceeded all expectations. If you like the El Suelo, make sure to try the Gran Habano Azteca Fuerte for more full-bodied enjoyment.

The limited-edition L'Atelier Côte d'Or 2017 (French for "gold coast") has returned for the third year in a row, featuring the same rare tobaccos and small production run as its predecessors. This cigar is draped in a dark, Ecuadoran leaf that L'Atelier calls Sancti Spiritus, a hybrid of Criollo and Pelo de Oro tobaccos. The cigar also contains Nicaraguan binder and filler leaf, with a small amount of Pelo de Oro tobacco incorporated into the filler, cultivated on the Garcia family farms in Nicaragua. (See more L'Atelier cigars )

You must know when Pete Johnson and Don Pepin get together to craft a cigar, it's going to be something special, and the L'Atelier Maduro just might be the one they were destined to create all along. Now, there were a few others experienced tobacco purveyors that partnered with Pete, and Señor Garcia's involvement is mainly through having each vitola rolled at his Esteli-based My Father Cigars, but the effect is much the same as their previous collaborations: Spectacular flavor, superb construction, and an experience like none other. To accomplish this, Johnson and Co. selected a gorgeous Connecticut Broadleaf to coat the same world-class Nicaraguan filler from the original L'Atelier. (See more L'Atelier cigars ) One of the main goals when creating the L'Atelier line was to come up with a profile unlike any of those Johnson had released before. Once you savor the taste and aroma of this Maduro, we think you'll agree that they have exceeded all expectations. Dry yet citrus-sweet with the first puffs, there is a deeper layer of cocoa and leather to be found just shy of the second third. Seemingly emboldened by your commitment to approach the nub, the thick smoke stops pulling punches halfway in with an ever richer complexity, though the strength remains medium-full. Expect tons of savory goodness, with spices, cedar, graham cracker, black pepper, and smoky char, all available in droves.

L'Atelier Lat 46 Selection Speciale is the latest cigar in the award-winning L'Atelier core series lineup. However, it is not technically part of the core series per se, but rather its own unique blend, the one thing setting it apart from the others being a more mature, higher-priming wrapper leaf. Made in Nicaragua at the world-famous My Father factory under the supervision of Don Pepin Garcia and company, Lat 46, like the rest of the L'Atelier cigars, is part of the Tatuaje brand and was introduced by brand owner "Tattoo" Pete Johnson. (See more L'Atelier cigars ) The blend of Lat 46 is mostly the same as the other L'Atelier core cigars: Nicaraguan fillers, a Nicaraguan binder, and a golden brown Ecuadorian wrapper leaf. This rare, yet up-and-coming wrapper leaf is grown on the Oliva farms using hybrid seeds from the Garcias. In the case of Lat 46, this Ecuadorian wrapper, known as Sancti Spiritus, is harvested from a higher priming of the plant, yielding richer, fuller flavor and a stronger overall feel. At 5 5/8" x 46, this corona gorda is one heck of a firecracker, and it is a darned tasty one for sure. Dark, golden brown and oily tobacco glistens under the simple, yet elegant band. With a Cuban-style pigtail cap and seamless construction, Lat 46 is as beautiful as it is delicious. A firm, yet very generous draw offers thick plumes of the heavy blue smoke so familiar with cigars from the My Father factory. The opening light-up is a trademark of sorts from the Garcia family as well, as the palate is greeted with a massive burst of spicy white pepper. In the case of Lat 46, this dosage of pepper remains throughout the smoke. Nutty, creamy flavors develop as the cigar progresses, along with a core of earthy tobacco goodness. A spicy finish and some hints of sweetness round out the profile, making this full-bodied treat a true classic of what the My Father factory has to offer. Tatuaje, My Father, L'Atelier, you name it. If it is made with the names Don Pepin or Pete Johnson behind it, it is no beginner cigar. This particular stick should dwell in the humidors of only the most experienced connoisseurs, as not only will beginners fail to appreciate the complexity of the blend, but the strength will simply be too much. However, for the right aficionado, Lat 46 is nothing short of an absolute gem. It leaves nothing to be desired and will satisfy just about any experienced palate to the fullest. Lat 46 is a classic Nicaraguan bomb of a cigar and pairs nicely with scotch or bourbon, and is best enjoyed after a meal. Regarding stature and flavor profile, those wanting a similar experience to that of the Lat 46 should check out the original My Father line, as well as the original Tatuaje series. Lat 46 is no doubt destined to become something huge, just like anything else that comes through the doors of the My Father Factory. If you have a taste for the more elegant things in life, get your hands on a L'Atelier Lat 46 today.

If you've ever wanted one of those secret-blend, limited-edition cigars that come out every so often but never wanted to pay the buyer's premium, then the L'Atelier Surrogates line is for you. Tatuaje's Pete Johnson, from within the halls of his new L'Atelier company, has created a frontmark where each vitola contains a different recipe of aged long-leaf while being offered at a price that makes every day a special cigar day. The Skull Breaker and Bone Crusher are different takes on Nicaraguan filler and Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, while the Crystal Baller is covered in a Habano and the Tramp Stamp in an Oscuro, both from Ecuador. (See more L'Atelier cigars ) Each L'Atelier Surrogates cigar is an invitation to an exclusive club you never thought you'd be able to join. You can't go wrong with whichever size you choose, but we do recommend trying them all and deciding which is your favorite. Once you've narrowed it down, which will no doubt be a tough choice to make, grab a box or two. At these prices, how can you afford not to?

The L'Atelier Trocadero is a mild to medium, everyday value cigar brought to you by the same man who has built the famed Tatuaje from an obscure boutique brand into one of the biggest names in flavorful and highly-rated smokes. Pete Johnson, in continual partnership with the Pepin family of My Father Cigars since 2003, has blended world-class stogies of all styles and prices and now he brings his particular brand of magic to the masses with a tasty cigar packed into mazos of 20 and priced to sell. And it's not just cheap, it's delicious. How could it not be, with fine Nicaraguan long-leaf filler beneath a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and Habano Rosado wrapper from Ecuador? (See more L'Atelier cigars ) Once lit the flavors of the cigar are reminiscent of the Havana IV but with a softer, more rounded approach to the familiar Pepin spice, plus additional hints of cocoa and earth. Created to give hope to those who are looking for affordable stogies that will still satisfy day in and day out, the L'Atelier Trocadero is destined to find a spot in many a humidor. As the cigar-buying landscape has changed with the times, there are many brands putting out bundled cigars with a quality and depth of flavor unimaginable just a few short years ago. Think Toraño Brigade or Casa Blanca. Pete Johnson's arrival means the trend will continue, which is good news for all.

La Aroma de Cuba Connecticut is the seventh addition to the world famous La Aroma de Cuba series from Ashton Cigars. Years in the making, this long-awaited release appeals to fans of classic sticks that reside on the milder side but still offer plenty of flavor and complexity, a breed that seems to have gone by the wayside in today’s ever-growing cigar industry. Like all La Aroma de Cuba cigars, this one is made at the state-of-the-art My Father factory in Nicaragua under the supervision of Jose “Don” Pepin Garcia. The blend is a simple and straightforward recipe of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco beneath a golden Connecticut wrapper grown in Ecuador. This seems like a recipe we have seen in so many cigars throughout the years, yet in the case of La Aroma de Cuba Connecticut, something just seems to be so much better. This seems to be a popular opinion, as soon after this blend was released, it promptly earned a series of 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado, the best being a rock-solid 92. (Shop other La Aroma de Cuba Cigars ) From the classic dress box to the embellished band, we have all come to know and love, La Aroma de Cuba Connecticut has some serious good looks to go with its amazing flavor profile. The construction leaves nothing to be desired, as the luxurious draw offers billowing clouds of flavorful smoke on each and every puff. From first light, the woody core of the flavor profile establishes its dominance, as sweet cedar becomes the star of the show. Hints of vanilla, sweet cream, and citrus all make appearances along the way, and a solid dose of spicy white pepper brings the whole package together. Mild-medium-bodied with a clean finish, this cigar is sure to bring back many memories of the Connecticut-wrapped masterpieces of the old days. This blend is mild-medium-bodied and easy on the palate. It’s safe to say just about anyone can enjoy it to the fullest. However, those with well-developed palates will surely be impressed at just how flavorful such an easy-going cigar can be. This blend pairs well with medium-bodied beer, white wine, or cognac and is suitable for any occasion, at any time of the day. The thing with Connecticut cigars is that they are so versatile and never over-powering, so you can even feel free to light one up first thing in the morning, knowing that your day is going to start off on the right foot. Fans of classics such as Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real or Perdomo Champagne will definitely find this blend to be nothing less than incredible. There is a vast array of options in the La Aroma de Cuba lineup, and a variation for just about any palate. La Aroma de Cuba Connecticut finishes off the spectrum beautifully, offering a delightfully mild and flavorful package at a wonderful price point.

Ashton introduced La Aroma de Cuba Edicion Especial in 2008 to go along with the original and the Mi Amor line of the very popular cigar series. Fans of both of those other iterations are in for a treat with this one. Made by the Garcia family in their famed Nicaraguan factory, La Aroma de Cuba Edicion Especial has full flavored Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco and an exquisite sun grown Ecuadorian wrapper. It is this wrapper which causes an increased rush of flavor and spice, as well as a fantastic earthiness. The blend of tobaccos used on the Edicion Especial offer a complexity of flavors expected from a Garcia made cigar. (Shop other La Aroma de Cuba Cigars ) The band is a beautiful yellow and gold accented with a secondary smaller red band with the simple lettering of EE. A wonderful medium brown wrapper leaf with minimal veins and a virtually invisible seam , the burn was fantastic and it held the ash very well. We used our trusty punch on this one and the draw was as smooth as can be. First light provided the spiciness expected from a Garcia cigar but this smoothed out with each subsequent puff. A creaminess comes out in the final act of the Edicion Especial which was unexpected but very welcome. La Aroma de Cuba Edicion Especial is a cigar worthy of both the Garcia and Ashton names. A fantastic construction and wonderful taste came through with each draw. Some may feel his is a medium-to-full body smoke, but we found it more in the medium range, especially when the creamy final third of the cigar kicked in. Perfectly paired with a pinot grigio or lighter beer, this is a perfect addition to any humidor. The original La Aroma de Cuba as well as Mi Amor are also fantastic smokes.

When it comes to award-winning cigars, the Garcia family are no slouches, and La Aroma De Cuba Mi Amor is just one of many in their arsenal. Made for Ashton in the My Father factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, the Mi Amor line was crafted as the maduro extension of the well-regarded La Aroma De Cuba brand, which was introduced in 2002. This full-flavored cigar is squarely in the medium-bodied range. The best Nicaraguan tobaccos are used for the binder and filler, but the real star is the Mexican Cuban-seed Maduro wrapper. The level of flavor and smoothness this tobacco brings is nothing short of astounding. (Shop other La Aroma de Cuba Cigars ) Many cigars in this blend have received multiple 90+ ratings, with the La Aroma de Cuba Mi Amor Belicoso earning a 95-point rating and being named the #9 Cigar of the Year for 2023 by Cigar Aficionado , highlighting its rich, complex flavor and expert craftsmanship. Banded with the classic La Aroma De Cuba band, there is a secondary band informing you it is a Mi Amor. Besides the additional band, the most striking thing is the wrapper leaf. Very dark brown and with almost no veins to speak of, we knew right away we were in for a treat. First light introduced our palate to a very slight tinge of spice, as is the case with most Garcia-made cigars, but this quickly subsided into a smooth creaminess. There was definitely a slight sweetness on the lips, but nothing too powerful. Most striking was the change in strength while smoking. What started as a full-on, medium-bodied cigar grew in strength with each third. Never getting too strong; La Aroma De Cuba Mi Amor ended up just a hair over the medium-body line. Another thing to note is the amazing construction. Burning straight as an arrow, we were able to keep the ash in place until almost the band. La Aroma De Cuba Mi Amor is a medium-bodied masterpiece perfect for everyone's humidor. The subtleties and increasing strength and flavor made this a perfect cigar for the morning. Paired perfectly with our morning cup of coffee, we were ready to start our day after enjoying this on our deck. For a slightly different flavor profile, we would also recommend the regular La Aroma De Cuba.

From the same minds and master blenders that brought us the La Aroma De Cuba and La Aroma De Cuba Mi Amor, Pepin Garcia and his son Jaime have another cigar befitting the taste and quality of the brand, La Aroma De Cuba Reserva . Made in the flagship My Father factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, the Garcia family pulled no punches with this beauty. Filled and bound with only the best, aged Nicaraguan tobacco, the key to the Mi Amor Reserva is the gorgeous Mexican oscuro wrapper. A traditional box-pressed cigar, this full-bodied smoke has rich flavors that will make you want to have another. (Shop other La Aroma de Cuba Cigars ) This blend reached the pinnacle of critical acclaim by being named one of the Top 25 Cigars of the Year by Cigar Aficionado in 2013 and subsequently earning a prestigious 94-rating in early 2014. It stands as a testament to the Garcia family’s blending prowess, offering a rich, full-bodied experience that remains incredibly smooth and balanced from start to finish. The well-known La Aroma De Cuba band is augmented with a band of red and gold, letting us know it is a Mi Amor Reserva. Without this band we would still know we we were in for something a little more special though. The deep, chocolatey-brown oscuro wrapper is something that needs to be seen. Pre-light, the wrapper left a slight sweetness on the lips, but post flame it was all about the spice. Never overpowering, the signature Pepin spice was always present, but so were tastes of cedar and a slight cocoa finish. One of the most astonishing things was how well this cigar held onto its ash. If we didn't tip it every so often, it seemed that ash would hold on until the very last puff. With its peppery core, yet sweet finish, La Aroma De Cuba Reserva is a cigar that needs to be experienced by everyone who loves full-bodied smokes. That unique flavor pairing went extremely well with a nice smoked brisket and a cool IPA. For different flavors but the same quality, you can not go wrong with either the La Aroma De Cuba or My Father cigars from the same factory.

La Aroma De Cuba is a cigar made for Ashton at the famed My Father factory in Nicaragua by Don Pepin Garcia. When Ashton was opening its first cigar bar in Philadelphia, it was looking to have a cigar that was an exclusive. La Aroma De Cuba Noblesse fits the bill perfectly. This cigar was so well received by bar patrons, that Ashton has decided to release this cigar publicly but on a very limited basis. This unique cigar is unlike any La Aroma De Cuba you have had before.

It took Ashton Cigars half a decade to introduce a new addition to their already world-class portfolio, but when La Aroma de Cuba Pasion hit the scene, the cigar world realized it was well worth the wait. The product of father-son team Jaime and Don Pepin Garcia of My Father Cigars, La Aroma de Cuba Pasion is the very first Nicaraguan Puro to wear a La Aroma de Cuba band. This means all tobacco used for this cigar is grown, cultivated, harvested, and cured in Nicaragua—wrapper, filler, and binder. We all know Nicaraguan puros are some of the best sticks around, but this one takes things up a notch. The unique wrapper leaf used for Pasion is a shade grown Nicaraguan leaf hailing from the Garcia family farms in Namanji, just East of Esteli. This region is about as ideal as it gets for growing tobacco, as the warm days, cool nights, and natural cloud cover shielding the area from the hot Nicaraguan sun lends to tobacco that is nothing but the best of the best. The Garcias obviously hit this one out of the ballpark, as it was promptly awarded a rock-solid 94 rating by Cigar Aficionado. (Shop other La Aroma de Cuba Cigars ) The clean, crisp packaging includes a luxurious white chest and ornate green and gold bands on each expertly rolled vitola. Speaking of construction, it is exactly what one would expect from something coming out of the world famous My Father factory, including a sharp burn, a long, tight ash, and a productive draw that paints the palate with each and every puff. Cedar is the main note at first light, soon followed by a sweet array of caramel, molasses, and nuts. The earthy core soon becomes the standout of the flavor profile, with bursts of white pepper between each puff. The finish is smooth, sweet, and spicy, and after all is said and done, this stick finishes smack dab between medium and full-bodied. A connoisseur's cigar to the "T," Pasion is blended for the experienced. The complex flavor profile, satisfying strength and body, and uncanny balance make this a cigar for those who have been there and done that, so to speak. Pasion pairs well with bourbon, red wine, or coffee, and makes for a wonderful celebration cigar. Similar sticks may include Flor de Las Antillas or My Father La Opulencia , two of the Garcia's other notable award-winning masterpieces. It was a long time coming, but La Aroma de Cuba Pasion is finally here, and if you are a fan of top shelf premium cigars, we are absolutely certain you'll love it!

Litto Gomez has been churning out cigar hits for over twenty years now, a remarkable achievement eclipsed only by the succulent new release created to celebrate this milestone: the La Flor Dominicana 1994. For those of you doing the math, yes it's true that LFD wasn't founded until '96 but this new smoke is meant to commemorate an earlier moment when Litto bravely leapt into the deep end of the cigar biz. Though that initial foray would last just a couple of years, it would lead directly to the La Flor we know and love today. Can you imagine a world where this didn't happen? Inconceivable is the nightmare scenario where Gomez's Dominican-based La Canela farm never became responsible for some of the best tobaccos ever tasted. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) Joyfully, our reality is a place where those lush soils provide for a wealth of luscious filler and binder jammed into each stick. An oily Mexican San Andres has been laid over the top to further smooth and refine the ligero-heavy blend found in each of the four LFD 1994 vitolas, plus it has the added benefit of providing a seamless appearance and a hefty barnyard aroma to the whole affair. From the outset, expect each richly rewarding draw to load the palate with a meaty earthiness spiked with black pepper and carrying a bundle of leather and cedar and cream. The glistening wrapper makes its presence known during the second half of the smoke, where a touch of stone fruit sweetness and plateau of strength at medium-full makes for a long, slow slide into happiness. Daily go-to or special occasion luxury? A seemingly easy enough question that will go right out the window the first time you light one up. You don't have to decide now so go ahead and grab some La Flor Dominicana 1994 to smoke at your earliest chance. We'll be here with more when you get back.

As the saying goes, true classics never get old, and in the world of cigars, this is personified by masterpieces like La Flor Dominicana Air Bender . Created by world-renowned blender and cigar maker Litto Gomez , this incredible example of tobacco art is crafted by loving hands at his own Tabacalera La Flor in the Dominican Republic. Built for power and velvety smoothness, Air Bender consists of a rich blend of estate grown Dominican filler and binder tobacco wrapped in a beautiful Habano leaf grown in the volcanic soil of Ecuador. Being a part of the celebrated LFD family is no small thing, but Air Bender has more than proved itself over the years, earning spots on no less than 3 separate Cigar Aficionado Top 25 lists and a slew of 90+ ratings that is too big to count, the highest being a phenomenal 94. Made for true connoisseurs, Air Bender takes everything you already know and love about La Flor Dominicana to an entirely new level. The unmistakable LFD logo forms the centerpiece of the black, red, and gold band, one that has become somewhat of an icon in the world of premium cigars over the years. Construction is impeccable, with each stick offering a smooth and productive draw and every flake of ash holding tight until properly knocked off. The silky blue smoke offers an initial blast of red pepper and sweet cedar . This paves the way for the backbone of earthy Dominican raw tobacco flavor that is wonderfully speckled with hints of cinnamon and black cherry . The finish is smooth and sweet, pulling everything together with a final dose of honey off the tip of the tongue. Complex, full-bodied , and incredibly satisfying, Air Bender demonstrates every quality an ultra-premium cigar could possibly include. By no means a beginners’ cigar, Air Bender is meant for the experienced . Full-bodied, rich, complex, and incomprehensibly balanced, this package requires a well-seasoned palate, a patient tempo, and someone who can tolerate a classic powerhouse cigar. Similar to the infamous Double Ligero series, Air Bender pairs beautifully with scotch, bourbon, cognac, or your favorite full-bodied beer, but make sure to smoke it on a full stomach. Who would have thought that nearly two decades after its debut, it would still be one of the most sought-after Dominican cigars on the market? Not only has it stood the test of time, Air Bender has proven that when a cigar is made with the utmost passion and enthusiasm, failure is never even a possibility. Enjoy one of the great cigars of our time and savor the strong side of Dominican cigars with La Flor Dominicana Air Bender.

La Flor Dominicana Air Bender Maduro used to be a limited release cigar that only came in a humidor style box which looked like a curing barn. The former Casa de Tobacco was a cigar made for anyone looking for a little more flavor than what was already in the flavorful Air Bender. For the first time ever, Litto decided to use a dark and hearty Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over the normal Dominican Air Bender binders and fillers. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) The dark Ecuadorian Habano has a great amount of reds, a good sign this is going to be strong and flavorful, which is classic Litto. It lives up to the hype as this is easily one of the most flavor LFDs of all time with notes of earth, cedar, espresso, chocolates, grass and even a bit of floral notes, all with a pepper that you'd expect from Litto Gomez and the Tabacalera La Flor factory. While the strength isn't immediately there, pretty quickly you know where the Casa de Tobaco stands: full strength, full flavor and full body. For those that wanted a bit more in every category from the popular La Flor Dominicana Air Bender, here's your answer in all its glory.

Cigar Aficionado Top 25 Cigars of 2016 - #1 - Rated 96! Imagine yourself a matador standing in a large bullring in the South of Spain; a crowd of rousing cigars from around the world filling the stands and vying for your attention when from behind you feel the hot breath of the LFD Andalusian Bull breathing down your neck. Turning slowly with cape in hand, you find yourself in the shadows of the #1 cigar of 2016, an imposing beast of a stick birthed by the hands of Litto Gomez within his legendary Tabacalera La Flor factory. A ruddy, nearly impenetrable Ecuadorian Corojo hide protects the slightly more delicate Dominican Criollo '98 and Pelo de Oro within, and you have no choice but to strike your lighter and press the attack. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) A tapered 6 1/2" inch figurado, reaching a full 64-ring gauge at the foot, the La Flor Dominicana Andalusian Bull unique shape is based on an old cigar mold found during travels through Belgium. The green and gold band, with its torero silhouette and Picasso's script, hearkens back to Gomez's Spanish homeland, but the cigar's heart dwells firmly in the New World. Freshly lit, rich dark chocolate and smooth, creamy leather will pour out of the barrel to signal the beginning of the struggle you will wage against near-overwhelming flavor. Throughout the two-and-a-half-hour experience, you will dig deep into thick layers of black pepper, aged hickory, and loamy earth underlying more subtle orange peel, burnt sugar, buttercream, and mint overtones showered down on your palette like bundles of flowers to the arena floor. A feeling of supreme satisfaction will wash over you as you finally lay down a still-smoldering LFD Andalusian Bull for the final time. You will have conquered a cigar few others get to experience, due to their scarcity and habit of flying off the shelves at the slightest provocation. It would behoove you to grab them right now if in stock, or you will end up running the streets in a futile search for more.

Cameroon wrapped cigars are not nearly as fashionable as they used to be, but don't tell that to a La Flor Dominicana Cameroon Cabinet. All it knows and cares about is delivering consistent flavor and satisfaction, the same qualities it's been dishing out since launching in 2007 and which led to Top 25 honors as recently as 2012. This persistence of character might be due to Litto Gomez' commitment to all aspects of his creation or it could be the choice Dominican and Nicaraguan blend that forms the heart of each stogie. Either way, this is one great stick. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) Perhaps one of the reasons you don't see more Cameroon cigars is that the leaf itself, especially from a higher priming like this one, is not particularly attractive, with some noticeable veins and a splotchy appearance. It's also thin and delicate which means it doesn't hide underlying lumps very well and is more prone to be damaged during rolling or boxing. Despite these minor aesthetic drawbacks, the wonderfully pungent fragrance should clue you in that the LFD Cameroon Cabinet is a force to be reckoned with. The characteristic spice of the leaf, like a cross between nutmeg and clove, breaks across the palate from the moment the cigar is lit. This is followed soon after by crisp cedar, white pepper and a touch of molasses all of which lasts through to the end.
