Available in rugged boxes of fifty, there are few better ways to fill your humidor than with a collection of La Flor Dominicana Cameroon Cabinets. They pair just as well with a morning coffee as they do beside a sipped evening whiskey so you'll probably end up burning them faster than expected. Just keep an eye on your stash so you don't run out. Having to wait for your favorite smoke is not much fun.

Some people might consider Litto Gomez a one trick pony capable only of producing cigars full of Dominican tobacco that defy convention by being unusually robust and flavorful, and at first glance his La Flor Dominicana Colorado Oscuro does nothing to dispel the notion. With a little bit of investigation, however, you’ll come to realize that while this smoke is indeed similar in strength and body to many of Gomez’ other cigars (those of you familiar with his Double Ligero know what we mean) it delivers a unique experience. This is because a considerable portion of well-aged Nicaraguan longleaf has been mixed into the filler while another Nicaraguan leaf, this time a lovely and dark Habano, is utilized as a wrapper. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) LFD cigars are always well dressed, and here the Colorado Oscuro is no exception with its band embellished with gold over a deep crimson background. Slick, carrying plenty of tooth and with just a few small veins, before being lit you’ll notice the type of funky aroma found in many of Nicaragua’s best cigars. For in-the-know connoisseurs this is a good sign, one which is fulfilled as soon as the cigar is lit and the cedar and white pepper blast through an easy draw. Full bore from head to foot, you can also expect some cane syrup, citrus, and cinnamon before time runs out.

In case you've been wondering, yes, the Coronado by La Flor cigar has been MIA recently but fans of that full-bodied beast can relax because it's now back under a new name: the La Flor Dominicana Coronado. Not much of a difference we know, but it helps to emphasize the cigar's status as a valued and important part of the LFD brand. What hasn't changed is the 93-rated blend, which led the Coronado to be named as the #2 cigar of 2006. Beginning with a sultry selection of LFD's own La Canela farm-grown filler and binder tobaccos, the torcedores at La Flor seal the deal by using a Nicaraguan Habano Sun Grown wrapper grown in the Jalapa Valley by Nestor Plasencia. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) With a crowned band proudly bearing the 'LFD' logo embossed in gold on a red field, the Coronado is ruggedly handsome and sits heavy in the hand. Unlit there is a pronounced fresh hay/barnyard aroma and a draw test delivers some spice alongside the robust tobacco essences. One might not expect a company like LFD, with their reputation for strong, ligero-laden smokes, to be able to provide for more nuanced flavors but the Coronado starts out exceedingly creamy. With plenty of smooth cedar, licorice and rich milk chocolate to compliment the robust black pepper and roasted coffee that form the base profile, you'll almost forget this is a medium-full strength stick until it hits you upside the head. If you're an aficionado who likes to hang onto old sticks, now is the time to smoke your Coronado by La Flor and make room for a new collection of La Flor Dominicana Coronado's. Not only will this prove what a little aging can do to an already great stick, it will give you something to look forward to. But you might want to pick up an extra box 'cause it'll be hard to keep your hands off all of them.

The Double Ligero line from La Flor Dominicana is one of the most famous cigar brands of all time. Noted for its immense potency, renowned craftsmanship, and unique, masterfully blended flavor profile, LFD Double Ligero is an unmistakeable cigar hall-of-famer. Made in Santiago, Dominican Republic under the discretion of master blender and tobacco expert Litto Gomez, this cigar contains a rich all-ligero filler and binder blend of smooth Dominican tobacco. It is then finished with a dark Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) Opening up with a barrage of spice and cedar, the intensity of this cigar makes its presence felt early on. The flavor profile quickly turns sweet, with heavy floral notes and chocolatey undertones. It goes well with dark rum or tawny port and makes a great smoke for before bed. Comparable sticks include Air Bender and JDN Antano. La Flor Dominicana Double Ligero: A timeless masterpiece.

La Flor Dominicana Double Ligero Maduro is a powerful ultra-premium cigar from Litto Gomez and friends down in the Dominican Republic. Continuing the extremely-full-bodied trend that LFD has seemingly perfected, Double Ligero Maduro is stuffed with a rich blend of libero filler and binder tobacco from the Dominican Republic. The finishing touch is a dark Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper with intense sweetness and extreme potency. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) In fact, the La Flor Dominicana Double Ligero Chiselito Maduro earned a #21 spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 Cigars of 2024 and received a 92 rating for its intense, powerful profile and rich, concentrated flavor. Double Libero Maduro is one heck of a wild ride, bursting with relentless spice and smooth sweetness. The floral aroma fills the room as the smoker enjoys heavy notes of cocoa and honey, with a hefty dose of black pepper tickling the nose on the exhale. LFD Double Libero Maduro is not a beginner's cigar. Only seasoned connoisseurs should attempt to light up one of these flavor bombs. Ultra-potent and pairing well with strong coffee or heavy red wine, these compare to Oliva Serie V and Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970. Incredibly strong, yet mellow enough to savor.

Do you remember your first La Flor Dominicana Ligero Oscuro cigar, with all of its raw yet supple power? How from the first moment you lit that broad and well-packed foot you discovered a mouth-watering pungency that left you completely satisfied, yet somehow still wanting to light another right away? We know that lately you've been wandering the wastelands searching for a similar experience, trying cigars left and right; searching for the same savory goodness, a comparable full-bodied dream machine. Come back home and take a seat at the feast of flavor provided by aged Domincan fillers and a prime Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) Although of comparable, if not the exact same, type as found on the original La Flor Dominicana Ligero, the Ligero Oscuro's outer leaf has been further fermented until it has taken on a beautifully dark and sultry color and a smooth, pleasing aroma. Beyond aesthetic considerations, this additional aging has also imparted distinct flavor characteristics which start on your lips and reach down into the furthest reaches of your soul as you smoke. Cocoa and currant, espresso and white pepper, your taste buds will thank you from the first time those thick plumes reach your tongue to the moment one last, cool retrohale leaves you happy and relaxed. First and foremost, a solid handmade built to find favor with smokers who prefer things a bit on the heavy side, the second best thing about these cigars is how affordable they are in relation to their flavor. Packed into generous cabinet boxes of twenty-four, La Flor Dominicana Ligero Oscuro serves as a daily treat with an iced tea just as well as it does as a special occasion stalwart with a single malt Scotch. Check 'em out today.

La Flor Dominicana makes some of the best regular production cigars in the industry. Most known for both their Double Ligero and Ligero lines, if there is a brand out there more synonymous with premium full-bodied cigars, we don't know what it is. When they come out and make a limited edition stick, you know it has got to be something special. Made from unique blends and extremely well-aged tobaccos, the La Flor Dominicana Limited Edition cigars are some of the best the factory produces. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars )

la-flor-dominicana-limited-edition-chapt.name: Limited Edition Chapter One Box-Pressed Chisel

note_sources.text: La Flor Dominicana Little Cigars are amazing when you think about it. A brand best known for their big and booming flavors, being able to get all those notes into such a tiny package is the true sign of a master cigar maker. With two different varieties available, Mojito is a deep and satisfying smoke, and the Carajos feature all the power and flavor of the well-known Ligero line, just in a much smaller size. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) Too often, people who love full-bodied cigars have to sacrifice when looking for smaller cigarillos. La Flor Dominicana is here to provide the shining light for all these smokers. Each little cigar is made with the same attention to quality and flavor as their bigger siblings, just in small and concise, and economical packages. La Flor Dominicana Little Cigars are perfect for the smoker that is on the go. Packaged in small packs which are easy to throw in your pocket, you will never be without your beloved LFDs again. No matter if you have 10 minutes in between meetings or a half hour on your lunch, these little cigars are sure to fit the bill.

La Flor Dominicana Litto Gomez Diez cigars are the culmination of years of hard work and sacrifice whose resulting characteristics far exceed expectations. The man who pushed to make it all happen is none other than LFD's resident mastermind Litto Gomez, who after having already made a mark on the tobacco world with plenty of potent and flavorful smokes made the risky decision to produce a cigar unlike any he had created before. Committing himself to cultivating filler, binder, and wrapper tobaccos grown only on his Dominican La Canela farm, he would have to wait a long four years before knowing if his gamble would pay off. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) And pay off it did. From the very beginning, with its mineral aroma and toothy appearance, this is a cigar you'll be happy to hold and even more excited to light. Rich puffs of velvety smoke swirl through the palate, chock full of dark roast coffee and toasted oak. Evolving nice and slow to match the burn, some leather backed by a sweet cinnamon spice enters during an ever more powerful second third. There's still some room for subtlety during the latter stages, with toast and loamy earth evident to create a complex profile still dominated by distinct Cubanesque tastes. Like many of the more powerhouse LFD offerings available, yes we're looking at you Double Ligero, expect a La Flor Domincana Litto Gomez Diaz to start out medium to full in strength and then continue to build until it hits full stride. Somewhat limited in release, we may not have all sizes in stock at all times so when you see your favorite it is time to act. If we're out, maybe you'll have some luck scoring a box of Pinar Del Rio's Flores y Rodriguez Cabinet Selection Habano instead.

One look at its flashy gold packaging and impeccable construction, and one would argue that La Flor Dominicana Oro is brand owner Litto Gomez’s crowning achievement. Available in several sizes and presentations since its debut many years ago, this blend has earned more 90+ ratings over the years than some entire brand names. Two appearances on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 list also belong to the golden one, as well as spots on numerous other “best of” lists throughout the cigar world. A world-class blend of Gomez’s own Dominican tobacco grown on his famed La Canela farms forms the filler and binder, and a stunning and unique Nicaraguan Habano wrapper leaf finishes things off. After all is said and done, you’re left with a cigar that is as delicious as it is beautiful, and there’s no doubt that it is one of Gomez’s most potent creations to date. Each vitola is adorned with an opulent golden band, paying homage to Litto Gomez’s former days as a jeweler before entering the cigar business. The roll is nearly seamless, and the heft of the cigar leads one to believe it has been crafted by some of the best hands on the planet. Once cut and lit, this incredible gem offers a smooth and productive draw that bathes the palate in silky blue smoke. Starting off with a wave of white pepper and cedar , things soon turn sweet before the first third is complete. A hefty dose of Gomez’s trademark floral sweetness forms the backbone of the flavor profile, and a bold cascade of earthy, spicy raw tobacco flavor lies beneath. Cocoa, espresso, and cinnamon dance around on the tip of the tongue, and the finish is heavy and sweet. To call it full-bodied does it no justice. This cigar is simply powerful. Made for the most seasoned of connoisseurs, the full-bodied powerhouse that is La Flor Dominicana Oro dazzles the taste buds while providing an intense smoking experience that you will never forget. Pair this one with the finest scotch or bourbon, or enjoy it alongside a stout glass of tawny port for a full, sweet, and rich experience. Fans of the famous Double Ligero or Air Bender lines will be sure to enjoy this treat, as it seems to take all the best parts of each and combine them into one bold package. “Oro” literally translates to “Gold,” and millions of cigar connoisseurs who have compared this stick to the most precious of metals can’t be wrong. It’s not every day that you come across something like this, and these babies aren’t exactly easy to come by, so don’t hesitate today to enjoy one of the finest full-bodied cigar masterpieces with La Flor Dominicana Oro.

La Flor Dominicana Reserva Especial is a cigar that combines elegance, power, and complexity with a blend of some of the finest tobaccos in the world. Made in the Dominican Republic, LFD Reserva Especial takes a small step outside the box, so to speak, when it comes to what the company has come to be known for over the years. When you hear La Flor Dominicana, your first thought is probably ultra-full-bodied powerhouse cigars aimed at strength freaks and long-seasoned connoisseurs. In reality, you'd be pretty much right on the money! However, this Reserva Especial blend is a completely new endeavor for Litto Gomez and his highly esteemed crew at LFD Cigars. It's made up of an ultra-smooth, yet hearty, filler and binder blend of some of the highest quality tobacco the Dominican Republic has to offer. The thing that makes Reserva Especial so special, however, is the light, golden brown, silky smooth Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf, which finishes the package. You heard that right, a modern offering from La Flor Dominicana with a Connecticut wrapper. This isn't just any Connecticut cigar, however. It's so much more than that. (See more La Flor Dominicana Cigars ) With the appearance of fine leather, the glistening Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf seamlessly hugs the elegant shape of the cigar. Fine white bands further add to the opulent appearance of this superb work of tobacco art. Expert construction means a firm, yet extremely productive draw, allowing the cigar to expel copious amounts of thick, blue smoke. The initial blast of crisp white pepper soon settles to a creamy array of earthy tobacco flavor. Hints of raisin, cayenne, black cherry, and nutmeg join the mix, before a smooth, sweet finish that brings the package together beautifully. Strength is indubitably at the low end of full-bodied. La Flor Dominicana Reserva Especial is essentially a resurrected version of El Jocko, the original stick that put La Flor Dominicana on the map some two decades ago. Beginners need not apply. Don't let the Connecticut wrapper fool you—this cigar is complex, full-bodied, and highly refined, and it's likely that only seasoned connoisseurs will truly appreciate the many attributes that make it so special. LFD Reserva Especial pairs well with bourbon, scotch, and even champagne, and is best enjoyed after a good meal. Similar Connecticut-draped full-bodied beauties include Camacho Connecticut and Padron Damaso . The blend that brought La Flor Dominicana into the spotlight years ago is finally back, ready to please even the most discriminating cigar freaks across the world. La Flor Dominicana Reserva Especial is most definitely a name to remember.

Few cigars have stood the test of time like the timeless masterpiece that is La Gloria Cubana Classic. Once touted as "one of the most sought-after cigars in the world," this 92-rated gem has been around for decades and continues to arouse the palates of both long-time connoisseurs and new smokers alike. Newly renamed and flaunting updated packaging, LGC Classic was originally rolled in El Credito, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's tiny boutique in Little Havana. Now owned by Swedish Match and General Cigar, the brand is produced down in the Dominican Republic, and has expanded tremendously over the years. The same original recipe is used for the modern offering, however, with a filler blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican leaves, a Nicaraguan binder, and a gorgeous Ecuadorian wrapper. Few classic cigars have truly emulated the Cuban experience the way La Gloria Cubana Classic has, and that is doubtless a major reason it continues to be a mainstay in millions of humidors around the world. Packed in classic Cuban style cedar chests of 25, today's La Gloria Cubana Classic wears a band quite similar to the original, just with a few modern updates. One big thing La Gloria Cubana has always been known for is the impeccable construction of their cigars. This remains true for this variety, as each and every cigar is rolled to perform, offering a smooth, easy draw and plenty of smoke to provide a phenomenal smoking experience. A burst of spicy white pepper at first light soon turns into a crisp, earthy core of aged tobacco flavor spiked with hints of cinnamon and cedar. Soft floral notes adorn the clean, spicy finish, and overall La Gloria Cubana Classic finishes as a solid medium-full-bodied cigar. This cigar has lasted so long in the cigar world for a reason. It is appropriate for anyone and everyone—beginners and experienced smokers alike. Medium-full-bodied and delightfully uncomplicated, La Gloria Cubana Classic just works. It pairs well with bourbon, dark rum, or medium-bodied beer and is great for any time of the day. Fans of classic sticks such as Punch , Partagas , or Romeo y Julieta will doubtless already be acquainted with the brand, but if not, why wait to give it a try? Classic, simple, and straight-forward, La Gloria Cubana Classic may cause one to question what makes it so special. However, anyone that has tried it can tell you that there is simply nothing else like it. You just have to smoke it to understand.

When it comes to legendary maduro cigars, few stand out quite like La Gloria Cubana Classic Maduro. A dark twist on the beloved classic, LGC Classic Maduro was originally blended and crafted by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo at the tiny El Credito factory in Little Havana. Like its natural counterpart, its production has since moved to the Dominican Republic, where the majority of the now General Cigar-owned La Gloria Cubana's cigars are now rolled. It keeps the original recipe of Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers and a Nicaraguan binder, but the star of this show is the jet-black Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. For decades, La Gloria Cubana's maduro cigars have been revered as some of the best in existence, and to this day they remain somewhat of a benchmark for maduros throughout the industry. Updated packaging means plain and simple Cuban-style cedar chests and modernized Cuban-style bands bearing the respected La Gloria Cubana logo. Each and every cigar is rolled with exacting precision and offers a delightful smoking experience from start to finish, including a smooth, soft draw and razor-sharp burn line. For this Maduro variant, the core of the flavor profile is earthy raw tobacco mixed with spicy Nicaraguan pepper. Unlike the Natural version, however, this journey quickly takes a dark turn into a medley of coffee and cocoa, with nuances of bakers' spices and brown sugar. A molasses note on the finish rounds out the beautifully balanced experience, along with hints of floral notes through the nose. Medium-full-bodied, La Gloria Cubana Classic Maduro offers a true Cuban experience that is unmatched by even the most popular maduros of today. Ideal for all levels of experience, La Gloria Cubana Classic Maduro is a medium-full-bodied masterpiece that has proven itself time after time over the years. Velvety smooth and sweet, it pairs beautifully with coffee or dark beer and is a great choice for any time of the day. Fans of other classic maduro mainstays such as Punch Maduro or Arturo Fuente Maduro will most definitely find this blend to be satisfying to say the least. Whether you are new to the game or you've been smoking cigars for decades, La Gloria Cubana Classic Maduro is a timeless gem that will doubtless leave you reaching for another.

When a new cigar bears the La Gloria Cubana name, there is usually a ton of excitement that follows, and such was exactly the case when La Gloria Cubana Medio Tiempo was released. The big story with this cigar is the use of medio tiempo tobacco in the filler blend. First utilized over a decade ago in the legendary Cuban Cohiba Behike BHK, medio tiempo tobacco is the very top priming of the tobacco plant, sprouting just above the ligero leaves when the plant is exposed to direct sunlight. Only certain strains of tobacco seeds yield these thick, flavor-rich leaves, so their use in cigars is not widely popular. However, when done right, medio tiempo leaves can take the flavor profile of a cigar to an entirely new level, as proven with this particular blend. La Gloria Cubana Medio Tiempo is rolled in the Dominican Republic at the General Cigar Dominicana factory and uses an elaborate 4-country filler blend consisting of long fillers from the Dominican Republic, Honduras, Nicaragua, and the USA. The medio tiempo leaves are from USA Connecticut Habano tobacco grown specifically for this cigar. The binder is Connecticut Broadleaf from the USA and the wrapper is a dark, oily Ecuador Sumatra leaf that ties the whole package together. The band is silver, gray, and black—different from the usual bright and happy yellow La Gloria bands we have all come to know and love. The packaging is modern and clean, and the construction of each vitola is nothing short of impeccable. An easy draw yields a massive cloud of smoke with each puff, leaving no chance of missing out on all the dark, rich flavor this stick has to offer. The profile begins with a rich, dense tobacco flavor mixed with earthy sweetness and a complimenting dose of white pepper. Moving along, hints of oak and cocoa make appearances, as well as a faint touch of black cherry on the finish. Smooth, sweet, and bold, La Gloria Cubana Medio Tiempo finishes just shy of the full-bodied mark, with no shortcomings in the flavor department. This blend is a great choice for an intermediate cigar enthusiast looking to get into fuller-bodied cigars. Medium-full-bodied and displaying satisfying complexity, it should please seasoned connoisseurs as well. It pairs well with coffee or dark beer and is appropriate for any time of the day. Fans of sticks such as La Gloria Cubana Serie R or Joya de Nicaragua Antano Dark Corojo would probably come to enjoy this blend, as it displays very similar flavor characteristics with a few new twists. "Medio Tiempo" literally translates to "half time," but we promise once you try La Gloria Cubana Medio Tiempo, you will likely be wanting to smoke it ALL the time!

La Gloria Cubana Serie R Black is the bigger, badder, bolder brother to the original Serie R, a cigar that was a go-to for many a cigar smoker back in the cigar boom era. The original blend focused on rich, classic flavor and was made for a broad audience, but this blend is made for the cigar freaks that want something seriously strong. Unlike the original, Serie R Black is made in Nicaragua and is in fact a Nicaraguan puro, meaning all tobacco used in the production is grown on Nicaraguan soil. Well-aged Cuban seed filler and binder tobacco is nestled snugly beneath a gorgeous dark Nicaraguan Tapado Ligero wrapper leaf. This package is not for the faint of heart, but for La Gloria fans who crave full-bodied sticks, it's a dream-come-true. A black and silver background surrounds the all-too-familiar yellow La Gloria Cubana logo and is quite an appropriate compliment to the cigar's dark, oily wrapper leaf. Rolled with precision, this stick is built to perform, pounding the palate with rich bursts of Nicaraguan spice with each and every puff. The thick smoke holds on to the peppery core while hints of honey and cedar soon join the party. Coffee and cream round out the earthy flavor profile, and the finish is crisp and spicy. Beginning to end, Serie R Black is a genuine full-bodied cigar. While this stick is definitely not for beginners, it is a great choice for just about any fan of fuller-bodied blends. It especially has a place for intermediate level smokers looking to make the leap into stronger cigars, and the flavor profile is simple enough to appeal to just about any well-developed palate. Serie R Black pairs well with full-bodied beer or strong coffee and is best enjoyed on a full stomach. Fans of the original Serie R should no doubt appreciate this bolder take on the blend, as well as fans of strong Nicaraguan cigars such as Don Pepin Black or Oliva Serie V . For a strong and revised take on a timeless classic, La Gloria Cubana Serie R Black is a fantastic choice.

Over the years, it has become apparent that every maduro cigar La Gloria Cubana puts its name on is an instant success, and La Gloria Cubana Serie R Black Maduro is certainly no exception. When the original Serie R Black came out, the big deal was that it was a Nicaraguan puro, something unusual to the classic, beloved Dominican brand. With this maduro version, everything that made Sere R Black a special cigar is taken to an entirely new level with the use of a dark, oily Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper leaf. The filler and binder blend remains all-Nicaraguan, however, lovingly aged to produce the rich, spicy flavors that fans of Nicaraguan cigars have come to know and love. Decked out in the modern black and silver Serie R Black bands, each vitola wears a red secondary band denoting the Maduro variety. The chunky sized offerings are rolled to offer a smooth draw which produces thick clouds of dense, blue smoke. For starters, Nicaraguan pepper is the major player in the flavor profile. After the spicy foundation is laid, a beautiful medley of coffee, dark chocolate, and bakers' spices slowly presents itself across the duration of the smoking experience. A long, rich finish rounds everything out, and all-in-all Serie R Black Maduro resides on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied. Long-time fans of La Gloria Cubana will no doubt be satisfied with this delicious maduro offering, as well as just about any maduro fan looking for a fuller-bodied, spicy cigar. Medium-full-bodied, Serie R Black Maduro pairs well with coffee, dark beer, and tawny port, and makes a great way to wind down in the evening. This blend joins La Gloria Cubana Classic Maduro and La Gloria Cubana Serie R Esteli Maduro to continue the incredible maduro legacy which is one of the many things the brand has come to be known for. If you love maduro cigars, don't settle for another cookie cutter blend. Rather, grab a La Gloria Cubana Serie R Black Maduro and enjoy the spicy Nicaraguan La Gloria that everyone has been talking about!

La Gloria Cubana Serie R Esteli Maduro is one of the latest cigars to grace the ever-growing portfolio of La Gloria Cubana Cigars. Traditionally a Cuban, then Dominican brand, La Gloria Cubana has since broadened their horizons to release Nicaraguan-based sticks. This Nicaraguan blending has been hugely successful for La Gloria Cubana, earning the original Serie R Esteli a spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 list in 2014. This cigar is mostly the same blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos, but with a jet-black Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. The added character brings forth an entirely new flavor profile, appealing this time not only to fans of Nicaraguan tobacco but all you Maduro freaks as well. Keeping with tradition, Serie R Esteli Maduro is available in big, chunky sizes for fans of larger ring gauge cigars. In fact, way back when, the original Serie R was among the first cigars to introduce the big 56+ ring gauge sticks to the market. Nearly 2 decades later, Serie R Esteli Maduro is offering even bigger sizes, along with bigger flavor! This beast of a cigar begins with spicy Nicaraguan pepper across the palate. Soon, the earthy profile develops notes of cocoa and leather, soon offering a rich raw tobacco flavor. Though the Nicaraguan tobacco adds plenty of spice, the sweetness of the Connecticut Broadleaf beautifully rounds out the flavor bouquet. Serie R Esteli Maduro is unmistakably medium-bodied. La Gloria Cubana has been around for decades. Not only that, many of us old school cigar nuts began our long journey with none other than La Gloria Cubana back in the day. Serie R Esteli Maduro can be thought of as a “new age” La Gloria. Not only will fans of the original brand appreciate the nostalgia, but fans of today’s big monster cigars will come to give much appreciation to this awesome new stick. Serie R Esteli Maduro pairs well with coffee, dark beer, or even red wine, and makes a great stick to enjoy with friends. If you were a fan of the original Serie R or the Serie R Esteli Natural , there’s entirely no doubt this cigar will blow your mind. La Gloria Cubana has come a long way since their humble beginnings. Though they may not have as many new releases annually as most other brands, you can take rest in knowing that just about anything that carries the La Gloria Cubana name will be nothing short of stellar, especially in the case of Serie R Esteli Maduro.

When the big ring gauge trend first emerged, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo was among the first to truly bring out the “big guns” with the introduction of La Gloria Cubana Serie R cigars . A pioneering masterpiece, the entire Serie R lineup features large ring gauge cigars that pack serious punch while still upholding the classic La Gloria Cubana quality standards. Handmade in the Dominican Republic, Serie R blends Dominican and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos, including a generous amount of power-packed ligero, with a spicy Nicaraguan binder. The finishing touch is a veiny, heavily aged Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, cultivated specifically for this cigar. The La Gloria Cubana Serie R No. 3 earned a 92 rating from Cigar Aficionado . The thick white smoke coats the palate with intense pepper, complemented by sweet hints of honey and black cherry. Roasted coffee notes round out the earthy profile, and though the finish is intense, it remains relatively short. It’s safe to say that Serie R is La Gloria Cubana on steroids. This full-bodied stick is best suited for experienced or intermediate smokers and pairs beautifully with port wine or a robust beer, making it an ideal, relaxing smoke before bed. Backed by the legacy of the La Gloria Cubana brand, each cigar undergoes meticulous scrutiny to ensure utmost quality. Similar cigars include MUWAT and Joya de Nicaragua Antaño. Big flavors, big cigars—that’s La Gloria Cubana Serie R.

It’s a day of celebration, a grand day of excitement and pure smoking pleasure with the launch of the latest La Gloria Cubana cigar, the sweet and robust La Gloria Cubana Serie S. Launched in 1972 and heralded as the first boutique cigar company, LGC has always focused more on crafting a quality lineup of large ring-gauge smokes instead of releasing blend after blend like some other brands. This means any new La Gloria Cubana is a big deal and we’re here for it one hundred percent. What makes Serie S so special? That would be the potent yet smooth Mexican San Andres wrapper coating each stick like it was poured over the chunky Estelí-grown binder that itself can barely contain the succulent Dominican and Nicaraguan longleaf filler tobacco stuffed into the core of each medium-full stogie. Oily and sleek, with just a bit of tooth on the flawlessly aged leaf, the San Andres wrapper has a ruddy tint and a lush aroma that brings to mind the rich volcanic soils in which it was grown. Pre-light reveals a steady draw highlighted with hints of coffee and fine exotic spice. It takes but a split second after being exposed to a hot flame for the well-packed foot of each La Gloria Cubana Serie S to leap into action, releasing thick clouds of smoke that coat the palate with dark earth, fresh-brewed espresso, nutmeg and allspice, and chocolate-coated marzipan. Additional flavors begin to be revealed as the vitola slowly burns, like black pepper, black-strap molasses, bursts of sweat cream, and a hint of black licorice. Perhaps the best news of all is that the La Gloria Cubana Serie S is a full production cigar. This means that you’ll be able to re-up at any time to make sure your varied collection of San Andres cigars, which no doubt includes some Partagas Valle Verde or even the Joya de Nicaragua Black, is fully stocked. That way you’ll never be without a premium, handmade cigar whenever the need for a great smoke presents itself.

It’s not every day that the famed artisans at the El Credito cigar factory release a new handmade cigar, but the La Gloria Cubana Serie S Maduro has been worth the wait. The novice aficionado might wonder what we’ve all been anticipating when it comes to La Gloria Cubana smokes, considering they’ve been a leading boutique cigar company since their inception in 1968. Turns out, despite crafting some of the world’s most delectable cigars for decades, LGC had never released a stogie wrapped in one of today’s most popular tobaccos, the Mexican San Andres. Until now. Containing a succulent filler blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican longleaf held within a sturdy Nicaraguan binder, the medium-full bodied Serie S Maduro is finished with a sweet and ruggedly aromatic San Andres wrapper that’s been naturally fermented to chocolatey perfection. Seamlessly smooth and oily to the touch, each chunky La Gloria Cubana Serie S Maduro vitola will stand out amongst your collection of stogies as a prime example of expert craftsmanship paired with quality tobaccos that have been blended and aged into a premium experience unlike any other. Opening with a burst of black pepper and earthy charred oak, this cigar lets you know from the start that it will deliver the potency and flavor you seek. The burn line will take its time reaching the sweet spot, but once it does the profile expands to include cocoa-dusted espresso bean, roasted and salted almonds, dried apricot, caramel, and a swirl of vanilla cream. From there, it’s time to just sit back and let your palate swim in the thick silky clouds of smoke produced by each delightful puff. If you’re a fan of Maduro cigars with both strength and character, like Aganorsa Leaf La Validacion Maduro or The Wise Man Maduro or even the Don Pepin Blue Label, then you can expect these fine sticks to be right in your wheelhouse. So why wait? Grab yourself a handful or box-full of La Gloria Cubana Serie S Maduros today and get ready for your next favorite smoke.

La Herencia Cubana CORE is among the first cigars blended by AJ Fernandez, long before he became the industry icon he is today. It was introduced as a value cigar, offering the incredible mixture of flavor, balance, and body that Fernandez has since come to be known for. Made in Nicaragua, La Herencia Cubana CORE consists of a hearty filler blend including Nicaraguan ligero leaves from Esteli and Ometepe, Honduran Jamastran ligero, and last but certainly not least, Pennsylvania Broadleaf. A Nicaraguan viso binder holds the package together, and the finishing touch is a dark Habano Ecuador sun grown ligero wrapper. Not for the faint of heart, La Herencia Cubana CORE is a true powerhouse of a cigar. Rustic packaging matches the rustic appearance of the cigar itself. Dark, toothy, and oozing with oils, La Herencia Cubana CORE is box-pressed and expertly rolled. In typical AJ Fernandez fashion, the draw is easy and smoke production is on another level. Introductory notes of black pepper and cream evolve into a rich, earthy core of raw tobacco flavor. Toasty notes of oak and light sweetness develop along the way, in addition to cinnamon and a tangy twist on the finish. Full-bodied, yet balanced, CORE delivers the classic powerhouse cigar experience every time. While not exactly a beginners' cigar, CORE definitely serves as a good gateway for anyone looking to set foot into full-bodied territory. It pairs very well with coffee or dark beer and, like most full-bodied sticks, is best enjoyed on a full stomach. This blend can be thought of as a preview of what has now become a phenomenon that has taken the cigar world by storm. Cigars such as New World or Ramon Allones by AJ Fernandez almost seem like tweaked and refined versions of CORE. Whether you are looking to explore some of the blends that put AJ on the map or you just want something bold and satisfying, La Herencia Cubana Core is most definitely a terrific choice.

The La Palina Classic is, for all intents and purposes a cigar not produced since its quiet discontinuation in 1926. Fortunately, the decedents of original creator Samuel Paley have reimagined the cigar for today's palates. At the same time, it continues to honor its namesake, Paley's wife Goldie, by remaining a classically styled and elegant smoke capable of satisfying any enthusiast regardless of their usual preferences. With the help of Avelino Lara, fabled Cuban Master Blender responsible for Castro's Cohibas as well as many of Graycliff's popular brands, Samuel's great grandson Bill has crafted an exquisite smoke rolled in the Dominican Republic and containing finely-aged Dominican and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos beneath a binder from Ecuador and a Habano wrapper from Brazil. (See more La Palina Cigars ) The first inch or so builds a rich earthiness on the tongue, while a thick vanilla creaminess is detected by the lips during the exhale, and the gray ash holds tight well into the first half when some soft spice is enhanced with savory charred cedar notes. These flavors continue to evolve through the remainder of the experience, sometimes adding in a honeyed sweetness or even a ripe hay-like expression. Want to get your buddy into stogies or perhaps you desire to impress your cigar-loving boss during salary negotiations? The La Palina Classic is perfect for either, and for any other reason you can imagine. Fans of recent medium-bodied hits like the Nat Sherman Timeless Collection or 7-20-4 will find much in common.

As the La Palina El Diario cigar proves, the legacy of a premium cigar doesn't have to begin with the story of a poor torcedor fleeing from Cuba with his family to the wilds of Nicaragua or Honduras. The original La Palina cigar was blended and sold in Chicago in 1896 by Sam Paley, a Ukranian immigrant who started his Congress Cigar Company after learning the ropes while reading for the rollers at a nearby factory. The Congress Cigar Company closed in 1926 ending the production of La Palina until Bill Paley, great-grandson of old Sam, resurrected it. The El Diario blend is an offshoot of the original La Palina line which uses a Honduran Rosado wrapper to expertly cloak a blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan Criollo and Corojo tobaccos. (See more La Palina Cigars ) The name El Diario means 'The Daily,' and this cigar is meant for daily enjoyment. While the price of the premier La Palina lines may be high for some to smoke daily, it is easy to imagine wanting an El Diario whenever the urge hits. A tall glass of iced-tea is a fine compliment to this cigar, and smokers who also enjoy La Aurora Corojo and Vegas Cubanas will find much to like about the La Palina El Diario.

Is it fair to call a cigar a "budget" stogie when, like the Le Perla Habana Black Pearl Oro, the only thing that makes it less than premium is the price? Sure, there are lots of sticks out there that cost relatively little and taste like it, but this fine smoke is loaded with the good stuff. Like many La Perla Habana cigars, the Black Pearl Oro starts with a robust blend of well-aged and expertly fermented Nicaraguan filler skillfully rolled beneath a Habano Criollo employed as a binder. Atop this marvel of flavor is a golden Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper, a soothing influence that distills the robust flavor of the interior tobaccos into a mild-to-medium strength daily go-to. (Shop other La Perla Habana Cigars ) A word of warning to those enthusiasts soon to have their own cache of La Perla Habana Black Pearl Oro's just hanging out in the humidor; it's wise to keep a napkin handy for those unexpected moments when the mouth starts watering in anticipation of smoking the next one. What's not to like? With a bright floral and hay aroma plus the cold draw tastes of wood and soft spice, the palate will thrill from the first cool puff to the last. Laden with the flavors of cream, cocoa, alfalfa, toasted cedar, almond, and white pepper, this cigar is ready for any time of day. We challenge you to find a more delicious Shade-wrapped cigar for less. Pair with a morning cup of coffee in the morning, have another after lunch, and then sip alongside some suds as the sun goes down. Sounds like our kind of fun.

La Perla Habana Black Pearl Rojo is an old-school boutique cigar that took the market by storm when it was first introduced. Now, having fallen beneath the shadows of today's rock star lineup of boutique sticks, this famous Nicaraguan puro still satisfies hardcore connoisseurs everywhere, but with a much more reasonable price point than in its glory days. All Nicaraguan tobacco makes up La Perla Rojo, including a delicious habana criollo wrapper that helped earn it a 90 rating in Cigar Aficionado. (Shop more La Perla Habana Cigars ) La Perla Habana Black Pearl Rojo is always well-made and easy-smoking, with a razor-sharp burn and billowing clouds of white smoke. The flavor profile is sweet and spicy, and flecked with notes of cocoa, cinnamon, and white pepper across the board. The finish is spicy, yet pleasant, and overall this medium-bodied gem makes a great choice for just about anyone. While the glory days of La Perla Habana may be long over, La Perla Habana Black Pearl Rojo remains a great choice for any time of the day. It pairs well with coffee and medium-bodied beer and can be compared to Joya de Nicaragua Celebracion and La Perla Habana Morado. Whether a beginner, someone that's been around the block and wants to expand horizons, or a seasoned aficionado looking for a great cigar at a wonderful price point, La Perla Habana Black Pearl Rojo is the cigar for you.

The La Perla Habana Classic is the cigar that started it all, over 10 years ago, for the brand that also boasts the Morado, the Rojo, and the Cobre.This cigar produces a rich volume of smoke and features an excellent construction with smooth notes that are perfect for the novice as well as the seasoned smoker. The La Perla Habana Classic features a filler blend of Nicaraguan, Honduran and Dominican tobacco. The binder is Ecuadorian and the cigar is wrapped in a dark, oily, toothy, Indonesian Sumatra leaf. With a rating of 91 from Cigar Aficionado, this stick is a smoke that is certain to please. Give this one some time to age in your humidor and you'll be really glad you did. The La Perla Habana Classic is one smoke that gets better with age.

La Perla Habana might not have the name recognition of some of the cigar game's big players or famous boutiques, but their Black Pearl Morado proves they have earned the right to play the same field. As one of the few small companies to survive the well-known Cigar Boom of the late 1990's, their focus remains on producing quality sticks regardless of their limited quantity. As La Perla Habana lacks the resources to run their own production facilities, all of their cigars are crafted by Toraño's skilled torcedors which ensures that every leaf of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco is properly cared for before being rolled beneath a leathery African Cameroon wrapper. While they are designated as La Perla Habana's Purple Label, you'll need to turn your attention away from the attractive young miss decorating each band to notice. Oily with just a few smell veins, the outer Cameroon is equally as handsome, carries a warm barnyard aroma, and acts as a solid framework for the lightly springy internal tobaccos. Earthy and rich once lit, filler and binder provide plenty of coffee and pepper while the wrapper layers some cinnamon spice into the crisp white clouds of smoke. With a strength that never reaches too far above medium, these are excellent sticks for morning, noon, and night. Priced like a bargain cigar, you'll understand after just your first Black Pearl Morado how La Perla Habana has been able to survive all of these years without gouging their customers or selling out by throwing as many stogies into the market as possible. Having earned a stellar 93 rating this is the superstar of their modest lineup, but you would be missing out if you didn't explore some of their other excellent offerings: Classic, Cobre, and Rojo.

Few cigars have shaped the modern premium cigar landscape quite like Liga Privada No. 9. What began as a private blend reserved exclusively for Drew Estate's executives quickly became one of the industry's most celebrated cigars, earning countless accolades and developing a fiercely loyal following around the world. A decade later, Drew Estate commemorates that remarkable journey with the Liga Privada 10 Aniversario —a limited-edition release that honors ten years of innovation while pushing the Liga Privada legacy into exciting new territory. Handcrafted at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate in Nicaragua, the 10 Aniversario showcases a remarkable Connecticut River Valley Criollo wrapper grown exclusively for Drew Estate in collaboration with some of the region's most respected tobacco farmers. Beneath this rare wrapper rests a bold Mexican San Andrés Otapan Negro Último Corte binder surrounding a carefully aged blend of premium Nicaraguan and Honduran long-fillers . The result is a full-bodied cigar that exemplifies Liga Privada's uncompromising commitment to exceptional tobacco and meticulous blending. Like every great Liga release, construction is flawless from the very first light. The distinctive Cola de Pescado (fishtail) cap and traditional closed foot not only create a striking appearance but also deliver an unforgettable opening burst of concentrated flavor. Thick, velvety smoke coats the palate with bold notes of black pepper, earthy richness, and aged tobacco , followed by layers of sharp cheddar, cedar, dark spice, and natural sweetness . As the cigar develops, the unique Connecticut Criollo wrapper reveals remarkable depth and complexity while maintaining the powerful character Liga Privada enthusiasts have come to expect. Produced in extremely limited quantities, the Liga Privada 10 Aniversario is more than a celebration of an iconic cigar, it is a testament to Drew Estate's relentless pursuit of perfection. Rich, bold, and unapologetically complex, this anniversary release captures everything that has made Liga Privada one of the most respected names in premium cigars. For longtime Liga devotees, collectors of rare releases, and smokers who appreciate full-bodied cigars crafted without compromise, the Liga Privada 10 Aniversario is a fitting tribute to ten extraordinary years of excellence.

Liga Privada Undercrown is among the most popular cigars to come out of the Drew Estate factory to date. Following in the footsteps of the now world-famous No. 9 and T52 , Undercrown can be considered part of the same family. In fact, if it weren't for its ultra-premium big brothers, Undercrown probably would have never come into existence. As the story goes according to Jonathan Drew, "In early 2009 we asked our torcedores to smoke less Liga Privada cigars because they were leaving too few to be exported… rather than being disgruntled they responded by blending their own signature liga(blend)." To do this, the folks at Drew Estate used many of the same rare tobaccos used in T52 and No. 9, but of different primings and vintages. Undercrown consists of a top shelf combination of Nicaraguan Cuban seed and Brazilian Mata Fina filler tobaccos, a T52 Connecticut River Valley stalk cut and cured Habano binder, and a rare San Andres Maduro wrapper known as Otapan Negro Ultimo Corte (Spanish for Last Cut Black Otapan). The end result went from a "throw-around" cigar enjoyed by rollers at the factory to a masterpiece that earned a spot on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 in no time flat. Firmly packed, masterfully rolled, and beautifully packaged, Undercrown truly shines in terms of appearance. However, that is only the beginning. The firm draw burns the cigar slowly, producing long, silky ribbons of translucent blue smoke that coats the palate like syrup. With earthy tobacco as the core flavor, Undercrown evolves into a luxurious array of nutty, creamy blasts of cocoa and sweet Nicaraguan spice. The overall profile is similar to the "classic maduro profile," yet much more refined. A sweet, thick finish completes the phenomenal bouquet of flavor, proving that Undercrown is definitely one of a kind. Medium-full-bodied in stature, Undercrown is available in a vast array of sizes, each one geared to the modern connoisseur. When Drew Estate comes out with a non-flavored cigar, you can just about bank on the fact that it's an aficionado-level stick aimed directly at those with well-seasoned palates. Undercrown is no different. Medium-full-bodied and extensively complex, Undercrown is literally made by cigar lovers, for cigar lovers, so you know you can't go wrong. It pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or red wine and is comparable to Liga Privada No. 9 and Liga Privada T52 , both of which Undercrown was based on. Speaking of Undercrown's name and purpose, Jonathan Drew declares, "It is always the master makers who are heralded, but the reality is that great cigars are the product of many talented people, most of whom toil in factories with no publicity ever. They are the uncelebrated heroes who make all of our lives more pleasurable with the cigars they craft." Thus, Liga Privada Undercrown was born. Never hesitate to stock up, as this gem of a cigar is perpetually in extremely high demand.

Liga Undercrown Shade cigars will seem like a vast departure from what fans of Drew Estate are used to from the company, but after the first few puffs, all doubts will be put at ease. Usually known for its hearty dark maduro wrappers on the Liga Privada No. 9 and regular Undercrown line, or the medium brown Stalk Cut Liga Privada T52 wrapper, Undercrown Shade is an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapped beauty. The Dominican Criollo 98, and Nicaraguan Corojo and Criollo filler tobaccos and Sumatran binder round out the blend on this cigar, and give it a wonderful medium bodied taste. While not as robust as a lot of the other blends that come out of Drew Estate's La Gran Fabrica factory in Nicaragua, Liga Undercrown Shade is by far not the mild cigar most people associate with a Connecticut wrapper. Complexity is king in this stick and that comes through before you even light up. The cold draw will greet your taste buds with notes of creamy vanilla and rich earth. As you get into this smoke, the sweet vanilla and a creaminess will take over your palate with a hint of pepper in the background that plays off everything else perfectly. The final third introduces a cinnamon like spice which pushes all the other flavors back slightly and begins to take hold. If you dismissed Liga Undercrown Shade as yet another mild Connecticut wrapped cigar, you are missing out on an incredibly complex, medium-bodied, tasty cigar. We are sure that once you try one, you will deem this cigar box worthy. Perfect anytime of day, the flavors in this stick mesh well with any pairing and will never overpower.

Fulfilling a legendary triumvirate foretold by ancient prophecy, or maybe just last year by Greg in accounting making a lucky guess, but either way the Liga Undercrown Sun Grown cigar is here. So, get ready for your next obsession. Following on the remarkable success of the original Liga Undercrown and the fantastic Undercrown Shade, Jonathan Drew challenged his master blender Willy Herrera to find the best use for a long-sought and newly-sourced sun grown Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Herrera went to work and with his team created the perfect Nicaraguan filler recipe, to include a single leaf of Nueva Segovia ligero, which allows the cigar's namesake tobacco to shine. Even without the name-bearing foot band, a deep burgundy red behind the familiar lion's head and crown on the main band makes the Liga Undercrown Sun Grown distinct from its brethren even at a glance. The golden-brown wrapper is even more of a distinct tell, and as soon as the foot is lit all pretense of confusion falls away. Mellow and smooth during the first few puffs, the flavor of the thick, creamy smoke quickly begins to set a solid, earthy foundation. The sweet spot is appropriately named, with chocolate, graham cracker, and allspice notes all making a mad dash towards the palate. The strength and flavor kick into high gear around the middle of the stick, with thick layers of spice, black peppercorns, leather, nuts, and salted caramel all making an appearance. Will there one day be a new Liga Undercrown with yet another wrapper? Even Greg is wishy-washy on the subject, but for now, it is enough that the Liga Undercrown Sun Grown is here. Built from day one to be an affordable alternative to some of Drew Estate's high-end stogies, these come packed 25 apiece into rugged boxes at a price that's almost unbelievable considering the quality of the cigar. Dig in!

Liga Privada No. 9 is among the most coveted and sought-after maduro cigars on the market today. It is the sister cigar of the famous T52 and has garnered much attention and numerous accolades since its inception years ago, including multiple 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado , a spot on numerous Top 25 lists, and recognition as one of the best cigars Jonathan Drew has ever taken credit for. Originally intended for use only in the private humidors of the head honchos at Drew Estate down in Nicaragua, No. 9 is an extraordinarily rich mash-up of some of the world's finest tobaccos. This includes a top shelf mixture of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers, a plantation grown Brazilian Mata Fina binder for added flavor, and a jet-black Connecticut Broadleaf Oscuro Ligero wrapper. Only a small handful of rollers at Drew Estate are certified to roll the Liga Privada series, so there is never a question regarding the quality of the end product.

Liga Privada T52 really is a cigar that doesn't need an introduction. Extremely limited and highly sought-after, T52 is a rare specialty blend hailing from Nicaragua that was put together with no expenses spared. A very complex, expertly-blended formula of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers is hugged by a spicy Brazilian Mata Fina binder. The icing on the cake is a (literally) one-of-a-kind Sun-Grown "Habano" leaf harvested especially for this cigar out of Connecticut, which ties the whole package together. Get ready for one serious ride, because T52 is an experience like no other.

Commemorating 10 years of success in the ever-growing cigar business, Undercrown 10 by Drew Estate is proof that even a long-time favorite can improve with a few tweaks. We all know the story behind Undercrown, how factory workers came up with their own blend similar to the famed Liga Privada, after being told to cut back on at-work consumption of the already limited ultra-premium sticks. Well, a full decade later, that same blend is still considered to be one of the finest cigars available, and the family at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate in Nicaragua have concocted a new factory blend to celebrate. That blend is now known as Undercrown 10, and like its predecessor, it features a dark, oily Mexican San Andres wrapper leaf. The rest of the blend is where the magic happens. Beneath the wrapper is a rich Connecticut Broadleaf binder from the Connecticut River Valley in the USA. The filler blend consists of spicy Nicaraguan leaves that really take the experience to the next level. Is it better than the original? Well, we will let you be the judge of that, but given all the hype surrounding its debut, it's safe to say that this is likely a cigar you will remember. The foot band reads "All Dekked Out," and it certainly seems accurate considering its luxurious contemporary packaging. A yellow ribbon is draped over each vitola, and the blend is denoted with a simple "10" beneath the iconic Undercrown logo on the band. Construction-wise, the folks at Drew Estate have left nothing to be desired, and each cigar is rolled to perform. Billowing clouds of smoke bring immense flavor with each puff, at first greeting the palate with spicy black pepper. Earth and chocolate are the secondary flavors, surrounded by a faint floral note hanging in the background. Woody and toasty flavors are constant with each puff, and there is a hint of espresso on the finish. Wonderfully balanced and impeccably complex, Undercrown 10 ends up just shy of the full-bodied mark, making it a bold, yet sustainable blend. While the original Undercrown blend and its variants were suitable for all audiences, Undercrown 10 is really intended for more experienced palates. Residing on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied and boasting a rather intense flavor profile, only seasoned cigar fanatics will truly be able to enjoy all the bells and whistles this blend provides. It pairs well with coffee, port wine, or cognac and is a great celebration stick. This blend will no doubt satisfy anyone who enjoys the original Undercrown or even higher-end cigars like Liga Privada No. 9 . Day in and day out, Jonathan Drew and company never cease to amaze the cigar community, and Undercrown 10 is a prime example of how dedicated they are to both their fans and cigar lovers as a whole.

The Undercrown story began on the factory floor at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate, where a group of rollers created a cigar for themselves that would eventually become one of the most beloved brands in the industry. Built on craftsmanship, creativity, and a willingness to challenge convention, the Undercrown lineup continues to evolve with the introduction of the Undercrown El Tigre Dominicano . While proudly handcrafted in Nicaragua, this latest release takes a decidedly Dominican-inspired approach, placing premium Dominican tobaccos at the heart of the blend while maintaining the bold character that has defined Undercrown from the very beginning. Named after the Spanish word for "The Tiger," El Tigre represents confidence, intelligence, and knowing exactly when to make your move. The blend reflects that philosophy beautifully. A carefully selected core of Dominican HVA and C-98 fillers provides balance, structure, and aromatic depth, while a Connecticut Corojo H99 Hybrid binder adds complexity beneath a flavorful Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The result is a medium-to-full-bodied cigar that delivers refinement and strength in equal measures. Presented in a soft box-pressed format, El Tigre Dominicano immediately stands out in the humidor. Construction is impeccable, producing a smooth draw, razor-sharp burn, and thick clouds of aromatic smoke. From the first light, notes of silky spice , white pepper , and roasted espresso emerge over a rich earthy foundation . As the cigar develops, layers of cedar , natural sweetness , and classic Dominican tobacco character reveal themselves, creating a profile that remains balanced, complex, and engaging from start to finish. Like the original Undercrown, El Tigre Dominicano was created for smokers who appreciate depth, craftsmanship, and flavor above all else. Medium-to-full-bodied and loaded with nuanced transitions, it offers a fresh take on the Undercrown experience while honoring the spirit that made the brand famous. Whether you're a longtime Undercrown devotee or simply curious to see what a Dominican-forward interpretation can bring to the table, the Undercrown El Tigre Dominicano is a cigar that demands attention and rewards every minute spent with it.
Pepper , Cocoa , Cedar , Coffee Drink. Created in celebration of the iconic brand's 40-year legacy, Macanudo 1968 is intricately-balanced with a celebratory freshness, from first draw to last

Macanudo is no strange name to anyone that has dabbled at all in the world of premium cigars. A monster of the industry, they have been one of the top brands over the past several decades due to their ability to pack so much flavor into a mild, user-friendly cigar. However, when it comes to Macanudo 1968, it's a whole new ballgame. This ultra-premium offering, released in 2008 and crafted to celebrate Macanudo's first 4 decades in business, is geared towards long-time connoisseurs that want something more from their cigars. Made in the Dominican Republic, this stick contains a 2-country filler blend from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. Nicaraguan leaves from Esteli and Ometepe give the 1968 a bold, earthy body when combined with the silky-smooth attributes of the Dominican fillers and rare Connecticut Habano binder. The star of the show, however, is the unique Honduran Olancho San Agustin wrapper leaf, one that almost appears to be a maduro but is just dark, mature, and very, very well-aged. This incredible combination of barrel-aged tobaccos works together to create a one-of-a-kind flavor profile that Macanudo, up until the time of its release, had never been known for. Widely accepted as the "Connoisseur's Macanudo," the Macanudo 1968 has earned several very respectable 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado. From the dark, luxurious black dress box to the crisp and classic gold and black bands, the packaging seems to go so well with the amazing flavor offered by the blend. Quality construction means a productive draw and a sharp burn line and guarantees each puff oozes with creamy white smoke. Rich cedar is the introductory note, soon followed by a rush of Nicaraguan white pepper. The cigar's earthy core is speckled with notes of cocoa, coffee, and cinnamon, and the finish is smooth and spicy. Medium-full-bodied and packed with flavor, it's easy to see why Macanudo 1968 has become such a respected cigar. This blend is for the mature pallet. From the delicate balance to the complex flavor profile, no beginner would be able to truly appreciate just how amazing 1968 really is. This cigar pairs well with coffee, red wine, or dark beer, and makes for a great way to celebrate life's special moments. On par with such medium-full-bodied dark beauties as Arturo Fuente Maduro or Don Pepin Black Label , the 1968 sits at the sweet spot for body, strength, and balance. Whether you are a long-time Macanudo fan or just love bold, rich, premium sticks, Macanudo 1968 fits the bill. As many have said over the years, it ain't your grandfather's Macanudo!
Sweetness , Creamy , Nutty , Woody Drink. Learn more about the Macanudo Cafe, individually handcrafted from an aromatic, flavorful blend, famously mellow, distinctively smooth and easy to smoke

The Macanudo Café cigar . What more needs to be said? It's the best-selling premium cigar for a reason, with a creamy smooth taste meant to satisfy without overwhelming even the most delicate of palates. You might think it doesn't take much effort to create such a cigar, but it actually requires a special talent to blend a sublime experience because any flaws in the flavor would be easy to detect as they would have nowhere to hide. The Macanudo Cafe Series has earned as high as a 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado , praised for its rich, balanced flavors and exceptional craftsmanship. Hand-crafted from the finest Mexican and Dominican Piloto Cubano tobaccos and coated with a smooth Connecticut shade wrapper, you will want to keep one of these sweet and clean-burning smokes on hand at all times. Once the cigar is lit, soft cedar and a bit of cream are layered beneath the crisp tobacco taste and aroma, with a hint of nutmeg to give the smoker something to think about. Experienced smokers are well aware of the Macanudo Café and may have dismissed it because of its mellow reputation; but don't knock it 'til you try it. There's plenty of interesting flavor to be found while sitting with a hot coffee on a misty morning, perhaps on the porch of a lake cabin while waiting for your fishing buddies to wake up after last night's festivities.

In an increasingly divided world, where the defenders of mild cigars trumpet subtle and sophisticated complexities to fend off the next onslaught of the "strongest ever" claims heralded by the champions of powerful stogies, sticks like the Top-25 rated Macanudo Cru Royale cigar stand astride the middle ground in relative comfort and quiet. Reaching out to smokers who prefer bold, modern flavors without a head-buzz, legendary General Cigar blender Benji Menendez marshaled a mix of tobaccos from the Dominican, Brazil, and Nicaragua into a proprietary "La Vega Especial" binder from the D.R. and placed it all under the influence of an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Macanudo Cru Royale is different in flavor and body than the cafe line that most associate with the brand. More complex in flavor and also in body, Cru Royale is a medium-bodied cigar. Starting off with a slight bit of spice, the more you smoke, the more that spice is toned down for an amazing combination of earth, cedar, and nuttiness. Each puff you take seems to introduce new flavors, but none overpowers the last. What you are left with is a cigar that is constantly changing. Classy yet approachable, the Macanudo Cru Royale can be enjoyed by most smokers, especially those who enjoy cigars like the medium-bodied 5 Vegas Classics or Joya de Nicaragua Cabinetta.

Macanudo Inspirado Orange cigars are the latest cigars from the folks at Macanudo that are sure to change the way you think about the brand that was once only known for their ultra-mild cigars. Introduced in Europe in 2014, Macanudo Inspirado Orange has spread like a wildfire, now selling in more than 40 countries worldwide and garnering huge success along the way. Finally available in the U.S. market, this Macanudo with an attitude is sure to take the American market by storm, appealing not only to die hard Macanudo fans, but all lovers of full-flavored, spicy cigars that are just plain different from the usual. Handmade in Honduras, Macanudo Inspirado Orange cigars are rolled using a robust filler blend of Honduran, Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos and a Honduran binder. The wrapper is a deep brown Olancho San Agustin leaf from Honduras, a rare but extremely flavorful type of tobacco. Inspirado Orange breaks the mold that Macanudo Cigars have formed over the years. It's new, modern, and bold, ready to satisfy just about anyone daring enough to light it up. Inspirado Orange has earned countless awards including a 93 rating and a Top 25 spot on the Cigar Aficionado 2017 list. Inspirado Orange is an impressive cigar, boasting a glistening chocolate brown wrapper leaf and a bright orange band. Masterfully rolled like any other Macanudo, it sports an easy draw and a super-sharp burn, providing massive clouds of white, silky smoke from beginning to end. Earthy, crisp, and complex, Inspirado Orange begins with grassy notes and a strong tobacco presence, but soon transitions into a vast array of spicy and sweet flavors. A tangy citrus note hangs in the background and a peppery cherry flavor rolls off the nose on the finish. Overall, a very impressive package that just feels right in every aspect. Medium-full-bodied and heavy on flavor , Macanudo Inspirado Orange makes a great cigar for intermediate to heavily experienced connoisseurs. The complexity is huge, but not so much that you need to be a lifetime aficionado to appreciate it. Inspirado Orange is that one cigar you reach for on Saturday night after dinner to kick back with and relax, forgetting all your worries and enjoying life the way it should be enjoyed. It pairs well with bourbon or red wine and shares similar flavor features with CAO OSA Sol , a cigar that utilizes the same Olancho San Agustin wrapper leaf and really should be compared side by side with Inspirado Orange for some interesting notes. Whether you're a long-time fan of Macanudo cigars or just someone that wants the latest and greatest, Macanudo Inspirado Orange cigars are definitely the sticks to reach for.

It's the dawning of a new day in the world of premium cigars with the release of the M by Macanudo. After decades as one of the most popular brands on the market, Macanudo has finally entered the one tobacco arena they have yet to conquer: Infused cigars. Yes, you read that correctly. Each succulent vitola in the line, in addition to containing longleaf Nicaraguan filler, a Philippine Isabella binder, and a finely aged Indonesian Bezuki wrapper, has been carefully imbued with the essence of single origin coffee from Colombia. The result is a truly magnificent medium-bodied confection. If there's one certainty in this world, it's the fact that Macanudo is never going to do anything cigar-wise with less than a full commitment to quality and taste. Where many infused stogies will use inferior tobaccos and rolling techniques expecting the flavor to do most of the heavy lifting in impressing the smoker, the M by Macanudo appears expertly crafted without a blemish or soft spot to be found. The rich brown wrapper beneath the boldly styled band is smooth to the touch and exudes a mocha-like aroma before tempting the lips with a syrupy kiss. In addition to the robust cane sugar and coffee-with-cream flavors which form the foundation of the smoke, the palate can expect to find all the regular hallmarks of a premium Nicaraguan cigar such as cedar, leather, baking spices, earth, and dark cocoa. Even if you're not usually a fan of infused cigars we think you'll be delightfully surprised by M by Macanudo, especially if you like pairing cigars with coffee like so many of us do. However, don't think that's going to be your only beverage option. Oh, no. Anything you might pour into your favorite java, such as Irish cream or whiskey, orange liquor, amaretto, or a fine Cognac will all serve as excellent companions to this delectable treat when sipped neat or over ice. MMMMM…Is your mouth watering too?
Bourbon , Cherry , Bitters Drink. The flavored cigar portfolio for Macanudo expands with a multi-dimensional new twist on a classic cocktail

Stir up an Old Fashioned and grab a comfy chair because it's a whole new ballgame now that Macanudo has entered the crowded field of infused cigars with the incredible M Bourbon by Macanudo. After dominating the traditional mild-to-medium market for what seems like forever, Macanudo more recently ran up the score with robust offerings like the 1968 and the Inspirado line, but this Bourbon-steeped smoke proves they haven't neglected their fundamentals. What would be a classically delicious and medium-bodied smoke built from fine Ecuadorian and Dominican longleaf is transformed by the essences of aged Bourbon, cherry, and aromatic bitters info a flavorful and inspired treat. As the well-built vitola is slipped from its cellophane wrapper like a golden dram from a bottle, the pungent aroma of a boozy oak barrel wafts from the flawless Connecticut Shade wrapper. The aged Dominican filler at the M Bourbon by Macanudo's core, skillfully held in place by a thick Ecuadorian binder, is where the taste and smell of cherry can be found ready to be unleashed through the open draw by a steady flame. Charred oak, caramel, and leather greet the palate during the first sips of the cool, voluminous smoke, with the sweet malt, spice, and vanilla of quality whiskey ever-present. The cherry, shifting from maraschino to black and back, is never overwhelming while serving as a sweet counterpoint to the bitters best experienced during the exhale. Certainly well-matched with an evening's after-dinner cocktail, try an M Bourbon by Macanudo with a rich black coffee on a lazy Sunday morning for a delightful contrast in flavors. Then have an M Coffee by Macanudo that night with a snifter of your favorite distilled libation. Now that's how you make the big leagues.

Macanudo may not be a name in the headlines of the cigar world these days, but there was a time when the Dominican brand was an absolute monster, occupying millions of humidors worldwide. In the present, however, the brand is known more for its special releases, some of the more popular ones being the Vintage series. Of the Vintage series, the most popular offering has been the Macanudo Vintage 1997 Maduro, the first and only cigar to date in the series to use a maduro wrapper. So why the name and date? Well, the tobacco used to wrap this blend is from a crop of Connecticut Broadleaf harvested in 1997. You read that right—the wrapper tobacco used for this blend is over a quarter-century old! Combined with a unique filler blend of leaves from Nicaragua, Brazil, and the Dominican Republic, along with a Honduran binder, this blend is a connoisseur’s dream come true. As for packaging, this cigar is best known for its shiny metal band. Apparently, this band is used not only as an elegant adornment for each vitola, but as a way to gauge humidity. Legend has it that if the cigar dries out too much, the band will become loose and start to slide, whereas if it is over-humidified, the band will appear to cinch around the cigar like a belt pulled too tight. The Vintage denotation is engraved across the front, along with the words “Reserva Dorada” on the back side, literally translating “Golden Reserve.” An opening of cedar and coffee greets the palate upon lighting, soon combining with hints of white pepper, chocolate, and cream. An earthy core holds throughout, along with blasts of espresso and brown sugar all along the way. The finish is long and intense, and the cigar burns slowly to give a wonderful display of flavor. Medium-bodied, Macanudo Vintage 1997 Maduro is a winner for any fan of refined maduro cigars. Made for long-time connoisseurs and enjoyed by only the most discriminating cigar fanatics, Macanudo Vintage 1997 Maduro has all you could want from a luxury cigar. With no shortage of flavor or body, this cigar pairs well with coffee, dark beer, or red wine, and can be smoked or gifted in a variety of celebratory ways. Fans of Macanudo Maduro or Inspirado Black should certainly come to appreciate the wonderful flavors this blend has to offer. Taking maduro to a whole new level and adding enough luxurious flare to catch the attention of the snobbiest cigar aficionados, Macanudo Vintage 1997 Maduro remains one of the most unique maduro experiences one can get.

Being one of the biggest names in the history of the cigar business, it’s no surprise that when Macanudo does something special, it’s REALLY special. Such is the case with Macanudo Vintage 2006. Here, we have a top-shelf Dominican offering from the name that basically made mild cigars popular. This guy isn’t so mild, however, as the rich filler blend consists of rich San Andres tobacco from Mexico and smooth, flavorful leaves from the Dominican Republic. Paired with a Mexican San Andres binder, this blend makes for an impressive flavor profile, but the real exciting part is the wrapper: A silky smooth Connecticut shade leaf grown in 2006! That’s right, the tobacco used to wrap this cigar has been patiently aging and fermenting in palm leaves for nearly 2 decades. So why was the vintage crop selected from the said year? It just so happens that 2006 was a phenomenal year for amazing tobacco crops, as the weather, soil, and growing conditions were all absolutely ideal at the time. This nearly perfect situation happens not more than a couple times every decade or so. Not surprisingly, this cigar has become one of the most popular cigars to wear the Macanudo name. Packaged in gorgeous mahogany boxes, Macanudo Vintage 2006 is certainly served up the way a luxury cigar should be. The most notable part of the packaging, however, is the iconic metal band that doubles as a humidity gauge. Too tight, and the cigar is overly humidified. Too loose, and maybe it’s a bit dry. Burning with a crisp ash line and smooth smoke production, this blend takes off on the woody side, with a bold blast of cedar upon first light. The smoke then turns creamy and presents a well-rounded classic Connecticut flavor profile of floral and grassy notes mixed with an earthy tobacco core. Smooth, sweet, and delicately blended, this medium-bodied blend is sure to impress even the most demanding fans of Connecticut cigars. Made for the experienced, this cigar shouldn’t be wasted on an underdeveloped palate. Only the most sensitive tastes of the most seasoned connoisseurs will be able to truly appreciate the incredible degree of aging and blending that went into this medium-bodied masterpiece. An accompanying glass of white wine, cognac, or Champagne certainly makes for a one-of-a-kind experience. Speaking of Champagne, this blend makes for one heck of a celebratory cigar. Fans of other higher-end Connecticut cigars such as Montecristo , Perdomo Champagne , or Macanudo Cafe will almost certainly enjoy this blend. Experience one of the finest Connecticut cigars in the world with Macanudo Vintage 2006.
