Man O' War Dark Aged Maduro is one of the harder-to-find cigars in the extensive Man O' War lineup. Making its debut in 2013, Man O' War Dark Aged Maduro was originally intended for sale only at brick and mortar stores. Thankfully, however, it eventually made its way to online retailers and became a bit more accessible to cigar lovers everywhere. Dark Aged Maduro consists of a bold filler and binder blend of all Nicaraguan tobaccos wrapped in an Ecuadorian Habano Maduro leaf. The recipe is simple, but includes nothing but extensively aged high-priming leaves harvested for their richness and strength. Dark, oily, and rolled with extreme precision, Man O' War Dark Aged Maduro is clothed with the standard Man O' War band and a thin foot band indicating the blend. A smooth draw produces gigantic plumes of thick, creamy smoke, offering a bold, spicy opening. The initial blast of pepper soon turns sweet, as hints of cocoa, cedar, and espresso come to the surface. A constant dark chocolate flavor beautifully complements the woody, earthy undertones throughout the duration of the cigar. A sweet, nutty finish completes the complex flavor profile beautifully. Full-bodied, eventful, and slow-burning, Man O' War Dark Aged Maduro is truly a cigar worth searching for. Many of Man O' War offerings are great sticks for beginners and intermediate smokers. For Dark Aged Maduro, this isn't the case. Only the most experienced and discriminating connoisseurs will be pleased to appreciate all the depth and complexity this stick has to offer. As a full-bodied maduro cigar, Dark Aged Maduro pairs well with black coffee, tawny port, or dark rum. Wondering if this cigar is right for you? If you enjoy powerful maduros such as Camacho Triple Maduro , CAO Brazilia , or Padron Maduro , chances are you won't want to skip over Dark Aged Maduro. Truly a hidden gem in a massive sea of boutique cigars, Man O' War Dark Aged Maduro is a maduro lover's dream come true.

A.J. Fernandez is a hot name in the cigar industry right now, and with good reason. His cigars, such as Diesel, San Lotano, and Man O' War, are some of the best and most flavorful sticks coming out of Nicaragua. The Man O' War Puro Authentico was personally blended by A.J. himself and was originally created just for him. Only available in a 5" x 42 corona, this smaller cigar can stand up to some of the much larger ones in terms of flavor and power. The beauty in this stick is found in the gorgeous dark Habano ligero wrapper leaf. A simple black and gold band featuring the iconic imagery of a centurion's helmet greats you as soon as you take one out of the box. The wrapper is dark and luscious with a tooth that is not seen enough these days. Each little dimple on the wrapper is a pocket of flavorful oils just waiting for the flame. Bold and rich are two words that can be overused at times, but perfectly describe the Man O' War Puro Authentico. Spicy undertones matched with a fantastic earthiness will grab you from the beginning and never let up. It could be said the Man O' War Puro Authentico is one of A.J.'s crowning achievements, but that is hard to do when he makes so many tasty cigars. The power behind this blend makes it hard to truly appreciate unless after a nice meal. Enjoyed with a great cup of dark and bitter coffee, this stick is truly like heaven. Other great cigars from AJ are Diesel and San Lotano, and we would also highly recommend those as well.

Yet, another amazing blend from AJ Fernandez and Tabacalera Fernandez is here. Enter the Man O' War Virtue cigar as the mild side of what has been, until now, an awfully full-flavored line-up. AJ Fernandez is responsible for the Man O' War, Man O' War Ruination, Diesel and San Lotano cigars along with some cigars for Rocky Patel, Padilla, and Indian tobacco. AJ was the protege of Don Robaina who has long been considered one of the "godfathers of tobacco."

There are some cigars that are special occasion cigars and then there are some that are everyday smokes. Mayorga Maduro fits squarely into the latter, but that doesn't mean you have to sacrifice taste and construction for price. Made by Plasencia, the Mayorga Maduro is a rigidly square-pressed cigar made with fine Nicaraguan filler and Binder tobacco and a black Costa Rican maduro wrapper. Medium-to-full in body, this cigar is a great stick to keep around for when you don't want to burn your celebration cigars. (See more Mayorga cigars ) A bright yellow band is a perfect contrast to the deep ebony maduro wrapper, just like the sweetness of the wrapper leaf meshes with the spiciness of the Nicaraguan filler. Not only will you be marveled that this rich, dark cigar tastes so extraordinary, but you will also be amazed at the outstanding construction. With every puff there is an easy draw, straight burn, and a plethora of flavors that play off your tongue. Cigar smokers are always on the hunt for a great inexpensive smoke, and Mayorga Maduro is a prize stag. Great taste, flawless construction, and a price that won't break the bank… what are you waiting for? For a slightly milder yet spicy taste, we would also recommend the natural version of Mayorga.

During the long and exhausting process of putting together blends that would potentially become Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua, AJ Fernandez and Rafael Nodal settled on two final candidates. One of those went on to become the targeted cigar, but the other just “needed a bit more age.” Fast forward a few years, and the one that needed to age further would become one of the finest cigars to ever wear a Montecristo band: Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Edicion Diamante . Translated as “Diamond Edition,” this Nicaraguan puro is made by hand at Nicaragua’s own San Lotano factory under the supervision of AJ Fernandez himself. The recipe contains all Nicaraguan leaves—wrapper, filler, and binder. The wrapper is the star of the show, a low-priming hybrid wrapper grown in Jalapa, one of Nicaragua’s richest growing regions. Patience proved to be a winning strategy with this one, as the extra few years of aging indubitably transformed good tobacco into incredible tobacco. So incredible, in fact, that this blend promptly earned a pair of respectable 93 ratings in Cigar Aficionado , along with a spot on the famed magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of 2023. The packaging is classic Montecristo style mixed with some special edition flare. The brown and gold bands feature a diamond logo, making it easy to differentiate between Edition Diamante and the original 1935. Each and every vitola is lovingly constructed and checked over multiple times to ensure an easy draw, a sharp burn, and plenty of voluminous, thick smoke with each and every puff. This cigar starts off with a heavy dose of spicy Nicaraguan pepper, soon smoothing out to an array of cocoa, nuts, and cedar. Leathery, earthy flavors seem to be the main theme of the flavor profile, while touches of dark chocolate and bakers’ spices adorn the retrohale. The finish is smooth, spicy, and rich, and overall, this stick finishes at the very strong end of medium-full-bodied. Like its predecessor, Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Edicion Diamante is meant to be enjoyed by the most seasoned connoisseurs only. A well-developed palate, plenty of patience when it comes to enjoying a cigar puff by puff, and a good understanding of complexity and balance are all necessities for truly appreciating a cigar of this stature. It pairs well with bourbon or cognac and is ideal as a special occasion cigar. If you loved the original Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua , this stick is a must-try. Compare the two and let us know which one you like better! If you are an experienced aficionado that takes cigars seriously, or if you are a long-time fan of Montecristo or AJ Fernandez, don’t hesitate to take the plunge and experience what people are calling the most luxurious Montecristo cigar to date: Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Edicion Diamante.

For ninety years, Montecristo has stood among the most revered names in premium cigars, earning a reputation built on timeless elegance, impeccable craftsmanship, and unforgettable smoking experiences. Since its founding in Cuba in 1935, the Montecristo name has become synonymous with luxury, captivating generations of aficionados around the world. To celebrate this remarkable milestone, Montecristo partnered with Rafael Nodal and the legendary Plasencia family to create the Montecristo 90th Anniversary —a limited-edition release that pays tribute to the brand's storied past while showcasing the future of premium cigar blending. Cigar Aficionado has given Montecristo 90th Anniversary Nacional blend a 90 rating . Handcrafted by Plasencia Cigars in Estelí, Nicaragua, this commemorative release is built entirely from extra-aged Nicaraguan tobaccos personally selected under Rafael Nodal's direction. A flawless Jalapa wrapper crowns a carefully balanced blend of premium tobaccos from Estelí, Condega, Jalapa, and Ometepe , creating an all-Nicaraguan masterpiece that reflects both Montecristo's rich heritage and Plasencia's world-renowned expertise. Every leaf was chosen to deliver exceptional balance, refinement, and complexity worthy of one of the cigar industry's most celebrated anniversaries. Construction is nothing short of spectacular. The draw is effortless, the burn razor-sharp, and each puff produces dense, velvety clouds of aromatic smoke. The flavor journey begins with silky notes of cream and roasted coffee , gradually unfolding into layers of cocoa, cedar, and warm baking spice . As the cigar develops, the sweetness of the aged tobacco emerges, weaving seamlessly through earthy undertones before culminating in a remarkably smooth, medium-bodied finish that remains elegant from first light to final draw. Presented in stunning commemorative boxes finished in regal shades of red, black, gold, and gray, the Montecristo 90th Anniversary is every bit as impressive visually as it is on the palate. Produced in limited quantities using some of the finest reserved tobaccos in the Plasencia family's aging rooms, this extraordinary release honors nine decades of cigar-making excellence while reminding us why Montecristo continues to define the standard by which premium cigars are judged. Whether you're a devoted Montecristo enthusiast, a collector of milestone releases, or simply searching for an unforgettable celebratory smoke, the Montecristo 90th Anniversary is a fitting tribute to one of the greatest names in cigar history.

Debuting in Cuba in 1935, Montecristo is a brand that has earned the moniker of Classic. In cigar factories in Cuba, it was not uncommon for cigar rollers to be entertained with someone reading to them. Legend has it one of the favorite titles was Count of Montecristo, and that is how the brand was born. Montecristo Classic is the epitome of this stalwart brand. A flawless Connecticut shade wrapper drapes the finest Dominican binder and filler tobaccos. Made in the Dominican Republic at the famed Tabacalera de Garcia factory since 1995, Montecristo Classic cigars are sure to please even the most discerning smokers of mild-to-medium bodied sticks. Celebrate a proven classic—select Montecristo Classic vitolas have earned an impressive 91-rating from Cigar Aficionado , confirming their status as some of the finest mellow premiums on the market. The classic Montecristo band is just slightly altered with the introduction of gold accents to let smokers know they are smoking something special. The wrapper is flawless and a beautiful mottled light brown. The creaminess which comes through on the first puff is present for the entire cigar. Montecristo Classic is a dense cigar full of filler making the draw have a tension which cools the smoke down perfectly. A slight earthy aftertaste lingers pleasantly on the palate making this a wonderful cigar you will remember throughout your day. With a construction as great as the flavor, this is a cigar you will surely want to keep stocked in your humidor. Montecristo classic is the perfect example of what a mild-to-medium smoke should be. Perfectly balanced, there is a flavorful puff awaiting you with each draw. We found this a fantastic cigar to start the day with, meshing with our morning coffee to a tee. Other great Montecristos to try are the Montecristo White for a slightly milder experience or the Platinum for a little more spice.

Destined to become a modern classic, the Montecristo Crafted by AJ Fernandez cigar is more than worthy of the famous name it carries. And it's a Montecristo too! Seriously, though, Fernandez gives the distinguished and near-century old front mark the respect it deserves by providing a richly complex taste balanced for all types of aficionados. But AJ was not looking to mimic the past or tread the same path as his forebears, so this is a box-pressed Montecristo rolled in Nicaragua containing a wealth of Nicaraguan and Honduran filler and finished with a Mexican San Andres binder and Ecuadoran Sumatra Oscuro wrapper. Never saw that coming, did you? The first thing you'll notice when pulling a Montecristo Crafted by AJ Fernandez from your humidor are the three white, red, and gold bands which cover most of each mahogany-colored vitola. Once this decoration is out of the way and the foot properly smoldering, the perfectly aged longleaf tobaccos will begin producing clouds of smoke laden with the heavenly flavors of cedar, mocha, and spice . The mid-point of the cigar is marked by a bright citrus revelation, with some sweet licorice, dark earth, and a hint of red pepper keeping the medium-strength cigar on track to the very end.

This rare limited edition represents the true artisanship and highly skilled blending that made the Montecristo brand famous throughout the world-a medium-bodied gem packed with valiant flavors and unparalleled complexity. The Montecristo Espada series has always represented the bold side of one of the cigar world's most legendary brands. Introduced in 2014 as Montecristo's first all-Nicaraguan blend , Espada showcased the remarkable tobaccos of Nicaragua through a collaboration between Altadis U.S.A., Rafael Nodal, the Grupo de Maestros, and the renowned Plasencia family. With the arrival of the Montecristo Espada Signature Limited Edition , that story continues in a more refined direction. Rather than emphasizing raw power, this exceptional release was crafted to highlight balance, elegance, and the natural complexity of vintage Nicaraguan tobacco. Handcrafted at the prestigious Plasencia factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, the Espada Signature is a true Nicaraguan puro. A flawless Colorado Claro wrapper harvested from the fertile fields of Jalapa surrounds a carefully selected binder and long-fillers from Estelí, creating a medium-bodied profile that showcases the remarkable harmony possible from Nicaragua's most celebrated growing regions. Every leaf was chosen to complement the others, resulting in a blend where refinement takes center stage without sacrificing the rich character that defines the Espada family. Presented exclusively in the handsome 6" x 55 Valiente vitola, the Espada Signature offers the ideal canvas for the blend's evolving personality. Construction is impeccable, delivering an effortless draw, a razor-straight burn, and thick, velvety clouds of aromatic smoke. The opening introduces lively notes of white pepper and warm spice before gradually settling into creamy layers of cedar, leather, molasses, and milk chocolate . Earthy undertones remain constant throughout the smoke, while subtle natural sweetness and a touch of bready richness carry the cigar to a smooth, yet satisfying finish that becomes progressively richer toward the final third. Produced in limited quantities and presented in elegant boxes of ten, the Montecristo Espada Signature Limited Edition is a fitting addition to one of Montecristo's most celebrated modern series. Whether you're already a fan of the original Espada line or searching for a more refined interpretation of the celebrated Nicaraguan puro, this beautifully balanced release delivers exceptional craftsmanship, remarkable complexity, and the unmistakable quality that comes from two of the industry's most respected names: Montecristo and Plasencia.

Any time a Montecristo cigar is made by AJ Fernandez , it never fails that a certain type of magic is bound to happen. We have seen it numerous times, and now we see it in the latest, seemingly most successful collaboration between these two monsters thus far: Montecristo M . Crafted by the skilled hands at the famed Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Nicaragua, Montecristo M is a simple, yet intriguing blend consisting of an all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend and a golden-brown Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf. This isn’t just any old Connecticut leaf, though. For this blend, they chose a crop no less than 20 years old for the wrapper. That’s right, the leaves have been aging for over two decades, the finished product being a mellow, silky-smooth body with bright and flavorful notes throughout the smoke. A top-tier ultra-premium cigar is the result, and one that has earned a very hefty roundup of 90+ ratings in the little time since its debut. The legendary Montecristo band is done in a gleaming gold for this version, accented with the usual white logo and accompanied by a secondary band bearing the bright red “M”. Nestled neatly in the most beautiful of wooden chests, each Montecristo M vitola boasts masterful construction and offers a smoking experience like no other. The soft and smooth draw produces the trademark billowing clouds of smoke that AJ Fernandez’s finest cigars are known for. A light dose of white pepper opens things up, quickly settling into a creamy and sweet medley of delicate Connecticut-style flavor. Notes of honey, toast, and earthy tobacco shine throughout the smoking experience, and the finish is creamy and spicy. Medium-bodied , yet dazzlingly flavorful, this cigar brings back memories of the ultra-high-class Connecticut sticks that decorated the market before the powerhouse trend became a thing. Obviously made for the most seasoned of connoisseurs, Montecristo M is a luxurious package that demands undivided attention at smoking time. Complex, smooth, and delightfully medium-bodied, it offers a classic flavor profile that pairs beautifully with a glass of fine scotch or bourbon. Fans of cigars such as Montecristo 1935 Nicaragua or Montecristo Classic are going to want to try this one out, as it has a way of showcasing all the best parts of each of the above, all in one package. On the lookout for ultra-premium goodness that only names like AJ and Montecristo can achieve? Don’t hesitate to grab a Montecristo M for your next special occasion and settle into a smoking experience that you’ll never forget.

Monte by Montecristo takes traditional flavor and infuses it with strength and vigor to create a medium-full cigar ready to thrill your palate. Drawing deep from skills developed over decades of creating many of the world’s most popular smokes, the fabled Grupo de Maestros has crafted this stogie to be the most robust in the Montecristo stable while retaining the brand’s legendary smooth and distinctive character. Filled with plump Dominican longleaf tobaccos and covered with a leathery Ecuadoran Habano wrapper, the true secret sauce of this vitola is the use of dual binders to really add some oomph to the blend: a zesty Dominican Olor and a thick, juicy Nicaraguan Corojo. Monte by Montecristo cigars earned a Top 25 of 2014 ranking at #9 with an impressive 93 rating from Cigar Aficionado. Announcing itself properly by wearing a bold black, red, and gold ‘MONTE’ band beneath the brand’s standard simple brown and white label, the hefty barrel of each cigar will have your mouth watering in anticipation. Pre-light, the fresh scent of fresh cut hay drying atop loamy earth fills the nostrils, the tongue capturing hints of wood and cardamom. Billowing white smoke lush with roasted coffee, vanilla cream, and a faint bite of red chili pour through a smoldering Monte by Montecristo, a touch of allspice detectable in the retrohale. Finishing with a rush of dark bittersweet chocolate, oak, and salted caramel, you’ll be reluctant to let go of the nub. Whether you’re looking to take the art of cigar smoking to the next level, need a legendary stash for an upcoming golf trip, or just want a delicious stogie to go with that bottle of Bourbon you’ve been hoarding, the Monte by Montecristo has you covered. Consider adding even more reimagined classics to your collection such as the incredible Partagas Legend or even the mind-bending M by Macanudo.

The Montecristo Platinum series sets standards for handmade luxury cigars. Montecristo Platinum Series – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Crafted with a select San Andrés Cubano wrapper grown in the legendary San Andrés Valley, along with a rich Dominican binder and a special blend of Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian long filler tobaccos, these exquisite cigars offer a rich, smooth, and sensual smoke.

A top shelf ultra-premium for the modern age, the Montecristo Platinum might just represent the pinnacle of your search for the consummate cigar. With a legacy that stretches back nearly a century, some newer smokers might consider the brand to be a relic of a bygone era, but wise aficionados know better. With a host of sticks of the utmost quality that cater to any preference, the various Montecristo cigars offer the best of the best to everyone. The luxurious Platinum is crafted for experienced palates, those able to withstand the veritable mosaic of full-bodied flavors supplied by rare Nicaraguan, Dominican, and Peruvian long-filler tucked firmly into a gorgeous and chocolatey Mexican San Andres wrapper. The Montecristo Platinum Series has earned multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado , praised for its rich, balanced flavors and exceptional craftsmanship. Perhaps a fortunate virtue for when your pals go rummaging through your humidor for a stogie, the true qualities of a Montecristo Platinum are easily overlooked by the unsophisticated eye. Wearing understated gold-trimmed platinum double bands that belie the care and skill with which the entire cigar is hand crafted, the ruddy and sleek outer tobacco leaf that covers the generously rolled vitola is so perfectly flawless it almost defies belief. However, once the supple triple cap is clipped, the broad foot well-lit, and rich clouds of smoke pour from the barrel, you’ll discover the truth. The profile it creamy and vibrant from the start, with bittersweet cocoa and hickory wood balanced by a marshmallow-like softness. As you are slowly lulled into contemplative relaxation, the flavors of sweet yet robust turkish coffee, leather, crisp pear, salted almonds, and earthy cinnamon arrive to keep you fully engaged until the nub becomes too small to hold. For a cigar of this price and pedigree, it’s common practice to tuck them away waiting for just the right special moment to light one up. While they will certainly age nicely, we say the Montecristo Platinum will make any occasion special so go ahead and enjoy whenever you like. If you already have the future day in mind, satisfy yourself in the meantime with some Romeo San Andres by RyJ or JFR XT Maduro.

Plenty of new, trendy cigar lines have come out bearing the Montecristo logo in recent years, and Montecristo Volume 1: 100 Days is among the newer releases from Altadis USA. Named after a chapter in the Count of Monte Cristo which tells of events that occurred 100 days after Napoleon Bonaparte's escape from the Isle of Elba, this special edition takes the "100 days" theme even further, as the cigars are aged in aromatic cedar bins for 100 days after rolling. The blend was put together by Altadis USA's Grupo de Maestros and is produced in Honduras at the Flor de Copan factory. The recipe includes Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, a Nicaraguan binder, and a golden Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. The vitolas are luxuriously dressed in silver and black bands covering nearly the entire body. The packaging is both clever and unique, as the 10-count boxes are made to resemble the famous Count of Montecristo novel by Alexandre Dumas. The construction of this cigar leaves little to be desired, as each vitola offers a streamlined and satisfying smoking experience. The thick white smoke first greets the palate with a massive burst of cedar, soon joined by Nicaraguan pepper and hints of cayenne and cocoa. There is a sweet floral finish through the nose, completing the simple, yet poetically constructed flavor profile. Montecristo Volume 1: 100 Days finishes as a medium-bodied cigar with impeccable balance and immense flavor. While this medium-bodied cigar may be suitable for all audiences, it is really aimed at cigar enthusiasts with more developed palates. As is the case with most Montecristo sticks, this blend makes for a great celebration cigar, or simply something to puff on when enjoying the company of good friends. It pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or white wine and is similar in stature to such other Montecristo masterpieces as Montecristo Platinum and Montecristo White . Over the years, countless memorable cigars have worn the Montecristo logo. Montecristo Volume 1: 100 Days continues the trend, and no doubt tells a story with each and every puff.

Montecristo Volume II: The Rendezvous opens yet another chapter in the ongoing cigar story written piece by piece by the Grupo de Maestros and the fine folks at Altadis USA. The second installment in an exclusive series of blends drawing inspiration from the unforgettable Count of Monte Cristo novel by Alexandre Dumas, Volume II: The Rendezvous hails from Honduras, constructed at the world-famous Flor de Copan factory by some of the most skilled rollers in the world. The recipe for this project includes filler tobacco from Honduras, a broadleaf binder, and a deep golden brown Habano 2000 wrapper leaf from Ecuador. A reference to the chapter in Volume II of the novel where the Count of Monte Cristo is introduced to the luxury of Parisian society, this cigar seems to be aptly named and intended to be enjoyed as the luxurious gem it truly is. Packaged in 10 count boxes resembling leather-bound hardcover books with gleaming silver and black bands covering nearly the entirety of each vitola, Montecristo Volume II: The Rendezvous certainly boasts some beautiful attire. The beauty doesn't stop there, however, as each cigar is constructed to the highest standards, displaying a near seamless roll that leads to a productive draw on each and every puff. A spicy introduction soon turns into a solid base of earthy raw tobacco spiked with notes of chocolate and cinnamon. White pepper remains throughout the smoke, but just enough to add some appreciated depth to the mix. The finish is clean and rich, with a slight hint of floral sweetness through the nose. Medium-bodied and delicately balanced, this blend is nothing short of a sheer delight. Produced for the pickiest of cigar snobs, this blend is in no way intended for a less-than-mature audience. A seasoned palate is a must when it comes to truly appreciating all the complex flavor and rich nuances this stick has to offer. Medium-bodied and heavy on flavor, it pairs beautifully with red wine, bourbon, or single malt scotch. If you enjoyed Montecristo Volume I: 100 Days , this blend should no doubt be next on your to-do list. It also compares to similar medium-bodied Montecristo releases such as Montecristo White or Montecristo Platinum , so fans of such beloved blends will likely enjoy this one as well. This masterpiece is red-hot and hard to find, so don't hesitate to turn the page and experience the next part of the ongoing story with Montecristo Volume II: The Rendezvous today!

A perfect addition to the Montecristo family, the Montecristo White was crafted to complement the original Montecristo. Prepare to be met with creamy and flavor Montecristo White Series – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 A perfect addition to the Montecristo family, the Montecristo White was crafted to complement the original Montecristo. Prepare to be met with creamy and flavorful smoke as rich as its history. Reminiscent of the original, the elegant Montecristo White boasts a lovely, hand-selected Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper. With a Nicaraguan binder and a blend of select Dominican and Nicaraguan long fillers, the White makes for a rich, creamy and flavorful, well-rounded smoke.

The Montecristo White Series is an epic cigar you'll wish you had tried sooner. Created by a brand that sits at the highest of heights when it comes to tobacco and handmade in the Dominican Republic by skilled torcedors who have perfected the art of the roll, these elegant vitolas are masterpieces of smooth, rich flavor. Beneath the stark white double bands emblazoned with gold markings, you'll find a flawless Ecuadoran Connecticut wrapped like a warm blanket atop a Nicaraguan binder that expertly contains the premium Dominican and Nicaraguan longleaf filler at the core. The Montecristo White Series earned an impressive 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado , celebrated for its smooth, creamy profile and refined balance of flavor and elegance. Like standing at the edge of a tobacco field in the warm sun, your senses are greeted by shimmering earth tones and a bright floral aroma as the leathery barrel of a Montecristo White is slipped from its cellophane. A taste of roasted peanut hits the tongue just prior to a flame being applied to the foot, then the lighting puffs bloom with oak and malted milk chocolate . As the burn slowly matures and the sweet spot is consumed, a burst of spice tempered by vanilla cream brings the strength and body to a succulent mild-medium. Steady throughout, while bringing out the robust flavors of espresso, buttered rye toast, and raw honey, this is a cigar to be enjoyed by everyone at any time. Pairing as well with an evening's Bourbon as a morning's coffee, or vice versa, make sure to grab enough of these premium cigars to not run out when it really matters. While we understand making the Montecristo White your go-to for all occasions, consider treating your palate to a rotating selection of delectable stogies by including some H. Upmann Vintage Cameroon and Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 2 to your order. Salud!

Montecristo White Series Vintage Connecticut is the newest cigar from the stalwart brand by Altadis. While there are two main changes from the regular and beloved White Label line, the main one is in the wrapper. Altadis is the only cigar manufacturer to own its own farm in Connecticut for its wrapper leaf, Gershel Farms. This new Montecristo uses the beautifully creamy and blonde Connecticut Shade wrapper from this exclusive barn to give the cigar a wonderfully mild-to-medium taste. With boxes and secondary bands adorned with beautiful artwork of a barn from the Gershel Farm, you know as soon as you open the box you are smoking something special. The subtle change from the normal Ecuador Connecticut wrapper of the regular White Series to the Shade used here is small but noticeable. The filler has a slightly different blend as well, utilizing Peruvian tobacco for the first time in this mild cigar line. This added leaf adds a bit of body and a bit spiciness found mostly on the retrohale. Montecristo White Series Vintage Connecticut is a perfect cigar for anyone who enjoys a nice creamy smooth smoke with just a hint of spice. Perfect for a nice cool day with a hot beverage of your choice, the first few puffs will put you in a state of instant relaxation. We would also recommend the regular Montecristo White Series to anyone who loves a mild cigar.

It's that wondrous time again folks when My Father Cigars releases both a new Le Bijou and a new Limited Edition and it's a two-for-one deal this year with the My Father Le Bijou Limited Edition 2016 cigar! My oh my, does it get any better than this? Individually nestled into cozy cedar coffins, each fine smoke patiently awaits the flame before exploding into Le Bijou's black pepper, oak, cream, and marzipan. The Oscuro wrapper adds an intense depth to the profile, full of cocoa and espresso and burnt sugar. Expect a solid two hours of full strength, full-bodied smoking that will leave you completely satisfied yet wanting just one more puff. If you're wondering how limited the My Father Le Bijou Limited Edition 2016 cigars actually are, here's the answer: Only 4000 boxes of 14 cigars each were produced so if you're planning on buying some it's a good idea to make your move now. There are some brands that are so deeply intermingled with the history of cigars, that you know the distinction came with only producing and selling the very best products and smokes out there. Nat Sherman is one of those brands, and their Host Selection cigars are another example of why they deserve the accolades. Made in Honduras, this mild-to-medium bodied smoke features some of the best Honduran filler and binder tobacco wrapped in a golden hued Connecticut shade wrapper. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) The classic Nat Sherman band is accented in a light blue and is striking against the blonde Connecticut wrapper. Notes of hay and nuts brush past your nose as you bring this cigar up to smoke. After lighting, an amazing creaminess enters your mouth and perfectly melds with a nutty finish and slight white pepper on the retrohale. The complexity of flavor is astounding for a cigar that is so mild. History and tradition are not the only thing on Nat Sherman’s side, they also make a darn good cigar. The Host is another great choice from the renowned company. This full-flavored yet mild cigar is great for the early afternoon with that coffee which helps us finish up the day. Another great Nat Sherman smoke is the Timeless Dominican.

Never a company to rest on their laurels, Nat Sherman has released the delectable Host Maduro cigar to great fanfare and acclaim. It has been fun in recent years watching this revitalized 80-plus-year-old cigar company just steamroll over the competition, producing a string of hits to gain a whole new generation of aficionado followers. This cigar, however, takes a couple of steps back to show the uninitiated that Nat Sherman has always known what they're doing. An update to the classic Connecticut-coated Host, the Host Maduro takes the smooth Honduran filler and binder recipe and turns it into an egalitarian treasure with the addition of a chocolatey Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper of exemplary quality and taste. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) Preferring to let the cigar speak for itself, Nat Sherman has dressed the Host Maduro in the same simple yet colorful and decorative band as its predecessor. The Broadleaf wrapper is oily, smooth, and expertly applied atop longleaf filler which wafts the aroma of plums and alfalfa from the foot. The cigar is sweet and creamy from the start, with almond and nougat evident within the cured tobacco and roasted coffee flavors that permeate the billowing smoke. Some leather and a touch of vanilla enter during the later stages of the slow, straight burn which keep this medium-bodied dream alive and kicking until the end. Find out for yourself why Nat Sherman has been able to thrive throughout the past decades by trying a Nat Sherman Host Maduro now. Just one puff and you'll come to understand why so many smokers young and old are flocking to the brand, with every puff afterward proving to yourself that you'll be doing the same time and again. Priced for everyone and able to be enjoyed by all, this is truly a historic cigar.

Originally made as an exclusive for a prominent New York gentlemen's club, Nat Sherman knew their Metropolitan cigars were too good not to offer to everyone. This fantastic mild bodied smoke is made in the Dominican Republic and is one of Shermans oldest and most well-known lines. The expertly aged Dominican wrapper and filler tobacco is draped in a gorgeous Connecticut shade wrapper leaf. Mild in body, this smoke is never lacking in flavor and is the perfect cigar to start out your day. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) With a vintage feel to the cigar comes the amazing band featuring the iconic Nat Sherman clock and logo. One look at the wrapper and you realize that this is the Connecticut wrapped masterpiece that all others should be judged against. When you light up a Metropolitan you are swept away to the pre-boom era with its sweet mild taste and amazing woodsy aroma. This may be mild but the amount of flavors that tickle your taste buds with every puff is sure to leave a lasting impression. From the beautiful Connecticut wrapper to the tantalizing aroma, Nat Sherman Metropolitan Natural is a cigar that every mild cigar smoker should try at least once, and most likely after that first one, more than once. Perfect for when you wake up, this is the cigar to start your day, and at an affordable price, this is a great stick to hand to friends to get them into the hobby. For a slightly stronger yet sweeter taste, give the Metropolitan Maduro a shot. It is sure to please as well.

The Nat Sherman Metropolitan Habano cigar is yet another stellar release from a company who, for a variety of very good reasons, is experiencing a resurgent popularity. Slinging fine cigars to all corners of New York society since 1930, Nat Sherman is now a worldwide phenomenon providing a range of smokes for every type of aficionado. The Metropolitan Habano is a Nicaraguan Puro tailored towards those who favor medium-full strength loaded with earthy, complex, full-bodied flavors. This is achieved through the judicious application of nothing but aged, perfectly fermented longleaf tobaccos skillfully rolled beneath a silky, golden-brown Habano wrapper. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) Resisting the urge to merely chomp into the sharply constructed Nat Sherman Metropolitan Habano due to its savory, nutty aroma and glistening appearance, the wise smoker will instead wield their favorite cutter to open a path to the thickly bunched longleaf within. An excellent draw and smoothly lit foot provide the palate with creamy clouds laden with cedar, roasted peanut, and chocolate flavors that dominate through the first third. French-roast coffee rises during the second third, backed by a sweetness reminiscent of marzipan and caramel. Finishing rich, with black pepper and citrus-laced sourdough toast, it is a cigar full of satisfaction. Exceedingly well-priced for a Puro of this quality and strength, grab an 18-count box or two and get ready to have the some of the best smoking times of your life. A Nat Sherman Metropolitan Habano cigar paired with a modern gin, a cooler-full of session ales, or a morning cup of joe, will elevate any moment. Just make sure you do not run out.

Nat Sherman Metropolitan Maduro has come a long way since its small introduction into the night club scene. Now mass produced by Nat Sherman Cigars in the Dominican Republic, Metropolitan Maduro has become a wonderful cigar for anyone looking for a mild-medium maduro experience. Using filler and binder tobacco from the Dominican Republic, Metropolitan Maduro is capped off with a dark Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) Nat Sherman Metropolitan Maduro is a classic maduro cigar. From chocolate to coffee to brown sugar to a sweet, subtle finish, this stick has it all. The construction is fantastic and the flavors are very crisp and clear. Well-balanced, easy to smoke, and a pleasant choice for any occasion, it's no wonder why Metropolitan Maduro has become so popular. Beginner to seasoned aficionado, basic tastes to discriminating pickiness, anyone and everyone will enjoy Nat Sherman Metropolitan Maduro. It pairs well with coffee, especially the "cafe con leche" (coffee with cream/milk) variety, and can be compared to other milder maduros such as Arturo Fuente Maduro and CAO Gold Maduro. There is a reason Nat Sherman Metropolitan Maduro has made it this far: the quality is always superb and the price is just right.

When was the last time you had a Nat Sherman cigar of any kind, let alone the Nat Sherman Timeless Prestige? Don't worry, you're not alone if you can't quite remember. Hailing from the 1930s the brand has been showing its age as of late, but fresh off of a Top 10 rating from Cigar Aficionado as part of their 25 Best of 2012 it might be time to revisit this New York-based cigar icon. Calling upon old friends like the Plasencia family for tobacco and Manuel Quesada for his blending expertise, the Timeless Prestige is rolled in the Dominican Republic using local and Nicaraguan leaves bound by a wrapper from Honduras. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) The cigar is so shiny with oils you wouldn't be faulted for expecting it to be dripping while the aroma is grassy and crisp. A cold draw delivers a pungent sharpness similar to that of fresh-rolled cigars, but once lit the volumes of smoke embody all of the characteristics and maturity of well-aged and perfectly fermented tobacco. This results in there being no single defining flavor at any one point in the smoking experience, just wave after wave of sensations that might be coffee and raisins one moment only to change to cherry stem and toffee and citrus the next. Overall, you'll find the Timeless Prestige a sophisticated, ever-changing medium to full bodied cigar you won't want to put down. With a classic taste that still manages to appeal to modern sensibilities, Nat Sherman has stepped forward with their Timeless Prestige to announce that the brand still has some life. Time will tell if they can keep it up but for now, their latest offering sits proudly alongside other top-25 cigars like the Rocky Patel Fifty and Kristoff Corojo Limitada .

The Nat Sherman Timeless Supreme cigar continues the resurgence of a brand that started a comeback in 2012 with a Top 10 best of the year rating for the Dominican Republic version of the same cigar. Now, for this Nicaraguan Puro, the decades-old Nat Sherman Company has enlisted the aid of Nestor Plasencia, a man who knows just a bit about tobacco and cigars. And yes, that's an understatement. He's sold tobacco to and made cigars for, pretty much everyone in the business at one point or another. Now with this cigar, he's applied his talents to one of the most exciting redemption stories in recent history. (See more Nat Sherman Cigars ) The flavor booms from the cigar right after lighting, the thick smoke loaded with a meaty fullness and tongue tingling tea-like sweetness. Complex from start to finish, this cigar is smooth and balanced but offers the chance for some spiciness in the nose during a retrohale. The strength starts out as a solid medium and builds throughout the smoking time to a potency that creates a nice buzz without causing much distress in the belly. Equally impressive when paired with spring water, a crisp cola, or a gin and tonic, the Nat Sherman Timeless Supreme will restore your faith in the good taste and classic sensibilities of old-fashioned tobacconists.

Nub Cameroon is another addition to the hugely popular Nub line of cigars by Studio Tobac and Oliva in Nicaragua. The idea behind the Nub brand is that given the correct combination of length and ring gauge, along with an expert blend of tobacco, the cigar will show its true colors, or its "sweet spot" within seconds of lighting. Whether or not this is the case, Nub has been a resounding success story since its introduction, and the Cameroon blend is among the favorites. This caramel-colored beauty consists of a hearty core of Nicaraguan filler, Nicaraguan binder, and a gorgeous, toothy Cameroon wrapper. Although much shorter than normal cigars, Nubs provide a similar smoking time to an average toro or churchill, depending on the size. The innovative short, large-ring format proved its merit in the industry when the Nub Cameroon 358 earned a 92 rating and was honored as the #23 Cigar of the Year in the Cigar Aficionado Top 25 of 2015 . Nub Cameroon has a classic Cameroon profile. It starts off earthy, yet sweet, then gradually gains strength as heavy notes of cedar and white pepper begin to come about. The finish is very crisp and clean, and Nub Cameroon is indubitably a true medium-bodied cigar . While the Nub cigars were originally intended for more experienced and demanding aficionados, the Cameroon version can be easily enjoyed by anyone. It's easy on the palate and never overwhelming, yet complex and enjoyable enough to smoke any time throughout the day. It pairs well with white wine or light beer and can be compared to Oliva Serie G and Arturo Fuente. Bigger isn't always better when it comes to cigars, and if you disagree, maybe you should try a Nub Cameroon today.

Four horsemen ride comfortably as Studio Tobac's standard Nub line of cigars, and it is the Nub Connecticut by Oliva that is mellowest of all. Of course, this is in comparison to robust and potent blends which start out full-flavored and full-bodied, so it's all relative. Since it contains a complex and hearty blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos throughout the entirety of its stout form, a lovely Cameroon binder, and finally the Ecuadorian shade wrapper on this Nub serves to bring strength and body into a range closer to medium rather than a truly mild smoke. Warm and rich from the moment it is lit, this is definitely not like those flimsy, watery, one-dimensional Connecticut stogies of yesteryear. Instead, soft leather and black coffee start blasting from the chunky cigar to fill your palate and nose with a robust taste and aroma. Almost immediately, flavors broaden and shift to produce hints of spice and oak with just enough of a shade wrapper's familiar grassiness. Once you reach the point where solid ash makes up half of what you hold in your hand, plenty of sweet cream and a little nuttiness will have smoothed the thick smoke into an awesome treat. Scrumptious! Looking for a quick smoke to fill the gaps in your day? Well, this is not it, since each Nub Connecticut contains enough tobacco to be considered a full-size cigar and will deliver at least an hour's worth of enjoyment even with the 'smallest' vitola. Perhaps you should consider going with something like the Café au Lait version of El Rey Del Mundo or, if you're into infused smokes, some Acid Krush Classic. However, if what you seek is a solid and well-made stick capable of pumping out reams of smoke with loads of flavor, then you've come to the right page.

Nub Dub is the second cigar in a series of limited releases by Studio Tobac, makers of Nub, Cain, and other Oliva side projects. Hailing from Nicaragua like all Oliva cigars , Nub Dub follows the rest of the hugely successful Nub cigars rolled in just the right size to start in the "sweet spot," the part of the cigar with the most intense flavor. Nub Dub is the exact same cigar in all aspects as the original Nub Maduro, except with a second maduro wrapper leaf to act as the binder, hence the name Nub Dub, or "Double," referring to the double Brazilian maduro leaves holding together the Cuban seed Nicaraguan filler blend. The result is a refined, bold, well-balanced cigar with top-notch complexity and luxurious flavor. Nub Dub is a stout, firmly packed package of power. Despite the small size, Nub Dub will smoke as long as a normal-sized cigar due to its large ring gauge and densely packed filler blend. In many cases, 2+ hours is not unreasonable. Nub Dub starts out bold from the get-go. A blast of spicy pepper is the initial greeting, followed by the rich, chocolate bouquet common with most fuller-bodied maduro cigars . An earthy, toasty core remains heavy and rich, all the while gaining intensity from the spicy Brazilian wrappers. Nutty cocoa is apparent on the finish. Overall, a very enjoyable smoke. The Nub cigars were invented with direct aim at seasoned connoisseurs. However, over the years the younger crowd has taken a huge liking to the Nubs, probably because of their innovative approach to achieving the best flavor possible in a small package. Nub Dub can be enjoyed by just about anyone, just keep in mind the entire experience rests on the heavy side of medium-full-bodied, so if you're not into strong sticks, it's probably not for you. Nub Dub should be a no-brainer for fans of maduro cigars, as it captures the true, textbook flavor profile of a stout maduro cigar that others attempt so desperately to accomplish. It pairs well with coffee, dark beer, and bourbon, and can be compared to Nub Maduro and Camacho Triple Maduro in terms of flavor, body, and construction. Nub Dub is a go-to for anyone looking for a cigar that takes classic maduro flavor and brings it into this new day and age where intense, bold cigars are all the rage.

Crafting a quality cigar is serious business, and creating something new is even more of a serious challenge, but the Nub Habano manages to achieve both while being a serious value. Seriously. Alright, alright, we'll stop. But you can't deny Nub as a brand has transcended its short, stout form to become a popular and well-regarded stogie with fans from all parts of the aficionado spectrum. You may think it gimmicky, but smoke just one, and you'll quickly come to love the complex and cool smoking blend of Nicaraguan filler and Indonesian binder tobacco covered in, what else, a delicious Habano wrapper. Being able to choose from among the best leaf to be found in Oliva's vast growing empire has given Nub's rollers a perfect excuse to show off their skills. With nothing less than a 58 ring gauge and no length longer than four inches there's so much tobacco packed into every vitola it would be understandable to find the occasional soft spot or plugged draw, but somehow each one is as flawless as the next. This means that all the smoker has to do is sit back and enjoy the crisp flavors of fresh roast coffee, oak, caramel, and a touch of red pepper. Okay, just one more time: Nub Habano cigars have garnered some seriously good ratings including an 88 and a solid 91. Reminiscent of an Oliva Serie V but priced to impress even the most frugal, your biggest problem will be having enough on hand to keep up with all of the reasons you'll find to smoke one. Good thing we've got plenty kept in perfect condition in our warehouse and shipped to you ultra-fast when you need them. You're needing some now, aren't you?

You can't really blame Oliva Cigars for being skeptical when Sam Leccia proposed what would become Nub Maduro . At the time, smokes of such stature were uncommon, and they really couldn't know if he could pull off his goal of creating a line of smokes able to fire up at the cigar's 'sweet spot'. However, when you're a legend, people tend to give you the benefit of the doubt. And good thing they did. Smooth and creamy from the get-go with aged Nicaraguan leaf throughout and a toothy Mexican wrapper seemingly gifted from the gods, each chunky stick places excellent flavor as priority Numero Uno! Unless you have been living under a rock, it is clear that taking classic cigar brands and giving them a new life has been quite a trend over the past few years. Additionally, there is one man behind just about every instance of this, and that man is AJ Fernandez, someone that has proven to be one of the most dominating forces in today’s premium cigar industry. In the case of Onyx Bold Nicaragua, we have a Cigar Boom classic that has all but disappeared, and it now makes its return as a phenomenal landmark in the Altadis USA portfolio. Made by hand at the legendary Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A., this impressive blend includes Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, a Nicaraguan binder beneath a nearly jet-black Mexican San Andres wrapper leaf. Though straightforward, this cigar has proven to be nothing short of incredible, and if there was ever a way to put Onyx back in the spotlight, this is it. Black cabinet boxes house the expertly crafted vitolas, each one wearing no less than three bands. Black, white, and silver are the color theme, and how appropriate, as this cigar is every bit as fancy as it is strong. Precision rolling leads to an easy draw and immaculate smoke production, and this smoke is not for the faint of heart. Spicy Nicaraguan pepper is the first flavor to greet the palate upon lighting, soon followed by a hefty dose of cedar and cocoa. The dominating earthy core is established quickly, and the hearty raw tobacco remains constant in the background. Notes of espresso and dark chocolate sweeten things up, and the finish is rich and earthy. Full-bodied, incredibly balanced, and uncompromisingly satisfying, Onyx Bold Nicaragua is a winner from the first light. Made for more experienced cigar enthusiasts, Onyx Bold Nicaragua is a true showcase of AJ Fernandez’s blending prowess when it comes to stronger cigars. Full-bodied but never overpowering, Onyx Bold Nicaragua easily compares to cigars costing twice as much. It is well paired with black coffee, dark beer, or port wine and is best enjoyed after a meal. Fans of cigars such as Trinidad Espiritu Series 3 or H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez will certainly enjoy the flavor profile and stout nature of this blend. It seems like astonishing the cigar world is a daily task for AJ Fernandez, and Onyx Bold Nicaragua proves that new life can certainly be given to a classic brand, even if it has become all but forgotten along the way.

A premium puro for just about every aficionado, the Onyx Vintage Nicaragua is a powerhouse cigar that destroys the line between excellent value and superior taste. Such a wondrous accomplishment would normally be cause for celebration and wonder but when you discover the creator of these all-Nicaraguan vitolas is A.J. Fernandez, that famous dark wizard of stogie-making magic, should come as no surprise. To craft this follow up to the immensely popular Onyx Bold, Fernandez dug into his collection of prime tobaccos to rediscover a cache of Nicaraguan Habano wrappers that were harvested in 2019 and then left in a dark warehouse corner to rest and develop ever since. Using this treasure as inspiration, A.J. then blended a choice selection of succulent Nicaraguan longleaf to serve as the filler and binder to produce a cigar that delivers the type of satisfying and medium-full smoking experience so many of us hope for on a daily basis. Departing from the usual near-black wrapper found on the other Onyx frontmarks, each Onyx Vintage Nicaragua is a naturally mottled brown, the well-aged and oily tobacco glinting with hints of gold and red. Wafting a mouthwatering aroma and with a sticky-sweet taste on the lips, the unlit cigar demands a strong flame able to get the packed foot fully alight and pumping out the initial flavors of robust cocoa, black pepper, and a chewy-rich earthiness. As the straight and sharp burn line slowly makes its way down the barrel, the palate will reveal to the tastes of smooth cedar, leather, toasted walnut, vanilla bean, and blackstrap molasses. The strength and body do rise a little during the final half-hour or so of smoking time, but the patient smoker will be rewarded with plenty of cool and creamy smoke to get them through. For those of you planning to wait to buy their allotment of these fine cigars, do be advised that the 2019 Habano wrapper is in limited supply, so the Onyx Vintage Nicaragua will eventually end up with a wrapper from a later harvest. They’ll certainly be as delicious thanks to the blending prowess of A.J. Fernandez, but for those who like their smokes a little on the rare side, such as the Rocky Patel Special Edition or even the Cain F Limited Edition, this is an opportunity to get in on the ground floor.

When life seems as though it is moving too fast, when days and weeks and even months pass in the blink of an eye, a slow-burning cigar like the Oscar Valladares 10th Anniversary Salomon gives you the chance to take a break from the hustle. Representing the best of the brand after ten hard fought years of quality smokes like Leaf by Oscar Valladares, The Oscar, and the totally heavy 92-rated McFly, this exquisite handmade is loaded with deliciously well-rested tobacco, as both the Honduran filler blend and Honduran binder are at least 5 years aged. Two wrappers are used to contain and elevate the potent longleaf within, the first is a naturally dark San Andres from Mexico that coats most of the stout vitola from the cap on down, while a bright and fragrant Honduran Candela covers approximately the first inch of the foot. A rare treat is for us all to have the time to enjoy a fine cigar, so nobody has time for a bland, boring, or simply bad smoke. Fortunately, these exceptionally well-crafted Oscar Valladares 10th Anniversary is ready to deliver massive flavor and delectable taste from the moment the head is clipped. A firm but steady cold draw brings hints of dark cocoa and warm spice soon to burst onto the palate as the barrel is lit. A crisp alfalfa-like freshness from the Candela accompanies a rich earthiness during the first long minutes of the smoke, with the profile shifting at the sweet spot towards creamy mocha, roasted peanuts, caramel, anise, and a touch of citrus. At some point during the session, expect to remove both colorful bands that decorate each stogie because this is a stick you’ll smoke down to the nub. Make sure to take your time when you light up your first Oscar Valladares 10th Anniversary because it’s an experience you’ll want to return to again and again. A heady, delicious cigar in the same league as fan favorites like CAO BX3 or even the Oliva Serie V Melanio, you won’t have to wait long for your stash because we’re ready to ship them to your door right now!

Oscar Valladares is known for making some of the most unique and marketable cigars in the business, cigars that stand out in the crowd and grab the attention of people looking for something special. That being said, it’s no surprise that a cigar as beautifully dressed as Oscar Valladares Ciseron would be one of the company’s standouts. Paying homage to famed Honduran artist Elmer Ciseron Bautista , this delectable blend is available in 5 variations: Black, Blue, Deep Purple, Green, and Yellow, and 500 boxes (20 cigars in each box) of each color were made . That makes this brand limited to 50,000 cigars in total, so keep that in mind if you catch yourself hesitating. For clarity, the different color variations only refer to the packaging, while the recipe is exactly the same across the board: Nicaraguan fillers, Nicaraguan binder, and a rich brown Ecuadorian wrapper . Ironically, this is the first cigar from Oscar Valladares that doesn’t contain Honduran tobacco. We have no complaints, though, because this is no doubt an incredible smoke. The theme here is art , and Valladares certainly did a wonderful job of making that the major selling point. Each box displays a piece of Bautista’s artwork , making the top of the box appear to be a displayable picture frame. Each cigar is clothed with a 3/4-body band, also displaying even more artwork. Solid construction by the skilled hands at the Oscar Valladares factory in Honduras lends to a productive draw that coats the palate with immense flavor on every puff. An introduction of cedar and nuts lays the foundation, and hints of cocoa, bread, and espresso show up as the cigar progresses. The main star is a solid layer of raw Nicaraguan tobacco flavor that is just spicy enough to open up the taste buds. Medium-bodied , Ciseron is a cigar that tastes every bit as good as it looks. This blend is available in one size, a 6” x 52 Toro that burns slow and provides plenty of time to bask in the satisfying flavor that was worked so hard for. Not exactly a beginner’s cigar, Ciseron should appeal to a more experienced crowd that has at least been around the block a few times, so to speak. Its layered flavor profile, alluring complexity, and medium body are meant to satisfy a well-seasoned palate. Pair this one with your favorite coffee, dark rum, or medium-bodied beer and experience a truly classic smoking experience. If you have come to love some of Oscar Valladares’ other edgy offerings, such as Super Fly or Raw Dog , this one should be the next one on your list. It pays tribute to fine art while being a work of art in its own right, delivering a refined smoking experience that only Oscar Valladares can produce.

After having decimated his own lineup in one of the most surprising shakeups since Sammy Hagar replaced David Lee Roth as frontman of Van Halen, esteemed tobacco-whisperer Ernesto Padilla, along with his brother Carlos, continue to fill out the new Padilla cigar roster with a Connecticut. If you are a fortunate smoker who has a history with Ernesto’s smokes, it’s time to reacquaint yourself with his talents. Taking a break from his potent Reserva and Reserva Maduro, Padilla scouted out a wrapper grown on shady slopes in beautiful Ecuador, where fertile volcanic soils are also responsible for the Habano leaf used as a binder, to place around his juicy blend of Corojo and Criollo from Nicaragua. An even more appropriate mascot when trimmed in gold and black, Padilla’s lion guards the oily and golden brown wrapper until ready to clip and light. Take the opportunity to perform a cold draw test to appreciate what can be accomplished through expert craftsmanship and savor crisp tobacco and grassy notes. Slowly and carefully char the foot to ensure a solid burn and once fully lit take a mouthful of velvety smoke to detect warm nutmeg and vanilla sprinkled with black pepper. Additional exploration will reveal a medium strength cigar at times full of fresh hay and cedar, other times kissed with molasses and cinnamon. Sitting firmly in the sweet spot between low price and high quality, a box of Padilla Connecticut will serve as a good friend with your morning coffee, after lunch paired with ginger ale, or to take the edge off during a long commute home. A shade wrapped cigar more in line with a Camacho Connecticut than a Montecristo, if you’re looking for loads of flavor and a little bit of a kick, this is the smoke for you.

The Padilla Reserva Habano cigar is hereby serving notice that Ernesto Padilla is back. Back big. Now that you think about it, you really haven't noticed many Padillas around lately, have you? Strange at it may sound for brand with a plethora of 90-plus ratings, this was by design. Ernesto wanted to get back to his roots as a boutique cigar maker so he discontinued a number of his too-big-to-fail frontmarks, hid away in what was probably a really cool and inspirational man-cave, and came out bearing the Padilla Reserva line. The Habano version is graced with an sleek Ecuadorian wrapper laid over a triple threat of Nicaraguan fillers from Esteli, Jalapa, and Condega. Picking right up where he left off, Padilla has another winner in the Reserva Habano cigar. With a complexity that rivals some of his previous smokes and a medium to full body, this cigar should please any connoisseur. While they're still in stock, you might want to compare to some of Ernesto's older cigars like the spectacular Padilla Signature 1932.

Padilla Single Batch Barrel Proof is the first cigar to be produced in the brand new Tabacalera Padilla in Nicaragua, which opened its doors in mid-2019. Being the first production cigar out of a new factory carries great expectations, especially when produced under the close supervision of such a superstar as long-time industry veteran Ernesto Padilla. Not surprisingly, those expectations were exceeded with this modern classic, which consists of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a dark, oily San Andres wrapper leaf from Mexico. The filler and binder leaves happen to be authentic Cuban seed Corojo grown on the famed Aganorsa farms in Jalapa. All tobacco used in the blend undergoes extensive aging, yielding a final product that is as smooth as it is rich.

As one of the most prolific names in the history of premium cigars, Padron has dazzled millions of cigar enthusiasts across the globe for many years. Whether you mention the heavily-awarded 1926 series, the mind-numbing Family Reserve, or even the meat-and-potatoes Thousand series, there is virtually zero likelihood of anything less than positive praise to be said in response. So what happens when a brand like Padron does something even more extraordinary than their usual? We get a prized gem like Padron Black Natural . Originally released over a decade ago as the Jose O. Padron Birthday Blend , Padron Black has become available in various sizes and through various avenues over the years, from a TAA Exclusive offering to a prize given to Cigar Rights of America donors, it wasn’t until just recently that you could casually pick one up at a retailer. Nuts and cinnamon begin to spice things up in the background, and a rich, earthy Nicaraguan tobacco core establishes itself as the dominant part of the flavor profile. Rich, deep, complex, and powerful, this undeniably full-bodied masterpiece will doubtless leave a lasting impression. Built for only the most distinguished, experienced, and discriminating cigar connoisseurs, Padron Black Natural is a stick that should be held in the highest regard. Full-bodied and complex, one can expect an unforgettable smoking experience along with a sense of being in the company of an elite few that have had the honor of enjoying one. Paired with the finest scotch or bourbon, Padron Black Natural becomes the epitome of a special occasion celebration. Fans of Padron Family Reserve or 1926 are sure to enjoy this one, but enjoy it with caution, as this might become your favorite. Sometimes, we as cigar enthusiasts have to fulfill the need to treat ourselves to something special. That being said, when it comes to fine cigars, it doesn’t get much more special than the legendary Padron Black Natural.

The Padron Family Reserve cigars will no doubt go down in history as some of the greatest cigars of all time. A rich family legacy, combined with unmatched quality and blending prowess and some of the world's finest tobacco, make the Family Reserve cigars so incredible that they retain a near permanent residence in Cigar Aficionado's Top 25. Partagas, a brand long known for amazing medium-bodied cigars, has ventured into a whole new arena with its 1845 Extra Fuerte line. Released as an extension of the heritage line in 2012, Extra Fuerte is General Cigars attempt to hit that ever growing market of full-bodied-cigar smokers, and it is an amazing success. With an Ecuadorian Habano ligero wrapper and Connecticut Habano binder, the extra power behind the Extra Fuerte is in the filler blend of Dominican Piloto Cubano and Nicaraguan tobaccos. Anyone who seeks this cigar out needs to put behind any notions of whatever Partagas they had in the past, because this will surely blow you away. The regal looking black and silver band lets the smoker know from the get-go that they are in for a special cigar. A fine aroma of sweet cedar and earth blows past your sinuses as you bring the stick up to be met with flame. The first few puffs will make your taste buds stand up and take notice as a strong flavor of pepper and a cinnamon-like spice dances over your palate. The pepper is most noticeable in the retrohale where it has an almost horseradish like sensation that is extremely pleasant. The construction, as one would expect from a brand like Partagas, is top notch and burned straight throughout the entire time with this masterpiece. If you like fuller-bodied cigars and have dismissed Partagas in the past, the 1845 Extra Fuerte will be the cigar to make you love this classic brand. Likewise if you are used to the normal medium-bodied blends, grab a seat and give this a whirl, it will surely open your eyes to a whole new world of cigar smoking. This is most definitely and after dinner cigar, and pairs perfectly with a nice dark roasted coffee.

A hearty and flavorful cigar from a brand that every aficionado should fully explore, the Partagas 1845 Extra Oscuro is destined to be your next new obsession. With a tobacco legacy stretching all the way back to the middle of the nineteenth century, Partagas has been the go-to frontmark for legions of smokers who know taste and quality are paramount. This supreme full flavored stogie is no exception, being stacked with barrel-aged Dominican and Nicaraguan Ligero longleaf filler beneath a rich Dominican La Vega Especial binder and finished with a dark and oily Connecticut Habano Oscuro of unsurpassed character. The glorious eagle adorning each regal purple and silver band is an apt metaphor, for these sleek vitolas will fly from your humidor with amazing grace and speed once their true deliciousness is discovered. Redolent with the aromas of cedar, fresh hay, and sourwood honey, the Partagas 1845 Extra Oscuro will have you and your smoking buddies chomping at the bit as a cutter and lighter make the rounds. The easy pulls during the first third come loaded with leather, dark chocolate, red pepper, and cane syrup. Midway through, the creamy smoke provides ample black coffee and mesquite flavors, while the final third pours on the charm with plenty of spice, earth, and even more delectable chocolate. Pinch yourself if you wish, but you'll be hard pressed to dream up a better deal for fistfuls of Partagas 1845 Extra Oscuros than you can find right here. You know you want some, especially if you're a fan of other dark and heavy sticks like the Camacho American Barrel Aged or 601 Habano Oscuro. However, even if this is your first foray into something with a little more kick than your usual smoke, you won't be disappointed.

Partagas Black Label Cigars can be considered a "new age" Partagas, created during the rise of the full-bodied cigar era to satisfy smokers who would become this generation’s connoisseurs of serious strength. Blended by Benji Menendez and his team, and handcrafted in the Dominican Republic, Partagas Black is a striking cigar made with a heavy blend of ligero fillers from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. The binder is a robust Dominican leaf, and the wrapper is a pitch-black Medio Tiempo Connecticut Broadleaf Oscuro, aged approximately 50% longer than most harvested leaves. The result is a bold, sweet, and utterly unforgettable smoking experience. The ultra-oily stick burns sharply and evenly, releasing powerful bursts of white pepper and rich espresso flavors . Sweetness is present throughout, finishing with a lingering and pronounced cocoa note. It’s a classic maduro flavor profile, elevated with additional intensity and sweetness. Partagas Black is not for the faint of heart. As one of the pioneering powerhouse cigars, it remains among the heaviest sticks on the market today. Pair it with coffee or port wine, and never smoke it on an empty stomach. Comparable cigars include Casa Magna Oscuro and La Gloria Cubana Serie R Maduro. If you’re ready to venture into the dark side of full-bodied smoking, do so with Partagas Black. See the Cigar Aficionado Ratings .

Hewing closely to the premium flavor and quality that is an integral part of a long and storied heritage, the Partagas Cifuentes cigar is a medium-strength dream come true for legions of smokers. There are any number of cigar brands new and old striving to recreate the historic experience of hand-rolled tobacco as it was meant to be, but few can claim to be the descendant of a man like Ramon Cifuentes. As former head of Partagas in Cuba, Cifuentes worked tirelessly to summon the tastes of his homeland once arrived on distant shores. This Dominican Puro, containing a wealth of Piloto Cubano longleaf beneath its flawless Corojo wrapper, proves his legacy lives on. Seemingly unremarkable beneath crisp cellophane, once in hand the densely packed Partagas Cifuentes exhibits a coating of delectable tooth amid the oily sheen which promises a lip-smacking experience. Smelling like an old barn full of leather and wood, each vitola responds with flavorful gusto at first to the cold draw and then to a steady flame. When sipped with a tawny port or dark liquor in the waning hours of the evening, the smoke which pours onto the palate is thick with sweet cedar, French-roast coffee, black cherry, and wet stone. As the minutes lengthen and the cigar's nub approaches ever slower, mind and body will relax even as the tongue thrills to long hidden pockets of salt and pepper pistachios, vanilla cream, and nutmeg. Forget your usual standbys that have become so routine, it's time to discover some delicious new cigar favorites even if they are the vintage brands known and loved for decades. In addition to the remarkably affordable Partagas Cifuentes, perhaps a Montecristo Platinum or H. Upmann 1844 Legacy will get you out of that rut. Your old man would be proud.

It’s been quite some time since any new blends have come out bearing the legendary Partagas name, so it goes without question that when Partagas Valle Verde hit the scene, it was big news. The first Partagas cigar to wear a Mexican wrapper, this top tier blend is made in Honduras at the STG Danli factory using a unique three-country blend of tobacco from the middle out. The filler consists of San Andres leaves from Mexico and Nicaraguan leaves from the lush tobacco regions of Esteli and Jalapa. All filler leaves come from the 2020 harvest. The binder, interestingly, is a Cameroon leaf from the 2015 harvest, and the beautiful dark brown wrapper is an oily, silky smooth San Andres leaf from Mexico, also from the 2020 harvest to match the fillers. Valle Verde literally translates to “Green Valley,” a reference to the famed growing region. Packaged in beautifully modernized green boxes, each vitola wears a sizable green and white band denoting the blend. Solid construction includes a near-seamless roll, a productive draw, and tight gray ash. Unlike many cigars utilizing a San Andres leaf as the wrapper, Valle Verde begins with warm, soft flavors with just the right amount of pepper in the background. This flavor soon turns sweet, with notes of cocoa and brown sugar surrounding a core of earthy tobacco flavor. The smoke is thick and creamy, the finish is short and crisp, and overall, Valle Verde finishes smack dab in the middle of the strength scale as a well-rounded medium-bodied cigar. Made for connoisseurs but suitable for just about anyone. Partagas Valle Verde can be summed up as a medium-bodied cigar with fantastic balance and a satisfying and interesting flavor profile. There is nothing overpowering, nothing too complicated, and nothing that should make a newer cigar enthusiast shy away from trying it. Valle Verde pairs well with red wine, cognac, or coffee and is just right for any time of day. Fans of darker, flavorful sticks such as Oliva Serie O Maduro or Perdomo Reserve Maduro should thoroughly enjoy this delightful new treat, as it, too, is technically a Maduro cigar that won’t disappoint in the flavor category. There are long-time Partagas fans, new smokers, and folks that just want to keep up with the newest cigars in the ever-growing premium tobacco business. Regardless of the group you fall into, Partagas Valle Verde is sure to be a great addition to your humidor.

pdr-a-flores-1975-serie-privada-capa-hab.name: A. Flores 1975 Serie Privada Capa Habano

note_sources.text: The PDR A. Flores Serie Privada Edicion Especial Habano is the type of cigar that makes you believe Abe Flores is capable of magic. How else to explain the transformation of humble tobacco into such a sublime experience with the simple addition of time and heat and air? Working deep within the heart of La Fabrica, Abe gathered the factory's oldest Habano and Corojo, long-leaf conjured from Nicaraguan and Domincan farms both large and small, and used them to summon complex flavors and pungent aromas to amaze and astound smokers across the globe. (See more PDR Cigars ) Medium Bodied CigarThe cigar starts out with rich leather and a cumin-like spiciness, adds in some bitter herbs and earth in the second third, and finishes with black pepper. Medium in the beginning, it transitions to a buzzing medium-full right around the halfway point, so a good meal is recommended to prevent a heavy hit to the belly. With the knowledgeable smoker sufficiently prepared, the Privada EE Habano offers major satisfaction and relaxation, even more so when paired with a fine malt whisky. As satisfying as a Rocky Patel Decade or even the legendary Padron 1964 Natural, this cigar is a definite must-try.

pdr-flores-y-rodriguez-cabinet-seleccion.name: Flores y Rodriguez Cabinet Seleccion Maduro

note_sources.text: As the seasons change so should your regular rotation of cigars, and the PDR Flores y Rodriguez Cabinet Seleccion Maduro deserves to be in the mix. Released at IPCPR in 2012, the Cabinet Seleccion line represents the most recent Dominican Puros from Pinar Del Rio, preceded only by the 1878 Reserva Domincana Habano and 1878 Reserva Dominicana Oscuro. For this latest creation, master of the blend Abe Flores decided to develop a more distinctive cigar by crafting a recipe using only one type of tobacco. As a result, the filler, binder, and wrapper leaves are all Habano from seed originally cultivated in Vuelta Abajo which is located in, where else, the Pinar Del Rio region of Cuba. (See more PDR Cigars ) Using an approach also explored by the Toraño Single Region Serie Jalapa, this Flores y Rodriguez is a medium-bodied treat that serves as a case study in the expert use of one particular tobacco. The cigar delivers thick waves of creamy smoke loaded with cocoa and coffee flavors plus sweet spices are prevalent throughout. Packed in boxes of 24, they are an affordable and delicious addition to the humidors of beginner and experienced smokers alike. Buy today and experience the joys of discovery.

Perdomo 20th Anniversary Connecticut is the mildest cigar in Nick Perdomo's 20th Anniversary lineup. In 2012, Perdomo Cigars celebrated their first 20 years in business with the release of a special blend available in two wrappers: Nicaraguan Sun Grown and Nicaraguan Maduro. It didn't take long, however, for long-time Perdomo fans to voice their disappointment in that there was no Connecticut version of the 20th Anniversary cigar. With the customers' best interests always in mind, Nick Perdomo finally brought out this tasty treat to compliment the first two blends in the lineup. The Nicaraguan-made Perdomo 20th Anniversary Connecticut is an ultra-premium blend of the finest Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos, along with a golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It goes without saying that the cigar received a very warm welcome from Connecticut fans across the globe.
Chocolate , Espresso , Rich Available. Learn about Perdomo 20th Anniversary Maduro Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on 20th Anniversary Maduro

Years from now you'll still be pounding your chest and calling out from mountaintops about the time you first lit a Perdomo 20th Anniversary Maduro cigar . Once you taste the exquisitely balanced and perfectly fermented Nicaraguan tobaccos, including a wrapper aged an extra fourteen months in bourbon barrels, every other cigar will be placed in comparison and you won't be able to imagine a world where there is even one smoker who has yet to try one. But before you rush out to begin your new career as an emissary for Tabacalera Perdomo, consider the fact that you'll be joining legions of existing Perdomo fanatics so you may have a hard time finding someone unfamiliar with their charms.
