You don't need to wait for an invitation to any celebration when you grab a Perdomo 20th Anniversary Sun Grown cigar so just fire up that sucker and get smoking! Rich and loaded with all sorts of tantalizing flavors, each stick is a culmination of Nick Perdomo's talent and decades-long blending experience paired with the rolling expertise of his best torcedors. Also worth noting is that every long leaf of tobacco comes from Nick's own carefully tended Nicaraguan farms located in the premier growing regions of Jalapa, Condega, and Esteli. Think it stops there? Oh no, because the wrapper was aged for 14 months in old bourbon barrels to impart a tantalizing aroma and a smooth, refined taste.

When Nick Perdomo comes out with an anniversary cigar, there is little doubt that it will be anything other than amazing, and such is precisely the case with Perdomo 30 th Anniversary Connecticut. Now celebrating three incredible decades in the cigar business, Nick Perdomo began his illustrious journey with a small side hustle. Nobody would have ever guessed he would someday become an industry icon, but here we are, and what better way to commemorate his achievements than with an ultra-premium delicacy. This series, like any other Perdomo specialty line, is offered in 3 variants: Connecticut, Maduro, and Sun Grown. The filler and binder blend remains the same across the board: Nicaraguan filler and binder leaves, some aged up to 15 years. For this version of the blend, Perdomo chose a golden-brown Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper aged in bourbon barrels for added depth of flavor. The mildest of the bunch, 30 th Anniversary Connecticut provides flavor like you have never experienced from a Connecticut cigar. A dapper dress box houses the gorgeous vitolas, each one wearing an ornate red, gold, and black band inclusive of the infamous Perdomo tobacco flower logo. Expert construction on every cigar leads to an easy draw, incredible smoke production, and a straight burn every time. Spicy pepper opens up from first light, soon settling down to a creamy and silky array of cedar, nuts, and caramel. Hints of cinnamon and coffee linger in the background, and the core of the profile is distinctive of earthy raw tobacco. The finish is short and sweet, with a woody aftertaste and a hint of spice. Balanced, complex, and satisfying, Perdomo 30th Anniversary Connecticut finishes smack dab in the middle of the spectrum as a true medium-bodied cigar. Let’s face it, the 30th Anniversary series is made specifically for the most experienced connoisseurs. Can a beginner enjoy it? Sure, but the complexity and depth offered by such a top-shelf specimen are only truly appreciated by a palate that has tasted hundreds, if not thousands of cigars. These pair well with bourbon or scotch, and of course can be utilized as a phenomenal celebration cigar. Fans of Perdomo’s most well-known stick, the Reserve 10th Anniversary Champagne , will likely appreciate the similarities and, dare we say, improvements, offered by the cigar in question. A true connoisseur’s Connecticut cigar, Perdomo 30th Anniversary Connecticut is viewed by many as one of Nick Perdomo’s finest offerings to date. See also:

Perdomo 30 th Anniversary Maduro celebrates Nick Perdomo’s first three decades in the cigar business, starting from a humble side hustle to becoming an industry icon. Made at the world famous Tabacalera Perdomo in Nicaragua, this 30 th Anniversary series is available in 3 delicious variations: Sun Grown, Connecticut, and this delicious Maduro. The recipe is simple: Nicaraguan filler and binder leaves and a dark, oily Nicaraguan Maduro wrapper. All tobacco used in the production of this line is aged no less than 15 years and includes time in bourbon barrels for added depth of flavor. The 30 th Anniversary line is considered by many to be the finest offering to ever come out of Nick Perdomo’s factory. A modern take on a classic dress box houses the beautiful cigars, each wearing an ornate red, blue, and gold band bearing the Perdomo tobacco flower logo. Each vitola is immaculately constructed and offers an easy draw which produces abundant clouds on every puff. Spicy white pepper starts things off, soon followed by a sweet and complex array of cocoa, espresso, and dark chocolate. Deep, rich tobacco flavor forms the core of the flavor profile, and the finish is long and bold. Medium-full-bodied, this cigar stands out as the boldest version of the 30th Anniversary line. Not a beginners’ cigar by any means, this stick is built to impress. It is made for long-time connoisseurs that appreciate ultra-premium cigars the way they were meant to be appreciated. This stick pairs well with coffee, dark rum, or port wine and is best enjoyed after a meal. It also makes for a great way to celebrate life’s most special occasions. Fans of the Perdomo 10th Anniversary Maduro will certainly see similarities in this stick, though most would agree this one is far more refined. Whether you love maduros and want to taste one of the latest and greatest or want to take part in celebrating Perdomo’s 30 years of excellence, awaken your senses and go for a Perdomo 30th Anniversary Maduro. See also:

Perdomo 30 th Anniversary Sun Grown celebrates Nick Perdomo’s first three decades of hard work, dedication, and most of all, success in the world of premium cigars. In 1992, Nick Perdomo began selling cigars as a side hustle to his regular job as an air traffic controller. Over the years, an unexpected, yet miraculous, turn of events made his cigar business grow more and more. Now, more than 30 years later, Perdomo is a household name as far as cigars are concerned, and his products reside in millions of humidors across the globe. For this anniversary celebration, Perdomo has gone all out, utilizing tobacco that has been aged no less than 15 years. In addition, all leaves used in the production of this line spend time in bourbon barrels to add an additional layer of flavor. The line, as any Perdomo line, is available in 3 different variants: Sun Grown, Maduro, and Connecticut. This Sun Grown version contains Nicaraguan binder and filler leaves and a golden-brown sun grown Nicaraguan wrapper. Made at the world-famous Tabacalera Perdomo in Nicaragua, the 30 th Anniversary series is among the finest selection of cigars ever to bear his name. Needless to say, the Sun Grown variety has earned numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado, the best being a very commendable 93. Classic dress boxes cradle these impeccably crafted cigars, each adorned with a striking red and gold band showcasing the Perdomo tobacco flower prominently at the center. The cigars' flawless construction ensures an even burn and a smooth draw, delivering thick clouds of smoke with every puff. The flavor profile opens with cedar and white pepper, supported by a touch of Nicaraguan intensity. This soon mellows into a spicy, earthy blend of classic aged tobacco flavors, accented by subtle hints of brown sugar and citrus. Each puff delivers a clean, crisp burst of flavor, with a short, peppery finish. While not overly complex, the Perdomo 30th Anniversary Sun Grown offers a perfectly balanced, medium-to-full-bodied smoking experience that is both satisfying and refined. Made for the most experienced connoisseurs, this cigar demands a well-developed palate and the patience to savor each and every puff. Nick Perdomo is known for offering a wide variety of cigars for every experience level, and this one is for the veterans. It pairs well with bourbon or scotch, but also goes well with a simple cup of coffee if you are looking to enjoy the depth of the cigar’s flavor to the fullest. Similar in stature to Perdomo’s 10th Anniversary Sun Grown , yet a bit more refined, this cigar is bound to become one of the company’s greatest hits. If you are a fan of ultra-premium Nicaraguan cigars, we can’t help but recommend awakening your senses with Perdomo 30th Anniversary Sun Grown. See also:

Some things only get better with age, and cigars are definitely one of them. In the case of Perdomo Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Connecticut, it’s a good bet that you’ve never had a Connecticut quite like it. The Double Aged Vintage series was released several years back, and as with just about any special series offered by the Nicaraguan giant, this blend is offered in 3 wrapper variants: Connecticut, Sun Grown, and Maduro. The line is made at Nick Perdomo’s own factory in Nicaragua, and to say some serious time has gone into this stick is a serious understatement. First things first, the filler and binder blend remain the same across all 3 variants, that blend being 100% Cuban seed Nicaraguan leaves grown on the Perdomo farms. For this Connecticut offering, the wrapper leaf chosen is a golden brown Ecuadorian Connecticut, bringing about a smooth, mellow flavor and keeping this blend from being too loud. The kicker about this series is that all tobacco used for each cigar—wrapper, filler, and binder—is bale-aged for no less than 10 years. After that, the leaves are aged an additional 2 years in charred white oak bourbon barrels to bring about just the right color, texture, and aroma, according to Perdomo. So is a cigar completely made of tobacco aged for 12 years really that good? The cigar world seems to think so, and this blend is touted as one of Perdomo’s finest to date. The unmistakable tobacco flower motif sprawled across the band clearly states that this is a top-end Perdomo cigar. Each red, black, and gold Vintage band is color-coded with a stripe as well to denote the blend, and in this case it is orange. The construction is textbook Perdomo style, offering a soft, productive draw and no shortage in the smoke department. The flavor journey begins with a greeting of warm cedar and buttery-smooth, earthy raw tobacco flavor. Hints of caramel and bread crumbs are detectable early on, and the creamy texture of the smoke rolls across the palate with each and every puff. The finish is rich, with just a touch of floral sweetness. Perdomo Double Aged Vintage Connecticut finishes as a full-flavored, medium-bodied cigar that exudes impeccable balance. While this stick could certainly be thoroughly enjoyed by someone without much experience, the line, as a whole, is aimed at more seasoned enthusiasts. As is usually the case with higher-end Connecticut cigars, the flavors are so delicate that a well-rounded palate is a necessity when it comes to picking apart all the things that make the recipe so amazing. This is a phenomenal stick to pair with your favorite scotch or bourbon, and it makes a great way to celebrate life’s happy moments. Similar sticks may include Perdomo’s own 10th Anniversary Champagne or even Padron’s celebrated Damaso . If you are a fan of those Connecticut cigars that offer just a bit more in the flavor department, Perdomo Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Connecticut is a cigar that absolutely belongs in your humidor. See also:

Perdomo Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Maduro is the third, and final, installment in the Double Aged Vintage series that has satisfied millions of cigar lovers since its introduction in 2014. Handmade in Nicaragua at the famed Tabacalera Perdomo, this incredible series of cigars uses tobacco with more than twice the age of your typical ultra-premium stogie. As the process goes, all tobacco used in the construction of this series undergoes no less than 10 years of bale aging to bring the leaves beyond full maturity. After this, and only after this, does the same tobacco get transferred to the second stage of aging, this time in charred white oak bourbon barrels. This part of the process lasts an additional 2 years, bringing the total to (at least) 12 years! Expect delectable flavor and unmatched balance with each and every Double Aged Vintage cigar. For this maduro version, we have Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler tobacco, a Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder, and a dark, ultra-oily Nicaraguan Maduro wrapper. The Perdomo tobacco leaf logo glistens with gold around the edges on each elaborate cigar band. The coded color for the band on this Maduro variant is violet, and it looks beautiful against the nearly-black wrapper leaf, which seems to ooze with oils that sparkle in the light. Trademark Perdomo construction ensures great performance every single time, so there will always be a steady stream of thick, blue smoke. White pepper and oak are the first detectable flavors, and they greet the palate in a big way. This spicy opening settles very quickly into a sweet and creamy array of dark chocolate, coffee, and cinnamon. A hint of cayenne spiciness lingers in the back of the throat, and the finish is smooth and rich. This medium-full-bodied treasure boasts all the classic maduro attributes, but adds some edgy Nicaraguan flare to round it out into a phenomenal specimen of a cigar. Made for connoisseurs, the Maduro version of the Double Aged series is usually the one people tend to go for. Its medium-full body, complex and unique maduro flavor profile, and top-shelf feel just seem to rub the real cigar lovers the right way. This pairs with bourbon, coffee, or port wine, and is best enjoyed in the evening after a hearty meal. Fans of Perdomo’s classic 10th Anniversary Maduro or even the Maduro version of the Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged series should thoroughly enjoy this darker version of the series in question. Whether you are an avid maduro fanatic or just want a rich, tasty cigar with a fantastic flavor profile, Perdomo Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Maduro is one you definitely won’t want to pass up. See also:

perdomo-double-aged-12-year-vintage-sun-.name: Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Sun Grown

note_sources.text: Perdomo is one of the biggest names in the cigar business, and it never ceases to amaze connoisseurs the world over when they bring amazing blends to the table at more-than-reasonable prices. One such blend is the Perdomo Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Sun Grown. Part of the Double Aged Vintage series, which also includes a Connecticut and Maduro variant, this Sun Grown is known to be aimed at an audience that wants just a bit more intensity out of their cigars. Like all Perdomo cigars, it is made by hand at Tabacalera Perdomo in Nicaragua. Unlike other cigars, however, the special part about this series is that all tobacco used for the cigars is bale aged for no less than 10 years. After that, the leaves spend an additional 2 years aging in charred white oak bourbon barrels to add yet another level of flavor. That means that for this blend, the Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco, as well as the Nicaraguan Sun Grown wrapper, are all aged for 12 years! In the world of premium cigars, such extensive aging is a rarity, and only a select few names dare to go this extra mile. It’s no wonder why this stick has become one of Perdomo’s top releases to date. The bands for the Double Aged Vintage series all include a black and gold theme with the unmistakable Perdomo tobacco flower front and center. Each blend is color-coded with a stripe, and for this one that color is black. Masterful construction is a constant trait when it comes to Perdomo cigars, and this blend is no different, offering a smooth, productive draw and ample amounts of thick, rich smoke on each and every puff. The flavor profile starts off with a large dose of black pepper and cedar, soon settling to an earthy array of rich tobacco flavor studded with hints of citrus and almonds. The texture of the smoke is smooth and creamy, with nuances of cinnamon and coffee beans lingering in the background. A short, spicy finish rounds things out, and this stick finishes as medium-full-bodied. Made for the experienced, this cigar has it all. A rich, medium-full body, a complex, evolving flavor profile, and balance and smoothness that can rival even the world’s most premier blends. It pairs very well with scotch and bourbon and even goes well with a simple cup of coffee. This stick compares to some of Perdomo’s other well-known Sun Grown varieties such as Reserve 10th Anniversary Sun Grown or Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged Sun Grown , though the extensive aging on this one definitely brings with it quite a bit more refinement. In a constantly expanding world of premium cigars, the Perdomo name continues to hold its own, and with cigars like Perdomo Double Aged 12 Year Sun Grown, it’s a safe bet that’s not going to change any time soon. The Perdomo Factory Tour Blend Connecticut cigar is a sneak peek into a little slice of heaven that is Tabacalera Perdomo. It should come as no surprise that visiting a cigar factory gives you access to cigars unknown outside the walls of the rolling or aging rooms. Experiments, rare batches too limited for commercial release, personal blends of various staff, etc. This cigar, comprised of gloriously succulent Nicaraguan filler and with a silky Ecuadorian wrapper, is a house blend that until now was only available during visits to the Tabacalera Perdomo Factory in Esteli.

Someday you just have to make the odyssey to Nicaragua to visit Tabacalera Perdomo, but until then you can experience that small slice of heaven through the Perdomo Factory Tour Blend Maduro cigar. Originally an exclusive smoke for those lucky few able to make a personal appearance at Nick Perdomo's renowned Central American estate, it is now available to be enjoyed by the rest of us. A true Nicaraguan Puro, as it had better be, this smoke pulls in longleaf from across the country's tobacco-growing region. The Esteli farms adjacent to the factory provide the robust filler, the binder is from nearby Condega, and the Maduro wrapper takes a slightly longer journey up from Jalapa.

Smoking a Perdomo Factory Tour Blend Sun Grown cigar is like sending your taste buds on an extended vacation from the bland and the every day. That's because this superb selection of all-Nicaraguan tobaccos was created by Nick Perdomo exclusively for those lucky travelers able to make their way to sunny Esteli to visit his Tabacalera Perdomo. But with word of these secret smokes having escaped to become a chorus of pleading requests, it is time to release them to the rest of the world. A full-bodied, red-blooded juggernaut, this stick is crammed full of a delightful blend of Esteli and Condega-grown longleaf squeezed into a slick Sun Grown wrapper from the Jalapa Valley.

Perdomo Cigars is always on the brink of new and exciting additions to the wonderful world of cigars, and the Bourbon Barrel Aged series is their latest masterpiece. Perdomo Habano Bourbon Barrel Aged Connecticut is hand made in Nicaragua using Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a golden brown Ecuador Connecticut wrapper. What makes this stick so special is that the wrapper leaf is aged for at least 6 months in used bourbon barrels to give it a truly unique flavor.
Chocolate , Coffee , Rich , Robust Available. Learn about Perdomo Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged Maduro Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged Maduro

The name alone should tell you everything you want or need to know about Nick Perdomo's boundary-pushing new cigar: Perdomo Habano Bourbon Barrel Aged Maduro . If you've been smoking cigars for more than a day—and this chunky stogie ain’t for beginners, pal—then you know all about Perdomo's reputation for quality, taste, and extraordinary bang for the buck. His Habano line holds so many awards and 90-plus ratings, there’s probably a room at Tabacalera Perdomo just to hold them all. And finally, the six-year-aged Broadleaf Maduro wrapper, which coats this Nicaraguan puro, was aged an additional 14 months in used Bourbon barrels. Yummy!
Oak , Cedar , Rich , Spicy Available. Learn about Perdomo Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged Sun Grown Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged Sun Grown

Perdomo Habano Bourbon Barrel Aged Sun Grown cigars are the newest and hottest release from Nick Perdomo and company down in Nicaragua. Always on the front lines of innovation and outside-the-box thinking, Nick Perdomo is one of the hardest working men in the cigar business. The Bourbon Barrel Aged series clearly demonstrates the ingenious blending prowess and passion that lies within the Perdomo name. Using all Nicaraguan tobaccos, including a sun grown Nicaraguan wrapper leaf aged up to 12 months in bourbon barrels, Bourbon Barrel Aged Sun Grown is nothing short of a connoisseur's dream.

Heeding the call from those smokers who just can't get enough of a fine cigar, the Perdomo Inmenso Seventy Maduro has returned in all its jaw-breaking glory. For those who may not have had a chance to check them out the first time around, prepare yourself for a massive amount of sweet smoke and lip-smacking tobacco flavor pouring from one of the biggest stogies around. Clocking in at a humongous 70-inch ring gauge, this Nicaraguan Puro contains only the best Cuban-seed longleaf aged to peak richness and taste, the glistening Maduro wrapper providing depth while also working hard to contain the staggering amount of expertly rolled filler.

The Perdomo Inmenso Seventy Sun Grown is a big cigar loaded with even bigger flavor, but size is not the only positive attribute this tasty stogie has going on. It's been built to the highest of standards by the incomparable Nick Perdomo and company, purveyors for decades of some of the finest premium cigars to come out of Nicaragua. Using their own homegrown, well-aged longleaf from across the country, the blend is designed to deliver a rich, complex experience in a medium-full strength package accessible to everyone. Finally, like they do for all their delicious smokes, Perdomo offers these jam-packed vitolas at affordable prices that must be seen to be believed.
Cedar , Honey , Smooth , Creamy Available. Learn about Perdomo Lot 23 Connecticut Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Lot 23 Connecticut

Perdomo Lot 23 Connecticut is the mildest cigar in the Lot 23 family , following the Maduro and Sun Grown varieties as part of the trio that put Perdomo Cigars on the map. Hand made in Tabacalera Perdomo down in Nicaragua, the Lot 23 series is known for being completely comprised of tobaccos grown on a single plot of land designated over two decades ago to be used specifically for this project. What started out as an experiment ended up being one of the best moves Nick Perdomo would ever make. This Connecticut version of the blend consists of Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a higher-priming Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. All tobacco used for Lot 23 cigars is aged for a minimum of 5 years to ensure a mature, velvety smooth flavor profile. What makes the Connecticut version of Lot 23 different is that because of its Ecuadorian wrapper leaf, it is the only cigar in the series that can not be considered a Nicaraguan puro. Nevertheless, Nick Perdomo knew what he was doing when he came up with this version of Lot 23, keeping an eye out for all those who love mild-medium-bodied cigars that still want loads of flavor.
Rich , Sweet , Oak , Espresso Available. Learn about Perdomo Lot 23 Maduro Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Lot 23 Maduro

Perdomo Lot 23 Maduro was destined for cigar greatness from the moment it was introduced. Part of Perdomo's most popular series, Lot 23 Maduro is crafted using tobaccos grown on a specific plot of land on the Perdomo family farms, designated exclusively for the production of Lot 23. Each cigar is lovingly handcrafted at Tabacalera Perdomo in Nicaragua using ultra-premium, heavily-aged Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler and binder leaves. For this Maduro example, the package is rounded out using a 5-year aged higher-priming Cuban seed Nicaraguan Maduro wrapper, adding an incredible amount of depth, complexity, and overall strength to the blend. This cigar has become a mainstay in the humidors of millions of maduro fanatics around the world.

Perdomo Lot 23 Sun Grown is not only one of the most popular cigars in the Perdomo lineup, but is part of one of the best selling cigar series in the world. Back in 2000, Nick Perdomo and his father designated a small, untouched plot of land on the family farms to grow experimental tobacco intended to be used specifically for this blend. Early releases of Lot 23 turned out to be surprisingly successful, and today the series includes 3 varieties: Connecticut, Maduro, and Sun Grown. The recipe for this Sun Grown version consists of Cuban-seed, Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco and a dark brown Nicaraguan Sun Grown wrapper leaf. Definitely the strongest cigar in the bunch, Lot 23 Sun Grown has earned multiple 90+ ratings over the years and remains one of the most easily recognizable Perdomo cigars.

Perdomo is a brand known for its consistency and quality, and their Mini Cigarillos are no different than the rest of their larger premium cigars. These cigars may be small in size but certainly deliver in flavor. Perfect for those moments when you do not have enough time to smoke even a robusto, Mini Cigarillos are offered in Connecticut, sun grown, and maduro.

Odds are, if you've smoked a Perdomo cigar , it was a Reserve 10th Anniversary Champagne . Famous for a reason, including but not limited to a stellar 93 rating by Cigar Journal , it is one of the smoothest, most balanced stogies available anywhere. It's old news by now that Nick Perdomo is one of the most customer-friendly cigar makers out there due to his efforts to keep his smokes affordable by absorbing tax hikes and keeping as much production in-house as possible, and the Reserve 10th Anniversary Champagne is no different. Priced about what they have been for years, each is still constructed with a filler and binder grown in dark Nicaraguan soils on Perdomo's own farms, and a true Connecticut shade wrapper seals the deal.

Back only until they're gone and in just one size, Perdomo's 'new' Reserve Limited Cameroon Edition is an encore performance of epic proportions despite their diminutive size. We've mentioned many times before how sometimes a cigar needs to be discontinued because one or more of its tobaccos are no longer available in either quality or quantity, and such is the case here. Faced with the choice between substitution or retirement, Nick Perdomo decided that once the original Reserve Cameroon's rare wrapper ran out it would be time to move on. Fortunately, he recently discovered he had just enough of the leaf remaining to create a few more boxes of petit coronas.

Perdomo Small Batch Series Connecticut was the first cigar released in the Small Batch 2005 series from Perdomo Cigars in Nicaragua. Originally released in 2015 and limited to 90,000 cigars annually, the Small Batch Series uses ultra-premium Nicaraguan tobacco aged no less than 10 full years. Furthering the "wow" factor, the wrapper leaves are aged in bourbon barrels, giving them a one-of-a-kind flavor to add depth and complexity to the overall blend. The Small Batch Series Connecticut utilizes the same all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend as its Maduro and Sun Grown counterparts, but is set apart by its golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf. The result is bold, complex flavor in a mellowed-out, well-rounded package. The Perdomo Small Batch Series, also known as "Small Batch 2005," was released in 2015 and aimed specifically at experienced aficionados.

Perdomo Small Batch Series Maduro is a cigar no fewer than 10 years in the making. Hand-rolled in Nicaragua under the supervision of Nick Perdomo Jr., Perdomo Small Batch Series Maduro, also known as Small Batch 2005, is a limited-release concoction featuring some of the finest tobacco the Perdomo Cigar Company has to offer. Originally released in 2015, Perdomo Small Batch Series features a blend that begins with a rich, spicy Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco. In the case of the Maduro version, the package is then finished with a beautiful dark brown Nicaraguan Maduro wrapper leaf, combining with the aforementioned blend to create a robust, full-bodied cigar tailored to maduro lovers of the highest caliber. All tobaccos used in the Small Batch Series are aged no less than 10 full years, with a portion of the aging done in bourbon barrels.

Perdomo Small Batch Series Sun Grown is the second cigar to be released in 2015's Small Batch 2005 Series from Perdomo and company. It follows the Connecticut version and precedes the Nicaraguan Maduro. The Small Batch Series from Perdomo is a limited-release ultra-premium cigar line using superb tobacco aged for no less than 10 full years. The wrapper leaves are aged in bourbon barrels, giving them an unusually pleasant character and further adding to the complexity of the blend. For the Small Batch Series Sun Grown, we have a Nicaraguan puro, meaning all tobacco used for the cigar is exclusively Nicaraguan—wrapper, filler, and binder. The particular wrapper leaf is a sun-grown variety, meaning a hefty dose of body and flavor can be expected. The Small Batch Series is in the upper tier of Perdomo's portfolio, so seasoned connoisseurs and those looking for highly-refined cigars can count on it to provide a pleasurable experience.

Perdomo Craft Series Amber is part of the new Craft Series of cigars released by Nick Perdomo, made to complement certain different styles of beer. This is actually a great idea, as while cigars are known for pairing well with whiskey and wine, a great number of cigar nuts choose to drink beer alongside their treasured stogies. This particular version, Craft Series Amber, consists of Cuban seed Nicaraguan fillers and binder tobacco and a Cuban seed Nicaraguan sun grown wrapper, making it a medium-to-full-bodied treat that goes great with, you guessed it, beer!

A Perdomo Special Craft Series Pilsner cigar is right in your wheelhouse if you're sick and tired of trying to decide on a beverage pairing when you smoke. Countless hours of discussion have been wasted in online forums and on back porches about the perfect libation to accompany certain cigars: a Scotch or a cola? A cup of hot (or iced) java or just some cool still water? Nick Perdomo has settled the arguments once and for all. This fine handmade, loaded with Nicaraguan tobacco for filler and binder, has been finished in a U.S. grown Connecticut wrapper to go perfectly with an icy and golden beer.

If you did a double take at the name of the Perdomo Special Craft Series Stout and wondered if it had anything to do with beer, you're already ahead of the game because it most certainly does. Craft beer as a whole has been riding high for a while and this success has started penetrating other industries. The only surprise here is that it's taken this long for a visionary like Nick Perdomo to make his move. Perhaps he was just taking his time finding the perfect blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos from Condega and Esteli to grace with the dark and toothy Nicaraguan maduro selected specifically for its ability to pair well with dark brews. ( See all Perdomo Cigars ) You'll be glad to know that Perdomo Craft Series are not beer-flavored cigars. Cigars flavored with cognac or coffee , sure bring 'em on, but beer…we'd rather just drink it. These longleaf and handmade cigars use traditional profile characteristics to bring out the best in your Irish stout, porter, dunkelwiess and the like. With a foundation of earth and dark cocoa, the cigar's medium-full strength holds up to the roasted barley and bread-like yeastiness of your brew. The taste of roasted coffee and hints of smoked paprika in the lush smoke, with a touch of molasses, will not be washed away with every sip but will linger to encourage puff after puff. Like beer? Love cigars? Then you know where we're going with this, so we'll get to the point. Since you can't have enough of either, we're helping you out here by making these gorgeous smokes cheap enough by the box that you can afford to pick up a couple of extra six-packs during your next beer run. Perdomo Special Craft Series Stout. What a beautiful time to be alive!

The Perla del Mar Maduro is a premium handmade cigar that nearly every aficionado will love, packed with savory and sweet flavors, high quality, and a low price that’s hard to beat. Such an accomplishment is no surprise coming from the family-owned J.C. Newman Cigar Company, creators of a swath of excellent and acclaimed stogies since 1895. The 91-rated Perla del Mar Maduro, crafted in honor of the original PDM from the early twentieth century and recently revamped for even more flavor, is built using a lush selection of Nicaraguan tobaccos. These tobaccos are grown not only in the dark soils of Condega and Jalapa, as expected, but also in the rare regions of La Reina and Pueblo Nuevo. Gently box-pressed, each of these delicious cigars is finished with a toothy, rich Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. Once in hand, resist the urge to bite into the sturdy, well-built vitola as though it were a candy bar—though by appearance and aroma, the Perla del Mar Maduro certainly resembles such a treat. Instead, use your favorite cutter to expose the thickly packed filler, test the lip-smacking draw, and fire this baby up! It’s no surprise that plenty of semi-sweet cocoa can be tasted in the clouds of billowing smoke, but these cigars offer much more flavor to explore. Beginning as a hearty medium-bodied smoke, the cigar launches with notes of roasted coffee bean, spice, and a touch of black pepper. As it reaches the sweet spot, bursts of candied orange peel flavor emerge, complementing the cedar, whole-wheat toast, dark chocolate, and salted almond notes that persist. The strength gradually builds to full just before the nub. Perfect for both daily enjoyment and as the cherry atop a special day, give in to your desires and order some Perla del Mar Maduro cigars today. Fans of dark and sultry smokes like the La Gloria Cubana Serie S Maduro or CAO MX2 will find much to love in these affordable sticks—so there’s no need to wait.

Thanks to inspired cigars like the Perla del Mar Shade, long gone are the days when a beige wrapper promised an extremely mild, simple, and often boring smoke. Despite their roots stretching back to 1895, the family-owned J.C. Newman Cigar Company has kept up with the times, bringing us this complex and supremely delicious Connecticut-covered creation. Built as an homage, but not a repeat, of the original PDM brand from the early twentieth century, the Perla del Mar Shade uses well-aged Nicaraguan longleaf for the filler and binder, giving the flavor profile a welcome kick. These premium tobaccos elevate the creamy, smooth Ecuadoran Connecticut wrapper into a medium-bodied experience you'll want to enjoy again and again. Who knows, these cigars might just become your new favorite daily treat. With its rich golden color, classic box press, and elegant green and gold band, the Perla del Mar Shade is almost too pretty to smoke. Almost. The aroma off the flawless Connecticut wrapper offers fresh hay and cedar, while a cold draw test through the gently squared barrel tantalizes the tongue with hints of spice and whole grain. Easily lit, this cigar nearly explodes with waves of fragrant smoke delivered directly to the pleasure center of your brain, as the palate discovers the early tastes of toasted almond, café con leche, and nutmeg. Some earthiness enters around the halfway mark, accompanied by malted barley, savory herbs, and a touch of caramelized sugarcane. Solidly mild-medium in strength throughout, the PDM Shade does take a turn towards the fuller side of the spectrum closer to the nub, but it’s nothing you can't handle—and well worth the wait. On par with some of the finest Shade-wrapped cigars out there, we're talking New World Connecticut, My Father Connecticut, and maybe even Perdomo 20th (or 30th!) Anniversary Connecticut, you'll want to stock up on these gilded wonders. Good thing we’ve got your allotment of Perla del Mar Shade cigars priced to move fast—so order your batch today.

At first, it might seem strange that we're about to make a big deal about the fact that the Plasencia Alma Fuerte cigar has 'Plasencia' right there on the gold embossed black band. After all, it's not a mark that appears on most of the famous sticks that your friends are always raving about, right? What if we were to tell you that there is a very good chance that the Plasencia family was directly responsible for the vast majority of those popular stogies by virtue of being the largest grower of tobacco in the world as well as creating finished cigars for dozens of other brands in their Segovia Cigar Factory. You can now understand our excitement, because with all that experience it takes a truly special stogie, such as this 93-rated and #9 of 2017 by Cigar Aficionado Nicaraguan Puro, to be good enough to carry the Plasencia name. You might be tempted to just clip the expertly finished triple cap with your favorite cutter and get to smoking, and we're certainly not going to blame you if you do, but it's worth taking a moment to appreciate the masterful skill necessary to craft each Plasencia Alma Fuerte vitola. Almost seamless, with an oily sheen and a touch of tooth, the uniformly dark Nicaraguan wrapper looks almost as if it were poured over the firmly packed barrel instead of rolled. A cold test provides a gentle draw that carries hints of minerals and mint through the four-region filler blend. Creamy and silky milk chocolate is the first pronounced flavor to hit the palate after lighting, alongside robust black coffee, hazelnuts, cedar, and cherry stems . A touch of licorice accompanies the molasses, salted peanut, and malt that characterizes the last couple of inches. For most enthusiasts, the medium to full-bodied Plasencia Alma Fuerte is most likely going to be a special-occasion cigar, but there are plenty of other highly rated sticks to enjoy in the meantime that still have that Plasencia touch. The full list is far too long, but you can't ever go wrong with Rocky Patel The Edge, Nat Sherman Timeless, Casa Magna Oscuro, or Alec Bradley Black Market Esteli, just to name a few. After five generations in the tobacco and cigar business, there's very little the Plasencias can't do very well.

Since they've been in the biz only a few short years, you might not be familiar with the Ventura Cigar Company or their flavorful Project 805 Cubra Maduro cigar, but you will be soon enough. The guys and gals over at Ventura like to forge new and exciting experiences for their customers and to this end they filled the 805 with a smokin' hot blend of Dominican long leaf filler and an Olor binder supplemented by a generous portion of Andullo, a uniquely fermented type of Dominican pipe tobacco never before used in cigars. At this point, the Brazilian Habano Criollo '98 wrapper is just the icing on the cake. (Shop other Project 805 Cigars ) Wise despite their youth for utilizing the legendary skills and experience found at the ancient La Aurora factory to roll their sticks, Ventura has reaped the benefits by releasing a cigar of polished beauty and solid construction. From the succulent scent to its buttery-smooth draw, the 805 Cubra Maduro just reeks of old world quality but what comes pouring out once the generously packed foot is lit speaks to fully modern origins. Medium to full in body and strength, there is plenty of earth and oak and cocoa to satisfy the discerning experienced smoker, though it is the distinct and not-too-subtle spicy molasses flavor and aroma provided by the Andullo that truly sets this cigar apart from the crowd.

Hopefully, you have moved well beyond the belief that shade wrapped cigars are meant only for beginners or breakfast, and the Psyko Seven Connecticut is here to prove the point. It is perhaps better if you never fell for the ruse, much like the false idea that a dark cigar equals a strong cigar, but if you have lingered under these misconceptions, there's nothing wrong with realigning your worldview. Utilizing a crushingly delicious multi-country blend of fine long leaf tobaccos as the core, the talented torcedors at the Ventura Cigar Company create a whole new definition of flavorful by adding a Dominican San Vicente binder and a mind-bendingly beautiful Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. (See more PSyKo Seven cigars ) There's no mistaking a Psyko Seven Connecticut cigar for anything else in your humidor. Mimicking a doctor's written prescription, the large outer band is easy to see and hard to ignore. Take a moment after removing it to appreciate the listing of the tobaccos used, information far too often hidden from the curious smoker, before clipping the cap and getting down to business. A flourish of mineral bite and fresh cut hay enliven the palate from the first puffs, evidence of the shade-grown leaf, and then the filler kicks in to provide plenty of leather, cedar, cocoa and a pleasing barnyard aroma in the retrohale. Finishing medium in strength with loads of body and soul, laying down the nub is a painful reckoning. Sure, the name and the packaging might be a little overboard for some smokers, but the taste and price of the Psyko Seven Connecticut are on point and worthy of a try by all. There's a little something for everyone in each vitola, and you may just discover a whole new outlook on life. A luxurious, relaxing, and enjoyable experience is the consolation prize for the rest of us.

The quest for knowledge can take a back seat when everyone's lives are hectic, so we'll make today's lesson an easy one by just letting you know that you are really going to enjoy the delicious Punch Gran Puro cigar. Our certainty can be summarized in three simple steps. First, Punch stogies are legendary for their succulent robust flavor, and the medium-full and 93-rated Gran Puro is no exception. Next, only the finest well-aged Honduran longleaf tobaccos are utilized for each vitola, from the dense and chewy filler to the flawless Honduran Havana Seed wrapper. Lastly, and you already know where this is going, we've got these premium sticks priced down to where they could be your new daily smoke.

Punch Gran Puro Nicaragua is a modern cigar from a company that is known for its classics. Over the years, the Punch brand has become known as the "Budweiser of Cigars" in that its offerings, though nothing out of the ordinary, are of superb quality and great for any occasion. Just recently, the original Punch Gran Puro was recognized as part of Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 Cigars of 2016. As of late, Punch has come quite a long way from Frank Llanaza's original blend that ruled the 90s. In this execution, we see a Punch cigar utilizing Nicaraguan tobacco, a long stretch from their usual Honduran recipes. The filler and binder blend does in fact consist of a high-end mixture of premium Nicaraguan tobaccos. However, though the name Gran Puro Nicaragua would lead us to believe it is made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco, the wrapper leaf is actually Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro, chosen by the good people at General cigar to give the profile a "layered, dimensional flavor not traditionally found in Nicaraguan cigars," according to Punch marketing director Ed Mckenna. Well, the idea worked, as Punch Gran Puro took a pair of 90 ratings from Cigar Aficionado soon after its release, implying that this isn't your average Punch cigar.

Even after all this time, Punch is still one of the biggest names in the game, and with Punch Knuckle Buster Habano , it’s easier than ever to enjoy a premium cigar bearing that world-famous name. The Habano blend was the original in a 3-part series under the Knuckle Buster umbrella, followed by Knuckle Buster Shade and Knuckle Buster Maduro. This one got the movement started, though, and it remains a fan favorite. Made in Honduras, Knuckle Buster Habano contains Nicaraguan Habano and Honduran Habano filler tobacco, a Nicaraguan Habano binder, and a beautiful dark Nicaraguan Habano wrapper leaf. The rich blend of tobacco works to make a cigar that is both flavorful and enjoyable, and that will by no means break the bank. Blue and gold cabinet boxes and blue and gold bands designate the Knuckle Buster Habano variation, and each and every cigar is lovingly rolled to offer maximum performance. An easy draw effortlessly produces billowing clouds of smoke that greet the palate at first with a blast of cedar and white pepper. The flavor profile soon turns into a delightful medley of earthy tobacco, caramel, and cinnamon , along with a touch of nuttiness on the finish. Medium-bodied, this Punch is one that just about anyone can enjoy to the fullest. Made for a wide array of cigar nuts, Knuckle Buster Habano is medium-bodied and flavorful, offering an enjoyable smoking experience for anyone that can appreciate a good stick. It pairs well with medium-bodied beer or coffee, and its mellow stature makes it a great choice for any time of the day. Fans of the legendary original Punch blend will definitely see some similarities here, but this one tends to be a bit more on the tame side. For a cigar that satisfies every single time and won’t hurt the wallet, Punch Knuckle Buster Habano is certainly a no-brainer.

Punch Knuckle Buster Maduro rounds out the 3-part Knuckle Buster cigar series with a dark and lovely appearance and rich, bold flavor to match. Like its sister cigars, Knuckle Buster Habano and Knuckle Buster Shade, this Maduro variety is made in Honduras using quality tobacco and superb craftsmanship. The Nicaraguan filler tobacco is hugged by an Indonesian binder, creating a classic flavor profile from the get-go. The dark brown Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper seals the deal, and just like that, we have a quality hand-made maduro cigar that will satisfy even your deepest maduro craving without breaking the bank. A black and gold box, black and gold bands, and the bold Knuckle Buster brass knuckles adorning the logo all point to a bold, dark blend that brings back memories of the maduro cigars of old. Precision rolling means an easy draw and sharp burn, and no shortage in the smoke department. An array of nuts and cocoa greets the palate at first light, along with hints of white and cayenne pepper . A rich molasses note carries on throughout the experience, and the finish is sweet, with a touch of coffee . Medium-bodied, Knuckle Buster Maduro is a sheer pleasure to enjoy. Made for and suitable for all audiences, Punch Knuckle Buster Maduro is medium-bodied and flavorful, making it a great stick to enjoy at any time of the day. Coffee, medium-bodied beer, and red wine all make for a lovely pairing, and any fan of the classic Punch Maduro will be sure to enjoy this one. Wallet-friendly, consistent, and satisfying to the core, Punch Knuckle Buster Maduro is a gem that may change the way you look at maduro cigars!

As far as premium cigars go, Punch is one of the biggest names of all time. They’ve been around literally forever, and to this day Punch remains one of the top selling brands on the planet. That being said, it’s no surprise that the Knuckle Buster series turned heads at its release, and since then we have seen several variants. The latest, however, seems to stand out above the rest: Punch Knuckle Buster Shade . Here, we have a cigar made by hand in Honduras using only the finest premium tobacco. The binder is Mexican, the wrapper leaf is a beautiful shade-grown Ecuadorian Connecticut, and for fillers we have a 4 country blend including Colombian, Nicaraguan, Dominican Olor, and Broadleaf. Not a bad package for the low price tag! Throw in a knockout 90 rating in Cigar Aficionado and you’ve got one of the premium cigar values on the entire market! Elegant white boxes house the gorgeous vitolas, each one wearing a white, silver, and black band adorned with the Knuckle Buster brass knuckle motif. Solid construction offers a smooth and productive draw and enough smoke to satisfy even the pickiest cigar nuts. At first light, there is t oast and cedar , but this soon joins a creamy array of earthy tobacco flavor mixed with sweetness . A touch of spicy pepper is present on the tip of the tongue, and there is a hint of cinnamon lingering in the background. Medium-bodied , Knuckle Buster Shade is extremely satisfying and incredibly easy to enjoy. Suitable for all audiences, Punch Knuckle Buster Shade is a cigar that is great for any occasion and surprisingly flavorful for a medium-bodied stick. It pairs well with medium-bodied beer, bourbon, or coffee and compares well to such flavorful Connecticut Shade cigars as Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real or Liga Undercrown Shade . Don’t let high cigar prices smack you in the face. Punch Knuckle Buster Shade puts the “Bang” in “Bang for your Buck!”

As one of the original Honduran cigars, Punch is known for its full-flavored smoking experiences. Few exemplify this more than Punch Maduro. Delivering the boldness you expect from the original Punch, Maduro is clad in a full-flavored, dark Broad Leaf maduro wrapper, for strength and flavor truly worthy of the Punch name.

Punch Signature cigars are a cigar that follows up one of the most famous brands ever introduced to the non-Cuban market. The original Honduran Punch line was brought into existence decades ago, a short time after the trade embargo blocked the importation of its Cuban counterpart. Over the years, the success has been nothing short of immense, and it remains a strong choice for any serious connoisseur. However, times are changing and today's cigar freaks want more. More strength, more flavor, more versatility, more value. This is what brought about a 21st century version of the old standby, and that version is Punch Signature. An Ecuadorian corojo wrapper, Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers, and a Nicaraguan binder blend together in amazing harmony to make Punch Signature highly rated masterpiece that it is. Just a few puffs in, and just about anyone will come to understand where the high rating comes from.

In 1974 the Quesada family emerged as cigar manufacturers after many years in the tobacco industry as leaf brokers. Since then, many great cigars and great brands have continuously defined the family's history. 45 years later in 2019, it was time to commemorate the year cigars became part of Quesada heritage. (See more Quesada Cigars ) Quesada 1974 is the result of a collective collaboration to establish Quesada as a modern brand, which stands upon the heritage it represents. Quesada 1974 features a marvelous oily Ecuadorian wrapper over a Dominican binder and fillers from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic that provide an inviting and complex smoke, full of flavors and aromas, with rich notes of cedar, pepper and dry fruits. A truly unique experience that both the new cigar enthusiast as well as the adept cigar aficionado will enjoy.

To celebrate 40 years in the cigar business, Quesada released an amazing 40th Anniversary cigar. This cigar was blended by Manuel Quesada's daughters, Patricia and Raquel, who are also known for the amazing Tres Reynas. Made in the Dominican Republic, this stick features a dark and oily Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper covering a Dominican binder and exquisite filler tobaccos from Nicaragua as well as the Dominican. (See more Quesada Cigars ) The Quesada 40th Anniversary Toro Real is an astounding 6" x 65 cigar that is going to get your mouth watering from the initial pull throughout the entire cigar. Each puff brings notes of earth, cedar, and pepper. The deeper you get into this stick the more the flavors meld into a slight coffee which plays off the spice nicely. Full-bodied right from the beginning to the nub, this cigar does not overpower but is jam packed with flavor. 40 years in the cigar industry is an amazing feat, and Manuel Quesada's daughters have created a great cigar to celebrate their father's accomplishment. Made with the same attention to quality, flavor, and construction for which Quesada is known, the 40th anniversary is a wonderful after-dinner cigar. If you are looking for a smaller ring cigar with similar quality we would also recommend the Quesada Heisenberg.

With the rise of craft beer culture, it was only natural that cigars like the Quesada Holiday Keg would bubble to the top. Blended to accompany a creamy and rich Irish Stout, these delightful sticks are of course excellent smokes in their own right. There's no reason to expect otherwise from the family owned boutique Quesada factory responsible for many of your favorites such as Casa Magna and Fonseca. Here, a premium brew of Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos compete for prominence beneath a pair of expertly fermented Dominican leaves; one spicy and sweet as a binder, the other a sultry and robust Corojo for the wrapper. (See more Quesada Cigars ) A rugged Toro with plenty of oily shine beneath the red and gold band, the Quesada Holiday Keg exudes a sweet aroma and a cold draw full of cocoa. Aflame, the slowly smoldering barrel begins with a medium bodied flow of charred cedar and dark chocolate. Each steady pull carries the smoker further and further into a state of satisfaction, where the flavors bottled within each stick are slowly released at just the right time. Some licorice and vanilla near the beginning give way to caramel and roasted malt during the second third, which in turn leads to a medium-full finale of molasses, black coffee, and nutmeg. Packed 10 a piece into little barrel-shaped boxes guaranteed not to fit into your humidor, you will still want one to store all the cool swag you will collect during that St. Patrick's Day or other special party. Priced to share, it is a good idea to hide some away from prying leprechauns to ensure enough to last you until next year. For a truly unique treat pair with a hefty pour of Irish Whiskey, which releases a subtle extra sweetness to both. It's magically delicious.

While Quasada would really like you to enjoy a nice German beer with their Oktoberfest cigars, it is not completely necessary. Just as Oktoberfest beers have to be brewed in Germany, Munich to be specific, Quesada's Oktoberfest is a puro as well. Made in the Dominican Republic using only leaf from that country. This stick gets a lot of its flavor and power from the mix of Dominican Olor, Viso, and Ligero filler tobacco. Bound with a Dominican binder, the wrapper is a gorgeous dark Dominican leaf from the Cibao Valley. This medium-to-full bodied stick is a great addition to just about any humidor. (See more Quesada Cigars ) The Oktoberfest theme is carried through to the band, which is colored like the German flag. The dark wrapper is oily and toothy. Surprisingly, there was a lack of an aroma prior to lighting the cigar, but once lit there was a flavor that exploded on our palate. Deep earthy flavors such as oats with just a tinge of honey where the first notes that crossed our lips and there was a wonderful cedar spice on the finish. With each third the flavors transformed as did the body. When all is said and done, the Quesada Oktoberfest briefly touches the line of full-bodied smoke but never crosses it. Break out your best lederhosen and stein and light up a Quesada Oktoberfest today. Even without those things, this is a perfect cigar for anyone who enjoys full, flavored and bodied cigars. Much like the name implies, this went perfectly with a nice strong ale or even a stout red wine.

Quesada Q D'Etat cigars are high-end Dominican puros released as a symbol of the resistance of cigar smokers against unfair taxation practices toward the tobacco industry. They are very limited and available in 3 sizes, all figurados. Being puros, all three components—wrapper, filler, and binder, are ultra-rich tobacco from the Dominican Republic. (See more Quesada Cigars ) The construction is very clean and precise and the draw is excellent. The flavor is indubitably Dominican. Starting off with a rich, leathery flavor on the opening draw, the cigar develops into a simple array of caramel, cedar, and faint coffee tastes. There are hints of spice and wood and the finish is very clean and semi-sweet, with just a touch of pepper on the tongue. These cigars are easy to smoke and full-bodied. They are complex and well-balanced and great for any intermediate to well-seasoned connoisseur. Bourbon is a must-have with this cigar, as the flavors compliment each other wonderfully. Comparable cigars include Arturo Fuente Hemingway and Montecristo White. Quesada Q D'Etat is a unique cigar with a strong symbolic meaning behind it.

Originally only available for Spain in three popular Spanish sizes, the Quesada Espana possesses a distinctive taste, yet is reminiscent of the Cuban cigars the Spanish are familiar with. (See more Quesada Cigars ) Quesada Seleccion Espana Cigars will offer the enthusiast a smooth and enjoyable smoke that is perfect for any time of the day. To create this medium body gem, Manuel, and company employed an exceptional combination of high quality tobaccos that perfectly compliment a rare and tasty Arapiraca wrapper leaf. Along with top-notch construction, a slow burn, and an effortless draw, you will take delight in scrumptious flavor notes of coffee bean, leather, caramel, and a subtle peppery finish. Seleccion Espana is yet another truly unforgettable smoke from the Quesada family that deserves a worthy home in your favorite cigar humidor. Quesada, formerly known as Matasa, is a family-owned business that began with a factory in the Dominican Republic, where it has been manufacturing various types of cigars since 1974. The brand began operations with only one type of cigar brand, but after many years, the Quesada luxury cigar company now boasts a diverse range of cigar brands, each offering a distinct taste and appeal to cigar enthusiasts and lovers. Quesada only manufactures premium handmade cigars of various brands and types, giving its customers a diverse selection to choose from. Try Quesada Seleccion España cigars today!

The Quesada Tributo cigar is a stick that was blended by the Quesada family with each vitola named for a family member or close friend who has passed on, including 3 that were killed in a tragic plane crash in 2002. (See more Quesada Cigars ) The cold draw was fruity akin to raisins, plums, and a faint hint of figs. The first third of the cigar boasts cinnamon and vanilla blended with a darker spice which I'm assuming comes from the Nicaraguan ligero filler leaf. The second third continued some of those baking spices and introduced salty wood, leather, and creamy milk chocolate notes. The final third brings in a citrus flavor that I have yet to taste in a cigar and I was pleasantly surprised to find here. The citrus makes for a long, wonderful finish and an interesting flavor note that adds complexity. These cigars are an excellent smoke for the money and fans of cigars made by Don Pepin will likely enjoy these cigars as well.

The Rocky Patel 15th Anniversary cigar was designed by Rocky Patel to honor his, you guessed it, 15 years in the cigar making business. It seems as if he were the cocky new kid on the block only yesterday, so let's give the man some kudos that we are here discussing the Rocky Patel Twentieth Anniversary cigar. Over the years, much ink has been spilled both good and bad regarding the vast plethora of RP cigars, but a celebration of the future is the headline for today. From humble beginnings (as a lawyer!), Rocky has certainly made a name for himself in the cutthroat cigar biz, crafting some real gems that go toe-to-toe with the most famous and sought after brands. The Twentieth Anniversary already seems destined to stand alongside them, with the exquisite blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos having garnered an early 90 rating.

The Rocky Patel Cameroon Especial is a Dominican filled, Honduran bound, and Cameroon wrapped cigar. This is a bundle priced cigar from one of the most talented blenders in the cigar world today. Combine that blending talent with an excellent farm with a reputation for rolling consistently good cigars and you have a winner on your hands.

Rocky Patel really knows how to create cigars for everyone, from the everyday smoker to the more discriminating aficionado, but the new Cargo is aimed squarely at all the thrifty bargain hunters out there. This is a route that Patel has explored before, for example his Cameroon Especial and The Edge Fumas are pretty darn affordable, but the Cargo might just be the motherlode. A 'Cuban sandwich' style bundled cigar , each well-packed Cargo is loaded with a luscious variety of mixed filler tobaccos from Nicaragua all packed beneath a fermented-until-it's-dark-and-smooth Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.

Rocky Patel seems to have more blends and brands than just about anyone in the cigar business, offering everything from high-dollar premiums to budget-friendly everyday sticks. When Rocky Patel Catch 22 was released, the name was chosen in a clever way. It’s a premium cigar that could be sold for more—and probably should be. That’s the catch! Easy on the wallet and uber-satisfying every time, Catch 22 is made in Honduras using an aged blend of Mexican and Honduran fillers with a Nicaraguan binder. The wrapper is a dark brown Honduran Corojo, adding incredible depth of flavor and just a bit of kick. Don’t let the low price tag fool you—this cigar is built to please. The original Catch 22 line features orange and white packaging. A refined dress box houses the cigars, each adorned with a single orange and white band. Construction is precise and clean, with a nearly seamless roll and an easy, smooth draw. An initial burst of white pepper sets the stage, soon settling into a rich, earthy medley of raw tobacco, cedar, and cocoa. Hints of sweetness emerge on the retrohale, while a deep, dark core of flavor ties everything together. Medium-bodied, well-balanced, and just complex enough to stay interesting, this cigar embodies everything a Rocky Patel should. Appropriate for just about anyone, Rocky Patel Catch 22 is medium-bodied and flavorful, ready to satisfy any pallet, regardless of experience level. Its earthy and spicy characteristics make it a great stick to pair with bourbon or scotch, but a hot cup of black coffee makes for a great pairing as well. Fans of some of Rocky’s other spicy and earthy sticks such as Edge Corojo or Decade will likely enjoy this one, and many would prefer to keep this one on hand due to its cost-effective price tag. A premium cigar at a value price? What’s the catch? Truth is, with Rocky Patel Catch 22, there’s really no catch. It’s just Rocky doing what Rocky does best: Offering great cigars at a great price.

When Rocky Patel came out with the Catch 22 series, he had an interesting reason for coming up with the name. “It’s a cigar that definitely could be sold for more, and probably should be. That’s the catch.” True indeed, and now the second installment of the series has arrived: Catch 22 Connecticut. This Honduran-made blend is rich and flavorful, but offers all the amazing characteristics of a Connecticut-wrapped cigar. Rocky and his team have kept the filler and binder recipe secret, as they have been known to do from time to time, but the obvious component, and the one that matters most here, is its beautiful golden brown Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. Expect a luxurious experience every time, but relax! This one won’t hurt the wallet at all! Turquoise is the color theme for Catch 22 Connecticut, and it covers both the classic dress box and the chic double bands adorning each stick. Construction is top-notch, so don’t let the price tag fool you. Each and every cigar is rolled to exacting standards, ensuring a good draw and plenty of rich, abundant smoke production. At the beginning, an opening of cedar and white pepper lovingly greets the palate. This soon turns into a rich mixture of spice, red pepper, cinnamon, and cream, all wrapped around a delicious earthy core. Though classic in terms of its Connecticut attributes, Catch 22 Connecticut clearly takes things a step further when it comes to having just a bit more. Expect a creamy, medium-bodied experience every time. It’s a wallet-friendly cigar, it’s a medium-bodied Connecticut, and it’s a Rocky Patel. Cigar enthusiasts of all experience levels are welcome here, and trying this fantastic treat is strongly encouraged. Catch 22 Connecticut pairs well with coffee, white wine, or scotch and is a great choice for just about any time of the day. Fans of standout Connecticut sticks such as Perdomo Champagne or Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real can certainly think of this blend as a more affordable “everyday” option. Rocky Patel never ceases to amaze us with his incredible concoctions and options for any and every cigar lover on the planet. With this one, you might be thinking, “What’s the catch?,” but we promise, Rocky Patel Catch 22 Connecticut is just one more fantastic gift Rocky has given to the cigar community.

The Rocky Patel Connecticut is a cigar from among his offerings that doesn't seem to get a lot of press. However, any one that has every smoked a Rocky Patel Vintage 1999 Connecticut or the new Xen by Nish Patel cigar knows that these guys can blend a great Connecticut-wrapped cigar.

That Patel guy is at it again, and this time he has a new version of the highly-rated Decade cigar: the Decade Cameroon. You read that right. Give yourself a break from the hustle by spending your precious free time, but not a lot of your hard-earned coin, with a delectable Rocky Patel Freedom Maduro cigar. The Rocky Patel Legends cigar, also known as the Legends Orange Label, shows that the man himself knows what to do with quality tobacco while still giving his fans a bargain smoke they can turn to day after day. The Legends series of cigars was created to give the biggest names in the business a challenge, to create a 5 ¾ x 54 ring cigar full of flavor at a affordable price. Rocky decided he could provide the most bang for the buck with an impressive blend of specially selected and well-rested Honduran long leaf filler tobaccos securely wrapped in a leathery, juicy Corojo leaf.

You know you've made it to the big time when a cigar has been created in your honor, and the Rocky Patel Ray Lewis Legend 52 cigar honors one of the most spectacular football players ever to take the gridiron. When the time came to honor the Super Bowl MVP linebacker who spent his entire career with the Baltimore Ravens, Patel pulled no punches and sourced only the best Honduran and Nicaraguan long leaf to create a blend unlike any other. When paired with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, these perfectly fermented tobaccos unite into an unstoppable force of flavor and slow-burning performance.

What if we told you that Rocky Patel, one of the biggest and most respected names in the world of premium cigars, now offers a fantastic cigar for an exceptional price ? You probably wouldn’t believe it, right? Well, believe it—because the Rocky Patel Seed to Smoke Classic is here! Made in the El Paraiso factory in Honduras, the Seed to Smoke Classic is a “Cuban Sandwich” style cigar, meaning it contains mixed-filler tobacco instead of long fillers. This tobacco primarily consists of trimmings from the many premium and ultra-premium Honduran blends produced at the factory. It is held together by a Honduran binder and wrapped in a beautiful Honduran wrapper leaf. Simple, easy to smoke, and undeniably satisfying, the Seed to Smoke Classic just might be the bundle cigar we’ve all been waiting for. Bundles of 20 cigars are the standard packaging, with each stick adorned with a gold and white band. If you’ve ever had a “Cuban Sandwich” cigar, you probably know that one of its best features is an effortless draw. It’s easy to smoke, burns well, and produces plenty of flavorful smoke. That’s exactly the case here—this cigar delivers! Spicy white pepper opens up the flavor profile, soon joined by woody, earthy notes accented with nuances of cocoa and coffee. The finish is crisp and spicy, making this simple, medium-bodied cigar both well-balanced and flavorful. There really couldn’t be a much better option for a beginner, for obvious reasons, but experienced connoisseurs will appreciate the level of quality offered here in such a wallet-friendly option. Medium-bodied, this cigar pairs well with bourbon, coffee, or medium-bodied beer, and is affordable enough to smoke all day, every day. Fans of sticks such as Isla del Sol or Factory Smokes by Drew Estate should like this blend, as its build and stature are quite similar. An ultra-affordable smoke from Rocky Patel? We aren’t kidding! Grab a bundle of Rocky Patel Seed to Smoke Classic today and enjoy one of the hottest value sticks we’ve ever seen.

Rocky Patel is a powerhouse in the cigar world, but he hasn’t forgotten about those who appreciate a quality smoke without breaking the bank. Enter the Rocky Patel Seed to Smoke Shade—a smooth, approachable alternative to the Seed to Smoke Classic. This budget-friendly bundle cigar has reshaped perceptions of the brand, proving that affordability and quality can go hand in hand. Crafted in a Cuban Sandwich style with mixed filler, this blend keeps costs down without sacrificing flavor. The filler combines Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos, primarily premium trimmings from cigars rolled at the El Paraiso factory in Honduras. A Honduran binder and a Honduran-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper complete the blend, delivering a refined smoking experience at an unbeatable price. Each vitola sports a red and gold band, giving these bundle cigars a surprisingly polished look. Construction is top-notch, providing a smooth draw and a sharp burn line. From the first puff, pepper and cedar take center stage, balanced by notes of coffee, cream, and brown sugar. Hints of floral and earthy tones tie it all together, creating a mild-to-medium-bodied smoke that’s effortless to enjoy. Seed to Smoke Shade proves that an affordable cigar can still be an exceptional one. Appropriate for all audiences, Seed to Smoke Shade is light, tame, flavorful, and versatile, and it makes a great stick to keep on hand for the times you want to enjoy a cigar but just don’t feel like burning one of your expensive ones. Easy on the pocketbook, this stick also makes a great cigar to share with friends, and it pairs well with light beer or bourbon. Fans of light-bodied bundle sticks such as Flor de Oliva Gold or Perdomo Fresco will surely be drawn to a cigar of this stature, and the price point will likely make this one even more appealing. Who knew a name like Rocky Patel could offer such a fantastic cigar at rock bottom prices? We promise, it’s not too good to be true! Try a Rocky Patel Seed to Smoke Shade today and be ready to have your eyes opened to just how good a bundle cigar can be!

A new day has dawned and it looks like Rocky Patel has decided to compete against the strongest full-bodied brutes in the premium cigar arena by carding a formidable champion-to-be with his Rocky Patel Super Ligero cigar. Of course, this is not Rocky's first time in the ring, not by a long shot. In fact, his release of the original The Edge nearly a decade ago could arguably be credited with launching the modern smoker's fascination with ever more robust cigars. The outer layers of the Super Ligero wear Ecuadorian Habano for wrapper and binder, but its true power is drawn from the Costa Rican and Nicaraguan Triple Ligeros at the core, blended to render unconscious those who seek to challenge fate.

Some cigars are created to celebrate milestones, while others are crafted to honor stories that deserve to be remembered. Rocky Patel The 1865 Project is more than a premium cigar release; it is a tribute to history, heritage, and the significant contributions African Americans have made to the cigar industry. Developed through a collaboration between Rocky Patel and 1865 Ventures, this unique project commemorates Juneteenth, the historic date of June 19, 1865, when the last enslaved people in the United States were informed of their freedom. More than simply recognizing the past, the project also looks toward the future, with a portion of proceeds supporting initiatives and educational programs through The Juneteenth Foundation. Handcrafted at Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A. in Estelí, Nicaragua, The 1865 Project combines premium tobaccos with the craftsmanship cigar enthusiasts have come to expect from Rocky Patel. A dark, rich Mexican San Andrés wrapper surrounds a dual binder combination from Honduras and Nicaragua , securing a core of carefully selected Nicaraguan fillers . The result is a balanced and complex blend that delivers both character and refinement from the first draw. The smoking experience opens with notes of black pepper and earth , gradually transitioning into richer layers of freshly brewed coffee, creamy leather, and cocoa . As the cigar develops, additional nuances of espresso, cloves, toasted bread, dark chocolate, and subtle spice emerge, creating a profile that continuously evolves while maintaining excellent balance. Medium-full bodied in strength with impressive complexity, this cigar delivers flavor without overwhelming the palate. Wrapped in a striking presentation featuring rich gold accents against a dark chocolate-brown wrapper, The 1865 Project is as visually distinctive as it is meaningful. Rich in flavor and rooted in purpose, this release stands as a reminder that great cigars can do more than deliver an exceptional smoking experience; they can also honor history, celebrate progress, and inspire future generations. Whether enjoyed for the story behind the blend or simply for the quality in the smoke itself, the Rocky Patel The 1865 Project offers a memorable experience from first light to final draw.
