Rocky Patel may be known for having one of the most extensive portfolios of anyone in the cigar business, but the Vintage series are what put him on the map way back before he was a household name. The fourth cigar in the Vintage series, the Vintage 2003 Cameroon, made a huge entrance when it was introduced as it was the first to employ a Cameroon wrapper leaf, something with which Rocky hadn’t experimented much at the time. This tasty new twist on the Vintage series soon exploded, earning the blend a 93 rating in Cigar Aficionado and even a spot on the publication’s Top 25 Cigars of 2016. Made in Honduras, this cigar contains a rich blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers, a Nicaraguan binder, and a gorgeous Cameroon wrapper leaf that has undergone no less than 8 years of aging. The Vintage line changed forever when this blend was introduced, and to this day Vintage 2003 Cameroon remains one of Rocky Patel’s major players.

Rocky Patel Vintage 2006 San Andreas is one of the newest cigars from industry giant Rocky Patel. The fifth cigar in the Vintage series, Vintage 2006 San Andreas made its debut at the 2017 IPCPR convention, rocking the world of cigars. See, when Rocky Patel releases something new, it is not always that big of a deal, considering just how many sticks he puts out.

Rocky Patel has probably released more individual brands and lines than just about any manufacturer in the game, but as any seasoned cigar freak would agree, it was the Vintage series that put his company on the map. That happened over two decades ago, and now we do what Rocky does best: celebrate! Rocky Patel Vintage 20th Anniversary celebrates the blends that took the Rocky Patel Cigar Company into the major leagues, and continue to keep him at the top today. Like the original Vintage series, this blend is appropriately crafted in Honduras, and uses only the finest Nicaraguan long fillers. A Brazilian binder holds everything together, and the package is capped off with a gorgeous Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper from the 2007 harvest. This is the first Rocky Patel Vintage to feature a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, as the famed Vintage 1990 in fact used a Honduran Broadleaf. A true vintage package, this cigar is sure to be a standout among serious connoisseurs. The Rocky Patel Vintage 20th Anniversary cigar blend has earned as high as a 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado , praised for its rich, balanced flavors and exceptional craftsmanship. A luxurious black chest houses the precision-built vitolas, and the color theme for this blend is teal and silver. The unmistakable Rocky Patel logo shines on the main band, and the secondary denotes the blend. Careful craftsmanship means each Vintage 20 th Anniversary cigar offers a productive and smooth draw, a sharp, clean burn, and a long and sturdy ash. Black pepper and dark, earthy undertones start things off, as oak and cocoa soon mix things up. A hearty fresh tobacco core makes up the backbone of the flavor profile, and classic maduro notes of coffee and chocolate round things out. The finish is long, and this flavor bomb of a cigar finishes as a stout full-bodied masterpiece. Made for the experienced, Vintage 20 th Anniversary is built with the hardcore cigar snob in mind. Basically, if you enjoyed the original Vintages when they came out and are still smoking, chances are that you’ll quickly fall in love with this one. Full-bodied and complex, this blend pairs well with any scotch or bourbon, but also goes well with black coffee or your favorite dark beer. For a fully enamored experience, compare it to the two blends that started it all: Vintage 199 0 and Vintage 1992 . Whether a long-time fan of Rocky Patel or just someone that appreciates the finer sticks on today’s market, Rocky Patel Vintage 20 th Anniversary offers a celebration to anyone fortunate enough to light one up.

The new RoMa Craft Intemperance BA XXI cigar is a weapon, a solid (yet tasty) cudgel to wield against the rising forces of government regulation assaulting our cigar hobby. Our cigar passion. Our cigar life. As you might guess, the name of the cigar, Intemperance, is in reference to the original fight against the 1919 passing of Prohibition, the draconian result of the temperance movement, and its eventual overturning by the 21 st amendment. Hence the ‘XXI’ in the name. It’s quite a history lesson we’re being taught by the newly formed RoMa Craft Tabac Company. And what about the ‘BA’ part? Well, that’s easy. It stands for the Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper that coats the Indonesian binder which envelops the aged Nicaraguan and Dominican longleaf filler within. A cigar that seeks to make a statement needs to be able to back it up flavor-wise, and the Intemperance BA XXI is no slouch in that department. The first thick plumes that flow from each dark and oily stick are pushed onto the palate by a steady draw and are full of earthy cocoa and toasted cedar. Syrupy molasses and dry minerals become evident during the second third of the smoke, the strength and body rising to a touch above medium. Towards the end, with the ash steady and the burn straight, rich cream and a bite of black pepper fight to leave a lasting impression. We all know that simply smoking a cigar isn’t by itself going to combat the push to ban cigar smoking in nearly all public areas in the US. But with cigars like the RoMa Craft Intemperance BA XXI, the industry if looking to create enough awareness and public action by aficionados across the country to make a difference. Take a stand today, and in doing so you might as well have a delicious stogie in your raised fist.

RoMa Craft Intemperance EC XVIII is the first cigar released by the all-new RoMa Craft Cigar Company. Over the past few years, RoMa Craft has literally exploded in the cigar industry. Beginning as a tiny boutique company with a cult following, RoMa Craft, through small magazine articles and social media exposure, has now become a household name among "Those who know" as it's said among fans of the world-class cigars in question. Intemperance EC XVIII was where it all started. With a name that brings to mind the history of prohibition, Intemperance EC XVIII can be called a celebration of freedom, so to speak. The XVIII (18) in the name refers to the 18th amendment, which prohibited the consumption of liquor. With no liquor in the recipe, Intemperance EC XVIII consists of a phenomenal blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, an Indonesian binder, and a golden Ecuador Connecticut wrapper leaf. The cigar is described by RoMa Craft to be "mild-bodied and medium-full-flavored." Regardless of how you choose to describe it, Intemperance EC XXVIII is a fantastic cigar. The band, like any from RoMa Craft, is undeniably simple, bearing a logo inspired by a famous artifact of the temperance movement, a political print by temperance hymnodist AD Fillmore from 1855. The construction of any RoMa Craft cigar is second to none, and this holds true with Intemperance EC XVIII as well. The draw is just right, allowing enough airflow to produce massive, dense clouds of silky, blue smoke. Beginning with a textbook tobacco flavor, Intemperance EC XXVIII soon evolves to a rich bouquet of cinnamon, white pepper, cherry, raisin, and sweet cream. This flavor profile is strikingly similar to a number of high-end exotic Dominican cigars that are in much higher of a price point than the cigar in question. Sweet cocoa on the finish ties the package together, making for an absolutely stunning smoking experience. RoMa Craft cigars appeal most to seasoned connoisseurs, due to the precision of the blends and incredible use of various high-end tobaccos. However, for those not looking for every tiny flavor nuance throughout the smoking experience, RoMa Craft sticks will fit the bill just fine as well. Intemperance EC XXVIII is mild enough for an intermediate cigar freak to enjoy and complex enough to satisfy an all-out cigar aficionado. Intemperance EC XVIII pairs very well with bourbon or scotch and is kin to its maduro counterpart, BA XXI . Fans of Intemperance EC XVIII may want to check out Arturo Fuente Don Carlos and Ashton ESG . "Intemperance" is defined as "Lack of moderation or restraint, or excessive consumption." It's safe to say, after the first puff of a RoMa Craft Intemperance EC XVIII, excessive consumption of many more will likely follow.

The Romeo y Julieta 150th Anniversary celebrates a legacy of passion, tradition, and fine cigar-making. Crafted in the Dominican Republic, this masterpiece feat Romeo y Julieta 150th Anniversary – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The Romeo y Julieta 150th Anniversary celebrates a legacy of passion, tradition, and fine cigar-making. Crafted in the Dominican Republic, this masterpiece features a Sumatra Ecuador wrapper, a robust Mexican San Andres binder, and rare fillers from Peru, Honduras, and the Dominican Republic. Marking a historic milestone, the Romeo y Julieta 150th Anniversary embodies 150 years of dedication to the craft of fine cigars. Meticulously handcrafted at the Tabacalera de Garcia Factory in the Dominican Republic, this commemorative cigar combines heritage and innovation to create an exceptional smoking experience. This cigar showcases a Sumatra Ecuador wrapper, meticulously aged and fermented by AJ Fernandez, paired with a robust Mexican San Andres binder supplied by the Turrent Family. The filler, cultivated by our partners at the Plasencia family, features a unique blend of rare Peruvian tobaccos, Honduran leaves from the Jamastran Valley, and premium Dominican tobaccos from Jose Mendez & Co. This composition is further enriched with an aged, undisclosed leaf that adds an extra layer of complexity. The result is a balanced yet dynamic flavor profile that begins with notes of cedar and spice, deepens into layers of chocolate and coffee, and finishes with an earthy sweetness. Designed to celebrate a legacy of craftsmanship and passion, the 150th Anniversary invites aficionados to savor a cigar that reflects the artistry and tradition of Romeo y Julieta.

Plenty of cigar brands have been around for a long time, but only a handful can really be considered legendary. 2025 marked 150 years since the foundation of Romeo y Julieta, which obviously had its beginnings in Cuba. Since then, not only has the original Cuban brand stayed true to its heritage, but the more mainstream non-Cuban offering from Altadis continues to make leaps and bounds year after year, still maintaining a permanent residence near the top of the cigar food chain. That being said, a commemorative cigar made to celebrate this anniversary had to be nothing short of stellar, and to say they hit the nail on the head would be an understatement. Behold, Romeo y Julieta 150 th Anniversary! Rolled by hand at the world-famous Tabacalera de Garcia in La Romana, Dominican Republic, this incredible delight contains tobacco from a handful of the most prominent growers on the planet. Peruvian and Honduran fillers from the Plasencia family start things off, along with more Dominican filler leaves from Jose Mendez and Co., followed by a Mexican San Andres binder from the Turrent family. The star of the show and the finishing touch is a gorgeous dark brown Sumatra wrapper leaf grown by none other than AJ Fernandez under the volcanic cloud cover of Ecuador. Special in every right, this masterpiece has already earned multiple 90+ ratings and is being celebrated across the globe. A cigar this phenomenal deserves packaging to match, and the folks at Altadis certainly spared no expense. White and gold wooden chests with cutouts around the outside resembling classic Italian architecture from the region where the play was set are just the beginning. Each box has an information card placed between two stacks of eight cigars, and each cigar wears white and gold double bands, textured and embossed in luxurious Romeo y Julieta style. Beautiful construction lends to brilliant smoke production and a razor-sharp burn every time. Nuts and cedar start things off, soon joined by hints of leather, coffee, and cocoa . Subtle spice is notable on the retrohale, but all in all this cigar is as smooth as silk and tells a story as it smokes. The core of earthy tobacco eventually comes to the forefront, further decorated by hints of cinnamon and citrus. Medium-bodied, flavorful, and immensely balanced, Romeo y Julieta 150 th Anniversary is certainly apt to celebrate the brand’s milestone. Obviously, this rare gem was never meant for an inexperienced audience. Cigars of this stature require a genuinely seasoned palate and plenty of patience to sit back and enjoy every ounce of enjoyment it has to offer. Medium-bodied , this blend pairs well with classic scotch or bourbon, but in true Cuban style, simple coffee certainly makes a fine accompaniment. Whether you have enjoyed the original Romeo y Julieta over the years, or any of the spin-offs such as Reserva Real , Reserva Real Nicaragua , or 1875 Nicaragua , you owe it to yourself to experience this one. Good cigars will come and go, but with Romeo y Julieta 150 th Anniversary, we celebrate a cigar brand that puts “good” in the rear view and replaces it with “Legendary”.

A bold blend that comes together for a deep, fuller-bodied smoke. Romeo y Julieta 1875 Reserve Maduro – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The Romeo y Julieta Reserve Maduro features a blackened Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, a tasty Nicaraguan binder, and a bold blend of Nicaraguan, Peruvian, and Dominican long fillers, creating a deep, fuller-bodied smoke with a lovely aroma and taste. Enjoy these flavorful cigars that appeal to both your taste buds and sense of smell.

Romeo y Julieta 1875 Reserve Maduro is yet another counterpart to the original core cigar from Romeo y Julieta, the 1875. It’s a shining example that experience, skill, and hard work can produce extraordinary results. The very first RyJ left the hands of an unknown Cuban torcedor way back in 1875, hence the name of this stick, and it’s been quite a ride since then. If there’s one thing that has remained constant, it’s the outstanding flavor produced by each and every fine vitola regardless of the country origin. The flavorful blend of these cigars contains aged Dominican, Nicaraguan and spiced Peruvian fillers, a Nicaraguan ligero binder, topped with a dark, rich and oily Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. The result of this masterful blend is a complex, robust, medium-full bodied cigar that’s loaded with flavor. Once lit, this cigar produces plentiful smoke, with hints of dark-roasted coffee, nuts, cedar and leather, all balanced with an earthy undertone. It provides a plethoric and indulgent smoking experience that's unique to this deep, dark maduro which makes it stand out in the Romeo y Julieta 1875 line of cigars. While the medium-full strength of the blend and the classic feel of the flavor profile would likely appeal generally to seasoned connoisseurs, Romeo y Julieta 1875 Reserve Maduro can easily be enjoyed by a wide variety of cigar enthusiasts. Complex yet balanced, this Cigar Aficionado 90-Rated blend from RyJ keeps things interesting from start to finish, and is sure to find a well-earned spot in your humidor.

Originally started in 1875 in Cuba, Romeo y Julieta is one of the cigar industry's oldest and most revered brands. Altadis has been producing the non-Cuban version of this cigar in the Dominican Republic for quite some time and it has risen to be one of the manufacturer's top-selling brands. In 2005, the Anniversario was released to celebrate Romeo y Julieta's 130 years of existence . This is the boldest iteration of the classic brand to date. A unique tri-country blend of Nicaraguan, Dominican, and Peruvian filler tobaccos are complimented with a Connecticut broadleaf binder and a medium-brown Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The full-flavor and body on this cigar may shock some fans of the original blend. The Romeo y Julieta Aniversario has earned widespread acclaim, receiving multiple 90+ ratings from Cigar Aficionado , including a high score of 92 and ranking #19 on their Top 25 Cigars of 2007 . The traditional red Romeo band is replaced with a black one, making the smoker aware that this is not your regular medium-bodied Romeo they are used to. The quality and construction are prevalent from the get-go, but it is that first light which may make you want to sit down. Spiciness, earthiness, and a small amount of sweetness come out as soon as you light the Anniversario, but it doesn't stop there. From beginning to end, this cigar doesn't let up, and seems to increase in both flavor and body with each puff. This isn't your grandpa's Romeo. Anniversario is a powerhouse of a cigar perfect for anyone that may have dismissed the original blend as being too light. Everything you would expect from buying a Romeo Y Julieta and more… a lot more. The full-bodied nature of this cigar needs to be paired with something such as a dark red wine or something else with bold flavors. If you are looking for a different Romeo experience, with much lighter flavors, you cannot go wrong with the Reserva Real line.

Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez cigars were destined from their inception to be something huge. A collaboration between two of the industry's monsters, Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez combines the incredible legacy of Romeo y Julieta and Altadis USA with the modern blending expertise of master cigar maker AJ Fernandez. The second in a line of “remastered classics,” this stick follows Hoyo de Monterrey Crafted by AJ Fernandez and has garnered some serious attention since its release in mid-2016. Handcrafted in Nicaragua at Tabacalera Fernandez, Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez uses an astounding assortment of filler and binder tobaccos from AJ's personal Nicaraguan farm, all harvested for this particular cigar. The finishing touch is a rich, oily Habana 2000 Maduro wrapper leaf which adds an immense amount of depth and character to this incredible cigar. One of the things AJ Fernandez is known for is the quality of his cigars. Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez follows suit, always offering an easy draw, billowing clouds of smoke, and mind-boggling barrages of luxurious flavor. Beginning with a sweet, spicy opening , Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez starts to pound the palate with rich notes of cocoa and mocha . Earthy tobacco maintains a presence in the background as classic Maduro flavors meet edgy Nicaraguan goodness . A sweet raisin finish seals the deal, putting a delightful touch on this profound demonstration of blending mastery. Medium-to-full-bodied , Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez is an outstanding choice for anyone who has a well-developed palate. Complex, rich, smooth, and immensely satisfying, it pairs wonderfully with scotch, rum, or port wine and makes a great close to any special evening. If you have not checked out AJ Fernandez's other blends, it is definitely worth it to pick up a few. In particular, New World and Bellas Artes would be similar in stature to this particular masterpiece. AJ Fernandez has not been in the game as long as most other big names in the business, but he has come up very quickly and already made his mark as one of the industry greats. Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez is just one more stick for him to brag about, and rightfully so. It is a true work of art.

Romeo y Julieta Devocion is one of the lesser-known special cigars in the Romeo y Julieta portfolio, but it might just be the hidden gem you've been looking for all these years. Released in 2020, Devocion is a collaboration project between Rafael Nodal of Altadis USA and the famous Grupo de Maestros. In case you didn't know, the Grupo de Maestros is made up of the most highly skilled rollers and blenders at Tabacalera de Garcia in the Dominican Republic, and are responsible for crafting many of the Montecristo lines. This blend, however, is made down in Honduras at the Flor de Copan factory, and consists of a heavily-aged mix of tobaccos including only the highest grade Dominican and Honduran filler leaves, an American binder, and a beautiful Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. The final product is relaxing, easy to smoke, and undeniably satisfying.

What we've got here is a new classic in the making, the wonderfully dark and delicious Romeo y Julieta Media Noche . For those of you who have forgotten their first year of Spanish class, 'Media Noche' translates to Midnight, a name which accurately describes the color of the spectacular Mexican San Andres Maduro wrapper blanketing each of these delectable stogies. Not content to sleep on a hard-won reputation for supreme quality and taste, Romeo y Julieta has blended the finest selection of aged Dominican longleaf tobacco for filler and binder to make this cigar one of their strongest and most complex ever. San Andres wrappers are well known for their deep, rich color and smooth flavor, but they certainly aren't going to win any beauty contests. Despite the flair brought by regal purple and gold double bands, the outer layer of a Romeo y Julieta Media Noche is noticeably rough and rugged, with some prominent veining and a good bit of tooth. However, once you spark the layered foot and take the first slow pulls through the free-flowing draw, you'll be taking this thing to the dance. At first flush with abundant coffee, black pepper, and earth, the palate soon detects more subtle hints of leather, almonds, coriander, citrus, and salt . A silky sweetness like butter cream enters during the second third, accompanied by a cedar and cocoa backbone to take you to the nub. Gone are the days when Romeo y Julieta cigars were commonly relegated to breakfast or lunch smokes, while more robust selections took care of business after the sun went down. The medium-full Romeo y Julieta Media Noche is dressed and ready to stand beside your smokiest Scotches, your Tawny-est Ports, and your smallest of small-batch Bourbons. For what little money these will set you back, you'll even have some cash left over to have a hearty breakfast before heading off to bed.

Woodsy flavor. Tender Aroma. Even the most demanding cigar connoisseurs are sure to love the Reserva Real. Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Since their introduction in 1875, Romeo y Julieta has remained one of the choicest cigars crafted, and one of the most often requested brands by connoisseurs. The Reserva Real blend is a carefully balanced recipe of Dominican leaf spiced with Nicaraguan leaf finished with a hand-selected blonde Connecticut Shade seed wrapper, grown in the valleys of Ecuador. Slightly mellow in flavor, it is an expertly crafted handmade smoke.

The Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real offers a softer, creamier, and more refined take on the classic Romeo y Julieta blend we all know and love. Building on the original, Altadis introduced a touch of Nicaraguan tobacco into the filler and enhanced the profile further with a Nicaraguan binder. However, the true star of the Reserva Real is its silky, light brown Ecuadorian Connecticut-shade wrapper. This exquisite wrapper transforms the smoking experience, elevating the blend beyond a mere variation—it feels like a rebirth for a new generation of aficionados. The Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real blend has earned ratings as high as 92 from Cigar Aficionado . Dressed in a striking red band reminiscent of the iconic Romeo y Julieta 1875, the Reserva Real also features a red and gold secondary band proudly bearing its name. Beyond its elegant appearance, this cigar delivers an exceptional smoking experience. From the first light, it produces voluminous clouds of smoke with ease. Though classified as mild to medium in strength , the Reserva Real never falls short on flavor. Its flawless burn and effortless draw make it a pleasure to smoke down to the nub. If anything, the only thing left to be desired is more time to enjoy it. The Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real is a stunning evolution of the classic 1875 brand, maintaining the impeccable construction and quality that smokers worldwide have come to expect. With a smooth, approachable character, it’s a perfect choice for a morning smoke—ideal for early tee times or a relaxing start to the day. And for those seeking a bit more strength, the Reserva Real Maduro makes for an excellent alternative.

Made with 100% Nicaragua Tobacco. Blended by Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez, the cigar is handcrafted at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Esteli, Nicaragua from tobac Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Made with 100% Nicaragua Tobacco. Blended by Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez, the cigar is handcrafted at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Esteli, Nicaragua from tobaccos grown on Fernandez’s farms. The Best Selling Reserva Real adds a Nicaraguan Experience. Cigar Master AJ

Some things are worth the wait, so we were thrilled when we heard that the Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua cigar had finally arrived. The original Dominican RyJ Reserva Real has been a fan favorite for years, thanks to a spicy kick from Nicaraguan longleaf filler in an otherwise mild shade-wrapped stogie. Now, renowned AJ Fernandez has crafted this new medium-to-full strength Nicaraguan puro, brimming with flavor. Fernandez selects the choicest, ripest tobaccos from his Esteli farms, expertly fermenting and aging them to delectable perfection. Rolled by some of the most skilled torcedors in the land, these masterpieces are now available. The Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua has earned multiple 90+ ratings reaching as high as 93 and secured its spot among the industry’s best when Cigar Aficionado named it the #9 Cigar of the Year for 2022 . Red has long been integral to Romeo y Julieta’s packaging, so it’s astonishing to see bright blue and gold bands adorning each uniformly russet-colored Reserva Real Nicaragua. However, that's just a small part of each stick’s charm. With an aroma reminiscent of milk chocolate and cold draw flavors evoking wild blackberries with whipped cream, the solidly constructed body of the cigar entices enthusiasts to grab their best cutter and lighter to ensure a superior smoking experience. Earth and espresso greet the palate initially in waves of silky smoke, as expected, but the tastes of vanilla, licorice, whole wheat cracker, and orange peel throughout are delightful surprises for experienced aficionados. Experience both history and the future with the Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua, a treat that stands shoulder to shoulder with great Nicaraguan Puros of the past, such as the old school Joya de Nicaragua, the famous Tatuaje Havana VI, or the potent 601 Habano Oscuro. Besides, you wouldn’t want your buddies to try these before you get a chance, would you?

The medium-full strength profile of the Midnight Twist offers a symphony of cedar, spice, and cashew flavors, creating a rich and complex smoking experience tha Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua Midnight Twist – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The medium-full strength profile of the Midnight Twist offers a symphony of cedar, spice, and cashew flavors, creating a rich and complex smoking experience that follows the narrative of the original Reserva Real Nicaragua. The Midnight Twist is expertly crafted by Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez in the renowned tobacco fields of Nicaragua, building on the legacy of the original Reserva Real Nicaragua. This line extension introduces a dual-cloak Nicaraguan wrapper, meticulously developed at the AJ Fernandez Factory, which perfectly complements the evening’s ambiance, providing a robust counterpart to the original blend enjoyed during the day.

AJ Fernandez and Altadis USA have forged a history of success, but few collaborations have made an impact quite like the Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua . A Top 25 cigar in its own right, it hardly needed a sequel—yet in 2024, Fernandez raised the bar once again with a striking new take: Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua Midnight Twist. Crafted at AJ Fernandez’s esteemed Nicaraguan factory, this special edition remains a Nicaraguan puro, composed entirely of aged tobaccos from the Fernandez family’s farms. However, what sets it apart is a bold visual and flavor-enhancing touch—a ribbon of dark Nicaraguan Maduro leaf spiraling around each vitola in a stunning barber pole design. This not only gives the cigar an eye-catching look but also deepens its complexity, adding an extra layer of richness. The result? A well-deserved 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado shortly after its dazzling debut. Housed in an elegant blue and gold box, each Midnight Twist vitola is adorned with a special edition Reserva Real Nicaragua band, now featuring its distinctive name in script. From the moment it’s lit, this cigar delivers the exceptional craftsmanship and performance aficionados expect from the brand. A smooth draw produces dense white smoke, a razor-sharp burn, and firm, white ash. The experience begins with an invigorating burst of Nicaraguan pepper, awakening the palate before giving way to a decadent medley of cocoa, citrus, and cinnamon, all balanced over a deep, earthy tobacco core. As the cigar progresses, it builds in intensity, culminating in a full-bodied crescendo of rich, well-balanced flavors. Tailored for seasoned connoisseurs, the Reserva Real Nicaragua Midnight Twist embodies the hallmarks of a true ultra-premium smoke. Its full strength, velvety smoothness, and intricate complexity make for a near-perfect package. Add to that its impeccable construction and flawless performance, and it’s clear why this cigar is destined to be a favorite among aficionados. It pairs beautifully with bourbon, port wine, or coffee, making it a fantastic choice for special occasions. While it shares the core DNA of the original Reserva Real Nicaragua , the Midnight Twist brings just enough extra flair to set itself apart. Whether you’re a longtime fan of the original or simply searching for a bold, conversation-starting Nicaraguan puro, Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua Midnight Twist is sure to impress. One puff, and you’ll understand why this cigar is making enthusiasts everywhere twist and shout!

The legendary Romeo y Julieta portfolio continues to evolve with the Reserva Real Nicaragua Profundo , a bold new expression that takes the beloved Reserva Real line into darker, richer territory. Crafted in collaboration between master blender AJ Fernandez and Rafael Nodal, this premium handmade cigar combines the deep character of Nicaraguan tobacco with the smooth refinement that has defined Romeo y Julieta for generations. Handmade at AJ Fernandez’s renowned factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, the Profundo is a true Nicaraguan puro, built entirely from premium tobaccos grown, fermented, and aged under Fernandez’s expert supervision. The blend is finished with a dark, extra-fermented Oscuro wrapper that immediately sets the tone for a richer and more intense smoking experience. The Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua Profundo has solidified its place among the industry's elite by earning multiple 90+ scores, most notably distinguished by a stellar 93 rating from Cigar Aficionado . From the first draw, the Reserva Real Nicaragua Profundo delivers a layered profile of espresso, dark chocolate, roasted earth, and toasted nuts, accented by hints of black pepper and dried fruit throughout the smoke. Despite its medium-to-full-bodied character, the cigar maintains the signature smoothness that Reserva Real fans have come to expect, creating a balanced and refined experience from start to finish. This release represents more than just another addition to the Romeo lineup, it’s a modern evolution of one of the cigar world’s most historic brands. As Mariana Hinestrosa, Brand Manager for Romeo y Julieta, explained, “The Profundo was developed to offer aficionados a new expression that reflects their evolving taste and growing appreciation for Nicaraguan tobaccos, while preserving the signature smoothness that defines the brand.” Rich, complex, and impeccably constructed, the Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua Profundo is a cigar designed for smokers who appreciate bold Nicaraguan flavor delivered with classic Romeo sophistication. Whether enjoyed after dinner, alongside a strong coffee, or paired with a dark spirit, this is a cigar that invites you to settle in and savor every draw.

The ultimate twist on a classic. Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Twisted – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The Romeo y Julieta story keeps getting better as the revered Reserva Real line expands with a twist. The Reserva Real Twisted Love Story and the Reserva Real Twisted Toro. Each cigar is rolled with two different wrapper varietals consisting of alternating Ecuadorian Habano and Ecuadorian Connecticut shade tobacco. Each hand-crafted cigar features filler made from the finest Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos available. The binder is Nicaraguan and, as noted above, the wrapper is alternating with specially selected Ecuadorian and Connecticut shade tobacco.

An attractive deep-brown, silky wrapper leaves top off the cigars, resulting in a more seasoned version of an old favorite. Romeo y Julieta Reserve – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Unlike any other Romeo you’ve experienced before. Handmade in Honduras at La Flor de Copán factory, these full-bodied beauties will captivate your senses with the distinguished smoothness of a Romeo intermingled with the rich, hearty flavors of the finest, hand-selected Honduran and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos.

Long celebrated for their smooth, mild-to-medium profiles, Romeo y Julieta delivers a bolder, more intense experience with the Romeo y Julieta Reserve . Produced at the prestigious La Flor de Copán factory in Honduras , this line represents the brand's successful venture into the full-bodied market. It is engineered for enthusiasts who demand a high-performance smoke without sacrificing the refined sweetness and balance that has made Romeo y Julieta a humidor staple since 1875. The construction of the Reserve is centered around a dark, oily Nicaraguan Habano wrapper that encases a complex interior of aged Nicaraguan and Honduran long-filler tobaccos. This blend results in a hearty, medium-to-full-bodied profile characterized by earthy textures and stout spices. The experience begins with a "tingle" of pepper on the lips and retrohale, which quickly settles into a rich medley of cedar, toasted nuts, and leather . Subtle notes of cinnamon and a creamy sweetness emerge as the burn progresses, providing a clean and refined finish. If you have previously overlooked Romeo y Julieta as a "mild-only" brand, the Reserve is designed to change that perception. It offers a powerful, slow-burning session that maintains its nuances even as the strength builds. Whether paired with a bold bourbon or enjoyed as a standalone after-dinner treat, the Romeo y Julieta Reserve— a 90-rated selection by Cigar Aficionado —proves that power and elegance can exist in the same vitola.

Romeo y Julieta 505 Nicaragua is known for being the most full-bodied cigar offered by the legendary Romeo y Julieta brand. With Cuban roots and a hugely successful long-lasting Dominican campaign, and with numerous non-Dominican blends and collaborations with some of the biggest names in the cigar business, it seems all that was left for Romeo y Julieta was to bring out a Nicaraguan puro. Well, here it is! Romeo y Julieta 505 Nicaragua is made by hand in sunny Nicaragua using a bold blend of Nicaraguan tobacco filler, binder, and wrapper. The rich filler blend contains leaves from all three major Nicaraguan growing regions—Jalapa, Esteli, and Condega. Both the binder and wrapper are habano leaves from the Jalapa region. After all is said and done, it's safe to say that this Nicaraguan puro from Romeo y Julieta was well worth the wait. The folks at Cigar Aficionado seem to think so, as the 505 Nicaragua earned a solid 91 rating soon after its release . A loud orange band simply hints at the enormous barrage of flavor about to be unleashed. A slight box press and precision roll offers a solid, plentiful draw. Gushing blue smoke slathers the palate with intense Nicaraguan spice, soon settling into a core of earthy, nutty goodness . Hints of coffee and cedar speckle the profile, along with soft notes of dried fruit . The finish is smooth, bold, and spicy, yet clean and easy. The solid, full-bodied flavor profile is uncommonly balanced and smooth. While we have all come to know and love the mild-to-medium-bodied cigars Romeo y Julieta has offered over the years, the 505 Nicaragua is a welcomed change. Built for connoisseurs, the 505 Nicaragua is offered in 4 delicious sizes and all a wonderful way to experience the intensity of the blend while enjoying a cool, mellow flow of thick smoke. While not for beginners, the 505 Nicaragua is a great all-around stick for smokers seeking full-bodied goodness. The rich, simple flavor profile is just complex enough to satisfy aficionados that have come to appreciate the modern powerhouse cigars on today's market. 505 Nicaragua pairs well with dark beer, coffee, or port wine, and is best enjoyed after a good meal. While the 505 Nicaragua is the first Nicaraguan puro marketed under the Romeo y Julieta name, the AJ Fernandez collaboration cigars share a similar stature, so you may want to give Romeo y Julieta Crafted by AJ Fernandez or H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez a try as well. 505 is the area code for Nicaragua, but according to the folks behind this stick, 505 is code among those "in the know" for indulging in the richest, boldest cigar experiences this life has to offer. Now is the time for you to indulge as well, so join the 505 movement today with a Romeo y Julieta 505 Nicaragua cigar.

It is hard to believe that a brand with as a long a history as Romeo y Julieta could be constantly innovating, but the new Romeo Anejo is proof that not only can they, but they can do it darn well. Anejo is Spanish for “aged” and every aspect of this cigar fits the moniker. From the dark and sultry Connecticut broadleaf wrapper from 2010, to the Dominican Olor binder from 2008, all the way to the Nicaraguan and Honduran filler tobaccos from 2009, this cigar is chock full of well aged tobacco. The result is an amazing smooth yet still medium-to-full bodied smoke. The exceptional craftsmanship of the ROMEO Añejo by Romeo y Julieta has not gone unnoticed by the industry’s top critics, with the blend earning impressive ratings as high as 91 from Cigar Aficionado for its rich complexity and flawless balance. Romeo Anejo has a smooth, sweet and earthy prelight draw and aroma which carries over to the first few relaxing puffs. Each draw brings in more of the chocolate and cinnamon sweet heat which is inherent in a well aged Connecticut wrapper. The true spice hides until the second half of the cigar where the power of the Nicaraguan and Honduran leaf shines. The body of Romeo Anejo is different than what you are used to from Romeo y Julieta, but the smoothness behind it lets you know that you are smoking a brand that is an expert in the crafting of a fine premium cigar. This cigar is perfect to pair with a dark espresso after a full meal and will hold up against even the smokiest of single malt scotches. For a different take on an Anejo cigar, we would recommend the Arturo Fuente Anejo , which was the first brand to enter the word in the cigar smoker’s lexicon.

A turn to the dark side is not always a tragedy, as evidenced by the Romeo San Andres by Romeo y Julieta cigar. Covered with a slick, near-black San Andres wrapper from the sunny fields of Mexico, this premium stogie is a beauty to behold and a love song to your palate. The creator of this masterpiece is none other than the incomparable A.J. Fernandez, the magic man behind many of your current favorite sticks whether you know it or not. Working with some of the best Dominican and Nicaraguan longleaf filler tobaccos available anywhere, A.J. has crafted the Romeo San Andres to be a full-bodied powerhouse that will thrill rather than overwhelm. Despite not being red, the design of the black, gold, and white bands which grace these marvelous vitolas will be immediately familiar to those who have enjoyed the original Romeo. Like that 94-rated wunderkind, this cigar breaks with the traditional flavors of the original yet still amazing RyJ front marks to appeal to the tastes of today's aficionados. Slow pulls on a freshly lit Romeo San Andres produce thick curtains of aromatic smoke that fill the room and also coat the tongue with the flavors of dry cocoa, white pepper, and oak . Before long, more exotic nuances make themselves known, primarily allspice, cherry stem, earthy molasses, and black walnuts . Destined to be remembered for its strength and impressively complex character, the Romeo San Andres by Romeo y Julieta is the perfect cigar to class up any gathering, whether it be a wedding or an informal backyard luau. Priced for sharing with friends and foe alike, everyone will be one big happy family by the time the last slow-burning nub is laid to rest. Your future self will thank you, so hop on it.

Sometimes it takes a return to the past to move into the future, and so it is with the Romeo y Julieta Viejo cigar . For a famous legacy brand already firmly rooted in the history of cigars, this means stripping away all pretense and creating a frontmark where the only consideration is taste. No flashy packaging, no glitteringly rare and grown-on-one-tiny-farm-atop-a-volcano-by-an-old-blind-man-and-his-wife wrapper, no BS. Just quality longleaf filler from Nicaragua, Honduras, and the Dominican beneath an unassuming but intensely flavorful Mexican San Andres Maduro outer covering, with each medium-strength stick given a light press before being packed into simple cabinet boxes.

The discerning smoker will never tire of this superlative cigar that is “truly a cigar for special occasions.” Romeo y Julieta Vintage – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 A premium blonde Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper and a Mexican binder contain a smooth blend of Dominican long fillers, resulting in a smooth- to medium-bodied smoke.

Step into a world of refined sophistication with the Romeo y Julieta Vintage No. III — a premium cigar crafted to celebrate life’s finest moments. Established in 1875, Romeo y Julieta is one of the most esteemed names in the cigar world, known for its rich heritage and exceptional quality. The brand flourished throughout the 20th century, captivating enthusiasts with its legendary offerings, including the famed vitola named in honor of Sir Winston Churchill. This Romeo y Julieta Vintage blend has earned accolades from Cigar Aficionado, receiving ratings as high as 90 for its rich, balanced flavor and expert craftsmanship. Today, the legacy of Romeo y Julieta continues to thrive, bringing you cigars that are the epitome of luxury and craftsmanship. The Vintage No. III is a superb example of this prestigious brand’s dedication to excellence, handmade in the Dominican Republic. This Robusto-sized masterpiece offers a refined and enjoyable smoking experience, perfect for both seasoned aficionados and those just beginning their cigar journey. Wrapped in a stunning Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper, the Vintage No. III is as beautiful as it is flavorful. The smooth, golden-hued wrapper hints at its mellow yet rich character, setting the stage for a remarkable smoking experience. The blend features a rich Mexican binder and carefully aged Dominican filler , creating a harmonious balance of mild-to-medium strength with a creamy, flavorful profile. From the first draw, the Romeo y Julieta Vintage III Robusto welcomes you with an inviting aroma of creamy vanilla and sweet cedar. As you continue to savor it, you will experience a delicate symphony of nutty undertones, roasted coffee, and smooth spices. Each puff reveals layers of earthy richness and honeyed sweetness, culminating in a consistently smooth finish that beckons you back for another draw. The 5” x 50 size of the Vintage III Robusto is ideal for a leisurely smoke. Whether you’re seeking a reliable everyday choice or a distinguished companion for a special celebration, the Romeo y Julieta Vintage No. III awaits to offer you a taste of excellence.

When Matt Booth, an amazing jeweler, decided to step into the cigar game, there had to be some thoughts of just another one off boutique flash in the pan, but his Room 101 cigars are anything but. All have amazing flavors and great construction. As a thank you to everyone who stayed by him and believed in his cigars Matt has created the Big Payback. Each has the same great quality that one would expect but at a fraction of the cost of the other Room 101 lines. This Nicaraguan puro uses fine Nicaraguan tobacco for the wrapper, binder, and filler and provides big flavor as well as some big sizes. A classy black and silver designed band is as flashy as some of Booth’s jewelry. The gorgeous, matte medium brown wrapper is bursting with flavor and a tingle on your lips gets you ready for the smoke that is ahead of you. Each puff brings an amazing array of flavor as spice, earth and sweetness dance past your tongue. You will be amazed at the level of craftsmanship that goes into each of these fantastically priced cigars. The Room 101 Big Payback cigar is a great introduction into the wonderful array of cigars Room 101 has to offer. Unlike some of their sticks though, these are a regular production run and will not have the limited quantities that some of their other blends have. After having a few of these we would also recommend giving the Room 101 San Andres a shot, or even the Room 101 Meet Your Maker Sampler. All of these cigars are worthy of anyone’s humidor.

Saint Luis Rey Carenas celebrates an encounter of two worlds – the Old and the New – with an extraordinary cigar that invites lovers of tradition to embark  Saint Luis Rey Carenas – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Saint Luis Rey Carenas celebrates an encounter of two worlds – the Old and the New – with an extraordinary cigar that invites lovers of tradition to embark on a cigar experience that transcends time. Created by the Grupo de Maestros of La Flor De Copan, the Saint Luis Rey Carenas is a flavor-packed smoke of earthy spices and salty notes making this a solid medium-bodied cigar. The cigar offers an impeccably smooth draw with an oily Nicaraguan wrapper. These decadent sticks with their immaculate appearance invite adult cigar aficionados to take a trip back to the heritage of the Saint Luis Rey brand.

It's always exciting when an old brand gets a new line extension and a modern makeover, and this is precisely the case with Saint Luis Rey Carenas. Altadis USA has an impressively gigantic portfolio packed with brands we have all come to know and love, some more familiar and some that have either never made it big or have fallen by the wayside. Saint Luis Rey is one of the classic brands that did in fact fall by the wayside and has for years been hidden in the shadows of the newer, more exciting brands of today's ever-growing cigar industry. Altadis has played with the brand a bit over the past few years with some success, but they needed something bigger and better to really give new life to the name. For this reason, they turned to the famed Grupo de Maestros to craft an all-new blend, this one coming out of the Flor de Copan factory in Honduras. The blend is classic, featuring a Nicaraguan wrapper, Honduran broadleaf binder, and Honduran fillers. The flavor is classic as well, in the opinion of many mimicking that of certain Cuban cigars. Maybe that's what they were going for, as the cigar's name refers to the Puerto de Carenas, or Port of Havana. The blend has turned out to be a huge hit, earning a rock-solid 92 rating in Cigar Aficionado and giving new excitement to the Saint Luis Rey name.

The Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar is a tribute to the early days of the cigar trade when sixteenth-century Spanish vessels traveled ‘ultramar,’ or oversea Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 The Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar is a tribute to the early days of the cigar trade when sixteenth-century Spanish vessels traveled ‘ultramar,’ or overseas, from Puerto Carenas in the New World to Spain carrying tobacco leaves. A tribute to the early days of the cigar trade when sixteenth-century Spanish vessels traveled ‘ultramar,’ or overseas, from Puerto Carenas in the New World to Spain carrying tobacco leaves. Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar is an extra-aged blend handmade at La Flor de Copan with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and Nicaraguan binder and filler. This blend boasts an exquisite Nicaraguan wrapper and binder.

The story of the Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar begins centuries before the first premium cigar was ever rolled. During the sixteenth century, Spanish ships sailed ultramar-"overseas"-from the New World to Spain carrying precious tobacco harvested in the Americas. As the tobacco made its long voyage across the Atlantic, time and the conditions aboard the ships naturally aged and mellowed the leaf. “This was the first known form of tobacco fermentation and aging,” says Gabe Diaz, brand manager for Altadis U.S.A. The Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar pays tribute to this fascinating chapter of cigar history, reimagining what those beautifully aged tobaccos may have tasted like after completing their legendary journey. This blend has earned multiple 90+ ratings by Cigar Aficionado! Handcrafted at the renowned La Flor de Copán factory in Honduras by Altadis' celebrated Grupo de Maestros , the Carenas Ultramar builds upon the acclaimed original Carenas blend with an extra-aged interpretation that delivers even greater depth and complexity. A gorgeous Nicaraguan Habano wrapper surrounds a carefully selected Nicaraguan binder and filler , creating a medium-to-full-bodied profile that highlights the natural richness of well-matured tobacco while preserving the signature character that made the original Carenas such a standout. Construction is exceptional, producing an effortless draw, an even burn, and dense clouds of smoke. The voyage begins with a rich earthy foundation before gradually revealing refined layers of cedar, leather, roasted nuts, and delicate saffron . Gentle touches of spice weave throughout the smoke, while a subtle butterscotch sweetness emerges on the finish, adding balance and elegance without overshadowing the cigar's rich tobacco core. Every transition feels deliberate, rewarding patient smokers with a profile that continues to evolve from first light to final draw. Following the success of the original Saint Luis Rey Carenas , which earned an impressive 92 rating and a place on Cigar Aficionado's 2021 Top 25 Cigars of the Year , the Carenas Ultramar takes the series to new horizons through additional aging and remarkable refinement. Rich in history, beautifully balanced, and masterfully crafted, this release offers a smoking experience that honors both the origins of the cigar trade and the timeless artistry of Saint Luis Rey.

Saint Luis Rey is a renowned brand that has been a stalwart of the cigar industry for decades, but smokers' tastes change as do their preferences for certain sizes. Recognizing this, Saint Luis Rey Gen 2 was released. With years of blending experience behind it, Gen 2 is a wonderful full-bodied cigar. Made in Honduras, this cigar has Nicaraguan and Honduran filler, a Nicaraguan binder and a dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The change in blend and the inclusion of more Nicaraguan tobacco is what gives this cigar the added kick over its predecessors.

Look no further for a bold cigar, full of tastes of coffee and tobacco to please the experienced cigar smoker. Saint Luis Rey Maduro – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Expertly crafted in Honduras, these exquisite cigars are beautifully packaged in lovely semi-boite nature boxes. Saint Luis Rey cigars achieve their exceptional full flavor and enticing aroma through a unique blend of Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Peruvian long filler tobaccos, a Nicaraguan binder and a San Andrés Marrón wrapper.

Saint Luis Rey Maduro cigars are back and better than ever. True, it was originally a Cuban brand whose origins are lost in the mists of time, but odds are most of you old-timers will fondly remember when these hailed instead from the Dominican Republic. It was then as now a fine medium-full bodied smoke priced far below its worth and with its re-invention as a Honduran cigar packed with the juiciest tobaccos blended to cater to today’s smokers we might just have a hit on our hands. Starting with a complex mix of Honduran, Nicaraguan and Peruvian longleaf, the torcedors at La Flor de Copán then envelop them beneath a sturdy Nicaraguan binder before sealing the deal with a San Andrés Morrón wrapper so dark and oily you can almost see your reflection.

Saint Luis Rey is a cigar that just about everyone is familiar with in some way. Originally produced in Cuba and later introduced to the American market as a Honduran premium cigar, Saint Luis Rey has hung around for ages, surviving the cigar boom era and continuing to prove as a mainstay even in today's ever-expanding market. A versatile cigar indeed, Saint Luis Rey is a bold, classic blend of Nicaraguan, Honduran, and Peruvian fillers inside a Nicaraguan binder and a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper leaf. This old school mixture brings about one heck of a smoking experience, alluding to the days of old when cigars were just a simple, enjoyable luxury.

In general, San Cristobal is an under-the-radar brand from a modern master of cigars, and the stellar medium-strength San Cristobal Elegancia is an easy way for every aficionado old and new to discover what he's all about. The inimitable Jose Garcia, or 'Don Pepin' as he's known to his legions of fans, has been creating some of the world's best smokes for decades. His original San Cristobal creation was an in-house frontmark for an old-school brick and mortar, but we make it easy to get your hands on these marvelous sticks, loaded as they are with choice Nicaraguan longleaf tobaccos beneath a silky, sultry Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. In addition to complexity, consistency, character, and good taste, another quality usually associated with Don Pepin Garcia cigars is potent strength. However, the man can produce a mean milder cigar that still carries his inspired brilliance and the San Cristobal Elegancia is proof indeed. After inhaling the musty, grassy aroma of the shade wrapper before the solidly-packed barrel is lit, the nose is primed for retrohaling rich, thick smoke which will first coat the palate with nutmeg, toasted almonds, and a touch of that Pepin-trademark black pepper. A buttery, spicy, nutty flavor almost like a rye cinnamon roll heralds the start of the second third, while the finale is marked by the arrival of robust coffee tempered with sugar and cream to wash it all down. If you count yourself among the innumerable fanatics who savor everything Garcia have ever created, from the classic Don Pepin Garcia Blues and Blacks, to a multitude of Tatuaje and My Father frontmarks, just to name a few, then the San Cristobal Elegancia is right up your alley. Maybe sitting back with a smooth Scotch and an even smoother cigar is what you crave. Well, then San Cristobal Elegancia is still the answer. In fact, it's the solution to just about every smoking conundrum you can imagine.

We're bombarded with so much new information in today's tech-heavy life it's rare when something can break through and really change our previously held beliefs, but the aptly named San Cristobal Revelation cigar can do just that. Of course, we're talking about the foolish notion that after having ascended to cigar-blending godhood in recent years, Don Pepin Garcia couldn't possibly create another 'His Best Ever' smoke. Well, Revelation just might give you a whole new worldview. From its silky Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper to a binder and filler of the finest Nicaraguan tobaccos, it represents a work of true inspiration. All four current San Cristobal blends carry the same band with its bright macaw and gold medal embellishment, so when you're digging through your humidor look for 'Revelation' on a secondary band with gold and robin's egg blue highlights. Chocolate in color and wafting a delicious alfalfa aroma, you'll struggle to remember to cut the cigar's triple cap before rushing to get a flame to its solidly packed foot. Some definite Pepin spice is apparent during the initial stages but as the wheel of time revolves, ever-shifting flavors of cream, roasted nuts, espresso, toast, and cedar swirl through your palate and into your subconscious. We can't promise you will attain enlightenment when you smoke one, but we do guarantee you'll have a great time trying. Whether enjoyed with a few cups of dark and strong coffee on a cold morning or during a meditative session of hanging out with close friends on a summer afternoon, the San Cristobal Revelation will be a faithful companion to the end, or whenever you decide to lay it down. Need more Don Pepin Garcia in your life? Try his classic Blue Label or the new La Reloba Mexico.

After years of being the man behind many acclaimed cigars, AJ Fernandez , the Cuban exile, finally did what many had long anticipated — he released his own national brand: San Lotano Requiem Connecticut . Introduced in three distinct wrappers, San Lotano cigars are expertly crafted at Tabacalera Fernandez in Nicaragua, the same factory responsible for Man O’ War and many other celebrated cigars. This San Lotano blend has earned an impressive 91-point rating from Cigar Aficionado . Fernandez is renowned for his deep tobacco knowledge, and that expertise shines through in the diverse selection of tobaccos used for each San Lotano blend. Adding to the lineup is the recently introduced San Lotano Oval, a unique mixture of aged and proprietary tobaccos that creates an entirely different experience. For the lightest expression in the San Lotano portfolio, AJ Fernandez selected a shade-grown Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, paired with a Honduran binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. From a distance, the cigar is immediately recognizable thanks to its rich, silky sheen. The flavor profile begins with a complex mix that quickly settles into notes of earth, aged tobacco, nuts, cedar, spice, and creaminess . It’s not your typical Connecticut—its flavor depth rivals cigars with much darker wrappers—yet the strength remains comfortably in the medium range. Construction is flawless, consistent with the rest of the San Lotano line, producing excellent ash, an even burn, and ample smoke. For those seeking a lighter version of AJ’s acclaimed blends, San Lotano Connecticut delivers exactly where it counts most—flavor.

If you’ve ever wondered what happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable object, we can tell you with confidence that the result is the creation of the San Lotano Dominicano cigar. It was inevitable after all, a meeting of the minds of two of the tobacco-blending powerhouses that fuel the modern era: brand owner A.J. Fernandez and the incomparable Jochy Blanco. Crafted at Jochy’s Dominican-based Tabacalera Palma, this stogie contains a binder and some portion of the filler from his own local farms, while the balance of the well-aged and expertly fermented longleaf at the core comes from A.J.’s fabled Nicaraguan fields. A leathery Cuban-seed Brazilian wrapper is all that protects us from the radiant medium-full strength flavor that takes but a flame to unleash. A creation of collaboration instead of competition, the San Lotano Dominicano is supremely balanced in all aspects of its character. It sits heavy in the hand and the uniformly solid barrel beneath the double gold and blue bands gives so very slightly under pressure, but a cold draw test requires only a soft pull to release hints of milk chocolate and whole wheat toast. A razor-sharp burn produces creamy rich clouds initially loaded with baker’s cocoa and pepper, with a touch of anise in the retrohale. Ever shifting between sweet and savory, the first and second thirds contain espresso, graham cracker, cedar, salt, and cane syrup. The finish is earthy and chewy, fully of dense yet surprisingly cool mouthfuls of smoke. The phenomenal San Lotano series of smokes have long been lauded for bringing maximum premium flavor at a reasonable daily-stick price, and the San Lotano Dominicano continues that tradition. Check out some of A.J’s other wondrous offerings; the Dias De Glorias and Ramon Allones are particularly remarkable. Jochy Blanco as well has a broad stable of delightful stogies to explore, from the hearty La Galera to the myriad tastes and complexities of the various Aging Room frontmarks. Come, join us and ride the lightning!

This is the San Lotano Habano cigar. You might think it just another temporary humidor dweller passing through unremarked during your quest to smoke everything you can get your hands on. However, then you remember having read about one of the San Lotano frontmarks before. Perhaps you have seen the stellar ratings by respected reviewers. It could have been the high rankings on various “Best of the Year” lists. There’s good reason to get excited when you find out A.J. Fernandez is the man behind a particular cigar, and this stick is no exception. Containing a choice mix of Nicaraguan and Honduran longleaf, this full-bodied, full-flavor powerhouse becomes a force to be reckoned with after being topped with an exclusive and exquisite Brazilian-grown Habano wrapper. Even without ‘San Lotano’ embossed in gold on the classically-styled band, it is an easy chore to identify this cigar among the rabble. Impeccably rolled and carrying a glistening brown color, minimal veins, and a bit of tooth, each hefty San Lotano Habano vitola represents the perfect marriage of craft and art. While reeking of crisp tobacco through the nose, a cold draw powders the lips with cocoa while soothing the palate with cedar. Alight, the seamless wrapper kicks in a wealth of dark chocolate and spice while the thick filler does the heavy lifting by providing dark loam, leather, vanilla toffee, and espresso. Destined to become a staple in your everyday smoking rotation due to its excellent quality to cost ratio, i.e., one of the best cigars you have ever had at an incredibly low price, you will still be hard-pressed to find a better special occasion smoke than a delicious San Lotano Habano. Try pairing it with a fine sipping Bourbon while masterfully grilling some prime steaks for your pals, or with a cheap lager while kicked back watching your brother-in-law ruin some burgers over the coals. It will make either situation the best cookout ever.

When the man with the plan is A.J. Fernandez, as is the case with the particularly luscious San Lotano Requiem Maduro cigar , the only thing you will have to worry about is finding a comfortable place to sit while smoking. That is because Fernandez has been producing world-class stogies almost from the very moment he stepped onto the scene, and he gives no indication of slowing down. Having access to some of the finest longleaf ever to grace a curing barn allows A.J. to dial in just the right flavor profile to complete his vision. For this revelation, each San Lotano Maduro is chock full of Nicaraguan and Honduran tobaccos combined with a dark, sweet Mexican San Andres wrapper for a full-flavored, medium-to-full strength gem. This San Lotano Requiem Maduro blend has earned multiple awards including a 92 rating by Cigar Aficionado . The ‘San Lotano’ frontmark is proclaimed loud and proud on the main green and gold band, with ‘Maduro’ equally pronounced on the secondary band, so confusing this stick with any other in your humidor is your own fault. Of course, the quality of construction, the sleek, oily, and rich brown color of the San Andres, and the overall allure of each hefty vitola are just as obvious. Bright and floral defines the aroma of the smoke which billows forth once the broad foot is lit, but the taste skews towards more carnal delights. Dark chocolate and red wine flavors dominate for a time, then a charred meatiness backed by toasted cedar and dark cherries comes to the fore. The wise smoker will let these flavors battle it out unimpeded over the long, slow burn towards the nub. There has been much buzz about San Lotano cigars, whether the Maduro or another blend, since their initial release, so most of you by now are at least aware of their existence. Current fans need no persuasion but if you have yet to try one, despite overwhelming evidence of their delightfulness, now is the time. A San Lotano Maduro with a dirty gin and a rousing card or dice game with friends is one of the best ways to make the most of a weeknight.

San Lotano Oval is a cigar that came out of nowhere to become one of the most highly praised projects in recent history. Made by the now famous AJ Fernandez as a “revival” of his grandfather’s original San Lotano recipe from Cuba many years ago, San Lotano Oval combines flavors of old with a modern twist on size and strength. AJ Fernandez was in the business long before he brought out the San Lotano lines, producing numerous highly-acclaimed sticks, but San Lotano Oval is the cigar that put AJ Fernandez on the map. The rest is history. San Lotano Oval consists of a rich blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers held together with a spicy Nicaraguan binder. A double-fermented Habano 2000 wrapper leaf tops off this extraordinary recipe that has garnered numerous 90+ ratings in various publications, including the famed Cigar Aficionado. Blended for both cigar enthusiasts and refined connoisseurs alike, San Lotano Oval offers one heck of a well-rounded package. Heavily box pressed and oozing with oils, San Lotano Oval is almost too beautiful to smoke. The band is simple, with a vintage appearance, and the gorgeous caramel brown wrapper leaf is nearly seamlessly applied, finished with a Cuban style triple cap. An easy draw ensures giant clouds of thick, delicious smoke every time, along with a clean burn and a tight gray ash. Beginning with a burst of spicy Nicaraguan pepper, San Lotano Oval mellows out to a gorgeous flavor story of cedar, tobacco, and nutty goodness. A hint of cinnamon and sweetness on the finish goes wonderfully with the rugged, Cubanesque profile to form a complete bouquet of fantastic depth and complexity. San Lotano Oval resides on the heavy end of medium-full and is amazingly balanced throughout the experience. It is easy to see why San Lotano Oval has garnered so much attention since its release years ago. There is simply nothing bad that can be said about this incredible masterpiece of a cigar. Intermediate level smokers will appreciate the strength to smoothness ratio, while more discriminating aficionados will take great pleasure in the complex, yet classic flavor profile. San Lotano Oval pairs beautifully with a number of accompanying beverages, including scotch, bourbon, or even a simple beer. San Lotano Oval is also offered in a Maduro version, as well as a non-box pressed San Lotano Original series for fans of more classic sizes. AJ Fernandez is one of the hottest names in the business today. Grab a San Lotano Oval and experience what started his skyrocketing journey to the top!

San Lotano Oval Maduro is the follow-up cigar to the award-winning San Lotano Oval Habano , one of the most successful cigars of recent years. AJ Fernandez is one of the hottest names in the business, crafting 90-rated stick after 90-rated stick at a seemingly impossible rate, and this particular masterpiece is made just for all you maduro lovers out there. Utilizing the same “family secret” blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers and a Nicaraguan binder, mimicking his grandfather’s old-time Cuban recipe as best as he can, AJ Fernandez chose a dark, toothy Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper for this version. Although the basic, celebrated flavor profile remains much the same, this beautiful wrapper adds just a hint of maduro goodness, but doubtless enough to satisfy maduro freaks worldwide. Rustic and oily in appearance, the heavily box-pressed San Lotano Oval Maduro flaunts the same fantastic craftsmanship as its Habano counterpart. An easy draw offers billowing clouds of thick, blue smoke, first pounding the palate with the familiar opening burst of Nicaraguan spice, but quickly settling to a rich, earthy mixture of cedar and nuts. Raw tobacco and cocoa flavors add to the depth of the blend, along with a long, sweet finish. Like the original Oval blend, Oval Maduro sits right on the borderline between medium-full and full-bodied, yet it is never overpowering and always wonderfully balanced and smooth. San Lotano Oval Maduro appeals to cigar lovers of just about any experience level, but the more developed the palate, the more appreciated the amazing flavor profile would be. San Lotano Oval Maduro will pair wonderfully with dark beer or even a hearty port wine, but it goes particularly well with a hot cup of coffee in the morning. The differences between the natural and maduro versions of the Oval are not overwhelming, but there’s a definite difference between the two. Similar to Padron and Padron Maduro , these San Lotano Oval blends both appeal to a vast audience of both maduro fans and non-maduro fans alike. San Lotano Oval Maduro is one of AJ Fernandez’s crowning achievements, and without a doubt a cigar every connoisseur should keep in the humidor year-round.

San Lotano cigars came out of nowhere to become somewhat of a household name among cigar freaks, and San Lotano The Bull takes the brand to a whole new level. Born in Nicaragua and made under the supervision of the famous AJ Fernandez, San Lotano The Bull is a San Lotano cigar that's made for those who want a little more kick. Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos sit underneath a spicy Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper leaf, making for a full-bodied "San Lotano on steroids," so to speak. Just about anything coming out of AJ's factory becomes a huge success, and The Bull is no exception by any means. It has garnered the attention of cigar fans everywhere, and has been given numerous accolades by top cigar magazines and websites. Near flawless construction makes for an easy draw and a clean burn. Plentiful smoke hits hard from first light, bringing a hurricane of spice Nicaraguan pepper furiously against the palate. Soon, the pepper settles down into a smooth cedary flavor profile spiked with hints of leather and coffee. A woody finish on the retrohale leaves the smoker drooling for more. Such a masterfully blended cigar should have a much higher price point, shouldn't it? Well, we better keep quiet for now. The Bull is all business and presents a delicious flavor profile comparable to many ultra-premium, high-dollar exotic cigars. For the price, just about anyone can enjoy The Bull. However, you had better be a fan of full-bodied cigars if you so choose to grab this one by the horns. San Lotano The Bull pairs well with full-bodied beer or whiskey and makes a fantastic choice to follow a hearty steak dinner. Be sure to try some of AJ's other hits along with The Bull, including the original San Lotano blend as well as San Lotano Oval . AJ Fernandez proves over and over again just how good he is at making mind-blowing cigars. San Lotano The Bull is just further proof that this isn't his first rodeo.

Sancho Panza Double Maduro is no doubt a cigar whose name rings a nostalgic bell for many a long-time connoisseur. One of the favorite old-time classics, the Sancho Panza brand has unfortunately fallen into the shadows in recent years, its glory days but a distant glimmer in the rear-view mirror and its present situation best described as “still hanging on.” However, in a recent, dramatic turn of events, the brand has been rejuvenated, reworked, and given new life, as one of the edgiest names in cigar history, Matt Booth, is now the creative director at the industry giant General Cigar, and has vowed to make Sancho great again! Okay, so maybe he didn’t actually say that verbatim, but the magic he’s worked with the brand is causing quite a stir in the world of premium cigars. In the case of this Double Maduro variety, the second release in the trio, we have a bold and flavorful concoction brewed up at the STG factory in Danli, Honduras using a filler blend from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. As for the “Double Maduro '' part, both the binder and wrapper are aged maduro leaves, the binder hailing from Esteli, Nicaragua and the wrapper being an Ecuadoran Sumatra leaf that ties the whole package together in gorgeous harmony. For a modestly priced cigar, this stick is definitely something to talk about. All-new blending meets all-new packaging, and that means new bands and boxes alike. According to Booth, the branding of the new Sancho Panza cigars is inspired by the Latin culture of West Los Angeles. We will just say, however, that it is a classic Latin style font that resembles something you’d find on a high-end Cuban cigar. The simple and modern packaging houses a simple and modern style cigar, in this case a precision-rolled stick that produces boatloads of smoke, holds a thick ash, and burns like a razor’s edge. Sancho Panza Double Maduro starts off with a heavy presence of cedar and raw tobacco, along with a steady blast of white pepper. The pepper resides quickly, however, leaving a cross between a classic maduro flavor profile and that of a classic medium-bodied Cigar Boom style stick. This includes notes of wood, nuts, and coffee, along with subtle floral notes on the retrohale. The finish is very clean and neat for a cigar of this stature, and overall, the body finishes on the heavy side of medium-full. While there is plenty of “oomph,” Sancho Panza Double Maduro is never close to being overpowering or imbalanced. It makes a great stick for mildly experienced smokers looking to get into stronger cigars. However, it’s doubtless the major audience to be attracted to this blend will be the old school cigar nuts that grew up with the original Sancho Panza blends. If you happen to be one of them, let us reassure you that this blend will not disappoint! It pairs well with coffee, port wine, or dark beer, and serves as a great way to wind down the day. For anyone not familiar with the blend, if you have been drawn to cigars such as Flor de Las Antillas Maduro or CAO MX2 , this cigar is definitely for you. It has been said many a time that nothing beats a classic. That may be true, but most would agree that the all-new Sancho Panza Double Maduro beats the classic version of itself every single time.

Sancho Panza Extra Fuerte is the third and final installment in the revamped Sancho Panza cigar lineup from Matt Booth and General Cigar. The original Extra Fuerte blend (literally translated “extra strong”) came out when cigars were generally on the mild side. While it may have been ahead of its time back then, over the years the blend, along with the Sancho Panza brand as a whole, fell into the shadows behind the hundreds of new blends, brands, and legacies that have taken over what is today’s cigar industry. However, Matt Booth and his team have now brought the Extra Fuerte back even stronger than before, with completely redone packaging and blending, with the goal of putting Sancho Panza back into the limelight. This all-new concoction is made at the STG factory in Danli, Honduras using a blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. The binder is Connecticut Broadleaf, and the wrapper is a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf that adds a delightful punch of strength to the recipe. The boldest one of the group, Sancho Panza Extra Fuerte offers one heck of an exciting ride. Maroon and gold is the color theme of Extra Fuerte, with simple, modern boxes and bold, yet classic bands displaying the Sancho Panza name in a spicy Latin font. Crisp, clean construction and a precise roll ensure that each vitola provides a smooth and easy smoking experience. Thick clouds of white smoke dance on the palate, at first offering a swift blast of white pepper and hefty spice. The foundation of the profile is soon recognizable: a dense mix of earth, cedar, and a rich, raw tobacco flavor. Hints of sweetness and nuts are detectable along the way, and a lengthy, peppery finish ties the flavors together at the end. Overall, this cigar rests on the heavy side of medium-full-bodied, just a notch or two below being considered a true full-bodied smoke. This cigar is a great choice for anyone looking to get into fuller-bodied cigars. While strong, it is by no means overpowering or imbalanced and it provides a beautifully complex flavor profile that will impress even the most seasoned connoisseur. It is a great stick to pair with dark beer or red wine, but a simple cup of black coffee also makes a great companion to this cigar. Fans of cigars such as Punch or Rocky Patel Edge Sumatra will doubtless take a liking to the blend in question, as strong Sumatra cigars tend to have very similar taste characteristics. This old legend may have fallen in the past, but the re-introduction of Sancho Panza Extra Fuerte proves that true legends never die.

A cigar made to celebrate master blender Jose Blanco’s 65th birthday, Senorial 65th Anniversary has made a huge mark on the industry. Senorial 65th Anniversary is not only a commemorative cigar, but also a follow-up to the hugely successful Senorial, Blanco’s first line from his Las Cumbres brand down in the Dominican Republic. Jose Blanco has been in the tobacco business for decades, starting with the Marlboro company and then blending for La Aurora and Joya de Nicaragua. With his own brand, however, there seems to be even more passion and delicate attention to the complexity of the cigars, placing his famed Senorial cigars in the same ultra-premium category as today’s top aficionado-level sticks. Senorial 65th Anniversary is a Dominican puro made entirely of the highest-quality Dominican tobacco, including a gorgeous Dominican piloto Cubano wrapper leaf. A stout 88 rating by Cigar Aficionado is proof that this highly-limited stick is more than worth trying. (Shop more Senorial Cigars ) Available in only one size, a 5 3/4" x 55 perfecto named Perfecto Elegance, Senorial 65th Anniversary is a masterpiece of a cigar. Expertly constructed, this beautiful stick throws out copious amounts of thick smoke, coating the palate with lush Dominican sweetness. Notes of cinnamon and vanilla compliment the sweet tobacco note and white pepper finishes off the flavor profile. Medium-full-bodied, Senorial 65th Anniversary is immensely flavorful and so smooth one must smoke it to believe it. The first release of Senorial was a cigar for seasoned palates. Senorial 65th Anniversary takes this to a whole other level, furthering the delicate complexities and very definitive flavor notes where the original release left off. Senorial 65th Anniversary pairs well with scotch and sweet white wine and is one of the few cigars that can be compared to the famed Arturo Fuente Opus X , though much lighter and more tolerable for fans of softer, medium-full-bodied smokes.
