Very limited and rolled to impress the most discriminating connoisseurs, Senorial 65th Anniversary is a cigar that no aficionado should delay getting their hands on.

Roaring out of the gate from the moment you light one, the Sons of Anarchy Clubhouse Edition cigar is a full-throttle thrill ride. Following on the heels of the first successful tribute smoke to the hit television show, this Clubhouse Edition was hand built by the outlaws over at Black Crown with more power and more attitude. To accomplish this, they hit the back roads of Nicaragua to hunt down the finest long leaf tobaccos to be found anywhere, including a gorgeous Sun Grown Habano wrapper so full of oils you could almost use it to lube up your bike. So yeah, this is a promotional cigar and you're going to be dealing with some fancy schmancy packaging to get to where the meat is. Deal with it. Once you crack open the crate-like box and peel back the large red and silver band proudly borne by each stogie, it's time to take a big sniff of the heady fumes pouring off the beast and then light that baby up. At once earthy and bold, with a sharp, peppery tang and a big nicotine kick, the smoke breaks onto the tongue like a wave of pure pleasure. A punch of molasses-like sweetness rolls in at the midpoint and by the time the cool finale arrives you'll be exhilarated from the ride. If you are having trouble deciding if you can handle the strength of this full-bodied smoke you should probably stay away until you have some more notches in your belt, but for those enthusiasts looking for excitement and adventure then it's time to mount up. Similar to fan faves like La Gloria Cubana Serie R Esteli and Espinosa Habano, it's time to check out these Sons of Anarchy Clubhouse Edition cigars before they ride off into the sunset forever.

There are few names as prestigious in not only the cigar world but in general as Dunhill, and the new Dunhill Heritage cigar continues this tradition. Founded in 1907, Dunhill has always been synonymous with quality and luxury. Heritage was created to link the current cigar smoker with the days of yesteryear not only in look with its retro red and gold band, but also its flavor due to the vintage tobaccos it uses. This Honduran cigar is comprised of Honduran leaf from 2007, and two different Nicaraguan tobaccos from 2005 and 2012. Bound in a Nicaraguan Jalapa leaf, the wrapper is a reddish hued and oily Ecuadorian Habano. (Shop other Full-bodied cigars ) Different than most other Dunhills made, Heritage is a full bodied and full flavored cigar. Despite being the first Dunhill made in Honduras since 1998, there is minimal tobacco from this nation used, and what is left is a characteristically strong and peppery Nicaraguan filled cigar. The first few puffs will put a tingle on your lips that will stay there until you are ready to nub it out. During the course of this smoke, you are also introduced to earth, cedar, and slightly sweet notes. Dunhill Heritage gives every smoker the chance to taste history. From the vintage band to the vintage tobaccos used, each puff brings back memories of days gone by. If you like full-bodied cigars, then this is one you owe yourself to keep in your humidor for those special occasions.

It's time to get psyched because we have another Garcia family blend ready and waiting for you with the affordable Tabacos Baez Serie S.F. cigar. At this point, we certainly don't need to clue you in to the legendary My Father's Cigars launched by the even-more-legendary 'Don Pepin' Garcia and his son Jaime. For at least the last couple of decades, it seems that every year one or the other of these two juggernauts of tobacco have created sticks consistently ranked among the best of the best. This humbler release is a 'Cuban sandwich'-style (hint: S.F. stands for Short Filler) Nicaraguan puro that nonetheless captures the magic that you've come to know and expect. When it comes to mixed-filler stogies, a conscientious cigar company will utilize a high-quality wrapper to squeeze the most flavor possible out of the bits and pieces that get trimmed from their more famous smokes, and here is the proof. Each Tabacos Baez Serie S.F. is coated with an oily Nicaraguan Habano wrapper that reeks of expert fermentation and long aging. Firmer and with a more consistent cold draw than it has any right to have provided (thanks to the majority of actual longleaf in the blend), each glistening vitola primes the palate with flavors of cocoa and a touch of mint. Starting with a burst of the Garcia's black pepper calling card, this medium strength and easy burning smoke is flush with cedar, walnut, and coffee all the way through. Budget cigars can be all over the map when it comes to taste and quality, but you'll never go wrong when choosing anything coming out of the My Father's factory no matter the price. That's why we heartily recommend the Tabacos Baez Serie S.F if you're looking to get your daily handmade fix for less than a cup of joe. Or use them to impress friends and family alike during you're next get together. We won't reveal your secret.

Released in 2013, the Tatuaje 10th Anniversary was made to celebrate a decade of Tatuaje cigars as well as 10 years of Pete Johnson's relationship with Don Pepin Garcia. This Nicaraguan puro is made in the renowned My Father factory under the watchful eye of Garcia and features some of the best aged tobaccos that Nicaragua produces. The Tatuaje 10th Anniversary is a medium-to-full-bodied gem that is perfect for this sort of celebration. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) With an exquisite brown and gold band, the Tatuaje 10th Anniversary has a striking deep brown and oily wrapper leaf. The signature Pepin spice hits you before you even set the foot aflame. What comes next is slightly unexpected. Instead of that blast of pepper that makes you realize you are enjoying something out of the My Father factory, you get a creamy coffee note with just an undertone of spice. The more puffs you take, the more you realize what an amazing and complex cigar this is as pepper mixes with sweetness in seemingly alternating breaths. The Tatuaje 10th Anniversary Cigar is a worthy smoke for any celebration such as a wedding, birthday, or just that fact that you woke up this morning. Featuring amazing construction, and outstanding flavor, this cigar is sure to earn a top spot in your humidor. The medium-to-full body makes this a better cigar for the evening, but it also goes great with a nice cup of afternoon coffee. We would also recommend the Tatuaje Miami Reserva as well as the Tatuaje Fausto for a stronger more peppery smoke.

In the middle of 2011, Pete Johnson announced that he had created a side-project to his newly announced Fausto line. Fausto, which is based on the popular Tatuaje T110, also known as the Thermonuclear. Tatuaje Avion is an annual released box-pressed Perfecto version of the Tatuaje Fausto. Pete Johnson plans on releasing a new size every year, but all will be box-pressed. Perfectos. Other than the branding, Avion is identical to Fausto. Both are rolled at Jaime García's My Father Cigars S.A., both using Nicaraguan binder and fillers with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) Avion is offered in boxes of twenty with classic red bands contrasting the dark and thick Habano wrappers. For those familiar with T110 and Fausto, Avion is much of the same. It's a full-bodied, full strength and full flavor Nicaraguan powerhouse. Compared to the original T110 and Fausto, expect more pepper mixed into the classic Nicaraguan sweetness that made the T110 one of Pete Johnson's most heralded releases. Underneath the pepper, the Tatuaje Avion features the signature sweet leather, earth, cocoa and hints of coffee. For the Tatuaje fan, the inaugural release of the Avion is a must try. You've been warned.

Nowadays you have to be living under a rock to not know about Tatuaje cigars , but believe it or not there was once a time when they were exotic and beautiful creatures and the Black Label was the rarest of the group . First released in 2007, they instantly became one of the biggest sensations ever among aficionados in the know. As word of their existence spread, they became more and more difficult to find until one day they were gone, seemingly vanishing in the wind never to return. Bowing to the wishes of fanatics who had snapped up every Tatuaje release from before or after, creator Pete Johson used the occasion of his tenth year in the cigar business to bring back this Nicaraguan puro. The Tatuaje Black earned a prestigious #3 ranking on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 Cigars of 2025, achieving an exceptional 96 rating. Legend traces this cigar's inspiration to an attempt by Johnson to recreate a rugged little handmade he had once smoked in Cuba, and the fact that Black Label instantly became his personal stick seems to indicate success. The rough and tumble appearance of each vitola certainly lends credence to the tale, but fact or not once the cigar is lit you won't care where he picked up the motivation. Starting with citrus and leather at the fore, the profile later crawls through cocoa, toast, and black pepper, plus you can expect some coffee and a charred cedar in the retrohale. Crafted for Johnson at My Father Cigars, the Tatuaje Black Label certainly lives up to the hype that surrounds it. However, we recommend approaching them with an open mind and a clear palate so you can judge for yourself what makes them so highly sought after. Just don't wait too long to make a decision to try them because they're not always in stock and when they are it's never for long. Make your move now if you can and thank yourself later. (See all Tatuaje cigars )

In the middle of 2009, Pete Johnson of Tatuaje released another one of his popular limited edition single store releases, the Tatuaje T110. The T110 was a shorter version of a cigar that Pete had made in Pepín García's Nicaraguan factory as a joke, dubbed the Thermonuclear. It was one of the more innovative releases, as the blend was comprised entirely of Ligero, a first of its kind. The Ligero puro was so strong, Pete thought, that there was no way anyone would smoke one, let alone want it released. Turns out, he was wrong, as the T110 would become one of the most heralded Tatuaje releases of all time. For the next two years, Tatuaje fans and retailers begged Pete Johnson to make the T110 blend a regular release — finally he gave in, and the Tatuaje Fausto was born. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) Released in July of 2011, Fausto features a Nicaraguan binder and fillers with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and is made at Jaime García's state-of-the-art My Father Cigars S.A., in Estelí Nicaragua. The blend is identical to the original T110, although Pete has stated that he will not release the exact T110 size as part of Fausto. Instead, there are four sizes of Fausto including the: FT127 (Robusto), FT140 (Robusto Extra), FT153 (Toro) and FT166 (Short Churchill). In addition, Pete created Avion, a box-pressed Perfecto that features the same tobacco blend as Fausto. For those familiar with the T110, you can expect the same full-bodied, full-flavor and full strength profile across the entire Fausto line. Flavor is a mixture of peppers, sweet leather, earth and cocoa. Subtle notes of coffee and wood can be picked up, as the cigar retains a unique balance despite its inherent strength. Fausto, a must for the Tatuaje lover.

We don't think even Pete Johnson himself could have imagined how wildly beloved his Tatuaje cigars would become when he launched them, but truth be told, these smokes deserve every single accolade they receive. The Miami line is an amazing stick made in the heart of Little Havana in the famed Calle Ocho neighborhood of Miami. Made with the finest of first-generation Cuban-seed Nicaraguan filler tobacco and a beautiful Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, Tatuaje Miami is a fantastic full-bodied and flavored smoke. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) The classic and simple brown band on a Tatuaje Miami makes you think of cigars bought in corner shops in years gone by, and the flavors match this feeling of nostalgia. Blended as a collaboration between Pete and Don Pepin Garcia, there is a definite spice as soon as you take that first puff, for which Garcia is known. This spice is there from beginning to end, but there's also an amazing interplay with cedar and just a hint of sweetness. An amazing burn and draw is what we expect from this duo, and it is exactly what we got. Tatuaje Miami is a fantastic full-bodied smoke that will hit all the right notes and nuances you want from a premium cigar. The subtle sweetness plays perfectly off the spice that is present throughout the entire smoke. This is an amazing cigar to have on the back porch after a barbeque while enjoying a bourbon. If you like this, we would also recommend anything from the My Father line of smokes.

Tatuaje Cigars are one of the newest micro-brands to hit it big in the cigar world. “Tatuaje” means tattoo in Spanish. These cigars are blended as a partnership between “Tattoo” Pete Johnson and the cigar master himself, Don Pepin Garcia. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) The Tatuaje Cojonu 2003, Gran Cojonu, Cojonu 2006, Cojonu 2009, RC 184, RC 233, Reserva A Uno, Reserva SW, and Reserva J21 are all made in Miami using Nicaraguan fillers and binders that are lovingly cradled with an Ecuadoran Habano wrapper. The Tatuaje Petite Tatuaje Reserva, Petite Cazadores Reserva, and 7th Reserva are all rolled by Jaime Garcia at the My Father Cigars Factory in Nicaragua using the same binder and filler as the Miami line but this time with a Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper. Despite being blended by Don Pepin, this cigar is slightly less flavorful than we've come to expect from him, but perhaps that is exactly what Pete Johnson was looking for. Judging by how many of these we sell, Pete's on the right track.

We've all heard of people celebrating Christmas in July, why not Halloween? With this tasty, spicy, and amazing 10-cigar sampler, you will be well on your way. Since 2008, Pete Johnson and his Tatuaje Cigars have released an extremely limited release Halloween cigar named after famous movie monsters. In 2012 he decided to supplement the yearly release with a sampler of those same exclusive blends but in much smaller sizes called the Little Monsters. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) This year's Pudgy Monsters sampler retains the ring gauge from all the original releases but uses the much smaller lengths of the Little Monsters. New to this sampler are two blends exclusive to this set, the Chuck and the Tiff, based on the popular Child's Play franchise. Get your orders in now because these will not last long.

After being retired in 2007, Tatuaje Nuevitas has made its way back into the world of ultra premium cigars, and is now better than ever! Of all the cigars to bear the Tatuaje name over the years, only 3 have been made outside the doors of the famed My Father factory in Nicaragua. Those cigars were from Pete Johnson's early years in the business, and were produced in a small Nicaraguan shop called Tabacalera Tropical, which was at that time undergoing major changes due to new management. As a result, those 3 cigars were discontinued, never to be seen or heard about again—until now. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) The cigars in question are Tatuaje Nuevitas, Nuevitas Jibaro No. 1, and Nuevitas Jibaro No. 2, and all three have been resurrected into this modern age, and this time under the supervision of the master himself, Jose "Don" Pepin Garcia! That's right, though the blend hasn't changed one bit, the Nuevitas family has made its way home to the world's most state-of-the-art cigar factory, My Father Cigars S.A., to be produced alongside all the other superstars in the Tatuaje portfolio. The blend consists of all Nicaraguan tobacco—filler, wrapper, and binder, and the finishing touch is a gorgeous Nicaraguan Corojo 99 wrapper leaf that adds the classic Cuban flavor Tatuaje fans have come to know and love over the years. How does Nuevitas do in this modern age? Good enough to earn a 93 rating and a number 9 spot on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 list, but who are we trying to kid, does that really come as a surprise? Boxed in old school cedar chests and bearing classic Cuban style orange bands, the packaging of the Tatuaje Nuevitas is delightfully simple. The difference between the Nuevitas and the 2 Nuevitas Jibaro is that the Jibaro versions sport an unfinished foot, as well as an orange-on-white band, as opposed to the white-on-orange bands dressing the Nuevitas. Aside from that, the blends are identical. The roll of the cigars is nothing short of expert level, and the overall construction is mind blowing. An easy draw provides billowing clouds of dense blue smoke, from the very first puffs pounding the palate with heavy white pepper. This is especially intense during the beginning of the Jibaro versions, where no wrapper is present for about a quarter of an inch. Soon, cedar and earth take over the show, raw tobacco flavor being in the spotlight. Spicy notes pepper the profile throughout the duration of the cigar, along with hints of sweetness, especially on the retrohale. This blend resides on the heavy side of medium-full and is impeccably balanced. Tatuaje Nuevitas is a cigar aimed at experienced connoisseurs. Though a throwback of sorts, it is still a Tatuaje, and it was still built to satisfy truly discriminating cigar enthusiasts. Medium-full-bodied and spicy, Nuevitas pairs well with full-bodied beer or bourbon, and is best enjoyed after a meal or as a nightcap. Before Tatuaje Miami or Tatuaje Havana VI , Nuevitas was actually the cigar that started it all for Pete Johnson. Those who may have missed it back in the day now have a chance to experience the classic taste of Tatuaje in its truest form. Light up the time machine and return to the glory days of boutique cigars with Tatuaje Nuevitas.

Tatuaje Reserva Broadleaf is a throwback to Cuban cigars of yesteryear, but with a delicious modern twist. Let's face it, when it comes to Cuban style flavor, few names do it better than Pete Johnson and Tatuaje. For years, the original Tatuaje Reserva has been praised as one of the finest blends to ever be produced in Don Pepin's My Father factory down in Nicaragua. In 2017, Pete Johnson and friends introduced what is essentially that same blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco, but with a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper in place of the standard Corojo leaf showcased in the original. The result is Tatuaje Reserva Broadleaf, a cigar that since its introduction has more than lived up to the reputation expected from fans of Tatuaje cigars the world over.

When you're looking for budget smokes, Tatuaje cigars are probably the furthest thing from your mind, but the Series P Sumatra will soon be at the top of your shopping list. For the longest time most of Pete Johnson's famous creations, all of them developed in collaboration with Don Pepin Garcia, were best suited for high rollers or special occasions. Now, the Series P are affordable mixed filler smokes which open the door to Tatuaje's flavor for any reason and any time. Containing a luscious mix of medium and long leaf tobacco, at about a 60 to 40 ratio, each stick is finished with an oily Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. (See all Tatuaje cigars ) Despite their interior makeup and the fact that they're seriously cheap, you'll notice right away that construction and aesthetics are still top notch. What else would you expect since My Father Cigars' masterful torcedors are responsible for their creation. Slightly lighter in the hand than their Tatuaje Havana VI brethren, draw and burn of the Series P still produce mouthfuls of heady, medium-bodied smoke full of pepper and leather, with some toasted wood during any retrohales and a hint of milk chocolate in the aftertaste.

Once upon a time, there was a quaint cigar brand that seemed to fade into the background among all the stars of the cigar boom, yet somehow it found its way into darn near every retailer’s humidor across the country. That cigar would end up becoming a go-to for beginners, a novelty for the experienced, and a predecessor to many ultra-premium projects over the next few decades. That cigar was Te Amo, the original brand that put Mexico on the map and introduced the cigar industry to what would be deemed some of the finest tobacco on the planet. Now, many moons later, the legend returns, and has shaken the world of premium cigars. Behold, Te Amo, the Original San Andres Valley Cigar! Made by the Turrent family, the ones responsible for the original Te Amo brand, this cigar is constructed by hand at at the family’s own Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V. in Mexico, the factory responsible for the famed Casa Turrent. Te Amo, the Original San Andres is a Mexican puro, containing 100% Mexican tobacco which is all grown in the San Andres region. The filler and wrapper are San Andres Habano, the binder is San Andres Negro, and all tobaccos are aged and fermented to exacting standards before being turned into the beautiful package offered here. Sleek and clean white and green boxes house the gorgeous vitolas, each one wearing a simple green, white, and gold band. The construction is fantastic, and each and every stick offers optimal performance and no shortage of opportunities to enjoy the rich, flavorful smoke produced generously on every puff. Opening up with a short burst of pepper, the flavor profile quickly turns mellow with hints of cedar, cereal, and floral notes. The overall core of the cigar is rich raw tobacco flavor, and the finish is smooth and crisp. Simple, straightforward, and never overpowering, Te Amo, the Original San Andres finishes on the light side of medium-full-bodied. This cigar is suitable for all audiences, but the main crowd looking at this one is likely to be those old school cigar nuts that remember the Te Amos of old. It’s safe to say that the brand has evolved, and this sure isn’t your grandfather’s Te Amo. It pairs well with scotch, medium-bodied beer, and, dare we say, tequila, and is suitable for just about any occasion. Fans of medium-full-bodied gems such as La Aroma de Cuba Pasion or the original Romeo y Julieta will likely find pleasure in enjoying this blend. “Te Amo” is literally translated “I Love You,” and it’s safe to say that after just a few puffs of Te Amo, the Original San Andres, you’ll probably be in love too!

The Griffin's is one of the most recognizable classic Dominican cigars on the market, surviving for what seems like centuries and still held in the highest esteem by lovers of mild-medium-bodied blends. Made by Davidoff and produced in the Dominican Republic, the Griffin's has come to be known as a more affordable way to experience the amazing flavor and quality offered by one of the most renowned ultra-premium brands on the planet. The delightful recipe consists of an all-Dominican blend of filler and binder tobacco and a caramel-brown Connecticut shade wrapper leaf. Simple? Yes. Mellow and tame? Yes. But the Griffin's has proven over many years that its particular version of a top shelf Dominican cigar is head and shoulders above the rest. Like its uber expensive Davidoff cousin, the Griffin's sports a white band and comes packaged in a classic wooden cabinet box. Also adhering to the Davidoff theme, the quality and consistency are second to none, each vitola boasting masterful construction and offering a cool, easy draw. Plentiful clouds of rich, blue smoke offer a mild, yet flavorful opening of earthy goodness, along with a burst of subtle cedar and hints of toast and tobacco flower. The flavor profile is creamy and buttery smooth through and through, the finish is crisp and clean, and overall the Griffin's is simple, mellow, and luxurious. The Griffin's is proof that a cigar doesn't need to have multiple layers of complexity in order to provide an extraordinary smoking experience. Like its Davidoff counterparts, The Griffin's takes simplicity to a whole new level of satisfying. Mild-medium-bodied and never lacking balance, the Griffin's makes a great cigar for just about anyone. It pairs well with white wine or even champagne, making it an ideal stick to celebrate with. As for comparable cigars, the obvious comparison would be Davidoff, but other premium Connecticut-wrapped masterpieces such as Avo Classic and Diamond Crown will doubtless be included by many in the same category. Maybe you are just starting out with cigars? Maybe you are a long-time cigar freak and just love milder stogies? Maybe you simply want to enjoy a timeless classic that never seems to lack in the satisfaction department? Whatever the case, The Griffin's is a perfect cigar for any occasion.

You already know about the Toraño legacy and the significance of the year identified in the Toraño 1916 Cameroon cigar, right? No? Well, let's fix that right now. 1916 was the year family patriarch Don Santiago Toraño emigrated from Spain to Cuba, and also the year he began growing tobacco in that island nation. This brave and seemingly small act planted the seed for what would eventually become the Toraño Family Cigar Company, creators of an array of varied and highly-rated handmade cigars. For the 1916, the Nicaraguan-grown Cameroon wrapper is fitted over a Nicaraguan binder and overlaid onto a fine blend of Cuban-seed Nicaraguan and Honduran tobaccos.

Like many traditional cigar producers, the Toraños developed their own private, family-only blend not available to the general public. But they eventually decided to release it as the Casa Toraño cigar. And we're glad they did. Knowledge gleaned from years of experience with every aspect of the cigar-making process, from planting the seed to aging the finished product, has resulted in a complex and refined stogie that is amazingly affordable. The Toraños started with a Nicaraguan binder from their own farms; used it to hug a mixture of Nicaraguan, Honduran, and what they call a "family blend" of Central and South American tobaccos, and finished with an Ecuadorian-Connecticut wrapper. (See more Toraño Cigars ) Rising to the level of other flavorful cigars like the Perdomo Exhibicion Connecticut or Rocky Patel The Edge Lite, the Casa Toraño is an excellent value for smokers looking for a mild to medium stick that can be enjoyed with anything from an iced tea to a Decadencia Port, a Toraño favorite libation. Buy now and become an honorary member of the family.

The Toraño Exodus 1959 cigar is a serious cigar meant to honor a serious event, namely the escape from post-revolution Cuba by many of the families involved in the newly-nationalized tobacco industry. Many of these exiles would continue their trade in other countries, and current company president Charlie Toraño's grandfather did just that by restarting the family tradition of cultivating tobacco. To memorialize the brave first steps taken by the men who would go on to create the modern cigar industry, Charlie created a 5-nation blend of long leaf filler from Dominican, Honduran, Mexican, Nicaraguan, and Costa Rican sources to be layered into a fine Honduran binder and Nicaraguan Habano wrapper. (See more Toraño Cigars ) Firmly in the medium-full category, the Toraño Exodus 1959 is nonetheless recommended for experienced and novice smokers alike. The evolution of flavors and strength allows each aficionado to approach the cigar on their own terms, whether laid down before the final crescendo or taken all the way through the nub. A good humidor companion to the Xikar HC Colorado, this cigar is a fitting tribute indeed.

We've already told you about the naming of the Exodus 1959 line of cigars, but with the milestone reaching its fiftieth year, Carlos Toraño knew he needed to do something special, and so the Toraño Exodus 1959 50 Year was born. For those of you unfamiliar, it was 1959, when Carlos' family left behind all they had known in Cuba to relocate to the Dominican Republic. From there they would work to build what would come to be one of the most highly recognized cigar-making families ever. To properly celebrate this anniversary, Carlos created a new blend of Esteli and Pueblo Nuevo Nicaraguan tobaccos and cloaked them beneath an amazing Brazilian Arapiraca. (See more Toraño Cigars ) The copper-highlighted double bands decorating each vitola are quite large, but a cigar with this amount of beauty is worthy of such elegant livery. Mahogany with uniform dark spots creating a mottled tortoiseshell appearance. The cigar exudes a pleasingly exotic spice aroma, and the flavor, through a cold draw is tongue-tingling. Sweet plumes of smoke pour through from the start, with a primary profile of espresso and cocoa, but there is a definite gingerbread quality to the smoke that builds in sweetness as the ash gets longer. Once the cigar enters the second half of its journey, plenty of rich molasses and creamy wood will be washing over your palate in a medium to full bodied flood of flavor.

If you think that cigar companies are only interested in producing stronger and heavier cigars, then let the Toraño Exodus 1959 Silver cigar dissuade you of that impression. The Toraño Family Cigar Company has been producing cigars since the mid-eighties, first for a host of other companies and finally under the Toraño name in the nineties, and they know how to create a entire range of quality smokes to satisfy any palate. The 1959 Silver is an affordable medium-bodied cigar suitable for special occasions and contains a blend of tobaccos quite different from many of the intense puros otherwise available today. The wrapper is from a familiar source, Nicaragua, but is the lesser known Criollo variety. The binder is a unique Costa Rican leaf, while the filler has more Costa Rican mixed with Honduran and even Mexican tobaccos. (See more Toraño Cigars )

Torano Hogshead is a cigar by Carlos Torano and company that proves that a stick doesn't have to cost an arm and a leg to be enjoyable. Paying homage to a time when cigars and alcohol were aged in large wooden barrels known as hogsheads, Torano Hogshead can be considered a smokable history lesson. Made by hand in Nicaragua, Torano Hogshead consists of a hearty medium-full-bodied blend of Nicaraguan, Dominican, and Pennsylvanian filler tobacco inside a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper leaf. Bold, yet not too intense, Torano Hogshead makes a great relaxing choice for those cool autumn afternoons when taking it easy seems like the only thing to do. (See more Toraño Cigars ) Rustic, rugged, and tasty, Torano Hogshead begins with a beefy introduction laced with heavy pepper and wood. This soon turns to an earthy mixture of leather and raw tobacco that carries through the entire cigar. The finish is simple and spicy, with a touch of coffee. Overall, Hogshead is simple and pleasant. There are very few rough spots and it's not overly complicated. It's just right. Appealing to a vast audience of cigar nuts, Torano Hogshead is a great, affordable cigar that's versatile and enjoyable at any time. It makes a great breakfast cigar, especially when paired with coffee, but it also pairs very nicely with bourbon. Torano Hogshead is medium-full-bodied and very straightforward, similar in stature to MUWAT and CAO Brazilia . The simple packaging, a rustic burlap sack, puts the finishing touch on the old fashioned theme presented with Torano Hogshead. Over the years, the Torano name has been hugely popular and has garnered much success. Cigars like Torano Hogshead are the reason, appealing to anyone and everyone, and always satisfying.

The products of Carlos Toraño may not be on the radar of many of today's newer smokers, but the Toraño Loyal cigar should live up to its name by creating a whole new group of followers. A testament to their commitment to high-value, top-quality cigars, the Toraño Family Cigar Company draws deep from the well of their decades of tobacco experience to deliver a flavorful and affordable stogie that has already garnered a 93 rating. From the toothy and thick Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper to the Nicaraguan Pueblo Nuevo and Dominican Piloto Cubano filler, the Loyal is one fine cigar. (See more Toraño Cigars ) Sipped alongside a cool Belgian triple ale, the Loyal can serve as a great introduction to the brand for those who have not had the pleasure of a Toraño cigar, while it stands as a reaffirmation for fans that the company remains committed to producing excellent cigars now and into the future. Once you've decided how good these are, you can explore other similar bargain cigars with the 5 Vegas Classic and La Reloba.

With a name like Toraño Master, the cigar so designated better be good. Really freaking good. Fortunately, the two men behind the cigar, Charlie Toraño and Felipe Sosa, are themselves masters of the leaf. Through their close collaboration, these legends were able to create a smoke worthy of a Top 3, and ratings of 91 and an extraordinary 98. What's their secret? There isn't one. Just hard work and a commitment to sourcing the best leaves from the Esteli and Jalapa regions of Nicaragua and rolling them with superior craftsmanship beneath a perfectly aged Habano leaf from Ecuador. (See more Toraño Cigars ) The Toraño Master would be well worth the experience at twice the price, but somehow the creators have found a way to keep it affordable so that anyone can keep their humidor well stocked alongside other masterful creations like the Rocky Patel The Edge Habano and San Lotano Habano. Paired with a frothy root beer on a sunny afternoon, this cigar could be the one to inspire you to reach your own pinnacle of achievement.

As a follow-up to a popular and well received predecessor, one can hardly do better than the Toraño Master Habano Maduro. The decision to create a Maduro version of their popular, 98-rated Toraño Master was an easy one for Charlie Toraño and his roller extraordinaire Felipe Sosa. The difficult choice was what type of Maduro would live up to their, and more importantly their customers, expectations. A San Andres? A Connecticut Broadleaf? After experimenting with numerous iterations, the honor was given to a sun grown Nicaraguan Habano Maduro. Saw that one coming, didn't you? (See more Toraño Cigars ) Able to hold its own among highly rated Maduros like the San Lotano Maduro or the Oliva Serie V Maduro, the Toraño Master Habano Maduro has earned a place in any humidor. Medium bodied yet full in flavor, it is appropriate for special occasions and everyday enjoyment alike. Go ahead and stockpile them. We won't judge.

Celebrating over 90 years of cigar-making, the Torano Noventa 90 cigar is a Nicaraguan puro utilizing a nearly flawless habano wrapper, a habano binder, and a complex blend of fillers from Jalapa, Esteli, Condega and Pueblo Nuevo. A smooth, creamy smoke with hints of wood and cedary spice. Torano cigars, one of the top cigar making families in the biz, spans four generations in the tobacco industry, and prides themselves on expert knowledge and top-notch quality. (See more Toraño Cigars ) Having their roots in Cuba, today the Torano family cultivates crops from the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Mexico, and Ecuador. Striving to create the most complex blends possible, they utilize tobaccos from these countries and more to deliver a unique experience to remember time after time.

We've already told you about the naming of the Exodus 1959 line of cigars, but with the milestone reaching its fiftieth year, Carlos Toraño knew he needed to do something special, and so the Toraño Exodus 1959 50 Year was born. For those of you unfamiliar, it was 1959, when Carlos' family left behind all they had known in Cuba to relocate to the Dominican Republic. From there they would work to build what would come to be one of the most highly recognized cigar-making families ever. To properly celebrate this anniversary, Carlos created a new blend of Esteli and Pueblo Nuevo Nicaraguan tobaccos and cloaked them beneath an amazing Brazilian Arapiraca. (See more Toraño Cigars ) The copper-highlighted double bands decorating each vitola are quite large, but a cigar with this amount of beauty is worthy of such elegant livery. Mahogany with uniform dark spots creating a mottled tortoiseshell appearance. The cigar exudes a pleasingly exotic spice aroma, and the flavor, through a cold draw is tongue-tingling. Sweet plumes of smoke pour through from the start, with a primary profile of espresso and cocoa, but there is a definite gingerbread quality to the smoke that builds in sweetness as the ash gets longer. Once the cigar enters the second half of its journey, plenty of rich molasses and creamy wood will be washing over your palate in a medium to full bodied flood of flavor.

The Toraño Family Cigar Company created the Salutem cigar in celebration of anyone who makes the most of life, as a tribute to those who face great challenges, as a toast to the men and women of character. Fortunately, any smoker can and should consider themselves worthy. And what an offering it is. For a company with roots all the way back to 1916 in Cuba, the Salutem is the first of their blends to feature, in addition to Nicaraguan and Dominican Corojo, a rich Cameroon leaf as a component of the filler instead of its more familiar use as a wrapper (see the Toraño 1916). That honor is given to a silky Ecuadorian Habano. (See more Toraño Cigars ) It's already been said this is a cigar for everyone, so all that is left is to buy Toraño Salutem and enjoy. That's why it was created and it is sure to satisfy even the most discriminating of palates, whether as a mid-afternoon boredom buster with a cup of coffee or as a dessert after dinner with a sweet liqueur.

The Toraño The Brick cigar was created to fulfill two of the biggest demands being made by increasing numbers of cigar-crazy lunatics: A bigger ring gauge and a better price. Some companies might bury their collective heads in the sand and keep hoping for a return to the way things were during the Cigar Boom of the late 90s when they called the shots, but not the Toraño Family Cigar Company. They know they must keep focused on their customer's requests and ever-changing preferences. For The Brick, this meant a cigar with healthy Honduran fillers and binder, an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, and rolled 54 ring or bigger with a firm box press. (See more Toraño Cigars )

Every handmade stogie the world over gives an interesting insight into the company that produced it and the Toraño Virtuoso cigar is no different. What it says about the Toraño Family Cigar Company is twofold: One, the Toraños remain as committed to the tobacco growing business as they were when they began the trade in 1916 Cuba. And two, they are not afraid to take their traditional approach to the crafting of cigars in a new direction. In testament to both qualities, the Virtuoso is the first time a Toraño cigar has utilized a sun grown wrapper from a Toraño farm. This Nicaraguan Nuevo Pueblo leaf has been patient aged before being laid over a mix of Nicaraguan, Honduran, and Panamanian tobaccos making this the fullest-bodied blend of any Toraño line. (See more Toraño Cigars ) Similar to the Arturo Fuente Rosado Sungrown, the Toraño Virtuoso sits squarely in the medium-full category but with a harmonized and smooth profile that won't overwhelm those looking for an evening of enjoyment with a stronger stick. Pair with a VSOP or XO cognac for a combination worthy of an encore.

Paying homage to the ‘golden years’ of cigars and Caribbean culture. Trinidad Espiritu – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Trinidad is one of the world’s iconic cigar brands, turning 50 years old this year. Trinidad Espriritu pays homage to the brands’ Heritage roots and takes adult cigar smokers back to the late 60’s and early 70’s, considered as the ‘golden years’ of cigars. Trinidad Espiritu, meaning ‘Spirit’, embodies a vintage presentation of Caribbean culture, with colorful and eye-catching branding and a cigar that speaks to the soul. The cigar has been blended in collaboration with AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, utilizing the finest tobaccos, crafting a complex tasting cigar with a full flavored experience.

Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 1 is the cigar that has brought fame and glamour back to the classic, all-but-forgotten Trinidad name. Over the years, Altadis USA has made several not-so-successful attempts to “bring back” the non-Cuban Trinidad brand. It wasn’t until they teamed up with Abel Fernandez down in Nicaragua that they finally hit the nail on the head. Blended by Abel himself and rolled at the famous Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, Trinidad Espiritu re-kindles the Cuban legacy behind the name and tells quite a story with its smoke. It is a Nicaraguan puro, meaning every single sliver of tobacco used in each cigar has its origin in Nicaragua, most of it coming from Fernandez’s own family farms. The blend is rich and flavorful, yet not overpowering, making for an extremely satisfying experience. How satisfying, exactly? Well, we will let the rock-solid 94 rating and 2023 #12 ranking in Cigar Aficionado answer that. The colorful packaging is inspired by 1960s era Havana and is in fact its own work of art. The real artwork, however, is in the cigar itself. Each vitola is expertly crafted and boasts a gleaming rosado brown wrapper leaf. As with all Fernandez cigars, construction is incredible and the draw is plenteous. A spicy opening leads the way to an array of tangy citrus and nutty goodness . White pepper, cream, and cedar become clearly noticeable along the way, in addition to a core of bready, toasty tobacco flavor. The finish is extremely crisp and clean, leaving no trace of an aftertaste. Distinctly medium-full-bodied, Trinidad Espiritu is more than a worthy remake of the Cuban original. Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 1 is a cigar for a more refined audience. The complexity of the blend requires a well-developed palate in order to be truly appreciated. Medium-full-bodied , Espiritu pairs well with scotch or red wine and is ideal for any time of day. Espiritu is similar in stature to higher end blends such as Enclave or H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez. Bold, yet balanced, refined and exciting, Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 1 is exactly the cigar that was needed to bring the Trinidad name back to the forefront. Try one today and experience the taste of yesteryear combined with the blending prowess of today.

Find what moves your spirit with Trinidad Espiritu Series No.2  Trinidad Espiritu No.2 – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Find what moves your spirit with Trinidad Espiritu Series No.2 Trinidad Espiritu honors the brand’s history with the skill and innovation of today’s cigar masters. Trinidad Espiritu Series No.2 is steeped in Brazilian spirit; crafted with tobaccos grown in Nicaragua and Brazil, blended in collaboration with Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez, wrapped in a Brazilian Arapiraca leaf. The combination of tobaccos produces a harmonious medium to full bodied cigar with extraordinary complexity and earthy notes.

There are some cigars best enjoyed during long moments of quiet contemplation, but the Trinidad Espiritu Series 2 cigar is built for those times when music, friends, and celebration are the most important parts of your year. Inspired by the boisterous jamboree of light and sound that is Rio's Carnival, the legendary duo of Rafael Nodal and A.J. Fernandez created these full-bodied gems to highlight the qualities of Brazilian tobacco. From playing a significant role in the complex blend alongside rich Nicaraguan filler to the spirited Arapiraca wrapper that coats each vitola, the exotic tastes imparted by the well-fermented longleaf will have you dancing the bossa nova with delight. This blend has been ranked as high as 92 by Cigar Aficionado . Dressed for the occasion in a multicolored band of blue, green, black, and gold, these oily sticks will be the life of the party both in your humidor and at the next barbecue or beach day. A veritable parade of flavor and aroma is evident as soon as the toothy, cocoa-colored Trinidad Espiritu Series 2 is brought to your lips, where a flourish of spice greets both nose and tongue. A strong flame begins the slow-burning festivities, where thick plumes of cool smoke carry the tastes of smoked Picanha steak, Brigadeiro chocolate fudge, dark and luscious Açaí berries, and creamy Cafe com Leite. An escape from the ordinary each and every time one is lit, the Trinidad Espiritu Series 2 will turn even the most mundane of days into something special. Complimentary smokes with that Brazilian dazzle include the obvious CAO Brasilia, but don't overlook the Diesel Whiskey Row Sherry Cask or the stellar Florida Sun Grown by Drew Estate. Book your flight to the Southern tropics today.

Trinidad Espiritu No. 3 is an exceptional cigar celebrating Mexican heritage, with a rich blend of Mexican and Nicaraguan tobaccos. Trinidad Espiritu No. 3 – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Trinidad Espiritu No. 3, a culmination of Trinidad’s series, is a testament to meticulous craftsmanship and heritage. Celebrating Mexican culture, this cigar offers a symphony of earthiness, spiciness, cocoa, and coffee, carefully crafted by AJ Fernandez & Rafael Nodal. Embracing a fusion of the finest global tobaccos, it provides an immersive journey of flavor, culture, and the vibrant celebration of life.

AJ Fernandez has been known in recent years to take classic cigar brands that have all but disappeared and give them new life, and most of the time, that new life is far better than before. Such is precisely the case with the Trinidad Espiritu series, a hugely popular lineup that has quickly risen to the top. First came the Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 1, a 94-rated beast that gave a whole new look to the Trinidad name. Then, there was Espiritu Series No. 2, a spicy, bold follow-up to its highly refined counterpart. Now, AJ Fernandez and Rafael Nodal team up again, and the Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 3 has more than proven its worth in terms of cigar excellence. Like the others, Series No. 3 is made at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, under the watchful eye of AJ Fernandez himself. The recipe for this one seems simple, but in fact was years in the making. Top-end Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos are nestled beneath a dark, oily Mexican Habano San Andres wrapper. The original blend used a Habano wrapper, and was bold, yet subtle. The second had a Brazilian leaf that added a spicy intensity. This version is somewhere in the middle, but as anyone who has enjoyed San Andres-wrapped cigars knows, it’s not your typical maduro experience. The Trinidad Espíritu Series No. 3 earned a standout #5 ranking on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 Cigars of 2025 , boasting a 95 rating and showcasing a masterful blend crafted by A.J. Fernandez for the Trinidad brand . Packaged in colorful boxes of 20 depicting classic Mexican artwork, each Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 3 wears double bands and displays the usual Espiritu theme. The thing that sets Series No. 3 apart from its predecessors is the distinct and sharp box press. This not only adds to the aesthetics of the cigar, but lends to its incredible performance, namely a soft and easy draw that produces an immense volume of smoke on each and every puff. This cigar begins with a spicy white pepper introduction, which is quite short-lived. The attention quickly goes from spicy to creamy, as decadent dark chocolate and espresso take over the spotlight. Wrapped around an earthy Nicaraguan core, these flavors team up with cinnamon, black cherry, and cedar . The finish is long and full, and overall Espiritu Series No. 3 finishes on the heavy side of medium-full-bodied. Made for connoisseurs like the others in the Espiritu lineup, Series No. 3 displays complexity, balance, and depth of flavor that can only truly be appreciated by a well-seasoned palate. Its precision construction and beautiful appearance only add to the allure, and many would call this a near-perfect ultra-premium specimen. This stick pairs well with coffee, dark rum, or port wine, and demands plenty of time to thoroughly enjoy everything that makes it so incredible. Some would compare it to such San Andres masterpieces as EP Carrillo La Historia or even Joya de Nicaragua Cinco de Cinco , so fans of these sticks should definitely give this one a shot. The Trinidad Espiritu series has proven to be an absolute force in the cigar world, and Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 3 is what many consider to be the best yet.

Trinidad Paradox is another cigar in the long line of traditional Altadis brands to get a facelift, much like the Monte by Montecristo and the Saint Luis Rey Gen 2. The Paradox is the first cigar out of Trinidad to combine their very old-school and traditional ways of cigar making with a modern feel. While the other reboots are focussing on heavier, fuller-bodied flavors, the Paradox is actually coming slightly down from the traditional Trinidad and is a medium-bodied smoke. Handcrafted in the Dominican Republic, Paradox has Nicaraguan filler, a Dominican binder, and a Mexican San Andreas Criollo 98 wrapper.

Rafael Nodal, boutique cigar crafter, reimagined the Cuban soul of Trinidad with this masterpiece, resulting in this Dominican puro full of character, complex f Trinidad Santiago – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Rafael Nodal, boutique cigar crafter, reimagined the Cuban soul of Trinidad with this masterpiece, resulting in this Dominican puro full of character, complex flavor and unique aromas. This exciting Trinidad is a Dominican puro rolled with tobaccos grown in the fertile Cibao Valley by legendary master blender José “Jochy” Blanco in collaboration with Rafael Nodal. Trinidad Santiago is a medium to full-bodied cigar with notes of cocoa, leather, toasted almonds, and a vibrant peppery finish.

Trinidad, a Cuban-heritage brand, has recently unveiled its first-ever Dominican puro - Santiago. This medium-to-full bodied recipe of handcrafted tobacco is sourced exclusively from the Dominican Republic. It consists of harmonious notes of cocoa, spices, leather, and nuts in classic shapes that promise an indulgent smoking experience. The Santiago release was born from a collaboration between Trinidad's creator Rafael Nodal and José "Jochy '' Blanco, an acclaimed Dominican cigar maker and tobacco grower. Together they created an exquisite blend of all-Dominican tobaccos grown by Blanco himself. When it comes to flavors and aromas, the Belicoso size offers an abundance of earthy notes. It includes coffee and licorice, that transition into a sweet aftertaste with hints of honey and wood. These cigars are crafted with the finest Dominican Republic tobacco, giving them a natural coloring and robust flavor. The wrapper originates from the Dominican Republic, and the wrapper leaf is also of Dominican provenance - adding an extra layer of complexity to the blend that makes this cigar stand out. With Trinidad Santiago Cigars, you get more than just a smoke; you get access to an exquisite taste, smell, and feel that will have you coming back for more. Whether enjoyed by an aficionado or a novice, these cigars are sure to please all who partake in their luxurious experience. Those who wish to indulge in a classic Cuban brand's take on Dominican tobaccos will find themselves in for quite the treat with this boutique release specially calibrated for the seasoned connoisseur. A creation worthy of bearing his name, Trinidad Santiago is sure to awaken your senses with its intricate combination of flavors. This provides a delightful smoking experience for those who seek out premium tobaccos like this one. Trinidad Santiago cigars offer a light and nutty flavor with hints of sweetness reminiscent of raisins. The construction is superb, with even combustion and a slow burn that allows for a peaceful smoking experience. Not to mention, they come with an entirely affordable price tag, given the quality they offer. Trinidad Santiago Cigars are one of the top choices when picking out a premium handmade cigar.

Trinidad X Tommy Bahama Island Collection embodies the seamless blend of refinement and laid-back island living. Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 Two iconic brands come together to celebrate the art of relaxation and the spirit of a tropical escape. Crafted in collaboration with renowned cigar makers AJ Fernandez and Rafael Nodal, this premium collection features exclusive Nicaraguan tobaccos, delivering a sophisticated, multi-dimensional profile. Each cigar offers a sensory journey that reflects the refined experience of the island lifestyle. With every draw, the Trinidad X Tommy Bahama cigars invite you to indulge in the harmony of craftsmanship and tranquility.

Some collaborations are built around a logo. Others are built around a shared philosophy. The Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection is the latter, bringing together Trinidad's long-standing reputation for premium cigar craftsmanship with Tommy Bahama's unmistakable embrace of relaxed luxury and island living. The result is a cigar that celebrates slowing down, savoring the moment, and enjoying life's finer pleasures wherever your favorite place to unwind may be. Developed through the combined expertise of Rafael Nodal, A.J. Fernandez, and the Altadis Grupo de Maestros, the Island Collection is handcrafted at A.J. Fernandez's renowned factory in Estelí, Nicaragua using tobaccos grown exclusively on Fernandez's Nicaraguan farms. This carefully selected all-Nicaraguan blend delivers a refined medium-bodied profile that balances richness with remarkable smoothness, showcasing the exceptional quality for which both Trinidad and A.J. Fernandez have become known. Construction is flawless, providing an effortless draw, an even burn, and dense clouds of smoke from beginning to end. The journey opens with notes of toasted cedar before creamy layers of warm vanilla and natural sweetness gradually emerge. Gentle touches of spice weave throughout the profile, while the rich Nicaraguan tobaccos add depth and complexity without overpowering the palate. Every draw remains balanced and inviting, creating a smoking experience that's as relaxing as it is flavorful. The Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection is more than a premium cigar; it's an invitation to embrace the island state of mind. Whether enjoyed overlooking the water, relaxing on the patio after a long day, or paired with your favorite aged rum or tropical cocktail, this distinctive collaboration delivers the perfect balance of heritage, craftsmanship, and effortless sophistication. It's a cigar designed not only to be smoked, but to remind you that sometimes the best moments are the ones where you simply slow down and enjoy the view.

Trinidad y Cia is an old-school bargain brand that's been around for years. Born and raised in Nicaragua, Trinidad y Cia pays homage to classic Cuban sticks sold on the streets of Havana in years past. Trinidad y Cia consists of a simple blend of Dominican filler leaves, a Honduran binder, and a smooth Ecuador Sumatra wrapper leaf. It should be noted that Trinidad y Cia is a mixed filler cigar, also known as a "Cuban Sandwich" style cigar, using a mixture of both long and short fillers to keep manufacturing costs down and maintain a consistent draw. Overall, Trinidad y Cia is a pretty decent knock-around cigar for the money. The classic bands on Trinidad y Cia add to the old fashioned Cuban feel of the experience. An easy draw and sharp burn are always to be expected. Voluminous clouds of white smoke deliver a simple, earthy flavor with a nutty, grassy character and hints of nutmeg and cinnamon. A pronounced raw tobacco note carries the flavor profile throughout. Very pleasant and easy to smoke. Trinidad y Cia is a great cigar for newbies, though even seasoned connoisseurs should give it a try simply for the nostalgia if nothing else. At an incredibly affordable price point, Trinidad y Cia makes a great "dog walker" or "grass cutter" cigar as well. Medium-bodied, Trinidad y Cia pairs well with white or red wine, bourbon, and light to medium beer. Other value-priced cigars to consider include Flor de Oliva and Mayorga . Jump in a time machine and taste the classic streets of Cuba with a uber-affordable Trinidad y Cia cigar today.

VegaFina 1998 is the new line that commemorates the brand’s year of creation. Handmade cigars with carefully selected tobacco leaves which have been aged for  VegaFina 1998 – Altadis USA – Crafting Cigars Great Since 1918 VegaFina 1998 is the new line that commemorates the brand’s year of creation. Handmade cigars with carefully selected tobacco leaves which have been aged for at least 3 years. VegaFina 1998 is a cigar with distinction that proposes a sophisticated blend in which the aging process provides the cigar with a unique and balanced character that is recognizable by its intense aroma and refined and rich flavor full of nuances, which represents a step forward in the complexity level of the brand.

Viaje only makes limited release cigars, but there are some that are more limited than others. The cigars listed on this page such as the Full Moon, Collaboration, and Cache all only come in one size and are very limited in production and release. With so many different blends it is hard to imagine how different each cigar can be from each other, but Andre Farkas has pulled it off. Each smoke is incredibly flavorful all with different notes and different strengths. The one thing that is the same is the exceptional quality you can expect from every cigar you pull out of the box. (See more Viaje Cigars )

Viaje is a brand that believes in quality over quantity. Made in very small batches, each of the Viaje blends is crafted with perfection in mind, and the Platino is no different. A Nicaraguan puro coming from the famed Casa Fernandez factory in the same country, the Platino's key power and flavor comes from its extraordinary Nicaraguan Corojo 99 wrapper. Some may list this as a medium-to-full body; but on our palate it was much closer to medium. Don't let that full you though, the Platino still packs some amazing flavor. With its flawless construction, fantastic flavor, and unparalleled quality, Viaje Platino is a great cigar for everyone's humidor. (See more Viaje Cigars ) Viaje Platino has a beautiful cream and silver band with an image of a tobacco leaf and the foot is wrapped in a silver silk band. The wrapper is astounding. Perfectly rolled to the point of really needing to look very closely in order to find either a vein or even the seam. The light was perfect and this stick never needed a touch up. The flavors that came through were incredibly complex. Pre light there was a distinct coffee flavor coming through the draw, and after torching it was mixed with a fantastic cedar and spice taste. Viaje Platino is the epitome of a fantastic medium-bodied boutique cigar. A great taste mixed with amazing construction makes this a perfect stick for just about any humidor. The coffee flavors pair perfectly with a bit of dark chocolate or a sweeter after-dinner cordial. For a slightly fuller-bodied Viaje, you should give the Oro a shot.

The Viaje Satori is another Limited Edition blend from the small batch masters at Viaje. This Nicaraguan puro features a dark oscuro wrapper. Satori means "sudden spiritual enlightenment" in Japanese. The Satori will be released every year unlike other Viaje limited releases such as the Skull and Bones or their Holiday releases. There have only been 150 – 25 count boxes released in each of the 3 vitolas. (See more Viaje Cigars ) If you like flavor bombs that lack complexity, the Viaje Satori is for you. Perhaps you have a short attention span and don't like to hunt for each and every flavor present in a cigar. If you are a straightforward kind of person, this is the cigar for you.

Villiger is one of those brands that is always lingering in the background while the big, new names take the spotlight, yet it never seems to disappear or go unnoticed. Then, right when you think it’s forgotten about, here comes a phenomenal new blend that takes off! This is certainly the case with Villiger 1888 Nicaragua, one of Villiger’s first blends made at their Nicaraguan factory, Villiger de Nicaragua, which is co-owned by the world-renowned Joya de Nicaragua brand. 1888 Nicaragua was introduced in Europe in 2022, brought to the USA a year later, and now it has exploded as one of Villiger’s biggest hits here in America. A filler blend from Nicaragua and the USA, including a dose of the fabled Pennsylvania Broadleaf, is hugged by a spicy Nicaraguan binder. The wrapper leaf is a golden-brown Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf that adds a bit of classic flavor to the mix and holds the whole package together. A beautiful blue and gold cabinet box houses this premium blend, each cigar wearing royal blue and gold double bands. The packaging screams “luxury,” and appropriately so, as each stick is crafted to offer a luxurious, relaxing smoking experience every single time. An easy draw and a sharp burn are just the start, as volumes of rich, white smoke dance across the palate with each and every puff. White pepper and cedar open things up, but quickly the body of the smoke becomes creamy and savory, with just a hint of citrus and sweetness in the background. Earthy raw tobacco is the star of the show, and notes of cocoa and coffee are noticeable on the crispy finish. Medium-full-bodied and delicately balanced, 1888 Nicaragua could change the way people look at Villiger cigars. Made for the experienced, Villiger 1888 Nicaragua is a medium-full-bodied gem that has everything one could desire from a premium cigar. Complexity, depth, precise construction and consistency, and gorgeous packaging to boot, this isn’t what we Americans have been used to seeing from Villiger. This stick pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or medium-bodied beer and is great for just about any occasion. Fans of such Nicaraguan sticks as Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real Nicaragua or Perdomo Lot 23 will certainly take a liking to the cigar in question, and comparing tasting notes could get very interesting. If you’re a fan of Nicaraguan cigars or just want to try something new and delicious, Villiger 1888 Nicaragua is certainly a cigar worth trying. Don’t take our word for it, though, grab one today and see for yourself!

Some five years after the unusually successful debut of Cuellar Connecticut Kreme, the good folks at Villiger decided it was time to offer something under the Cuellar umbrella on the other end of the spectrum, the darker side, obviously. And so, Villiger Cuellar Black Forest was born. Made like its Connecticut-wrapped sibling at Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic, this dark beauty offers an entirely different smoking experience from what we are used to from Villiger. For this blend, Dominican filler and binder tobacco are used in conjunction with a nearly jet-black Mexican Maduro wrapper. A bold flavor profile combined with precision construction makes for a stick that has earned numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado, the highest being a rock-solid 93 . A black and silver cedar box and black, silver, and green double bands keep the luxurious theme at the forefront, and every single cigar is rolled and box pressed with exacting standards, offering a smooth draw and a razor sharp burn. Cinnamon and black pepper open things up, and are soon joined by the classic maduro profile including coffee, cocoa, and notes of dark espresso. Hints of tea and cedar linger in the background, and the dark chocolate finish is long and heavy. Medium-full-bodied , deep, and complex, Cuellar Black Forest is certainly a cigar that will leave a lasting impression. Made for a more intermediate audience, Cuellar Black Forest is one of the stronger and more flavorful options offered in today’s Villiger lineup. It smokes beautifully and offers a medium-full-bodied journey loaded with flavor and satisfying complexity. Pair this one with your favorite black coffee or dark beer for an amazing smoking experience that will keep you coming back for more. Fans of dark sticks such as La Historia or Rocky Patel Sun Grown Maduro will likely enjoy this blend, as it boasts a similar dark and bold flavor profile. The Black Forest name comes from the Black Forest in Germany, said to have been the inspiration for folklore such as Hansel and Gretel, Rapunzel, and Sleeping Beauty. The real story here, however, is getting a phenomenal smoke at a great price, so take your own venture into the forest today and enjoy one stick that will surely change the way you look at Villiger: Cuellar Black Forest.

Villiger is a brand that has been huge overseas for years, but is just beginning to really take off on the American premium cigar market. Releases such as San D’Oro and Flor de Ynclan certainly turned a huge chunk of the cigar-loving population on to the brand, but the Cuellar lines take the cake in terms of popularity. In particular, the fan favorite award likely goes to Villiger Cuellar Connecticut Kreme . Named after the first Spaniard governor of Cuba, Cuellar Connecticut Kreme is a premium long-filler cigar made at Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic using aged Dominican filler and binder tobacco. The wrapper is a golden brown Connecticut seed leaf, lovingly cultivated in the shady volcanic region of Ecuador. This blend debuted in 2014 and is regarded as one of the smoothest, creamiest Connecticut-wrapped cigars on the market. It has earned many accolades over the years, including a solid 90-rating in Cigar Aficionado . White and gold packaging gives this brand quite the luxurious feel. Lacquered cedar chests and embossed double bands scream of the blend’s opulence and character. A beautiful roll lends to an easy draw every single time. Hints of white pepper, bread crumbs, and vanilla open things up, and soon a cedar note is detectable as the flavor profile builds. Nuances of earthy tobacco and cream mingle together to establish a delightful texture and balance. Floral on the finish, Cuellar Connecticut Kreme finishes as a mild-medium flavor bomb of a cigar. Great for newbies, but truly appreciated by the experienced, this blend leaves nothing more to desire. Mild-medium-bodied, creamy and balanced, it is an easy smoke to enjoy at any time of the day. Whether paired with cafe con leche or your favorite white wine or light beer, this treat will provide a truly relaxing and satisfying smoking experience. Fans of such creamy Connecticuts as Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real or Montecristo Classic will surely come to enjoy the rich, yet mild flavor profile offered by this Dominican beauty. Villiger isn’t just a big name for small cigars anymore. Try a Cuellar Connecticut Kreme today and experience the premium side of Villiger that deserves a spot in every serious connoisseur’s humidor.

Villiger San D'Oro Colorado is among the latest ultra-premium cigar offerings from the infamous Villiger company based in Switzerland. Though they have been around since the 1800s, Villiger has only recently dabbled in the realm of premium cigars. However, their premium portfolio is growing larger year by year, and the San D'Oro line may just be Villiger's best yet. Offered in three formats, Maduro, Claro, and Colorado, the San D'Oro Cigars are made with the serious connoisseur in mind. This gorgeous Colorado version is made down in Nicaragua at Oliva's famous TABOLISA factory using a delicious blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a dark, golden Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Sounds awesome, right? Well, the folks at Cigar Aficionado Magazine thought so too and decided to slap it with a 92-rating and a spot on the Top 25 Cigars of 2016. How's that for making your mark in the premium cigar business? Reddish brown, oily, and slightly rugged in appearance, San D'Oro Colorado shows the characteristics of a Colorado shade cigar. Expert construction and seamless rolling are demonstrated with San D'Oro Colorado, making for a sharp, even burn and a soft, full draw. Thick clouds of white smoke pound the palate with incredible amounts of flavor, beginning with robust Nicaraguan white pepper and soon evolving to a creamy, nutty profile. Hints of cedar, cocoa, and nutmeg linger in the background as a soft honey note finesses the tip of the tongue. A sweet, spicy finish ties the package together, rounding out this phenomenal flavor bouquet in true Oliva fashion. San D'Oro Colorado is medium-bodied and full-flavored, making it a great transition for someone looking to go from lighter sticks into the more full-bodied realm of the cigar world. However, only real aficionados with highly developed palates will be able to appreciate San D'Oro for all it is worth: A well-rounded, complex flavor profile and a full, yet smooth body. San D'Oro Colorado pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or rum, and is made by the same folks responsible for such amazing creations as Oliva Serie V Melanio and Oliva Serie O . So what does San D'Oro mean, anyway? Well, according to the folks at Villiger, tobacco lore says that when Christopher Columbus brought tobacco back to Europe for the first time, it became known as "The Sacred Healing Plant of India," translated from the original Latin "Indorum Sang Sancta," or the Spanish "San D'Oro." Moreover, thus the Villiger San D'Oro series pays homage to such tobacco lore. Cool history lesson, huh? Well, healing plant or not, we cigar freaks love our tobacco, and Villiger San D'Oro Colorado is truly a prime demonstration of just how delicious tobacco can be!

Continuing their trek across the globe looking for the next best place to find the most delicious tobaccos, Warped Cigars has now set foot in the Dominican Republic to bring us the Warped Chinchalle. With a preference for narrow ring-gauges and complex smoking experiences, Warped founder Kyle Gellis is always seeking new sources of rare and well-rested longleaf. He found what he was looking for in Santiago, D.R., the Tabacalera LA iSLA, where a bounty of succulent Dominican tobacco is expertly rolled beneath a sweet Dominican binder, then topped with a silky-smooth Ecuadorian Habano Rosado 2000 wrapper to create a delectable medium-bodied smoke agreeable to a wide range of palates. Easily identified by the idealized illustration of an actual Chinchalle (the Cuban nickname for a very small cigar factory) and the words "Flor Fina" found embossed onto its elegant gold and black band, the Warped Chinchalle offers a richer and more rewarding smoke than you might expect from a simple vitola. Launching with a burst of cedar and vanilla cream, the cigar's thick clouds of smoke soon take on layers of leather and earth and warm spice. Syrupy with the tastes of candied stonefruit and Turkish coffee, the middle third of each stogie will keep your tongue dancing even as the profile shifts one last time during the last couple of inches to contain cocoa, browned butter, and a touch of savory herbs. Whether saved for a special occasion or serving as a high-end daily smoke, the Warped Chinchalle is an excellent addition to your humidor alongside other standout Dominican cigars like the Arturo Fuente Natural or even the AVO Classic. Come see for yourself what makes Warped cigars one of the hottest boutique brands around, we guarantee you won't be disappointed.

A Warped Cloud Hopper cigar will lift your taste buds to realms far above your usual smoking experience, a journey you’ll be looking forward to repeating time and time again. A true boutique brand focused on sourcing tobaccos from the finest growing regions on the planet, Warped Cigars delivers pure flavor and premium quality in every slim stick they produce. Inspired and informed by a love of travel, brand founder Kyle Gellis has built the core of the Cloud Hopper by pairing rich and spicy Nicaraguan Corojo ‘99 with earthy and luxurious Criollo ‘98 longleaf. To complete this high-flying stogie, a Shade Grown Corojo ‘99 from Jalapa brings both balance and excitement to the medium-plus strength profile. Aficionados used to large cigars with huge diameters of an inch or more, of which there have been very many over the past decade, might worry that the sub-50 ring gauge of the Warped Cloud Hopper could deliver the goods. Fear not, for these well-crafted vitola’s are all business and no fluff, ready to soar from the moment of cutting. Starting with a peppery burst, the cigar flares to life at a mere hint of a flame, instantly transforming from an innocent little rocket to a massive flavor-bomb after just a few puffs. Creamy and sweet yet loaded with the tastes of cocoa and orange peel and roasted peanuts and leather and exotic spice to add strength and complexity, your palate might never want to come back down to earth. Comparable in style, flavor, and substance to lofty Nicaraguan smokes like My Father by Don Pepin or the Camacho Corojo, it’s time to board your flight to a new smoking destination with a selection of Warped Cloud Hopper cigars. The best part of the ride is that the ‘Yes Smoking’ sign is always lit for these amazing stogies.

Marking an exciting evolution of Warped Cigars’ celebrated Corto line, Warped Corto Maduro brings a darker, bolder, and more intense expression to one of the brand’s most distinctive series. Originally launched in 2015 as a compact full-bodied Nicaraguan puro, Corto established itself as a flavorful short format crafted for moments when time is limited but quality is essential. A decade later, Warped expanded this beloved marque with Corto Maduro, a line that maintains Corto’s compact, box-pressed identity while introducing a luscious Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over an all-Nicaraguan binder and long-filler core enriched with medio tiempo tobacco for added depth, strength, and complexity. Demonstrating the exceptional quality of the blend, the Warped Corto Maduro X46 earned an impressive 91-point rating from Cigar Aficionado , with tasters praising its bold profile of dark chocolate. Warped’s approach to Corto Maduro stays true to the brand’s boutique philosophy: small batches, thoughtful blending, and intense flavor in a compact format. The maduro wrapper brings a deeper color and richer profile to the Corto platform, layering dark chocolate, black cherry, spice, earth, and natural sweetness with hints of leather and oak for a genuinely full-bodied experience . Produced at the Nicaragua American Cigars S.A. (NACSA) factory in Estelí under the direction of master blender Kyle Gellis, Corto Maduro is available in box-pressed vitolas that preserve that tight, concentrated flavor while delivering optimal draw and balance. Whether you enjoy the flagship X46 (4½″ × 46) or larger maduro formats like the X54, each cigar in the Corto Maduro line offers bold complexity in an expertly crafted short smoke, ideal for aficionados seeking depth without the commitment to a long session.

Warped Eagles Descent is a highly sought-after limited release treat especially intended for the most discriminating lovers of fine cigars. Originally released in 2019 at Hawaii's exclusive R. Field Wine Company, this special concoction takes the idea of a boutique cigar to the extreme. Shortly after its unveiling in Hawaii, Eagles Descent was made available on a national level, but on a very limited basis. The cigar is made in Nicaragua at the AGANORSA-owned TABSA factory and uses only the finest aged tobacco leaves. Being a Nicaraguan puro, all leaves are grown on AGANORSA farms and all come from Nicaragua—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler blend is made up of Corojo and Criollo leaves, meaning the total package is never going to be lacking in the flavor department. The original release was limited to only 4,000 total cigars and is set to be available only at select retailers. Needless to say, those fortunate enough to get their hands on one have had nothing but positive things to report. One simple band adorns each stick, depicting an ornate eagle atop a jet black background. As we all know with Warped cigars, however, the packaging is always simple, but the blend never follows suit. The construction is everything one would expect from a top shelf boutique cigar, meaning a soft, productive draw and plenty of thick, billowing smoke. From the get-go, the rich, earthy core makes its presence known. Around this core, bold notes of cedar and white pepper dance across the palate, tingling the lips with every puff. Cinnamon, raw tobacco, and a faint espresso note round out the profile, and the finish is spicy and clean, with just a hint of citrus on the tip of the tongue. Finishing on the heavy side of full-bodied, Eagles Descent proves to be a bold, yet intricate work of art. It goes without saying that Eagles Descent is meant only for long-time cigar fanatics with highly developed palates. Though the overall theme of the flavor profile may seem simple at a glance, the subtle complexities throughout the smoking experience demand experience in order to be truly appreciated. This stick pairs well with bourbon, Scotch, or dark beer and makes an excellent celebration cigar. Fans of similar premium Nicaraguan puros such as Padron 1964 or Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua should feel right at home while enjoying such a treat as this. Warped Cigars is known for their unique blends, incomparable quality, and exclusive content, and Eagles Descent is certainly a stick that resides in all three departments. Grab it while you can, and thank us later!

Warped never ceases to amaze the cigar world with their ultra-premium concoctions, and the Warped Isla de Cocodrilo cigar is certainly one of their latest and greatest. Made by hand at the small, but busy Tabacalera La Isla factory in the Dominican Republic, this stick uses quite an interesting recipe. The filler blend consists of Nicaraguan leaves, and the cigar has two binders—one Brazilian Arapiraca and the other Ecuadorian Habano 2000. The wrapper is an Ecuador Habano leaf that has been culled using the “Desflorado Method,” where the flower of the tobacco plant is removed in the field, allowing the leaves themselves to grow stronger, yielding a more potent final product. “Isla de Cocodrilo” literally translates to “Island of the Crocodile,” a nickname given to Cuba because some say it is shaped like a crocodile. We are all for cool names, but in all honesty, this one could simply be named “Awesome Cigar” and it would be quite fitting, especially after the prompt pair of 91 ratings this stick earned in Cigar Aficionado shortly after its debut. A single black and gold band done in the classic Warped style adorns each cigar, beautifully complimenting the gorgeous construction and traditional Cuban style triple cap. An easy draw leads to massive smoke production, each puff pounding the palate with an overdose of rich flavor. Isla de Cocodrilo starts off with black pepper and cedar , soon settling into an earthy mix featuring herbal notes and hints of coffee and cinnamon . The main backbone of the cigar is a definitive classic tobacco flavor, much like the classic Cuban cigars of old. Medium-bodied, balanced, and delicious, this cigar displays everything Warped Cigars is known for. Made for the seasoned connoisseur, Isla de Cocodrilo is a cigar that deserves to be savored slowly and with undivided attention. It is complex, easy to smoke, and tame enough for just about any occasion, though those of the “special” variety seem to work best.
