This cigar pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or medium-bodied beer and is similar in stature to cigars such as Montecristo Platinum or Oliva Serie G . Warped may be one of those brands for “those who know,” but it’s no secret that they never fail to produce an amazing cigar. Grab an Isla De Cocodrilo today and experience some of the best of what Warped Cigars has to offer.

La Hacienda First Growth is one of the more popular regular production cigars from Warped. Made at the Casa Fernandez factory in Nicaragua, also known as TABSA, La Hacienda is a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning all leaves used in the production of the blend hail from Nicaragua—wrapper, filler, and binder. The tobacco used for this cigar isn't just any old Nicaraguan leaves, however. In fact, all three components are high-priming, heavily aged Corojo 99 from the AGANORSA Leaf farms. For the filler blend, a dash of Criollo 98 was added to round things out, and the end result is a top-shelf stick that earned a 90 rating soon after its release. Not only is La Hacienda one of the biggest stars of the Warped lineup, but its reasonable price point makes it all the more attractive. Packaged in nearly nondescript cedar chests with each vitola bearing a single, ornate black band, La Hacienda keeps with Warped's theme of keeping things simple. That is, except for when it comes to the flavor profile! When it comes to that, Warped La Hacienda really displays its special attributes. An easy and productive draw offers billowing clouds of silky white smoke, at first light pounding the palate with spicy Nicaraguan white pepper. Soon, aromas of cedar and nuts join the party, along with an underlying black cherry sweetness lingering in the background. An earthy core of robust tobacco flavor holds the package together, and it is appropriate to say that this, like many other Warped blends, truly mimics the unforgettable flavor of the Cubans of old. Medium-full-bodied and beautifully balanced, this cigar offers all the characteristics any true connoisseur could ask for. The First Growth is a 4" x 50 short robusto that offers massive amounts of flavor. The size was named after the term "First Growth" in the Bordeaux Wine Classification of 1855, which denotes top tier vineyards, or the "best of the best." Most Warped sticks are aimed at a more experienced audience, and La Hacienda is no different. The robust medium-full-bodied nature and complex and spicy flavor profile demand a palate that has been there and done that. This cigar pairs well with bourbon or medium-full-bodied beer, but is completely appropriate to pair with coffee as an exciting way to start the day. Fans of fuller-bodied Nicaraguan cigars like Guardian of the Farm or Tatuaje will doubtless be impressed with the Cuban-esque flavor qualities of this blend. With all Warped Cigars, you can always count on getting a high quality cigar for a reasonable price. With Warped La Hacienda First Growth, you can be sure you won't finish one without wanting another.

Warped is one of those cigar brands that lives beneath the radar, yet somehow everyone has heard of it. It’s no surprise, really, as their underground fame can’t help but leech out into the open with incredible cigars like Warped Nicotina. Here, we have a brand that was originally produced in Havana in 1880. Fast forward about a century and a half, and new life is given to the name by none other than the fine folks at Warped, in collaboration with AGANORSA, of course. Blended by Kyle Gellis, and like so many other amazing Warped blends, Nicotina is a true Nicaraguan puro, made in Nicaragua at the TABSA factory using nothing but the finest Nicaraguan leaves from the AGANORSA vault—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler blend is made up of Nicaraguan Criollo ‘98 and Corojo ‘99, and the wrapper is a shade grown Jalapa Corojo ‘99 grown in Nicaragua (an extremely rare specimen in and of itself). Straight out of the gate, Nicotina earned a solid 91 rating in Cigar Aficionado and to this day remains one of Warped’s most successful regular brands. Beautifully simple packaging adds to the splendor of the brand. Simple wooden chests, black and white bands, and nearly nondescript branding make Nicotina as mysterious as it is beautiful. Speaking of its beauty, Nicotina comes in one size: a 5 ½” x 52 box pressed 109, or gentle belicoso, as some would describe it. The slightly tapered head makes for easy cuts, a comfy feel between the teeth, and concentrated, rich flavor. The easy and productive draw of Nicotina produces continuous strands of silky blue smoke, the clouds increasing in size with each puff. Beginning with red pepper and cedar, the flavor profile seems simple and straightforward at first. However, an inch or two in and the real beauty of Nicotina makes itself known: a dazzling array of creamy sweet tobacco, spicy Nicaraguan white pepper, and blasts of chocolate dancing around in the background. An earthy core holds the package together, and the finish is crisp, clean, and strong. This blend finishes as a true full-bodied stick, and appropriately so, as Nicotina is literally Spanish for “Nicotine.” Only the experienced should reach for this cigar. Not only is the profile far too complex to be appreciated by an immature palate, but the strength would be too much for any mere newbie. This full-bodied work of art pairs well with coffee, red wine, or full-bodied beer, and is best enjoyed on a full stomach. It is likely to appeal to a more mature audience, those drawn to full-bodied Nicaraguan cigars such as My Father or Don Pepin Blue Label . Whether you are a long-time fan of the brawny boutique company or just want something rich, strong, and tasty, Warped Nicotina is a top-tier stick more than worth checking out.

Holding hands with the devil has never been more enjoyable than smoking a fine Warped Devil's Hands cigar. Putting to rest the notion that a larger cigar is a tastier cigar, Warped founder Kyle Gellis focuses on maximizing smoking enjoyment while using more traditional small ring vitolas. The Devil's Hands is a 6" x 44 lonsdale, a Nicaraguan Puro packed full of Criollo '98 and Corojo '99 longleaf filler capable of pumping maximum flavor through the stogie's slim barrel. Another Criollo is used as the cigar's binder while the wrapper is a beautifully toothy and aromatic Jalapa Corojo '99 tobacco leaf that has been slowly Shade Grown and aged to creamy perfection. A long and elegant cigar, each Warped Devil's Hands is flawlessly rolled and impeccably dressed in the leathery Jalapa wrapper. Held aloft by the hands of the horned devil depicted on the stick's bright-red band are a trident and a leaf of tobacco, his pose both welcoming and little menacing. The same can be said for the rich smoke that pours in great plumes from the narrow barrel as soon as it is lit, where first there's a spicy kick of black pepper and smoked paprika only to have the palate soothed by butterscotch soon after. As the cigar steadily burns, layers of earthy toasted oak and black walnut build upon each other, with bursts of mocha, cinnamon, vanilla rice pudding, and just a touch of chili pepper to conjure a sinfully delicious experience you'll wish could last for eternity. Released in 2021 after years of planning, you won't have to sell your soul to get your own hands on some Warped Devil's Hands. Packed into generous boxes of 25, these are excellent and reliable medium-full strength companions to bring balance to your collection of light and heavenly Montecristo White and potent, beast-like Perdomo Inmenso Seventy Sun-Grown .

Every so often, the fine people at Davidoff Cigars give us something new to get excited about, and such is exactly the case with Zino Nicaragua. The latest cigar to bear the Zino name, Zino Nicaragua is actually made in Honduras, at the famous Diadema Cigars de Honduras S.A. owned by Davidoff. The theme for this blend seems to be simplicity and value, all at the same time not sacrificing in the flavor department. Speaking of flavor, there is no shortage here, as a whopping filler blend boasts of tobacco from all 3 major cigar countries, including San Vicente and San Vicente Mejorado Secos from the Dominican Republic, Olancho and Jamastran Visus from Honduras, and Ometepe Visus from Nicaragua. The binder is a Nicaragua Semilla 56 Seco leaf, and a golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper ties it all together.
Spicy , Chocolate , Vanilla Available. Learn about Zino Platinum Crown Series Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Platinum Crown Series

Developed for the discerning aficionado, the Zino Platinum Crown Series is a luxury cigar for the sophisticated palate. No expense was spared and no shortcuts were taken by their creators, those kings of quality at Oettinger Davidoff. To bring about this paragon of smoking enjoyment, three types of Dominican ligero, a Piloto and two types of San Vicente, are used to create the bulk of the strikingly complex blend. The remaining 25% of the filler is also ligero, a top quality longleaf Habano from Peru. These tobaccos were rested for up to 5 years before being rolled within a US Connecticut binder, itself aged for 4 years before being encased beneath an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.
Coffee , Cocoa , Nutty Available. Learn about Zino Platinum Scepter Series Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Platinum Scepter Series

Zino Cigar by Davidoff is a name synonymous with high quality and flavorful mild cigars, and their Platinum Scepter series is no exception. Blended by the master Henke Kelner at the renowned Tabadom Factory, this cigar may be mild but it sure packs a lot of flavor. A unique filler of 3-year aged Dominican filler mixed with rare Peruvian tobacco is bound by a 4-year aged Connecticut binder and an ultra-sleek 1-year-aged Ecuadorian wrapper. The nuances in flavor found in this cigar are the epitome of luxury. Packaged in unique tubes, cannisters, or three-packs, the sight of the silver band with the classic Zino "Z" is the first sign the Platinum Scepter is something special. On close inspection it is hard to find a flaw in the wrapper, and as expected the burn was straight as an arrow. When feeling the cigar it is amazingly dense, but the draw is extraordinarily smooth. The beauty of the Zino Platinum Scepter is the mild-bodied body that allows the fantastic flavors of the tobacco shine. A fantastic aroma fills the nose as subtle earthiness envelops that palate. A fantastic smoke with a long finish that never crosses over to being harsh. The price may be a bit of a sticker shock, but Zino Platinum Scepter is an amazing smoke for those special occasions that warrant a great cigar. The smoothness of this cigar pairs well with lighter cocktails such as a white wine or a gin and tonic. Other great Zino cigars are the Zino Crown Series or the Zino Z-Class.

note_sources.text: Zino is well known for its fantastic and luxurious mild-bodied cigars, and while the Platinum Z-Class is still two of those things, it is a departure from the mild realm into the heavier medium-to-full-bodied range. Created after the wild success of the Platinum Crown and Scepter series, Z-Class was created to embody ambition and opulence. A new blend of a perfectly aged Dominican wrapper, a Peruvian binder, and Nicaraguan and Honduran filler tobacco give this stick a wonderful body and a very complex flavor.

hoyo-de-monterrey-le-hoyo-de-rio-seco.name: Le Hoyo de Río Seco

note_sources.text: Habanos S.A. (2019/2020 launch): 'Le Hoyo de Rio Seco' (factory vitola Aromosos, 56 x 140 mm) joins the Linea Le Hoyo. Seco, volado and ligero leaves come exclusively from the San Juan y Martinez district, a Protected Appellation of Origin in Vuelta Abajo, forming a smooth flavour blend that is consistent and intense thanks to the area's soil. Described as delicate, aromatic, with great elegance and complexity - 'an appealing option for those who like Habanos with less strength'. Sold in 25-count SLB and later 10-count boxes, plus tubos.

Cigar Aficionado (91 pts, medium): 'floral atop a foundation of assorted nuts, chocolate, oak and a hint of graham cracker.' Cigar Obsession: medium-full body; creamy, nutty opening with zesty earthiness, then deeper earth, honey and dry cocoa on the finish; midpoint sweet cream, earth, cocoa with a light coffee finish.

specs.filler: Cuba (San Juan y Martinez, Vuelta Abajo)

hoyo-de-monterrey-le-hoyo-de-rio-seco.research_note: Full name is 'Le Hoyo de Rio Seco' (Linea Le Hoyo). Habanos positions it as lower strength; CA rates medium, Cigar Obsession medium-full body. 'mild to medium' chosen per Habanos; 'medium' is also defensible. 'graham cracker' mapped to bread; 'chocolate' to dark_chocolate.

note_sources.text: Same brand copy as the rest of the JLP range: filler tobaccos grown only in the Remedios region, hand-made short filler; retailer (C.Gars Ltd) describes the Brevas as delivering 'a medium Cuban flavour' and being 'a reliable everyday smoke'.

CigarsLover: body very mild rising to mild-to-medium, strength 'quite minimal'. Pre-light mild earth and walnut. Smoke opens with a dominant mineral note, intense bark, medium coffee, walnut and background balsamic notes; later a growing slight bitterness and a papery taste, bark and walnut persist, little evolution.

specs.filler: Cuba (short filler, Remedios / Vuelta Arriba region)

note_sources.text: Habanos S.A. value brand, filler grown only in the Remedios (formerly Vuelta Arriba) region. Made 'totalmente a mano, tripa corta' (hand-made, short filler). Retailer/Habanos brand copy: a distinct, somewhat rustic, medium-to-full taste from the Remedios tobaccos; 'a cigar for the great outdoors'. (C.Gars Ltd / Smoke King brand text; no vitola-specific Habanos flavour text found.)

halfwheel (2021): starts mild, builds to just short of medium. Peanut butter and cedar dominate, with cinnamon, earth, leather, hay and pencil lead behind; white pepper and vanilla on the retrohale. Second half: dank earth, tree bark, leather, sourdough bread, citrus, popcorn, cocoa nibs, tea leaves, touch of floral. CigarsLover: medium strength; pepper, wood and coffee with light bitterness, coffee shifting to espresso.

specs.filler: Cuba (short filler, Remedios / Vuelta Arriba region)

MUWAT (My Uzi Weighs a Ton) cigars are full-bodied monsters that are the product of collaboration between Drew Estate and Joya de Nicaragua. It all started in the renowned Joya de Nicaragua factory during a consumer blending session on a Cigar Safari Tour back in 2010. After hosting blending sessions for the tour at their own factory over the previous 3 years, Drew Estate decided to reach out to Joya de Nicaragua. Long story short, Jonathan Drew ended up forming a tight relationship with Joya de Nicaragua and over the next several months came up with an ultra-premium, surprisingly bold and flavorful cigar set to be named “The Uzi.” That was, until the fateful day Jonathan Drew picked up a satchel of the freshly rolled monster cigars and exclaimed “My Uzi weighs a TON!” Thus the new name would stick around forever. The blend itself is simple, yet perfectly put together. Bold Nicaraguan and Brazilian filler leaves are rolled in Connecticut broadleaf maduro binders and then embraced in a jet-black San Andres Negro wrapper. They are ultra-powerful and not for the faint of heart. Ultra modern packaging includes extra large bands with military style lettering. The fateful collaboration between Joya de Nicaragua and Subculture Studios is boldly noted beneath the name. Expert construction provides a well-built cigar comparable to some of the finest cigars in the world. The draw is easy and the huge cigars give off a plenteous amount of thick gray smoke. Following a steady, heavy dose of pepper in the back of the throat, bold coffee and cocoa flavors join subtle sweetness and a core of rich tobacco to bring together a rich, velvety smooth beast of a cigar. Whether you’re a strength junkie, a fan of massive cigars, or a Drew Estate nut, MUWAT is a must try. It is an example of how two of the biggest names in the business can join forces to make a knockout smoke that will indubitably dominate the market. Rich, bold, and on the far end of the full-bodied category, MUWAT pairs well with any strong red wine or dark beer. Comparable cigars include Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970 , Liga Privada T52 , and Nica Rustica —all cigars under the ever-expanding Drew Estate umbrella. The name is different, the blend top-notch, and the sizes are out of this world. Bottom line: Don’t let the funny name fool you—MUWAT is a serious cigar for serious smokers.
